Matthew.title: The Main Event—Jesus is Born
paragraphs: Think of this as Jesus’s ancestry report. It proves he has the royal bloodline of King David and traces his roots all the way back to Abraham, the father of the Jewish faith.
Instead of reading a massive list of hard-to-pronounce names, here is the breakdown of how the generations stack up:
§Era 1: The Founding Fathers
There were fourteen generations from Abraham (who started it all) down to King David (the warrior king).
§Era 2: The Kings and the Collapse
There were fourteen generations from King David until the time the nation of Israel got conquered and dragged off to Babylon as prisoners.
§Era 3: The Waiting Game
There were fourteen generations from the time they were taken to Babylon all the way up to the birth of Jesus, the Messiah.
Here is how the birth of Jesus Christ actually went down.
His mom, Mary, was engaged to be married to Joseph. But before the wedding, and before they had ever slept together, Mary found out she was pregnant by the Holy Spirit.

Joseph was a really good, honorable guy. He obviously knew the baby wasn't his, but he didn't want to ruin Mary’s life or embarrass her in front of the whole town. So, he made a plan to quietly break off the engagement and just walk away.
But while he was stressing out and trying to figure this all out, he fell asleep. An angel of God showed up in his dream and said:

"Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to go ahead and marry Mary. The baby she is carrying is from the Holy Spirit. She is going to have a son, and you are going to name him Jesus (which means 'God saves'), because he is going to save his people from their sins."
This whole crazy situation actually happened to back up a promise God had made through a prophet hundreds of years earlier. The prophet had said:
"Watch this: a virgin will get pregnant and have a baby boy. They will call him Immanuel" (which translates to "God is right here with us").

When Joseph woke up from the dream, he didn't hesitate. He stepped up and did exactly what the angel told him to do. He went through with the wedding and brought Mary home as his wife. However, they didn't sleep together until after she had the baby.
When the baby was born, Joseph named him Jesus.

Matthew.title: The Stargazers, the Psycho King, and the Escape
paragraphs: Jesus was born in the town of Bethlehem during the rule of King Herod. Not long after, a group of scholars (basically ancient astronomers) arrived in Jerusalem from the East. They started asking around, "Where is the newborn King of the Jews? We saw his star rising and came to pay our respects."

When King Herod heard this, he panicked. He was notoriously paranoid, and the idea of a rival king made him lose his mind. He called a secret meeting with the religious experts and asked them exactly where the Messiah was supposed to be born. They told him: "Bethlehem."
Herod secretly met with the scholars and told them, "Go find the kid. When you do, let me know so I can go 'worship' him too." (Spoiler: He actually wanted to assassinate him.)

The scholars followed the star right to the house where Jesus was. They were blown away. They bowed down, worshipped him, and unpacked some incredibly expensive gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh. But that night, God warned them in a dream not to trust Herod, so they snuck back to their home country using a different route.
§The Midnight Road Trip

After the scholars left, an angel woke Joseph up in the middle of the night: "Get up! Take the baby and his mom and run to Egypt. Herod is sending a crew of enforcers. Stay there until I give you the all-clear."
Joseph didn't ask questions; he packed up and they fled under the cover of darkness.
When Herod realized the scholars had ghosted him, he went into a blind rage. He ordered his soldiers to go into Bethlehem and kill every baby boy under the age of two. It was an absolute tragedy.

Eventually, Herod died. The angel appeared to Joseph again in Egypt and said, "It's safe now. You can go back." But because Herod's brutal son was now in charge of the southern region (Judea), Joseph took his family north to the region of Galilee. They settled in a tough little town called Nazareth.

Matthew.title: Enter John the Baptist
paragraphs: Fast forward about thirty years. Jesus's cousin, John the Baptist, showed up in the Judean desert preaching a massive wake-up call.

John was a wild guy. He wore clothes made of rough camel hair with a leather belt, and his diet consisted of locusts and wild honey. His message was simple: "Change your life! God's kingdom is right here, right now!" People were flocking out to the desert by the thousands to admit their mistakes and get baptized by him in the Jordan River.
But when John saw the stuck-up religious leaders (the Pharisees and Sadducees) showing up, he called them out:

"You bunch of snakes! Who warned you to run from the coming fire? Don't just show up and expect a free pass because you have a religious background. Prove it! Show me that your life has actually changed!"
Then, the main event happened: Jesus walked up to the river to be baptized. John tried to stop him, saying, "Wait, I need you to baptize me."
But Jesus insisted, "Do it anyway. It's the right way to do things."

The moment Jesus came up out of the water, the sky split open. The Spirit of God came down like a dove and landed on him, and a booming voice from heaven said: "This is my Son. I love him, and I am incredibly proud of him."

Matthew.title: The Desert Showdown and the First Crew
paragraphs: Immediately after his baptism, the Spirit led Jesus deep into the wilderness to be tested by the devil. Jesus went without food for forty days and forty nights. He was starving.
The devil stepped in and tried to get in his head.
§Strike 1
"If you're really God's Son, turn these rocks into bread." Jesus shut him down: "People need more than bread to survive; they need the words of God."
§Strike 2
The devil took him to the highest point of the Temple. "Jump! The angels will catch you." Jesus replied: "Don't test God."
§Strike 3
The devil showed him all the kingdoms of the world. "I'll give you all this power and wealth if you just bow down to me." Jesus ordered him out: "Get out of here, Satan. You only worship God."
The devil lost, packed up, and left. Angels came and took care of Jesus.

Building the Team Jesus moved to the town of Capernaum by the lake and officially started his mission. Walking down the beach, he saw two brothers—Peter and Andrew—throwing their nets into the water. They were commercial fishermen.

Jesus called out, "Drop the nets and follow me. I'll teach you how to fish for people!" They didn't even hesitate. They dropped their gear and followed him. A little further down, he saw two more brothers, James and John, fixing their nets in a boat with their dad. Jesus called them too. They left the boat, left their dad, and joined the crew.
Word about Jesus went viral. He started healing everyone—people with diseases, chronic pain, seizures, you name it. Massive crowds from all over the country started following him everywhere.

Matthew.title: The Sermon on the Mount (The Rulebook Flip)
paragraphs: Seeing the massive crowd, Jesus hiked up a hill, sat down with his disciples, and started dropping absolute truth bombs. This is the greatest speech ever given, where Jesus explains that living God's way is the exact opposite of what the world tells you.
§The Beatitudes
"You're blessed when you're at the end of your rope. With less of you, there is more of God and his rule."
"You're blessed when you feel you've lost what is most dear to you. Only then can you be embraced by the One most dear to you."
"You're blessed when you're content with just who you are—no more, no less. That's the moment you find yourselves proud owners of everything that can't be bought."
"You're blessed when you've worked up a good appetite for God. He's food and drink in the best meal you'll ever eat."
"You're blessed when you care. At the moment of being 'care-full,' you find yourselves cared for."
"You're blessed when you get your inside world—your mind and heart—put right. Then you can see God in the outside world."
"You're blessed when you can show people how to cooperate instead of compete or fight. That's when you discover who you really are, and your place in God's family."
"You're blessed when your commitment to God provokes persecution. The persecution drives you even deeper into God's kingdom."

"Count yourselves blessed every time people put you down or throw you out or speak lies about you to discredit me. What it means is that the truth is too close for comfort and they are uncomfortable. You can be glad when that happens—give a cheer, even!—for though they don't like it, I do! And all heaven applauds. You are in good company. My prophets and witnesses have always gotten into this kind of trouble."
§Salt and Light

"Let me tell you why you are here. You're here to be salt-seasoning that brings out the God-flavors of this earth. If you lose your saltiness, how will people taste godliness? You've lost your usefulness and will end up in the garbage."

"Here's another way to put it: You're here to be light, bringing out the God-colors in the world. God is not a secret to be kept. We're going public with this, as public as a city on a hill. If I make you light-bearers, you don't think I'm going to hide you under a bucket, do you? I'm putting you on a light stand. Now that I've put you there on a hilltop, on a light stand—shine! Keep open house; be generous with your lives. By opening up to others, you'll prompt people to open up with God, this generous Father in heaven."
§Completing God's Law

"Don't suppose for a minute that I have come to demolish the Scriptures—either God's Law or the Prophets. I'm not here to demolish but to complete. I am going to put it all together, pull it all together in a vast panorama. God's Law is more real and lasting than the stars in the sky and the ground at your feet. Long after stars burn out and earth wears out, God's Law will be alive and working."

"Trivialize even the smallest item in God's Law and you will only have trivialized yourself. But take it seriously, show the way for others, and you will find honor in the kingdom. Unless you do far better than the Pharisees in the matters of right living, you won't know the first thing about entering the kingdom."
§On Anger

"You're familiar with the command to the ancients, 'Do not murder.' I'm telling you that anyone who is so much as angry with a brother or sister is guilty of murder. Carelessly call a brother 'idiot!' and you just might find yourself hauled into court. Thoughtlessly yell 'stupid!' at a sister and you are on the brink of hellfire. The simple moral fact is that words kill."

"This is how I want you to conduct yourself in these matters. If you enter your place of worship and, about to make an offering, you suddenly remember a grudge a friend has against you, abandon your offering, leave immediately, go to this friend and make things right. Then and only then, come back and work things out with God."
§On Lust

"You know the next commandment pretty well, too: 'Don't go to bed with another's spouse.' But don't think you've preserved your virtue simply by staying out of bed. Your heart can be corrupted by lust even quicker than your body. Those ogling looks you think nobody notices—they also corrupt."

"Let's not pretend this is easier than it really is. If you want to live a morally pure life, here's what you have to do: You have to blind your right eye the moment you catch it in a lustful leer. You have to choose to live one-eyed or else be dumped on a moral trash pile."
§On Divorce

"Remember the Scripture that says, 'Whoever divorces his wife, let him do it legally, giving her divorce papers and her legal rights'? Too many of you are using that as a cover for selfishness and whim, pretending to be righteous just because you are 'legal.' Please, no more pretending."
§On Oaths

"And don't say anything you don't mean. This counsel is embedded deep in our traditions. You only make things worse when you lay down a smoke screen of pious talk, saying, 'I'll pray for you,' and never doing it, or saying, 'God be with you,' and not meaning it. You don't make your words true by embellishing them with religious lace. In making your speech sound more religious, it becomes less true. Just say 'yes' and 'no.' When you manipulate words to get your own way, you go wrong."
§On Revenge

"Here's another old saying that deserves a second look: 'Eye for eye, tooth for tooth.' Is that going to get us anywhere? Here's what I propose: 'Don't hit back at all.' If someone strikes you, stand there and take it. If someone drags you into court and sues for the shirt off your back, giftwrap your best coat and make a present of it. And if someone takes unfair advantage of you, use the occasion to practice the servant life. No more tit-for-tat stuff. Live generously."
§On Enemies

"You're familiar with the old written law, 'Love your friend,' and its unwritten companion, 'Hate your enemy.' I'm challenging that. I'm telling you to love your enemies. Let them bring out the best in you, not the worst. When someone gives you a hard time, respond with the energies of prayer, for then you are working out of your true selves, your God-created selves."

"This is what God does. He gives his best—the sun to warm and the rain to nourish—to everyone, regardless: the good and bad, the nice and nasty. If all you do is love the lovable, do you expect a bonus? Anybody can do that. If you simply say hello to those who greet you, do you expect a medal? Any run-of-the-mill sinner does that."
"In a word, what I'm saying is, Grow up. You're kingdom subjects. Now live like it. Live out your God-created identity. Live generously and graciously toward others, the way God lives toward you."

Matthew.title: How to Actually Live It Out (Sermon on the Mount, Part 2)
paragraphs: Jesus kept rolling with his speech, shifting to how we practice our faith. His main point? Don't be a show-off.
§On Giving

When you help someone out or give to charity, don't hire a marching band to announce it. Do it quietly. Keep it a secret between you and God. If you do it just to get applause from people, that applause is all the reward you’re going to get.
§On Prayer

When you pray, don't act like a theatrical actor just trying to impress the crowd. And don't just babble on and on thinking God only hears you if you use a lot of words. God is your Father; he already knows what you need.
The Playbook for Prayer Jesus gave them a template for how to pray. It goes like this:

"Our Father in heaven, show us who you are. Make the world down here look exactly like it does up there. Keep us alive with three square meals today. Forgive us for the stuff we’ve done wrong, exactly how we forgive the people who mess up against us. Keep us safe from ourselves and the Devil."

On Money and Stress: Don't spend your life hoarding a bunch of stuff that will just rust, break, or get stolen. Invest in things that actually matter to God. You can't worship both God and money. You have to pick a side.

On Worrying: Stop stressing out about what you're going to eat or what you're going to wear. Look at the birds—they don't have bank accounts, but God feeds them. Look at the wildflowers—they don't go shopping, but they look awesome. You are way more important to God than birds and flowers. Stop worrying about tomorrow. Tomorrow has enough trouble of its own. Just focus on honoring God today.

Matthew.title: Stop Playing Referee (Sermon on the Mount, Finale)
paragraphs: Jesus wrapped up his massive speech with some hard-hitting advice:

On Judging Others: Stop playing referee for everyone else's life. Don't pick on someone for having a tiny speck of sawdust in their eye when you have a massive telephone pole sticking out of your own. Fix your own mess first.
The Golden Rule: It all boils down to this: Treat other people exactly how you want them to treat you.
The Two Paths: Enter through the narrow gate. The road to hell is a massive, multi-lane highway, and everyone is on it. The road to life is an off-road trail, and it takes effort to find it.

The Rock vs. The Sand: If you listen to my words and actually do them, you are like a smart builder who builds his house on solid rock. When the storms come and the wind batters the house, it stands firm. But if you hear these words and ignore them, you're like a fool who builds his house on the beach. When the hurricane hits, that house is going to collapse completely.
When Jesus finished, the crowd was completely mind-blown. He didn't sound like their boring old religious teachers; he spoke with absolute authority.

Matthew.title: Jesus Shows His Power
paragraphs: When Jesus came down the mountain, the crowds followed him, and things got crazy. This chapter is basically a highlight reel of Jesus proving he has power over everything.
§Power over Disease
A guy covered in leprosy (a highly contagious, flesh-eating skin disease) walked right up to Jesus. Everyone else would have run away, but Jesus reached out, touched him, and instantly healed him.
§Power over Distance

A Roman military commander (a Centurion) came to Jesus, begging him to heal his paralyzed servant. Jesus offered to go to his house, but the commander said, "No need. I know how authority works. You don't have to be there; just say the word, and my servant will be healed." Jesus was amazed by his faith and healed the servant from miles away.
§Power over Nature

Jesus and his crew got into a boat to cross the lake. Jesus fell asleep. Suddenly, a massive, life-threatening storm whipped up. The disciples were terrified and woke him up screaming, "We're going to drown!" Jesus stood up, told the wind and the waves to "Chill out," and the lake went dead calm instantly. His crew was terrified, whispering, "Who is this guy? Even the weather listens to him!"
§Power over Demons

On the other side of the lake, two insanely violent guys possessed by demons charged at Jesus. The demons recognized Jesus, got terrified, and begged him to send them into a nearby herd of pigs instead of destroying them. Jesus said, "Go." The demons went into the pigs, and the entire herd stampeded off a cliff into the lake.

Matthew.title: The Haters Show Up
paragraphs: Jesus crossed back over the lake to his home base.

Some guys brought their paralyzed friend to Jesus on a stretcher. Jesus looked at the paralyzed man and said, "Cheer up, buddy. Your sins are forgiven." The religious leaders in the room started grumbling under their breath, "Who does this guy think he is? Only God can forgive sins! This is blasphemy."

Jesus knew exactly what they were thinking. He said, "What's harder to say: 'Your sins are forgiven' or 'Get up and walk'?" Just to prove he had the authority to do both, he looked at the paralyzed guy and said, "Get up, grab your mat, and go home." The guy stood right up and walked out. The crowd went wild.

Drafting the Traitor Later, Jesus saw a guy named Matthew sitting at a tax collection booth. (Note: Tax collectors were hated because they worked for the occupying Roman army and usually scammed their own people out of money). Jesus just walked up and said, "Follow me." Matthew quit his job on the spot and threw a massive dinner party for Jesus, inviting all his shady friends. The religious leaders were disgusted that Jesus was hanging out with "losers and sinners." Jesus heard them and dropped this line: "Healthy people don't need a doctor—sick people do. I didn't come to recruit the 'perfect' people; I came for the misfits."

Jesus then went on a healing spree: he cured a woman who had been bleeding uncontrollably for twelve years, brought a dead twelve-year-old girl back to life, gave two blind men their sight, and healed a guy who couldn't speak.

Matthew.title: The First Road Trip
paragraphs: Jesus looked at the massive crowds and felt a deep ache in his gut for them. They were confused and aimless, like a flock of sheep without a shepherd.

He realized he needed a bigger team. He officially appointed his twelve main disciples (Peter, Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon, and Judas Iscariot) and gave them his own authority to heal the sick and kick out demons.
He gave them their pre-game locker room speech before sending them out on their first mission:

"Don't pack extra bags, extra money, or backup shoes. Just go. Heal the sick, raise the dead, and tell them God's kingdom is here. But listen to me: I am sending you out like sheep into a pack of wolves. You need to be as sharp as snakes but as innocent as doves. People are going to hate you because of me. You’ll get dragged into courts and beaten up. But don't panic about what to say—the Spirit of God will give you the words when the time comes. Don't be afraid of guys who can only kill your body. Fear the God who holds your actual soul. You are incredibly valuable to Him; He even knows exactly how many hairs are on your head. If you claim me in front of the world, I'll claim you in front of my Father. If you ghost me, I'll ghost you. This isn't a safe, easy path. If you want to follow me, you have to be willing to lose everything. But if you give your life away for my sake, you'll finally figure out what it means to actually live."

Matthew.title: Doubts, Whiners, and Real Rest
paragraphs: John the Baptist had been locked up in prison, and sitting in a dark cell was messing with his head. He sent his own crew to ask Jesus, "Are you really the Messiah we've been waiting for, or should we keep looking?"

Jesus told them, "Go back and tell John exactly what you're seeing: blind people are getting their sight back, paralyzed guys are walking, deaf people are hearing, and the dead are waking up. Tell him not to second-guess me."
§After they left, Jesus talked to the crowd about John:

"What did you expect to see out in the desert? A guy in a fancy silk suit? No, those guys live in palaces. John is a prophet—the toughest, greatest guy who ever lived. But honestly, even the least important person in God's kingdom is better off than him."

Then Jesus called out the people of his generation for being absolutely impossible to please. They were like whiny kids playing games in the street. When John came, he was super strict and didn't drink, and people said he had a demon. When Jesus came, he went to parties and ate with shady people, and they called him a glutton and a drunk.
The Ultimate Invitation Jesus then dropped one of his most famous, comforting lines for anyone feeling burned out:

"Are you tired? Worn out? Exhausted from trying to follow all the religious rules perfectly? Come hang with me. I'll show you how to take a real rest. Walk with me and work with me—watch how I do it. Learn the unforced rhythms of grace. I won't lay anything heavy or ill-fitting on you. Keep company with me and you'll learn to live freely and lightly."

Matthew.title: Rule-Breakers and the Unforgivable Sin
paragraphs: It was the Sabbath (the strict day of rest), and Jesus's crew was hungry. They were walking through a wheat field and grabbed a few handfuls of grain to snack on. The religious police (the Pharisees) immediately threw a flag on the play: "Look! Your guys are breaking the rules by 'harvesting' on the day of rest!"
Jesus shut them down: "Haven't you read what King David did when his guys were starving? He ate the holy bread from the temple. Listen, I am in charge of the Sabbath."

Later that day, Jesus went into their meeting place and saw a guy with a crippled hand. The Pharisees watched closely, waiting to see if he'd heal the guy so they could arrest him for "working" on the weekend. Jesus looked at them and said, "If your only sheep fell into a pit on a Saturday, you'd pull it out. A human is way more valuable than a sheep!" He told the man to stretch out his hand, and it was instantly healed. The Pharisees stormed out and started plotting how to assassinate Jesus.
The Logic Drop Jesus later healed a guy who was blind, mute, and demon-possessed. The Pharisees tried to spread a rumor that Jesus was getting his power from Satan.

Jesus called them out on how foolish that sounded: "Why would Satan fight his own guys? A country that fights a civil war destroys itself. If I'm kicking out demons, I'm doing it by God's Spirit, which means God's kingdom just crashed your party."

The Pharisees then demanded he do a magic trick to prove he was from God. Jesus said, "The only sign you're getting is the sign of Jonah. Just like Jonah spent three days inside a massive fish, the Son of Man is going to spend three days buried in the earth."

Matthew.title: The Master Storyteller
paragraphs: Jesus went down to the lake, and the crowd was so massive he had to get into a boat and teach from the water while everyone sat on the beach. He started teaching in "parables" (stories that hide a massive truth inside an everyday example).
The Story of the Dirt He told them about a farmer planting seeds:
Some seed fell on the hard path, and birds ate it immediately. (People who hear God's word but don't care, so evil snatches it away.)
Some fell in gravel. It sprouted fast but burned up in the sun because it had no roots. (People who get hyped about God at a camp or retreat, but quit the second life gets tough.)
Some fell in the weeds and got choked out. (People who hear the message, but get too distracted by trying to get rich or looking cool, so their faith dies.)
Some fell in good, rich dirt and produced a massive harvest. (People who hear it, understand it, and actually let it change their lives.)
§More Truth Bombs
The Treasure: God's kingdom is like finding a massive treasure chest buried in a field. You'd happily go sell your phone, your Xbox, your shoes—literally everything you own—just to buy that field.
The Pearl: It's like a collector finding the rarest pearl on earth. You trade everything else away to get it because it's worth it.

Jesus eventually went back to his hometown of Nazareth, but the people there wouldn't take him seriously. They said, "Wait, isn't this the carpenter's kid? We know his brothers." Because they refused to believe in him, he didn't do many miracles there.

Matthew.title: A Gruesome Death and Walking on Water
paragraphs: Trigger warning: Things get dark for a second. King Herod (the ruler of that area) heard what was being said about Jesus. He told his servants, "This has to be John the Baptist come back from the dead. That's why he's able to work miracles!"

Here's the backstory: Herod had arrested John, put him in chains, and sent him to prison to placate Herodias, his brother Philip's wife. John had provoked Herod by naming his relationship with Herodias "adultery." Herod wanted to kill him, but he was afraid because so many people revered John as a prophet of God.

But at his birthday celebration, he got his chance. Herodias's daughter danced for the guests. She swept Herod away. In his drunken enthusiasm, he promised her on oath anything she wanted. Already coached by her mother, she was ready: "Give me, served up on a platter, the head of John the Baptist." That sobered the king up fast. Unwilling to lose face with his VIP guests, he did it—ordered John's head cut off and presented to the girl on a platter. She in turn gave it to her mother. Later, John's disciples got the body, gave it a reverent burial, and reported to Jesus.
§Feeding the 5,000

When Jesus got the news, he slipped away by boat to an out-of-the-way place by himself. But someone saw him and the word got around. Soon a lot of people from the nearby villages walked around the lake to where he was. When he saw them coming, he was overcome with compassion and healed their sick.
Toward evening the disciples approached him. "We're out in the country and it's getting late. Dismiss the people so they can go to the villages and get some supper."
But Jesus said, "There is no need to dismiss them. You give them supper."
"All we have are five loaves of bread and two fish," they said.

Jesus said, "Bring them here." Then he had the people sit on the grass. He took the five loaves and two fish, lifted his face to heaven in prayer, blessed, broke, and gave the bread to the disciples. The disciples then gave the food to the congregation. They all ate their fill. They gathered twelve baskets of leftovers. About five thousand men were fed, plus women and kids.
§Walking on Water

As soon as the meal was finished, he insisted that the disciples get in the boat and go on ahead to the other side while he dismissed the people. With the crowd dispersed, he climbed the mountain so he could be by himself and pray. He stayed there alone, late into the night.

Meanwhile, the boat was far out to sea when the wind came up against them and they were battered by the waves. At about four o'clock in the morning, Jesus came toward them walking on the water. They were scared to death. "A ghost!" they said, crying out in terror.
But Jesus was quick to comfort them. "Courage, it's me. Don't be afraid."
Peter, suddenly bold, said, "Master, if it's really you, call me to come to you on the water."
He said, "Come ahead."
Jumping out of the boat, Peter walked on the water to Jesus. But when he looked down at the waves churning beneath his feet, he lost his nerve and started to sink. He cried, "Master, save me!"
Jesus didn't hesitate. He reached down and grabbed his hand. Then he said, "Faint-heart, what got into you?"
The two of them climbed into the boat, and the wind died down. The disciples in the boat, having watched the whole thing, worshiped Jesus, saying, "This is it! You are God's Son for sure!"
§Healing at Gennesaret

On return, they beached the boat at Gennesaret. When the people got wind that he was back, they sent out word through the neighborhood and rounded up all the sick, who asked for permission to touch the edge of his coat. And whoever touched him was healed.

Matthew.title: Fake Rules and a Savage Faith
paragraphs: Some religious experts came from Jerusalem to complain about Jesus's crew: "Why don't your disciples follow the tradition of doing the special ceremonial hand-washing before they eat?"
Jesus fired back, "Why do you guys break God's actual commandments just to keep your own made-up traditions? You guys are hypocrites. You act so holy on the outside, but your hearts are corrupt."

He pulled the crowd close and said, "Listen and understand this: It's not the food you put into your mouth that makes you dirty or toxic. It's the garbage that comes out of your mouth—the lies, the trash-talk, the hate—that proves you're toxic on the inside."

A Mother won't take No for an answer Jesus left Israel and went into foreign territory. A Canaanite woman (a total outsider to the Jews) started screaming, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy! My daughter is tortured by a demon!"

Jesus ignored her at first to test her, and his disciples tried to shoo her away. Finally, Jesus said to her, "I was sent to help the lost sheep of Israel. It's not right to take the children's food and toss it to the dogs."
She didn't flinch. She clapped right back, "That's true, Lord. But even the dogs get to eat the crumbs that fall off their master's table."
Jesus smiled. "Woman, your faith is absolutely massive! You've got what you asked for." Her daughter was healed that exact moment.

Jesus then headed back to the lake, healed a bunch more people, and pulled off another massive catering miracle—this time feeding 4,000 men (plus families) using just seven loaves of bread and a few little fish.

Matthew.title: The Ultimate Question and a Brutal Wake-Up Call
paragraphs: The religious leaders (the Pharisees and Sadducees) teamed up to test Jesus again, demanding he pull off a miracle on the spot to prove he was from God. Jesus rolled his eyes at them: "You guys can look at a red sky at night and predict the weather for tomorrow, but you are completely blind to the obvious spiritual signs happening right in front of you. I'm not doing a magic trick for you."

Later, Jesus warned his crew to watch out for the "yeast" of the religious leaders. At first, the disciples thought he was mad they forgot to pack bread. Jesus corrected them: "I'm not talking about baking! I'm talking about their toxic, fake teaching. A tiny bit of it will infect your whole life."

The Big Moment: "Who am I?" Jesus took the guys on a retreat to a place called Caesarea Philippi. He asked them, "Who is everyone saying I am?" They replied, "Some say John the Baptist resurrected. Others say Elijah or Jeremiah." Then Jesus looked right at them. "But what about you? Who do you say I am?" Peter stepped up and nailed it: "You're the Christ, the Messiah, the Son of the living God."

Jesus was thrilled. "Simon Peter, you didn't figure that out on your own—my Father in heaven revealed that to you. You are the Rock, and on this rock I'm going to build my church, and the forces of hell won't be able to stop it."

The Plot Twist Right after that massive high, Jesus hit them with a reality check: "We're going to Jerusalem. I'm going to be arrested, tortured, and killed by the leaders. But on the third day, I'll be raised back to life." Peter pulled Jesus aside and actually tried to scold him. "No way, Lord! We will never let that happen to you." Jesus spun around and rebuked Peter hard: "Get behind me, Satan! You are looking at this from a human point of view, not God's."
Jesus then laid down the ultimate challenge to the crowd:

"If any of you want to follow me, you have to put yourself second. You have to take up your cross and follow my lead. If you spend your life desperately trying to save yourself, you'll lose it. But if you give up your life for me, you'll find true life. What's the point of owning the entire world if it costs you your actual soul?"

Matthew.title: The Mountaintop Transformation
paragraphs: Six days later, Jesus took his three closest guys—Peter, James, and John—hiking up a massive mountain.

Suddenly, right in front of them, Jesus's appearance completely transformed. His face shone blindingly bright like the sun, and his clothes became intensely white. Suddenly, Moses and Elijah (two of the greatest heroes from the Old Testament who had been dead for centuries) appeared out of nowhere and started talking with Jesus.

Peter, terrified and not knowing what to say, blurted out, "Lord, this is awesome! Let me build three shrines up here for you guys!" While he was still babbling, a bright cloud enveloped them, and a voice thundered: "This is my Son, whom I love. Listen to him!" The three disciples hit the dirt, absolutely paralyzed with fear. Jesus walked over, touched them, and said, "Get up. Don't be afraid." When they looked up, it was just Jesus again.

Moving Mountains When they got back down to the crowd, a man begged Jesus to heal his son who was having severe, life-threatening seizures caused by a demon. The man said, "I asked your disciples to heal him, but they couldn't." Jesus sighed, healed the boy instantly, and the demon left. Later, the disciples asked Jesus privately, "Why did we fail?" Jesus told them straight up: "Because your faith is too small. If you had faith even the size of a tiny mustard seed, you could tell this mountain to move, and it would move. Nothing would be impossible for you."

Matthew.title: How to Handle Conflict and Forgive Like a Boss
paragraphs: The disciples started arguing about who was going to be the most important, top-ranking official in Jesus's kingdom.
Jesus called a little kid over, stood him right in the middle of these grown men, and dropped a truth bomb:

"Unless you guys dramatically change your attitude and become as humble and trusting as this little kid, you're not even getting into the kingdom, let alone running it. The greatest person in my kingdom is the one who makes themselves the lowest."
He then talked about how much God cares for the underdog. If a shepherd has 100 sheep and just one wanders off, he will leave the 99 to go rescue that one lost sheep. That's how God views people.

The 70 x 7 Rule Peter asked a practical question: "Lord, if someone keeps doing me dirty, how many times do I have to forgive them? Like, seven times?" Jesus shocked him: "Not seven times, Peter. Seventy times seven." (Basically: Stop keeping score.)

Jesus told a story to explain it: A king decided to audit his officials. One guy owed the king an impossible amount of money—millions of dollars. The king ordered him and his family to be sold as slaves to pay the debt. The guy fell on his knees and begged for a second chance. The king felt pity, canceled the massive debt completely, and let him walk free.

But as soon as that guy left, he ran into a co-worker who owed him twenty bucks. He grabbed him by the throat and choked him, demanding his money. When the co-worker begged for time, the guy refused and threw him in jail. When the king heard what happened, he was furious. He called the guy back in: "I forgave your massive debt because you begged me. Shouldn't you have showed the same mercy to your buddy?" The king threw the unforgiving guy into maximum security prison. Jesus ended with: "That's exactly how my Father in heaven will treat you if you refuse to forgive your brothers and sisters from your heart."

Matthew.title: The Rich Young VIP
paragraphs: People started bringing their little kids to Jesus so he could pray for them. The disciples tried to act like bouncers and shoo them away, thinking Jesus was too important to waste time on kids. Jesus got angry with his crew: "Stop it! Let the kids come to me. The kingdom of heaven belongs to people exactly like them."

The Impossible Needle A really wealthy, successful young guy walked up to Jesus and asked, "Teacher, what good thing do I have to do to guarantee eternal life?" Jesus said, "Keep the commandments. Don't murder, don't cheat, don't steal, honor your parents, and love your neighbor." The young guy proudly said, "Done. I've kept all those rules since I was a kid. What am I missing?" Jesus looked right at him and said, "If you want to go all the way, go sell everything you own, give the money to the poor, and come follow me. Your treasure will be in heaven."
The young guy's face dropped. He turned around and walked away totally depressed, because he was incredibly rich and his stuff was his actual god.

Jesus turned to his disciples: "I'm telling you the truth, it is ridiculously hard for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven. It’s actually easier to jam a massive camel through the tiny eye of a sewing needle than for a rich guy to get into God's kingdom." The disciples were mind-blown. "Then who can possibly be saved?!" Jesus looked at them and said, "Humanly speaking, it's impossible. But with God, everything is possible."

Matthew.title: The Unfair Paycheck and Upside-Down Leadership
paragraphs: Jesus told a story to explain how God's grace works: A farm owner went out at 6:00 AM to hire day laborers to work in his vineyard. They agreed on a standard full-day's wage. At 9:00 AM, the owner saw more guys standing around unemployed, so he hired them too. He did the same thing at noon, at 3:00 PM, and even at 5:00 PM when there was only one hour of work left in the day.

When it was time to get paid, the boss told his manager to pay the guys hired at 5:00 PM first. He gave them a full day's wage. When the guys who had been sweating in the sun since 6:00 AM stepped up, they expected a massive bonus. But the boss gave them the exact same full-day's wage they had agreed on. The early crew was furious. "This is completely unfair! We worked twelve hours in the blistering heat, and you paid those lazy guys the same amount!" The boss replied, "Friend, I didn't cheat you. We agreed on a price, and I paid it. Take your money and go. Can't I be generous with my own money? Are you jealous because I'm kind?" Jesus summed it up: "The last will be first, and the first will be last."

A Mom's Ambitious Request As they got closer to Jerusalem, the mother of James and John (two of the disciples) came up to Jesus and kneeled down. "When you become King, promise me that my two boys can be your right-hand and left-hand men." Jesus looked at the brothers. "You have no idea what you're asking. Can you drink from the cup of suffering I'm about to drink from?" They confidently said, "We can handle it." Jesus said, "You will suffer like me, but I don't assign the VIP seats. My Father does."
When the other ten disciples heard about this, they were absolutely furious at James and John for trying to bypass them for the best jobs. Jesus called a team meeting to shut it down:

"You guys know how the Romans do leadership—they boss people around, flex their power, and make everyone serve them. It is not going to be like that with you. > Whoever wants to be a leader among you must be your servant. Whoever wants to be first must be your slave. I, the Son of Man, didn't come here to be served by you. I came to serve you, and to give my life to buy freedom for many."

Matthew.title: Jesus Makes A Scene
paragraphs: As Jesus and his crew got close to Jerusalem, he sent two disciples on a mission. 'Go into that village,' he said, 'and you'll find a donkey and her colt. Untie them and bring them to me. If anyone gives you a hard time, just say, ‘The Master needs them,’ and they’ll let you go.' So they did it, and Jesus rode into town on the donkey. The crowd went absolutely wild, throwing their jackets on the ground like a red carpet and waving palm branches. They were all screaming, 'Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in God's name!'

The whole city was buzzing, like, 'Who IS this guy?' The crowd with Jesus was shouting, 'This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth!' Then Jesus went straight to the Temple and lost it. He started flipping tables of the loan sharks and kicking over the stalls of people selling pigeons. He went beast mode, quoting the scriptures: > My house was designated a house of prayer; You have made it a hangout for thieves. After he cleared them out, the blind and the crippled came to him and he healed them right there.

The religious leaders were fuming when they saw all the incredible things he was doing. But what really set them off were the kids running around the Temple shouting, 'Hosanna to the Son of David!' They confronted Jesus, all heated. 'Do you hear what these kids are saying?' Jesus just looked at them and said, 'Yeah, I hear them. Haven't you ever read the scripture that says, ‘From the mouths of children and babies I’ll furnish a place of praise’?'. Mic drop. He was so over their drama that he just turned and walked out of the city to spend the night in Bethany.

The next morning, Jesus was walking back to the city and feeling hungry. He saw a fig tree by the road and went to get some breakfast, but it only had leaves. So he said to the tree, 'No more figs from you—ever!' And right then, the tree withered up into a dry stick. His disciples saw it and their jaws dropped. 'How did that tree just die on the spot?' they asked. Jesus told them, 'Seriously, if you have faith and don’t doubt, you can do more than this. You could tell this mountain, ‘Go jump in the lake,’ and it would. If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer.'

Back in the Temple, the high priests and elders cornered him while he was teaching. 'Show us your credentials,' they demanded. 'Who gave you the authority to do all this?' Jesus shot back, 'I'll answer you, but first, you answer me. John the Baptist’s baptism—was it from heaven or from humans?' They were totally stuck. They huddled up, whispering, 'If we say ‘from heaven,’ he’ll ask why we didn’t believe John. If we say ‘from humans,’ the crowd will riot because they all think John was a prophet.' So they came back and said, 'We don’t know.' Jesus replied, 'Then I’m not telling you who gave me my authority either.'

Then Jesus dropped a story on them. 'A man had two sons. He told the first, ‘Go work in the vineyard today.’ The son said, ‘I don’t want to,’ but later he changed his mind and went. The father told the second son the same thing, and he said, ‘Yes, sir!’ but he never went. Which one did what the father wanted?' They answered, 'The first one.' Jesus looked them dead in the eye and said, 'Well, I’m telling you, the tax collectors and prostitutes are getting into God’s kingdom ahead of you. John the Baptist came and showed you the right way to live, and you dissed him, but they believed him. Even after seeing their lives change, you still didn’t change your minds and believe.'

He wasn't done yet. 'Listen to this. A landowner planted a vineyard, built a wall around it, and rented it to some farmers before going on a trip. When it was harvest time, he sent his servants to collect his share. But the farmers beat one up, killed another, and stoned a third. He sent more servants, and they did the same thing. Finally, he sent his son, thinking, ‘They’ll respect my son.’ But when the farmers saw the son, they said, ‘This is the heir! Let’s kill him and take his inheritance!' So they grabbed him, threw him out of the vineyard, and murdered him.'

Jesus paused and asked the leaders, 'So when the owner of the vineyard comes back, what will he do to those farmers?' They replied, 'He’ll bring those wretches to a wretched end, and he’ll rent the vineyard to other farmers who will give him his share at harvest time.' Jesus said, 'Exactly. And you've read the scripture: > The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This is the Lord’s doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes. Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit.' When the religious leaders heard his stories, they knew he was talking about them. They wanted to arrest him, but they were scared of the crowd, who all thought Jesus was a prophet.

Matthew.title: Party Crashers & Gotcha Questions
paragraphs: Jesus dropped another parable on them. He said, "God's kingdom is like a king who planned this epic wedding for his son. He sent out the invites to all the VIPs, but they totally ghosted him. Can you believe it? They just wouldn't come!"

The king tried again, sending more servants saying, 'Look, the party is ready to go, the food is amazing, everything is set! Just come!' But the guests couldn't be bothered. One went off to his farm, another to his business. The rest of them actually attacked the servants, beat them up, and killed them. The king absolutely lost it, went beast mode, and sent his army to destroy those murderers and burn their city down.

Then he told his crew, 'The wedding banquet is ready, but the people I invited were a total flop. So go out to the main streets and invite anyone and everyone you find.' The servants went out and gathered a huge crowd of anyone they could find, good and bad, and the wedding hall was finally packed. But when the king came in, he spotted one guy who wasn't wearing the right clothes for the wedding. He asked him, 'Friend, how did you get in here without the proper attire?' The guy had nothing to say. So the king ordered, 'Tie him up and throw him out into the darkness.' Jesus finished with this mic drop: 'Many are invited, but few are chosen.'

The religious leaders were seriously trying to trip Jesus up. They sent their followers along with some government loyalists to trap him. They started by buttering him up, 'Teacher, we know you're legit and teach the way of God, seriously. You don't care about what people think. So tell us, is it right to pay taxes to Caesar or not?' Jesus knew they were being shady and called them out. 'Why are you testing me? Show me the coin used for the tax.'

They handed him a coin, and he asked, 'Whose face and name is on this?' They replied, 'Caesar's.' Jesus then delivered the knockout punch: > "So give back to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's." They were completely stunned and had no comeback. They just left, totally speechless.

Later, some Sadducees, a group who didn't even believe in life after death, came to Jesus with a wild hypothetical. 'Teacher, Moses said if a man dies without kids, his brother should marry the widow. So, here's the tea: there were seven brothers. The first one died, then the second, and so on, all seven marrying the same woman. Finally, the woman died. So, at the resurrection, whose wife is she gonna be?'

Jesus told them, "You're way off because you don't know the Scriptures or the power of God. When people rise from the dead, it's not going to be like a reality TV dating show. People won't be getting married. They will be like the angels in heaven. And about the resurrection, haven't you read what God said to you? He said, 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.' He is the God of the living, not the dead." The crowd was blown away by his teaching.

When the Pharisees heard how Jesus had shut down the Sadducees, they regrouped for another attack. One of them, a legal expert, asked him a question to test him: 'Teacher, which is the greatest commandment in the Law?' Jesus replied, > "‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’ This is the first and greatest commandment. And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments."

Matthew.title: Jesus Calls Out on the Hypocrites
paragraphs: Jesus gathered his crew and the huge crowd and dropped a bomb. He called out the religious leaders, the so-called experts in God's Law. 'Listen, these guys know the rules, but they don't play by 'em. They talk a good game, but their lives are a total mess. It's all for show, like a perpetual fashion show. They love the VIP seats at church dinners and getting called 'Doctor' or 'Reverend.' Don't be like them. They're fakes.

Then Jesus flipped the script. He told his followers to ditch the obsession with status and titles. 'Don't let people put you on a pedestal. You have one Teacher, and you're all just classmates.' He made it clear that the only one who deserves that kind of authority is God. The ultimate flex? Being humble. > 'Do you want to stand out? Then step down. Be a servant. If you puff yourself up, you’ll get the wind knocked out of you. But if you’re content to simply be yourself, your life will count for plenty.'

Jesus went full beast mode, calling the religious leaders 'frauds' and 'roadblocks to God's kingdom.' He was like, 'You won't enter, and you won't let anyone else in either!' He called them out for their ridiculous, nit-picky rules. They cared more about tithing every last penny than about actual important things like fairness, compassion, and being committed to God. He said they looked silly, focusing on commas while their whole life story was a fail.

He kept going, comparing them to cups that are sparkling clean on the outside but are full of rotten, maggoty greed on the inside. 'Foolish Pharisees! Scour the insides, and then the gleaming surface will mean something.' Then he hit them with another one: 'You're like a perfectly manicured graveyard. Looks beautiful with fresh-cut grass and bright flowers, but underneath it's all rotting bones and worm-eaten flesh. You look like saints, but you're total frauds underneath.'

Jesus didn't hold back. He called them 'snakes' and 'cold-blooded sneaks.' He accused them of being just like their ancestors who murdered the prophets. They build fancy tombs for the prophets now, but they're cut from the same cloth. He promised that he would keep sending wise people and prophets, and they would keep treating them like dirt. The guilt for every drop of innocent blood spilled, from Abel to the prophet Zechariah, was going to land right on their heads.

Finally, Jesus looked out over the city and his heart broke. 'Jerusalem! Jerusalem! You murder the prophets and kill the messengers God sends you! How many times have I wanted to gather you up, like a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you wouldn't let me.' His voice was filled with pain. 'Now your city is a ghost town. I'm out of here. You won't see me again until you're ready to say, ‘God has blessed him! He’s come, bringing God’s rule!’'

Matthew.title: The Real Tea on the End Times
paragraphs: As Jesus and his crew were leaving the Temple, his disciples were totally geeking out over the amazing architecture. 'Hey, Jesus, check out these buildings! So epic!' Jesus just stunned his head. 'You think this is impressive? Seriously, every single one of these stones is going to end up in a pile of rubble.' Later, they were chilling on the Mount of Olives, and the disciples cornered him. 'Okay, spill. When is all this going down? And give us a sign so we know when you're coming back and the world as we know it is over.'

Jesus got real serious. 'First thing: Don't get played. A bunch of fakes are gonna show up claiming to be me, the Messiah, and they're gonna fool a lot of people. You'll hear about wars, and rumors of more wars, but don't panic. That's just normal, messed-up history. It's not the end. Countries will throw down with other countries, there will be famines and earthquakes. That's just the warm-up act.'

'Then things get personal. They're gonna turn on you, hate you, and even kill you just because you're on my team. It's going to be brutal, a total dog-eat-dog world where everyone betrays each other. Lying preachers will be everywhere, and the world will get so evil that most people's love will just turn to ash. But you gotta hang in there. The one who stays loyal to the end, that's the one who is saved. And through all the chaos, the good news about God's kingdom will be preached everywhere on the planet. Then the end will come.'

'So, when you see the 'Monster of Desecration' that the prophet Daniel wrote about standing in the holy Temple—you'll know what I'm talking about—it's time to bounce. If you're in Judea, run for the hills. Don't even go back in the house to grab your phone charger. It's going to be an awful time, worse than anything the world has ever seen. It'll be so bad that if God didn't cut it short, no one would survive. But for the sake of his chosen ones, he'll hit the brakes on the chaos.'

'During that time, if someone says, 'Quick, the Messiah is over here!' or 'There he is!'—don't buy it. These fake Messiahs and scam-artist preachers will be putting on a big show, doing crazy signs and wonders to trick even the smartest people. I'm giving you the heads-up now so you don't fall for it. My return isn't some secret event you have to RSVP to. It will be like a flash of lightning that lights up the whole sky. Everyone will see it.'

'Right after that terrible time, the universe is gonna go haywire. The sun will go dark, the moon will refuse to shine, stars will fall out of the sky, and all the cosmic powers will be shaken. Then, finally, the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. Everyone on earth who isn't ready will totally lose it, crying and mourning as they see me arrive on the clouds with insane power and glory. I'll send out my angels with a massive trumpet blast, and they'll gather all my chosen people from every corner of the globe.'

'Learn from the fig tree. As soon as its branches get tender and it starts growing leaves, you know summer is coming. In the same way, when you see all these things happening, you'll know my arrival is right at the door. I'm telling you, this generation won't pass away until all this stuff starts to happen. Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words are forever.'

'But nobody knows the exact day or hour. Not the angels, not even me. Only the Father knows. My arrival will be like the days of Noah. People were just living their lives—eating, drinking, getting married—right up until the day Noah got on the ark. They had no clue what was coming until the flood hit and swept them all away. That's how it will be when I return. So you have to stay ready. You have no idea when your Master is showing up. Be vigilant, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you don't expect.'

Matthew.title: Stay Ready or Get Left Behind
paragraphs: Jesus dropped another parable. He said, ‘God's Kingdom is like ten bridesmaids waiting for the groom to show up for the wedding party. Five of them were totally clueless and the other five were on top of their game. The clueless ones brought their lamps but forgot to bring extra oil, like showing up to a party with 1% battery and no charger. The smart ones? They brought a whole backup supply.

The groom was running late, so all the girls ended up crashing for a nap. Then, in the middle of the night, someone screamed, 'He's here! The groom is finally here! Let's go!' All ten of them jumped up and got their lamps ready. But the five unprepared girls started to panic. 'Our lamps are dying! Quick, give us some of your oil!'

The smart girls said, 'Sorry, no can do. There isn't enough for all of us. You'll have to run to the store and buy your own.' So they left to go buy more, but while they were gone, the groom arrived. The girls who were ready went into the wedding feast with him, and the door was locked. A little while later, the clueless crew finally showed up, banging on the door. 'Master, let us in!' But he just said, 'Do I even know you? I don't think so.' Then Jesus looked at his crew and said, 'So for real, stay alert. You have no idea when the time will come.'

Then Jesus hit them with another story. 'It's like a boss who was going on a long trip. He called in his top three employees and gave them some major cash to manage. To one, he gave $5,000, to another $2,000, and to the last one $1,000—all based on what he knew they could handle. The first guy immediately went out and hustled, doubling the investment. The second guy did the same. But the third guy, the one with the $1,000, just dug a hole and buried it. He played it way too safe.'

After a super long time, the boss came back to see what was up. The guy with the $5,000 showed him the $10,000 he made. The boss was thrilled! 'Let's go! You killed it! You're not just my employee anymore, you're my partner.' The guy with the $2,000 showed him his $4,000, and the boss said the exact same thing. But then the third guy came up and said, 'Look, I know you're a tough boss and you don't mess around. I was scared I'd mess up and lose your money, so I just hid it. Here's your $1,000 back, safe and sound.'

The boss absolutely lost it. 'You're a terrible employee! It's criminal to be that cautious! If you knew I was serious about results, why did you do the absolute least? You could have at least put it in a savings account and gotten some interest!' Then he told his other guys, 'Take his $1,000 and give it to the one who made the most. And throw this play-it-safe guy out. He's getting kicked out of the company for good.'

Jesus wasn't done. He dropped a bomb. 'When the Son of Man comes back in all his glory with his angel squad, he's going to sit on his throne and judge everyone. All the nations will be lined up, and he'll separate people like a farmer separates sheep from goats. The sheep will be on his right, and the goats on his left.'

Then the King will turn to the sheep on his right and say, 'Come on in, you're blessed by my Father! Your spot in the kingdom has been ready since day one. Why? Because when I was hungry, you fed me. When I was thirsty, you gave me a drink. When I was a stranger, you took me in. When I was freezing, you gave me clothes. When I was sick, you checked on me. When I was in jail, you visited me.'

The sheep will be totally confused. 'Wait, what? When did we ever see you hungry or thirsty or in jail?' And the King will say, > 'I'm telling you the honest truth: whenever you did one of these things for the least important person, you were doing it for me.'

Then he'll turn to the goats on his left and go beast mode. 'Get out of here, you useless goats! You're headed for eternal fire. Why? Because I was hungry, and you didn't give me any food. I was thirsty, and you gave me nothing to drink. I was a stranger, and you ignored me. I was freezing, and you didn't offer a coat. I was sick and in jail, and you never even thought to visit.' They'll argue back, 'Master, when did we ever see you in need and not help?' And he'll reply, 'Seriously, whenever you failed to help someone who was overlooked, you were failing to help me.' And those goats will be sent to their eternal punishment, but the sheep will enter eternal life.

Matthew.title: The Final Hours
paragraphs: Jesus dropped a bomb on his disciples, saying, 'You know Passover is in two days? That's when I get betrayed and crucified.' At the same time, the religious VIPs were plotting to arrest and kill him on the down-low, because they were scared of a riot if they did it publicly.

While Jesus was having dinner at Simon the Leper's house, a woman came in and did something totally extra. She poured a whole bottle of super expensive perfume on his head. The disciples lost it, saying, 'What a waste! That could have been sold and the money given to the poor!' But Jesus shut them down, saying, 'Why are you giving her a hard time? She did a beautiful thing for me. You'll always have the poor with you, but you won't always have me. She was preparing me for my burial. I promise you, wherever the good news is preached, what she has done will be told in memory of her.'

That's when Judas, one of the twelve, went full-on snake. He went to the chief priests and asked, 'What will you give me if I hand him over to you?' They offered him thirty pieces of silver, and from then on, he was looking for the right moment to betray Jesus.

At the Last Supper, things got real. Jesus told them, 'One of you is going to betray me.' The disciples were stunned, each one asking, 'It's not me, is it?' Jesus explained it was the one who dipped his bread in the bowl with him. Then Judas, playing innocent, asked, 'It's not me, is it, Rabbi?' Jesus just said, 'You said it.'

During the meal, Jesus took some bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to his disciples. > Take, eat. This is my body. Then he took a cup of wine, thanked God for it, and said, > Drink this, all of you. This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

Later, in the garden of Gethsemane, Jesus was in agony, praying, 'My Father, if it is possible, may this cup be taken from me. Yet not as I will, but as you will.' He found his disciples sleeping and said to Peter, 'Couldn't you keep watch with me for one hour?' He prayed two more times, each time finding them asleep. The last time, he said, 'Are you still sleeping? Look, the hour is near, and the Son of Man is delivered into the hands of sinners. Rise, let us go. Here comes my betrayer.'

Right on cue, Judas showed up with a mob armed with swords and clubs. He had told them, 'The one I kiss is the man; arrest him.' He went up to Jesus, said, 'Greetings, Rabbi!' and kissed him. As the mob grabbed Jesus, Peter went beast mode, pulled out a sword, and sliced off a servant's ear. But Jesus told him to put it away, saying, 'Do you think I cannot call on my Father, and he will at once put at my disposal more than twelve legions of angels?' Then all the disciples bailed.

They took Jesus to the high priest, Caiaphas, for a sham trial. They brought in a bunch of liars to testify against him, but their stories were all over the place. Finally, two came forward and said, 'This fellow said, 'I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.'' The high priest stood up and asked Jesus, 'Have you no answer?' But Jesus stayed silent. So the high priest said, 'I charge you under oath by the living God: Tell us if you are the Messiah, the Son of God.' Jesus replied, 'You have said so. But I say to all of you: From now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Mighty One and coming on the clouds of heaven.' The high priest lost it, tore his clothes, and yelled, 'Blasphemy!' The whole council condemned him to death and then they started spitting on him and beating him.

Meanwhile, Peter was outside in the courtyard, and a servant girl came up to him and said, 'You also were with Jesus of Galilee.' But he denied it, saying, 'I don't know what you're talking about.' He went out to the gateway, where another girl saw him and said, 'This fellow was with Jesus of Nazareth.' He denied it again, with an oath: 'I don't know the man!' A little later, the bystanders said to Peter, 'Surely you are one of them; your accent gives you away.' Then he began to call down curses, and he swore to them, 'I don't know the man!' Immediately a rooster crowed, and Peter remembered what Jesus had said: 'Before the rooster crows, you will disown me three times.' And he went outside and wept bitterly.

Matthew.title: The King They Crucified
paragraphs: As soon as the sun was up, the religious VIPs put the final touches on their shady plan to execute Jesus. They tied him up and hauled him off to the governor, Pilate, like a criminal.

When Judas, the friend who betrayed him, saw that Jesus was actually going to be killed, he totally lost it. He was wrecked with guilt and tried to give the thirty silver coins back to the priests. 'I sinned! I betrayed an innocent man!' he cried. They shot back, 'So? That's your problem.' Judas threw the money into the Temple, ran out, and hung himself. So much for blood money.

Jesus stood before Governor Pilate, who asked him, 'Are you the King of the Jews?' Jesus replied with a quiet confidence, 'You said it.' But when the priests and elders started piling on the accusations, Jesus didn't say a word. Pilate was baffled. 'Don't you hear all this stuff they're accusing you of?' he asked. Still, Jesus remained silent. The governor was seriously impressed.

It was a custom to release one prisoner chosen by the crowd during the Passover festival. They had a famous bad guy named Barabbas in jail. Pilate, knowing the religious leaders were just jealous, asked the crowd, 'Who should I release? Barabbas, or Jesus, the so-called Christ?' But the leaders had already hyped up the crowd to demand Barabbas. 'What should I do with Jesus?' Pilate asked. The crowd went wild, screaming, 'Nail him to a cross!' Pilate, confused, yelled, 'But why? What crime has he committed?' But they just screamed louder.

Pilate saw a riot was about to pop off and that he was getting nowhere. He washed his hands in front of everyone and dropped a bomb: 'I'm innocent of this man's blood. This is on you.' The crowd went nuts, shouting, 'We'll take the blame! Us and our kids!' So Pilate freed Barabbas, had Jesus brutally whipped, and handed him over to be crucified.

The governor's soldiers took Jesus into the palace and the whole squad gathered to make fun of him. They stripped him and put a scarlet robe on him, twisted a crown of thorns for his head, and put a staff in his hand like a fake scepter. They knelt down, mocking him, 'Hey, hail King of the Jews!' Then they spit on him and beat him on the head with the staff. When they were done, they put his own clothes back on and led him away to be killed.

On the way out, they forced a random guy from Cyrene, Simon, to carry Jesus' heavy cross. They got to Golgotha, which means 'Skull Hill.' They offered Jesus wine mixed with a painkiller, but after tasting it, he refused. They nailed him to the cross, and then gambled for his clothes. Above his head, they posted the charge: THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS. They crucified two criminals with him, one on his right and one on his left.

People walking by hurled insults, shaking their heads. 'You were gonna destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, right? So save yourself! If you're the Son of God, get down from that cross!' The religious leaders joined in the trash talk: 'He saved others, but he can't save himself! King of Israel, huh? Let's see him come down from the cross, and then we'll believe! He trusted God? Let God rescue him now if he wants him!' Even the criminals crucified next to him dissed him.

From noon until three in the afternoon, the whole land went dark. Around three, Jesus cried out in agony, 'Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?' which means, 'My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?' At that moment, the massive Temple curtain ripped in two from top to bottom. The earth stunned, rocks split, and tombs opened. After Jesus rose from the dead, many of God's people who had died were raised to life and appeared to others in the city. The Roman captain and his soldiers who were guarding Jesus were terrified by the earthquake and everything happening. They said, 'Seriously, this man was the Son of God.'

Matthew.title: He's Back. And It's Everything.
paragraphs: After the Sabbath, at the crack of dawn on Sunday, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to pay their respects at Jesus' tomb. Out of nowhere, the ground started shaking like crazy. A legit angel of God came down from heaven, rolled away the massive stone like it was nothing, and then just sat on it, chilling. The angel was blazing with light, like lightning, and his clothes were whiter than fresh snow. The guards hired to protect the tomb were so freaked out they literally couldn't move. They were basically frozen in fear.

The angel looked at the women and said, "Don't be scared. I know you're looking for Jesus, the one who was crucified. But he's not here. He has risen, just like he said he would. Come on, check out the spot where he was laid." The women peeked inside, and sure enough, the tomb was empty. The angel then gave them their mission: "Now, go quick and tell his disciples that he's risen from the dead and is on his way to Galilee. You'll see him there. That's the message."

The women were a mix of terrified and totally ecstatic. They took off running from the tomb to find the disciples and tell them the insane news. Suddenly, Jesus himself was right there in front of them. "Good morning!" he said. They dropped to their knees, grabbed his feet, and just started worshiping. Jesus told them, "Don't be afraid. Go tell my brothers to head to Galilee. I'll meet them there."

Meanwhile, some of the guards who had fled the scene went into the city and spilled the beans to the high priests about everything that had just gone down. The religious leaders called an emergency meeting and came up with a seriously shady plan. They paid the soldiers a huge amount of money to spread a lie: "Tell everyone his disciples came in the middle of the night and stole his body while we were asleep." They even promised the soldiers they'd have their backs if the governor found out they were sleeping on the job. The soldiers took the cash and did what they were told. And that fake news story is still floating around today.

The eleven disciples booked it to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had told them to meet him. When they saw him, they worshiped him, but some of them were still a little hesitant, not fully sure if they could handle this level of commitment. But Jesus didn't let their doubts slow him down. He came to them and dropped this bombshell:

> "God has given me all authority in heaven and on earth. So go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And for sure, I am with you always, to the very end of the age."

Mark.title: The Ultimate Hype Man and a Fast Start
paragraphs: The good news of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, starts right here.

It began exactly how the ancient prophet Isaiah said it would: "Watch closely—I'm sending my messenger ahead of you to clear the path. He's going to be a voice shouting in the desert, telling everyone to get ready for the Lord."

That messenger was John the Baptist. He showed up in the desert telling people, "Turn your life around, get baptized, and God will forgive your sins." Everyone from Judea and Jerusalem was pouring out into the desert to hear him and get baptized in the Jordan River. John was rugged—he wore clothes made of camel hair, rocked a leather belt, and survived on a diet of locusts and wild honey. His main message was: "The guy coming after me is way out of my league. I'm not even worthy to untie his shoes. I'm dunking you in water, but he is going to baptize you with the Holy Spirit."
§The Baptism and the Desert

Jesus traveled from Nazareth to the Jordan River, and John baptized him. The second Jesus came up out of the water, the sky ripped open, and the Holy Spirit came down on him like a dove. A voice from heaven boomed: "You are my Son, and I love you. I am incredibly proud of you."

Immediately after that, the Spirit pushed Jesus out into the harsh wilderness. He was out there for forty days, surrounded by wild animals, getting completely tested and tempted by Satan. But angels stepped in and took care of him.
§Drafting the Crew and Wrecking Demons
After John got arrested, Jesus went to the Galilee region and started preaching: "Time's up! God's kingdom is right here. Change your ways and believe the good news!"

Walking down the beach, Jesus saw two brothers, Simon (Peter) and Andrew, throwing their fishing nets into the water. Jesus called out, "Come follow me! I'll teach you how to fish for actual people." They dropped their nets on the spot and followed him. A little further down, he saw James and John fixing nets in a boat. He called them, and they immediately left their dad in the boat and joined the crew.

They went into the town of Capernaum. On the Sabbath (the day of rest), Jesus went to the local gathering place and started teaching. People were mind-blown because he spoke with absolute authority, not like their boring religious teachers.
Suddenly, a guy possessed by an evil spirit started screaming at him: "What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth?! Did you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God!"

Jesus didn't flinch. "Be quiet and get out of him!" he commanded. The evil spirit violently threw the man into a spasm, shrieked, and left. The crowd was stunned. "Who is this guy? Even the evil spirits take orders from him!"
After that, Jesus went to Peter's house and healed his sick mother-in-law. By sunset, the whole town was at the door bringing sick and possessed people, and Jesus healed them all.

Later, a guy covered in leprosy (a highly contagious, flesh-eating disease) fell on his knees and begged Jesus, "If you want to, you can heal me." Jesus felt deep pity for the guy, reached out, and actually touched him. "I want to," Jesus said. "Be healed." Instantly, the leprosy vanished.

Mark.title: Ripping Off the Roof and Breaking the Rules
paragraphs: A few days later, Jesus was back in Capernaum. Word got out, and the house he was in got packed so tight nobody could even get through the front door.

Four guys brought their paralyzed friend on a stretcher, but they couldn't get past the crowd. So, they climbed up onto the roof, literally ripped a hole in it, and lowered their paralyzed buddy down on ropes right in front of Jesus.
When Jesus saw how massive their faith was, he looked at the paralyzed guy and said, "Son, your sins are forgiven."
Some stuck-up religious experts sitting right there started thinking, "This is blasphemy! Who does this guy think he is? Only God can forgive sins."

Jesus knew exactly what they were thinking. He said, "Why are you getting triggered? What's easier to say: 'Your sins are forgiven' or 'Get up and walk'? Just to prove the Son of Man has the authority to forgive sins here on earth..." He turned to the paralyzed guy: "Get up, grab your mat, and go home."
The guy stood right up, grabbed his mat, and walked out while everyone stared in total shock, praising God.
§Hanging with the Outcasts
Later, Jesus saw a tax collector named Levi (Matthew) sitting at his booth. Jesus said, "Follow me," and Levi quit his job and followed him.

Levi threw a massive dinner party at his house with Jesus, his disciples, and a ton of other shady tax collectors and "sinners." The religious leaders saw this and asked his disciples, "Why does he eat with outcasts?"
Jesus overheard them and dropped this logic: "Healthy people don't need a doctor—sick people do. I didn't come to invite the rule-followers; I came to invite the misfits."
§The Sabbath Showdown

One weekend, Jesus and his guys were walking through a wheat field. The disciples were hungry and pulled off some heads of grain to snack on. The religious police threw a fit: "Look! They are breaking the Sabbath rules by working!"

Jesus shut them down: "Did you ever read what King David did when his guys were starving? He ate the holy bread from the temple. Listen to me: The Sabbath was made to help people; people weren't made to be slaves to the Sabbath. I'm the boss of the Sabbath."

Mark.title: The Starting Lineup and Unforgivable Trash Talk
paragraphs: Jesus went back to the meeting place, and there was a guy there with a crippled, shriveled hand. The religious leaders watched Jesus like hawks, waiting to see if he would heal the guy on the Sabbath so they could arrest him.

Jesus told the crippled man, "Stand up right here in the middle." Then Jesus asked the leaders, "Is it legal to do good on the Sabbath, or to do evil? To save a life, or kill?" They sat there in dead silence.
Jesus looked around at them, absolutely furious and deeply heartbroken by how stubborn and cold they were. He told the man, "Stretch out your hand." The man did, and it was perfectly healed.
The religious leaders immediately stormed out and held a secret meeting with corrupt politicians to figure out how to assassinate Jesus.
§Drafting the 12

The crowds following Jesus were getting dangerously huge. People from all over the country were crushing in on him just to touch him and get healed. He had to have his disciples keep a small boat ready just in case he got trampled.

Jesus hiked up a mountain and called up the specific guys he wanted on his core team. He appointed twelve of them to be his official "apostles" (messengers). They were: Peter, James, John (he called those two "Sons of Thunder"), Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon, and Judas Iscariot (the guy who eventually betrayed him).
§The Unforgivable Sin
Jesus went home, but the crowd was so crazy he and his guys couldn't even eat. His own family heard about it and came to drag him away, thinking, "He’s lost his mind."
The religious experts from Jerusalem showed up and started a rumor: "He's possessed by Beelzebul (Satan). He's only kicking out demons because he's getting his power from the boss of the demons."

Jesus called them over and exposed how clueless that logic was: "Why would Satan kick out Satan? If a kingdom goes to war against itself, it collapses. If you want to rob a strong man's house, you have to tie him up first. That's what I'm doing to Satan."

Then he gave them a hardcore warning: "You can be forgiven for almost any sin or trash-talk. But if you deliberately trash-talk the Holy Spirit and call the work of God the work of the devil, that is unforgivable. You carry that guilt forever."

Mark.title: Stories in the Dirt and a Wild Storm
paragraphs: Jesus went back to teach by the lake. The crowd was so massive he had to get into a boat and teach from the water. He taught them using "parables" (stories with hidden meanings).
§The Dirt Story
"Listen up! A farmer went out to plant seeds.
