Jesus asked, "Weren't all ten guys cleansed? Where are the other nine? Was no one else willing to return and give praise to God except this foreigner?" He told the man, "Stand up and go. Your faith has made you well."
When is the Kingdom Coming?
The Pharisees demanded to know exactly when God's kingdom was going to arrive.
Jesus said, "It's not something you can track with a telescope or a calendar. You can't say, 'Here it is!' or 'There it is!' because the kingdom of God is already right here among you."

He told his disciples that when the Son of Man actually returns at the end of the world, it won't be a secret. "It will be like a massive flash of lightning that lights up the entire sky from one end to the other. But first, he must suffer and be rejected by this generation.

It will be exactly like the days of Noah. Everyone was partying, eating, and getting married right up until the second Noah walked into the ark. Then the flood hit and destroyed them all. Don't get so distracted by the world that you miss what's coming. Remember what happened to Lot's wife—she looked back at the destruction, and it cost her everything. Whoever tries to keep their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life will preserve it."

Luke.title: The Annoying Widow and the Blind Beggar
paragraphs: Jesus wanted to teach his guys that they should always pray and never give up. He told them this story:
"There was a corrupt judge in a town who didn't fear God and didn't care about people. A widow kept coming to him, demanding, 'Give me justice against my enemy!'

For a long time, the judge completely ignored her. But she was so relentlessly annoying that he finally said to himself, 'I don't care about God or people, but this widow is driving me absolutely crazy. I'm going to give her justice just so she stops bothering me before she wears me out completely!'"
Jesus explained: "If even a corrupt judge will do the right thing when pressed, don't you think God will quickly bring justice to his chosen people who cry out to him day and night?"
§The Arrogant VIP vs. The Broken Scammer
He aimed this next story directly at people who thought they were spiritually superior to everyone else:
"Two guys went up to the Temple to pray. One was a strict, rule-following Pharisee, and the other was a shady tax collector.

The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed, 'God, I thank you that I am not like other guys—robbers, evildoers, cheaters, or even like this tax collector right here. I fast twice a week and give a full ten percent of everything I make.'
But the tax collector stood far away in the back. He wouldn't even look up to heaven. He beat his chest in absolute sorrow and prayed, 'God, have mercy on me, a sinner.'

I'm telling you, it was the broken tax collector—not the arrogant Pharisee—who went home right with God that day. For everyone who flexes will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be elevated."
§The Impossible Needle
A super wealthy, powerful ruler asked Jesus, "Good teacher, what do I have to do to inherit eternal life?" He swore he had kept all the commandments since he was a kid.
Jesus said, "You still lack one thing. Sell absolutely everything you own, give the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me."
The ruler became incredibly sad, because his massive wealth was his actual idol.
Jesus looked at him and said, "It is easier to jam a camel through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."
The people listening panicked. "Then who can be saved?!"
Jesus said, "What is completely impossible for human beings is absolutely possible with God."

As they got close to Jericho, a blind beggar sitting by the road heard the massive crowd walking by. When he found out it was Jesus, he started screaming, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!" The crowd told him to be quiet, but he just yelled louder. Jesus stopped, called him over, and asked, "What do you want me to do for you?"
"Lord, I want to see."
Jesus said, "Receive your sight; your faith has healed you." The guy instantly got his vision back and followed Jesus, praising God.

Luke.title: The Tree Climber and the Triumphal Parade
paragraphs: Jesus entered Jericho. There was a guy living there named Zacchaeus. He wasn't just a regular tax collector; he was the chief tax collector, and he was insanely rich from scamming people.

He desperately wanted to see Jesus, but Zacchaeus was a really short guy, and the crowd was massive. So, he literally sprinted ahead of the crowd and climbed up into a sycamore-fig tree just to get a glimpse.
When Jesus reached the tree, he stopped, looked straight up, and said, "Zacchaeus, come down immediately. I must stay at your house today."
Zacchaeus scrambled down and welcomed him gladly. The entire crowd started grumbling and complaining: "He has gone to be the guest of a total 'sinner.'"

But Zacchaeus stood up and made a massive public promise to Jesus: "Look, Lord! Right here and now, I give half of all my wealth to the poor. And if I have cheated anybody out of anything, I will pay them back four times the amount."
Jesus smiled. "Salvation has come to this house today. For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost."
§The Story of the Gold Coins (The Minas)
Because they were getting close to Jerusalem and people thought the kingdom of God was going to appear magically right then, Jesus told them a story:
"A nobleman went to a distant country to be crowned king. Before he left, he called ten of his servants and gave them each a bag of gold. 'Put this money to work until I get back,' he ordered.
But his subjects hated him and sent a message saying, 'We don't want this guy as our king.'
When he returned as king, he called his servants in for an audit.
The first guy said, 'Sir, your gold has earned ten more bags.' 'Awesome job!' the king said. 'Because you were trustworthy with a little, I'm putting you in charge of ten cities.'
The second guy earned five bags, and he got put in charge of five cities.
But another servant came and said, 'Sir, here is your bag of gold. I wrapped it in a cloth and hid it because I was terrified of you. You're a hard man.'

The king was furious. 'You lazy, wicked servant! If you knew I was a hard man, why didn't you at least put my money in the bank to earn some interest?' He took the gold and gave it to the guy who had ten.
Jesus's point: If you use the gifts God gives you, you'll be trusted with more. If you hide them out of fear and do nothing, you'll lose everything."
§The Donkey Parade

When they reached the Mount of Olives just outside Jerusalem, Jesus told two disciples: "Go into the village ahead. You'll find a young donkey tied up that no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here. If anyone asks, just say, 'The Lord needs it.'"

They brought the donkey, threw their cloaks on its back, and Jesus rode it down the massive hill toward the city. The massive crowd of disciples went absolutely crazy, throwing their coats on the road like a red carpet, shouting: "Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!"
Some tight-lipped Pharisees in the crowd yelled, "Teacher, tell your disciples to be quiet!"
Jesus replied, "I tell you, if they keep quiet, the actual rocks on the ground will start cheering."

As Jesus looked at the massive city of Jerusalem spread out below him, he openly wept. He knew they were going to reject him, and he predicted the horrific destruction that would hit the city years later because they didn't recognize God when He visited them.

Then Jesus rode straight into the Temple area and started physically throwing out the merchants who were scamming people. "It is written," he yelled, "My house will be a house of prayer, but you have turned it into a hangout for thieves!" Every day after that, he taught in the Temple, while the religious leaders desperately tried to figure out a way to assassinate him without starting a riot.

Luke.title: Traps, Taxes, and the Ultimate Authority
paragraphs: One day, while Jesus was teaching the massive crowds in the Temple courtyard, the chief priests, religious lawyers, and elders stormed up to him.
"Tell us by what authority you are doing all these things!" they demanded. "Who gave you the right to throw people out and teach here?"
Jesus didn't back down. "I'll answer you if you answer one question for me first: John the Baptist's baptism—was it from heaven, or was it just a human idea?"

They held a quick, panicked huddle. "If we say 'from heaven,' he'll ask why we didn't believe John. But if we say 'from humans,' the massive crowd will stone us to death because they are convinced John was a real prophet."
So they cowardly answered, "We don't know."
Jesus replied, "Then I won't tell you by what authority I'm doing these things either." The Story of the Evil Farmers
Jesus then told a story directed right at the corrupt leaders:

"A man planted a massive vineyard, rented it out to some farmers, and moved away. At harvest time, he sent a servant to collect his share of the fruit. But the farmers beat the servant up and sent him away with nothing. The owner sent a second servant; they beat him too. He sent a third; they wounded him and threw him out.
Finally, the owner said, 'I will send my own son, whom I love. They will respect him.'
But when the farmers saw the son, they plotted: 'This is the heir! Let's murder him, and the vineyard will be ours!' So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.
What will the owner do to those guys?" Jesus asked. "He will come, completely destroy those farmers, and give the vineyard to others."

The religious leaders realized Jesus was talking directly about them (they were the evil farmers, God was the owner, and Jesus was the son they were about to kill). They wanted to arrest him right then and there, but they were too afraid of the crowd.
§The Tax Trap and the Resurrection Trap
Next, they sent spies to trap him with a political question: "Teacher, is it legal for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?"
Jesus saw right through their scam. "Show me a denarius coin. Whose portrait and name are on it?"
"Caesar's," they replied.
Jesus dropped the hammer: "Then give back to Caesar what is Caesar's, and give back to God what is God's." They were totally stunned into silence.

Then the Sadducees (a religious group who didn't believe in the afterlife or resurrection) tried to trap him with a ridiculous hypothetical question about a woman who had been married to seven different brothers sequentially after they each died. "At the resurrection, whose wife will she be?" they mocked.

Jesus shut them down: "You guys don't understand heaven. People who rise from the dead don't get married; they are like angels and never die again. And as for the dead rising, even Moses proved it when he called the Lord 'the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.' He is not the God of the dead, but of the living! To him, they are all alive."
Some of the teachers of the law actually said, "Well said, Teacher!" And after that, nobody had the guts to ask him any more trick questions.

Luke.title: The Widow’s Pennies and the End of the World
paragraphs: Jesus was hanging out at the Temple, watching rich people flex by dropping massive bags of cash into the offering boxes. Then he saw a poor widow walk up and drop in two tiny copper coins.

He looked at his guys and said, "I'm telling you the truth, this poor widow just out-gave all of them. The rich people just tossed in their spare change, but she is completely broke and still gave everything she had to live on."
§The Temple Takedown
Later, some people were talking about how incredibly beautiful the Temple was, with its massive stones and expensive decorations.

Jesus completely popped their bubble: "Take a good look at all this. The day is coming when this massive building is going to be completely leveled. Not a single stone will be left stacked on top of another."
They panicked. "Teacher, when is this going to happen? What's the warning sign?"
§Jesus gave them a heavy reality check about the future:
"Don't get scammed. A bunch of guys are going to show up claiming, 'I am the Messiah!' Don't follow them.
You're going to hear about massive wars and revolutions. Don't panic. That stuff has to happen first.
There will be massive earthquakes, famines, and deadly diseases. There will be terrifying events in the sky.
But before any of that, the world is going to turn on you. They will arrest you, drag you into court, and throw you in prison just because you have my name.
But here is the game plan: Don't practice your defense speeches ahead of time. I will personally give you the words and the wisdom, and your enemies won't be able to argue with you at all.

Your own parents, brothers, and friends will betray you. Some of you will be killed. Everyone will hate you because of me. But not a single hair on your head will ultimately be destroyed. Stand firm, and you will win your souls."
§The Grand Finale
Jesus told them that Jerusalem would eventually be surrounded by armies and completely crushed.

"Then, the whole world is going to see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with massive power and blinding glory. When you see all this chaotic stuff start to happen, stand up straight and lift your heads high, because your rescue is right around the corner."

He warned them to stay sharp: "Be careful! Don't let your hearts get weighed down by partying, getting drunk, or stressing out about the anxieties of everyday life. If you do, that day will snap shut on you like a trap. Stay awake, and pray that you'll have the strength to survive all this and stand in front of the Son of Man."

Luke.title: The Setup, The Supper, and The Sellout
paragraphs: The Festival of Unleavened Bread (Passover) was approaching, and the corrupt chief priests were desperately looking for a quiet way to assassinate Jesus without the massive crowds rioting.

Suddenly, Satan entered Judas Iscariot, one of the original Twelve. Judas snuck off to the religious mafia and the Temple police, and they worked out a deal: they would pay him cash, and he would text them Jesus's location when no crowds were around.
§The Last Supper
Jesus sent Peter and John to prep the Passover meal. That evening, he sat down with his core crew.
"I have been dying to eat this Passover meal with you before my suffering begins," Jesus said.
He took some bread, gave thanks to God, broke it, and handed it to them: "This is my body, which is given for you. Do this to remember me."

After supper, he took a cup of wine: "This cup is the new covenant sealed in my blood, which is poured out for you. But look—the hand of the guy who is going to betray me is resting on this very table."
Right after this incredibly heavy, spiritual moment, the disciples actually started arguing again about which one of them was the greatest.

Jesus roasted their egos: "The kings of this world boss people around and demand to be called 'Benefactors.' You guys are not going to operate like that. The greatest guy among you needs to act like the youngest, and the boss needs to act like the servant. Who is greater: the guy eating at the table, or the guy serving the food? Obviously the guy eating. But look at me—I am among you as the guy who serves."

Jesus turned to Peter: "Simon, Simon. Satan has asked to sift all of you like wheat. But I have prayed specifically for you, Simon, that your faith won't completely fail. When you eventually turn back to me, you need to strengthen your brothers."
Peter puffed out his chest: "Lord, I am ready to go to prison with you, and even die with you!"
Jesus looked at him sadly. "Peter, before the rooster crows tomorrow morning, you will deny you even know me three separate times."
§The Ambush in the Dark

They went out to the Mount of Olives. Jesus told them, "Pray that you don't fall into temptation." He walked about a stone's throw away, fell to his knees, and prayed in absolute agony. "Father, if you are willing, take this cup of suffering away from me. But not what I want—what you want." He was in such intense psychological stress that his sweat fell to the ground like massive drops of blood.
When he got up and went back to his guys, they were completely passed out, exhausted from sorrow. "Why are you sleeping?!" he asked. "Get up and pray!"
While he was still talking, a massive, heavily armed mob showed up out of the dark. Judas walked right up to the front and kissed Jesus on the cheek.
Jesus said, "Judas. Are you really betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?"
When Jesus's guys realized what was happening, one of them pulled a sword, swung wildly, and sliced off the right ear of the high priest's servant.
Jesus yelled, "No more of this!" He reached out, touched the guy's bloody ear, and completely healed it.

Then he looked at the religious mafia leading the mob: "Am I some kind of dangerous terrorist, that you had to come after me with swords and clubs? I was with you in the Temple every single day, and you didn't touch me. But this is your hour—the time when darkness rules."
§Peter's Absolute Fail
They arrested Jesus and dragged him to the high priest's massive house. Peter followed from a safe distance and sat down by a fire pit in the middle of the courtyard to blend in.
A servant girl stared at him in the firelight. "This guy was with him!"
Peter panicked. "Woman, I don't even know him!"
A little later, a guy looked at him. "You're definitely one of them."
"Man, I am not!" Peter shot back.
About an hour later, another guy insisted, "This guy is absolutely one of them. He has a Galilean accent!"
Peter lost it. "Man, I don't know what you're talking about!"
The exact second those words left his mouth, a rooster crowed.
Jesus, who was being held nearby, turned and looked straight at Peter. Peter suddenly remembered what Jesus had said. He ran out of the courtyard and completely broke down, sobbing uncontrollably.
Meanwhile, the guards holding Jesus blindfolded him, beat him, and mocked him: "Prophesy! Who just hit you?"
At dawn, the council of religious elders put Jesus on trial. "If you are the Messiah, tell us!"
Jesus replied, "If I tell you, you won't believe me. But from now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the mighty God."
They all shouted, "So, are you the Son of God then?"
Jesus answered, "You say that I am."
They yelled, "We don't need any more witnesses! We heard it from his own mouth!"

Luke.title: The Trials and The Cross
paragraphs: The whole religious council dragged Jesus to Pilate, the Roman governor, and started throwing fake political charges at him: "This guy is trying to start a rebellion, telling people not to pay taxes, and claiming he's a king!"
Pilate asked Jesus, "Are you the king of the Jews?"
"You have said so," Jesus replied.
Pilate looked at the chief priests and the massive crowd. "I don't find any reason to charge this guy with a crime."

But the leaders kept screaming, so Pilate tried to pass the buck. He found out Jesus was from Galilee, which meant he was under King Herod's jurisdiction. Herod happened to be in Jerusalem, so Pilate sent Jesus to him.

Herod was thrilled. He had heard the hype and wanted to see Jesus perform a magic trick. But Jesus refused to answer a single one of Herod's questions. Herod and his soldiers got bored, mocked Jesus, threw an elegant robe on him as a joke, and sent him back to Pilate.
Pilate called the crowd together again. "Listen, neither Herod nor I found this guy guilty of anything. I'm going to have him whipped and then let him go."
But the mob went completely feral. "Kill him! Give us Barabbas instead!" (Barabbas was a literal murderer and a terrorist who had started a riot in the city).

Pilate tried to argue with them, but the mob just kept screaming, "Crucify him! Crucify him!" Their shouting was so intense that Pilate completely caved. He released the murderer and handed Jesus over to be executed.
§The Walk to the Skull

As they led Jesus away, he was so physically destroyed that he couldn't carry the heavy wooden cross. The guards grabbed a random guy out of the crowd named Simon from Cyrene and forced him to carry it behind Jesus.

A massive crowd followed, including women who were weeping and wailing for him. Jesus turned to them and said, "Daughters of Jerusalem, don't cry for me. Cry for yourselves and your kids, because incredibly dark days are coming to this city."
When they reached the place called The Skull (Golgotha), they nailed him to the cross, right between two criminals.
Even while they were murdering him, Jesus prayed: "Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing."
The Roman soldiers sat around and rolled dice to see who got to keep his clothes. The religious leaders sneered, "He saved others; let him save himself if he's really God's Messiah!"
One of the criminals hanging next to him started trash-talking too: "Aren't you the Messiah? Save yourself and us!"

But the other criminal shut him down. "Don't you fear God? We are getting exactly what we deserve for our crimes. But this guy hasn't done anything wrong." Then he looked at Jesus. "Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom."
Jesus looked back at him and said, "I am telling you the truth: today you will be with me in paradise."
§The Sky Goes Dark
At noon, the sun literally stopped shining, and darkness covered the entire land for three hours. The massive, thick curtain hanging inside the Temple ripped right down the middle.
Jesus called out with a massive voice, "Father, into your hands I commit my spirit." When he said this, he died.
The Roman Centurion running the execution saw exactly how Jesus died. He praised God and said, "Surely this was a righteous man."

A good, honorable Jewish leader named Joseph from Arimathea (who hadn't agreed with the council's decision) went to Pilate and bravely asked for Jesus's body. He took the body down, wrapped it in linen cloth, and placed it in a tomb cut right out of solid rock, where nobody had ever been buried. It was Friday afternoon, and the Sabbath was about to start, so the women who followed Jesus went home to prepare spices and perfumes to anoint his body on Sunday.

Luke.title: The Empty Tomb and The Epic Comeback
paragraphs: Very early on Sunday morning, the women took the spices to the tomb.
They found the massive stone rolled completely away from the entrance! They walked in, but the body of the Lord Jesus was gone.
While they were standing there totally confused, two men wearing clothes that literally flashed like lightning suddenly stood beside them. The women were terrified and dropped face-down to the dirt.

The glowing men said to them: "Why are you looking for the living among the dead? He isn't here; he has risen! Remember what he told you back in Galilee: The Son of Man had to be handed over to sinners, be crucified, and on the third day rise again."
Then it clicked. They remembered his words.
They sprinted back from the tomb and told the eleven apostles and everyone else what happened. (It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and a few others).

But the guys thought the women were talking absolute nonsense and didn't believe a word of it. Peter, however, jumped up and literally sprinted to the tomb. He bent over, looked in, and saw only the strips of linen lying there. He walked away completely mind-blown, wondering what in the world had happened.
§Undercover on the Road to Emmaus
That exact same day, two of Jesus's followers were walking to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles outside Jerusalem. They were talking about the insane events of the weekend.
While they were debating, Jesus himself walked up and started traveling with them, but God kept them from recognizing him.
Jesus asked, "What are you guys arguing about?"
They stopped dead in their tracks, looking absolutely devastated. One guy, Cleopas, said, "Are you the only visitor in Jerusalem who doesn't know what just happened?"
"What things?" Jesus asked.

"About Jesus of Nazareth!" they replied. "He was a massive prophet. We totally thought he was the one who was going to rescue Israel. But the chief priests handed him over, and they crucified him. And now, some women from our group totally blew our minds. They went to the tomb this morning, couldn't find his body, and claimed they saw angels who said he was alive! Some of our guys went to check, and the tomb was empty, but they didn't see him."

Jesus essentially said, "You guys are so slow to catch on! Didn't the Messiah have to suffer all these things before entering his glory?" Then, starting all the way back with Moses and the prophets, Jesus explained exactly how the entire Old Testament pointed straight to him.
When they got to Emmaus, Jesus acted like he was going to keep walking. But they begged him, "Stay with us, it's getting dark!" So he went in.
When they sat down at the table, Jesus took the bread, gave thanks, broke it, and handed it to them.
Instantly, their eyes were opened, and they realized it was him! And the second they recognized him, he literally vanished into thin air.
They looked at each other. "Weren't our hearts burning inside us when he was explaining the Scriptures on the road?!"

They didn't even care that it was dark; they got up immediately and ran all seven miles back to Jerusalem. They burst into the room where the Eleven were hiding and yelled, "It's true! The Lord has risen!"
§The Final Boss Move
While they were still telling the story, Jesus himself suddenly materialized right in the middle of the room. "Peace be with you," he said.
They absolutely lost their minds with terror, thinking they were seeing a ghost.

Jesus laughed. "Why are you so freaked out? Why are you doubting? Look at my hands and my feet. It's really me! Touch me and see. Ghosts don't have flesh and bones like I do." He showed them the nail scars.
They were so full of joy and shock they still couldn't process it. So Jesus asked, "Do you guys have anything to eat here?"
They handed him a piece of broiled fish, and he ate it right in front of them just to prove he was physically, totally alive.

He looked at his team. "This is exactly what I told you when I was still with you: Everything written about me in the Law, the Prophets, and the Psalms had to be fulfilled." Then he opened their minds so they could finally fully understand the Bible.

"This is what is written: The Messiah will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day. Now, forgiveness of sins will be preached in his name to all nations, starting right here in Jerusalem. You are my official witnesses. I am going to send you what my Father promised; but stay in the city until you are completely clothed with power from heaven."
Jesus led them out to the vicinity of Bethany. He lifted his hands and blessed them. While he was blessing them, he physically left them and was taken straight up into heaven.
His disciples fell down and worshipped him, and then returned to Jerusalem with massive, unstoppable joy. They stayed continually at the Temple, praising God.

John.title: The Cosmic Opening and the First Draft
paragraphs: John doesn’t start with a manger or a baby. He goes all the way back to before the universe even existed.

"In the absolute beginning was the Word. The Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was there before anything was created. Through him, literally everything was made. He brought life and light into the dark world, and the darkness could not stop it."
Then John drops the ultimate plot twist: The Word became actual flesh and blood and moved into our neighborhood. That "Word" was Jesus.
§The Hype Man Points Him Out
John the Baptist was out in the desert baptizing people. The religious leaders sent a squad from Jerusalem to interrogate him: "Who are you? Are you the Messiah? Elijah? A prophet?"
John the Baptist said, "No, no, and no. I'm just the hype man shouting in the desert to get the road ready for the Lord."

The very next day, John the Baptist saw Jesus walking toward him. John pointed right at him and yelled to the crowd: "Look! The Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the entire world! This is the guy I was talking about. I saw the Holy Spirit come down on him like a dove. He is the Son of God!"
§Drafting the First Guys
The next day, two of John the Baptist’s followers (Andrew and John) heard him hype up Jesus again, so they just started following Jesus down the road. Jesus turned around: "What do you guys want?"
They were awkward. "Uh... Rabbi, where are you staying?"
Jesus smiled. "Come and see." They hung out with him the rest of the day.
Andrew was so excited he immediately ran to find his tough brother, Simon. "We found the Messiah!" Andrew brought him to Jesus.
Jesus took one look at Simon and said, "You are Simon. From now on, your name is Cephas (Peter, which means 'The Rock')."
The next day, Jesus found a guy named Philip and told him, "Follow me."
Philip immediately ran to find his buddy Nathanael. "We found the guy Moses and the prophets wrote about! It's Jesus from Nazareth!"
Nathanael threw some massive shade: "Nazareth? Can anything good even come out of that nowhere town?"
Philip said, "Come and see."
As Nathanael walked up, Jesus said, "Look, a true Israelite with zero fake in him!"
Nathanael was suspicious. "How do you know me?"
Jesus dropped a casual flex: "Before Philip even called you, when you were sitting all by yourself under that fig tree miles away... I saw you."
Nathanael’s jaw dropped. "Rabbi! You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!"
Jesus laughed. "You believe just because I said I saw you under a tree? Buckle up, man. You are going to see heaven ripped open and angels going up and down on the Son of Man."

John.title: The Wedding Crash and the Temple Whip
paragraphs: Three days later, there was a massive wedding party in a town called Cana. Jesus, his mom (Mary), and his new disciples were all invited.
In that culture, running out of wine at a wedding was a massive social disaster that would humiliate the family forever. And they ran out.
Mary came up to Jesus and whispered, "They have no more wine."
Jesus said, "Mom, why are you involving me? My official time hasn't come yet."
Mary totally ignored his hesitation. She just looked at the servants and said, "Do exactly whatever he tells you."
Jesus saw six massive stone water jars that held about 20 to 30 gallons each. He told the servants, "Fill them to the brim with water." They did. "Now dip some out and take it to the head waiter."

When the waiter tasted it, the water had turned into the absolute highest-tier, most expensive wine imaginable. He pulled the groom aside: "Listen, everyone serves the cheap stuff after people are drunk, but you saved the best for last!"
This was Jesus's very first miracle, and it completely solidified his disciples' faith.
§The Temple Whip

It was almost time for the Jewish Passover, so Jesus went to Jerusalem. He walked into the massive Temple courtyard and saw an absolute scam going on. People were selling cattle, sheep, and doves at insane markups, and corrupt money changers were ripping people off.
Jesus didn't just yell. He sat down, braided a literal whip out of ropes, stood up, and absolutely cleared the place out.

He chased the animals out, flipped the money changers' tables, scattered their coins all over the floor, and yelled, "Get this garbage out of here! Stop turning my Father's house into a shopping mall!"
The religious leaders ran up, furious. "What miracle sign can you show us to prove you have the authority to do this?!"
Jesus dropped a massive, confusing mic-drop: "Destroy this temple, and I will raise it back up in three days."
They laughed in his face. "It took 46 years to build this Temple, and you're going to rebuild it in three days?!"
They didn't realize he wasn't talking about the building; he was talking about his own body. (His disciples remembered this line three years later when he rose from the dead).

John.title: The Midnight Meeting and the Famous Verse
paragraphs: There was a Pharisee named Nicodemus. He was a highly educated VIP on the Jewish ruling council. He knew the other leaders hated Jesus, so he snuck out to meet Jesus secretly in the middle of the night.
"Rabbi," Nicodemus said, "we know you are a teacher from God, because nobody could pull off these miracles unless God was with him."
Jesus cut right to the chase: "I'll give it to you straight. Unless a person is born again, they cannot see the kingdom of God."
Nicodemus was a literal thinker and got super confused. "How can an old guy be born again? He can't climb back inside his mother's womb!"

Jesus explained: "I'm not talking about physical birth. Flesh gives birth to flesh, but the Spirit gives birth to spirit. Don't be shocked. You can't see the wind, but you can see what it does. It's the same with the Holy Spirit."
Nicodemus was still lost. "How is this possible?"
Jesus roasted him a little: "You're supposed to be Israel's top teacher, and you don't here's the thing? I'm telling you about heavenly things."
Then Jesus dropped the most famous, ultimate summary of the entire Bible (John 3:16):

"For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life. For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through him."
§John the Baptist Steps Aside
Later, Jesus and his squad were out in the countryside baptizing people. John the Baptist was nearby doing the same thing.

Some of John's followers got jealous and ran to complain to him: "Hey! That Jesus guy you hyped up is baptizing people, and now literally everyone is going to him instead of us! We're losing followers!"
John the Baptist's response is the ultimate definition of humility:

"Guys, a person can only receive what God gives them. I told you from day one I am not the Messiah. I'm just the best man at the wedding. The bride belongs to the groom. I'm just happy to hear the groom's voice. He must become greater; I must become less."

John.title: The Woman at the Well and the Long-Distance Miracle
paragraphs: Jesus had to travel from Judea to Galilee. The standard route went completely around the region of Samaria because Jews and Samaritans absolutely hated each other. They were bitter, racist rivals who wouldn't even use the same cups.
But Jesus purposely walked right straight through the middle of enemy territory.

He sat down by an ancient well in the middle of the day, exhausted. A Samaritan woman came out to draw water. (She came at noon, the hottest part of the day, because she had a terrible reputation and wanted to avoid all the other women).
Jesus casually asked her, "Will you give me a drink?"
She was shocked. "You're a Jewish guy, and I'm a Samaritan woman. Why are you even talking to me?"

Jesus said, "If you knew who you were talking to, you would have asked me, and I would have given you living water. Anyone who drinks from this well will get thirsty again. But whoever drinks the water I give them will never thirst. It will become a spring of eternal life inside them."
She said, "Sir, give me this water so I don't have to keep hauling buckets out here."
Jesus tested her: "Go call your husband and come back."
She looked down. "I don't have a husband."
Jesus read her entire life like an open book: "You're right. You've had five husbands, and the guy you're sleeping with right now isn't your husband."
She stepped back, stunned. "Sir, I can see you're a prophet." She tried to change the subject to a religious argument about where people should worship.
Jesus shut down the argument: "It's not about the location anymore. True worshippers worship the Father in Spirit and in truth."
The woman said, "Well, I know the Messiah is coming eventually. He'll explain everything."
Jesus looked right at her: "I, the one speaking to you—I am he."
She completely forgot her water jar, sprinted back into town, and yelled to everyone, "Come see a guy who told me everything I ever did! Could this be the Messiah?!"
Because of her testimony, the whole Samaritan town came out, and Jesus stayed with them for two days. Massive numbers of "enemies" believed in him.
§The Long-Distance Flex
Jesus left and went back to Cana in Galilee. A powerful royal official tracked him down and begged Jesus to come to Capernaum (about 20 miles away) to heal his son, who was on his deathbed.
Jesus looked at the desperate dad and simply said, "Go. Your son will live."
The official took him at his word and started the long walk home. On the road, his servants ran up to meet him: "Your boy is alive and completely recovered!"
The dad asked exactly what time the fever broke. The servants said, "Yesterday at 1:00 PM." It was the exact second Jesus had spoken the words. The official and his entire household believed.

John.title: The Pool of Bethesda and the Boss Claim
paragraphs: Jesus went back to Jerusalem for a festival. Near the Sheep Gate, there was a pool called Bethesda surrounded by massive covered colonnades. It was packed with blind, crippled, and paralyzed people who believed the water had magical healing properties if it got stirred up.
Jesus walked through the crowd and saw a guy who had been an invalid, paralyzed on his mat, for 38 straight years.
Jesus walked right up to him and asked, "Do you want to get well?"
The guy made excuses. "Sir, I have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred. Someone else always beats me to it."
Jesus didn't offer to help him into the water. He just gave an order: "Get up! Pick up your mat and walk."
Instantly, the 38-year paralysis vanished. The guy grabbed his mat and walked away.
§The Sabbath Trap and the God Claim
But there was a catch: it was the Sabbath.
The religious police saw the guy carrying his mat and threw a fit: "It is illegal for you to carry your mat on the Sabbath! You're breaking the rules!"
The guy panicked. "The man who healed me told me to pick it up!"
They demanded, "Who told you to do that?!" But the guy didn't even know Jesus's name because Jesus had slipped away into the crowd.

Later, Jesus found the guy in the Temple and said, "Look, you are well now. Stop sinning, or something worse may happen to you." The guy immediately ran and informered to the Jewish leaders that it was Jesus who healed him.
The leaders tracked Jesus down and started aggressively interrogating him for breaking their Sabbath rules.
Jesus didn't back down. In fact, he doubled down with a claim that made them want to murder him: "My Father is always at his work to this very day, and I too am working."
The leaders absolutely lost their minds. Not only was he breaking the Sabbath, but he was calling God his own personal Father, literally making himself equal with God.
They tried to kill him right there, but Jesus dropped a massive, unbreakable speech about his authority:
"I'll give it to you straight: the Son can do nothing by himself; he can only do what he sees his Father doing. The Father loves the Son and shows him everything.
The Father judges no one, but has handed all ultimate judgment over to the Son, so that everyone will honor the Son exactly as they honor the Father. If you don't honor me, you don't honor God.
A time is coming, and has now come, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live. I have the authority to grant life.

You diligently study the Scriptures because you think you have eternal life in them. But those very Scriptures point straight to me, and you refuse to come to me to get actual life! Don't worry, I won't accuse you before the Father. Moses will accuse you. Because if you actually believed Moses, you would believe me, because Moses wrote about me."

John.title: The Ultimate Catering Miracle and the Hard Truth
paragraphs: A massive crowd of thousands was tracking Jesus because they saw him healing the sick. Jesus hiked up a mountainside near the Sea of Galilee and sat down with his disciples.

He looked up, saw the massive mob coming toward them, and tested Philip: "Where can we buy enough bread to feed all these people?" Philip panicked. "Boss, half a year's wages wouldn't buy enough for everyone to even get one bite!" Andrew chimed in, "Well, there's a kid here who has five small barley loaves and two small fish. But what is that going to do for thousands of people?"

Jesus said, "Have everyone sit down." There was a lot of grass there, so the men (about 5,000 of them, plus families) sat down. Jesus took the loaves, thanked God, and started handing out the food. He did the same with the fish. He literally created food out of nowhere until every single person was completely stuffed. "Gather the leftovers," Jesus told his crew. "Don't waste anything." They filled twelve massive baskets with just the leftover bread!
The crowd was so excited they wanted to grab Jesus by force and make him their political King right then and there. But Jesus slipped away by himself further up the mountain.
§Defying Gravity

When it got dark, his disciples got into a boat to cross the lake back to Capernaum. A brutal wind started howling, whipping the water into massive waves. They had rowed about three or four miles, fighting for their lives, when they suddenly saw Jesus casually walking on the water right toward the boat. They were absolutely terrified. But he called out over the storm: "It is I; don't be afraid." They gladly pulled him into the boat, and instantly, the boat teleported to the exact shore they were heading for.

The Bread of Life Drop The next day, the massive crowd realized Jesus had vanished, so they rented boats, crossed the lake, and tracked him down in Capernaum. "Rabbi, when did you get here?" they asked. Jesus saw right through them. "You guys aren't looking for me because you saw spiritual signs. You're looking for me because you got free food and your stomachs are full. Stop working so hard for food that spoils. Work for the food that gives eternal life."

The crowd asked, "What miracle are you going to do so we'll believe you? Our ancestors got manna (bread from heaven) in the desert from Moses." Jesus corrected them: "Moses didn't give them that bread; my Father did. And right now, God is giving you the true bread from heaven. I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty."

Then Jesus took it to an intense, graphic level to test who was actually serious about following him: "I'm telling you the truth, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you." (Note: He was talking about spiritually taking him in completely, sacrificing his body on the cross, but the crowd took it literally).

The people were completely grossed out. "This teaching is way too hard. Who can accept it?" From that exact moment, massive numbers of his followers just quit and walked away. Jesus looked at his core Twelve. "You guys want to leave too?" Peter stepped up with an epic response: "Lord, who else would we even go to? You have the words of eternal life. We have come to believe and know that you are the Holy One of God."

John.title: Undercover at the Festival
paragraphs: The Jewish Festival of Tabernacles (a massive, week-long camping festival in Jerusalem) was coming up. Jesus's own brothers were mocking him: "Why don't you go to Judea and show off your miracles? You can't be a public figure if you're hiding out here." (Even his own brothers didn't believe in him yet). Jesus told them, "My time hasn't come yet. You guys go. I'm staying."

But after they left, Jesus went to the festival in Jerusalem completely undercover. The entire city was buzzing about him. Half the crowd was whispering, "He's a good guy." The other half was saying, "No way, he's a scammer." But nobody talked too loud because everyone was terrified of the religious mafia.

Halfway through the festival, Jesus walked right into the Temple courtyard and started teaching openly. The leaders were mind-blown. "How does this guy know so much without any official theological degrees?" Jesus answered: "My teaching isn't mine. It comes straight from the God who sent me. If anyone actually wants to do God's will, they will realize my teaching is legit. You guys are trying to kill me because I healed a guy's whole body on the Sabbath. Stop judging by appearances and make a right judgment!"

The crowd was confused. "Wait, isn't this the guy they are trying to assassinate? He's speaking publicly, and they aren't arresting him. Do the bosses actually think he's the Messiah?" Jesus yelled out, "You know me, and you know where I am from. But I am not here on my own authority. The one who sent me is true. You don't know him, but I do, because I came directly from him."
The leaders were so furious they sent the Temple SWAT team to arrest him.

The Water Flex On the very last and greatest day of the festival, Jesus stood up and shouted to the massive crowd: "Let anyone who is thirsty come to me and drink! Whoever believes in me, rivers of living water will flow from within them." (He was talking about the Holy Spirit, which hadn't been given yet).

The Temple guards who were sent to arrest him came back to the chief priests empty-handed. "Why didn't you bring him in?!" the priests demanded. The tough guards were completely hypnotized: "No one has ever spoken like this man." The Pharisees sneered. "Did you fools get fooled too? Do you see any of the real leaders believing in him? Only this cursed, ignorant mob believes that garbage." Nicodemus (the guy who met Jesus at night) tried to defend him: "Doesn't our law require a fair hearing before we condemn a guy?" They mocked him. "Are you from Galilee too? Look into it—no prophet comes out of Galilee."

John.title: The Trap, The Light, and the Ultimate Mic Drop
paragraphs: The next morning, Jesus was back teaching in the Temple. The Pharisees and religious experts dragged in a woman who had been caught in the actual act of adultery. They made her stand right in the middle of the crowd. "Teacher," they said, "this woman was caught cheating. The Law of Moses says we have to stone her to death. What do you say?"

It was a brilliant, deadly trap. If Jesus said "Let her go," he was breaking the Law of Moses. If he said "Kill her," he was breaking Roman law (only Romans could execute people) and ruining his reputation of mercy.

Jesus didn't say a word. He just bent down and started writing in the dirt with his finger. They kept aggressively questioning him. Finally, he stood up, looked right at them, and said, "Let any one of you who is completely without sin be the first to throw a stone at her." Then he bent down and kept writing in the dirt.

The leaders froze. One by one, starting with the oldest guys, they dropped their rocks and walked away in absolute shame, until only Jesus and the woman were left. Jesus stood up. "Woman, where are they? Did no one condemn you?" "No one, sir," she said. "Then neither do I condemn you," Jesus declared. "Go now, and leave your life of sin."

The Light and the Argument Later, Jesus dropped another massive statement: "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life." The Pharisees challenged him: "You're testifying about yourself. That doesn't count in court." Jesus said, "Even if I testify about myself, my testimony is valid because I know exactly where I came from and exactly where I am going. You guys have no clue. I judge with the Father who sent me."

The argument got incredibly heated. Jesus told them, "You are from below; I am from above. You belong to this world; I do not. If you don't believe that I am who I claim to be, you will die in your sins."

He then said, "If you hold to my teaching, you are really my disciples. Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free." They got incredibly offended. "We are descendants of Abraham! We have never been slaves to anyone!" Jesus went straight for the throat: "Everyone who sins is a slave to sin. I know you are Abraham's descendants physically, but you are trying to murder me! If you were truly Abraham's children, you would act like him. But you belong to your actual father, the devil, and you want to carry out your father's desires. He was a murderer from the beginning and the father of lies."

The religious leaders absolutely lost it. "Aren't we right in saying you are demon-possessed?!" Jesus said, "I am not possessed. I honor my Father, and you dishonor me. I'm telling you, whoever obeys my word will never see death." They snapped. "Now we know you have a demon! Abraham died. The prophets died. Are you greater than our father Abraham?!"
Jesus delivered the ultimate, universe-shaking mic drop:

"Your father Abraham rejoiced at the thought of seeing my day; he saw it and was glad." "You aren't even fifty years old!" they screamed. "And you have seen Abraham?!" Jesus looked right at them. "Very truly I tell you, before Abraham was even born, I AM!"

(Note: "I AM" is the sacred, unutterable name of God from the Old Testament. Jesus literally just told them He is the eternal God). The leaders immediately grabbed heavy stones to execute him on the spot, but Jesus hid himself and slipped out of the Temple grounds.

John.title: Spit, Mud, and the Blind Guy Who Roasted the Pharisees
paragraphs: Walking down the street, Jesus saw a guy who had been completely blind since the day he was born. His disciples asked a theological question: "Rabbi, whose fault is this? Did this guy sin in the womb, or did his parents sin?" Jesus said, "Neither. This happened so that the absolute works of God could be displayed in his life."
Jesus then did something incredibly unconventional. He spit in the dirt, mixed it into mud, and rubbed the mud onto the blind guy's eyes. "Go," Jesus told him. "Wash off in the Pool of Siloam."
The guy blindly felt his way to the pool, washed his face, and for the first time in his entire life, his eyes opened. He could see perfectly.

His neighbors were completely freaked out. "Wait, isn't this the blind beggar?" Some said yes. Others said, "No, it just looks like him." The guy kept shouting, "It's me! The guy they call Jesus made some mud, put it on my eyes, and now I can see!"

Because Jesus made mud and healed on a Sabbath, the neighbors brought the guy to the Pharisees. The Pharisees aggressively interrogated him. "How did this happen?!" The guy said, "He put mud on my eyes, I washed, and now I see." Some Pharisees said, "This Jesus guy is not from God, because he doesn't keep the Sabbath rules." Others argued, "But how can a sinner do such crazy miraculous signs?" They were completely divided.

They didn't even believe the guy was actually born blind, so they dragged his parents in. "Is this your son? Was he born blind? How can he see?" His parents were terrified of getting kicked out of the synagogue, so they dodged the question: "He is our son, and he was born blind. But we have no idea how he can see now. Ask him. He's an adult."

The Pharisees called the healed guy back in. "Give glory to God! We know this Jesus guy is a sinner." The formerly blind guy dropped an absolute legendary response: "Whether he's a sinner or not, I don't know. I just know one thing for an absolute fact: I was blind, and now I see." They kept pressing him. "What did he do to you? How did he do it?!" The guy got sarcastic and completely roasted them: "I already told you! Didn't you listen? Why do you want to hear it again? Do you guys want to become his disciples too?"

The Pharisees went ballistic. "You are his disciple! We are disciples of Moses! We don't even know where this guy comes from!" The guy laughed at them: "This is remarkable! You are the religious experts, and you don't know where he comes from, yet he opened my eyes! Nobody in the history of the world has ever opened the eyes of a man born blind. If this guy were not from God, he couldn't do anything." Furious that a beggar was lecturing them, they yelled, "You were steeped in sin at birth! How dare you lecture us!" And they permanently kicked him out of the synagogue (ruining his social life).

Jesus heard they kicked him out and tracked the guy down. "Do you believe in the Son of Man?" Jesus asked. "Who is he, sir?" the man asked. "Tell me so I can believe in him." Jesus said, "You have now seen him. In fact, he is the one speaking with you." The man dropped to his knees. "Lord, I believe," and he worshipped him.

John.title: The Good Shepherd and the Hanukkah Showdown
paragraphs: Jesus kept the momentum going, calling out the corrupt religious leaders by comparing them to terrible shepherds who steal and slaughter the sheep. Jesus said: "I tell you the truth, I am the gate for the sheep. All those who came before me were thieves and robbers. I am the gate; whoever enters through me will be completely saved. The thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy. I have come that they may have life, and have it to the absolute max."
§Then he dropped another famous claim:

"I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. The hired hand isn't a real shepherd. When he sees a wolf coming, he abandons the sheep and runs away to save himself. I am the good shepherd. I know my sheep and my sheep know me. No one takes my life from me, but I lay it down completely of my own free will. I have the authority to lay it down, and the authority to take it up again." The crowd was massively divided again. Some said, "He's insane and demon-possessed!" Others said, "A demon can't open the eyes of the blind!"

The Hanukkah Showdown Fast forward to winter. It was the Festival of Dedication (Hanukkah) in Jerusalem. Jesus was walking in the Temple courts. The religious mafia completely surrounded him, trying to box him in. "How long are you going to keep us in suspense? If you are the Messiah, just say it plainly!"

Jesus answered, "I did tell you, but you refuse to believe. The massive miracles I do in my Father's name prove exactly who I am. But you don't believe because you are not my sheep. My sheep listen to my voice. I know them, and they follow me. I give them eternal life, and no one will ever snatch them out of my hand."
Then Jesus dropped the final nail in the coffin: "I and the Father are one."

The Jewish opponents immediately picked up large stones to crush him to death. Jesus didn't flinch. "I have shown you many great miracles from the Father. For which of these are you trying to stone me?" "We are not stoning you for any good work," they screamed. "We are stoning you for blasphemy! Because you, a mere human being, claim to be God!"

They lunged to arrest him, but Jesus flawlessly slipped right out of their grasp. He left Jerusalem and crossed back over the Jordan River to the place where John the Baptist had been baptizing, and he stayed there out of their reach. Many people went out to him and believed in him.

John.title: The Ultimate Flex (Raising the Dead)
paragraphs: There was a guy named Lazarus who was incredibly sick. He lived in the town of Bethany with his two sisters, Mary and Martha. (This is the same Mary who later poured the expensive perfume on Jesus’s feet).

The sisters sent an urgent text to Jesus: "Lord, your absolute best friend is sick." When Jesus heard it, he didn't panic. He told his crew, "This sickness isn't going to end in death. It's happening so that God's glory can be shown, and so the Son of God can be glorified through it."

Even though Jesus loved Martha, Mary, and Lazarus deeply, he purposely stayed exactly where he was for two more full days. Finally, he said to his disciples, "Let's head back to Judea." His guys were shocked. "Rabbi, just a few days ago the religious leaders there were literally trying to stone you to death! And you want to go back?!" Jesus basically told them that as long as they were walking in the "light" (doing God's will), they wouldn't stumble. Then he said, "Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I'm going there to wake him up." The disciples took it literally: "Lord, if he's sleeping, he'll get better on his own. Let him rest." Jesus had to give it to them straight: "Lazarus is dead. And for your sake, I'm actually glad I wasn't there, so that you can finally truly believe. Let's go to him." Thomas (the pessimist of the group) looked at the rest of the squad and said, "Well, we might as well go with him so we can all die together."

The Confrontation and the Resurrection By the time Jesus arrived, Lazarus had been completely dead and rotting in a stone tomb for four solid days. Since Bethany was only about two miles from Jerusalem, a massive crowd of Jews had come over to comfort Mary and Martha.

When Martha heard Jesus was coming, she ran out to meet him on the road. "Lord," she said, "if you had been here, my brother wouldn't have died! But I know that even now, God will give you whatever you ask." Jesus looked at her. "Your brother will rise again." Martha nodded. "I know he will rise again in the resurrection at the end of time." Jesus dropped one of the most massive, universe-shifting claims in history:

"I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die; and whoever lives by believing in me will never truly die. Do you believe this?" "Yes, Lord," she said. "I believe you are the Messiah, the Son of God."

Martha went back and got Mary. When Mary reached Jesus, she collapsed at his feet, sobbing. "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died." When Jesus saw her crying, and saw the massive crowd weeping with her, he was deeply moved in his spirit and incredibly troubled. "Where have you laid him?" he asked. "Come and see, Lord," they replied. Jesus wept.
The crowd whispered, "Look how much he loved him!" But some of the haters muttered, "He opened the eyes of a blind man. Couldn't he have stopped his friend from dying?"

Jesus, deeply moved again, walked up to the tomb. It was a cave with a massive stone rolled across the entrance. "Take away the stone," Jesus ordered. Martha panicked. "Lord, by now the smell of rotting flesh is going to be horrific! He's been in there for four days!" Jesus looked at her. "Didn't I tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?"

They shoved the heavy stone out of the way. Jesus looked up to the sky and said, "Father, I thank you that you have heard me. I know you always hear me, but I'm saying this out loud for the benefit of the crowd standing right here, so they will believe that you sent me." Then he shouted with a booming, commanding voice: "Lazarus, come out!"

The dead man literally hopped out of the dark cave. His hands and feet were still completely wrapped in strips of linen, and a cloth was wrapped around his face like a mummy. Jesus turned to the shocked crowd and casually said, "Take off his grave clothes and let him go."

The Hit gets Ordered Because of this massive miracle, a ton of people who saw it instantly believed in Jesus. But some informeres ran straight to the Pharisees and told them what happened. The chief priests and Pharisees called an emergency meeting of the ruling council. "What are we doing?!" they panicked. "This guy is performing massive signs. If we let him keep doing this, everyone will believe in him, and then the Romans will come and destroy our Temple and our entire nation!" Caiaphas, the high priest that year, stood up. "You guys know nothing. Don't you realize it is better for one man to die for the people than for the whole nation to be destroyed?" (He didn't realize he was actually prophesying that Jesus would die to save everyone). From that exact day forward, they officially plotted the assassination of Jesus. Jesus stopped walking publicly among the Jews and retreated with his disciples to a village near the desert.

John.title: The Perfume, The Traitor, and The Parade
paragraphs: Six days before the Passover festival, Jesus came back to Bethany. They threw a dinner in his honor. Martha was serving the food, and Lazarus (the guy who used to be dead) was chilling at the table with Jesus.

Mary came in carrying a pint jar of pure nard—an incredibly rare, insanely expensive perfume worth an entire year's salary. She cracked it open, poured it all over Jesus's feet, and then humbly wiped his feet with her own hair. The whole house smelled amazing.

But Judas Iscariot—the disciple who was about to betray him—threw a fit. "Why wasn't this perfume sold for three hundred denarii and the cash given to the poor?!" (John drops a quick author's note here: Judas didn't actually care about the poor. He was a thief. As the keeper of the team's money bag, he regularly embezzled and stole the cash for himself).

Jesus shut Judas down immediately. "Leave her alone. It was intended that she should save this perfume for the day of my burial. You will always have the poor among you, but you will not always have me."

Meanwhile, a massive crowd of Jews found out Jesus was at the house. They didn't just come to see Jesus; they wanted to see Lazarus, the walking miracle. Because of this, the chief priests secretly made plans to murder Lazarus too, because he was the walking proof that Jesus was God.

The Triumphal Parade The next day, the massive crowds that had come for the Passover festival heard Jesus was heading into Jerusalem. They grabbed palm branches and went out to meet him, screaming at the top of their lungs: "Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Blessed is the king of Israel!"

Jesus found a young donkey and rode it into the city, perfectly fulfilling an ancient prophecy from the Scriptures. At the time, his disciples had no idea what was going on, but after Jesus was glorified, they connected the dots. The Pharisees watched the massive, chaotic parade and threw their hands up in frustration. "Look! This is getting us nowhere. The entire world has gone after him!"
The Kernel of Wheat and the Thunder Some Greeks who were in town for the festival tracked down Philip and asked, "Sir, we want to see Jesus." Philip and Andrew went and told Jesus.

Jesus responded with a heavy prediction about his upcoming death: "The hour has finally come for the Son of Man to be glorified. I'm telling you the absolute truth: Unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a single seed. But if it dies, it produces a massive harvest of many seeds. Anyone who loves their life will lose it, while anyone who hates their life in this world will keep it for eternal life. Whoever serves me must follow me."

Suddenly, the weight of the cross hit him. "Now my soul is deeply troubled. What should I say? 'Father, save me from this hour'? No, this is the exact reason I came to this hour! Father, glorify your name!"

Instantly, a massive voice thundered from heaven: "I have glorified it, and will glorify it again." The crowd standing there heard it and thought it was actual thunder. Others said, "An angel just spoke to him!" Jesus told them, "That voice didn't happen for my benefit, it happened for yours. Now is the time for judgment on this world; now the prince of this world (Satan) will be completely driven out. And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself." (He said this to show exactly what kind of death he was going to die—being lifted up on a cross).

Even after all his massive miracles, a lot of people still refused to believe in him. However, many of the actual leaders did believe in him, but they kept it a complete secret because they were terrified the Pharisees would kick them out of the synagogue. They loved the praise of humans more than the praise of God.

John.title: Dirty Feet and the Setup
paragraphs: It was the night before the Passover festival. Jesus knew that the clock had run out and it was time for him to leave this world and go back to the Father. He had loved his squad his entire ministry, and now he was going to show them the ultimate, fullest extent of his love.

The evening meal was being served. The devil had already planted the idea of betrayal into the heart of Judas Iscariot. Jesus knew he had all power from God, so he did the most unexpected thing possible.

He stood up from the meal, took off his outer clothes, and wrapped a servant's towel around his waist. He poured water into a basin, actually got down on his hands and knees, and started washing his disciples' filthy, dust-caked feet, drying them with the towel.

When he got to Simon Peter, Peter completely rejected it. "Lord, are you going to wash my feet?!" Jesus replied, "You don't realize now what I am doing, but later you will understand." "No," Peter insisted. "You shall never wash my feet!" Jesus looked him dead in the eye. "Unless I wash you, you have no part with me."

Peter immediately completely overcorrected. "Then, Lord, not just my feet but my hands and my head too! Give me a full bath!" Jesus smiled. "Those who have had a bath need only to wash their feet; their whole body is clean. And you guys are clean... but not every single one of you." (He knew exactly who was going to betray him).

When he finished washing their feet, he put his clothes back on and returned to his spot at the table. "Do you understand what I just did for you? You call me 'Teacher' and 'Lord,' and you're right. Now that I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you absolutely must wash one another's feet. I just gave you the ultimate example. No servant is greater than his master. Now that you know these things, you will be blessed if you actually do them."
Exposing the Traitor Jesus's spirit became incredibly heavy. "I'm telling you the absolute truth: one of you is going to betray me."

His disciples stared at each other, completely baffled, trying to figure out who he meant. John (the disciple writing this book) was reclining right next to Jesus at the table. Peter motioned to John and mouthed, "Ask him who it is." John leaned back against Jesus's chest and whispered, "Lord, who is it?" Jesus whispered back, "It is the one to whom I will give this piece of bread when I have dipped it in the dish." He dipped the bread and handed it straight to Judas Iscariot. The exact second Judas took the bread, Satan fully entered into him. Jesus looked at Judas and said, "What you are about to do, do quickly." Nobody else at the table understood what was happening. Because Judas was the treasurer, they assumed Jesus was telling him to go buy more supplies for the festival or give cash to the poor. As soon as Judas took the bread, he got up and walked out into the pitch-black night.

The New Rule and the Harsh Reality Check Once Judas was gone, Jesus looked at his loyal guys. "My children, I will be with you only a little longer. Where I am going, you cannot come. "So I am giving you a brand new command: Love one another. Exactly as I have loved you, so you must love one another. By this, everyone in the world will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another."

Simon Peter interrupted. "Lord, where are you going?" Jesus replied, "Where I am going, you cannot follow now, but you will follow later." Peter puffed out his chest. "Lord, why can't I follow you now? I will lay down my life for you!" Jesus gave him a brutal reality check. "Will you really lay down your life for me? Very truly I tell you, before the rooster crows tomorrow morning, you will disown me three separate times!"

John.title: The Way, The Truth, and The Promise
paragraphs: The disciples were completely freaked out. Jesus had just said he was leaving them, and he just told Peter that Peter was going to betray him. The vibe in the room was incredibly heavy.

Jesus looked at his squad and comforted them: "Don't let your hearts be totally stressed out and troubled. You trust God, right? Trust me too. My Father's house has massive amounts of room. If that wasn't true, I would have told you. I am going there right now to prep a place specifically for you. And if I go prep a place for you, I will absolutely come back and take you to be with me, so that you can be exactly where I am. You guys know the way to the place where I am going."

Thomas (who always needed hard proof) spoke up: "Lord, we have no idea where you are going, so how can we possibly know the way?" Jesus looked at him and dropped one of the most famous, exclusive claims in all of history:

"I am the way, and the truth, and the life. Absolutely no one gets to the Father except through me. If you really know me, you will know my Father as well. From right now on, you do know him and have seen him."

Philip still didn't quite get it. "Lord, just show us the Father, and that will be enough for us." Jesus replied, "Philip, I've been with you guys for this long, and you still don't know who I am? Anyone who has seen me has seen the Father! How can you say, 'Show us the Father'? Don't you believe that I am in the Father and that the Father is in me? The words I say to you aren't just my own ideas. It is the Father, living inside of me, doing his work. Believe me when I say this. Or at the very least, believe it because of the massive miracles you've seen me do."

Jesus then promised them ridiculous power: "I'm telling you the absolute truth, whoever believes in me will do the exact same works I have been doing. In fact, they will do even greater things than these, because I am going to the Father. And I will do whatever you ask in my name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son."

The Ultimate Backup (The Holy Spirit) "If you love me, keep my commands. And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate to help you and be with you forever—the Spirit of truth. The world can't accept him because it doesn't see him or know him. But you know him, because he lives with you and will actually be inside you.

I will not leave you guys abandoned like orphans; I will come to you. Before long, the world won't see me anymore, but you will see me. Because I live, you also will live. On that day, you will finally realize that I am in my Father, and you are in me, and I am in you."

Judas (not Iscariot, a different Judas) asked, "Lord, why are you only going to show yourself to us and not to the rest of the world?" Jesus answered, "Anyone who loves me will obey my teaching. My Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them. I have told you all this while I'm still here. But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things and will remind you of absolutely everything I have said to you.

Peace I leave with you; my own peace I give you. I do not give to you the way the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not be terrified. I have told you this now, before it happens, so that when it does happen, you will believe. I don't have much more time to talk with you. The prince of this world (Satan) is coming. He has no hold over me, but he comes so that the world may learn that I love the Father and do exactly what my Father has commanded me. Come on, let's leave this place."

John.title: The Vine, The Branches, and the Haters
paragraphs: As they walked through the dark, Jesus gave them a powerful visual metaphor about how to survive spiritually.

"I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener. He cuts off every single branch in me that bears no fruit. And every branch that does bear fruit, he prunes it (cuts it back) so that it will be even more massively fruitful. You guys are already clean because of the word I've spoken to you.

Here is the key: Remain in me, as I also remain in you. No branch can bear fruit by itself; it has to stay physically connected to the vine. Neither can you bear fruit unless you remain completely connected to me. I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear a massive harvest. But cut off from me, you can do absolutely nothing. If you don't remain in me, you are like a dead branch that is thrown away, tossed into the fire, and burned.

As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you. Now remain in my love. I have told you this so that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be absolutely complete. My command is this: Love each other exactly how I have loved you. Greater love has no one than this: to lay down one's life for one's friends. And you are my friends if you do what I command. I don't call you servants anymore, because a servant doesn't know his master's business. I call you friends, because everything I learned from my Father I have shared with you. You didn't choose me; I chose you and appointed you so that you might go and bear fruit that will actually last."

The World Is Going to Hate You Jesus then gave them a harsh reality check about how the world was going to treat them. "If the world hates you, keep in mind that it hated me first. If you belonged to the world, the world would love you as its own. But you don't belong to the world anymore. I have chosen you out of the world. That is exactly why the world hates you.

Remember what I told you: 'A servant is not greater than his master.' If they persecuted me, they will persecute you too. They will treat you like dirt because of my name, for they do not know the one who sent me. If I hadn't come and spoken to them, they wouldn't be guilty of sin, but now they have no excuse. Whoever hates me hates my Father as well. But this is all happening to fulfill what is written in their Law: 'They hated me without reason.'
When the Advocate comes, the Spirit of truth who goes out from the Father, he will testify about me. And you also must testify, because you have been with me from the very beginning."

John.title: Grief Turns to Explosive Joy
paragraphs: "I have told you all this so that you won't stumble or quit when things get insane. They are going to kick you out of the synagogues. In fact, a time is coming when anyone who murders you will actually think they are offering a holy service to God! They will do these things because they have never known the Father or me. I'm warning you now so that when the time hits, you will remember I warned you.

Right now, none of you are asking me, 'Where are you going?' because you are completely paralyzed by grief. But I'm telling you the truth: It is actually better for you that I leave. If I don't go away, the Advocate won't come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you. When he comes, he will prove the world is completely wrong about sin, righteousness, and judgment.

I have so much more to say to you, more than you can handle right now. But when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all the truth. He will not speak on his own; he will speak only what he hears, and he will tell you what is yet to come. He will glorify me."

Weeping Now, Rejoicing Later Jesus said, "In a little while, you won't see me anymore. And then after a little while, you will see me." The disciples started whispering to each other, "What does he mean by 'a little while'? We don't understand what he's saying."

Jesus saw they wanted to ask him, so he explained: "Are you asking yourselves what I meant? Very truly I tell you, you will weep and mourn while the world completely parties and rejoices. You will grieve, but your grief will suddenly turn to joy.

Think about a woman giving birth to a baby. She is in intense pain because her time has come. But the second the baby is born, she completely forgets the absolute agony because of the massive joy that a child has been brought into the world. It's the same with you. Right now is your time of intense grief, but I will see you again. And then your hearts will be filled with unstoppable joy, and no one will ever be able to take that joy away from you.
In that day, you will ask the Father directly in my name. Until now you have not asked for anything in my name. Ask and you will receive, and your joy will be complete.

I came from the Father and entered the world; now I am leaving the world and going back to the Father." His disciples finally felt a wave of clarity. "Now you are speaking plainly! Now we can see that you know all things. This makes us believe that you came from God."

Jesus looked at them. "Do you finally believe? Listen to me, a time is coming—in fact, it's already here—when you will be completely scattered, each to your own home. You will run away and leave me all alone. Yet I am not alone, for my Father is with me.
I have told you all these things so that in me you may have peace. In this world you will have trouble, pressure, and pain. But take heart! Stand up straight! I have completely overcome the world."

John.title: The Epic High Priestly Prayer
paragraphs: After saying all this, Jesus physically looked up toward heaven and prayed out loud so his crew could hear exactly what was on his heart before he went to the cross.

"Father, the exact hour has come. Glorify your Son, so that your Son may glorify you. For you granted him absolute authority over all people so that he might give eternal life to all those you have given him. And this is eternal life: that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent. I have brought you glory on earth by completely finishing the work you gave me to do. And now, Father, glorify me in your presence with the glory I had with you before the universe was even created.

Praying for His Squad I have revealed you to those you gave me out of the world. They were yours; you gave them to me, and they have obeyed your word. For I gave them the words you gave me, and they accepted them. They knew with absolute certainty that I came from you, and they believed that you sent me.

I pray for them. I am not praying for the world right now, but for those you have given me, because they are yours. I will remain in the world no longer, but they are still in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, protect them by the power of your name, so that they may be completely unified as one, exactly as we are one. While I was with them, I protected them and kept them safe. None has been lost except the one doomed to destruction (Judas), so that Scripture would be fulfilled.

I am coming to you now, but I say these things while I am still in the world, so that they may have the full measure of my joy within them. I have given them your word, and the world hates them because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world. My prayer is not that you take them out of the world, but that you protect them from the evil one. Sanctify them by the truth; your word is truth. As you sent me into the world, I have sent them into the world.

Praying for Us (All Future Believers) My prayer is not for them alone. I pray also for those who will believe in me through their message. I pray that all of them may be one, Father, just as you are in me and I am in you. May they also be in us so that the world may absolutely believe that you have sent me. I have given them the glory that you gave me, that they may be one as we are one—I in them and you in me—so that they may be brought to complete unity. Then the world will know that you sent me and have loved them exactly as you have loved me.

Father, I want those you have given me to be with me where I am, and to see my glory, the glory you have given me because you loved me before the creation of the world. Righteous Father, though the world does not know you, I know you, and these guys know that you have sent me.
