They gathered it every morning, each person according to their need. Then when the sun got hot, it melted. On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much bread, about four quarts per person.
Then the leaders of the community came to Moses and reported it.

Moses said, “This is what God was talking about: Tomorrow is a day of rest, a holy Sabbath to God. Whatever you plan to bake, bake today; and whatever you plan to boil, boil today. Then set aside the leftovers until morning.” They set aside what was left until morning, as Moses had commanded. It didn’t smell bad and there were no worms in it.
Moses said, “Now eat it; today is a Sabbath for God. You won’t find any of it on the ground today. Gather it for six days, but the seventh day is the Sabbath; there won’t be any of it on the ground.”
On the seventh day, some of the people went out to gather anyway, but they didn’t find anything.

God said to Moses, “How long are you all going to disobey my commands and not follow my instructions? Don’t you see that God has given you the Sabbath? That’s why on the sixth day he gives you bread for two days. So, each of you, stay home. Don’t leave your home on the seventh day.”
So the people rested on the seventh day.
The Israelites named it manna (What is it?). It looked like coriander seed, whitish. And it tasted like a cracker with honey.
Moses said, “This is God’s command: ‘Keep a two-quart jar of it for future generations so they can see the bread that I fed you in the wilderness after I brought you out of Egypt.’”
Moses told Aaron, “Take a jar and fill it with two quarts of manna. Place it before God, keeping it safe for future generations.”
Aaron did what God commanded Moses. He set it aside before The Testimony to preserve it.
The Israelites ate the manna for forty years, until they arrived at the land where they would settle. They ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.
An omer is about one-tenth of an ephah, according to ancient measurements.

Exodus.title: Moses' Arms Got Tired & They Almost Lost?!
paragraphs: So, God told the whole crew of Israelites to pack up and move out from the Sin Wilderness. They rolled out in stages and eventually set up camp at a place called Rephidim. But plot twist: there was literally no water. Not a single drop. So the people started coming at Moses, like, 'Yo, we need water.' But Moses was like, 'Why are you all up in my face? Are you seriously trying to test God right now?'

But the people were seriously dehydrated. They started complaining to Moses again, 'For real, why did you make us leave Egypt just to bring us out to this wasteland to die of thirst with our kids and all our animals?'
Moses was stressed and prayed to God, 'What am I supposed to do with these people? They're about to cancel me, for real. I think they might actually kill me!'

God hit Moses back, 'Alright, go out in front of everyone, and bring some of the elders with you. And don't forget that staff you used to smack the Nile River. Just go. I'll be waiting for you on the rock at Horeb. I want you to hit that rock, and water will come gushing out for everyone to drink.'

So Moses did exactly what God said, with all the elders watching. He named the place Massah, which means 'Testing-Place,' and Meribah, which means 'Quarreling,' because the Israelites were beefing and testing God, asking, 'Is God even with us or not?'

Then, this dude Amalek and his army showed up and started a fight with Israel at Rephidim. Moses told Joshua, 'Pick some guys and go fight Amalek. Tomorrow, I'll be on top of the hill with God's staff.'

Joshua did what Moses said and went to fight Amalek. Moses, Aaron, and Hur went to the top of the hill. And get this: whenever Moses held his hands up, Israel was winning. But whenever he lowered them, Amalek started winning. It was wild. But Moses' arms got super tired. So they found a rock for him to sit on, and Aaron and Hur held his hands up, one on each side. They kept his hands steady until the sun went down. And Joshua totally wrecked Amalek and his army.
God told Moses, 'Write this down so Joshua never forgets it, because I'm about to completely erase Amalek from history.'
Moses built an altar and called it 'God is My Banner.' He said,
'Salute God's rule! God is at war with Amalek. Always and forever!'

Exodus.title: Moses' Father-in-Law Gives Him the Ultimate Life Hack
paragraphs: So, Moses' father-in-law, Jethro, who was a priest over in Midian, heard all about the wild stuff God had been doing for Moses and his people, Israel. Like, he got the news that God had totally sprung Israel from Egypt. Jethro had been crashing with Zipporah, Moses' wife that he'd sent back home for a bit, and their two sons. The first son was named Gershom, which is like 'foreigner,' 'cause Moses was like, "I'm basically an alien in this country." The other son was named Eliezer, which means 'God's my helper,' because he was like, "My dad's God is my ride-or-die and literally saved me from Pharaoh's death sentence."

Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought Moses his sons and wife out to the desert where he was camped by the mountain of God. He'd sent a heads-up to Moses, like, "Yo, it's your father-in-law. I'm coming to see you, and I'm bringing your wife and two sons with me."

Moses went out to greet his father-in-law, gave him a respectful bow and a kiss. They asked each other how life was treating them, and then they went inside the tent. Moses gave his father-in-law the full rundown of everything God did to Pharaoh and the Egyptians to help Israel out, all the drama they went through on the road, and how God came in clutch and saved them.

Jethro was seriously stoked about all the good things God did for Israel by saving them from the Egyptians who were treating them so badly. Jethro said, "Props to God who saved you from the power of Egypt and Pharaoh, who saved his people from how awful the Egyptians were. Now I know for sure that God is greater than all the other gods, because he did this to all those people who were so arrogant to Israel."
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a big offering and sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and all the elders of Israel came and had a meal with Moses' father-in-law with God there with them.

The next day, Moses set up shop to be the judge for the people. And legit, people were lined up in front of him all day, from morning 'til night. When Moses' father-in-law saw everything he was doing for the people, he was like, "What is even happening right now? Why are you doing all this by yourself, with everyone waiting on you from morning to night?"

Moses told his father-in-law, "Well, the people come to me with their questions about God. When a problem comes up, they come to me. I make the call between two people and teach them God's rules and how to live."

Moses' father-in-law said, "Bro, this is not the way. You're gonna burn out, and you're gonna take all these people down with you. This is way too much for one person—you can't do this alone. Now, listen up. Let me give you some advice so God can be in on this with you. You should still be the guy who represents the people to God, and bring the big issues to him. Your job is to teach them the rules and what to do, show them how to live right. But then, you need to find some solid guys—men who respect God, have integrity, and can't be bribed—and make them leaders over groups of a thousand, a hundred, fifty, and ten. They'll handle the day-to-day judging for the people. They'll bring the super hard cases to you, but they'll judge the normal stuff. They'll share the work with you, and that'll make it way easier on you. If you do it this way, you'll actually have the energy to do whatever God tells you to, and all the people will be able to live their best lives too."

Moses actually listened to his father-in-law's advice and did everything he said. Moses picked out some capable men from all of Israel and made them leaders over the people, who were split into groups of a thousand, a hundred, fifty, and ten. They took over the everyday judging for the people. They brought the tough cases to Moses, but they judged the easy ones themselves. Then Moses said bye to his father-in-law, who went back home to his own country.

Exodus.title: God's Epic Mountain Meetup
paragraphs: So, three months after they bounced from Egypt, the Israelites rolled into the Sinai Wilderness. They took the route from Rephidim, got to the Sinai Wilderness, and set up camp right there in front of the mountain.

As Moses was heading up to meet God, God hollered down to him from the mountain: “Yo, tell the House of Jacob, the People of Israel: ‘You guys saw what I did to the Egyptians, right? How I basically airlifted you out on eagles’ wings and brought you straight to me. So here's the deal: if you actually listen to what I say and keep our agreement, you'll be my special crew out of all the people on earth. The whole world is mine, but you guys are special to me: a whole kingdom of priests, a holy nation.’
“This is what you need to tell the People of Israel.”
Moses went back, got all the elders of Israel together, and laid out everything God had told him.
And everyone was on the same page, like, “Whatever God says, we're in.” So Moses took their answer back to God.

God said to Moses, “Alright, get ready. I’m about to roll up in a thick cloud so the people can hear me talking with you and will totally trust you from now on.” And again, Moses told God what the people said.

God told Moses, “Go to the people. For the next two days, get them prepped to meet the Holy God. Have them wash their clothes so they're fresh for the third day, because on day three, God is coming down on Mount Sinai where everyone can see. Set up a perimeter for the people all around and tell them, ‘Warning! Don’t even think about climbing the mountain or even touching the edge. Anyone who touches the mountain is gonna die, for real. And no one should touch that person; they have to be stoned. Yeah, stoned. Or shot with arrows. Animal or person, doesn't matter—they're dead.’
“When you hear a long blast from the horn, that's the signal that it's safe to come up the mountain.”
So Moses went down the mountain to the people and got them ready for the holy meeting. They all did their laundry. Then he told them, “Be ready in three days. And no funny business with the ladies.”

On the third day, right at sunrise, there was this insane thunderstorm, flashes of lightning, a super thick cloud covering the mountain, and a trumpet blast so loud it was ear-splitting. Everyone in the camp was shaking.
Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God. They all stood at the bottom of the mountain, paying attention.

Mount Sinai was completely covered in smoke because God had descended on it like a fire. The smoke was pouring out like a furnace, and the whole mountain was shaking like crazy. The trumpet blasts just kept getting louder and louder. Moses would speak, and God would answer him with thunder. God came down to the very top of Mount Sinai. God called Moses up to the peak, and Moses climbed up.

God said to Moses, “Go back down. Warn the people not to try and break through the barriers to get a look at God, or a bunch of them will die. The priests too, tell them to get themselves ready for this holy meeting, or I might have to break out against them.”
Moses said to God, “But the people can’t climb Mount Sinai. You already gave us a clear warning: ‘Put a boundary around the mountain. Respect the holy mountain.’”
God told him, “Just go down, and then bring Aaron back up with you. But make sure the priests and the people don’t break through and come up to God, or I might have to break out against them.”
So Moses went down to the people and told them what was up.

Exodus.title: God Drops the Top 10 Rules
paragraphs: God dropped all these rules on them:
Yo, I'm God, your God. The one who got you out of Egypt, where you were living like slaves. So for real, no other gods. Just me.

Don't make any statues or idols of anything—not birds, not animals, not fish, whatever. Don't bow down to them or serve them, because I'm your God, and I'm lowkey a jealous God. I'll hold kids accountable for the sins their parents pass down, even to the third or fourth generation of those who hate me. But for the thousands who love me and keep my commands, I'm loyal forever, no cap.
Don't use my name, the name of God your God, as a curse or in some dumb joke. God's not gonna let it slide if you're disrespectful with his name.

Make sure you keep the Sabbath day holy. You get six days to do all your work. But the seventh day is a Sabbath for me, your God. Nobody does any work—not you, your son, your daughter, your male or female servants, your animals, or even any foreigners staying with you. Because in six days I made the heavens, the earth, the sea, and everything in them, and then I rested on the seventh day. That's why I blessed the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy.
Respect your father and mother so you can live a long time in the land that I, your God, am giving you.
Don't murder.
Don't cheat.
Don't steal.
Don't lie about your neighbor.
Don't be all jealous of your neighbor's house—or their spouse, or their workers, or their animals. Don't get fixated on anything that belongs to your neighbor.

All the people saw the thunder and lightning, heard the trumpet, and saw the mountain smoking. It was wild. They were scared, so they backed up and stood far away. They told Moses, "You talk to us and we'll listen, but don't have God talk to us or we'll literally die."
Moses told the people, "Don't be afraid. God came to test you and make you have a deep respect for him so you won't sin."
The people kept their distance while Moses went up into the thick cloud where God was.

God told Moses, "Give this message to the Israelites: 'You guys saw for yourselves how I talked to you from heaven. So don't make gods of silver and gold and put them next to me. Make me an altar out of dirt. Sacrifice your burnt offerings and peace offerings, your sheep and your cattle on it. Everywhere I make my name known in your worship, I'll show up and bless you. If you use stones to make my altar, don't use cut stones. If you use a tool on the stones, you'll make the altar unholy. And don't use stairs to get to my altar, because that would expose you.'"

Exodus.title: Ancient Rules for Modern Messes
paragraphs: Alright, here are the rules you need to lay down for them:

If you get a Hebrew servant, they're with you for six years. On the seventh year, they get to walk free, no charge. If they came to you single, they leave single. If they were married, their wife leaves with them. But if you, the boss, give them a wife and they have kids, the wife and kids stay with you, and the servant leaves by himself. But what if the servant is like, ‘Yo, I actually love my boss and my family—I don’t want to be free’? Then you gotta take him to a sacred spot, stand him by a door or a doorpost, and pierce his ear with an awl. That’s the sign that he’s your servant for life.

Now, if a guy sells his daughter as a servant, she doesn't get to just leave after six years like the guys do. If her new owner isn't happy with her, her family has to buy her back. The owner can't just sell her off to some random foreigners because he broke his promise to her. If he decides to give her to his son, he has to treat her like his own daughter. If he marries another woman, the servant girl still gets all her rights to food, clothes, and, you know, wifely duties. If he fails to provide any of these three things, she gets to leave, completely free.

If someone straight up hits another person and they die, that's a death sentence. But if it wasn't on purpose—like a total accident, an 'act of God'—I'll set up a safe place where the killer can run for protection. But if it was a planned-out, sneaky murder, you drag that killer away, even from my holy Altar, and they get put to death.
Anyone who hits their own father or mother gets the death penalty.
Kidnapping someone? That's a death sentence, whether you sold them or they're still with you.
Cursing your father or mother? Death penalty.

If two people get into a fight and one whacks the other with a rock or their fist, and the injured person doesn't die but is stuck in bed for a while, and then later they can get around with a crutch, the one who hit them is off the hook. Except, they have to pay for the person's lost time and make sure they're totally healed.

If a slave owner hits their male or female slave with a stick and the slave dies right there, that slave has to be avenged. But if the slave hangs on for a day or two, the owner is in the clear—the slave is their property, after all.

If people are fighting and a pregnant woman gets hit and has a miscarriage but is otherwise okay, the person responsible has to pay whatever her husband demands. But if there's more serious injury, then it's life for a life—eye for an eye, tooth for a tooth, hand for a hand, foot for a foot, burn for a burn, wound for a wound, bruise for a bruise.

If a slave owner hits their slave's eye and messes it up, they have to let the slave go free because of the eye. If the owner knocks out a slave's tooth, the slave gets to go free because of the tooth.

If an ox gores a man or a woman and they die, the ox has to be stoned to death. You can't eat its meat, but the owner is fine. But if the ox was known for goring people and the owner knew it but didn't do anything about it, and then it kills someone, the ox gets stoned and the owner gets the death penalty. However, if they agree on a ransom instead of death, the owner has to pay the full amount to save his life. The same rule applies if the ox gores a son or a daughter. If it gores a slave, thirty silver shekels have to be paid to the owner, and the ox gets stoned.

If someone uncovers a well or digs a pit and just leaves it open, and an ox or a donkey falls in, the owner of the pit has to pay the animal's owner what it was worth, but they get to keep the dead animal.

If someone's ox injures a neighbor's ox and it dies, they have to sell the live ox and split the money. They also have to split the dead animal. But if the ox had a history of being aggressive and the owner knew it and did nothing, the owner has to pay an ox for an ox, but they can keep the dead one.

Exodus.title: Spill the Tea: God's Rules on Stepping Out of Line
paragraphs: Alright, so check it. If you steal someone's cow or sheep and then, like, butcher it or sell it, you're in deep. You gotta pay them back five cows for the one you took, or four sheep for the one you jacked. But if you get caught breaking in at night and someone hits you and you die, no one's in trouble. But if it's daytime, then yeah, someone's gotta pay.

A thief has to pay back everything they stole, for real. If you can't pay, you get sold to pay for your crime. If you're caught with the stolen stuff, and the cow or donkey or sheep is still alive, you gotta pay back double.
If you're letting your animals graze and they wander into someone else's field and start munching, you have to pay them back with the best stuff from your own field or vineyard. No cap.
If a fire you started gets out of control and burns up someone's crops or their whole field, you're paying for all of it. Every last bit.

If you give your neighbor some money or stuff to keep safe and it gets stolen from their house, if they catch the thief, the thief has to pay back double. If they don't find the thief, the owner of the house has to go before God to see if they were the one who actually took the stuff.

Basically, anytime something's stolen—a cow, a donkey, a sheep, clothes, whatever—and someone's like, 'Yo, that's mine,' both people have to go to the judges. Whoever the judges say is guilty has to pay the other person back double.

If you're watching someone's animal—a donkey, a cow, a sheep, whatever—and it dies or gets hurt or just disappears and nobody saw what happened, you have to make a promise to God that you didn't do anything to it. The owner just has to accept that, and you don't have to pay. But if it turns out the animal was stolen, you gotta pay the owner back. If a wild animal killed it, you have to show them the dead animal as proof, and then you don't have to pay.

If you borrow an animal from your neighbor and it gets hurt or dies when the owner isn't around, you have to pay for it. But if the owner was with it, you're good, you don't have to pay. If you rented the animal, the rental fee covers it.
If a guy sleeps with a virgin who isn't engaged, he has to pay the marriage price and marry her. If her dad is totally against it and says no way, the guy still has to pay the money for virgins.
Don't let a sorceress live. Period.
Anyone who has sex with an animal? Death penalty.
Anyone who sacrifices to any god other than the one true God has to be put to death.
Don't be a jerk to strangers or take advantage of them. Remember, you guys were strangers in Egypt once.

Don't mess with widows or orphans. If you do and they cry out to me, you better believe I'm gonna hear them. I'll get super angry and come at you with a sword, and then your wives will be widows and your kids will be orphans.
If you lend money to my people, to anyone who's struggling, don't be a loan shark and charge them a ton of interest.

If you take your neighbor's coat as a deposit, give it back before it gets dark. It might be the only thing they have to keep warm at night. And if I hear them crying out because they're cold, I'll step in—I'm a compassionate God.
Don't curse God, and don't bad-mouth your leaders.
Don't be stingy when you're making wine.
Give me your firstborn sons. Same with your cows and sheep—let them stay with their mom for seven days, then give them to me.
Be holy for me.
Don't eat meat from an animal you find dead in a field; throw it to the dogs.

Exodus.title: God's Top Rules for Living Right
paragraphs: Don't spread fake news or rumors.

Don't team up with bad people and lie for them in court. Don't just follow the crowd when they're doing wrong, and don't change your story just to be popular. Also, don't automatically side with someone just because they're poor.
If you see your enemy's pet wandering around, take it back to them. If you see an animal of someone you don't like struggling, don't just ignore it. Help it out.
When poor people are involved in a legal case, make sure they get treated fairly.
Don't make false accusations. Don't be the reason innocent people get hurt or killed. I make sure the wicked get what's coming to them.
Don't take bribes. It messes with your judgment and makes you say things you don't mean.
Don't take advantage of foreigners. You know what it's like to be the new kid, you were foreigners in Egypt.

For six years, you can farm your land and harvest the crops. But in the seventh year, let the land chill and take a break. Let the poor eat from it, and whatever they leave, the wild animals can have. Do the same with your vineyards and olive groves.
Work for six days, but on the seventh day, you rest. This is so your animals and workers can also get a break and recharge.
Listen up to everything I'm telling you. Don't even think about other gods, don't even say their names.
Three times a year, you're going to have a big festival for me.

Hold the Festival of Unraised Bread in the spring. For seven days, you'll eat bread made without yeast, just like I told you. This is to remember the month you left Egypt. And don't show up to my party empty-handed.
Hold the Festival of Harvest in the summer, when you bring in the first crops from your fields.
Hold the Festival of Ingathering in the fall, at the end of the season, when you've harvested everything for the year.
Three times a year, all the guys need to show up and meet with me, your God.
Don't offer the blood of a sacrifice to me with anything that has yeast in it.
Don't leave the fat from my festival offering out overnight.
Bring the best of your first harvest to my house.
Don't boil a baby goat in its mother's milk. That's just messed up.

Alright, listen up. I'm sending my Angel ahead of you to protect you on your journey and lead you to the place I've prepared. Pay attention to him and do what he says. Don't rebel against him, because he's got my authority. If you listen to him and do everything I say, I'll be against your enemies and fight anyone who fights you. My Angel will lead you to the land of all those other people, and I'll wipe them out. So don't worship their gods or do any of the weird stuff they do. I'm going to completely destroy them and their idols.
You serve me, your God, and I'll bless your food and water. I'll keep you from getting sick, and everyone will have kids if they want them. I'll make sure you live a long, full life.
I'll send my Terror ahead of you and freak out all the people you're about to face. Your enemies will be running away from you.

I'll send Despair ahead of you, and it will push out the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites. But I won't get rid of them all at once, or the land will get overgrown with weeds and wild animals. I'll do it little by little, while you get your farms going and take over the land. I'm giving you all this land, from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean, and from the Wilderness to the Euphrates River. I'm putting everyone in that land under your control, so go and drive them out.
Don't make any deals with them or their gods. They can't live in the same country as you, or they'll make you sin by worshiping their gods. Seriously, that's a huge trap.

Exodus.title: God's Exclusive VIP Party on the Mountain
paragraphs: God told Moses, "Yo, you and Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel's elders need to climb the mountain to meet with me. They gotta worship from a distance, though. Only you, Moses, can get close to God. The rest of them can't come near, and the people can't even set foot on the mountain."
So Moses went and told the people everything God had laid out—all the rules and everything. They all answered back together, "Whatever God said, we'll do it."

Then Moses wrote down everything God had said. He got up super early the next morning and built an altar at the bottom of the mountain, using twelve stone pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel. Then he had some young Israelite guys offer up burnt offerings and sacrifice bulls as peace offerings. Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls, and the other half he splashed against the altar.
Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it out loud so all the people could hear. They said, "Everything God said, we'll do. Yeah, we'll obey."
Moses then took the rest of the blood and sprinkled it over the people, saying, "This blood is the seal of the covenant that God has made with you based on all these words I've spoken."

After that, they went up the mountain—Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and the seventy elders of Israel—and they saw the God of Israel. He was standing on something that looked like a pavement made of sapphires, like a perfectly clear blue sky. And he didn't even harm these top leaders of the Israelites. They saw God, and then they ate and drank.

God said to Moses, "Climb up higher on the mountain and wait for me there. I'm gonna give you stone tablets with the teachings and commandments I've written to instruct them." So Moses got up with his assistant Joshua, and Moses climbed up the mountain of God.
He told the elders of Israel, "Just wait here for us until we get back. You've got Aaron and Hur with you, so if any problems come up, go to them."

Then Moses climbed the mountain, and a cloud covered it. The Glory of God settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day, God called out to Moses from inside the cloud. To the Israelites watching from below, the Glory of God looked like a crazy, raging fire on top of the mountain.
Moses went right into the middle of the cloud and kept climbing the mountain. He was on the mountain for forty days and forty nights.

Exodus.title: God's Epic DIY Project: Building the Sanctuary
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and was like, 'Yo, tell the Israelites it's time to bring some offerings for me. But only from the people who are actually down to give. Here's the list of stuff I'm looking for: gold, silver, bronze, some cool blue, purple, and red fabrics, nice linen, goat hair, tanned ram skins, dolphin skins, acacia wood, lamp oil, spices for anointing oil and for some sweet-smelling incense, onyx stones, and other gems to put in the Ephod and the Breastpiece. I want them to build a Sanctuary for me, a place where I can come and hang out with them. Make sure you build it exactly like the plans I'm giving you, for the whole setup and all its furniture.'

Alright, first up, have them build a Chest out of acacia wood. It should be 3.75 feet long and 2.25 feet wide and deep. Slap a layer of pure gold on it, inside and out, and add a gold trim all the way around. Make four gold rings and stick them on the four corners, two on each side. Then, make some poles from acacia wood, cover them in gold too, and slide them into the rings on the sides of the Chest so you can carry it. And for real, leave the poles in the rings. Don't take them out.
Put the Testimony I'm about to give you inside that Chest.
Next, make a solid gold lid for the Chest. It's called the Atonement-Cover, and it needs to be 3.75 feet long and 2.25 feet wide.

Then, sculpt two winged angels out of hammered gold for each end of the Atonement-Cover, one on each side. They should be all one piece with the cover. The angels should have their wings spread out, covering the Atonement-Cover, and they should be facing each other but looking down at it. Put this Atonement-Cover on top of the Chest, and inside the Chest, put the Testimony I'm gonna give you. I'll meet you there at specific times and talk to you from above the Atonement-Cover, from between the two angel statues on it. I'll give you all the commands for the Israelites from there.

Next, make a Table out of acacia wood. Make it three feet long, one and a half feet wide, and two and a quarter feet high. Cover it with a layer of pure gold and put a gold trim all around it. Make a border a hand's width wide all around it and a gold rim for the border. Make four gold rings and attach them to the four legs, right under the tabletop. These will hold the poles for carrying the Table. Make the poles out of acacia wood and cover them with gold. You'll use these to carry the Table.
Make some plates, bowls, jars, and jugs for pouring out offerings. Make them all out of pure gold.
And always keep fresh Bread of the Presence on the Table in front of me.

Now, make a Lampstand out of pure hammered gold. The stem, branches, cups, calyxes, and petals should all be one single piece. It needs to have six branches, three on each side. Put three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with a calyx and petals, on one branch, three on the next, and do that for all six branches. On the main stem of the Lampstand, make four cups shaped like almonds, with a calyx and petals, with a calyx coming out from under each pair of the six branches. The whole Lampstand should be made from one piece of hammered pure gold.
Make seven lamps for the Table. Set them up so they light up the area in front of it. The candle snuffers and trays should also be made of pure gold.
You're gonna need a 75-pound brick of pure gold to make the Lampstand and all its accessories. Make sure you study the design I showed you on the mountain and make everything just like that.

Exodus.title: Building God's Epic Tent
paragraphs: Alright, so God was like, "Build me a house, but make it a tent." This wasn't just any tent, though. It was gonna be legit. He said, "Make the main part, The Dwelling, out of ten huge tapestries. Use the best linen, and weave it with blue, purple, and scarlet threads. And get a pro to stitch in some cool angel designs."

Each tapestry had to be massive, like 46 feet long and 6 feet wide. Then, you connect five of them together to make one giant sheet, and do the same with the other five. Along the edges where they'll connect, you put a bunch of blue loops—fifty on each side. Then, you make fifty gold clips to hook the two big sheets together, making The Dwelling one whole epic tent.

Next up, you make another layer of tapestries, this time out of goat hair, to go over The Dwelling like a tent cover. You'll need eleven of these, each one 45 feet long and 6 feet wide. You join five together, and then the other six. The extra one gets folded over at the front of the tent. Then, you put fifty loops on the edges of these big goat-hair sheets and use fifty bronze clips to hook them together. That way, the whole tent cover is one piece.

Any extra tapestry material hangs over the back of The Dwelling. The overlap on the sides, about 18 inches on each, will cover the sides of the main tent. To top it all off, you put a layer of tanned ram skins dyed red, and over that, a final layer of tough dolphin skins. Talk about weatherproof.

Now for the frame. You build it with acacia wood planks. Each plank is 15 feet tall and a little over 2 feet wide, with two pegs at the bottom to lock it in place. All the frames have to be exactly the same. You need twenty frames for the south side, and you'll make forty silver bases for the pegs to fit into—two for each frame. The north side is built the exact same way. For the back of the tent, which faces west, you make six frames, plus two extra for the corners. These corner frames are double-thick from top to bottom and fit into a single ring. So that's eight frames in the back with sixteen silver bases, two for each frame.

To hold it all together, you make crossbars out of acacia wood. Five for the frames on one side, five for the other side, and five for the back. The middle crossbar runs all the way from one end to the other, halfway up the frames. Then, you cover all the frames with a thin layer of gold, make gold rings to hold the crossbars, and cover the crossbars with gold too. Once all the pieces are ready, you put The Dwelling together exactly like God showed you on the mountain.

Then, you make a sick curtain out of blue, purple, and scarlet material with fine linen. A skilled artist has to weave a design of angels into it. You hang this curtain with gold hooks on four acacia wood posts that are also covered in gold and set in four silver bases. After you hang the curtain, you bring the Ark of the Covenant (the Chest of The Testimony) behind it. This curtain separates the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place (the Holy-of-Holies).

Inside the Most Holy Place, you put the special lid, the Atonement-Cover, on top of the Ark. Outside the curtain, in the Holy Place, you put the Table and the Lampstand. The Lampstand goes on the south side, and the Table goes on the north side, opposite it.

Finally, you make a screen for the entrance of the tent. It's woven from blue, purple, and scarlet material and fine linen. You hang it on five acacia wood poles that are covered in gold, using gold hooks. And you make five bronze bases for these poles.

Exodus.title: God's Holy Hangout: Altar & Courtyard DIY
paragraphs: Alright, so first up, you're gonna build an altar out of acacia wood. Make it 7.5 feet square and 4.5 feet high. It needs to have horns at each of the four corners, all one piece with the altar, and then cover the whole thing in bronze. You'll also need some gear: bronze buckets for the ashes, shovels, basins, forks, and fire pans. Make a bronze mesh grate and put bronze rings on the four corners. This grate goes under the altar's ledge, right at the halfway point. You'll also need some acacia wood poles for carrying the altar, and you'll cover those in bronze too. Just slide the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar when you need to move it. And hey, make sure the altar is hollow on the inside, made with boards.

Next, you're gonna make a courtyard for the Dwelling. The south side should be 150 feet long, with hangings made of fine twisted linen. It'll have twenty posts, twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands. The north side is gonna be the exact same.

For the west end of the courtyard, you'll need 75 feet of hangings with ten posts and bases. Across the 75 feet at the front, or east end, you'll need 22.5 feet of hangings, with their three posts and bases on one side and the same for the other side. At the door of the Courtyard make a screen thirty feet long woven from blue, purple, and scarlet stuff, with fine twisted linen, embroidered by a craftsman, and hung on its four posts and bases. All the posts around the Courtyard are to be banded with silver, with hooks of silver and bases of bronze. The Courtyard is to be 150 feet long and seventy-five feet wide. The hangings of fine twisted linen set on their bronze bases are to be seven and a half feet high. All the tools used for setting up The Holy Dwelling, including all the pegs in it and the Courtyard, are to be made of bronze.

Now, order the Israelites to bring you pure, clear olive oil for light so that the lamps can be kept burning. In the Tent of Meeting, the area outside the curtain that veils The Testimony, Aaron and his sons will keep this light burning from evening until morning before God. This is to be a permanent practice down through the generations for Israelites.

Exodus.title: God's Holy Drip: Priest Fit Check
paragraphs: “Yo, from now on, your brother Aaron and his sons are officially my priests. That’s Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. You need to make them some sacred outfits that are all about glory and beauty.

Get the best craftsmen on it, the ones I’ve given mad skills to. Have them make Aaron’s holy gear so he’s set apart to serve me as a priest. Here’s the list of what they need to make: a special breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban, and a sash. This is the holy drip for your brother Aaron and his sons to wear when they’re on duty as my priests. They’ll need gold, plus blue, purple, and scarlet fabric, and some fine linen.

“First up, the Ephod. It needs to be made by a master craftsman using gold, blue, purple, and scarlet material, and fine twisted linen. It should have two shoulder pieces so it can be fastened at the corners. The decorated band on it has to be the same style and all one piece with it, made of the same stuff: gold, blue, purple, and scarlet material, and fine twisted linen. Then, get two onyx stones and carve the names of Israel’s sons on them, in order of their birth—six names on one stone, and the other six on the second stone. An expert jeweler should engrave these names like a seal. Mount the stones in gold settings. Then attach these two stones to the shoulder pieces of the Ephod. They’re like memorial stones for the people of Israel. Aaron will carry their names on his shoulders as a reminder before God. The settings have to be gold filigree. Also, make two chains of pure gold, braided like cords, and attach them to the settings.

“Next, make a Breastpiece of Judgment. This also needs a skilled craftsman, just like the Ephod. Use gold, blue, purple, and scarlet material, and fine twisted linen. It should be nine inches square and folded in half. Mount four rows of precious gemstones on it.
First row: carnelian, topaz, and emerald. Second row: ruby, sapphire, and crystal. Third row: jacinth, agate, and amethyst. Fourth row: beryl, onyx, and jasper.
“Set them in gold filigree. These twelve stones represent the twelve sons of Israel, with each of their names engraved on one stone, like a seal for each of the twelve tribes.

“Then, make braided chains of pure gold for the Breastpiece, like cords. Make two gold rings for the Breastpiece and attach them to the two ends. Fasten the two gold cords to the rings at the ends of the Breastpiece. Then, attach the other ends of the cords to the two filigree settings, connecting them to the front of the Ephod's shoulder pieces. Make two more gold rings and put them on the two ends of the Breastpiece, on the inside edge that faces the Ephod. Then, make two more gold rings and attach them to the front of the Ephod, on the lower part of the shoulder pieces, near the seam above the decorated band. Use a blue cord to tie the Breastpiece's rings to the Ephod's rings so it stays securely on the decorated band and doesn’t get loose.

“So, every time Aaron enters the Holy Place, he’ll be carrying the names of the sons of Israel over his heart on this Breastpiece of Judgment. It’s a constant reminder in God’s presence. Also, put the Urim and Thummim inside the Breastpiece. They’ll be over Aaron’s heart whenever he comes before God. This way, Aaron will always carry the means of judgment for Israel with him in God’s presence.

“The robe for the Ephod should be made completely of blue. It needs an opening for the head in the middle with a reinforced hem so it doesn’t tear. Around the bottom hem, you need to make pomegranates out of blue, purple, and scarlet material, and put gold bells in between them. So it goes gold bell, pomegranate, gold bell, pomegranate, all the way around the hem of the robe. Aaron has to wear this whenever he’s doing his priest duties. The bells will jingle when he enters the Holy Place to come before God, and when he leaves, so that he won’t die. Lowkey a life-saving feature.

“Now, make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it, just like a seal: ‘Holy to God.’ Tie it with a blue cord to the front of the turban. It has to sit right on Aaron’s forehead. He’ll be the one to take on any guilt from the sacred offerings the Israelites bring, no matter what they are. It will always be on his forehead so that their offerings are accepted by God.

“Weave the tunic from fine linen. Make the turban from fine linen. The sash should be embroidered. Also, make tunics, sashes, and hats for Aaron’s sons to show glory and beauty. Put these clothes on your brother Aaron and his sons. Anoint them, ordain them, and set them apart to serve me as priests.

“Finally, make them linen underwear to cover them from their waist to their thighs. Aaron and his sons have to wear them whenever they go into the Tent of Meeting or get close to the Altar to serve in the Holy Place. This is so they don’t mess up and die. This is a permanent rule for Aaron and all his descendants who become priests.”

Exodus.title: The Official Priesting Ceremony: How to Level Up
paragraphs: Alright, here's the game plan for making them official priests. First, you'll need a young bull and two rams, both totally perfect, no defects. Then, grab some fine wheat flour—no yeast!—and make three things: regular bread, cakes mixed with olive oil, and super thin wafers with a bit of oil spread on them. Put all that bread stuff in a basket and bring it over with the bull and the two rams. Then, get Aaron and his sons, bring them to the entrance of the main tent, and have them wash up.

Next, it's time to get them dressed. You'll suit up Aaron in all the official gear: the tunic, the special robe, the ephod, and the chestpiece with all the gems. You'll tie it all together with that fancy embroidered belt. Put the turban on his head and the sacred crown right on top of it. Then, take the special anointing oil, pour it over his head, and boom, he's anointed. After that, bring his sons out, put their tunics on, wrap the sashes around them and Aaron, and pop their hats on. This priest gig is legit, backed by law, and it's a forever thing for their family.

So this is how you officially ordain Aaron and his crew. Bring the bull to the front of the Tent of Meeting, and have Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head. Then, you'll slaughter the bull right there in front of God. Take some of its blood with your finger and wipe it on the horns of the altar, and pour the rest of the blood at the altar's base. Next, take all the fat from inside the bull—the stuff covering its organs, the fat around the liver, and the two kidneys—and burn it all on the altar as an offering. But the rest of the bull—the meat, the hide, even the poop—you've got to burn it completely outside the camp. It's a special kind of offering to make things right, an Absolution-Offering.

Now, grab one of the rams. Have Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head. Slaughter it, take its blood, and splash it against all sides of the altar. Then, cut the ram into pieces, wash its guts and legs, and put all the pieces, including the head, together on the altar and burn the whole thing. This is a Whole-Burnt-Offering to God, and it creates a smell that God finds pleasing—it's a fire offering to God.

Then you take the second ram. Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head. You slaughter it, and take some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear, and on his sons' right earlobes too. Also put it on their right thumbs and their right big toes. You splash the rest of the blood against all sides of the altar. After that, take some of the blood from the altar, mix it with the anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his clothes, and on his sons and their clothes. This makes them and their priestly outfits totally holy.

From that same ram, you're gonna take all the fatty parts: the fat tail, the fat covering the organs, the long part of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh. This is the special ordination ram. On top of that, you'll take one loaf of bread, one cake made with oil, and one wafer from that basket of bread you brought before God.

Put all this stuff into the hands of Aaron and his sons. They're going to hold it up and wave it in front of God as a special Wave-Offering. After they've done that, you take it from their hands and burn it on the altar along with the other burnt offering. It's a smell that pleases God, a gift for God.
Now, from that same ordination ram, you take the breast meat and wave it before God as a Wave-Offering. That part is for you.

So, make sure you set aside the breast from the Wave-Offering and the thigh that was held up. These parts from the ordination ram are specifically for Aaron and his sons. It's a rule that the Israelites have to give this portion from their Peace-Offerings to the priests forever.

Aaron's holy clothes are to be passed down to his kids and grandkids. They'll wear them when they get anointed and ordained, just like he did. The son who takes over as the main priest after him has to wear these clothes for seven days straight when he goes into the Tent of Meeting to do his job in the Holy Place.

Take the rest of the ordination ram and boil the meat in the Holy Place. Aaron and his sons will eat the boiled meat and the bread from the basket right at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. They are the only ones who can eat it because it's part of the ceremony that made them holy and set them apart. No one else is allowed to eat it; it's sacred. If there's any meat or bread left over by the morning, you have to burn it. Don't eat it; it's holy now.

Okay, so you're going to do this whole ordination process for Aaron and his sons for seven days straight, exactly like I've told you. Every day, you'll offer a bull as a special offering for forgiveness. You'll offer it on the altar to make things right, then you'll anoint the altar to make it holy. You'll do this for seven days, and the altar itself will become super holy—so holy that anyone who even touches it will become holy too.

Now, here's what you need to offer on the altar every single day, no exceptions: two one-year-old lambs. One lamb in the morning, and the second one in the evening. With the morning lamb, you'll also offer about two quarts of fine flour mixed with a quart of the best olive oil, plus a quart of wine as a drink offering. You'll do the exact same grain and drink offering with the evening lamb. This creates a pleasing smell, a gift to God.

This Whole-Burnt-Offering has to happen every single day, for all future generations, right at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. That's our meeting spot. That's where I'll talk to you. That's where I'll meet the people of Israel, in the place that is made holy by my own Glory. I will make the Tent of Meeting and the altar holy. I will make Aaron and his sons holy to serve me as priests. I'm going to move in and live with the Israelites. I will be their God. And they will know for sure that I am their God, the one who brought them out of Egypt so I could come and live among them. I am God, your God.

Exodus.title: God's Secret DIY Recipes
paragraphs: “Alright, first up, make an Altar for burning incense. Build it from acacia wood, about one and a half feet square and three feet high, with its horns all one piece with it. Cover the whole thing in a layer of pure gold—its top, sides, and horns—and put a gold molding around it with two gold rings under the molding. Put the rings on opposite sides to hold the poles for carrying it. Make the poles from acacia wood and cover them in gold too.

“Place this Altar right in front of the curtain that hides the Chest of the Testimony, in front of the Atonement-Cover over the Testimony, which is where I'll meet you. Aaron has to burn some good-smelling incense on it every morning when he cleans the lamps, and he has to do it again in the evening when he lights them up. This is so there’s always incense burning before God, for all time. But listen, don’t burn any random, unholy incense on this Altar, and no other kinds of offerings either. And don’t pour any drink offerings on it. Once a year, Aaron needs to purify the Altar's horns using blood from a special offering. He has to do this every single year. This thing is super holy to God.”

God told Moses: “When you do a headcount of the Israelites, everyone counted has to pay a tax to God for their life. It’s like an atonement fee, so nothing bad happens to them for being registered. Everyone who gets counted has to give half a shekel—that’s the standard weight they use in the Sanctuary. It’s a half-shekel offering to God. Everyone twenty years old and up has to give this offering. The rich don’t pay more, and the poor don’t pay less than the half-shekel. This money is the atonement tax for your lives. Take this tax money from the Israelites and use it for the upkeep of the Tent of Meeting. It’ll be a reminder for the Israelites before God, making things right for your lives.”

God told Moses: “Make a bronze Washbasin with a bronze base. Put it between the Tent of Meeting and the Altar, and fill it with water. Aaron and his sons will wash their hands and feet in it. Whenever they go into the Tent of Meeting or get close to the Altar to serve or give offerings to God, they have to wash up so they don’t die. They must wash their hands and feet so they won’t die. This is a forever rule for Aaron and his sons, for all their generations to come.”

God told Moses: “Get the best spices: about twelve and a half pounds of liquid myrrh, half of that (so, six and a quarter pounds) of fragrant cinnamon, six and a quarter pounds of fragrant cane, and twelve and a half pounds of cassia. Use the official Sanctuary weight for all of them. And get a gallon of olive oil. Mix all this into a holy anointing oil, like a professional perfumer would.

“Use this oil to anoint the Tent of Meeting, the Chest of The Testimony, the Table and all its stuff, the Lampstand and its gear, the Altar of Incense, the Altar of Whole-Burnt-Offerings and all its tools, and the Washbasin and its base. Dedicate them so they become soaked in holiness. That way, anyone who even touches them will become holy.

“Then, anoint Aaron and his sons. Set them apart as my priests. Tell the Israelites, ‘This is my holy anointing oil forever.’ Don’t just pour it on any regular person. And don’t try to copy this recipe for yourselves. It’s holy, so treat it as holy. Anyone who mixes up something like it, or puts it on a regular person, will be kicked out of the community.”

God told Moses: “Take some fragrant spices—gum resin, onycha, galbanum—and add pure frankincense. Mix them in equal amounts to make a special incense, like a perfumer would make it, salted and pure—totally holy. Now, crush some of it into a fine powder and put it before The Testimony in the Tent of Meeting where I will meet you. For you, it will be the most holy of holy things. When you make this incense, you can't copy the recipe for your own use. It’s holy to God, so keep it that way. Whoever copies it for their own personal use will be excommunicated.”

Exodus.title: God's Dream Team for the Holy Tent
paragraphs: God told Moses, "Yo, check it out. I’ve handpicked Bezalel, son of Uri, from Judah's tribe. I’ve filled him with the Spirit of God, giving him mad skills, know-how, and expertise in all kinds of crafts. He can come up with sick designs and work with gold, silver, and bronze; he can cut and set gemstones, carve wood—he’s a legit master craftsman.

And that's not all. I’ve also assigned Oholiab, son of Ahisamach from the tribe of Dan, to be his wingman. Plus, to everyone who's already got a talent for crafting, I’ve given them the skills to make all the things I've commanded: the Tent of Meeting, the Ark of the Covenant with its cover, all the gear for the Tent, the table and its stuff, the pure gold lampstand and all its accessories, the Altar of Incense, the main altar for burnt offerings and all its tools, the washbasin and its stand, the official robes for Aaron the priest and his sons, the anointing oil, and the special incense for the Holy Place. They'll make everything exactly how I told you."

Then God said to Moses, "Tell the Israelites, ‘Look, the most important thing is to keep my Sabbaths. It’s a sign between me and you forever, so you always know that I am the God who makes you holy. Keep the Sabbath; it's sacred to you. Anyone who disrespects it will be put to death, no questions asked. Whoever works on that day will be cut off from the community. You have six days for work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of pure rest, holy to God. Anyone who works on the Sabbath will be put to death. The Israelites must keep the Sabbath, observing it for all generations as a permanent promise. It’s a lasting sign between me and the Israelites. Why? Because in six days God made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day, he stopped and took a long, deep breath.’"
When he finished talking with him on Mount Sinai, he gave Moses two stone tablets of the Testimony, written with the very finger of God.

Exodus.title: Moses Is GONE, So We're Making a GOLDEN COW?!
paragraphs: When the people saw that Moses was taking, like, *forever* to come down from the mountain, they all ganged up on Aaron. They were like, "Yo, do something! Make us some gods to lead us. As for this Moses guy, the one who got us out of Egypt—who even knows what happened to him?"

So Aaron told them, "Alright, take off the gold earrings from your wives, sons, and daughters and bring them to me." Everyone did it; they took off their gold earrings and brought them to Aaron. He took the gold from them, melted it down, and shaped it into a calf using a tool.
The people were super hyped and shouted, "These are your gods, Israel, the ones who brought you up from Egypt!"
Aaron saw how things were going and built an altar in front of the calf.
Then Aaron announced, "Tomorrow is a festival for God!"
Early the next morning, they got up and gave burnt offerings and peace offerings. The people sat down to eat and drink, and then they started to party. It got seriously wild.

God told Moses, "Go! Get down there! Your people, the ones you brought out of Egypt, have totally lost it. It took them no time at all to turn away from what I commanded. They made a golden calf and are worshipping it. They've sacrificed to it and said, 'These are the gods, Israel, that brought you out of Egypt!'"

God said to Moses, "I've been watching this people—and wow, they are so stubborn and hard-headed. Just leave me alone for a sec; let my anger flare up and completely destroy them. But I'll make a great nation out of you."

Moses tried to calm God down. He said, "God, why would you get so mad at your own people? You're the one who brought them out of Egypt with such incredible power and strength. Why would you let the Egyptians say, 'He had a grudge against them—he brought them out just to kill them in the mountains and wipe them off the face of the earth.' Chill out. Reconsider bringing this disaster on your people! Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants who you promised, telling them 'I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, and I'll give this land to them as their own forever.'"
And God did reconsider. He decided not to bring the disaster he had threatened on his people.

Moses turned and went down the mountain, carrying the two stone tablets of the Testimony. The tablets were written on both sides, front and back. God himself had made the tablets and engraved the writing on them.
When Joshua heard the noise of the people shouting, he said to Moses, "It sounds like there's a war in the camp!"
But Moses said,
"That's not the sound of people winning, and it's not the sound of people losing. I hear the sound of a party."

And he was right. When Moses got close to the camp and saw the calf and the people dancing, he got furious. He threw the tablets down and smashed them to pieces at the base of the mountain. He took the calf they had made, melted it in the fire, ground it into powder, scattered it on the water, and made the Israelites drink it.
Moses said to Aaron, "What in the world did these people do to you that made you lead them into such a massive sin?"

Aaron replied, "Don't be angry, sir. You know what these people are like and how they're bent on doing wrong. They said to me, 'Make us gods who will lead us. This Moses guy who brought us out of Egypt, we have no idea what happened to him.'
"So I just said, 'Who has gold?' They took off their jewelry and gave it to me. I threw it in the fire, and... this calf came out."

Moses saw that the people were running completely wild—Aaron had let them, and they were making a fool of themselves in front of their enemies. He stood at the entrance to the camp and shouted, "Whoever is on God's side, come to me!" All the Levites joined him.

He then told them, "This is what God, the God of Israel, orders: 'Every man strap on your sword. Go back and forth through the camp from one end to the other. Kill your own brother, friend, and neighbor.'"
The Levites did what Moses ordered. About three thousand people were killed that day.
Then Moses said, "You have been ordained today—and it cost you a lot, even your own sons and brothers. And God has blessed you."
The next day, Moses told the people, "You have committed a huge sin. But I'm going to go up to God; maybe I can get you forgiven."

So Moses went back to God and said, "This is awful. These people have sinned—it's a massive sin. They made gods of gold for themselves. Now, if you would just forgive their sin... But if not, then erase me from the book you have written."

God said to Moses, "I will only erase from my book those who have sinned against me. For now, you go and lead the people to the place I told you. Look, my angel will go ahead of you. But when the day of reckoning comes, I will definitely hold them accountable for their sin."
And God sent a plague on the people because of the calf that they and Aaron had made.

Exodus.title: God's Presence is Everything
paragraphs: God told Moses, "Alright, time to get going. You and the people you brought out of Egypt, head to the land I promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I'm giving it to their descendants, just like I said. I'll send an angel ahead of you to clear out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It's a super lush place, but I'm not going with you personally. You guys are so stubborn, I'd probably lose my temper and wipe you out on the way."
When the people heard this, they were totally bummed out. No one felt like dressing up or putting on their jewelry.

God said to Moses, "Tell the Israelites, 'You're a seriously stubborn bunch. If I were to hang out with you for even a second, I'd probably destroy you. So take off all your fancy jewelry for now while I figure out what to do with you.'" So the Israelites took off all their bling from Mount Horeb onwards.

Moses had this tent he'd set up outside the main camp, a little ways off. He called it the "Tent of Meeting." Anyone who needed to connect with God would go there. Whenever Moses went to the Tent, everyone would stand up at their own tent's entrance and watch him until he went inside. As soon as he entered, a huge pillar of cloud would come down and hang out at the entrance, and God would talk with Moses. When the people saw the cloud, they'd all stand up and bow down in worship, right at their tent doors.
God and Moses would talk face-to-face, like two friends just chatting. When Moses would head back to camp, his young assistant, Joshua, would stay behind and hold down the fort at the Tent.

Moses said to God, "Look, You're telling me to lead these people, but You haven't told me who's going with me. You say You know me and that I'm special to You. Well, if I'm so special, then let me in on Your plans. That way, I'll know we're still good. And don't forget, these are Your people, Your responsibility."
God replied, "My presence will go with you. I'll be with you all the way."

Moses said, "If You're not coming with us, then just cancel the whole trip right now. Seriously. How will anyone know that You're on our side, with me and Your people, if You're not with us? That's what makes us different from everyone else on Earth."
God said to Moses, "Okay, fine. I'll do what you're asking. I know you well, and you're special to me. I know you by name."
Moses then said, "Please, let me see Your glory."

God said, "I'll make all my goodness pass right in front of you, and I'll say my name, 'God,' right before you. I'll be good to whoever I want to be good to, and I'll be kind to whoever I want to be kind to."
God continued, "But you can't see my face. No one can see me and live."

God said, "Look, there's a spot right next to me. Stand on that rock. When my glory passes by, I'll hide you in a crack in the rock and cover you with my hand until I've passed. Then I'll move my hand, and you'll see my back. But you won't see my face."

Exodus.title: The Ten Commandments 2.0 & Moses's Glow-Up
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and was like, "Yo, cut two more stone tablets, just like the first ones, and I'll write the same words on them that were on the ones you smashed. Be ready by morning to climb Mount Sinai and meet me at the top. And listen, nobody else can come with you; the whole mountain has to be empty. No people, and not even any animals—like, no sheep or oxen grazing anywhere near the mountain."

So, Moses cut two stone tablets just like the originals. He got up super early and climbed Mount Sinai like God told him to, carrying the two stone tablets. God came down in a cloud and stood there with him and called out his own name, Yahweh. Then God walked in front of him and called out, "Yahweh, Yahweh! The God of compassion and mercy! I am slow to get angry and filled with unfailing love and faithfulness. I show love to thousands of generations. I forgive all kinds of sin, but I don't just let guilty people go. I make sure to deal with the sins of the fathers, and this affects their children and grandchildren to the third and even fourth generation."

Moses immediately bowed down to the ground and worshiped. He said, "Please, Lord, if you're cool with me, please come with us. I know these people are stubborn, but please forgive our wickedness and our sin. Claim us as your own people."

And God said, "Alright, check it out. I'm making a covenant with you. In front of all your people, I'm going to do miracles that have never been done anywhere on earth or in any nation. All the people you live with will see how awesome my work is, the work I'll do for you. Pay close attention to what I'm commanding you today. I'm about to drive out the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites for you. Be careful not to make any deals with the people who live in the land you're going to, or they'll become a trap for you.

"You have to tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, and chop down their Asherah poles. Don't worship any other god, because I, God—whose name is Jealous—am a jealous God. Be careful not to make a treaty with the people of the land. If you do, when they chase after their gods and sacrifice to them, they'll invite you, and you'll end up eating their sacrifices. And if you let your sons marry their daughters, their daughters will draw your sons into worshiping their gods too.
"Don't make any idols.

"Make sure you celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days, eat bread made without yeast, just as I commanded you. Do this at the set time in the month of Abib, because that's when you came out of Egypt.
"The firstborn of every womb is mine, including all the firstborn males of your livestock, whether from your cattle or your sheep.
"You can buy back a firstborn donkey with a lamb, but if you don't, you have to break its neck.
"You have to buy back all your firstborn sons.
"And nobody should show up to worship me without bringing a gift.
"You have six days to work, but on the seventh day, you have to rest. Even during plowing and harvest season, you have to rest.
"Celebrate the Festival of Weeks with the first of your wheat harvest, and the Festival of Ingathering at the end of the year.

"Three times a year, all your men have to appear before the Lord, the God of Israel. You don't have to worry about your land when you come to appear before your God three times a year. I will drive out the nations before you and expand your territory. Nobody's going to try to steal your land while you're away.
"Don't offer the blood of a sacrifice to me with anything that has yeast in it.
"And don't leave any of the Passover sacrifice until the next morning.
"Bring the best of the first harvest from your soil to the house of your God.
"Don't cook a young goat in its mother's milk."
Then God said to Moses, "Write down these words, because this is the covenant I'm making with you and with Israel."
Moses was there with God for forty days and forty nights. He didn't eat any bread or drink any water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant—the Ten Commandments.

When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the covenant in his hands, he had no idea that his face was glowing because he had been talking with God. When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, his face was radiant, and they were too scared to go near him.

But Moses called out to them. So Aaron and all the leaders of the community came back to him, and he talked with them. After that, all the Israelites came near, and he gave them all the commands that God had given him on Mount Sinai.

When Moses finished talking with them, he put a veil over his face. But whenever he went in to speak with God, he would take the veil off until he came out. Then he would tell the Israelites what he had been commanded. They would see that his face was glowing, so he would put the veil back on his face until he went back in to speak with God.

Exodus.title: Israel's Got Talent: Building God's House
paragraphs: Moses got all the Israelites together and said, 'Alright, listen up, fam. God has a few things He wants you to do. You get six days to do your thing, but the seventh day is a holy day of rest. It's God's chill day, so no work. And I'm dead serious, anyone who works on the Sabbath has to be put to death. Also, no lighting fires in your homes on the Sabbath.'

Then Moses said to all the Israelites, 'Here's what God is asking. He wants you to bring offerings, whatever you feel like giving. We're talking gold, silver, bronze, and some sick fabrics in blue, purple, and scarlet. Also, fine linen, goat hair, tanned ram skins, dolphin skins, and acacia wood. Plus, we need lamp oil, spices for anointing oils and incense, and some onyx and other gems for the Ephod and the Breastpiece. And for all you talented people, it's your time to shine. God wants you to build His Dwelling with its tent and all the parts, the Ark of the Covenant, the fancy table for the holy bread, the lampstand, the altar for incense, the big altar for burnt offerings, the washbasin, and all the curtains and pegs for the courtyard. Oh, and the special outfits for Aaron the priest and his sons.'

So everyone left, and then they came back, all the people who were super pumped and felt led to give. They brought all their stuff for the Tent of Meeting and for worship. Guys and girls, everyone who was feeling generous, brought brooches, earrings, rings, necklaces—all their gold jewelry—and gave it to God. And anyone who had blue, purple, and scarlet fabrics, fine linen, goat hair, tanned leather, or dolphin skins brought them too. If you had silver, bronze, or acacia wood, you brought it. All the women who were good at weaving brought their woven stuff, and the women who were good at spinning spun goat hair.

The leaders brought onyx and other precious stones for the Ephod and the Breastpiece. They also brought spices and olive oil for the lamps, anointing oil, and incense. Every single person in Israel who felt moved to bring something for the work God had commanded through Moses brought it as a free-will offering to God.

Moses told the Israelites, 'Check it out, God has handpicked Bezalel, from the tribe of Judah. He's filled him with the Spirit of God, giving him mad skills, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of crafts. He can design and work with gold, silver, and bronze, carve and set stones, and carve wood. He's a master craftsman. And God also made him a teacher, him and Oholiab, from the tribe of Dan. God has gifted them with the know-how for all sorts of things, from carving and designing to weaving and embroidering. These guys can make and design anything.'

Exodus.title: God's Ultimate Collab Project
paragraphs: “Alright, Bezalel and Oholiab, and everyone else God has gifted with the skills and know-how to build everything for the Sanctuary, just like God commanded—it's time to get to work.”

So Moses called up Bezalel, Oholiab, and all the other super-skilled people God had blessed with talent. These guys were seriously hyped to start building. They collected all the materials the Israelites had brought for the Sanctuary project. And get this—people just kept bringing more free-will offerings, every single morning.

It got to the point where all the artisans working on the Sanctuary had to stop what they were doing, and one by one they went to Moses and were like, “Yo, the people are bringing way more than we need to get this job done that God commanded!”
So Moses had to send out an announcement across the camp: “Okay guys and girls! No more offerings for the Sanctuary build!”
The people were literally told to stop bringing stuff! There was plenty of material for all the work. More than enough, for real.

Then all the skilled builders got to work on The Dwelling. They made ten huge tapestries from fine twisted linen in blue, purple, and scarlet, with a sick design of angel-cherubim woven right in. Each tapestry was 46 feet long and 6 feet wide. They stitched five of them together to make one big piece, and did the same with the other five. They added blue loops along the edge of the first set and the second set. They made fifty loops on each panel, so the loops lined up perfectly. Then they made fifty gold clasps to hook the tapestries together, making The Dwelling one massive, unified structure.

Next up, they made tapestries from woven goat hair to create a tent to go over The Dwelling. They made eleven of these panels. Each one was 45 feet long and 6 feet wide. They joined five panels together, and then the other six. They did this by putting fifty loops on the edge of one panel and fifty on the edge of the other, then used fifty bronze clasps to connect them, bringing the whole tent together. To top it off, they covered the whole thing with a layer of tanned rams' skins dyed red, and then another layer of dolphin skins.

They built the frame for The Dwelling using vertical planks of acacia wood. Each frame section was fifteen feet tall and a little over two feet wide, with two pegs to lock them in place. They made all the frames exactly the same: twenty frames for the south side, with forty silver bases to hold the pegs from each frame. They did the exact same thing for the north side. For the back of The Dwelling, which faced west, they made six frames, plus two extra for the corners. These two corner frames were double-thick from top to bottom and fit into a single ring. That made eight frames in total with sixteen silver bases, two under each frame.

They made crossbars out of acacia wood—five for the frames on one side of The Dwelling, five for the other side, and five for the back side facing west. The middle crossbar ran all the way from one end to the other, halfway up the frames. They covered the frames with a thin layer of gold, made gold rings to hold the crossbars, and then covered the crossbars with gold too.

They made the main curtain out of blue, purple, and scarlet fabric and fine twisted linen, weaving a design of angel-cherubim into it. They made four posts from acacia wood, covered them in gold, and made four silver bases for them to stand on.

Finally, they made a screen for the entrance of the tent, weaving it from blue, purple, and scarlet material and fine twisted linen with detailed embroidery. They framed this screen with five poles of acacia wood covered in gold, made gold hooks to hang it, and created five bronze bases for the poles.

Exodus.title: God's GOATED Gear: The Ultimate Unboxing
paragraphs: So this guy Bezalel built the Ark of the Covenant using acacia wood. It was almost four feet long and a little over two feet wide and deep. He totally decked it out, covering the inside and outside with pure gold and adding a gold trim all around. Then he made four gold rings and attached them to its four feet, two on each side. He also made some poles from acacia wood, covered them in gold too, and slid them into the rings so they could carry the Ark around.
Next up, he made a solid gold lid for the Ark, called the Atonement-Cover. It was the same size as the Ark, almost four feet long and a bit over two feet wide.

Then he sculpted two awesome winged angels, called cherubim, out of hammered gold. He put one at each end of the Atonement-Cover, and they were all one piece with the lid. The angels had their wings spread out like they were about to take off, hovering over the cover. They were facing each other but looking down at the lid, which is pretty cool.

After that, he built the Table, also from acacia wood. It was three feet long, a foot and a half wide, and a little over two feet high. He gave it the gold treatment too, covering it with pure gold and adding a gold trim. He even made a border around it and put a gold rim on that. Then he made four gold rings and attached them to the legs, so they could slide poles through them to carry the Table. And you guessed it, the poles were made of acacia wood and covered in gold.
He didn't stop there. He made all the dishes for the Table out of pure gold – plates, bowls, jars, and jugs for pouring drinks.

Then he made a Lampstand out of pure hammered gold. The whole thing—stem, branches, cups, and all the little details—was made from one single piece. It had six branches, three on each side. Each branch had three cups shaped like almond blossoms with all the fancy details. The main stem had four cups like that. The entire Lampstand was just one solid piece of hammered gold. He also made seven lamps and all the tools for them out of pure gold.
Get this: he used a whole seventy-five-pound brick of pure gold to make the Lampstand and all its accessories. That's some serious bling.

Next, he made an Altar for burning incense from acacia wood. It was a square, a foot and a half on each side, and three feet high. The horns on the corners were part of the altar itself. He covered the whole thing in pure gold—top, sides, and horns—and put a gold molding around it. He added two gold rings on opposite sides to hold the poles for carrying it. And yup, the poles were acacia wood covered in gold.
Finally, like a master perfumer, he mixed up the holy anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense.

Exodus.title: Building God's Epic Hangout Spot
paragraphs: First, he built the Altar for burnt offerings from acacia wood. It was a square, 7.5 feet by 7.5 feet, and 4.5 feet high. It had these horns on each of the four corners, all carved from the same piece as the Altar, and then covered in bronze. He also made all the tools for the Altar out of bronze: the buckets for the ash, shovels, basins, forks, and fire pans. He made a bronze mesh grate that sat under the ledge, halfway up the Altar. Then he cast four rings for the corners of the grate to hold the poles. The poles were made of acacia wood and covered in bronze too. He'd slide the poles through the rings on the sides to carry the Altar. The whole thing was hollow, made of boards.
He made the bronze Washbasin and its stand from the mirrors donated by the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Talk about a glow-up!

Then he set up the Courtyard. The south side had hangings made of fine twisted linen, 150 feet long. They were held up by twenty posts with twenty bronze bases, and had silver hooks and bands. The north side was identical.

The west end of the Courtyard was 75 feet wide with ten posts and bases, and silver hooks and bands. The front, or east end, was also 75 feet across. It had 22.5 feet of hangings with three posts and bases on each side of the entrance. All the hangings around the Courtyard were made of fine twisted linen. The bases for the posts were bronze, but the hooks and bands on them were silver. The tops of the posts were also capped and banded with silver. The screen for the entrance was this amazing embroidery of blue, purple, and scarlet fabric on fine twisted linen. It was 30 feet long and 7.5 feet high, just like the other hangings. It had four posts with bronze bases and silver hooks, and the tops were capped and banded in silver. All the pegs for the Dwelling and the Courtyard were made of bronze.

Here's the final inventory of everything for the Dwelling, which held the Testimony. It was all recorded by the Levites under the direction of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest, just as Moses ordered. Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah, was the master craftsman who made everything God commanded Moses. And his right-hand man was Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan. This guy was a total artist—a designer and embroiderer who worked with blue, purple, and scarlet fabrics and fine linen.
Gold. The total amount of gold used for the Sanctuary, all of it given willingly, was about 1,900 pounds, according to the official Sanctuary weight.

Silver. The silver came from everyone in the community who was counted in the census. It totaled 6,437 pounds. That worked out to a beka, or half a shekel, from every guy twenty years or older who was registered. There were 603,550 of them.
