“If a guy sleeps with another guy like you would with a girl, they’ve both done something super messed up. They have to be put to death, and it’s on them.
“If a guy marries a woman and her mom, that’s just sick. All three of them have to be burned to death to get that evil out of the community.
“If a guy has sex with an animal, he has to be put to death, and you have to kill the animal too.
“If a woman has sex with an animal, you have to kill both the woman and the animal. They have to be put to death, and they’re responsible for their own deaths.

“If a guy marries his sister, from either his dad’s or mom’s side, and they sleep together, that’s a total disgrace. They have to be publicly kicked out of the community. He’s violated his sister and has to face the consequences.
“If a guy sleeps with a woman when she’s on her period, he’s messed with her flow and she’s shared it. Both of them have to be cut off from the community.
“Don’t sleep with your aunt, on either your mom’s or dad’s side. That’s a violation of a close relative. You’ll both be held responsible.
“If a guy sleeps with his aunt, he’s dishonored his uncle. They’ll be held responsible and won’t have kids.
“If a guy marries his brother’s wife, that’s just wrong. He’s shamed his brother. They won’t have kids.

“So do what I tell you, all my rules and laws. Live by them so the land I’m giving you doesn’t get sick of you and throw you up. You absolutely cannot live like the other nations I’m kicking out for you. They did all this stuff, and I hated every second of it.

“But I told you, remember, that you’re gonna get their land. I’m giving it to you, a land that’s awesome, flowing with milk and honey. I’m your God, and I’ve set you apart from all the other nations. So act like it. Know the difference between clean and unclean animals and birds. Don’t make yourselves gross with any animal or bird or bug that I’ve told you is unclean.
“Live holy lives for me, because I, God, am holy. I’ve set you apart from all the other nations to be my special people.
“Any man or woman who is a medium or a sorcerer has to be put to death. You have to stone them. They’re responsible for their own deaths.”

Leviticus.title: The Holiness Code: Rules for God's Crew
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and was like, “Yo, tell the priests, Aaron’s sons, the deal. A priest can’t just make himself spiritually unclean by touching a dead body. The only exceptions are your immediate family: your mom, dad, son, daughter, brother, or a sister who isn’t married and still depends on you. For them, it’s okay to get unclean. But for anyone else, like your in-laws? Nah. That just makes you look bad and desecrates your role.

“Also, priests can’t be shaving their heads in weird ways, trimming their beards, or cutting their bodies. They have to be holy for their God and not drag God's name through the mud. Because their main gig is presenting God's gifts—God's food—they have to be holy.

“Because a priest is set apart for God, he can't marry a woman who's been a prostitute or is divorced. You gotta see him as holy because he serves the food of your God. Treat him as holy because I, God, who make you holy, am holy myself.

“And this is super serious: if a priest’s daughter messes up and gets into prostitution, she’s not just disgracing herself, she’s disgracing her father. She has to be burned at the stake. It's that big of a deal.

“The head priest, the one who got the special oil poured on his head and wears the official gear, has even stricter rules. He can’t let his hair get all messy, and he can’t wear torn clothes. He can't even go into a room with a dead body. He can't make himself unclean, not even for his own mom or dad. He can't just ditch the Sanctuary of his God or treat it like it's nothing, because he's been set apart by the anointing oil. I am God.

“He has to marry a young virgin. Not a widow, not a divorced woman, not a former prostitute. He has to marry a virgin from his own people. He can’t mess up his family line among his people, because I am the God who makes him holy.”

Then God said to Moses, “Tell Aaron this: None of your descendants, for all time, who has any kind of physical defect can offer up the food of his God. That means anyone who’s blind or lame, has a disfigured face or a deformed body part, a crippled foot or hand, is a hunchback or a dwarf, has eye problems, has nasty sores, or has damaged testicles. No descendant of Aaron the priest with a defect can present gifts to God. He has a defect, so he can't offer the food of his God. He can still eat God's food, both the super holy and the regular holy stuff, but because of his defect, he can't go near the special curtain or the Altar. That would desecrate my Sanctuary. I am the God who makes them holy.”
So Moses told all this to Aaron, his sons, and all the people of Israel.

Leviticus.title: God's Rules for Offerings: The Dos and Don'ts
paragraphs: God told Moses, "Yo, tell Aaron and his sons to be super careful with the holy offerings the Israelites give me. They can't be disrespecting my holy name. I'm God, for real."
"Tell them, from now on, if any of their future kids come near the holy offerings while they're 'unclean,' they're basically kicked out of my presence. I'm God, and I'm not playing."

"Every single one of Aaron's descendants who has some nasty skin thing or a discharge can't eat any of the holy offerings until he's clean. Also, if he touches anything defiled by a dead body, or has a wet dream, or touches a creepy crawly, or touches someone who's unclean for whatever reason—if you touch any of that stuff, you're unclean until evening and you can't eat any of the holy offerings unless you wash up real good. After the sun goes down, he's clean and can go ahead and eat the holy offerings; they're his food. But he can't make himself unclean by eating roadkill or something a wild animal got to. I am God."
"The priests have to follow my rules, or they'll be found guilty and die for treating the offerings like they're nothing. I am God, and I'm the one who makes them holy."

"No regular person can eat anything that's set apart as holy. Not even a priest's guest or his hired worker can eat holy stuff. But if a priest buys a slave, that slave can eat it; and the slaves born in his house can eat his food too. If a priest's daughter marries a regular guy, she can't eat from the holy contributions anymore. But if the priest's daughter is widowed or divorced and doesn't have any kids and moves back into her dad's house like before, she can eat her dad's food. But no regular person can eat it."
"If someone accidentally eats a holy offering, he has to give it back to the priest and add twenty percent to it."

"The priests can't be treating the holy offerings from the Israelites like they're nothing, or they'll mess up and make themselves guilty when they eat the holy offerings. I am God, the one who makes them holy."

God told Moses, "Tell Aaron and his sons and all the people of Israel, every single one of you, whether you were born here or you're a foreigner, when you bring a whole-burnt-offering to God to keep a promise or just because you want to, you have to make sure it's a male with no defects from your cattle, sheep, or goats for it to be accepted. Don't even try to slip in some animal that has something wrong with it—it won't be accepted. Whenever anyone brings an offering from cattle or sheep as a peace-offering to God to keep a promise or just because you want to, it has to be perfect, with no defects, to be accepted. Don't try giving God an animal that's blind, crippled, mutilated, or has gross sores, a rash, or mange. Don't put any of those on the altar as a gift to God. You can, however, offer an ox or sheep that's a little deformed or stunted as a freewill-offering, but it's not okay for keeping a promise. And don't offer God an animal with bruised, crushed, torn, or cut-off testicles. Don't do that in your own land, and don't take them from foreigners and offer them as food for your God either. Because of their deformities and defects, they won't be accepted."

God told Moses, "When a calf or lamb or goat is born, it has to stay with its mom for seven days. After the eighth day, it's good to go as an offering, a gift to God. Don't slaughter a cow or ewe and its baby on the same day. When you sacrifice a thanksgiving-offering to God, do it right so it will be accepted. Eat it on the same day; don't leave any leftovers until morning. I am God."
"Do what I say; live by what I say. I am God."
"Don't trash my holy name. I demand to be treated with holy respect among the people of Israel. I am God who makes you holy and brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I am God."

Leviticus.title: God's Official Holiday Schedule
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and said, "Yo, tell the people of Israel, these are my official holidays, the ones you gotta announce as special holy meetups.
Work for six days, but the seventh day is the Sabbath. That means total and complete rest, a holy get-together. Don't do any work. Wherever you're living, it's a Sabbath for God.
So here's the list of God's official holidays, the sacred meetups you need to schedule at the right times:
First up, God's Passover. It starts at sundown on the fourteenth day of the first month.

Then comes God's Feast of Unraised Bread, on the fifteenth day of the same month. For seven days, you're only eating bread made without yeast. The first day is a holy meetup; no regular work. You'll give special fire-gifts to God for seven days. On the seventh day, have another holy meetup and, again, no regular work."

God spoke to Moses again: "Tell the Israelites, when you get to the land I'm giving you and you harvest your crops, bring the priest a bundle of the very first grain you harvest. He'll wave it in front of God so He'll accept it on your behalf. The priest will do this the morning after the Sabbath. On that same day, you'll offer a perfect one-year-old male lamb as a big burnt offering to God. With it, you'll give a grain offering of four quarts of fine flour mixed with oil—a fire-gift for God that smells amazing—and also a drink offering of a quart of wine. Don't eat any bread, or roasted or fresh grain until you've given this offering to your God. This is a rule that lasts forever for all your future generations, no matter where you live.

Next, you're gonna count seven full weeks from the morning after the Sabbath when you brought the grain bundle as a wave offering. That's fifty days until the morning of the seventh Sabbath. Then, you'll present a new grain offering to God. From wherever you live, bring two loaves of bread made from four quarts of fine flour, baked with yeast, as a wave offering of the first ripe grain for God. Along with the bread, offer seven perfect yearling male lambs, one bull, and two rams. They'll be a huge burnt offering to God, along with their grain and drink offerings—fire-gifts that smell awesome to God. Also, offer one male goat to say you're sorry for your sins and two yearling lambs as a peace offering. The priest will wave the two lambs before God as a wave offering, along with the bread from the first ripe grain. They are holy offerings to God that belong to the priest. Announce that day as a holy meetup. No regular work. This is a forever rule wherever you live, for all your generations.
And when you're harvesting your land, don't be greedy and harvest every last bit. Leave the corners of your field and any dropped stalks for the poor and for foreigners. I am God, your God."

God then said to Moses: "Tell the people of Israel, on the first day of the seventh month, you're to have a day of rest, a holy meetup—you'll mark it with loud blasts from a ram's horn. Don't do any regular work. Just offer a fire-gift to God."

God also said to Moses: "The tenth day of the seventh month is the Day of Atonement. You'll have a holy meetup, you'll fast, and you'll offer a fire-gift to God. Don't work at all that day because it's the day when things are made right for you before your God. Anyone who doesn't fast on that day gets cut off from the community. And I'll personally get rid of anyone who works on that day. So, no work. None. This is a forever rule for all your generations, wherever you end up living. It's a Sabbath of complete and total rest, a day of fasting. You'll observe your Sabbath from the evening of the ninth day of the month until the next evening."

God said to Moses: "Tell the Israelites, God's Feast of Booths kicks off on the fifteenth day of the seventh month. It goes for seven days. The first day is a holy meetup; no regular work. You'll offer fire-gifts to God for seven days. On the eighth day, have another holy meetup and offer a gift to God. It's a big, serious gathering. No regular work.

So, these are God's official holidays that you'll announce as holy meetups for giving fire-gifts to God: the big burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices, and drink offerings for each specific day. These are on top of the offerings for God's Sabbaths and any other gifts you've promised or just feel like giving to God.

So, to sum it up: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, after you've gathered all your crops, you'll celebrate the Feast of God for seven days. The first day is a total chill day, and the eighth day is also a total chill day. On the first day, grab the best fruit from the best trees, get some palm fronds, branches from leafy trees, and willows from the creek, and just celebrate with your God for seven days—yep, a full seven-day festival for God. Every year from now on, celebrate it in the seventh month. You'll live in little huts or booths for seven days—every single person in Israel is to move into these booths. This is so your kids and their kids will know that I had the people of Israel live in booths when I brought them out of Egypt. I am God, your God."
And that's the tea. Moses then posted the calendar for all of God's official holidays that Israel was supposed to celebrate.

Leviticus.title: Don't Disrespect The Name
paragraphs: God told Moses, "Tell the Israelites to bring you top-quality olive oil for the light, so the lamps can stay lit all the time. Aaron's job is to keep these lamps burning from evening till morning before God, right in front of the curtain that hides the Ark of the Covenant. This is a rule forever, for all your descendants. Aaron is in charge of keeping the lamps on the pure gold lampstand burning before God, always."

"Then, take fine flour and bake twelve loaves of bread. Arrange them in two rows, six in each, on the pure gold table before God. Put some pure incense along each row to represent the bread as a memorial offering, a gift to God. Every Sabbath day, this bread needs to be set before God regularly. It's a permanent promise from the people of Israel. Afterwards, the bread belongs to Aaron and his sons. They have to eat it in a holy place because it's their super holy share of the gifts given to God. This is a permanent rule."

So, one day, this guy whose mom was an Israelite and whose dad was Egyptian was hanging out with the Israelites, and he got into a fight with an Israelite man in the camp. During the fight, the son of the Israelite woman blasphemed God's name and cursed. They took him to Moses. (His mom's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.) They put him in jail, waiting to find out what God wanted them to do.

Then God spoke to Moses, "Take the guy who blasphemed outside the camp. Have everyone who heard him put their hands on his head, and then the whole community has to stone him to death. And tell the Israelites: Anyone who curses their God will be held responsible. Anyone who blasphemes God's name must be executed. The whole community has to stone them. It doesn't matter if they're a foreigner or a native—if they blaspheme the Name, they die."

"If someone attacks and kills another person, they must be put to death. If someone kills another person's animal, they have to pay it back—a life for a life. If you injure your neighbor, you get the same injury back: a fracture for a fracture, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. Whatever injury they caused, the same will be done to them. So, if you kill an animal, you pay it back, but if you kill a person, you're put to death. There are no double standards; the same rule applies to foreigners and natives alike. I am God, your God."
Moses then told all this to the Israelites. They brought the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him. The people of Israel did exactly what God had commanded Moses.

Leviticus.title: The Ultimate Reset Button: Jubilee Year!
paragraphs: God hit up Moses on Mount Sinai and was like, "Yo, tell the Israelites, when you get to the land I'm giving you, the land itself is gonna get a Sabbath for God. For six years, you can plant your fields, trim your vineyards, and bring in your crops. But that seventh year? The land gets a full-on Sabbath of complete rest, a Sabbath for God. You can't plant your fields or trim your vineyards. Don't even harvest the stuff that grows by itself; don't pick the grapes from your wild vines. The land gets a whole year of total chill. But you can totally eat whatever the land serves up on its own during that Sabbath year—you, your servants, your hired workers, the foreigners living with you, and yeah, even your cattle and the wild animals. Whatever the land gives, you can eat."

"Count off seven of those Sabbath years—so, seven times seven years, which is 49 years. Then, on the tenth day of the seventh month, the Day of Atonement, you gotta blast the ram's horn super loud all over the country. Make the 50th year a holy year. Announce freedom for everyone living in the land—it's a Jubilee for you. Every single person gets to go back to their family's property and link up with their extended family again. The 50th year is your Jubilee year, so no planting, no harvesting the volunteer crops, and no picking from the wild vines because it's the Jubilee and it's a holy year for you. You're allowed to eat whatever grows on its own in the fields."
"In this Jubilee year, everyone goes back home to their family's land."

"If you sell or buy land from one of your own people, don't rip them off. You gotta figure out the price based on how many years it's been since the last Jubilee. And the seller has to set the price based on how many harvests are left until the next Jubilee. The more years left, the higher the price. But the fewer years left, the lower the price. What you're really buying and selling is the number of crops you're gonna get. So don't cheat each other. Fear your God. I am God, your God."

"Stick to my rules and follow my laws, and you'll live securely in the land. The land will produce its fruit, you'll have more than enough to eat, and you'll be safe and sound. And if you're thinking, 'What are we gonna eat in the seventh year if we don't plant or harvest?' I'm telling you, I'll send such a huge blessing in the sixth year that the land will produce enough for three whole years. While you're planting in the eighth year, you'll still be eating the old food and you'll keep eating it until the harvest of the ninth year comes in."
"The land can't be sold forever, because the land is mine and you're just foreigners—you're my tenants. You have to make sure there's a way to buy back any land that you own."

"If one of your relatives becomes poor and has to sell some of their land, their closest family member should come and buy back what they sold. If someone doesn't have anyone to buy it back, but then they get successful and make enough money to buy it back themselves, they need to calculate the value since they sold it and give the rest of the money back to the person they sold it to. Then they can go back to their own land. If they can't get enough money together to pay it back, what they sold stays with the buyer until the Jubilee year. In the Jubilee, it will be returned and they can go back and live on their land."

"If someone sells a house in a walled city, they have the right to buy it back for a whole year after the sale. They can redeem it anytime during that year. But if it's not bought back before the year is over, it becomes the permanent property of the buyer and their family. It doesn't get returned in the Jubilee. However, houses in villages without walls are treated the same as fields. They can be bought back and have to be returned at the Jubilee."

"When it comes to the Levite cities, houses in the cities owned by the Levites can always be bought back. Levite property can always be redeemed if it's sold in a town they own, and it goes back to them in the Jubilee, because the houses in the Levite towns are their property among the Israelites. The pastures that belong to their cities can't be sold; they're their permanent property."

"If one of your relatives becomes poor and can't support themselves, you have to help them out, just like you would a foreigner or a guest, so they can keep living in your community. Don't scam them with high interest rates; out of respect for your God, help your relative keep living with you. Don't take advantage of their bad situation by charging crazy interest on their loans, and don't sell them food to make a profit. I am your God who brought you out of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God."

"If one of your relatives becomes so poor that they have to sell themselves to you, don't treat them like a slave. Treat them like a hired worker or a guest. They'll work for you until the Jubilee, and after that, they and their children are set free to go back to their family and their ancestral land. Because the Israelites are my servants who I brought out of Egypt, they must never be sold as slaves. Don't be a tyrant to them; fear your God."

"Your male and female slaves have to come from the nations around you; you're allowed to buy slaves from them. You can also buy the kids of foreign workers who are living with you temporarily and from their families who are living with you and were born in your land. They become your property. You can pass them down to your children as property and make them slaves for life. But you must not be a tyrant to your fellow Israelites."

"If a foreigner or a temporary resident living with you gets rich and one of your relatives becomes poor and sells themselves to that foreigner or to a member of the foreigner's family, they still have the right to be bought back after they've sold themselves. One of their relatives can buy them back. An uncle or a cousin or any close relative can redeem them. Or, if they get the money together, they can buy themselves back. What happens then is they and their owner figure out the time from the year they sold themselves to the Jubilee year; the buy-back price is based on a hired worker's wages for that many years. If there are a lot of years left before the Jubilee, they have to pay back a bigger part of their purchase price, but if there are only a few years left until the Jubilee, they figure out the price accordingly. They should be treated like someone hired year by year. You have to make sure their owner doesn't treat them like a tyrant."

"If they're not bought back in any of these ways, they go free in the Jubilee year, them and their children, because the Israelites are my servants, my servants whom I brought out of Egypt. I am God, your God."

Leviticus.title: The Ultimate 'Follow the Rules' Challenge
paragraphs: “Alright, listen up. Don’t go making your own little gods, setting up statues or sacred stones to bow down to. I’m your God, and that’s final.
“Make sure you keep my Sabbaths, and show some respect for my Sanctuary. I’m God.

“If you actually live by my rules and follow my commands, I’ll make sure the rain comes when it should, the ground will give you amazing crops, and the trees will be loaded with fruit. You’ll be harvesting grain all the way to grape season, and picking grapes right up until you need to plant again. You’ll have more than enough food and can chill out, safe and sound in your own land.

“I’ll make your country a peaceful place. You’ll be able to sleep without worrying about a thing. I’ll get rid of any dangerous animals and stop any wars from happening. You’ll chase off your enemies and totally own them. Like, five of you will make a hundred of them run, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand. I’ll be looking out for you, making sure you thrive and your population grows, and I’ll keep my promises to you. You’ll have so much food left over from last year that you’ll have to clear it out to make space for the new stuff.

“I’ll come and live in your neighborhood. I won’t ghost you or avoid you. I’ll walk around with you. I’ll be your God, and you’ll be my people. I’m the God who personally rescued you from Egypt so you wouldn’t be slaves anymore. I broke the chains of your slavery so you can walk tall and be free.

“But, if you ignore me and don’t follow my commands, if you hate my rules and disrespect my laws, basically trashing our agreement, then I’m going to have to step in and bring the drama. I’m talking serious sickness, burning fevers, blindness, and your life just draining away. You’ll plant crops, but your enemies will be the ones eating them. I’ll turn my back on you, and you’ll get crushed by your enemies. People who hate you will be in charge. You’ll be running scared even when no one is chasing you.

“And if that doesn’t get your attention, I’ll have to discipline you seven times worse for your sins. I’ll shatter your pride. The sky will be like a metal roof and the ground like hard iron. You’ll work like crazy, but nothing will grow. No crops, no fruit.

“If you still defy me and refuse to listen, your punishment will get seven times worse. I’ll send wild animals to attack you. They’ll snatch your kids, kill your cattle, and your population will drop so much it’ll feel like a ghost town.

“And if even *that* doesn’t work and you keep ignoring my discipline and defying me, then I’ll have to defy you back. I, myself, will punish you seven times over for your sins. I’ll unleash war on you to get back at you for breaking our deal. When you’re all hiding in your cities, I’ll send a plague, and you’ll be totally helpless. When I cut off your food supply, ten women will have to share one oven and hand out bread in tiny rations. You’ll eat, but you’ll still be starving.

“And if—get this—even *that* doesn’t work and you still won’t listen, still defy me, I’ll lose it. In my anger, I’ll defy you, punishing you seven times over. The famine will be so insane that you’ll end up doing the unthinkable—cooking and eating your own sons and daughters. I’ll destroy all your pagan shrines and the junk that goes with them, and I’ll pile your dead bodies on top of your worthless idols. I’ll be disgusted by you. I’ll turn your cities into wastelands and wreck your holy places. I won’t be interested in your sacrifices anymore. I’ll make your land so desolate that even your enemies who take it over will be shocked. I’ll scatter you across the world and hunt you down. Your land will be empty, your cities deserted. With you gone, the land will finally get a break and enjoy its rest years. All the time it’s empty, it will get the rest it never got when you were living there.

“As for the survivors, I’ll make them so paranoid that even the sound of a leaf blowing in the wind will make them freak out. They’ll run for their lives even when no one is chasing them, tripping over each other in chaos. You won’t be able to stand up to your enemies. You’ll die in foreign lands; the land of your enemies will swallow you up. Whoever is left will waste away because of their sins, and the sins of their ancestors.

“But, on the other hand, if they confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors—how they betrayed me and defied me, which made me defy them and send them away; if they finally humble their stubborn hearts and accept the punishment for their sin, then I’ll remember my promise to Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham. And I’ll remember the land.

“The land will be empty, enjoying its rest while they’re gone. They’ll pay for their sins because they rejected my laws and hated my rules. But even then, while they’re in their enemies’ lands, I won’t completely reject or destroy them. I won’t break my promise to them, because I am their God. For their sake, I’ll remember the promise I made to their ancestors, who I brought out of Egypt while all the other nations watched, so that I could be their God. I am God.”
These are the rules, laws, and instructions that God set up between himself and the people of Israel, through Moses at Mount Sinai.

Leviticus.title: The Ultimate Guide to Making Deals with God
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and said, "Alright, tell the Israelites the deal. If someone wants to make a vow to God by dedicating the value of a person, here's the price list. A guy from 20 to 60 is worth 50 silver shekels, and a woman is 30 shekels. If they're between 5 and 20, it's 20 shekels for a guy and 10 for a girl. For the little ones, from one month to five years old, a boy is 5 silver shekels and a girl is 3. If they're over 60, a man is 15 shekels and a woman is 10. But hey, if someone's too broke to pay that, they just show the person to the priest, and the priest will set a fair price based on what the person making the vow can actually afford."

"Now, if you vow an animal that's legit for an offering to God, that animal is God's, period. It becomes sanctuary property. You can't swap it out—no trading a good one for a bad one, or a bad one for a good one. If you try to pull a fast one and substitute it, both the original animal and the substitute become holy property. If you vowed an animal that's not clean, one you can't offer to God, you have to show it to the priest. He'll decide its value, high or low. Whatever the priest says, goes. If the owner has second thoughts and wants to buy it back, they have to add an extra 20% to its value."

"If you dedicate your house to God, making it sanctuary property, the priest checks it out and sets the price, high or low. Whatever value the priest puts on it, that's the final word. If the guy who dedicated it wants to buy it back, he has to pay the price plus an extra 20%, and then it's his again."

"If someone dedicates a piece of their family's land to God, its value is based on how much seed it needs. The rate is 50 silver shekels for every six bushels of barley seed. If he dedicates the field during the Year of Jubilee, that price is locked in. But if it's after the Jubilee, the priest has to calculate the value based on how many years are left until the next Jubilee, and the price goes down. If the person who dedicated it wants to buy it back, they have to add 20% to its value, and it's theirs again. But if they don't buy it back, or if they sell it to someone else, it can never be redeemed. When the field is released in the Jubilee year, it becomes holy to God, like, it's literally God's field and belongs to the priests."

"If a man dedicates a field he bought—one that wasn't originally his family's land—the priest will figure out its value based on the time left until the next Jubilee. The guy has to pay that amount on the spot, and it becomes holy to God. Then, in the Year of Jubilee, the land goes back to the original owner he bought it from. All these valuations are based on the official sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs."

"Also, lowkey, you can't dedicate the firstborn of an animal. The firstborn already belongs to God by default, whether it's a cow or a sheep. It's already His. If it's an unclean animal, the owner can buy it back at its assessed value plus 20%. If he doesn't redeem it, it gets sold at its assessed value."

"But, for real, anything a person *irrevocably* devotes to God—whether it's a person, an animal, or family land—can't be sold or bought back. Ever. Anything devoted like that is super holy; it's God's property, no take-backs."
"Any human who has been devoted to destruction can't be redeemed. They have to be put to death. Wild, I know."

"A tenth of everything the land produces, whether it's grain from the field or fruit from the trees, belongs to God. It's holy to God. If you want to buy back any of that tenth you've given, you have to add 20% to its value. And for your herds and flocks, every tenth animal that passes under the shepherd's staff is holy to God. You're not allowed to cherry-pick the good ones or swap them out. If you try to cheat and make a substitution, both the original and the substitute become holy property and can't be bought back."
These are the commands God gave Moses on Mount Sinai for all the people of Israel.

Numbers.title: God's Army Roll Call Is Wild
paragraphs: God hit up Moses in the Sinai Wilderness. It was at the Tent of Meeting, on the first day of the second month, two years after the Israelites bounced from Egypt. God said, “Yo, I need a headcount of the entire Israelite community. Go clan by clan, family by family, and get the name of every single guy. You and Aaron need to register every dude who is 20 or older and can fight in the army. To make this happen, you'll need some help. Pick one leader from each tribe, the head of his family, to assist you. Here's the squad that will be helping you out:

From Reuben, you've got Elizur son of Shedeur. From Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai. From Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab. From Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar. From Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon. From Joseph's sons—from Ephraim, it's Elishama son of Ammihud, and from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur. From Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni. From Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai. From Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran. From Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel. And from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.”
From Reuben: Elizur son of Shedeur
From Simeon: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai
From Judah: Nahshon son of Amminadab
From Issachar: Nethanel son of Zuar
From Zebulun: Eliab son of Helon
From the sons of Joseph,
From Ephraim: Elishama son of Ammihud
From Manasseh: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur
From Benjamin: Abidan son of Gideoni
From Dan: Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai
From Asher: Pagiel son of Ocran
From Gad: Eliasaph son of Deuel
From Naphtali: Ahira son of Enan.”
These were the guys hand-picked from the community, all leaders of their ancestral tribes and heads of Israel's military units.

So Moses and Aaron got these chosen dudes together and gathered the whole community on the first day of the second month. The people all registered by their tribes and families, listing all the guys who were 20 or older, exactly like God told Moses to do. He counted them all right there in the Sinai Wilderness.
The breakdown for Reuben, Israel's firstborn son: they counted every single guy 20 and up who could go to war, registered by their tribes and families. The tribe of Reuben had 46,500 men.
The count for Simeon's line: every guy 20 and older ready for battle was counted, registered by their clans and families. The tribe of Simeon clocked in at 59,300.
The total for Gad's descendants: they counted every male 20 and up who could fight, registered by clans and families. The tribe of Gad had 45,650 men.
For the tribe of Judah: every guy 20 and older who could fight was counted, registered by clans and families. The tribe of Judah was huge, with 74,600 men.
Next up, Issachar's line: they counted every male 20 and up ready for war, registered by their clans and families. The tribe of Issachar had 54,400.
For Zebulun's tribe: they counted every guy 20 and older who could fight, registered by clans and families. The tribe of Zebulun came in at 57,400.
Now for Joseph's line. From his son Ephraim, they counted every male 20 and up who could fight, registered by clans and families. The tribe of Ephraim had 40,500 men.
And from his other son, Manasseh, they counted every guy 20 and older ready for battle, registered by clans and families. The tribe of Manasseh numbered 32,200.
For the tribe of Benjamin: every guy 20 and older who could fight was counted, registered by clans and families. The tribe of Benjamin had 35,400 men.
Next, Dan's line: they counted every male 20 and up who could go to war, registered by their clans and families. The tribe of Dan was stacked, with 62,700 men.
For Asher's tribe: they counted every guy 20 and older ready for a fight, registered by clans and families. The tribe of Asher had 41,500 men.
And finally, Naphtali's line: they counted every male 20 and up who could fight, registered by their clans and families. The tribe of Naphtali numbered 53,400.

So these are the numbers Moses and Aaron got, with the help of the twelve leaders of Israel, each one representing his family's tribe. The grand total of the Israelite men, 20 years and older, who were able to fight in the army, counted by their ancestral families, was 603,550.

The Levites, though, were a different story. They weren't counted with the others. God had told Moses, “The tribe of Levi is an exception. Don't register them or include them in the main count of the Israelites. Instead, put the Levites in charge of the Dwelling of the Testimony—all its furniture and everything that goes with it. Their job is to carry the Dwelling and all its stuff, take care of it, and camp around it. When it's time to move the Dwelling, the Levites will take it down, and when it's time to set it up, they'll do that too. And no cap, anyone else who even gets near it will be executed.

“The rest of the Israelites will set up their tents by their companies, every man in his own camp with his own flag. But the Levites will camp around the Dwelling of the Testimony to make sure God's anger doesn't come down on the Israelite community. The Levites are basically security for the Dwelling of the Testimony.”
And the People of Israel did everything just as God commanded Moses. They followed every single order.

Numbers.title: Israel's Ultimate Camp Layout
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and Aaron and was like, “Yo, here’s the deal. The Israelites need to set up their camp in a big circle around the Tent of Meeting, and everyone has to face it. Each group camps under their own special tribe flag.”
On the east side, facing the sunrise, that’s where Judah’s crew sets up under their flag. Their leader is Nahshon, son of Amminadab. His squad is massive, like 74,600 troops.
Next to them, the tribe of Issachar camps. They’re led by Nethanel, son of Zuar, and they’ve got 54,400 people.
And then the tribe of Zebulun is right next to them, led by Eliab, son of Helon, with a crew of 57,400.
The total for Judah's whole section, squad by squad, is a wild 186,400. They get to lead the march whenever everyone moves out.
Down on the south side, you’ve got the camp of Reuben under their flag. Their leader is Elizur, son of Shedeur, with 46,500 troops.
Camping next to them is the tribe of Simeon, led by Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai. They’re packing 59,300 people.
And right next to them is the tribe of Gad, led by Eliasaph, son of Deuel, with a squad of 45,650.
The grand total for Reuben’s side, counting all the troops, is 151,450. They’re the second group in the marching line.

Then, smack in the middle of everyone, you have the Tent of Meeting with the Levites' camp. When it's time to move, every tribe marches in the exact same order they camped, each repping their own flag.
Over on the west side are the squads from the camp of Ephraim under their flag, led by Elishama, son of Ammihud. His crew has 40,500 troops.
Next to them, the tribe of Manasseh sets up their camp, led by Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur. They’ve got 32,200 people.
And right beside them is the camp of Benjamin, led by Abidan, son of Gideoni, with a squad of 35,400.
The total number of guys for Ephraim's camp, troop by troop, is 108,100. They’re the third group in the marching order.
Up on the north side are the companies from the camp of Dan under their flag, led by Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai. His crew is 62,700 strong.
The tribe of Asher will camp next to them, led by Pagiel, son of Ocran. They have 41,500 troops.
And next to them is the tribe of Naphtali, led by Ahira, son of Enan, with a squad of 53,400.
The total for Dan's camp is a huge 157,600. They’re the last ones to march out, under their flags.

So yeah, that’s all the People of Israel, counted by their family lines. The grand total in all the camps, troop by troop, was 603,550. But, per God's command to Moses, the Levites weren't counted with the rest of Israel, so they're not in that number.
The Israelites did everything exactly how God told Moses to do it. No cap. They camped under their flags and marched out by tribe with their families.

Numbers.title: God's Special Ops Team: The Levites
paragraphs: So, here's the rundown on Aaron and Moses's family from when God talked to Moses on Mount Sinai.

Aaron’s sons were Nadab (the oldest), Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. They were all set up to be priests, but then Nadab and Abihu messed up big time. They made some kind of rogue offering to God in the Sinai Wilderness and got zapped, dying right there. They didn't have any kids, so only Eleazar and Ithamar were left to serve as priests while their dad, Aaron, was still around.

God hit up Moses and was like, “Yo, bring the tribe of Levi over to Aaron. They’re gonna be his support crew. They’ll work for him and the whole community at the main tent, doing all the hands-on work for The Dwelling. Their whole gig is to manage all the furniture and equipment, basically running the place while the Israelites come to do their thing. Just hand the Levites over to Aaron and his sons; they're the designated full-time crew. Make sure Aaron and his sons are the only ones doing priest stuff. Anyone else who tries to jump in on that action will be taken out. No cap.”

Then God said to Moses, “Listen up. I’ve picked the Levites from all the Israelites to be a stand-in for every firstborn son. So, the Levites? They're mine. All the firstborn are mine. Remember when I took out all the firstborn in Egypt? I set aside every firstborn in Israel for myself, both people and animals. They belong to me. I’m God.”

God spoke to Moses again in the Sinai Wilderness: “I need you to count the Levites. Go through their families and clans and count every guy who is a month old or older.” So Moses did exactly what God told him to do.
These are the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
And here are the clans from Gershon: Libni and Shimei.
Kohath’s clans were from his sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Merari’s clans were from his sons: Mahli and Mushi.
So yeah, those are the clans of Levi, family by family.

Gershon was the ancestor of the Libnite and Shimeite clans. All the guys a month or older added up to 7,500. The Gershonite clans camped on the west side, right behind The Dwelling. Their leader was Eliasaph, son of Lael. At the main tent, the Gershonites were in charge of The Dwelling itself, its tent, the covers, the curtain at the entrance, the courtyard hangings, the courtyard entrance screen, and all the ropes—basically, everything connected to that stuff.

Kohath was the ancestor of the Amramite, Izharite, Hebronite, and Uzzielite clans. All the guys a month or older in these Kohathite clans numbered 8,600. They were in charge of the Sanctuary. The Kohathite clans camped on the south side of The Dwelling, and their leader was Elizaphan, son of Uzziel. They were responsible for the Ark, the Table, the Lampstand, the Altars, all the holy items used in worship, and the screen—everything to do with that.

Merari was the ancestor of the Mahlite and Mushite clans. The guys a month or older in these Merarite clans numbered 6,200. Their leader was Zuriel, son of Abihail, and they camped on the north side of The Dwelling. The Merarites were in charge of the frames of The Dwelling, its crossbars, posts, bases, and all its equipment—you know, all that structural stuff. Plus the posts for the courtyard, their bases, pegs, and ropes.

Moses, Aaron, and his sons camped on the east side of The Dwelling, facing the sunrise, right in front of the main tent. They were in charge of the Sanctuary for the Israelites and all the worship rituals. And the rule was, anyone else who tried to do their job would be put to death. Seriously.
The grand total of Levites that Moses and Aaron counted, just like God said, clan by clan, all the guys one month and older, was 22,000.

Then God told Moses, “Okay, now count all the firstborn sons of the Israelites who are a month or older. Get a list of their names. Then you’re going to set apart the Levites for me—remember, I’m God—and they’ll take the place of all the firstborn Israelites. And their livestock will take the place of the Israelites' livestock. I am God.”
So Moses did what God said and counted all the firstborn of the Israelites. The total number of firstborn guys a month or older, all listed by name, was 22,273.

God spoke to Moses one more time. He said, “Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of Israel, and the Levites' livestock in place of their livestock. The Levites are mine. I am God. Now, to buy back the 273 extra firstborn Israelites who outnumber the Levites, you need to collect five shekels for each of them. Use the official Sanctuary shekel. Give that money to Aaron and his sons to redeem those extra Israelites.”

So Moses collected the redemption money from the families of the extra firstborns. From those 273 guys, he collected 1,365 shekels of silver. Then Moses gave the money to Aaron and his sons, exactly as God had commanded him.

Numbers.title: God's Holy Moving Crew
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and Aaron and was like, “Yo, count up the Kohathite guys from the Levite crew, but only the dudes between thirty and fifty who are old enough to work in the Tent of Meeting.
“Here’s the job for the Kohathites in the Tent of Meeting: they’re in charge of the most holy things.

“When the camp is about to move, Aaron and his sons need to go in, take down the curtain, and cover the Ark of the Testimony with it. Then they put a dolphin skin cover on it, a solid blue cloth over that, and slide in the poles.

“Next, they’re to throw a blue cloth over the Table of Presence and put all the plates, incense dishes, bowls, and jugs for drink offerings on it. The special bread that’s always there stays on the table. They cover all that with a scarlet cloth, then a dolphin skin cover, and slide in the poles.
“They’re to use a blue cloth to cover the lampstand and all its gear—the lamps, snuffers, trays, and oil jars. Then they wrap it all up in a dolphin skin cover and put it on a carrying frame.
“They’re to spread a blue cloth over the Gold Altar, cover it with dolphin skins, and put it on a carrying frame.
“They’re to take all the stuff used for serving in the Sanctuary, wrap it in a blue cloth, cover it with dolphin skins, and put it on a carrying frame.

“They need to clean the ashes off the Altar and spread a purple cloth over it. Then they put all the altar tools on it—the firepans, forks, shovels, and bowls, everything—cover it with dolphin skins, and slide in the poles.

“After Aaron and his sons have finished covering up all the holy furniture and items, and the camp is ready to go, the Kohathites will come and carry everything. But, and this is a big deal, they must not touch the holy things, or they will die. The Kohathites are the designated movers for everything in the Tent of Meeting.

“Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, is in charge of the lamp oil, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering, and the anointing oil. He’s basically the manager of the whole Dwelling and everything in it, including all the holy furniture and items.”

God told Moses and Aaron, “Don’t let the Kohathite families get wiped out from the Levite tribe. To keep them safe so they live and don’t die when they get near the super holy stuff, Aaron and his sons have to go in before them and assign each guy his specific job and what he has to carry. But the Kohathites themselves can’t even peek at the holy things, not for a second, or they will die.”
God told Moses: “Count the Gershonites by their families and clans. Get all the guys from thirty to fifty years old who are eligible to work in the Tent of Meeting.

“The Gershonites’ job is to carry the heavy stuff: the sanctuary curtains, the Tent of Meeting, its cover, the outer dolphin skin cover, the entrance screens, the ropes, and all the equipment. The Gershonites are responsible for all the work related to these things. All their lifting and moving has to be supervised by Aaron and his sons. You need to tell them exactly what to carry. This is the job of the Gershonite clans at the Tent of Meeting, and Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest, will be their supervisor.
“Now, count the Merarites by their families and clans. Get all the guys from thirty to fifty years old who are eligible to work at the Tent of Meeting.

“This is their specific job at the Tent of Meeting: to carry the frames of the Dwelling, its crossbars, posts, and bases, plus the posts for the surrounding courtyard with their bases, tent pegs, ropes, and all their gear. Assign each man exactly what he is supposed to carry. This is the work of the Merarite clans at the Tent of Meeting, supervised by Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.”

So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the community counted the Kohathites by their clans and families. All the men between thirty and fifty who were eligible to work in the Tent of Meeting, counted by their clans, added up to 2,750. This was the total number of Kohathites who served in the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them just like God told them to through Moses.

The Gershonites were counted by their clans and families. All the men between thirty and fifty who were eligible to work in the Tent of Meeting, counted by their clans and families, came to 2,630. This was the total number of Gershonites who served in the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them just as God commanded.

The Merarites were counted by their clans and families. All the men between thirty and fifty who were eligible to work in the Tent of Meeting, counted by their clans, were 3,200. This was the total from the Merarite clans. Moses and Aaron counted them just as God commanded through Moses.

So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel counted all the Levites by their clans and families. All the men between thirty and fifty who came to do the work of serving and carrying the Tent of Meeting numbered 8,580. Following God’s command through Moses, each man was assigned his work and what to carry.
And that’s the story of how they were all counted, just as God commanded Moses.

Numbers.title: The Craziest Purity Test in History
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and said, “Tell the Israelites to kick anyone out of the camp who has a nasty skin disease, a weird discharge, or has touched a dead body and gotten spiritually grimy. Doesn't matter if they're a guy or a girl, send them out. I'm living in your camp, and I don't want it getting all defiled.”
The Israelites did just that, kicking them out of the camp. They followed God's orders through Moses, no questions asked.

Then God told Moses, “Tell the Israelites, if a man or woman messes up and sins, they've basically broken God's trust. They're guilty. First, they have to own up to their sin. Then, they have to pay back the person they wronged in full, plus an extra 20 percent. If the person they wronged is gone and has no family to receive the payment, then the money goes to God, which means it's given to the priest. They also have to bring a ram to make things right. And from now on, any holy offerings the Israelites bring to a priest, belong to that priest. What's yours is yours, but what you give to the priest is his to keep.”

God then said to Moses, “Okay, tell the Israelites this. Let's say a guy's wife cheats on him, sleeping with another man, but he has no clue. She's defiled herself, but there were no witnesses, she wasn't caught red-handed. But then, the husband starts getting this crazy jealous feeling, and he's lowkey convinced his wife is impure. It doesn't even matter if she's actually innocent and his jealousy is all in his head. Here's what he has to do: he takes his wife to the priest. He also has to bring an offering for her—two quarts of barley flour. No fancy oil or incense on it, because this is a jealousy offering, an offering to bring the truth out into the light.

“The priest will then take her and make her stand before God. He'll grab a clay jar with some holy water and mix in some dust from the floor of the holy tent. After the priest has her stand there in God's presence, he'll un-tie her hair and put the special offering in her hands—the jealousy offering—while he holds the bitter water that brings a curse. Then the priest puts her under oath, saying, ‘If you haven't slept with anyone else, and you haven't cheated and become impure while married to your husband, then this bitter, curse-bringing water won't hurt you. But if you HAVE cheated while married, and you HAVE defiled yourself by sleeping with another man...’—and here the priest lays down the curse—‘then may God make you a curse word among your people. He will make your womb shrivel up and your belly swell. Let this curse-water enter your body, make your belly swell and your womb shrivel.’
“And the woman has to say, ‘Amen. Amen.’

“The priest then writes these curses on a scroll and washes the ink into the bitter water. He then makes the woman drink the bitter water that brings the curse. This water will go inside her and cause some serious pain. The priest will take the jealousy offering from her hands, wave it before God, and bring it to the altar. He'll then take a handful of the offering, as a symbol, and burn it on the altar. After that, he makes her drink the water. If she was unfaithful and defiled herself, when she drinks the curse-water, it will enter her and cause intense pain; her belly will swell up and her womb will shrivel. She'll be a cautionary tale among her people. But if she's innocent and hasn't defiled herself, she'll be cleared and will be able to have kids.

“So that's the law for jealousy. It's for when a wife cheats and defiles herself while married, or when a husband is just consumed by jealousy and suspects his wife. The priest has to make her stand before God and do this whole ritual. The husband will be cleared of any wrongdoing, but the woman will have to pay the price for her sin.”

Numbers.title: The Ultimate God-Mode Vow
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and was like, "Yo, tell the Israelites, if any of you—guy or girl—wants to make a special Nazirite vow, like a full-on commitment to God, here's the deal. You gotta lay off all wine and beer, any kind of alcohol, not even grape juice. For real, you can't even eat grapes or raisins. For the whole time you're consecrated, nothing from a grapevine is allowed—not the seeds, not even the skin.
Also, for the entire time you're doing this, you can't get a haircut. Your long hair is the sign that you're set apart for God.

And another major rule: while you're consecrated to God, you can't go near a dead body. Even if it's your own dad, mom, brother, or sister who passed away, you can't make yourself spiritually unclean, because the sign of your commitment to God is right there on your head.
For the whole time of your vow, you are holy to God.

Now, if someone just drops dead right next to you, and your consecrated hair gets 'defiled,' you have to shave your head on the seventh day, the day you get purified. Then on the eighth day, bring two doves or two pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the main tent. The priest will offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to make you right with God after being near the corpse. You re-dedicate your hair that same day and restart your Nazirite vow by bringing a one-year-old lamb as a special offering. You basically have to start over; the time before doesn't count because your vow got messed up.

Okay, so when your special time of being dedicated to God is over, here are the instructions. First, you go to the entrance of the main tent. Then you give your offerings to God: a healthy one-year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, a healthy one-year-old female lamb for a sin offering, a healthy ram for a peace offering, and a basket of bread made without yeast—loaves made with fine flour mixed with oil, and wafers spread with oil, along with the regular grain and drink offerings. The priest will go to God and offer up your sin offering and burnt offering. He'll sacrifice the ram as a peace offering to God with the basket of bread, and finally, the grain and drink offerings.
At the entrance of the main tent, you'll shave off all that hair you grew out and throw it into the fire that's burning under the peace offering.

After you've shaved, the priest will take a boiled shoulder from the ram, a piece of the bread, and a wafer from the basket and put them in your hands. The priest will then wave them in front of God as a special wave offering. They're holy and belong to the priest, along with the breast and thigh that were also offered.
And now, you're finally free to drink wine again.

So yeah, those are the rules for Nazirites when they bring their offerings to God for their special vow, on top of any other offerings they give. They have to follow through with the vow they made, exactly as these instructions say.
Then God told Moses, "Tell Aaron and his sons, this is how you should bless the people of Israel. Say to them:

May God bless you and keep you safe,
May God's face shine on you and be super gracious to you,
May God look you right in the eye and give you peace.
By doing this, they will put my name on the people of Israel—and I'll make it happen by blessing them."

Numbers.title: The Ultimate 12-Day Unboxing Spree
paragraphs: When Moses was done setting up the holy tent, he blessed it and made it sacred, along with everything in it. He did the same for the altar and all its gear.

The leaders of Israel, the heads of the family tribes who were in charge of the big count, brought their gifts. They came to God with six covered wagons and twelve oxen—a wagon for every two leaders and an ox from each one.
God told Moses, “Take these to use for moving the Tent of Meeting. Give them to the Levites based on what they need for their jobs.”

Moses took the wagons and oxen and handed them over to the Levites. He gave two wagons and four oxen to the Gershonites for their work, and four wagons and eight oxen to the Merarites for theirs. They were all working under Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest. But Moses didn't give any to the Kohathites because their job was to carry the holy items on their own shoulders.

When the altar was blessed, the leaders brought their offerings to dedicate it. They presented them right in front of the altar because God had told Moses, “One leader each day will bring his offering to dedicate the altar.”
On day one, Nahshon son of Amminadab, from the tribe of Judah, brought his gift. His offering was:
a silver plate that weighed over three pounds and a silver bowl that was almost two pounds (using the official Sanctuary weights), both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a Grain-Offering;
a gold dish weighing four ounces, full of incense;
a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old lamb for a Burnt-Offering;
a male goat for a Sin-Offering;
and for a Peace-Offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old lambs.
That was the offering from Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On day two, Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar, brought his gift. His offering was:

The grand total of animals for the Burnt-Offering, plus the Grain-Offering, was:

For the Sin-Offering:

The grand total of animals for the Peace-Offering sacrifice was:
twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, sixty one-year-old lambs.
These were all the offerings for dedicating the altar after it was blessed.

When Moses went into the Tent of Meeting to talk with God, he heard the Voice talking to him from between the two angel-cherubim on top of the Atonement-Cover on the Ark of the Covenant. He spoke with him.

Numbers.title: Level Up: The Levites' Glow Up for God's Service
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and said, “Tell Aaron, ‘Set up the seven lamps so they shine light out in front of the Lampstand.’”

So Aaron did exactly that. He set up the lamps to light up the area in front of the Lampstand, just like God told Moses. The whole Lampstand was made of hammered gold, from the base to the flower designs. It was a perfect copy of the design God had shown Moses.

Then God said to Moses, “Take the Levites out from the rest of the Israelites and get them cleaned up and ready to serve me. Here’s how you’ll do it: Sprinkle them with water that makes them pure, have them shave their whole bodies, and make them wash their clothes. Then they'll be officially clean.

“Get them to bring a young bull with the grain offering that goes with it—that’s fine flour mixed with oil. And you'll need a second young bull for a 'we're-sorry' offering. Bring the Levites to the front of the Tent of Meeting and get the whole community of Israel to gather around. Present the Levites to God, and have the Israelites lay their hands on them. Then Aaron will present the Levites to God as a special offering from the people, so they’re ready to do God’s work.

“Have the Levites put their hands on the bulls' heads. One bull is for the 'we're-sorry' offering, and the other is for the burnt offering to God to make things right for the Levites. Then have the Levites stand in front of Aaron and his sons, and present them as a special offering to God. This is how you officially set the Levites apart from everyone else in Israel; the Levites are 100% mine.

“After you’ve made them pure and presented them as a special offering, they can start their jobs at the Tent of Meeting. The Levites have been hand-picked from the Israelites just for me; they’re taking the place of every firstborn son from an Israelite family. Every firstborn in Israel, whether it's a person or an animal, is mine. When I took out all the firstborns in Egypt, I set them apart for my holy use. But now, I’m swapping in the Levites for every firstborn son in Israel. I’ve picked them out and given them to Aaron and his sons to do all the work at the Tent of Meeting for the rest of the Israelites and to make things right for them, so that nothing bad happens to the people when they get close to the Holy Place.”

Moses, Aaron, and the whole community of Israel did all this with the Levites, exactly as God had commanded Moses. The Levites got themselves clean and washed their clothes. Then Aaron presented them as a special offering to God and made things right for them to make them pure. Only after all that did the Levites start their work at the Tent of Meeting. Aaron and his sons were in charge, telling them what to do based on the instructions God had given.

God then told Moses, “Okay, here are the rules for the Levites: When they turn twenty-five, they start working at the Tent of Meeting. When they hit fifty, they have to retire. They can still help out their buddies with tasks at the Tent, but they can’t do the main work themselves. These are the official rules for the Levites’ jobs.”

Numbers.title: God's GPS: When to Go, When to Stay
paragraphs: So, God hit up Moses in the Sinai Wilderness. It was the first month of the second year after they bounced from Egypt. He was like, 'Tell the Israelites to celebrate Passover on the exact day. No excuses. Do it on the evening of the fourteenth day of this month, and follow all the rules.'
Moses passed the message to the Israelites, and they did it. They celebrated Passover in the Sinai Wilderness on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month, just like God told Moses.

But, plot twist. Some guys couldn't celebrate because they were 'unclean' from touching a dead body. So they went to Moses and Aaron and were like, 'Yo, we're unclean because of a corpse, but why do we have to miss out on giving God our offering with everyone else?'
Moses was like, 'Hold up, let me ask God what to do in your situation.'

Then God told Moses, 'Alright, tell the Israelites this: If you're unclean from a corpse, or you're on a long road trip, you can still celebrate Passover. Just do it on the fourteenth day of the *second* month in the evening. Eat the lamb with flatbread and bitter herbs. Don't save any leftovers for the morning, and don't break any of the lamb's bones. Follow all the rules.'

'But if someone is clean and not on a trip and *still* skips Passover, they're cut off from the community. They didn't bring God's offering at the right time, so they have to face the consequences for their sin.'

'And any foreigner living with you who wants to celebrate Passover can totally do it, but they have to follow all the same rules. The rules are the same for everyone, whether you're a foreigner or born here.'

The day the Tabernacle was set up, a cloud covered it. From sunset to sunrise, the cloud over the Tabernacle looked like fire. It was always like that—a cloud by day and what looked like fire by night.

Whenever the cloud lifted from the Tent, the Israelites would pack up and move. And wherever the cloud settled, they'd set up camp. They moved when God said move, and they stayed when God said stay. As long as the cloud was over the Tabernacle, they stayed put. Even if the cloud stayed for a long time, they respected God's command and didn't move. They stayed in camp, following God's orders, as long as the cloud was there. But the second God gave the signal, they were on the move. If the cloud only stayed from evening to morning and then lifted, they marched. Day or night, it didn't matter—when the cloud lifted, they marched. It didn't matter if the cloud stayed for two days, a month, or a whole year. As long as the cloud was there, they were there. And when the cloud went up, they got up and marched. They camped when God said to, and they marched when God said to. They were living on God's schedule, as told to them by Moses.

Numbers.title: Time to Hit the Road!
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and was like: “Make two trumpets out of hammered silver. Use them to call everyone together and to give the marching orders to the camps. When you blow them both, the whole community will gather at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

“When you blow a single short blast, that’s the signal for the leaders, the heads of the clans, to meet up. When you give a long blast, that’s the signal to march. The first long blast, and the tribes camped on the east side head out. The second long blast, the camps on the south side head out. The long blasts are for marching. The call to get everyone together is a different sound from the marching signal.

“Aaron’s sons, the priests, are the ones who have to blow the trumpets; that’s their job forever. When you go to war against an enemy who’s coming at you, blow a long blast on the trumpet so God will notice you and save you from your enemies. Also, on your celebration days, your appointed feasts, and New Moon festivals, blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and peace offerings. They’ll be a reminder to focus on God. I am God, your God.”

In the second year, on the twentieth day of the second month, the Cloud lifted from over the Dwelling of the Testimony. That was the signal, and the people of Israel started their journey from the Wilderness of Sinai. The Cloud finally stopped and settled in the Wilderness of Paran. They started their march just like God had commanded through Moses.

First up, the flag for the camp of Judah led the way, squad by squad, under the command of Nahshon son of Amminadab. Nethanel son of Zuar was in charge of the tribe of Issachar's forces, and Eliab son of Helon was in charge of the tribe of Zebulun's forces. As soon as the Dwelling was taken down, the Gershonites and Merarites, who carried it, set out.

Next up was the flag for the camp of Reuben, with Elizur son of Shedeur in command. Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was in charge of the tribe of Simeon's forces, and Eliasaph son of Deuel was in charge of the tribe of Gad's forces. Then the Kohathites, who carried the holy items, left. The plan was for the Dwelling to be set up by the time they got to the new spot.

The flag for the tribe of Ephraim moved out next, with Elishama son of Ammihud in command. Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was in charge of the tribe of Manasseh's forces, and Abidan son of Gideoni was in charge of the tribe of Benjamin's forces.

Last of all, under the flag of the tribe of Dan, the rear guard for all the camps marched out, with Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai in command. Pagiel son of Ocran was in charge of the tribe of Asher's forces, and Ahira son of Enan was in charge of the tribe of Naphtali's forces.
These were the marching groups of the people of Israel. They were on their way.

Moses said to his brother-in-law, Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, “Yo, we’re heading to the place God promised, saying, ‘I’ll give it to you.’ You should come with us; we’ll make sure you’re good. God has promised awesome things for Israel.”
But Hobab was like, “Nah, I’m not coming. I’m going back to my own country and my own family.”

Moses shot back, “Please, don’t leave us. You know all the best spots to camp in the wilderness. You’re like our GPS. If you come with us, we’ll make sure you get a piece of all the good stuff God does for us.”

So they finally marched out. They marched for three days from the Mountain of God, with the Chest of the Covenant of God leading the way to find them a place to camp. The Cloud of God was over them during the day as they marched. Whenever the Chest started moving, Moses would say:
“Get up, God! Scatter your enemies! Make the haters run for the hills!”
And when the Chest was set down, he would say:
“Rest with us, God. Stay with the thousands and thousands of Israel.”

Numbers.title: The People vs. Manna & God's Wild Response
paragraphs: The people started complaining big time about their tough life. God heard it, and let's just say He wasn't thrilled. His anger flared up, and a fire literally blazed out and started burning the edges of the camp. The people freaked out and screamed for Moses to help. Moses prayed to God, and the fire died down. They named that place Taberah, which means 'Blaze,' because, well, a fire from God had blazed up against them.

Then, this group of troublemakers who were hanging around got a major craving, and pretty soon they had all the Israelites whining, 'Ugh, can't we get some meat? Remember the fish we used to eat in Egypt—for free! Not to mention the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic. But out here, nothing tastes good. All we ever get is this manna, manna, manna.'

Manna was this seed-like thing that looked kinda shiny, like resin. The people would go around, gather it, and then grind it up or pound it into a powder. They'd boil it and make little cakes out of it. It tasted like a fancy pastry cooked in olive oil. When the dew came down on the camp at night, the manna just showed up with it.
Moses heard all the whining. Every family was just complaining right outside their tents. God's anger was boiling over, and Moses could see things were getting really bad.

So Moses just unloads on God, 'Why are you doing this to me? What did I do to you to get stuck with this? Did I give birth to these people? Am I their mom? So why are you making me responsible for them? Why are you telling me to carry them around like a baby, all the way to the land you promised their ancestors? Where am I supposed to get meat for all these people who are whining at me, ‘Give us meat; we want meat.’ I can't handle this by myself—it's way too much. If this is how you're going to treat me, just do me a favor and kill me now. I'm so done. Just let me out of this.'

God said to Moses, 'Gather seventy men from Israel's leaders, guys you know are respected and responsible. Bring them to the Tent of Meeting, and I'll meet you there. I'll come down and talk with you, and I'll take some of the Spirit that's on you and put it on them. They'll be able to help you carry the burden of these people, so you won't have to do it all alone.'

'And tell the people: Get yourselves ready. Tomorrow, you're gonna eat meat. You've been whining to God, ‘We want meat! Life was better in Egypt!’ Well, God heard you, and he's gonna give you meat. You're gonna eat it. And not just for one day, or two, or five, or ten, or twenty. You're gonna eat meat for a whole month. You'll eat so much meat it'll start coming out of your nose. You'll be so sick of it you'll want to puke just thinking about it. And you know why? Because you've rejected God, who's right here with you, and you've whined to his face, ‘Ugh, why did we ever leave Egypt?’’

Moses was like, 'Dude, I'm standing here with 600,000 guys, and you're saying you'll give them meat every day for a month? Where's that gonna come from? Even if we butchered every single one of our flocks and herds, would that be enough? Even if we caught every fish in the ocean, would that be enough?'
God shot back at Moses, 'So, you think my arm is too short? You're about to see whether what I say happens or not.'

So Moses went out and told the people what God said. He got seventy of the leaders together and had them stand around the Tent. God came down in a cloud, spoke to Moses, and took some of the Spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy leaders. When the Spirit rested on them, they started prophesying. But it was a one-time thing; it didn't happen again.

Meanwhile, two guys named Eldad and Medad had stayed behind in the camp. They were on the list of leaders but didn't go to the Tent. But the Spirit came on them too, and they started prophesying right there in the camp.
A young guy ran and told Moses, 'Hey, Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!'
Joshua, the son of Nun, who had been Moses's top assistant since he was young, was like, 'Moses, my dude, you gotta stop them!'
But Moses said, 'Are you getting jealous for my sake? Man, I wish all of God's people were prophets. I wish God would put his Spirit on all of them.'

Then Moses and the leaders of Israel went back to the camp. A wind sent by God blew in a ton of quail from the sea. They piled up like three feet deep all over the camp, and for a day's walk in every direction. The people were out gathering quail all day, all night, and all the next day—it was a crazy amount. Even the slowest person gathered at least sixty bushels. They spread them all out around the camp to dry. But while the meat was still in their mouths, before they'd even really swallowed, God's anger exploded against them. He hit them with a terrible plague. They ended up naming that place Kibroth Hattaavah, which means 'Graves of the Craving,' because that's where they buried the people who had been craving meat.
From Kibroth Hattaavah, they moved on to Hazeroth and stayed there for a while.

Numbers.title: Miriam Gets CANCELED for Dissing Moses
paragraphs: So, Miriam and Aaron started lowkey talking smack about Moses behind his back because he’d married a Cushite woman.
They were like, “For real? Is Moses the ONLY one God talks through? Doesn’t He talk through us too?”
And yeah, God totally overheard them.
Quick side note: Moses was a super humble guy, probably the most humble person on Earth, no cap.
Then God just suddenly dropped in on Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, saying, “You three, get over to the Tent of Meeting. Now.” So the three of them went.
God came down in a massive pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance to the Tent. He called for Aaron and Miriam. When they stepped up, He said:

“Listen up, I’m being for real. If there’s a prophet of God here, I make myself known to them in visions, I talk to them in dreams. But it’s not like that with my servant Moses. He has the run of my entire house. I talk to him directly, like, face-to-face, in plain English, no riddles. He literally sees the form of God. So why weren’t you scared to talk against my servant, against Moses? That was wild.”
The anger of God just blazed out at them. And then He was gone.
When the cloud lifted from the Tent, oh man… Miriam had turned leprous, her skin as white as snow. Aaron took one look at Miriam and saw she was a leper!

He said to Moses, “Please, my guy, please don’t hold this stupid, thoughtless sin against us. Please don’t let her be like a stillborn baby, coming out of its mother’s womb with half its body rotted away.”
And Moses prayed to God:
“Please, God, heal her. Please, heal her.”
God answered Moses, “If her own father had spit in her face, wouldn’t she be shamed for seven days? So, quarantine her outside the camp for seven days. Then she can come back.”
So Miriam was quarantined outside the camp for seven days. The people didn’t move on until she was brought back in. Only then did the people leave Hazeroth and set up camp in the Wilderness of Paran.

Numbers.title: We Checked Out the New Land... It's Complicated
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and was like, "Yo, send some guys to scout the land of Canaan, which I'm giving to the Israelites. Pick one leader from each of the main family groups, and make sure they're legit."
So, following God's orders, Moses sent them out from the Paran Desert. All of them were the top dogs in Israel, one from each tribe. Here's the squad list:

from Reuben: Shammua son of Zaccur
from Simeon: Shaphat son of Hori
from Judah: Caleb son of Jephunneh
from Issachar: Igal son of Joseph
from Ephraim: Hoshea son of Nun
from Benjamin: Palti son of Raphu
from Zebulun: Gaddiel son of Sodi
from Manasseh (a Joseph tribe): Gaddi son of Susi
from Dan: Ammiel son of Gemalli
from Asher: Sethur son of Michael
from Naphtali: Nahbi son of Vophsi
from Gad: Geuel son of Maki.
from Reuben: Shammua son of Zaccur
from Simeon: Shaphat son of Hori
from Judah: Caleb son of Jephunneh
from Issachar: Igal son of Joseph
from Ephraim: Hoshea son of Nun
from Benjamin: Palti son of Raphu
from Zebulun: Gaddiel son of Sodi
from Manasseh (a Joseph tribe): Gaddi son of Susi
from Dan: Ammiel son of Gemalli
from Asher: Sethur son of Michael
from Naphtali: Nahbi son of Vophsi
from Gad: Geuel son of Maki.
Those are the names of the dudes Moses sent to check out the land. Btw, Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun a new name—Joshua, which is pretty cool.

When Moses sent them to scout Canaan, he gave them the mission briefing: "Head up through the Negev and into the hills. Get the full scoop on the land, see what it's like. Size up the people: are they tough or nah? Is it a huge population or just a few? Check if the land itself is a vibe or if it's trash. Peep their towns: are they just open camps or are they like actual fortresses? And the soil—is it good for farming or is it dead? See if there are any forests. Oh, and try to bring back some of their food so we can see what's up. It's grape season, so grab some if you can."

And just like that, they were off. They explored the whole area from the Zin Desert all the way to Rehob, near Lebo Hamath. Their route took them through the Negev to Hebron, where these giants, the descendants of Anak, were living—Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai. Fun fact: Hebron was built seven years before Zoan in Egypt. When they got to Eshcol Valley, they found a cluster of grapes so massive it took two guys to carry it on a pole. They also grabbed some pomegranates and figs.
