They named the place Eshcol Valley (which basically means Grape-Cluster-Valley) because of that wild bunch of grapes. After 40 days on their recon mission, they headed home.

They showed up in front of Moses, Aaron, and all the Israelites at Kadesh in the Paran Desert. They gave their report to everyone and showed off the fruit they brought back. Then they spilled the tea on their trip:

"We went to the land you sent us to, and whoa, it's seriously flowing with milk and honey! Just look at this fruit! The only problem is, the people there are fierce, and their cities are huge and super fortified. Even worse, we saw the descendants of the giant Anak there. Amalekites are all over the Negev; Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites are in the hills; and the Canaanites have the coast and the area along the Jordan River."
Caleb cut them off, telling everyone to chill and listen to Moses. He said, "Let's go up and take the land—right now. We can totally do it."

But the other guys were like, "No way, we can't attack them; they're way stronger than us." They started spreading scary rumors among the Israelites, saying, "We scouted the whole land, and it's a place that just eats people up. Everyone we saw was massive. Bro, we even saw the Nephilim giants—the Anak giants are part of them. Next to them, we felt like grasshoppers. And that's exactly how they looked at us, like we were nothing."

Numbers.title: Israel's Epic Fail & 40-Year Timeout
paragraphs: The whole community basically had a meltdown, crying and complaining all night. All the Israelites were grumbling about Moses and Aaron. The whole crowd was in on it, saying, “We should’ve just died in Egypt! Or even out here in the wilderness! Why did God bring us to this country just to get us killed? Our wives and kids are gonna be captured. Seriously, why don’t we just go back to Egypt? Like, right now!”
Pretty soon, they were all saying to each other, “Let’s get a new leader and head back to Egypt.”
Moses and Aaron just fell on their faces in front of everyone, who had gathered for this emergency meeting.

Joshua, son of Nun, and Caleb, son of Jephunneh, who were part of the spy team, tore their clothes in frustration. They told the crowd of Israelites, “The land we checked out is seriously amazing—like, no cap. If God is happy with us, He’ll lead us into that land, a place that’s flowing with milk and honey, just like they say. And He’ll give it to us. Just don’t rebel against God! And don’t be scared of those people. Man, we’ll crush them. They have zero protection, and God is on our side. Don’t be afraid of them!”
But now the whole community was furious and started talking about stoning them.

Just then, the super bright Glory of God showed up at the Tent of Meeting. Every single Israelite saw it. God said to Moses, “How long are these people going to disrespect me? How long will they refuse to trust me, even after all the miracles I’ve done for them? I’ve had it—I’m about to send a plague and wipe them out. But I’ll make you into a nation that’s bigger and stronger than they ever were.”

But Moses said to God, “The Egyptians are going to hear about this! You brought these people out of Egypt with a huge display of power, and now this? The Egyptians will tell everyone. They already know you are God, that you’re on this people’s side, that you’re right here with them. They see you with their own eyes in your Cloud that hangs over them, and in the Pillar of Cloud that leads them by day and the Pillar of Fire by night. If you kill all these people at once, all the nations who’ve heard about you will say, ‘God couldn’t bring these people into the land He promised them, so He just killed them in the wilderness.’
“So now, please, let your power be shown, make it huge, just like you said before when you told us,

‘God, you are slow to get angry and full of loyal love, forgiving wickedness, rebellion, and sin. But you never just ignore sin. You let the consequences of parents’ sins affect their children, even to the third and fourth generation.’
“Please forgive the messed-up actions of this people because of your huge, loyal love, just like you’ve been forgiving them this whole time since they left Egypt.”

God said, “I forgive them, because you asked. But as surely as I live and as the Glory of God fills the whole Earth—not a single person who saw my Glory and the miracles I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and who has tested me over and over again, ignoring me every time—not one of them will see the land I solemnly promised their ancestors. No one who has treated me with such constant disrespect will see it.
“But my servant Caleb—he’s a different story. He has a different attitude; he follows me with his whole heart. I’ll bring him into the land he scouted, and his kids will inherit it.
“Since the Amalekites and Canaanites are living in the valleys, for now, you need to turn around and go back into the wilderness, following the path to the Red Sea.”

God spoke to Moses and Aaron: “How much longer do I have to put up with all this complaining from this evil community? I am so done with the complaints from these grumbling Israelites. Tell them, ‘As I live—this is God’s decree—I’m going to do this to you: Your dead bodies are going to be scattered all over this wilderness—every single one of you twenty years or older who was counted, this whole generation of complainers. Not one of you will enter the land and live there, the land I solemnly promised you, except for Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.’

“Your kids, the ones you said would be captured, I’ll bring them in to enjoy the land you rejected. Meanwhile, your bodies will be rotting in this wilderness. Your children will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years, dealing with the consequences of your unfaithfulness, until the last one of your generation is a corpse in the wilderness. You scouted the land for forty days; so your punishment will be a year for each day—a forty-year sentence for your sins. That’ll be a long lesson in what it means to make me unhappy.
“I, God, have spoken. I will definitely do all these things to this entire evil community that has ganged up against me. They will meet their end in this wilderness. They will die here.”

And that’s what happened. The men Moses had sent to scout the land, who came back and spread fake news about it, making the whole community grumble against Moses—all those men died. They died in a plague right in front of God for spreading lies about the land. Only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh survived out of the men who went to scout the land.

When Moses told all this to the Israelites, they were devastated and mourned for a long time. But early the next morning, they started heading for the high hill country, saying, “We’re here, we’re ready! Let’s go up and take the land God promised us. We sinned, but we’re ready now.”

But Moses said, “Why are you disobeying God’s command again? This isn’t going to work. Don’t attack. God isn’t with you on this—you’ll get totally wrecked by your enemies. The Amalekites and Canaanites are waiting for you, and they’ll kill you. Because you stopped following God obediently, God is not going to be with you in this.”

But they went anyway. Super reckless and arrogant, they climbed up to the high hill country. But the Ark of the Covenant and Moses didn’t move from the camp. The Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in the hills came down, attacked them, and beat them badly, chasing them all the way down to a place called Hormah.

Numbers.title: Rules for Worship & What NOT to Do (Warning: Graphic Content)
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and was like, "Speak to the Israelites. Tell them, when you finally roll into the homeland I'm giving you and you make a fire-gift sacrifice to God—a burnt offering or whatever from your herd or flock for a vow or just because—make it a pleasing aroma for God. The one bringing the offering has to present a grain offering of two quarts of fine flour mixed with a quart of oil. With every lamb for the burnt offering or other sacrifice, you gotta prepare a quart of oil and a quart of wine as a drink offering.

For a ram, you gotta bring a grain offering of four quarts of fine flour mixed with one and a quarter quarts of oil and the same amount of wine for a drink offering. Present it as a pleasing aroma to God.

When you prep a young bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice for a special vow or a peace offering to God, bring with the bull a grain offering of six quarts of fine flour and two quarts of oil. Also, bring two quarts of wine as a drink offering. It'll be a fire-gift, a pleasing aroma to God.
Every bull or ram, every lamb or young goat, has to be prepped this way. You gotta do this for each one, no matter how many you're preparing.

Every native-born Israelite has to follow this procedure when he brings a fire-gift as a pleasing aroma to God. And for future generations, when a foreigner or a visitor living with you for a while presents a fire-gift as a pleasing aroma to God, they have to follow the exact same procedures. The community has the same rules for you and the foreigner living among you. This is the standard rule for all time. You and the foreigner are the same before God. The same laws and regulations apply to both you and the foreigner who lives with you.

God spoke to Moses again: "Tell the People of Israel, when you enter the land I'm bringing you to, and you eat the food from that country, set some aside as an offering for God. From the first batch of your bread dough, make a round loaf as an offering—it's an offering from the threshing floor. For all future generations, you have to make this offering to God from the first batch of dough.

But what if you mess up and don't keep all the commands God gave Moses? Any of the things God commanded you through Moses, from the very first command up until now, and if it was a genuine mistake that the whole community wasn't aware of, then the whole congregation has to sacrifice one young bull as a burnt offering. It's a pleasing aroma to God, and it needs its grain and drink offerings like the rules say, plus a male goat as a sin offering. The priest will make things right for the whole community of Israel, and they'll be forgiven. The sin wasn't on purpose, and they brought the fire-gift and sin offering to God for their mistake. The whole community of Israel, including the foreigners living there, will be forgiven, because everyone was involved in the error.

But if it's just one person who sins by mistake, not realizing what they're doing, they have to bring a one-year-old female goat as a sin offering. The priest will then make things right for the person who accidentally sinned, to make atonement before God so it won't be held against them.
The same rule applies to everyone who sins by mistake; native-born Israelites and foreigners follow the same rules.

But the person, whether native or foreigner, who sins defiantly, straight-up blaspheming God, must be cut off from their people. They've despised God's word and violated God's command. That person must be kicked out of the community, totally ostracized, and left alone in their wrongdoing.

One time, during those years in the wilderness, a man was caught gathering wood on the Sabbath. The people who caught him dragged him in front of Moses, Aaron, and the whole community. They put him in custody until it was clear what should be done with him. Then God told Moses: "The man gets the death penalty. For real, kill him. The whole community has to stone him to death outside the camp."
So the whole community took him outside the camp and stoned him. It was an execution commanded by God through Moses.

God spoke to Moses: "Tell the People of Israel that from now on, they have to make tassels on the corners of their clothes and put a blue thread on each corner tassel. When you look at these tassels, you'll remember and keep all of God's commandments, and you won't get distracted by everything you feel or see that tempts you to be unfaithful. The tassels will be a reminder to remember and obey all my commandments, to live a holy life for God. I am your God who rescued you from Egypt to be your personal God. Yes, I am God, your God."

Numbers.title: Korah's Rebellion: You vs. God's Chosen One
paragraphs: So one day, this guy Korah, who was a Levite, got all full of himself and decided to start a rebellion against Moses. He got a few guys from the Reubenite tribe—Dathan, Abiram, and On—to join him. And get this, he also convinced 250 other well-known leaders from the Israelite community to back him up. They all ganged up on Moses and Aaron and said, 'You guys have gone too far! This whole community is holy, and God is with all of us. So why do you act like you're the bosses of everyone?'
When Moses heard this, he just fell flat on his face on the ground.
Then he said to Korah and his crew, 'In the morning, God will show us who really belongs to him and who is holy. God will stand with the person he chooses.'

'Now, Korah, this is what I want you and your whole gang to do: Tomorrow, each of you grab a censer. In front of God, put fire and incense in them. Then we'll see who is truly holy, who God picks. Seriously, you sons of Levi are the ones who have gone too far!'

Moses kept going, talking to Korah, 'Listen up, sons of Levi. Isn't it a big enough deal that the God of Israel chose you out of everyone to be close to him, to work in God's own Dwelling, and to serve the community? He brought you and all your fellow Levites into his inner circle, and now you're trying to grab the priesthood too? You're not just ganging up on us; you're ganging up against God himself. What's your problem with Aaron that makes you trash-talk him?'

Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, but they were like, 'Nah, we're not coming. Isn't it bad enough that you dragged us from a land that was awesome, with plenty of food and water, just to let us die out here in the desert? And now you're still trying to act like our king! Let's be real, you failed. You didn't bring us to some amazing new land, and you didn't give us any fields or vineyards. You'd have to literally blind us to make us not see what's really going on. So forget it, we're not showing up.'
Moses got super angry. He said to God, 'Don't accept their offering. I haven't taken a single thing from them, not even a donkey. I haven't hurt any of them at all.'

Then Moses told Korah, 'You and all your followers need to show up before God tomorrow. You be there, they be there, and Aaron will be there too. Every single man needs to bring his censer with incense in it and present it to God—all 250 of them. You and Aaron, you do the same.'
So, they all did it. They brought their censers, filled them with fire and incense, and stood at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron were there too.
Korah had gathered his whole squad against Moses and Aaron right at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Then, the whole community saw the incredible Glory of God appear.
God said to Moses and Aaron, 'Get away from these people, so I can wipe them out right here and now.'
But Moses and Aaron threw themselves on their faces and begged, 'Oh God, the God of all living things, is it fair for you to be angry with the whole community when only one man sinned?'
God told Moses, 'Speak to the community. Tell them to get away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.'

So Moses got up and went over to Dathan and Abiram, with the leaders of Israel following him. He told the community, 'Get away from the tents of these wicked men! Don't even touch anything that belongs to them, or you'll get swept away with them because of their sins.'

So everyone backed off from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. By then, Dathan and Abiram had come out and were standing at the entrance of their tents with their wives, their sons, and their little kids.

Moses then said to everyone, 'This is how you'll know that God sent me to do all these things, and that I didn't just make this stuff up. If these men die a normal death like everyone else, then you'll know God didn't send me. But if God does something totally new—if the ground splits open and swallows them and all their stuff, and they go down to the grave alive—then you'll know for sure that these men have disrespected God.'

He had barely finished speaking when the ground split right open beneath them. The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them whole—them, their families, all of Korah's people, and everything they owned. That was it for them, sent alive straight to the grave. The earth closed back up over them, and they were gone from the community forever.
When they heard their screams, all the Israelites around them ran for their lives, yelling, 'The earth is going to swallow us too!'
Then, fire shot down from God and burned up the 250 men who were offering the incense.

God then said to Moses, 'Tell Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, to collect the censers from the ashes and scatter the coals far away, because those censers are now holy. Take the censers of the men who sinned and died, and have them hammered into thin sheets to cover the Altar. They were offered to God, so they are holy. Let them be a sign to the people of Israel.'

So Eleazar the priest collected all the bronze censers from the men who had been burned up, and they hammered them flat to cover the Altar, just like God had told Moses. This was to be a reminder to the Israelites that only descendants of Aaron were allowed to burn incense before God. Anyone else who tried would end up just like Korah and his crew.
The very next day, the whole Israelite community started complaining about Moses and Aaron, saying, 'You have killed the Lord's people!'
But as the community gathered against Moses and Aaron, they looked toward the Tent of Meeting, and suddenly the Cloud covered it, and the Glory of God appeared for everyone to see.
Moses and Aaron went to the front of the Tent of Meeting. And God said to Moses, 'Get away from this community so I can destroy them in an instant.'
They fell on their faces again.

Moses yelled to Aaron, 'Grab your censer, put fire from the Altar in it, and add incense. Run to the community as fast as you can and make things right for them. God is furious—a plague has already started!'

Aaron did exactly what Moses said. He grabbed the censer and ran into the middle of the crowd. The plague had already broken out. He put the incense in and made atonement for the people. He stood right between the living and the dead, and the plague stopped.
In total, 14,700 people died from that plague, not even counting those who died with Korah. Then Aaron went back to Moses at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. The plague was over.

Numbers.title: God's Mic Drop Moment with a Stick
paragraphs: So God hit up Moses and was like, 'Yo, talk to the Israelites. I need you to collect a staff from each of the twelve tribe leaders. Make sure to write each guy's name on his own staff. Put Aaron's name on the one for the tribe of Levi. Then, lay them all out in the Tent of Meeting, right in front of the Ark of the Covenant, where I meet with you. Get this: the staff of the guy I pick is gonna sprout. I'm about to shut down all this complaining the Israelites have been doing about you.'

Moses told the Israelites what was up. The leaders gave him their twelve staffs, one from each tribe, and yeah, Aaron's was in the mix. Moses then arranged the staffs in front of God in the Tent of Testimony.

The next day, Moses went into the Tent of Testimony and, no cap, Aaron's staff—the one for the Levi tribe—had totally sprouted. It had buds, flowers, and even actual almonds on it! Wild. Moses brought all the staffs out from God's spot and showed them to everyone. They all stared, and each leader took back his own staff.
God told Moses, 'Put Aaron's staff back in front of the Ark. It's gonna be a sign for all the rebels. This should finally stop them from complaining and keep them from getting themselves killed.'
Moses did exactly what God told him to do.
The Israelites freaked out and said to Moses, 'We're dead. It's over for us. Anyone who even gets near God's place is a goner. Are we all just gonna die?'

Numbers.title: God's Holy Crew & Their Paycheck
paragraphs: Alright, so God tells Aaron, 'Look, you, your sons, and your whole fam are on duty for any mess-ups related to the holy Sanctuary. And yeah, that includes any slip-ups with the priesthood itself. So, grab your cousins from the Levi tribe, they're gonna be your crew. They'll help you and your sons out with your jobs at the Tent of Testimony. They'll report to you and handle their tasks around the Tent, but make sure they don't touch the sacred stuff on the Altar. Seriously, that's a death sentence for them AND for you. They're your support team for the Tent of Meeting, for all the work that goes down there. No randoms allowed, this is a closed crew.'

Your main gig is to manage the Sanctuary and the Altar. Why? To make sure God doesn't get angry with the Israelites again. I've hand-picked your bros, the Levites, from everyone in Israel. Think of them as a gift from me, a God-gift, to help with all the work at the Tent of Meeting. But listen up, only you and your sons get to be the actual priests, the ones working the Altar and going behind the curtain. This priesthood thing is a special gift just for you, you can't pass it off to someone else. Any outsider who tries to crash the Sanctuary gets taken out. Period.

Then God said to Aaron, 'Yo, I'm making you the manager of all the stuff people give to me—all the holy gifts from the Israelites. I'm handing it all over to you and your kids for you guys to use. That's the deal, forever. You and your sons get the leftovers from the offerings, whatever isn't completely torched on the Altar. We're talking the extra Grain-Offerings, Absolution-Offerings, and Compensation-Offerings. Eat it with respect, 'cause it's super holy. All the guys can eat it. Just treat it as sacred.'

'You also get the Wave-Offerings from the Israelites. I'm giving them to you, your sons, and your daughters as a gift. This is a permanent rule. Anyone in your house who's considered 'clean' can eat it. I'm also giving you the best of the best: the finest olive oil, the top-shelf new wine, and the grain they bring to God from their first harvest—all those firstfruits are yours. Anyone in your family who's clean can have some.'

'You get every single 'Totally-Devoted' gift. Every firstborn offered to God, whether it's an animal or a person, is yours. Well, not the actual firstborn, but the cash to buy them back. Firstborn humans and unclean animals get redeemed, and you get that redemption money. When a firstborn baby is a month old, they have to be bought back for five silver shekels, based on the official Sanctuary weight.'

'On the other hand, you don't redeem a firstborn ox, sheep, or goat—those are holy. Instead, you splash their blood on the Altar and burn their fat as a Fire-Gift, which smells amazing to God. But you get to keep the meat, just like you get the chest from the Wave-Offering and the right thigh. All the holy offerings the Israelites set aside for God, I'm giving to you and your kids. That's the permanent rule for you and your family—it's a 'Covenant-of-Salt,' which means it's eternal and can't be changed before God.'
God told Aaron, 'You're not getting any land as an inheritance, not even a tiny piece. I am your inheritance, your plot of ground among the Israelites.'

'I'm giving the Levites all the tithes in Israel as their salary for the work they do at the Tent of Meeting. From now on, the other Israelites can't just wander into the Tent of Meeting. If they do, they'll be hit with a penalty, and that penalty is death. It's the Levites, and only the Levites, who work in the Tent of Meeting, and they're responsible if anything goes wrong. This is the rule forever. They don't get an inheritance like the other Israelites; instead, I'm giving them the tithes that the people offer to God. That's why I made the ruling: They get no land inheritance among the People of Israel.'

God told Moses, 'Go talk to the Levites. Tell them, 'When you get the tithe from the Israelites, which is the inheritance I'm giving you, you have to give a tithe of that tithe as an offering to God. Your offering will be counted just like anyone else's gift of grain or wine. This is how you make offerings to God from all the tithes you get from the people: give God's share from these tithes to Aaron the priest. And make sure God's portion is the absolute best and holiest part of everything you receive.'

'Tell the Levites, 'When you offer that best part, the rest is considered the same as the grain or wine that others give. You and your families can eat the rest of it whenever, wherever—it's your payment for working at the Tent of Meeting. By offering the best part, you won't be guilty of anything, you won't disrespect the holy offerings of the Israelites, and you won't die.'

Numbers.title: The Wildest Purification Ritual Ever
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and Aaron with a new rule. He was like, 'Alright, tell the Israelites to find a perfect red cow. It's gotta be healthy, spotless, and never been used for work. Give it to Eleazar the priest, take it outside the camp, and then it gets butchered while he watches. Eleazar's gonna take some of its blood and flick it seven times toward the main tent where everyone meets God.'

Then, with Eleazar watching, the whole cow gets burned—skin, meat, blood, even its poop. The priest then grabs a cedar stick, some hyssop, and a scarlet cloth and chucks them onto the fire. After that, the priest has to wash his clothes and take a good bath. He can come back to camp, but he's still technically 'unclean' until evening. The guy who burned the cow also has to wash his clothes and take a bath. He's also unclean until evening.

Then, a guy who is 'clean' will gather up the cow's ashes and put them in a clean spot outside the camp. The Israelites will keep these ashes to make a special cleansing water, which is like a spiritual reset button.
The guy who gathered the ashes has to scrub his clothes and is also unclean until evening. This is a permanent rule for both the Israelites and any foreigners living with them.

Anyone who touches a dead body is considered 'unclean' for seven days. They have to use the cleansing water to purify themselves on the third day, and on the seventh day, they'll be clean. But if they skip the third and seventh-day steps, they're not clean. Anyone who touches a dead body and doesn't get clean messes up God's sacred space and gets kicked out of the community. As long as the cleansing water hasn't been sprinkled on them, they're still unclean.
This is the rule for when someone dies in their tent: anyone who goes into the tent or is already in there is 'unclean' for seven days, and any open container without a lid is also unclean.

Anyone out in the open who touches a dead body, whether they died violently or naturally, or even just a human bone or a grave, is unclean for seven days. For this unclean person, you take some of the ashes from the burnt offering and mix it with fresh water in a bowl. Find a 'clean' guy to dip a hyssop branch in the water and sprinkle it on the tent, all the furniture, the people who were in the tent, the person who touched the bones, and whoever touched a grave. Then he has to sprinkle the unclean person on the third and seventh days. On the seventh day, they're considered clean. The person who is now clean has to scrub their clothes and take a bath; by evening, they're all good. But if an unclean person doesn't do this cleansing stuff, they get kicked out of the community because they've disrespected God's holy place. The cleansing water wasn't sprinkled on them, so they're still unclean. This is the permanent rule for these situations.
The guy who sprinkles the cleansing water has to scrub his clothes, and anyone else who touches the cleansing water is also unclean until evening.
Anything the unclean person touches becomes unclean, and whoever touches what they touched is also unclean until evening.

Numbers.title: Moses LOSES IT & Gets BANNED From The Promised Land?!
paragraphs: So, in the first month, the whole crew of Israelites rocked up to the Zin Desert and set up camp in Kadesh.
But then, some heavy news: Miriam died and was buried there.

And then things got real, 'cause there was no water for the community. Everyone totally ganged up on Moses and Aaron. They went off on Moses, like, “We wish we’d just died with our brothers in front of God! Why’d you drag God's people out to this wasteland to die, us and our animals? And for real, why’d you make us leave Egypt just to bring us to this awful place? There’s no grain, no figs, no grapes, no pomegranates—and now not even any water!”
Moses and Aaron dipped from the crowd, went to the Tent of Meeting, and just fell on their faces. Then, they saw God's glory appear.

God told Moses, “Grab the staff. Get the whole community together, you and your brother Aaron. Speak to that rock right in front of them, and it will pour out water. You’re going to bring water out of the rock for them, so the people and their cattle can all drink.”

So Moses grabbed the staff from God's presence, just like he was told. He and Aaron got everyone together in front of the rock. Then Moses said, “Listen up, you rebels! Do we have to get water from this rock for you?”
And with that, Moses lifted his arm and smacked the rock with his staff—not once, but twice. Water just started gushing out. The whole community and all their animals drank.

But then God said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you didn’t trust me and didn’t show you thought I was holy in front of all the Israelites, you two will not lead this community into the land I’m giving them.”
This all went down at the Waters of Meribah, which means 'Bickering,' 'cause that's where the Israelites bickered with God, and He showed them He was holy.

From Kadesh, Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom with a message: “From your brother, Israel. You know all the struggles we’ve been through. Our ancestors went down to Egypt and lived there for ages, and the Egyptians were super cruel to us and them. But when we cried out to God for help, He heard us. He sent an angel and got us out of Egypt. So now we’re here in Kadesh, a town right on your border.

“Can you please let us pass through your land? We promise we won’t go through your fields or vineyards, and we won’t drink from your wells. We’ll stick to the main road, the King’s Highway, and won’t turn off it until we’ve crossed your border.”
But the king of Edom replied, “No way. If you even step one foot in my country, I’ll come out and kill you.”
The Israelites said, “Look, we’ll stay on the main road. If we or our animals drink any of your water, we’ll pay for it. We’re not trying to cause trouble—we’re just a bunch of tired travelers.”
He shot back again: “No. You can’t come through.” Then Edom came out with a huge, armed-up crew to block them. Since Edom refused to let them pass, Israel had to take a detour around his country.
The whole group of Israelites left Kadesh and traveled to Mount Hor.

At Mount Hor, on the border of Edom, God said to Moses and Aaron, “It’s time for Aaron to join his ancestors. He won’t enter the land I’m giving the Israelites, because both of you rebelled against my command at the Waters of Meribah. So take Aaron and his son Eleazar up Mount Hor. Take off Aaron’s special clothes and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered to his people there; he will die.”

Moses did exactly what God commanded. They climbed Mount Hor while the whole community watched. Moses took off Aaron’s clothes and put them on his son Eleazar. Then Aaron died right there on top of the mountain. After that, Moses and Eleazar came back down. When the whole community heard that Aaron had died, they mourned for him for thirty days.

Numbers.title: Snake Attack & Epic Battles?! Israel's Wild Road Trip
paragraphs: So, the Canaanite king of Arad, who was in charge of the Negev area, got word that the Israelites were coming up the road to Atharim. He wasn't having it, so he straight up attacked them and took a bunch of them as prisoners.
Israel made a promise to God, like a super serious vow: 'If you help us beat these guys, we'll totally wreck their towns and give you all the credit for this holy victory.'

God heard their prayer and was like, 'Bet.' He handed the Canaanites over to them. The Israelites completely destroyed them and their towns, a holy destruction for real. They even renamed the place Hormah, which means 'Holy Destruction.'

They bounced from Mount Hor and took the long way around Edom on the Red Sea Road. The whole time, the people were getting super cranky and started complaining to God and Moses, like, 'Yo, why'd you bring us out to this wasteland to die? There's no good food, no water, and we're seriously over this nasty bread.'

So God sent these gnarly poisonous snakes, and they started biting people, and a lot of Israelites died. Then the people ran to Moses and were like, 'Okay, our bad. We messed up by talking trash about God and you. Can you please pray and ask God to get rid of these snakes?'
So Moses prayed for the people.
God told Moses, 'Make a snake and put it on a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at it and will live.'
So Moses made a snake out of shiny copper and stuck it on top of a pole. And it worked! Anyone who got bitten by a snake just had to look at the copper snake, and they lived.

The Israelites packed up and camped at Oboth. Then they left Oboth and camped at Iye Abarim, out in the wilderness east of Moab. From there, they went and set up camp in the Zered Valley. Their next spot was by the Arnon River, which is the border between the Amorites and Moab. This place is even mentioned in The Book of the Wars of God:
'Waheb in Suphah, the canyons of Arnon; along the canyon ravines that lead to the village of Ar and press up against the border of Moab.'
They moved on to a place called Beer (which means 'The Well'), where God told Moses, 'Get everyone together; I'm gonna give them water.' That's when the Israelites busted out this song:
'Erupt, Well! Sing the Song of the Well, the well the princes dug, that the leaders of the people carved out with their scepters and staffs.'

From the wilderness, they went from Mattanah to Nahaliel to Bamoth (The Heights), and then to the valley that opens up into the fields of Moab, where you can see Pisgah (The Summit) overlooking the wasteland of Jeshimon.

Israel sent messengers to Sihon, the Amorite king, with a message: 'Hey, can we just pass through your land? We promise we won't mess with your fields or drink your water. We'll stick to the main road, the King's Road, until we're out of your territory.'

But Sihon was like, 'Nah.' He got his army together and marched out to the wilderness to fight Israel. He attacked them at Jahaz. But Israel fought back hard, totally beat him, and took over his land from the Arnon River all the way to the Jabbok, right up to the Ammonite border. They stopped there because the Ammonite border was super fortified. Israel took over and lived in all the Amorite cities, including Heshbon and all the little towns around it. Heshbon was the capital city of King Sihon of the Amorites. He had actually attacked the old king of Moab and taken all his land up to the Arnon River. That's why the singers have this song:
'Come to Heshbon to rebuild the city, restore Sihon’s town.'

'Fire once shot out of Heshbon, flames from Sihon's city; it burned up Ar of Moab, the people on Arnon’s heights. You're doomed, Moab! The people of the god Chemosh are finished! His sons are refugees, his daughters are prisoners of the Amorite king, Sihon.'

'Fire once shot out of Heshbon, flames from Sihon's city; it burned up Ar of Moab, the people on Arnon’s heights. You're doomed, Moab! The people of the god Chemosh are finished! His sons are refugees, his daughters are prisoners of the Amorite king, Sihon.'
'Oh, but we totally wrecked them: Nothing left of Heshbon all the way to Dibon; total destruction as far as Nophah, scorched earth all the way to Medeba.'
'Oh, but we totally wrecked them: Nothing left of Heshbon all the way to Dibon; total destruction as far as Nophah, scorched earth all the way to Medeba.'
So Israel moved in and took over the Amorite country. Moses sent some guys to scout out Jazer. They captured its villages and kicked out the Amorites who lived there.
Then they turned and headed north on the road to Bashan. Og, the king of Bashan, came out with his whole army to fight Moses at Edrei.
God told Moses, 'Don't be scared of him. I'm giving him to you as a gift—him, all his people, and his land. Do the same thing to him that you did to Sihon, the Amorite king who ruled in Heshbon.'
So they attacked him, his sons, and all his people—not a single person survived. Israel took over the land.

Numbers.title: My Donkey TALKS?! Wild Storytime
paragraphs: So the Israelites kept moving and set up camp on the Plains of Moab, right across from Jericho.

Balak, son of Zippor, got the news about everything Israel did to the Amorites. The people of Moab were lowkey freaking out because of Israel. There were just so many of them! They were totally shook.
Moab told the leaders of Midian, “Yo, this massive crew is about to wipe us out, like a clean sweep.”
So Balak, who was the king of Moab at the time, sent messengers to get this guy Balaam, son of Beor. He was from Pethor, by the Euphrates River.

Balak’s messengers said, “Listen up. A whole nation of people came out of Egypt, and now they’re everywhere, crawling all over the place! And they’re closing in on me. You gotta come and curse them for me—they’re way too strong. Maybe then I can actually fight them and kick them out of the country. Everyone knows your reputation: whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed. No cap.”
The leaders of Moab and Midian hit the road, with the cash for the curse packed and ready. When they got to Balaam, they gave him Balak’s message.
Balaam said, “Just crash here for the night. In the morning, I’ll give you the answer God gives me.”
The Moabite officials stayed with him.
Then God showed up to Balaam and asked, “So, who are these guys with you?”

Balaam answered, “Balak, son of Zippor, the king of Moab, sent them with a message: ‘Look, the people who came out of Egypt are swarming everywhere! Come and curse them for me. Maybe then I’ll be able to fight them and drive them out.’”
God told Balaam, “Don’t go with them. And you are NOT to curse those people—they are blessed.”
The next morning, Balaam got up and told Balak’s officials, “Go on back home; God said no, He won’t let me go with you.”
So the Moabite officials bounced, went back to Balak, and said, “Balaam refused to come with us.”

So Balak sent another group of officials, this time even more important and high-ranking. They came to Balaam and said, “Balak, son of Zippor, says, ‘Please, don’t say no! I’ll give you major honors and rewards—literally anything you ask for, I’ll do it. I’ll pay whatever. Just come and curse these people for me.’”

Balaam replied to Balak’s servants, “Look, even if Balak gave me his entire palace stuffed with silver and gold, I can’t go against the orders of my God to do anything, big or small. But hey, you can stay the night like the other guys did; I’ll see what else God has to say.”
That night, God came to Balaam and said, “Since these men came all this way for you, go ahead and go with them. But—and this is a big but—you will only do exactly what I tell you to do.”

Balaam got up in the morning, saddled his donkey, and left with the officials from Moab. But as he was going, God got super angry. The angel of God stood in the road to block his path. Balaam was riding his donkey, and his two servants were with him. When the donkey saw the angel blocking the road with a sword out, she swerved off the road into a field. Balaam beat the donkey to get her back on the road.
Then, as they were passing through a vineyard with walls on both sides, the donkey saw God’s angel again and scraped against the wall, crushing Balaam’s foot. Balaam hit her again.

God’s angel moved again and blocked the path in a super narrow spot where there was no room to get by on the left or right. Seeing the angel, Balaam’s donkey just sat down right under him. Balaam completely lost his temper and started wailing on the donkey with his staff.
Then, plot twist, God made the donkey talk. She said to Balaam, “What did I ever do to you that you’ve hit me these three times?”
Balaam yelled back, “Because you’re making me look like a fool! If I had a sword, I would’ve killed you by now!”
The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey, the one you’ve ridden your whole life until today? Have I ever done something like this to you before? Have I?”
He said, “No.”
Then God opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw it: God’s angel was standing in the road, blocking his way with a sword drawn. Balaam immediately fell to the ground, face down.

God’s angel said to him, “Why did you beat your poor donkey these three times? I came here to block you because you’re getting way ahead of yourself. The donkey saw me and turned away from me these three times. If she hadn’t, I would have killed you by now, but I would have let her live.”
Balaam said to God’s angel, “I messed up. I had no idea you were standing in the road to block me. If you’re not cool with what I’m doing, I’ll just go back home.”
But God’s angel said to Balaam, “Go ahead and go with the men. But you will only say what I tell you to say—nothing else.”
And so Balaam continued on his way with Balak’s officials.
When Balak heard that Balaam was finally coming, he went out to meet him in a Moabite town on the Arnon River, right at the edge of his territory.
Balak said to Balaam, “Didn’t I send an urgent message for you? Why didn’t you come right away? Did you think I couldn’t pay you enough or something?”
Balaam said to Balak, “Well, I’m here now. But I can’t just say whatever I want. I can only speak the words that God gives me—that’s it.”
Balaam then went with Balak to Kiriath Huzoth. Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
At sunrise, Balak took Balaam up to Bamoth Baal (The Heights of Baal), so he could get a good look at some of the people.

Numbers.title: Epic Fail: King Tries to Curse God's People
paragraphs: Balaam was like, “Yo, build me seven altars here, and get seven bulls and seven rams ready.”
So Balak did it. Then Balaam and Balak sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam told Balak, “Alright, you stand here and watch your offering while I go off by myself. Maybe God will show up. Whatever he tells me, I’ll report back to you.” Then he bounced.
And guess what? God actually met up with Balaam. Balaam said, “I set up seven altars and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.”
Then God gave Balaam a message: “Go back to Balak and tell him this.”
He went back and found Balak posted up next to his offering, with all the important Moab dudes. Then Balaam dropped his message:

“Balak brought me all the way from Aram, the king of Moab dragged me from the eastern mountains. He was like, ‘Go curse Jacob for me; go put a hex on Israel.’ But for real, how can I curse someone God hasn’t cursed? How can I diss someone God hasn’t dissed? From these high rocks I see them, from the hills I’m watching them. Look, they’re a whole nation just vibing by themselves, thinking they’re different from everyone else. Who could even count all of Jacob’s people, or even get a headcount of Israel? Lowkey, I wanna die a good death like them. I want my end to be just like theirs.”
Balak was shook. “Bro, what are you doing? I brought you here to curse my enemies, and you’re out here blessing them!”
Balaam answered, “Look, I gotta say what God tells me to say, right?”
Balak told him, “Okay, fine. Come with me to another spot where you can only see the edge of their camp—you won’t see all of them. From there, curse them for me.”
So he took him to this place called Watchmen’s Meadow on top of Mount Pisgah. He built seven altars there and offered a bull and a ram on each one.
Balaam said to Balak, “You stay here by your offering while I go meet with him over there.”
God met up with Balaam again and gave him a message. He said, “Go back to Balak and give him the message.”
Balaam went back and found him standing by his offering with all the Moab leaders. Balak asked him, “What did God say?” Then Balaam delivered his message:

“Get up, Balak. Listen up, son of Zippor: God isn’t a human who tells lies, and he’s not some guy who changes his mind. If he says something, he does it. If he makes a promise, he keeps it. I was brought here to bless, and now he’s blessed them—how can I undo that? God has no beef with Jacob, he sees nothing wrong with Israel. God is with them, and they’re with him, shouting praises to their King. God brought them out of Egypt, going wild like a beast. No curse can touch Jacob, no magic can stop Israel. People will look at Jacob and Israel and say, ‘Wow, look what God did!’ Look, they’re a nation getting hyped, stretching like a lion, a king of the beasts, wide awake. They won’t rest until they’ve won and enjoyed their victory.”
Balak said to Balaam, “Okay, fine! If you can’t curse them, at least don’t bless them!”
Balaam shot back, “Didn’t I tell you before? ‘I can only say what God tells me to say.’”

Balak said to Balaam, “Please, let me take you to one more place. Maybe God will be cool with you cursing them for me from there.” So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooked a wasteland.
Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars for me here and get seven bulls and seven rams ready for the sacrifice.”
Balak did it and offered a bull and a ram on each of the altars.

Numbers.title: Balaam's Final Prophecy Drop is WILD
paragraphs: Okay, so Balaam finally got the memo that God was all-in on blessing Israel. He ditched the magic tricks he'd been trying and just looked out at the wilderness. When he saw all the tribes of Israel just chilling in their camps, the Spirit of God hit him hard, and he started spitting facts:

This is the official word from Balaam, son of Beor, a guy who's seeing things crystal clear. The guy who hears God's voice, who sees the visions the Almighty sends him. The guy who bows down and gets the real scoop on what's happening.

Man, your setup is amazing, Jacob! Your homes are gorgeous, Israel! It's like a vibe of peaceful valleys and riverside gardens. Like God himself planted a garden of fresh herbs and cedar trees. You're gonna be overflowing with blessings, and your influence will be everywhere. Your king is gonna be on a whole other level, way above guys like Agag. Your kingdom? Totally epic. God brought you out of Egypt, going beast mode like a wild ox, just plowing through your enemies, snapping their bones and their weapons. Israel's just chilling now, like a lion taking a nap. Who's dumb enough to mess with the king of the jungle? Whoever blesses you is blessed, and whoever messes with you is toast.

Balak totally lost it with Balaam. He was so mad, shaking his fist and everything. He yelled, "I brought you here to curse my enemies, and what do you do? You bless them! Three times! Get out of here! Go home! I was gonna pay you big time, but now you get nothing. And it's God's fault!"

Balaam just said to Balak, "Dude, didn't I tell you from the start? Even if you gave me a palace full of cash, I can't go against what God says. I'm heading home now, but let me give you a little heads-up about what these people are gonna do to your people in the future." Then he dropped another prophecy:

This is the word from Balaam, son of Beor, the guy with the 20/20 vision. The guy who hears what God says, who knows what the Most High is up to. The one who sees what the Almighty shows him, who bows down and sees the truth. I see him, but not right now. I sense him, but he's not here yet. A star is gonna rise from Jacob, a ruler from Israel. He's gonna crush the leaders of Moab and all the loudmouths. Edom will be conquered, and Israel will be walking away with all the loot. A ruler is coming from Jacob who will take out anyone left in the city.
Then Balaam saw Amalek and gave this prophecy:
Amalek, you think you're number one right now, but you're gonna end up last. Totally wrecked.
He saw the Kenites and said this about them:
Your crib is in a sweet, safe spot, like a nest on a cliff. But you're still gonna look pretty dumb when Assyria comes and takes you prisoner.
Balaam gave one last prophecy:
Oh man, it's over. Who can survive when God gets started? People from across the sea will come and mess with Assyria and Eber, but they'll end up as nothing too, just like everyone else.
Then Balaam got up and went home. Balak went his way too.

Numbers.title: Israel's Wild Party Ends BADLY
paragraphs: So, the Israelites were chilling at a place called Shittim, and some of the guys started hooking up with Moabite girls. It all started when the girls invited them to these wild religious parties. They'd eat together and then worship their gods. Before you know it, Israel was all in on worshiping this god called Baal of Peor. God was lowkey furious, like, seriously mad at Israel.
God told Moses, “Take all the leaders of Israel and execute them. Hang them up in public for everyone to see. That’s the only way to get my anger to chill out.”
Moses then told the judges of Israel, “Each of you has to execute the men in your group who started worshiping Baal of Peor.”

But then, get this: while everyone was crying and repenting at the main tent, this one Israelite guy, with no shame at all, brings a Midianite woman into his tent right in front of Moses and everyone. Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, saw this go down, grabbed his spear, and followed them into the tent. With one move, he speared both of them, the Israelite guy and the woman, right through their stomachs. That finally stopped the plague that was spreading through Israel. But not before 24,000 people had already died. It was a whole disaster.

God then said to Moses: “Phinehas, son of Eleazar, the priest, has turned my anger away from the Israelites. He was just as serious about my honor as I am, so I didn't end up destroying everyone in my anger. So, tell him I'm making a peace treaty with him. He and his descendants will be priests forever, because he was passionate for his God and made things right for the people of Israel.”

The Israelite guy who was killed with the Midianite woman was named Zimri, son of Salu. He was a leader from the Simeonite family. And the Midianite woman who was killed was named Cozbi. She was the daughter of Zur, who was a chief of a Midianite tribe.

God then told Moses: “From now on, the Midianites are your enemies. You need to fight them hard. They totally tricked you with that whole Peor situation, and with that woman Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite leader, who was killed during the plague that happened because of Peor.”

Numbers.title: Israel's New Headcount! Who Made the Cut?
paragraphs: Alright, so after that gnarly plague, God hit up Moses and Eleazar, Aaron's priest son, and was like, “Yo, I need a headcount of the entire Israelite community. Go family by family and count everyone twenty and up who’s able to fight in the army.”

So, Moses and Eleazar did what God said. They gathered everyone on the Plains of Moab, right by the Jordan River across from Jericho, and announced, “Time for a census! Everyone twenty or older, line up.”
These were the people of Israel who bounced from Egypt:
First up, Reuben, Israel’s oldest son. His sons and their clans were:
Hanoch and the Hanochite clan,
Pallu and the Palluite clan,
Hezron and the Hezronite clan,
Carmi and the Carmite clan.
That was the whole Reubenite squad. They clocked in at 43,730 dudes.
Pallu’s son was Eliab.

Eliab’s sons were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. (Quick history refresh: Dathan and Abiram were those community leaders from Korah's crew who rebelled against Moses and Aaron. It was a whole thing against God, really. The ground literally opened up and swallowed them and Korah's gang when that fire consumed 250 of them. Even after all this time, their story is a major warning sign. But plot twist, Korah's own kids didn't die out.)
Next, the sons of Simeon and their clans:
Nemuel and the Nemuelite clan,
Jamin and the Jaminite clan,
Jakin and the Jakinite clan,
Zerah and the Zerahite clan,
Shaul and the Shaulite clan.
These were the Simeon clans, totaling 22,200 guys.
The sons of Gad and their clans:
Zephon and the Zephonite clan,
Haggi and the Haggite clan,
Shuni and the Shunite clan,
Ozni and the Oznite clan,
Eri and the Erite clan,
Arodi and the Arodite clan,
Areli and the Arelite clan.
These were the Gad clans, adding up to 40,500 men.
Judah’s sons Er and Onan had died way back in Canaan. So, Judah’s clans were from his other sons:
Shelah and the Shelanite clan,
Perez and the Perezite clan,
Zerah and the Zerahite clan.
Perez’s sons were:
Hezron and the Hezronite clan,
Hamul and the Hamulite clan.
These were the clans of Judah, a massive crew of 76,500.
The sons of Issachar by their clans:
Tola and the Tolaite clan,
Puah and the Puite clan,
Jashub and the Jashubite clan,
Shimron and the Shimronite clan.
These were the Issachar clans, numbering 64,300.
The sons of Zebulun by their clans:
Sered and the Seredite clan,
Elon and the Elonite clan,
Jahleel and the Jahleelite clan.
These were the Zebulun clans, with a headcount of 60,500.
Joseph's descendants came through his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim. From Manasseh:
Makir and the Makirite clan (Makir was Gilead's dad, btw),
Gilead and the Gileadite clan.
The sons of Gilead were:
Iezer and the Iezerite clan,
Helek and the Helekite clan,
Asriel and the Asrielite clan,
Shechem and the Shechemite clan,
Shemida and the Shemidaite clan,
Hepher and the Hepherite clan.
Now, Hepher’s son Zelophehad had no sons, only daughters. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. Total girl power moment.
These were the clans of Manasseh, and they numbered 52,700.
Now for the sons of Ephraim by their clans:
Shuthelah and the Shuthelahite clan,
Beker and the Bekerite clan,
Tahan and the Tahanite clan.
Shuthelah’s son was:
Eran and the Eranite clan.
These were the clans of Ephraim, with a headcount of 32,500.
So those were all of Joseph's descendants, clan by clan.
The sons of Benjamin by their clans:
Bela and the Belaite clan,
Ashbel and the Ashbelite clan,
Ahiram and the Ahiramite clan,
Shupham and the Shuphamite clan,
Hupham and the Huphamite clan.
Bela’s sons, Ard and Naaman, also started their own clans:
Ard and the Ardite clan,
Naaman and the Naamite clan.
These were the Benjamin clans, numbering 45,600.
The sons of Dan by their clan:
Shuham and the Shuhamite clan.
That's basically all the Dan clans, all from Shuham. They numbered 64,400.
The sons of Asher by their clan:
Imnah and the Imnite clan,
Ishvi and the Ishvite clan,
Beriah and the Beriite clan.
Beriah’s sons were:
Heber and the Heberite clan,
Malkiel and the Malkielite clan.
Asher also had a daughter named Serah.
These were the clans of Asher, with a total of 53,400 people.
The sons of Naphtali by their clans:
Jahzeel and the Jahzeelite clan,
Guni and the Gunite clan,
Jezer and the Jezerite clan,
Shillem and the Shillemite clan.
These were the Naphtali clans, and they numbered 45,400.
The grand total number of the People of Israel was a whopping 601,730.

Then God spoke to Moses: “Okay, now divide up the land for them to inherit based on this population count. A bigger group gets a bigger piece of land; a smaller group gets a smaller piece. Each one gets their inheritance based on their numbers.
“But make sure the land is assigned by drawing lots.
“Each group’s inheritance is based on their population, the number of names listed for their tribe, and it'll be divided among the big and small groups by drawing lots.”
And here's the headcount for the Levites by their clans:
Gershon and the Gershonite clan,
Kohath and the Kohathite clan,
Merari and the Merarite clan.
The Levite clans also included:
the Libnite clan,
the Hebronite clan,
the Mahlite clan,
the Mushite clan,
the Korahite clan.

Kohath was Amram’s dad. Amram’s wife was Jochebed, a descendant of Levi born while they were all in Egypt. Jochebed had Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam with Amram. Aaron was the father of Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. But, Nadab and Abihu died when they offered some unauthorized fire sacrifice to God. Big yikes.
The number of all the Levite males, from one month old and up, was 23,000. They weren't counted with the rest of the Israelites because they didn't get any land as an inheritance.

So these are the people counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, the People of Israel who were tallied up on the Plains of Moab at Jordan-Jericho. And get this: not a single one of them was from the group that Moses and Aaron had counted in the first census in the Sinai Wilderness. Because God had said about them, “They’ll all die in the wilderness.” And they did. Not one was left, except for Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. No cap.

Numbers.title: These Girls Fought for Their Rights... and WON!
paragraphs: So, these sisters, the daughters of a guy named Zelophehad, showed up. Their dad's family tree was pretty legit, tracing all the way back to Joseph's son Manasseh. The sisters' names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

They walked right up to the main tent where all the important meetings happened and stood in front of Moses, the head priest Eleazar, and all the leaders and everyone else. They were like, "Listen up. Our dad died out in the desert. He wasn't with that troublemaker Korah and his crew who went against God. He died for his own mistakes, and he didn't have any sons. But for real, why should our family name just disappear from the records just because he didn't have a son? That's not fair. So, give us our own piece of land, our inheritance, just like our dad's other relatives get."
Moses was like, "Good point." So he took their problem straight to God.

And God's verdict was: "Yo, Zelophehad's daughters have a totally valid point. No cap. Give them their own property, just like their dad's relatives. Hand over the inheritance that would've been their dad's.

"And from now on, tell the Israelites this is the new rule: If a guy dies and doesn't have a son, his daughter gets the inheritance. If he doesn't have a daughter, it goes to his brothers. No brothers? It goes to his uncles on his dad's side. If his dad didn't have any brothers either, then it goes to the closest relative. The point is to keep the property in the family. This is the new law, straight from me, God, through Moses."

Then God said to Moses, "Go climb the Abarim Mountains and get a good look at the land I'm giving to the people of Israel. After you've seen it, it'll be your time to go, and you'll be buried with your ancestors, just like your brother Aaron. This is because of what happened back in the Zin Desert when everyone was arguing. You didn't trust me and show them I was holy when it came to the water situation—you know, the 'Waters of Meribah' incident at Kadesh."

Moses said back to God: "Please, God, you're the God who knows everyone's spirit. Appoint a new leader for this community, someone who can lead them out and bring them back, so your people won't be like a bunch of sheep wandering around with no shepherd."

God told Moses, "Get Joshua, son of Nun—he's got the Spirit in him!—and lay your hand on him. Have him stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the whole community, and commission him right there in front of everyone. Pass on your authority to him so that the entire community of Israel will listen to him. He'll need to check in with Eleazar the priest, who will use the special Urim oracle to get my advice for him. Joshua will be the one to lead the people of Israel in everything they do, wherever they go."

Moses did exactly what God told him. He got Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole community. He laid his hands on him and officially made him the new leader, just like God had instructed him.

Numbers.title: God's Official Worship Schedule
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and was like, "Alright, tell the People of Israel what's up. Let them know they're in charge of bringing my food—my Fire-Gifts that smell amazing—at the scheduled times. Tell them this is the Fire-Gift you gotta bring to God: two healthy one-year-old lambs every single day as the regular Burnt-Offering. One lamb in the morning, the other in the evening. With that, bring two quarts of fine flour mixed with a quart of olive oil for a Grain-Offering. This is the standard Burnt-Offering we set up back at Mount Sinai, a fire-gift to God that smells awesome. The Drink-Offering that goes with it is a quart of strong beer for each lamb. Pour that out for God in the Holy Place. Then, do the second lamb in the evening with the same Grain-Offering and Drink-Offering as the morning one. It's a Fire-Gift, and God loves the smell.

On the Sabbath, you're gonna offer two healthy one-year-old lambs, plus their Drink-Offering and a Grain-Offering of four quarts of fine flour mixed with oil. This is the special Sabbath Burnt-Offering, and it's on top of the regular daily Burnt-Offering and its Drink-Offering.
On the first day of each month, you'll bring a Burnt-Offering to God: two young bulls, one ram, and seven male one-year-old lambs—all have to be perfect, no flaws.

A Grain-Offering of six quarts of fine flour mixed with oil goes with each bull, four quarts of fine flour mixed with oil for the ram, and two quarts of fine flour mixed with oil for each lamb. This is for a Burnt-Offering, a smell that pleases God, a Fire-Gift to Him. Also, you'll pour out Drink-Offerings: two quarts of wine for each bull, one and a quarter quarts for the ram, and a quart for each lamb.
This is the monthly Burnt-Offering you'll do all year. On top of the regular Burnt-Offering and its Drink-Offering, you also have to offer a male goat to God as an offering to make things right.
God’s Passover is on the fourteenth day of the first month. Then on the fifteenth day, it's festival time.

For seven days, you can only eat bread made without yeast. The first day is for a special worship gathering; nobody does any regular work. You'll bring a Fire-Gift to God, a Burnt-Offering: two young bulls, one ram, and seven male one-year-old lambs—all healthy. You'll also prep a Grain-Offering of six quarts of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, four quarts for the ram, and two quarts for each lamb, plus a goat as an offering to atone for your sins.

You'll offer these in addition to the regular morning Burnt-Offering. You've gotta prepare this food for the Fire-Gift, which has a smell that pleases God, every day for seven days. Do this on top of the regular Burnt-Offering and Drink-Offering.
Wrap up on the seventh day with another holy worship gathering; no regular work on that day either.

On the Day of Firstfruits, when you bring a new grain offering to God during your Festival of Weeks, get together for holy worship and don't do any regular work. Bring a Burnt-Offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male one-year-old lambs as a pleasing fragrance to God. Prepare a Grain-Offering of six quarts of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, four quarts for the ram, and two quarts for each lamb, plus a male goat as an Absolution-Offering to atone for you.
These are all extra, on top of the daily Burnt-Offering and its Grain-Offering and the Drink-Offering. And remember, the animals have to be healthy, no cap.

Numbers.title: God's Lit Festival Schedule
paragraphs: "Okay, so on the first day of the seventh month, everyone needs to gather for a special worship service. No regular work, got it? This is the Day of Trumpet Blasts. You're gonna offer a big sacrifice to God that smells amazing to Him: one young bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all totally healthy. Then, for the grain offering, you'll need six quarts of top-quality flour mixed with oil for the bull, four quarts for the ram, and two quarts for each lamb. Plus, you'll offer a male goat to get right with God and make up for your mistakes.
This is all on top of the usual monthly and daily sacrifices with their grain and drink offerings that you're already supposed to do. It's a fire-gift to God that He's really into.
Then, on the tenth day of the same month, you'll have another holy gathering. You've gotta humble yourselves and not do any work.

Bring a sacrifice to God that smells awesome to Him: one young bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all healthy. For the grain offering, prepare six quarts of fine flour mixed with oil for the bull, four for the ram, and two for each of the seven lambs. Also, bring a male goat to make things right, on top of the regular daily sacrifice with its grain and drink offerings.

Next up, on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, get together for a holy meeting. No regular work. You're gonna celebrate a festival for God that lasts seven days. Bring a burnt offering, a fire-gift that God will love: thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all in perfect condition. For the grain offering, you'll need six quarts of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, four quarts for each ram, and two quarts for each of the fourteen lambs. And don't forget the male goat for forgiveness, in addition to the regular daily sacrifice with its grain and drink offerings.

On day two: twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all healthy. Prepare the grain and drink offerings for all the animals, just like the recipe says. And bring a male goat for an absolution-offering, on top of the regular daily sacrifice stuff.

On the third day: eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all healthy. Prepare the grain and drink offerings for them, following the instructions. And bring a male goat for forgiveness, plus the regular daily sacrifice with its offerings.

On the fourth day: ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all healthy. Prepare their grain and drink offerings according to the rules. And bring a male goat for an absolution-offering, on top of the regular daily sacrifice.

On the fifth day: nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all healthy. Prepare the grain and drink offerings for them, just like you're supposed to. And bring a male goat for forgiveness, in addition to the regular daily sacrifice.

On the sixth day: eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all healthy. Prepare their grain and drink offerings, following the recipe. And bring a male goat for an absolution-offering, on top of the regular daily sacrifice.

On the seventh day: seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all healthy. Prepare their grain and drink offerings as prescribed. And bring a male goat for forgiveness, in addition to the regular daily sacrifice.

On the eighth day, you'll have another holy gathering. No regular work. Bring a fire-gift to God that smells great, a burnt offering of one bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all healthy. Prepare the grain and drink offerings for them according to the instructions. And bring a male goat for an absolution-offering, on top of the regular daily sacrifice.

So yeah, you guys have to offer all this stuff to God as a group during your scheduled festivals: your burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, and peace offerings. This is all separate from any personal promises or freewill gifts you might give."
Then Moses told the people of Israel everything God had commanded him.

Numbers.title: God's Rules on Making Promises
paragraphs: Moses laid it all out for the leaders of Israel's tribes: “Here’s the command from God: If a guy makes a serious promise to God or swears to do something, he can’t just back out. He has to do exactly what he said he would.

“Now, if a young woman, still living at her dad's place, makes a promise to God, and her dad hears about it but doesn’t say anything, then she’s locked in. She has to follow through. But if her dad hears about it and immediately says, ‘No way,’ then all bets are off. Her promises are void, and God lets her off the hook because her dad stopped her.

“If she gets married after making a promise, maybe even a rash one she blurted out, and her husband finds out but is cool with it, then she has to keep her word. But if her husband hears it and is like, ‘Uh, I don’t think so,’ he cancels it right then and there. The promise is off, and God releases her.
“For widows or divorced women, any promise they make is 100% on them. It’s binding.

“If a married woman makes a promise or an oath, and her husband hears about it but stays quiet and doesn't object, then her promises stick. They're valid. But if her husband shuts it down as soon as he hears it, then none of what she promised is binding. Her husband canceled it, so God lets her go. Basically, any promise she makes that could be a bad deal for her, her husband can either give the green light or shut it down. But if he hears about it and says nothing day after day, his silence means he's good with it, and she has to follow through. If he waits a while and then tries to cancel it, then the consequences are on him.”
These are the rules God gave Moses for how things work between a husband and wife, and between a father and his young daughter who’s still living at home.

Numbers.title: Payback Time: The Midianite Takedown
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and said, “Alright, it’s time to get payback on the Midianites for what they did to the Israelites. After this, you’ll be joining your ancestors.”
So Moses told the people, “Gear up. We’re picking guys to go to war against Midian and give them God’s payback. We need a thousand from each tribe.”

They ended up with a squad of twelve thousand soldiers, a thousand from each tribe in Israel. Moses sent them out to battle, along with Phinehas, Eleazar’s son. He was the army’s priest, and he brought the holy gear and the trumpets for signaling.

They rolled up on Midian, just like God told Moses to, and they didn’t leave a single man alive. They even took down the five Midianite kings—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. Oh, and they got Balaam, son of Beor, with a sword too. The Israelites captured the Midianite women and kids, and they took all their animals, herds, and everything they owned as loot. They burned down all the towns where the Midianites lived and all their camps. They took everything—people, animals, you name it. Then they brought all the captives and the loot back to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the whole Israelite crew who were camped out on the Plains of Moab, right by the Jordan River near Jericho.

Moses, Eleazar, and all the community leaders went out to meet the army as they were coming back. But Moses was lowkey furious with the army officers, the commanders of thousands and hundreds. He was like, “Seriously? You let the women live? These are the women who, thanks to Balaam, made the Israelites turn their backs on God at Peor. That’s what caused the plague that hit our people! You gotta finish the job. Kill all the boys. And kill every woman who’s slept with a man. You can keep the younger women who are still virgins for yourselves.”

“And here’s the deal now: You gotta set up your tents outside the main camp. Anyone who’s killed someone or even touched a dead body has to stay out here for seven days. On the third and seventh days, you need to purify yourselves and your captives. And wash every piece of clothing and anything made of leather, goat hair, or wood.”

Then Eleazar the priest laid it down for the soldiers: “This is the rule God gave Moses. Anything that can handle fire—gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead—has to go through the fire to be made clean. Then it also has to be washed with the special cleansing water. Anything that can’t handle fire just gets the water treatment. On the seventh day, wash all your clothes, and you’ll be officially clean. Then you can come back to camp.”

God told Moses, “You, Eleazar the priest, and the family leaders need to count up all the captives, both people and animals. Then, split all the loot 50/50 between the soldiers who fought and everyone else in the community.”

“From the soldiers’ half, you need to set aside a tax for God: one out of every five hundred, whether it’s people, cattle, donkeys, or sheep. That’s God’s cut, and you give it to Eleazar the priest. From the community’s half, you’ll tax them one out of every fifty, whether it’s people, cattle, donkeys, sheep, or whatever. Give that share to the Levites, since they’re in charge of taking care of God’s Dwelling.”
So Moses and Eleazar did exactly what God told them to do.
The rest of the loot the army took was:
675,000 sheep
72,000 cattle
61,000 donkeys
32,000 women who were virgins
The half that went to the soldiers who fought was:
337,500 sheep, with 675 of them taxed for God
36,000 cattle, with 72 of them taxed for God
30,500 donkeys, with 61 of them taxed for God
16,000 people, with 32 of them taxed for God
Moses gave the tax, God’s portion, to Eleazar the priest, just like God had told him.
The other half belonged to the Israelite community, which Moses had separated from the soldiers’ share. It was:
337,500 sheep
36,000 cattle
30,500 donkeys
16,000 people
From the community’s half, Moses took one out of every fifty people and animals, just as God had commanded, and gave them to the Levites who were in charge of God’s Dwelling.

Then the army officers, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, came to Moses and said, “Sir, we counted all the soldiers under our command, and not a single one is missing. So we’ve brought our own offerings to God from the gold stuff we found—armlets, bracelets, rings, earrings, all of it—to make things right with God for our lives.”

Moses and Eleazar the priest took all the gold from them, all this amazing handcrafted jewelry. The total weight of the gold that the commanders offered as a gift to God was about 600 pounds. This was all from the soldiers who had taken it as plunder. Moses and Eleazar took the gold from the commanders and brought it to the Tent of Meeting. It was a reminder for the Israelites of what God had done.

Numbers.title: Don't Bail On Us Bro!
paragraphs: So, the Reuben and Gad families had, like, a crazy amount of animals. They scoped out the lands of Jazer and Gilead and were like, "Whoa, this place is prime real estate for our herds." So they rolled up to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the other leaders and said, "Yo, check it. Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon—that whole area God helped us take down? It's legit perfect for livestock, and we've got a ton."
They kept going, "If you think we've been solid contributors, let us have this land as our inheritance. Please don't make us cross the Jordan River."

Moses was not having it. He shot back at the Gad and Reuben families, "Hold up. Are you seriously saying you're gonna chill here while your brothers go off to fight? Why would you even think of psyching out the Israelites and making them lose morale right when they're about to enter the land God promised them? That's the exact same stunt your ancestors pulled when I sent them from Kadesh Barnea to scout the land. They went up to the Eshcol Valley, took one look, and were like, 'Nah, we're out.' They totally crushed the spirit of the Israelites, who then didn't want to enter the land God had given them. And God was furious. Like, seriously mad. He swore, 'None of the people who came out of Egypt, twenty years or older, will ever see the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. They weren't all-in on following me. The only exceptions are Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun; they followed me with their whole heart.'
God's anger burned against Israel. He made them wander in the desert for forty years until that whole generation that did evil in His sight died off.

"And now here you are, another crew of sinners, stepping up to be just like your ancestors, adding more fuel to God's already blazing anger against Israel. If you ditch Him, He'll do it all over again. He'll leave them in the desert, and it'll be all your fault."

They got closer to him and said, "Look, all we wanna do is build some pens for our animals and towns for our families. Then we'll grab our weapons and be the front-line soldiers, leading the Israelites to their new home. We can leave our families here, safe in fortified towns, protected from the locals. But we promise we won't go back to our homes until every single Israelite has their own inheritance. We're not asking for any land west of the Jordan; we're claiming our inheritance here on the east side."

Moses said, "Alright, if you actually do what you say—if you arm yourselves for God and go into battle, and cross the Jordan together, ready to fight until God has cleared out His enemies—then, once the land is secure, you'll have done your duty to God and Israel. Then this land will be yours to keep, with God's blessing.

"But if you don't keep your word, you'll be sinning against God, and you can bet your sin will find you out. So, go on. Build towns for your families and pens for your animals. But you better do what you promised."

The families of Gad and Reuben told Moses, "We'll do exactly as our master commands. Our kids, wives, and all our animals will stay here in the towns of Gilead. But every one of us who can fight will arm up and cross the river to fight for God, just like our master said."

So Moses gave orders about them to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the Israelite tribes. Moses said, "If the families of Gad and Reuben cross the Jordan with you, all armed and ready to fight for God, then after the land is secure, you can give them the land of Gilead as their inheritance. But if they don't cross over with you, they'll have to get their land with the rest of you in Canaan."
The families of Gad and Reuben replied, "We'll do what God has said. We'll cross the Jordan ready to fight for God. But the land we inherit will be here, east of the Jordan."

Moses gave the families of Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh (Joseph's son) the kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, and the kingdom of Og, king of Bashan—the whole deal, the land, its towns, and all the territories around them.
The Gadites rebuilt Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer, Atroth Shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah, Beth Nimrah, and Beth Haran as fortified cities; they also built pens for their animals.
The Reubenites rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kiriathaim, plus Nebo and Baal Meon and Sibmah. They even renamed the cities they rebuilt.

The family of Makir, Manasseh's son, went to Gilead, conquered it, and kicked out the Amorites who lived there. Then Moses gave Gilead to the Makirites, the descendants of Manasseh. They moved in and settled down.
Jair, another one of Manasseh's sons, captured some villages and named them Havvoth Jair (which means Jair's Tent-Camps).
