Nobah captured Kenath and all its surrounding villages. Then he renamed it after himself, Nobah.

Numbers.title: Israel's Ultimate 40-Year Road Trip Log
paragraphs: Alright, so here's the complete travel log of every single place the Israelites camped after they bounced from Egypt. Moses and Aaron were leading the squad, military-style. God told Moses to keep a detailed journal of every move they made, camp by camp.

They rolled out of Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month, right after Passover. They left with their heads held high, super confident. Meanwhile, the Egyptians were all busy burying their firstborn sons that God had taken out. They watched the Israelites leave, probably realizing their own gods were a total joke.
The People of Israel's journey went like this:
They left Rameses and first camped at Succoth.
Left Succoth, next stop was Etham, right on the edge of the wilderness.
Left Etham, looped back around to Pi Hahiroth, which is east of Baal Zephon, and set up camp near Migdol.
Left Pi Hahiroth and cut straight through the Sea into the wilderness. After a three-day trek into the Etham Wilderness, they camped at Marah.
Left Marah and pulled up to Elim. This place was legit, with twelve springs and seventy palm trees. They chilled there for a bit.
Left Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
Left the Red Sea and camped in the Sin Wilderness.
Left the Sin Wilderness and camped at Dophkah.
Left Dophkah and camped at Alush.
Left Alush and camped at Rephidim, which was a total bust because there was zero water for anyone to drink.
Left Rephidim and camped in the Sinai Wilderness.
Left the Sinai Wilderness and camped at Kibroth Hattaavah.
Left Kibroth Hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
Left Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
Left Rithmah and camped at Rimmon Perez.
Left Rimmon Perez and camped at Libnah.
Left Libnah and camped at Rissah.
Left Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
Left Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
Left Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
Left Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
Left Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
Left Tahath and camped at Terah.
Left Terah and camped at Mithcah.
Left Mithcah and camped at Hashmonah.
Left Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
Left Moseroth and camped at Bene Jaakan.
Left Bene Jaakan and camped at Hor Haggidgad.
Left Hor Haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
Left Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
Left Abronah and camped at Ezion Geber.
Left Ezion Geber and finally camped at Kadesh in the Zin Wilderness.

After they left Kadesh, they camped at Mount Hor, right on the border of Edom. This is where Aaron the priest, following God's command, climbed Mount Hor and died. It was the first day of the fifth month in the fortieth year since the Israelites had left Egypt. Aaron was 123 years old when he passed away on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who was in charge of the Negev part of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming.
So they left Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
Left Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
Left Punon and camped at Oboth.
Left Oboth and camped at Iye Abarim on the Moab border.
Left Iyim and camped at Dibon Gad.
Left Dibon Gad and camped at Almon Diblathaim.
Left Almon Diblathaim and camped in the Abarim mountains, where they could see Nebo.
After leaving the Abarim mountains, they camped on the Plains of Moab at Jordan-Jericho. Their camp was huge, stretching all the way along the Jordan riverbanks from Beth Jeshimoth to Abel Shittim.

Then God spoke to Moses there on the Plains of Moab by Jordan-Jericho: “Tell the Israelites, when you cross the Jordan into Canaan, you have to drive out all the people who live there. Destroy all their carved idols and metal statues, and tear down all their sacred places. You're taking over the land to live in it; I've given it to you. It's all yours.

“You'll divide up the land by drawing lots, based on the size of your clans. Bigger clans get bigger pieces of land, smaller clans get smaller pieces. Whatever the lot decides, that's final. You'll divide it up according to your ancestral tribes.

“But listen up, this is serious. If you don't drive out the people living there, every single one you let stay will become like a cinder in your eye and a thorn in your side. They will give you non-stop trouble right in your own land. And if that happens, I'll end up doing to you what I was planning to do to them.”

Numbers.title: God Drops the Ultimate Land Reveal
paragraphs: Alright, so God hits up Moses and is like, 'Yo, tell the Israelites the deal. When you roll into Canaan, this is the land you're inheriting. Peep the borders:'

'Your southern border is gonna include a piece of the Zin Desert next to Edom. It kicks off east of the Dead Sea, dips south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, keeps going south of Kadesh Barnea, then hits up Hazar Addar and Azmon. From there, it hooks a northwest turn to the Brook of Egypt and straight out to the Mediterranean Sea.'
'Your western border? That's easy. It's the Mediterranean Sea.'

'For the northern border, draw a line from the Mediterranean to Mount Hor. From Mount Hor, go to Lebo Hamath, link up with Zedad, keep it moving to Ziphron, and finish at Hazar Enan. Boom, that's your northern line.'

'Your eastern border starts at Hazar Enan and goes to Shepham. Then it drops south from Shepham to Riblah, east of Ain, and cruises along the hills east of the Sea of Galilee. After that, it just follows the Jordan River all the way down to the Dead Sea.'
'And that's it. Your land, all four borders locked in.'

Moses then tells the Israelites, 'Alright people, this is the land. We're divvying it up by lottery. God's orders are for it to go to the nine and a half tribes. Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh already got their spot; those two and a half tribes got their land east of the Jordan near Jericho, on the sunrise side.'

God then tells Moses, 'These are the guys who will be in charge of handing out the land: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun. And get one leader from each tribe to help them out. Here's the squad:'
'Caleb son of Jephunneh from the tribe of Judah;'
'Shemuel son of Ammihud from the tribe of Simeon;'
'Elidad son of Kislon from the tribe of Benjamin;'
'Bukki son of Jogli, the leader from the tribe of Dan;'
'Hanniel son of Ephod, the leader from the tribe of Manasseh, Joseph's son;'
'Kemuel son of Shiphtan, the leader from the tribe of Ephraim, Joseph's son;'
'Elizaphan son of Parnach, the leader from the tribe of Zebulun;'
'Paltiel son of Azzan, the leader from the tribe of Issachar;'
'Ahihud son of Shelomi, the leader from the tribe of Asher;'
'Pedahel son of Ammihud, the leader from the tribe of Naphtali.'
These were the guys God commanded to handle the land assignments for the Israelites in Canaan.

Numbers.title: Murder vs. Oopsie: The OG Rules for Sanctuary Cities
paragraphs: So, God hit up Moses on the Plains of Moab, right by the Jordan near Jericho, and was like, “Tell the Israelites they need to give the Levites some towns to live in from their own inheritance. And make sure there’s a bunch of pastureland around those towns. That way, they’ll be all set with places to live and fields for their cows, sheep, and all their other animals.

“The pasture around the Levites’ towns should go out 1,500 feet in every direction from the town wall. The total area should be a square, 3,000 feet on each side—east, south, west, and north—with the town smack in the middle. Every town gets its own pasture.

“Now, six of these towns you give them will be special ‘sanctuary cities.’ If someone accidentally kills another person, they can run there for safety. On top of that, you’ll give them another forty-two towns. So, that’s 48 towns in total, with all their pastures. When you’re handing out these towns from the Israelites' land, do it proportionally. A big tribe gives more towns, a small tribe gives fewer.”

Then God said to Moses, “Tell the People of Israel, when you cross the Jordan River into Canaan, you need to set up these sanctuary cities. These are towns where someone who accidentally kills a person can go to be safe. They’re a refuge from the victim’s family member who wants revenge, so the person accused of murder doesn’t get killed before they can even go to court. You’ll set up six of these cities. Three on the east side of the Jordan, and the other three in Canaan itself. These sanctuary cities are for everyone—Israelites, foreigners, and any visitors or guests. Anyone who accidentally kills someone can run to one of these six cities.
“But, for real, if the killer used something made of iron, that’s straight-up murder. He’s a murderer, no cap, and he has to be executed.
“Or if he had a rock in his hand that was big enough to kill someone, and the person dies, that’s murder. He’s a murderer and has to be executed.
“Or if he was holding a wooden club that was heavy enough to kill, and the person dies, that’s murder. He’s a murderer and has to be executed.
“In those cases, the ‘avenger of blood’—like a family member of the victim—has the right to kill the murderer as soon as they find them. They can do it on the spot.

“And if someone shoves another person out of pure hate, or ambushes them and throws something that kills them, or gets angry and punches them to death, that’s murder. They have to be executed. The avenger has the right to kill them when they catch them.

“BUT, if someone just randomly pushes another person without any bad history between them, or they just, like, impulsively threw something, or they accidentally dropped a heavy stone tool—like a hammer or something—and it hit and killed someone they didn’t even know was there, and there’s no reason to think they had beef, then the community has to step in and judge between the killer and the avenger based on these rules. It’s the community’s job to protect the killer from the avenger. They have to send him back to the sanctuary city he ran to. He has to stay there until the High Priest dies—the one who was anointed with the holy oil. But if the killer ever leaves the sanctuary city, and the avenger finds him outside the city limits, the avenger can kill him, and it wouldn’t be considered murder.
“So, it’s super important that he stays in his sanctuary city until the High Priest dies. After the High Priest is dead, he’s free to go back to his own property.
“These are the rules for how you make judgments from now on, wherever you end up living.
“Anyone who kills someone can only be executed if there are eyewitnesses. You can’t execute someone based on just one person’s testimony.
“Don’t take bribe money for a murderer’s life. He’s guilty and deserves the death penalty. You have to execute him.
“And don’t take bribe money to let someone who fled to a sanctuary city go back home before the High Priest dies.
“Don’t mess up the land you live in. Murder makes the land dirty, and the only way to clean it up from the blood of a murder is with the blood of the murderer.
“Don’t disrespect the land you live in. I live there too—I, God, am living right there with the People of Israel.”

Numbers.title: The OG Girlbosses Who Saved Their Inheritance
paragraphs: So, the leaders of the Gilead family clan, who were descendants of Joseph, went up to Moses and the other Israelite family leaders.

They said, "Look, God told you to give out the land to the Israelites by lottery, and you were also told by God to give the inheritance of our relative Zelophehad to his daughters. But what happens if they marry a guy from another Israelite tribe? Their inheritance will be taken from our family's tribe and added to the tribe they marry into. Then, when the Year of Jubilee comes, their inheritance will get lumped in with the tribe they married into, and our family's ancestral land will be gone!"

Moses, following God's command, gave this order to the Israelites: "The tribe of Joseph has a good point. This is God's command for Zelophehad's daughters: They are free to marry anyone they want, as long as they marry within their own ancestral clan. The inheritance of the Israelites must not be passed from tribe to tribe. No, everyone must keep the tribal inheritance within the family. Every daughter who inherits land, no matter the tribe, must marry a man from her father's tribal clan. Every Israelite is responsible for making sure the inheritance stays within the ancestral tribe. No inheritance can be passed from one tribe to another; each Israelite tribe must hold on to its own land."

Zelophehad's daughters did exactly what God commanded Moses. Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, all married their cousins on their father's side. They married within the families of Manasseh, son of Joseph, and their inheritance stayed within their father's family.
These are the commands and rules that God gave through Moses to the people of Israel on the Plains of Moab, near the Jordan River across from Jericho.

Deuteronomy.title: That Time We Blew Our Shot at the Promised Land
paragraphs: Alright, so here's the deal. These are the talks Moses gave to all of Israel when they were hanging out east of the Jordan River in the middle of nowhere—the Arabah Wilderness. They were across from Suph, near Paran, Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab. Just so you know, it's an eleven-day hike from Horeb to Kadesh Barnea if you take the Mount Seir road.

So, it was the fortieth year, eleventh month, first day. Moses sat the Israelites down and told them everything God had commanded him to say. This was right after he wrecked Sihon, the Amorite king who was ruling from Heshbon, and Og, the king of Bashan who ruled from Ashtaroth in Edrei. It was there, east of the Jordan in Moab, that Moses started breaking down this whole message.
He said:

Way back at Horeb, our God told us straight up: "You've been camping at this mountain long enough. It's time to pack up and get a move on. Head for the Amorite hills and all the places people are living—the Arabah, the mountains, the foothills, the Negev, the coast. All that Canaanite land, and Lebanon, all the way to the big river, the Euphrates. Look, I've basically handed you this land. Now go in and take it. It's the same land God promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and all their kids after them."

Back then, I told you, "Look, I can't handle all of you by myself. It's too much. Your God has made you so numerous, you're literally like the stars in the sky. And I pray that the God of your ancestors keeps it going, multiplies you a thousand times more, and blesses you just like he promised. But for real, how can I, by myself, deal with all your drama, your baggage, and your arguments? So, go pick some wise, understanding, and experienced guys from your tribes, and I'll make them your leaders."
You all answered me, "Yeah, that's a solid plan."
So I took the top guys from your tribes, the wise and experienced ones, and made them your leaders—leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, with officials for every tribe.

At the same time, I told your judges: "Listen super carefully to every complaint and argument between your fellow Israelites. Judge fairly, whether it's between two Israelites or an Israelite and a foreigner. Don't pick favorites. Treat the little guy and the big shot the same. Don't be intimidated by important people, because this is God's justice you're delivering. If a case is too hard for you, bring it to me, and I'll handle it."
I gave you orders back then for everything you'd have to deal with.

Then we left Horeb and marched toward the Amorite hill country. We went through that massive, terrifying wilderness you saw—all on God's command—and finally got to Kadesh Barnea. I told you there, "You've made it to the Amorite hill country that our God is giving us. Look, your God has put this land right in front of you as a gift. Go take it. The God of your ancestors promised it to you. Don't be scared. Don't chicken out."

But then, every single one of you came to me and said, "Hold up, let's send some spies ahead to check out the land for us. They can bring back a report on the best way to go and what the towns are like."

That actually sounded like a good idea to me, so I picked twelve guys, one from each tribe. They headed out and went up into the hills. They got to the Eshcol Valley and scoped it out. They even brought back some of the fruit from the land and told us, "The land our God is giving us is legit good!"

But then you guys totally refused to go up. You rebelled against God's clear command. You just sat in your tents and whined: "God hates us. He dragged us out of Egypt just to hand us over to the Amorites to be destroyed. It's a death sentence! How can we possibly go up there? We're trapped. Our own brothers made us lose all our nerve, telling us, 'The people there are bigger and stronger than us, their cities are huge with insane defenses—we even saw giants there!'"

I tried to calm you down: "Don't freak out. Don't be terrified of them. Your God is leading the way; he's fighting for you. You literally saw with your own eyes what he did for you in Egypt, and you saw what he did in the wilderness. You saw how your God carried you like a dad carries his kid, the whole way until you got here. But now that you're here, you won't trust your God—the same God who goes ahead of you to find a place to camp, with a fire by night and a cloud by day to show you the way."

When God heard what you were saying, he completely lost it. He swore an oath: "Not a single person from this messed-up generation is even going to see the good land I promised to give your ancestors. Not one—except for Caleb, son of Jephunneh. He'll see it. I'm giving him and his kids the land he walked on because he was 100% committed to following God, no holding back."

And guess what? I got in trouble too. Because of you, God's anger spilled over onto me. He said, "You're not getting in either. Your assistant, Joshua son of Nun, he'll go in. You need to hype him up, because he's the one who's going to lead Israel to take their inheritance. And all your little kids, the ones you said would be captured, the ones who don't even know right from wrong yet—they're the ones who will get in. I'm giving the land to them. They'll be the new owners. But not you. Turn around and go back into the wilderness, the way you came, toward the Red Sea."

Then you had the nerve to say, "We've sinned against God. We'll go up and fight, we'll follow all the orders our God commanded." You all grabbed your weapons and got ready for battle—you thought it would be a piece of cake to take those hills!
But God told me, "Tell them, 'Don't do it. Don't go up to fight. I'm not with you on this. Your enemies will absolutely crush you.'"

I told you, but you wouldn't listen. You rebelled against God's plain and simple word. You puffed out your chests and swaggered into the hills. And the Amorites who lived in those hills swarmed you like a hive of angry bees. They chased you all the way from Seir to Hormah and handed you a stinging defeat. You came back and cried your eyes out before God, but he didn't pay you any attention. God basically ghosted you. You ended up staying in Kadesh for a long, long time—pretty much as long as you had stayed there before.

Deuteronomy.title: The 40-Year Detour to the Promised Land
paragraphs: So, we turned back and headed into the wilderness toward the Red Sea, just like God told me. We spent a super long time wandering around the hills of Seir.

Then God said, “You’ve been circling these hills long enough; go north. Tell the people, ‘You’re about to pass through the territory of your relatives, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They’re scared of you, but you need to chill. Don’t start a fight with them. I’m not giving you any of their land, not even a tiny piece, because I’ve given the hill country of Seir to Esau as his own. You have to pay them for any food you eat and any water you drink.”’

For real, the Lord your God has blessed you in everything you’ve done. He’s watched over you as you’ve traveled through this massive wilderness. For forty years, the Lord your God has been with you, and you haven’t lacked a single thing.
So we went around our relatives, the descendants of Esau who live in Seir. We avoided the Arabah road that goes up from Elath and Ezion-geber and instead took the road through the wilderness of Moab.
God told me, “Don’t mess with the Moabites or start a fight with them, because I’m not giving you any of their land. I’ve given Ar to the descendants of Lot as their possession.”

The Emites used to live there—a strong and numerous people, as tall as the Anakites. They were also considered Rephaites, just like the Anakites, but the Moabites called them Emites. The Horites also used to live in Seir, but the descendants of Esau drove them out and destroyed them, taking their place, just as Israel did in the land the Lord gave them.
God said, “Okay, now it’s time to cross the Zered Valley.” So we crossed the Zered Valley.

It took us thirty-eight years to go from Kadesh Barnea to the Zered Valley. That’s how long it took for the whole generation of fighting men to die off from the camp, just as the Lord had sworn they would. The Lord’s hand was against them until he had completely removed them from the camp.

When the last of these fighting men had died, God said to me, “Today you are to cross the border of Moab at Ar. When you get near the Ammonites, don’t bother them or start a fight with them, because I’m not giving you any of their land. I’ve already given it to the descendants of Lot as their possession.” That area is also considered the land of the Rephaites, who used to live there. The Ammonites called them Zamzummites—a strong and numerous people, as tall as the Anakites. God destroyed them, and the Ammonites moved in and took their place. It was the same for the descendants of Esau who live in Seir—God destroyed the Horites who lived there before them, and they took their place, as you can see today. As for the Avvites who lived in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorites from Crete wiped them out and settled in their place.

“Get ready and cross the Arnon Ravine. Look, I’ve handed over Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land to you. Go ahead and take it. Start a war with him. From this day on, I will make all the people around here terrified of you. They will hear reports about you and will tremble and be in anguish because of you.”

From the wilderness of Kedemoth, I sent messengers to King Sihon of Heshbon with a peaceful offer: “Let us pass through your country. We’ll stay on the main road and won’t turn off to the right or to the left. We will pay you for any food we eat and water we drink. Just let us pass through on foot.
“The descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar let us do this. We just need to get across the Jordan into the land the Lord our God is giving us.”
But King Sihon of Heshbon refused to let us pass. The Lord your God made him stubborn and hard-hearted so that he could hand him over to you, as you can see has now happened.
Then God said to me, “Look, I’ve started to hand Sihon and his land over to you. Go ahead and take possession of his land.”

Sihon and his whole army came out to fight us at Jahaz. God handed him over to us, and we defeated him, his sons, and his whole army. We captured all his cities at that time and completely destroyed them—men, women, and children. No one was left alive. We only took the livestock and the loot from the cities we captured for ourselves. From Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Ravine and the town in the ravine, all the way to Gilead, not a single town was too strong for us. The Lord our God gave them all to us.
The only land you didn’t go near, following God’s command, was the land of the Ammonites, the land along the Jabbok River and around the cities in the hill country.

Deuteronomy.title: Taking Down King Og's Giant Kingdom
paragraphs: So, we changed direction and headed up the road to Bashan. That's when King Og of Bashan and his whole crew rolled out to fight us at Edrei.

But God told me, "Don't even sweat it. I'm handing him, his entire army, and all his land over to you. You're gonna do to him exactly what you did to Sihon, the Amorite king who was ruling from Heshbon."

And boom, just like that, our God handed King Og of Bashan over to us—Og and all his people. We totally wrecked them, like, no survivors. We also captured all his cities at the same time. Out of sixty cities, we didn't miss a single one. We took the entire region of Argob, which was Og's kingdom in Bashan. These were all fortress cities with massive walls and locked gates. There were also a bunch of smaller villages without walls. We went in and completely destroyed them, like a holy mission. It was the same move we pulled on King Sihon of Heshbon—a total wipeout of every city, every man, woman, and child. But we kept all the animals and the loot from the cities for ourselves.

During that whole time, we took over the land from the two Amorite kings who were running things east of the Jordan River, all the way from the Arnon Brook to Mount Hermon. (The Sidonians call Hermon "Sirion," and the Amorites call it "Senir.") We captured all the towns on the plateau, everything in Gilead, and all of Bashan, all the way to Salecah and Edrei, which were the border towns of Og's kingdom in Bashan.

King Og of Bashan was actually the last of the Rephaites, who were like giants. His bed was made of iron and was insane—over 13 feet long and 6 feet wide. You can still go see it in Rabbah, the city of the Ammonites.
So, from the land we took, I gave the tribes of Reuben and Gad the area north of Aroer along the Arnon Brook, plus half of the hill country of Gilead with its towns.
I gave the other half of Gilead and all of Bashan (which was Og's kingdom) to the half-tribe of Manasseh. This included the whole Argob region, which used to be called the Land of the Rephaites.

Jair, one of Manasseh's descendants, took over the Argob region all the way to the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites. He even named the villages in Bashan after himself, calling them Havvoth Jair, which means "Jair's Tent-Villages." They're still called that today.
I gave Gilead to Makir.

And to the tribes of Reuben and Gad, I gave the land from Gilead down to the Arnon Brook (the middle of the brook was the boundary line) and as far as the Jabbok River, which was the border with the Ammonites. The western border was the Jordan River in the Arabah valley, stretching from the Sea of Galilee all the way down to the Dead Sea, right at the base of Mount Pisgah on the east.

I gave you guys this command back then: "Your God has given you this land to own. All your fighting men, armed and ready, have to cross the river ahead of your fellow Israelites. Only your wives, kids, and livestock (and I know you have a ton of livestock) can stay behind in the towns I've already given you. You'll wait until God gives your brothers a place to live, just like he did for you, and they've taken over the land west of the Jordan that God is giving them. After that, you can all come back to the land I've given you here."

I also told Joshua, "You saw with your own eyes what your God did to those two kings. Well, God's gonna do the same thing to all the kingdoms you're about to face across the river. Don't be scared of them. Your God is fighting for you."

Around that same time, I was basically begging God. I was like, "God, my Master, you've shown me the beginning of your greatness and power—I mean, what god in heaven or on earth can pull off the stuff you do! So please, just let me cross the river and see that amazing land on the other side, the beautiful hills and the Lebanon mountains."

But God was still mad at me because of what you all did. He wouldn't hear it. He just said, "That's enough. Don't say another word about it. Go climb to the top of Mount Pisgah and look west, north, south, and east. Get a good look at the land with your own eyes, because you are not crossing the Jordan.

"Instead, go give Joshua his orders. Build up his courage and make him strong. He's the one who will lead this people across the river. He's the one who will make them inherit the land that you can only look at."
And that's why we've been camping out in this valley near Beth Peor.

Deuteronomy.title: God's Top Rules: Don't Mess This Up
paragraphs: Alright Israel, listen up. I'm about to drop some serious rules on you that I'm teaching you to follow. If you do, you'll get to live and go in and take over the land that God, the God of your ancestors, is giving you. Don't add a single word to what I'm commanding you, and don't take anything away either. Just stick to the commands of God, your God, that I'm giving you.

You literally saw with your own eyes what God did at Baal Peor. He completely wiped out every single person from your group who got involved in the messed-up parties for Baal Peor. But you guys, the ones who held on tight to God, your God, you're all still here, alive and well today.

Yo, pay attention. I'm teaching you the rules and regulations that God himself commanded me, so you can live by them in the land you're about to go in and own. Keep them. Actually do them. It'll make you look super wise and smart. When other people hear about these rules, they'll be like, 'Wow, what a great nation! They're so wise and understanding. We've never seen anything like it.'

For real, what other big nation has gods that are as close to them as our God is to us? He's always there, ready to listen whenever we call. And what other great nation has rules and laws as good and fair as this whole set of teachings I'm laying out for you today?

Just make sure you stay focused. Keep a close watch on yourselves. Don't you dare forget a single thing you've seen. Don't let your mind wander. Stay sharp for your whole life. And make sure you teach everything you've seen and heard to your kids and your grandkids.

Remember that day you stood before God, your God, at Horeb? God told me, 'Get the people together in front of me to hear my words. I want them to learn to have a healthy respect for me as long as they live in the land, and then they'll teach the same things to their children.'

You all gathered around and stood at the base of the mountain. The mountain was blazing with fire, shooting flames way up into the sky. It was super dark with thick clouds. Then God spoke to you from the middle of the fire. You heard the sound of words, but you didn't see anything—no shape, just a voice. He announced his covenant, the Ten Commandments, which he ordered you to live by. Then he wrote them down on two stone tablets.
And right then, God commanded me to teach you the rules and regulations you have to live by in the land you're about to cross the Jordan River to take over.

On the day God spoke to you at Horeb from the fire, you didn't see any kind of form. Remember that. Be super careful so you don't get corrupted and make some kind of idol, carving a statue that looks like a man or a woman, or like some animal on the ground, or a bird in the sky, or a snake on the ground, or a fish in the water. And also be careful that you don't look up at the sky and see the sun, the moon, and the stars—all the stuff up there—and get tempted to bow down and worship them. God put them there for everyone in the world to see. But you? God grabbed you right out of an iron furnace, out of Egypt, to make you the people who are his own special inheritance—and that's exactly what you are today.

But God was mad at me because of you guys and the things you said. He swore that I would never cross the Jordan River and never enter the good land that God, your God, is giving you as your own. This means I'm going to die here in this land. I'm not crossing the Jordan. But you guys will cross it, and you'll take over that good land.

So stay alert. Don't forget for one second the covenant that God, your God, made with you. And don't make any carved idols, no shapes of any kind—God, your God, was crystal clear when he commanded you not to. God, your God, is not someone to be played with—he's like a consuming fire, a jealous God.

When the time comes that you have kids and grandkids, and you've been in the land for a long time and start taking things for granted, if you then get corrupt and make any kind of carved idol, no matter what it looks like, doing what is straight-up evil in God's eyes and making him angry—I'm calling it right now, with Heaven and Earth as my witnesses, it will be game over for you. You'll get kicked out of the land you're about to cross the Jordan to own. Seriously, your time there will be super short. You'll be completely wrecked. God will scatter you all over the place; only a few of you will survive here and there in the nations where God sends you. There you can worship your homemade gods all you want, your awesome gods of wood and stone that can't see or hear or eat or smell.

But even from there, if you start looking for God, your God, you'll be able to find him if you're actually serious about it, searching for him with your whole heart and soul. When you're in trouble and all this terrible stuff is happening to you, in the future you will come back to God, your God, and actually listen to what he says. God, your God, is a super compassionate God. In the end, he won't leave you hanging, he won't destroy you, and he won't forget the covenant he swore to your ancestors.

Go ahead, ask around. Find out what's been happening for all the years before you were born. From the day God created humans on this Earth, and from one end of the sky to the other—as far back and as far away as you can possibly imagine—has anything as huge as this ever happened? Has anyone ever heard of something like this? Has any group of people ever heard a god speaking from the middle of a fire, like you did, and lived to tell the tale?

Or has a god ever even tried to pick out a nation for himself from inside another nation by using trials, miracles, and war, showing his strong hand and reaching out his long arm, doing awesome and mind-blowing things, the way God, your God, did for you in Egypt while you were standing right there watching?

You were shown all of this so you would know that God is, well, God. He's the only God. That's it. He let you hear his voice from heaven to teach you. And down on Earth, he showed you that huge fire, and you heard his words again, this time from the fire. He loved your ancestors and chose to work with their kids. He personally and powerfully brought you out of Egypt to kick out nations that were bigger and stronger than you, bringing you out and giving you their land as your inheritance. And it's happening right now. This very day.

So know this for sure. Take it to heart right now: God is in heaven above, and God is on the earth below. He's the one and only God. So, obey his rules and commands that I'm giving you today so that things will go well for you and for your kids after you—and so you'll live a long, long time in the land that God, your God, is giving you for good.

Then Moses set aside three towns on the east side of the Jordan River. These were safe places for someone who had accidentally killed a person to run to. If the killing wasn't on purpose and there was no bad history between them, the killer could run to one of these cities and be safe.
These towns were: Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau for the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead for the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan for the tribe of Manasseh.

This is the Revelation that Moses presented to the people of Israel. These are the official statements, rules, and regulations Moses gave to the Israelites after they came out of Egypt and got to the east side of the Jordan, in the valley near Beth Peor. This was the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled from Heshbon. Moses and the Israelites fought and beat him after they left Egypt and took his land. They also took the land of Og, king of Bashan. The two Amorite kings had controlled the country on the east of the Jordan, from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Brook all the way north to Mount Siyon (which is Mount Hermon), the whole Arabah plain east of the Jordan, and as far south as the Sea of the Arabah (the Dead Sea) below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.

Deuteronomy.title: God's Top 10 Rules Drop
paragraphs: Moses got all the Israelites in one place and was like, "Yo, Israel, listen up. Pay attention to the rules I'm dropping on you today. You gotta learn them and actually live by them.

Our God made a deal with us at Mount Horeb. And this wasn't just some old deal with our parents; it was with us, all of us who are here right now. God literally spoke to you from a fire on the mountain. I was the one standing between you and God, passing on his message. You were all freaked out by the fire and wouldn't go up the mountain, remember? This is what he said:
I'm your God, the one who got you out of Egypt, where you were basically slaves.
I'm your God,
who got you out of Egypt,
from that house of slavery.

It's just me, no other gods. Don't make any statues of gods, no matter what they look like—flying things, walking things, swimming things, whatever. Don't worship them or serve them, because I'm your God, and I get super jealous. I'll hold parents accountable for the messed-up stuff they pass down to their kids, even to the third and fourth generation. But for the thousands who love me and follow my rules, I'm loyal like you wouldn't believe. Don't throw my name around like it's nothing, in curses or stupid jokes; God's not gonna let that slide. Don't work on the Sabbath. Keep it special, just like God told you. You've got six days to do all your work, but the seventh day is for rest. No work for anyone—not you, your kids, your workers, your animals, or even any visitors. That way, your workers get a break too. And don't forget you were slaves in Egypt, and God pulled you out of there with some serious power. That's why he's telling you to have a day of rest. Respect your parents—God's orders! You'll live a long time, and the land God's giving you will be awesome. No killing. No cheating. No stealing. No spreading lies about people. Don't be jealous of your neighbor's wife. And don't be wanting their house, their field, their workers, their animals, or anything they own!
It's just me, no other gods.

Don't make any statues of gods, no matter what they look like—flying things, walking things, swimming things, whatever. Don't worship them or serve them, because I'm your God, and I get super jealous. I'll hold parents accountable for the messed-up stuff they pass down to their kids, even to the third and fourth generation. But for the thousands who love me and follow my rules, I'm loyal like you wouldn't believe.
Don't throw my name around like it's nothing, in curses or stupid jokes; God's not gonna let that slide.

Don't work on the Sabbath. Keep it special, just like God told you. You've got six days to do all your work, but the seventh day is for rest. No work for anyone—not you, your kids, your workers, your animals, or even any visitors. That way, your workers get a break too. And don't forget you were slaves in Egypt, and God pulled you out of there with some serious power. That's why he's telling you to have a day of rest.
Respect your parents—God's orders! You'll live a long time, and the land God's giving you will be awesome.
No killing.
No cheating.
No stealing.
No spreading lies about people.
Don't be jealous of your neighbor's wife. And don't be wanting their house, their field, their workers, their animals, or anything they own!

Those were the words God spoke to everyone at the mountain. He said it in this crazy loud voice from the fire, the cloud, and the thick smoke. And that was it. No more words. Then he carved them onto two stone tablets and gave them to me.
So, when you heard the voice coming out of that dark cloud and saw the mountain on fire, all your leaders and tribe heads came to me and said,

"Our God just showed us how amazing and powerful he is. We heard him talk from the fire today! We've seen that God can talk to people and they can actually survive. But why push our luck? This massive fire is gonna burn us up if we stick around. If we hear God's voice again, we're toast. For real, has anyone ever heard the voice of the living God like we did and lived to tell the tale?
"From now on, you go listen to what our God says, and then you tell us whatever he tells you. We'll listen and we'll do it."

God heard what you said to me and was like, "I heard what the people said to you. They're right—that's some good, real talk. I wish they'd always feel this way, always respecting me and following my rules; they and their kids would have a great life forever!

"Go tell them to go back to their tents. But you, you stay here with me so I can give you all the commands and rules that you have to teach them. That way, they'll know how to live in the land I'm giving them."

So, be super careful to do exactly what God tells you. Don't get sidetracked. Just walk the path God has laid out for you, so you can have a good life and live for a long time in the land you're about to get.

Deuteronomy.title: The #1 Rule You CAN'T Forget
paragraphs: Alright, this is the main commandment, all the rules and regs that God, your God, told me to teach you so you can live it out in the land you're about to go take over. The whole point is so you'll have some serious respect for God your whole life, following all his rules that I'm giving you—you, your kids, and your grandkids—so you can all live long, awesome lives.

So listen up, Israel, and actually do what he says. If you do, you'll have a great life, a life that's totally full and blessed, just like God promised, in a land that's basically overflowing with good stuff.
Yo, Israel! Pay attention!
God is our God! He's the one and only!
Love God, your God, with your whole heart. Like, love him with everything you are, with all you've got!

Make sure these commandments I've given you today are written on your heart. Get them deep inside you, and then get them inside your kids. Talk about them wherever you are—chilling at home, walking down the street. Talk about them from the moment you wake up until you crash at night. Tie them on your hands and put them on your foreheads to remember them. Write them on the doorframes of your house and on your city gates.

When God, your God, brings you into the land he promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, you're gonna walk into huge, busy cities you didn't even build. You'll get fully furnished houses you didn't buy, find wells you didn't dig, and see vineyards and olive groves you didn't plant. When you're taking it all in, living the good life, and feeling super content, you better not forget how you got there—God was the one who rescued you from being slaves in Egypt.

Respect God, your God, on a deep level. Serve and worship only him. When you make a promise, only use his name to back it up. Don't mess around with other gods, like the ones your neighbors worship. Because God, your God, who is right there with you, is a jealous God. Don't even try to provoke him. You don't want to make him so angry he just wipes you off the face of the planet. Don't test God, your God, like you did that day at Massah, the 'Testing Place.' Be super careful to keep the commands of God, your God, and all the rules he gave you. Do what's right and good in God's eyes. That way, you'll live a good life and be able to go in and take over that amazing land God promised your ancestors, kicking out all your enemies, just like God said.

The next time your kid asks you, 'Hey, what's the deal with all these rules and regulations that God, our God, commanded?' you tell them this: 'We were basically slaves to the king in Egypt, and God came in with some serious power and got us out of there. We saw it with our own eyes—God pulled off these insane miracle-signs and crazy wonders, bringing down judgment on Egypt, on Pharaoh, and his whole crew. He pulled us out of that mess so he could bring us here and give us the land he swore to our ancestors. That's why God told us to follow all these rules, so we would always live with respect for God, our God, as he gives us this good life and keeps us going for a long, long time.'
'It's how we get our lives right and put everything together. We just have to make sure we follow this entire commandment in front of God, our God, exactly like he told us to.'

Deuteronomy.title: God's Chosen People: No Cap, You're Special
paragraphs: Alright, so check it. When God, your God, brings you into the land you're about to take over, He's gonna clear out all the big shots that were there before you: the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. Yeah, those seven nations are way bigger and stronger than you, but don't even trip. God's got your back. He's gonna hand them over to you, and you're gonna totally own them. You have to completely wipe them out, like a holy reset.
Don't even think about making deals with them.
No exceptions, no mercy.

And definitely don't start marrying their people. Don't give your daughters to their sons, and don't take their daughters for your sons. Before you know it, you'll be worshiping their fake gods, and God will get super mad and just delete you.
Here's the game plan:
Tear down their altars, smash their weird pillars, chop down their gross sex-and-religion trees, and burn all their carved-up idols.
Why? Because you're a special crew, set apart for God, your God. He literally chose you out of everyone on Earth to be His personal treasure. That's some VIP treatment right there.

It's not like God picked you because you were this huge, popular group. Lowkey, you guys were pretty small-time. He did it all out of love, because He promised your ancestors. God swooped in and saved you from being slaves in Egypt, freeing you from that psycho Pharaoh. So you better know this: God, your God, is the real deal. He's a God you can count on. He keeps His promises of loyal love for a thousand generations to those who love Him and follow His rules. But for those who hate Him? He pays them back, and it's not pretty. He's not slow about it either; He pays them right on time.
So, stick to the commands and rules I'm giving you today. Just do it.
And here's what's up: if you obey these rules and follow them, God will keep His promise of loyal love that He made with your ancestors.
He'll love you, bless you, and make your crew grow.

He'll bless you with lots of kids, and your farms will be overflowing with grain, new wine, and oil. Your cows will have calves, and your sheep will have lambs, all in the land He promised your ancestors. You'll be more blessed than anyone else. No one in your group, not even your animals, will have trouble having babies. God will keep you healthy and get rid of all sickness. And all the nasty stuff you went through in Egypt? He's not gonna put that on you, but on everyone who hates you.
You're gonna crush all the nations that God, your God, gives you. Don't feel bad for them. And whatever you do, don't worship their gods. That's a trap, for real.

I know what you're thinking: 'Whoa, there are way more of them than us! We'll never beat them!' But listen, don't be scared. Remember what God, your God, did to Pharaoh and all of Egypt. You saw it with your own eyes: the miracles, the crazy signs, God's mighty hand reaching out and pulling you out of there. Well, God's gonna do the same thing to these people you're so scared of now.
And just for fun, He's gonna send hornets after them until every last person hiding is gone.

So don't be intimidated. God, your God, is with you—He's a majestic and awesome God. He'll get rid of these nations for you, little by little. You can't just wipe them all out at once, or the wild animals will take over. But God will clear them out for you. He'll make them panic until there's nothing left. He'll hand their kings over to you, and you'll erase them from history. No one will be able to stand against you; you'll finish them all.

And make sure you burn all their carved gods. Don't be greedy and take the silver and gold off them for yourselves—you'll get trapped by it for sure. God hates it; it's a total abomination to Him. And don't even think about bringing one of those disgusting things into your house, or you'll end up just like it, totally destroyed. No way. It's forbidden. Hate it. Despise it. Destroy it and keep things holy for God.

Deuteronomy.title: Don't Forget Who Got You Here
paragraphs: Alright, listen up. You gotta follow every single rule I'm giving you today. Do that, and you'll not only live, but you'll thrive. You'll get to move into that amazing land God promised your ancestors and actually own it. And don't you forget the journey God put you on for the last 40 years in the desert. He was totally pushing you to your limits, testing you to see what you were really made of, to see if you'd actually stick to his commands or just bail. He let things get tough. He let you get hungry. But then, He hooked you up with manna—this food you and your parents had never even heard of. Why? To teach you that people don't just live on food alone; we live on every single word that comes from God. I mean, for 40 years your clothes didn't fall apart and your feet didn't even get blisters. Deep down, you learned that God disciplines you just like a dad disciplines his kid.

So, it's super important that you stick to the commands of your God, walk the paths he shows you, and give him the respect he deserves. God's about to lead you into a seriously good land. It's a place with streams, rivers, springs, and lakes, with water flowing from the hills and through the valleys. It's a land full of wheat and barley, grapevines, fig trees, and pomegranates, plus olive oil and honey. It's a place where you'll never be hungry—there will always be food on the table and a roof over your head. It's a land where you can literally get iron from rocks and mine copper from the hills.
When you've eaten and you're full, make sure you thank God, your God, for the awesome land he's given you.

Seriously, don't forget your God by ignoring his commands, rules, and regulations that I'm giving you today. Make sure that when you've eaten and you're satisfied, when you build nice houses and settle down, when you see your herds and flocks getting huge and the money rolling in, when you watch your whole lifestyle leveling up—make sure you don't get so full of yourself and all your stuff that you forget God, your God.

He's the God who rescued you from being slaves in Egypt. The God who led you through that massive, terrifying wilderness—that dry, empty wasteland crawling with poisonous snakes and scorpions. The God who made water gush out of a hard rock for you. The God who gave you manna to eat in the desert, something your ancestors had never even heard of, all to give you a taste of the hard life and test you, so you'd be ready to live well in the future.

If you start thinking, "I did all this by myself. I'm rich. It's all mine!"—you better think again. Remember that it was God, your God, who gave you the power to get all this wealth, to confirm the promise he made to your ancestors—and that's still true today.

But if you forget—if you actually forget your God and start chasing after other gods, serving and worshiping them, I'm telling you right now, loud and clear: that's the end for you. I'm not kidding—total destruction. You'll be doomed, just like the nations God is wiping out before you. And it'll be because you wouldn't listen to the voice of God, your God.

Deuteronomy.title: Don't Get It Twisted, Israel
paragraphs: Alright, listen up, Israel!

Today's the day you're crossing the Jordan River to go in and take over nations that are way bigger and stronger than you. We're talking huge cities with fortress walls that are basically skyscrapers, and legit giants, the descendants of the Anakites—you've heard the stories, you know the saying, "Nobody can take on an Anakite."

But know this today: GOD, your God, is going ahead of you across the river, and He's like a consuming fire. He's going to crush these nations and put them under your control. You're going to kick them out and wipe them out super fast, just like God promised you.

But when God pushes them out for you, don't get it twisted and start thinking, "Wow, God brought me in here to take over these nations because I'm so good and righteous." Nah, the real reason is because of how wicked these other nations are. Seriously, it has nothing to do with how good you are or what amazing track record you have. It's because these nations are so messed up that GOD, your God, is kicking them out for you, so He can keep the promise He made to your ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

Get this and never forget it: It's not because you're so righteous that God is giving you this awesome land to own. Not even close! You guys are stubborn as anything. Just remember and don't ever forget how much you ticked off GOD, your God, in the wilderness. You've been complaining and fighting against God from the day you left Egypt until you got to this spot—total rebels the whole time. You made God so mad at Mount Horeb, so angry that He was about to destroy you. When I went up the mountain to get the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant God made with you, I was up there for 40 days and 40 nights straight. I didn't eat or drink anything. Then God gave me the two stone tablets, written on by the finger of God himself. They had every single word that God spoke to you from the fire on the mountain, on the day you all gathered.

At the end of those 40 days and nights, God gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant. And God said to me, "Get up and get down there, fast. Because your people, the ones you led out of Egypt, have completely messed up. It took them like, no time at all to leave the path I laid out for them and go make some cast metal idol for themselves."

God said, "I'm looking at these people, and all I see are a bunch of hardheaded, stubborn rebels. Get out of my way right now so I can destroy them. I'm about to wipe them off the face of the earth. Then I'll start over with you and make a nation that's way better and bigger than they could ever dream of being."

I turned around and started heading down the mountain—which was blazing with fire by this point—carrying the two tablets of the covenant in my arms. And that's when I saw it: There you were, sinning against GOD, your God. You had made yourselves a metal idol shaped like a calf! You had already abandoned the path God commanded you to walk on. I held up the two stone tablets and just threw them down, smashing them into a million pieces right in front of you.

Then I just threw myself down in front of God, just like I did at the beginning, for another 40 days and nights. No food, no water. I did this because of you, because of all your sins, sinning against God, doing what's evil in His eyes and making Him so angry. I was terrified of God's insane anger, his burning rage. I was sure he was going to destroy you. But, once again, God listened to me. And Aaron! God was so furious with Aaron—He was ready to destroy him too. But I prayed for Aaron at the same time.

And that sin-thing you made, that calf-idol, I took it and burned it in the fire, then pounded it and ground it up until it was just fine dust, and then I threw the dust into the stream that flows down the mountain.
And don't forget about what happened at Taberah (which means Blaze), Massah (Testing-Place), and Kibroth Hattaavah (Graves-of-the-Craving)—all more times you made God furious with you.

And the most recent time was when God sent you out from Kadesh Barnea, telling you: "Go. Take the land that I'm giving you." And what did you do? You rebelled. You straight-up rebelled against the clear orders of GOD, your God. You refused to trust him. You wouldn't obey him. You've been rebels against God since the very first day I met you.

When I was on my face, laid out before God for those 40 days and nights after God said He was going to destroy you, I prayed to God for you, "My Master, GOD, please don't destroy your people, your own inheritance that you redeemed with your incredible generosity, using your massive strength to get them out of Egypt.

"Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Don't get hung up on how stubborn this people is, their evil and their sin. Otherwise, the Egyptians you rescued them from will say, 'God couldn't do it; He got tired and wasn't strong enough to bring them to the land He promised. He just ended up hating them and ditched them in the wilderness to die.'
"They are still your people, your inheritance that you rescued with your power and sovereignty."

Deuteronomy.title: God's Plan B: The Ten Commandments Reboot
paragraphs: God was like, “Okay, carve out two stone tablets just like the first ones. Climb the mountain and meet me here. Also, make a wooden chest. I’m going to write the same words on these tablets that were on the ones you shattered. Then you’ll put them in the chest.”

So I made a chest from acacia wood, shaped two new stone tablets exactly like the first ones, and climbed the mountain with them in my arms. He engraved the tablets with the same stuff as before—the Ten Commandments that he spoke to you from the fire on the day of the big assembly. Then God gave them to me. I turned around, came down the mountain, and put the tablets in the chest I had made. They’ve been in there ever since, just like God told me to do.

The people of Israel traveled from the wells of the Jaakanites to Moserah. That's where Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar took over as priest. From there, they went to Gudgodah, and then to Jotbathah, a place with a bunch of streams.

That’s when God set aside the tribe of Levi for a special job: to carry the Ark of the Covenant, to be on duty in God's presence, to serve him, and to give blessings in his name, which they still do today. And that’s why the Levites don’t get their own piece of land like their relatives. God is their inheritance, just like your God promised them.
I stayed up on the mountain for forty days and nights, just like the first time. And God listened to me again, just like before. He decided not to wipe you out.
God told me, “Alright, get up. Lead the people so they can continue their journey and take over the land I swore to their ancestors I would give them.”

So, Israel, what does God actually want from you? It’s pretty simple: Respect him and live in his presence, follow the path he lays out for you, love him, and serve your God with everything you’ve got. Follow the commands and rules I’m giving you today—it’s for your own good, so you can live a good life.

I mean, look around. Everything belongs to God—the sky, the universe, the earth, and everything on it. But out of all the people in the world, it was your ancestors that God fell in love with. And he chose their kids—that’s you!—from all the nations. And that’s where we’re at right now. So, for real, drop the attitude and stop being so stubborn. Your God is the God of all gods, the Master of all masters. He's a huge, powerful, and awesome God. He doesn’t pick favorites or take bribes. He makes sure orphans and widows are treated right, and he shows love to foreigners by making sure they have food and clothes.

You have to treat foreigners with that same love—don't forget, you were once foreigners in Egypt. Seriously respect your God, serve him, stick close to him, and when you make a promise, make it in his name. He’s the one you should be praising! He’s your God! He’s the one who did all those incredible, mind-blowing things you saw with your own eyes.
When your ancestors went to Egypt, there were only seventy of them. And now, look at you—you’re as numerous as the stars in the sky. Your God did that.

Deuteronomy.title: The Ultimate Choice: Blessings or Curses?
paragraphs: Alright, so here's the deal: Love your God. Like, for real. Pay attention to his rules and stick to his commands, always.

Look, this is about YOU, not your kids. They weren't there to see all the wild stuff God did. They didn't see the miracles, they didn't get the life lessons, they didn't witness His awesome power. They missed how He totally owned Pharaoh and all of Egypt, how He dealt with their entire army, horses and chariots, by literally burying them in the Red Sea when they were chasing you. God just wiped them out. And here you are, still standing. Your kids also didn't see how God had your back in the wilderness all this time, or what He did to Dathan and Abiram. You know, when the ground just opened up and swallowed them, their families, their tents, everything—gone, right from the middle of everyone. No, it was YOU. Your own eyes saw every single incredible thing God did.

So now it's your job to follow every single command I'm giving you today. That'll give you the strength to go in and conquer the land you're about to cross into. Obey, and you'll get to live a long, full life in the land God promised your ancestors and their kids—a land that's basically overflowing with good stuff, like milk and honey.

The land you're about to take over isn't like Egypt where you came from, where you had to work your butt off just to water your crops. Nah, this new land is full of mountains and valleys, and it gets its water straight from the sky when it rains. It's a land that God Himself takes care of—He's the head gardener, keeping an eye on it 24/7, all year long.

So if you actually listen and obey the commands I'm giving you today—to love your God and serve him with your whole heart—He'll make sure the rain comes right on schedule, in the fall and spring. That means you'll get to harvest your grain, grapes, and olives. He'll even make sure your animals have plenty of grass to eat. You'll have more than enough food.

But you gotta stay sharp. Don't get sidetracked and start worshipping other fake gods. If you do, God will get seriously angry. He'll shut off the rain, your fields will dry up, and you'll be starved out of this amazing land He's giving you in no time.

Lock these words in your heart. Get them deep inside you. Tie them to your hands, wear them on your forehead—do whatever it takes to remember. Teach them to your kids. Talk about them all the time, whether you're chilling at home or walking down the street. From the moment you wake up to when you crash at night. Write them on your doorframes and city gates. Do this, and you and your kids will live long, blessed lives in the land God promised your ancestors—a promise that'll last as long as the sky is above the earth.

For real. If you're diligent and keep all these commands I'm giving you—love your God, do what He says, and stick close to Him—then God will clear out all the nations in your way. Yeah, He'll get rid of nations way bigger and stronger than you. Every single place you step will be yours. Your territory will stretch from the desert all the way to the mountains of Lebanon, from the Euphrates River to the Mediterranean Sea. No one will be able to stop you. God will make sure everyone is terrified of you, just like He promised.
So today, I'm giving you a choice: Blessing or Curse.
The Blessing: if you listen and obey the commands of your God that I'm giving you today.
The Curse: if you ignore the commands of your God and stray from the path I'm setting for you, chasing after other gods you don't even know.

Here's what's next: When God brings you into the land you're going to take over, you need to announce the Blessing from Mount Gerizim and the Curse from Mount Ebal. You'll find them after you cross the Jordan River, just follow the road west, past the Canaanite towns in the valley near Gilgal and the big oak trees of Moreh.
You're about to cross the Jordan to go in and take the land your God is giving you. So be ready. Pay attention and follow all the rules and regulations I'm laying out for you today.

Deuteronomy.title: God's Place vs. Fake Shrines
paragraphs: Alright, listen up. These are the rules you gotta follow for as long as you're living in the land that God, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.

Go in and absolutely wreck all the places where the nations you're kicking out worship their gods. Doesn't matter if it's on a hill, a mountain, or under some trees—tear it all down. Smash their altars, break their weird pillars, burn their shrines, and get rid of their carved idols. Erase the names of those fake god spots completely.
And for real, stay away from those places. Don't let the messed-up stuff they did there mess up how you worship the real God, your God.

Instead, you need to find the one place that God, your God, will choose. He'll put His name there, and it'll be the central spot for all the tribes of Israel. That's where you'll gather. You'll bring your offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, your special gifts, the offerings you promised, your freewill gifts, and the firstborn of your animals. You'll have a feast there with God, your God, and celebrate all the awesome things you and your families have accomplished because God blessed you.

And look, you can't keep doing things the way we are now, with everyone just doing their own thing. You haven't reached the final destination yet—the place of rest, the inheritance that God, your God, is giving you. But as soon as you cross the Jordan River and settle in the land God is giving you, He'll give you peace from all your enemies. You'll finally be able to live in safety.

From that point on, you have to bring everything I'm commanding you to the one place God chooses to put His name. That's where you'll bring your offerings, sacrifices, tithes, special gifts, and the best of what you promised to God. You'll celebrate there in God's presence—you, your kids, your servants, and even the Levites who live in your towns, since they don't have their own land.

Be super careful: don't just offer your sacrifices wherever you feel like it. Only offer them in the one place God chooses in one of your tribal areas. That's the only place you're supposed to bring everything I'm commanding you.

But it's totally cool to eat meat in your own towns. You can butcher animals like gazelle and deer and eat as much as you want, with God's blessing. It doesn't matter if you're ceremonially clean or not—everyone can eat it.

Just one rule: you can't eat the blood. You have to pour it out on the ground like water. Also, you can't eat the tithe of your grain, wine, or oil there in your own towns. Same goes for the firstborn of your herds, any offerings you promised, your freewill gifts, or your special contributions. You have to eat all of that stuff in the presence of God, your God, at the place He chooses. You, your family, your servants, and the Levites in your town will celebrate together before God for all the good stuff you've accomplished.
And make sure you never, ever forget to take care of the Levites as long as you live in your land.

When God, your God, makes your territory bigger like He promised, and you're craving some meat, you can go ahead and eat as much as you want. If the special place God chose is too far away, it's fine to butcher animals from your herds that God has given you, just like I said. You can eat as much as you want in your own towns. Just like you'd eat a gazelle or a deer, anyone can eat it, whether they're considered 'clean' or 'unclean.'

But seriously, no blood. Don't eat the blood. The blood is the life, and you shouldn't eat the life with the meat. Don't eat it; pour it on the ground like water. If you don't eat it, things will go well for you and your kids after you. Just do what's right in God's eyes.

And one more thing: take your holy offerings and the things you've vowed to give, and bring them to the place God chooses. You'll offer your sacrifices—the meat and the blood—on the altar of your God. Pour the blood on the altar, and then you can eat the meat.
Pay close attention and obey all these things I'm telling you. If you do what is good and right in the eyes of God, your God, you and your kids will have a good life for a long, long time.

When God, your God, gets rid of the nations whose land you're about to take, and you move in and settle down, be careful. Don't get curious about their gods after they're gone. Don't start thinking, 'I wonder how they worshiped their gods. Maybe I should try it.' Don't do that to your God. They did all sorts of disgusting things for their gods that God absolutely hates. They even burned their own kids as sacrifices! It's wild.
So, make sure you do everything I command you, exactly how I command it. Don't add anything to it, and don't take anything away.

Deuteronomy.title: Don't Get Played by Fake Prophets
paragraphs: So, if some prophet or psychic dude shows up in your town and calls out a miracle or some wild sign, and the crazy thing they predicted actually happens, and then they're like, “Yo, let’s go worship these other gods” (gods you've literally never heard of), “let’s serve them,” you better not listen to a word that prophet or psychic says. Your God is just testing you to see if you're legit, to see if you love him with your whole heart and soul. You gotta follow ONLY your God, give him mad respect, keep his commands, actually listen when he talks, serve him—and hold on to him like your life depends on it.

And that prophet or psychic? They gotta be taken out. No cap. They told you to rebel against your God, the one who bailed you out of Egypt and saved you from a life of slavery, and who told you exactly how to live. You gotta get that toxic influence out of your squad.

And if your own brother, your son or daughter, or even the wife you love or your literal BFF comes to you on the low and whispers, “Hey, let’s go worship some other gods” (gods you and your ancestors knew nothing about, gods of the people around you, whether they're close by or on the other side of the world), don’t you dare go along with them. Don't even listen. Don't feel sorry for them, don't cover for them. You have to end them. For real, kill them. You have to be the first one to act, then the whole community has to jump in. Stone them 'til they're dead. They tried to make you turn your back on your God, the one who got you out of slavery in Egypt.
Every single person in Israel will hear about it and be shook. No one will ever dare to pull a stunt like that again.

If you hear a rumor from one of the towns God is giving you, and it says that some sketchy people have shown up and convinced some of the locals to dip, saying, “Let’s go worship other gods” (gods you know nothing about), then you gotta do a full-on investigation. Ask questions, dig deep. If it turns out the rumor is true and this messed-up thing really happened in your community, you have to execute everyone in that town. Take them all out and set the whole place aside for God—the city, everything in it, even the animals. Pile up all their stuff in the main square and burn it all—the town and all the loot—as a holy offering to your God. Let it stay a pile of ruins forever. Don't ever build there again. And don't even think about pocketing any of the stuff that was supposed to be destroyed. Get rid of it all so God can switch from being angry to being compassionate, and so he can bless you and make you prosper, just like he promised your ancestors.
Yeah, for real. Just listen to your God. Keep all the commands I'm giving you today. Do what's right in his eyes.

Deuteronomy.title: God's Food Rules & How to Tithe
paragraphs: Yo, you're God's kids, for real. So don't go doing wild stuff like hurting yourselves or shaving your heads when you're sad about someone dying. You're a special crew, set apart for God. He literally chose you out of all the people on Earth to be his personal treasure.

Alright, let's talk about food. Don't eat anything nasty. Here's the approved list of animals: cows, sheep, goats, deer, and basically any animal that has a split hoof and chews its cud. But, you gotta say no to camels, rabbits, and rock badgers. They chew cud but don't have the split hoof, so they're considered 'unclean'. And pigs? Definitely not. They have the split hoof but don't chew cud, so they're unclean too. Don't even touch a dead pig.
For seafood, if it has fins and scales, it's all good. But if it's missing fins or scales, you can't eat it. It's unclean.
You can eat any 'clean' bird. But here's the do-not-eat list: eagles, vultures, falcons, ravens, owls, and a bunch of other birds of prey. And yeah, bats are on the no-fly list too.
Flying insects? Nah, don't eat them. But other clean winged creatures are okay.
Since you're God's holy people, don't eat anything you just find dead. But you can give it to a foreigner living in your town to eat, or sell it to them.
And here's a weird one, but it's a rule: don't boil a baby goat in its mother's milk.

Every year, you need to give ten percent, a 'tithe', of everything you grow in your fields. Bring it to the place God chooses for worship, and eat your tithe of grain, wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks, in God's presence. This is how you'll learn to always have a deep respect for God. But if the place God chooses is too far away and you can't carry your tithe all that way, it's cool. God will still bless you. You can sell your tithe for money, take the cash to the place of worship, and then buy whatever you want to eat and drink - cattle, sheep, wine, whatever looks good. Then you and your family can have a feast in God's presence and have a great time.
But hey, don't forget about the Levites in your towns. They don't get their own land like you do, so make sure you take care of them.

At the end of every three years, take the tithe from that year's produce and store it up. This is for the Levites, and also for the foreigners, orphans, and widows in your community. That way, they'll have plenty to eat, and God will bless you in everything you do.

Deuteronomy.title: The Ultimate 7-Year Reset Button
paragraphs: Alright, listen up. Every seven years, you need to hit a reset button on all debts. Here's the deal: anyone who loaned money to a neighbor has to just let it go. You can't chase them down for it, because God has declared it's the year of 'All Debts Canceled.' Now, you can still collect from foreigners, but any debt from a fellow Israelite? You gotta wipe it clean.

The goal here is that there should be no one struggling among you. God is ready to pour out major blessings on you in the land He's giving you, but there's a catch: you have to actually listen to God and follow through on all the commands I'm giving you today. And yeah, God will bless you like crazy, just like He promised. You'll be the one lending to other nations, not borrowing. You'll be in charge, not the other way around.

So, if you see someone in your community who's broke or needs help, don't just look away and act like you didn't see them. Don't clutch your wallet. No, you look them in the eye, open your wallet, and lend them whatever they need, no questions asked. Don't even start with that selfish thought like, 'Ugh, but the seven-year debt cancellation is almost here!' and then ghost them. If you do that, they'll cry out to God, and you'll be caught in a major sin.

Give generously, without even thinking about it. Don't be stingy. How you handle stuff like this is what unlocks God's blessing in everything you do. The reality is, there will always be people who are poor and in need. So I'm commanding you: always be generous, with an open wallet and open hands, for your neighbors who are hurting.

Now, if a Hebrew man or woman was sold to you as a servant and works for you for six years, in the seventh year, you have to set them free. And when you do, don't just send them off with nothing. Hook them up with some animals, plenty of food and wine—load them up with the same kind of blessings God has given you. Never forget that you were slaves in Egypt, and God was the one who redeemed you.
That's why I'm commanding you to do this today.

But, if your servant says, 'I don't want to leave you,' because they genuinely love you and your family and have a good life, then you can make it official. Take a sharp tool, an awl, and pierce their earlobe against the doorpost. That marks them as your servant for life. You do the same for your female servants who want to stay.
And don't act like this is some huge burden, setting your servant free. Real talk, they've worked for you for six years for basically half the price of a regular hired worker. So it's a good deal.
Trust me, God will bless you in everything you do for this.

Also, you need to set apart all the firstborn male animals from your herds and flocks for God. Don't use the firstborn bulls for work, and don't shear the firstborn sheep for wool. Instead, you and your family are to eat them every year in a special meal in God's presence, at the place He chooses for worship. But if the animal has something wrong with it—like it's lame or blind—don't sacrifice it to God. You can just eat it at home. Anyone, whether they're considered 'clean' or 'unclean,' can eat it, just like you'd eat a gazelle or a deer. The only rule is, you absolutely cannot eat its blood. Just pour the blood out on the ground like water.

Deuteronomy.title: God's Epic Festival Guide
paragraphs: Yo, make sure you celebrate the Passover to your God in the month of Abib. That's the month God busted you out of Egypt in the middle of the night. You gotta bring your Passover sacrifice to the special place God chooses for his name to be honored. And with that sacrifice, no yeast bread, you hear? For seven days, you'll eat unleavened bread—the bread of hard times—because you bounced from Egypt in a rush. This bread will be a forever reminder of that escape.
For a whole week, not a speck of yeast should be found anywhere in your land. And whatever meat you sacrifice in the evening, don't leave any of it for the next morning.

Don't just hold the Passover sacrifice in any old town God gives you. Only do it in the one place God picks for worship. That's where you'll offer the sacrifice in the evening as the sun sets, right at the time you fled Egypt. Cook it up and eat it at that designated spot. Then, when the sun comes up, you can head back home.
For six days, you'll eat that yeast-free bread. The seventh day is a full-on holiday for God, so no work allowed.

Next up, the Feast of Weeks. Start counting seven weeks from the day you first start harvesting your grain. You'll celebrate this by bringing a freewill offering to God. Be generous, just as God has been generous with you. It's a party for everyone in God's presence: you, your kids, your servants, the Levites in your town, and the foreigners, orphans, and widows living among you. Everyone rejoices at the place God sets apart for worship.
Never forget you were slaves in Egypt. So, for real, stick to these rules.

Then there's the Feast of Booths, which you'll celebrate for seven days after you've gathered your harvest. This is another big party. You, your kids, your servants, the Levites, the foreigners, the orphans, and the widows in your town—everyone celebrates. For seven days, you'll party before God at the place he chooses. Since God has blessed your harvest and all your work, you have to go all out and celebrate big time!
