Three times a year, all the guys have to show up before God at his chosen place: for the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Booths. And don't come empty-handed. Everyone should bring a gift, as much as they can, based on the blessings God has given them.

In all the towns God is giving you, you need to appoint judges and officials for each tribe. Their job is to judge everyone fairly and with total honesty. Don't bend the rules. Don't play favorites. And absolutely no bribes—a bribe can make even the wisest person blind to the truth and mess up the plans of good people.
Justice, and only justice, is what you need to chase after! That's the only way you'll truly live and get to keep the land your God is giving you.
And one more thing, don't plant one of those Asherah trees for fertility next to the Altar of God you build. And don't set up any of those phallic pillars. God seriously hates that stuff.

Deuteronomy.title: Rules for Kings & Justice, No Cap
paragraphs: Alright, so first rule: don’t be bringing a busted-up ox or sheep as a sacrifice to your God. If it’s got any flaws, it’s a no-go. That’s like a major insult to God, for real.

And listen, if you find someone in one of the towns God is giving you who’s doing shady stuff in God’s eyes, like breaking his promises and worshipping other gods—you know, bowing down to the sun, the moon, or any of those other weird sky-gods—you gotta investigate. Like, for real, check the evidence. If it’s true, if someone’s really done something that messed up in Israel, you have to take them outside the city gates and stone them until they’re dead. Yeah, it’s that serious.

But—and this is a big but—you can only do this if there are two or three witnesses. You can’t just put someone to death because one person said so. No cap. The witnesses have to be the ones to throw the first stones, and then everyone else can join in. You gotta get that evil out of your community, period.

Now, if a case comes up that’s too tricky for you to solve—like a murder, a legal battle, or a big fight—take it to the main place of worship God has chosen. Bring it to the priests and the judge who’s on duty. Ask them, and they’ll give you the final decision.

And whatever they decide, you have to follow it. Exactly as they say. Don’t add your own spin, don’t leave anything out. If anyone gets arrogant and ignores the decision from the priest or judge who’s representing God, they’re basically signing their own death warrant. You gotta remove that person to get rid of the evil in Israel. That’ll make everyone else think twice before acting all high and mighty.

Later on, when you’ve settled in the land God is giving you, you might start saying, “Hey, we want a king, just like all the other countries.” If you do, make sure you pick the king God chooses. He has to be one of your own people—no foreigners. And this king? He can’t go crazy building up a huge army with tons of horses and chariots. He’s definitely not allowed to send people to Egypt to get more horses, because God was clear: “You’re never going back there.” Also, he can’t have a massive harem of wives who will just distract him. And he can’t be all about stacking up silver and gold.

Here’s the deal for the king: as soon as he takes the throne, his first job is to write his own copy of this law on a scroll, with the priests watching to make sure he gets it right. He has to keep that scroll with him all the time and read it every single day. This is so he learns to respect God and actually follow all these rules. He can’t get a big head and think he’s above the law, changing things whenever he feels like it. If he sticks to the script, he and his sons will have a long and successful reign in Israel.

Deuteronomy.title: How to Spot a Real Prophet vs. a Fake One
paragraphs: Alright, so check it out. The priests from the tribe of Levi, like the whole tribe, they don't get a piece of land like the rest of Israel. Instead, they get to live off the offerings people give to God. That's their inheritance. So yeah, no land for them, because God is their inheritance, which is pretty epic.

Here's the deal for what the priests get from the people's offerings, like if they bring an ox or a sheep: the shoulder, the cheeks, and the stomach. You also gotta give them the first bit of your grain, wine, and oil, and the first wool you get from your sheep. Why? Because God chose them and their kids out of all the tribes to serve him forever.

If a Levite decides to move from his town in Israel—and he's totally free to do that—and comes to the special place God chose for worship, he can serve God there just like his fellow Levites. And he gets an equal share of the food, even if he has his own money from selling his family's stuff.

When you get into the land God is giving you, don't even think about copying the messed-up things the other nations there do. Seriously, don't you dare sacrifice your own son or daughter. And stay away from stuff like fortune-telling, sorcery, witchcraft, casting spells, talking to ghosts, or trying to channel the dead. God thinks all that stuff is disgusting. That's exactly why he's kicking those nations out for you.
Just be 100% loyal to your God. Those nations you're about to kick out? They're all into sorcerers and witches. But that's not for you. God has made that super clear.

God is going to send a prophet for you. He'll be one of your own people, a prophet just like me. You have to listen to him. This is actually what you guys asked for back at Mount Horeb. You were all gathered there and said, 'We can't handle hearing God's voice directly anymore, and that fire is too much. We're gonna die!'

And God told me, 'They've got a point.' So he said, 'I'll raise up a prophet for them from their own people, someone just like you. I'll give him the words to say, and he'll tell them everything I command. And if anyone doesn't listen to the words he speaks in my name, I'll personally deal with them.'
But if some prophet fakes it, and claims to speak for me when I haven't told him anything, or speaks for other gods, that prophet has to be put to death.

So you're probably wondering, 'How can we tell if a prophet is legit or just making stuff up?' Here's the secret: if a prophet says something in God's name and it doesn't happen, then obviously God wasn't in on it. The prophet was just capping. You can totally ignore him.

Deuteronomy.title: Cities of Refuge? Lowkey Genius
paragraphs: Alright, so check it. When God, your God, boots out the other nations from the land He's giving you, and you move into their cities and houses, you gotta set aside three cities that are super easy to get to. These are gonna be your 'safe zones' in the land God's giving you.
Basically, you'll split the land into three parts and build good roads to these cities. This is so anyone who accidentally kills someone can book it over there and be safe.

Here's the rule for a killer who runs there for safety: It has to be someone who killed their neighbor completely by accident, with no bad history or beef between them. For example, say a guy goes into the woods with his neighbor to chop down a tree. He swings the axe, the head flies off the handle, and it hits and kills his neighbor. That guy can run to one of these cities and save his own life. If the city is too far, the victim's family member, who's gonna be raging, might catch him on the way and kill him, even though he didn't deserve to die. It wasn't his fault, and they were cool before. That's why I'm telling you: set up these three cities for yourselves.

Later, when God expands your territory like he promised your ancestors, giving you all the land he said he would—because you're actually following the commands I'm giving you today, which is to love God and do what he says your whole life—you'll need to add three more cities to the first three. This is to make sure no innocent person gets killed in your land. God is giving you this land as your own, and you don't want to mess it up with innocent blood and have that guilt on you.

But, on the flip side, if a guy has always hated his neighbor, sets up an ambush, attacks and kills him, and then tries to hide in one of these cities? That's a whole different story. The leaders of his own town have to send for him, bring him back, and hand him over to the victim's avenger to be executed. Don't even feel bad for him. You gotta get rid of that evil of a wrongful murder from Israel so you can all live good lives in a clean place.
Also, don't move your neighbor's property markers—the old landmarks that your ancestors set up to show what belongs to who. That's just not cool.
You can't convict someone of a crime based on just one witness. You need two or three witnesses to actually make a case stick.

If a sketchy witness comes forward to accuse someone of a crime, both people in the dispute have to go before God, with the priests and judges who are in charge at the time. The judges have to do a serious investigation. If it turns out the witness was lying and tried to frame a fellow Israelite, you give him the exact same punishment he wanted for the other person. Get that evil out of your community. When people hear about it, they'll be shook, and it'll stop that kind of thing from happening again. Don't feel sorry for the liar: the punishment has to match the crime—a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot.

Deuteronomy.title: War Rules: Who Gets a Pass?
paragraphs: Alright, so when you roll up to a battle and see the other side has way more soldiers, horses, and chariots than you, don't even trip. Remember your God, the one who got you out of Egypt, is right there with you. When it's about to go down, the priest will step up and give the troops a pep talk. He'll be like, 'Listen up, Israel! You're about to face your enemies. Don't get all shaky. No fear, no hesitation, no panicking. Your God is literally in this with you, fighting alongside you to get that W.'

Next, the officers will take the mic and say, 'Ayo, is there anyone here who just built a new house but hasn't had the housewarming party yet? You can bounce. Go home so you don't die in battle and have someone else move in. What about anyone who planted a vineyard but hasn't even tasted the wine? You can dip too, go home before you die and someone else drinks your profits. And if you're engaged but not married yet? Head home, man. You don't want to die and have some other dude marry your girl.'
The officers will keep going, 'And for real, is anyone here lowkey scared or buggin' out? It's cool, just go home. We don't need your bad vibes messing everyone else up.'
Once the officers are done with their announcements, they'll pick commanders to get the troops organized.

When you're about to attack a city, first you gotta ask, 'We cool?' If they say 'Yeah, we're cool' and open the gates, then everyone inside becomes your workforce. They gotta work for you. But if they're not about peace and want to throw down, then it's on. Go ahead and attack. Your God will hand them over to you. Take out all the guys. But the women, kids, and animals are yours to keep. You can take all the stuff in the town as loot—your God is giving it to you. This is how you handle the towns that are far away, not the ones from the nations right next door.

But for the towns that your God is giving you as your own turf, it's a whole different story: you can't leave anyone alive. It's a holy destruction kinda thing. The Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—you gotta wipe them out, just like your God commanded. This is so they don't teach you all the messed-up stuff they do for their gods, and you end up sinning against your God.

When you're laying siege to a town and it's taking forever, don't just start chopping down all the trees. Those are your future snacks, so don't cut 'em down. Like, are the trees soldiers fighting you? The only trees you can chop down are the ones that don't make food. You can use that wood to build stuff to help you take over the city until it finally gives up.

Deuteronomy.title: Murder Mysteries, War Brides & Rebel Sons? Wild Old Testament Rules
paragraphs: Okay, so get this: if someone finds a dead body just lying in a field in the land God gave you, and no one has a clue who did it, the local leaders have to measure which town is closest. The leaders of that town then have to take a young cow that's never been worked, bring it to a valley that's never been farmed, and break its neck there. Then the priests come, and all the town leaders wash their hands over the cow and have to say, 'We didn't kill this person, and we didn't see it happen. God, please forgive your people and don't hold us responsible for this murder.'
Doing this officially clears them of any guilt in the murder. By following these steps, you've done what's right in God's eyes and washed your hands of the whole situation.

When you go to war and God gives you the W, you'll probably take prisoners. If you see a beautiful woman among them and you're feeling her and want to marry her, here's the deal: you take her home, she shaves her head, cuts her nails, and gets rid of the clothes she was captured in. She then gets a full month to mourn her parents. After that, you can sleep with her and be married. But, if you're not vibing with her later on, you have to let her go free. You can't sell her or treat her like a slave, since you already humiliated her by taking her captive.

If a guy has two wives, one he loves and one he, well, doesn't, and they both have sons, but his firstborn son is from the wife he doesn't love—he can't just play favorites when it's time to give out the inheritance. He can't give the 'firstborn' title to the son of the wife he loves. Nah, he has to acknowledge the real firstborn, the son of the unloved wife, and give him a double share of everything. That son is the first proof of his manhood, so the rights of the firstborn are his, period.

If a guy has a stubborn, rebellious son who straight up refuses to listen to his parents, and even after they discipline him he still won't obey, his mom and dad are supposed to drag him to the town leaders at the city gate. They're to announce, 'This son of ours is a stubborn rebel; he won't listen to a thing we say. He's a glutton and a drunk.'
Then, all the men of the town are to stone him to death. It's about purging that evil from the community. All of Israel will hear about it and be shook.

And if someone commits a crime worthy of death and is executed and hung on a tree, you can't just leave their body hanging there overnight. You have to bury them that same day. You don't want to desecrate the land God gave you—a dead body hanging like that is considered a curse from God.

Deuteronomy.title: Respect the Drip & Other Life Hacks
paragraphs: Yo, so if you see your neighbor's ox or sheep just wandering around, don't just ghost it. You gotta return it. If they're not around or you don't know who it belongs to, just take it home and look after it until they come asking. Then give it back. Same deal if it's their donkey, their coat, or anything else they lose. Don't just ignore it.
If you see your neighbor's donkey or ox hurt on the road, don't just walk past. Help them get it up and moving again.
A girl shouldn't wear a guy's clothes, and a guy shouldn't wear a girl's clothes. God is lowkey not a fan of that kind of stuff.

If you find a bird's nest, and the momma bird is there with her babies or eggs, don't take the mom with the kids. You can take the babies, but let the mom go free. That's how you'll live a long and blessed life, for real.
When you build a new house, put a little wall around the roof so nobody falls off and dies, and your family doesn't get blamed for it.
Don't plant two different kinds of seeds in your vineyard. If you do, you'll lose everything you planted, the whole harvest.
Don't try to plow with an ox and a donkey together. It's just not a good look.
Don't wear clothes made of mixed fabrics, like wool and linen together.
Make tassels for the four corners of your cloak.

Okay, so if a guy marries a girl, sleeps with her, and then starts trashing her, saying she wasn't a virgin, this is what happens. The girl's parents take the proof of her virginity to the town leaders. The dad says, 'I gave my daughter to this guy, and now he's dissing her and spreading rumors. But look, here's the proof.' Then they show the leaders the bloody wedding sheets. The leaders will then punish the husband, fine him a hundred pieces of silver, and give it to the girl's dad. The guy messed up by giving a good Israelite girl a bad name. He has to keep her as his wife and can never divorce her.

But if the accusation is true, and there's no proof she was a virgin, the townspeople will take her to her dad's house and stone her to death. She brought shame to Israel by acting like a prostitute while still living at home. You gotta get rid of that evil from your community.
If a guy is caught sleeping with another man's wife, they both have to die. Get rid of that evil from Israel.

If a guy finds a virgin in town who's engaged to someone else and sleeps with her, you take both of them to the town gate and stone them to death. The girl dies because she didn't scream for help, and the guy dies because he violated his neighbor's fiancée. You have to get rid of that evil.

But if it happened out in the country, and the guy forced himself on her, only the guy dies. Don't do anything to the girl; she didn't do anything wrong. It's like if someone attacks and murders their neighbor in the middle of nowhere. When the engaged girl screamed for help, there was no one around to save her.

If a guy finds a virgin who's not engaged, forces himself on her, and they get caught, the guy has to pay her dad fifty pieces of silver. He has to marry her because he took advantage of her, and he can never divorce her.
A guy can't marry his dad's ex-wife. That would be a major violation of his dad's rights.

Deuteronomy.title: Who's In & Who's Out: God's Squad Rules
paragraphs: A guy who's a eunuch can't join God's crew.
Someone whose parents weren't married can't join God's crew either, and this goes for their kids for like, ten generations.

No Ammonite or Moabite can join God's crew, not even after ten generations of their families. Like, ever. It's because those guys were not cool to you when you were traveling out of Egypt. They didn't even give you food or water. And on top of that, they hired this dude Balaam to curse you. But your God, who is awesome btw, refused to listen to Balaam and flipped the curse into a blessing. That's how much God loves you! So don't even try to be friends with them or do them any favors. Ever.
But don't be a hater to an Edomite; he's your relative.
And don't hate on an Egyptian; you guys were foreigners in their country once.
Kids born to Edomites and Egyptians can join God's crew in the third generation.

When you're camped out for war against your enemies, you gotta be extra careful to stay away from anything that would make you spiritually unclean. If one of your guys has a wet dream and becomes unclean, he has to go outside the camp and stay there. In the evening, he can wash up and then come back at sunset.

You need to have a designated spot outside the camp to go to the bathroom. And you should have a small shovel with your gear. After you do your business, you have to dig a hole and cover it up. This is because your God is walking around in your camp, ready to rescue you and help you beat your enemies. So you have to keep the camp holy. Don't let anything gross or offensive be in God's sight.
A slave who runs away to you for safety? Don't send him back to his master. Let him live wherever he wants in your city, where he feels safe. And don't you dare take advantage of him.

No daughter of Israel is allowed to be a temple prostitute, and no son of Israel is allowed to be a temple prostitute either. And don't bring money earned from being a prostitute or a pimp to God's house to pay for a promise you made. God thinks both of those things are totally disgusting.

Don't charge your own people interest on a loan. Not for money, not for food, not for anything. You can charge foreigners interest, but not your own people. If you follow this, your God will bless all your work in the new land you're about to own.

When you make a promise to your God, don't wait around to do it. God expects you to keep your word, and if you don't, it's a sin. But if you don't make a promise in the first place, then it's not a sin. If you say you're gonna do something, then do it. You willingly made a promise to your God, so you better keep it.

If you're walking through your neighbor's vineyard, you can eat as many grapes as you want right there, but you can't fill up a bag to take with you. And if you're walking through your neighbor's grain field, you can pick some grain to eat, but you can't bring a sickle and start harvesting their whole field.

Deuteronomy.title: Divorce, Newlyweds, and Being a Good Person
paragraphs: Alright, so check this out. If a guy marries a girl but then decides he's not feeling it anymore because he found something about her that's a deal-breaker, he can give her official divorce papers and send her on her way. After she leaves, if she becomes another man’s wife and he also comes to hate her and this second husband also gives her divorce papers, puts them in her hand, and sends her off, or if he should die, then the first husband who divorced her can’t marry her again. She has made herself ritually unclean, and her remarriage would be an abomination in the Presence of God and defile the land with sin, this land that God, your God, is giving you as an inheritance.
When a guy gets married, he gets a whole year off from military duty or any other big responsibilities. He gets one year off simply to be at home making his wife happy.
Don't take someone's small handmill—the thing they use to make food—as collateral for a loan. You’d be seizing someone’s very life.
If someone gets caught kidnapping another Israelite to sell them into slavery, that kidnapper has to be put to death. You gotta get that kind of evil out of your community, no cap.

Heads up! If there's an outbreak of a gnarly skin disease, you have to follow the rules the priests lay down, like, to the letter. Follow them precisely as I commanded them. And don't forget what God, your God, did to Miriam when you guys were leaving Egypt.

If you loan something to your neighbor, don't just barge into their house to get what they promised as collateral. Wait outside. Let the guy you loaned to bring it out to you. And if he's really poor, don't keep his cloak overnight. Give it back to him at night so he can sleep in it and be grateful to you. God will see that as a super righteous move.

Don't take advantage of a worker who is poor and needy, whether they're a fellow Israelite or a foreigner living in your town. Pay them their wages at the end of each day; they're living paycheck to paycheck and they need it. If you don't pay them, they'll cry out to God, and you'll be in big trouble.
Parents won't be put to death for their kids' mistakes, and kids won't be put to death for their parents' mistakes. Each person is responsible for their own actions.

Make sure that foreigners and orphans get a fair shot. And don't take a widow's cloak as collateral for a loan. Never forget that you were once slaves in Egypt and God, your God, rescued you. That's why I'm telling you to do all this.

When you're harvesting your grain and you accidentally leave a bundle of it in the field, don't go back to get it. Leave it for the foreigners, orphans, and widows, so that God, your God, will bless all your work. When you're shaking the olives from your trees, don't go back and pick every single one. Leave some for the foreigners, orphans, and widows. And when you're harvesting grapes from your vineyard, don't be greedy and take every last one. Leave some for the foreigners, orphans, and widows. Never forget that you were slaves in Egypt. That's why I'm commanding you to do this.

Deuteronomy.title: Spit In His Face?! Wild Ancient Laws
paragraphs: Alright, so if two people have a legal beef, they gotta go to court. The judges will figure out who's innocent and who's guilty. If the guilty person deserves to be punished, the judge will have them lie down and get whipped for as many lashes as the crime is worth, but—and this is a big but—no more than forty. If you hit them more than forty times, you're basically disrespecting them as a human being.
Don't put a muzzle on an ox when it's helping you thresh grain. Let the big guy snack while he works.

Okay, this next part is a bit wild. If brothers are living together and one of them dies without having a son, his widow can't just go marry some random guy outside the family. Her husband's brother is supposed to step up, marry her, and fulfill his duty as a brother-in-law. The first son they have will be named after the dead husband, so his family name doesn't just disappear in Israel.

But what if the brother is like, 'Nah, I'm not into it, I don't want to marry her'? In that case, the widow goes to the city leaders at the gate and says, 'My brother-in-law is refusing to keep his brother's name alive in Israel; he won't do his duty.' Then the leaders will summon the brother and talk to him. If he's stubborn and says, 'I don't want her,' then his sister-in-law is supposed to walk up to him, pull his sandal right off his foot, spit in his face, and declare, 'This is what happens to the man who refuses to build up his brother's family!' From then on, his family will be known in Israel as 'The Family with No Sandal.' Lowkey savage.
Now, if two guys are fighting and one guy's wife tries to rescue her husband by grabbing the other man's... private parts, you have to cut off her hand. No cap, show no pity.

Don't be shady with your business. Don't carry around two different weights, a heavy one and a light one, to cheat people. And don't have two different-sized measuring cups. Use only one set of weights and measures, and make sure they're legit and honest. If you do that, you'll live a long and good life in the land God is giving you. God absolutely hates dishonest business deals and all that corruption.

And don't you ever forget what the Amalekites did to you on your way out of Egypt. Remember how they ambushed you when you were exhausted and could barely walk, and they mercilessly attacked the people lagging behind? They had zero respect for God. So, when your God gives you peace from all your enemies in the land you're about to inherit, you are to completely wipe out the memory of Amalek from the face of the earth. Do. Not. Forget.

Deuteronomy.title: First Fruits & Being God's Treasure
paragraphs: Alright, so once you get to the land God's giving you—your new home base—and you're all settled in, here's the deal. You've gotta take the very first and best stuff you grow, put it in a basket, and head over to the special place God has picked out for worship. When you get there, find the priest on duty and tell him, 'Yo, I'm officially here in the land God promised our ancestors He'd give us.' The priest will then take your basket and put it on God's altar. Then, right there in front of God, you're gonna say this:

My ancestor was basically a homeless nomad from Aram. He went down to Egypt with just a few family members, but they blew up and became this huge, powerful nation. But then the Egyptians were super abusive to us, making us slaves and treating us horribly. So we cried out to God, the God of our ancestors, and He actually listened. He saw how messed up things were for us, how much we were struggling. And then, like a superhero, God got us out of Egypt with some seriously awesome power, doing insane miracles and signs. He brought us here, to this amazing place that's literally flowing with milk and honey. So, yeah, here I am, bringing the first and best of the crops from the land you gave me, God.

After you say that, put the basket down in front of God and take a deep bow. Then it's time to party! Celebrate all the awesome stuff God has given you, your family, the Levites, and even the immigrants living among you.

Every three years, during the special 'tithe' year, you're supposed to give a tenth of everything you've harvested to the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows so they can eat and be full in your towns. Then, in front of God, you need to declare this:

I've set aside the holy portion and given it to the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows, just like you told me to. I haven't messed up or forgotten any of your commands. I didn't eat any of it while I was mourning, I didn't touch it when I was unclean, and I didn't use it for funeral stuff. I've listened to you, my God, and done everything you commanded.
Look down from your holy home in heaven and bless your people Israel and the land you gave us, just like you promised our ancestors—this land that's flowing with milk and honey.
Look down from your holy home in heaven and bless your people Israel and the land you gave us, just like you promised our ancestors—this land that's flowing with milk and honey.

Today, God is telling you to follow all these rules and live them out with your whole heart. You've basically re-upped your contract today, saying that God is your God, you'll live His way, do what He says, and listen to Him.

And today, God has confirmed that you're His special treasure, just like He promised. You're the people in charge of keeping His commandments, a people He has lifted up higher than all the other nations He made—high in praise, fame, and honor. You are a people who are holy to God. That's His promise.

Deuteronomy.title: Blessings & Curses: The Ultimate Test
paragraphs: Moses, along with the leaders of Israel, gave the people a command: "Yo, make sure you follow every single one of these rules I'm giving you today. The day you cross the Jordan River into the land God's giving you, you need to set up some huge stones and cover them with plaster. As soon as you're across, write down all the words of this Revelation on them. This is your ticket into the land God's giving you, a land that's literally flowing with milk and honey, just like the God of your ancestors promised.

So, after you cross the Jordan, set up these stones on Mount Ebal and plaster them up. Then, build an altar to your God on that mountain. Don't use any iron tools on the stones; build the altar with natural, uncut stones. You'll offer up your big-time burnt offerings to God there. And when you have your peace offerings, you'll eat them right there, just vibing in God's presence.
Make sure you write all the words of this Revelation on the stones, and write them super clearly.

Then Moses and the Levitical priests got everyone's attention and said, "Alright, listen up, Israel. Today, you've officially become the people of your God. So, you better listen to what God says and follow all the commands and rules I'm giving you today.

That same day, Moses gave another order: "After you cross the Jordan, these tribes—Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin—will stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people. And these other tribes—Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali—will stand on Mount Ebal for the curse.
The Levites will be the MCs, and they'll shout this out to all of Israel:
God's curse on anyone who makes a carved or cast idol—something God totally hates, made by some random craftsman—and sets it up in secret.
And everyone will be like, "Yes. Absolutely."
God's curse on anyone who disrespects their parents.
And everyone will be like, "Yes. Absolutely."
God's curse on anyone who messes with their neighbor's property line.
And everyone will be like, "Yes. Absolutely."
God's curse on anyone who gives bad directions to a blind person.
And everyone will be like, "Yes. Absolutely."
God's curse on anyone who denies justice to foreigners, orphans, or widows.
And everyone will be like, "Yes. Absolutely."
God's curse on anyone who sleeps with their father's wife; that's a major violation.
And everyone will be like, "Yes. Absolutely."
God's curse on anyone who has sex with an animal.
And everyone will be like, "Yes. Absolutely."
God's curse on anyone who sleeps with their sister, whether she's their half-sister or full sister.
And everyone will be like, "Yes. Absolutely."
God's curse on anyone who sleeps with their mother-in-law.
And everyone will be like, "Yes. Absolutely."
God's curse on anyone who secretly kills their neighbor.
And everyone will be like, "Yes. Absolutely."
God's curse on anyone who takes a bribe to kill an innocent person.
And everyone will be like, "Yes. Absolutely."
God's curse on anyone who doesn't actually live out the words of this Revelation.
And everyone will be like, "Yes. Absolutely."

Deuteronomy.title: Blessings & Curses: The Ultimate Consequences
paragraphs: Alright, so here's the deal. If you actually listen to what God, your God, is saying and for real obey all the commands I'm giving you today, God will put you on a whole other level, way above every other nation.
All these awesome things will happen for you and totally overflow in your life, just because you listened to God, your God:

God’s blessing in the city, God’s blessing in the countryside. You'll be blessed with kids, your fields will be poppin', your animals will have tons of babies—calves, lambs, you name it. Your pantry will be full, and your bread will always be fresh. You'll be blessed when you come home and blessed when you head out.
God will make sure any enemies that try to come for you get totally wrecked. They might roll up on you from one direction, but they'll be scattering in seven different directions when they flee.
God will command a blessing on your storage and everything you put your hands to. He'll bless you in the land he's giving you.
God will set you up as his own special crew, a holy people, just like he promised. That is, if you stick to his commands and live the way he showed you.
Then everyone on Earth will see that you're repping God's Name, and they'll have a healthy respect for you, lowkey fear even.

God will absolutely shower you with good stuff: lots of kids, healthy animals, and amazing crops from the land he swore to your ancestors he'd give you. God will crack open the sky and send rain for your land right on time and bless all your work. You'll be the one lending money to other nations, not the one needing a loan. God will make you the head, not the tail. You'll always be the top dog, never the underdog, as long as you listen up and follow the commands of God, your God, that I'm laying out for you today. Don't even think about straying from these words, not even a little, by chasing after other fake gods.

But... if you don't listen to the voice of God, your God, and don't bother to keep all the commands and rules I'm giving you today, then this is what's gonna happen. All these curses will come down on you and hit you hard:

God's curse in the city, God's curse in the country. A curse on your pantry and your food. A curse on your kids, your crops, your baby animals—all of it. A curse when you come in, and a curse when you go out.
God will send The Curse, The Confusion, and The Chaos on everything you try to do until you're just wiped out and gone—all because you did evil stuff and abandoned me.
God will hit you with a plague that will completely erase you from the land you're about to go and take over.
God will send wasting diseases, fevers, inflammation, scorching heat, drought, blight, and mildew after you. They will hunt you down until you're dead.

The sky above you will feel like it's made of iron, and the ground under you will be like a slab of bronze. God will make it rain dust and powder from the sky until you're totally buried and suffocated.

God will let your enemies defeat you. You'll march out to fight them on one road but end up running for your lives down seven different roads. You'll become a horror story for all the kingdoms of the Earth. Your dead body will be a feast for vultures and wild animals, with no one around to shoo them away.

God will strike you with the same kind of boils they had in Egypt, plus tumors, scabs, and an itch you can never scratch. He'll make you lose your mind, go blind, and be in a constant state of panic. You'll be stumbling around in broad daylight like a blind person in the dark, never getting anywhere. You'll be constantly oppressed and robbed, with no one to rescue you.

You'll get engaged to someone, but another guy will sleep with her. You'll build a house, but you'll never get to live in it. You'll plant a vineyard but never even get to taste the fruit. You'll watch your own ox get butchered, but you won't get a single bite of the meat. Your donkey will be stolen right from under your nose, and you'll never see it again. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and nobody will lift a finger to help you.

Your sons and daughters will be handed over to a foreign nation. You'll wear your eyes out watching for them to come back, but you'll be totally helpless. A nation you don't even know will eat up all your crops and the fruits of your labor. You'll be oppressed and crushed for the rest of your life. The things you see will literally drive you insane.
God will strike you with painful boils on your knees and legs that can't be healed, spreading from the bottom of your feet to the top of your head.

God will drag you and the king you chose to a nation that neither you nor your ancestors have ever heard of. There, you'll end up worshiping other gods, fake gods made of wood and stone. You'll become a cautionary tale, a joke, a horror show to all the nations where God sends you.

You'll plant a ton of seed in your fields but harvest almost nothing because locusts will eat it all. You'll plant vineyards and take care of them, but you won't get to drink any wine because worms will devour the grapes. You'll have olive trees everywhere, but you won't have any oil because the olives will just drop off the trees. You'll have sons and daughters, but they won't stay yours for long; they'll be taken away as captives. Swarms of locusts will take over all your trees and crops.

The foreigner living among you will climb higher and higher, while you sink lower and lower. They'll be the one lending you money, not the other way around. They'll be the head, and you'll be the tail.

All these curses will come for you. They'll chase you down and overtake you until you're completely destroyed because you didn't listen to the voice of God, your God, or keep the commands and rules he gave you. These curses will be a terrifying sign and a warning for you and your descendants forever.

Because you didn't serve God, your God, with a joyful and happy heart when you had everything, you will have to serve the enemies God sends against you. You'll be starving, thirsty, wearing rags, and in complete misery. He'll put a heavy iron yoke on your neck until he has destroyed you.

Yeah, God will bring a nation from the ends of the earth to attack you, swooping in like an eagle. You won't understand their language, and they'll be a fierce-looking people who show no mercy to the old or the young. They'll devour the young of your livestock and the crops of your land until you're wiped out. They won't leave you any grain, new wine, or oil, no calves from your herds or lambs from your flocks, until they've destroyed you. They will surround you in all your cities until the high, fortified walls you trusted in come crashing down. They will lay siege to all your cities throughout the country God, your God, has given you.

The siege will get so bad, the suffering so extreme, that you'll end up eating your own children, the sons and daughters God, your God, has given you. Even the most sensitive and gentle man among you will turn evil. He'll give a dirty look to his own brother, the wife he loves, and his surviving children, refusing to share even a tiny piece of the flesh of his child that he is eating. He'll have nothing left, having lost his humanity in the terrible suffering of the siege your enemy brings against all your cities.

And the most gentle and delicate woman among you, someone so delicate she wouldn't even step on the ground, will turn evil against the husband she loves and against her own son and daughter. She'll hide the afterbirth from her womb and the children she bears, planning to eat them in secret because she has nothing left during the suffering of the siege your enemy will bring against your cities.

If you don't carefully follow all the words of this law, which are written in this book, and if you don't revere this glorious and awesome name—the LORD your God—then God will hit you and your descendants with insane disasters, huge and never-ending catastrophes, and terrible, chronic illnesses. He'll bring back all the diseases of Egypt that you were so scared of, and they'll stick to you. And yeah, every other sickness and disaster you can think of—even the ones not written in this Book of the Law—God will bring on you until you are destroyed.
You had become as numerous as the stars in the sky, but you'll be left as just a few people, because you didn't obey the LORD your God.

And here's how it'll be: Just like God once took joy in making you successful and increasing your numbers, he will then take joy in ruining and destroying you. He'll pull you up from the very land you're entering to take over. He'll scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other. There you will worship other gods—gods of wood and stone that neither you nor your ancestors have known. Among those nations, you won't find any peace or a place to rest. God will give you a stressed-out heart, eyes that are tired from watching, and a soul full of despair. Your life will constantly be on the line. You'll be terrified day and night, never sure if you're going to make it.
In the morning you'll say, 'I wish it were evening!' and in the evening you'll say, 'I wish it were morning!' because of the terror in your heart and the horrifying things you'll see.
God will send you back to Egypt in ships on a journey I said you'd never have to take again. There, you'll try to sell yourselves as slaves to your enemies, but no one will even want to buy you.

Deuteronomy.title: The Covenant Gets a Reboot & The Consequences Are REAL
paragraphs: Alright, so here's the deal. This is the new agreement God told Moses to make with the Israelites while they were in Moab. It was like a reboot of the first agreement they made back at Mount Horeb.

So Moses got all the Israelites together and was like, 'Yo, you guys literally saw everything God did back in Egypt. You saw what he did to Pharaoh and his crew, and the whole country. You were there for all the crazy stuff, the huge signs and insane miracles. But it's like, until today, you guys didn't really *get* it. God hadn't given you the brains to understand, the eyes to really see, or the ears to really listen.'

I led you through the desert for 40 years, and get this—your clothes never got old, and your sandals never fell apart. You guys were living good without any bread, wine, or beer. That was all to prove to you that I am your God, for real.

When we got here, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan were ready to throw down, but we totally wrecked them. We took their land and gave it to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh as their new spot.
So for real, stick to the terms of this agreement. Do what it says, and you'll be successful in everything you do.

You're all standing here today in front of God, your God—all your leaders, officials, everyone in Israel: your kids, your wives, and even the foreigners in your camps who chop your wood and get your water. You're about to enter into this super serious, sworn agreement that God is making with you today. This agreement confirms that you are his people, and he is your God, just like he promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

And I'm not just making this agreement and promise with you guys here today. I'm making it with you who are standing here in front of God, our God, but also with everyone who isn't here today. You know what it was like living in Egypt and how we had to travel through all those other nations. You saw all their nasty idols, their fake gods made of wood, stone, silver, and gold. So don't let your guard down. Don't let anyone—man or woman, family or tribe—get distracted from our God and start messing with the fake gods of those nations. Don't let some toxic idea sprout up and poison everyone. You don't want someone hearing the words of this sworn agreement and thinking, 'Nah, I'm good, I'll just do whatever I want.' That kind of attitude will ruin it for everyone. God will not let that person slide. God's anger and jealousy will blow up like a volcano on them. All the curses written in this book will crush them. God will literally erase their name from history. God will single them out from all the tribes of Israel for a special punishment, based on all the curses of the agreement written in this Book of the Law.

The next generation, your kids who come after you, and foreigners from far away will be totally shocked when they see how messed up the land is, how God made the whole country sick. They'll see a burnt-out wasteland of sulfur and salt, with nothing planted, nothing growing, not even a single blade of grass—just like when God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim in his fiery anger.
All the other nations will be like, 'Why did God do this to this country? What could have possibly made him this mad?'

And your kids will answer, 'It's because they broke the agreement of the God of their ancestors, the one he made with them after he brought them out of Egypt. They went and worshiped other gods, gods they had never even heard of, gods they had no business messing with. So God's anger exploded against that land, and all the curses written in this book came down on it. God, in his crazy anger, ripped them out of their land by the roots and threw them into another country, which is where they are now.'
God, our God, will handle the secret stuff, but the stuff he has revealed is on us. It's our job, and our kids' job, to follow all the rules in this Law.

Deuteronomy.title: Choose Life or Death: The Ultimate Choice is Yours
paragraphs: Alright, so here's the deal. When you're scattered all over the world, just like I said would happen, and all the good and bad stuff I warned you about actually goes down, and you and your kids finally get it and decide to come back to God with your whole heart, for real this time, and actually do what I'm telling you today, then God's gonna turn things around. He'll have your back, and He'll come and get you from all the places you've been scattered. Like, no matter how far you are, God will literally come and get you and bring you back to the land your ancestors had. It's gonna be yours again. He's gonna make your life awesome and you'll have even more people than your ancestors did.

God's gonna do a heart-check on you and your kids, like, He'll get rid of all the hard stuff around your heart so you can actually love Him with everything you've got and, like, *live* for real. And all those curses? God's gonna flip the script and put them on your enemies, the ones who were hating on you and trying to bring you down.

And you'll get a fresh start, actually listening to God and following all the rules I'm giving you today. God's gonna go all out to make your life good: you'll have families, your animals will have babies, your crops will grow—like, your whole life will be blessed. Seriously, God will be so happy for you again, just like He was with your ancestors.

But here's the catch: you've gotta actually listen to God and keep the rules written in this book. No half-hearted stuff. You have to go all-in for God, with your whole heart and soul, no holding back.

This rule I'm giving you today isn't some impossible task. It's not out of reach. It's not like it's on some super high mountain and you need to hire a pro climber to get it for you. And it's not across the ocean, so you don't have to send a ship to go get it. Nah. The word is right here, right now—as close as the words in your mouth and the feelings in your heart. Just do it!
Look, I've laid it all out for you today: Life and Good, or Death and Evil.
And I'm telling you today: Love God. Follow His ways. Keep His rules and commands so you can live, like, *really* live, an amazing life, blessed by God in the land you're about to go and own.
But I'm warning you: if you change your mind, refuse to listen, and decide to go worship other gods, you're gonna be totally wrecked. You won't last long in the land you're about to enter.

I'm calling on heaven and earth to witness this today: I'm giving you the choice between Life and Death, a Blessing and a Curse. Choose life, so you and your kids can live. Love God, listen to Him, and stick with Him. Seriously, He is your life, and He'll give you a long life in the land He promised to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

Deuteronomy.title: The Ultimate Handover: Moses to Joshua
paragraphs: So, Moses got all the Israelites together and laid it all out for them. He said, “Yo, I’m 120 years old today. I can’t get around like I used to, and God told me straight up, ‘You’re not crossing the Jordan River.’

“But God, your God, is gonna cross the river ahead of you and totally crush the nations in your path so you can take their land. (And Joshua will be leading the charge, just like God said.) God’s gonna give them the same treatment he gave the Amorite kings, Sihon and Og, and their land; he’s gonna completely destroy them. God will hand them over to you, and you have to treat them exactly like I commanded.
“Be strong. Be brave. Don’t get scared and don’t even think twice about them, because God, your God, is marching right ahead of you. He’s with you. He won’t fail you or ditch you.”

Then Moses called Joshua over. In front of everyone in Israel, he said, “Be strong. Be brave. You’re the one who will lead these people into the land God promised their ancestors he’d give them. You will make sure they get it. God is marching ahead of you. He’s right there with you. He won’t fail you or ditch you. So don’t be scared. Don’t worry.”

Moses wrote down this whole Revelation and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the Ark of the Covenant of God, and to all the leaders of Israel. And he gave them these instructions: “At the end of every seven years, during the Year-All-Debts-Are-Canceled, at the Festival of Booths when all of Israel shows up to meet God at the place he chooses, you have to read this Revelation out loud for everyone to hear. Get everyone together—men, women, kids, and even the foreigners living with you—so they can listen up, learn to respect God, your God, and be careful to follow everything in this Revelation. And do it so their kids, who don’t know any of this yet, will also hear it and learn to respect God, your God, for as long as you live in the land you’re crossing the Jordan to take over.”
God told Moses: “You’re about to die. So call Joshua. Meet me in the Tent of Meeting so I can give him his official commission.”
So Moses and Joshua went and stood in the Tent of Meeting. God showed up in the Tent in a Pillar of Cloud. The Cloud was right near the entrance of the Tent.

God said to Moses: “You’re about to die and be buried with your ancestors. And as soon as you’re gone, these people are gonna start chasing after the foreign gods of the land they’re entering. They’ll abandon me and break the covenant I made with them. I’m gonna get angry, like, seriously angry. I’ll walk away and leave them on their own, won’t even look their way. Then a ton of disasters and bad stuff will hit them because they have no defense. They’ll say, ‘Isn’t it because our God wasn’t here that all this bad stuff happened to us?’ But I’ll stay out of their lives, looking the other way because of all the messed-up things they did, chasing after other gods!

“But for now, write down this song and teach it to the People of Israel. Make them learn it by heart. It will be my evidence against them. When I bring them into the land I promised their ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey, and they eat until they’re full and fat, and then start messing with other gods and worshiping them, and then everything starts to fall apart and a bunch of terrible things happen, this song will be right there as a witness to who they are and what went wrong. Their kids won’t forget this song; they’ll be singing it. Don’t think I don’t know what they’re already planning to do, and they’re not even in the land I promised them yet.”
So Moses wrote down this song that very day and taught it to the People of Israel.
Then God commanded Joshua son of Nun, “Be strong. Be brave. You will lead the People of Israel into the land I promised to give them. And I’ll be right there with you.”

After Moses finished writing down every single word of this Revelation in a book, he told the Levites who were in charge of carrying the Ark of the Covenant of God, “Take this Book of Revelation and put it next to the Ark of the Covenant of God, your God. Keep it there as a witness.

“I know how rebellious you guys are, how stubborn you can be. You’re rebelling against God even now, while I’m still alive and here with you. How much worse is it going to be after I die? So get all the leaders of the tribes and the officials here. I have something I need to say directly to them, with Heaven and Earth as my witnesses. I know that after I die, you’re going to mess things up big time, ditching the path I commanded and bringing all kinds of bad consequences on yourselves in the future. You’re determined to do evil in God’s eyes—I know you are—deliberately making him angry with your actions.”
So with all of Israel gathered and listening, Moses taught them the words of this song, from beginning to end.

Deuteronomy.title: God's Diss Track on His Own People
paragraphs: Yo, listen up, heavens! And you too, Earth! I've got something major to say. My words are about to drop like a soft rain, like the dew on a fresh morning. Think of it like a light sprinkle on new grass or a spring shower in a garden. I'm here to talk about God's name, so you better believe in the greatness of our God! He's our Rock, always coming through with perfect plans. He's always fair and just in everything He does. He's a God you can count on, 100%, no cap. A totally straight-up God. But His kids? They're a hot mess, totally mixed-up, acting like they're not even His. They try to throw shade at Him, but it never sticks.

Are you seriously treating God like this? That's just wild. Have you got no respect? Isn't He the Father who made you, who gave you your spot on Earth? You should check your history, for real. Dig into the past and understand where you come from. Ask your parents what it was like, or the old folks. They'll tell you what's up.

When God the Most High was handing out land to the nations and giving everyone their place, He put each group under the watch of divine guardians. But God Himself took charge of His own people, making Jacob His personal project.

He found him in the middle of nowhere, in a windy, empty wasteland. He wrapped His arms around him, gave him tons of attention, and protected him like the apple of His eye. He was like an eagle watching over its nest, hovering over its babies, then spreading its wings to carry them and teach them how to fly. God was the only one leading him; no other fake gods were in the picture. God took him to the top of the hills so he could feast on the best crops. He gave him honey from a rock, oil from a granite cliff, fresh cheese and milk, the best cuts of lamb and goat, fancy rams, top-quality wheat, and the best wine you could ever drink!

Jeshurun (that's Israel) got fat and started acting up. You got chubby, then obese, like a total lard-ball. He ditched the God who made him and made fun of the Rock who saved him. They made God jealous with their trendy new foreign gods, and their disgusting habits ticked Him off big time. They started sacrificing to demons, not gods, to gods they didn't even know—brand new gods, fresh off the shelf, that your ancestors would never have even considered gods. You just walked out on the Rock who gave you life, forgetting the God who brought you into this world.

God saw all this and was like, "I'm out." He was so angry and hurt by His own sons and daughters. He said, "I'm not looking at them anymore. Let's see what happens to them. They're such a messed-up, backward generation! Who even knows what they'll do next? They've provoked me with their fake gods, made me furious with their worthless idols. So I'm gonna provoke them with a 'no-people,' and make them mad with a nation of fools. My anger is like a wildfire, burning deep down in the grave, then shooting up to burn the whole Earth and its crops, setting mountains on fire from top to bottom. I'm gonna pile on the disasters, shoot all my arrows at them: starvation, scorching heat, deadly diseases. I'll send wild animals to attack them and poisonous snakes to bite them. There will be death in the streets and terror in their homes. Young men and women will be struck down, even babies and old people."

I could have just said, "I'll chop them to pieces and wipe them off the face of the Earth." But I was worried the enemy would take all the credit, bragging, "Look what we did! God had nothing to do with this."

They're a nation of idiots; they don't even have the sense to come in out of the rain. If they were smart, they'd get it. They'd see what's coming for them. How could one soldier chase a thousand of them, or two guys make two thousand run away, unless their Rock had sold them out, unless God had given them up? Their 'rock' is nothing compared to our Rock; even our enemies know that. They're like a vine from Sodom, with roots in Gomorrah. Their grapes are poison, their grape-clusters bitter. Their wine is like snake venom, a deadly cobra poison.

Don't you get it? I've got all this stored up, locked away behind iron doors. I'm the one in charge of revenge and payback. I'm just waiting for them to mess up. Their day of doom is coming, and it's gonna be fast and furious.

Yeah, God will judge His people, but He'll do it with so much compassion. When He sees they're weak and that no one is left, whether slave or free, He'll ask, "So where are their gods now? The 'rock' they ran to for safety? The gods who ate the fat from their sacrifices and drank their wine offerings? Let's see them step up and help you now!"

"Do you see it now? Do you see that I'm the only one? That there's no other god but me? I'm the one who brings death and gives life. I'm the one who wounds and who heals. No one can escape from me! I'm raising my hand and making a promise. As surely as I live forever, I promise this: When I sharpen my lightning-fast sword and bring my judgment, I will get my revenge on my enemies and pay back everyone who hates me. My arrows will be drunk with blood, and my sword will feast on flesh, on the bodies of the slain and the captives, on the heads of the proud enemy leaders."
So celebrate, all you nations, and praise His people with joy! He gets justice for His servants who were killed. He pays back His enemies with vengeance and purifies His land for His people.

Moses came with Joshua, son of Nun, and recited all the words of this song for the people to hear. When he finished, he said, "Take all these words to heart. I'm your witness today. Command your children to obey every single word of this law. This isn't some small thing; it's your life. If you keep this word, you'll live a long and good life in the land you're about to cross the Jordan to possess."

That very same day, God told Moses, "Go climb the Abarim Mountains to Mount Nebo in Moab, across from Jericho. Take a look at the land of Canaan, which I'm giving to the Israelites. You will die on that mountain and join your ancestors, just like your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor.

"This is happening because you both broke faith with me in front of all the Israelites at the waters of Meribah Kadesh in the Zin desert. You didn't honor my holiness among the people. So you'll get to see the land from a distance, but you won't get to enter it—the land I'm giving to the people of Israel."

Deuteronomy.title: Moses' Last Words: Blessing the Whole Squad
paragraphs: Alright, so this is the final blessing Moses, the man of God, gave to the people of Israel before he passed away. He said:

God showed up from Sinai, like the sun rising over Seir. He was shining bright from Mount Paran, rolling deep with ten thousand holy angels. Fire was literally streaming from his right hand. Man, he really loves his people. All his holy ones are safe in his hand. They're sitting at his feet, soaking up his wisdom, the same teachings Moses commanded, which is the inheritance of all of Jacob's crew. That's how God became king in Jeshurun, when all the leaders and tribes of Israel got together.
For Reuben, he said:
"Let Reuben live, not completely disappear, but man, his crew is gonna be small."
For Judah:
"God, listen to what Judah's saying. Bring him back to his people. Make him strong, and have his back when he's up against his enemies."
For Levi:

"Your Thummim and Urim belong to your loyal one, the one you put to the test at Massah, and argued with at the Waters of Meribah. He was so real with you that he said to his own parents, 'I don't even know you.' He turned his back on his own family because he was all about keeping your commands and your covenant. So let him teach your rules to Jacob and your wisdom to Israel. Let him keep the good smells of incense rising up to you and the offerings on your altar. God, bless his dedication, and show everyone you approve of what he's doing. And for anyone who comes against him, take them down. Make sure we never hear from his haters again."
For Benjamin:
"God's favorite, for real. God's with him 24/7. He's surrounded by God all day long, and God is right there at home with him."
For Joseph:

"May God bless his land with the best stuff: fresh dew from heaven, and springs from deep in the earth. The best sunshine and the best moonlight. The most beautiful mountains and the best hills that last forever. The best gifts the earth can give, and the approval of the one who was in the burning bush. May all of this be on Joseph, the one who was set apart from his brothers. He's as majestic as a firstborn bull, with horns like a wild ox. He's gonna take down nations with those horns, pushing them to the ends of the earth. Ephraim will do this by the ten thousands, and Manasseh by the thousands."
For Zebulun and Issachar:

"Zebulun, have a blast when you go out, and Issachar, enjoy your time at home. They'll invite people to the mountain and give the right kinds of sacrifices, because they'll be bringing in riches from the sea and treasures from the beaches."
For Gad:

"Blessed is the one who makes Gad's territory bigger. Gad is like a lion, tearing off arms and crushing skulls. He saw the best land for himself and took it, a portion fit for a leader. He took his place at the head and made sure everyone followed God's righteous ways and rules for Israel."
For Dan:
"Dan is a young lion, jumping out from Bashan."
For Naphtali:
"Naphtali is overflowing with blessings, spilling over with God's favor as he takes over the sea and the south."
For Asher:
"Asher is the most blessed of all the sons! May he be his brothers' favorite, and have his feet dipped in oil. May his gates be locked with iron, and his strength last as long as he lives."

There's no one like God, Jeshurun. He rides through the skies to rescue you, with his majesty shining in the clouds. The eternal God is your home, and his arms are always there to support you. He kicked out your enemies and said, "Destroy them!" So Israel lived in safety, the people of Jacob were undisturbed in a land full of grain and wine, and the heavens dripped with dew.

Israel, you're so lucky! Who's got it as good as you? A nation saved by God! He's the shield that protects you and the sword that brings you victory. Your enemies will come crawling to you, and you'll walk all over them.

Deuteronomy.title: Moses' Final View & Mysterious Death
paragraphs: So Moses went up from the Plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, right to the top of Pisgah, across from Jericho. And God showed him the whole land—from Gilead all the way to Dan, all of Naphtali, the territories of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah stretching to the Mediterranean Sea, the Negev desert, and the whole plain surrounding Jericho, the City of Palms, all the way down to Zoar. It was a wild view.

Right then and there, God told him, "This is it. This is the land I swore to your ancestors—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—that I'd give to their descendants. I'm letting you see it with your own eyes, but real talk... you're not gonna get to go in."

Moses, God's servant, died right there in Moab, exactly as God said would happen. God Himself buried him in a valley in Moab, across from Beth Peor. And to this day, nobody has a clue where his grave is. Lowkey mysterious.

Moses was 120 when he passed, but get this—his vision was still perfect, and he still had that energy, you know? The Israelites mourned for him on the Plains of Moab for a full 30 days. After that, the official time of mourning was over.

Joshua, son of Nun, was basically glowing with wisdom because Moses had passed the torch to him by laying his hands on him. So the Israelites listened to Joshua and followed his lead, just like they did when God was giving commands through Moses.

No cap, there has never been another prophet in Israel like Moses. This dude knew God face-to-face. There's been nothing like the signs and crazy miracles God had him do in Egypt to Pharaoh and his whole crew. Nothing compares to the power he had and all the awesome and kinda scary things Moses did right in front of all of Israel.

Joshua.title: New Leader, Who Dis? Joshua Steps Up
paragraphs: So, after Moses, God's main guy, passed away, God hit up Joshua, who was Moses's right-hand man. He was like:

"Yo, my servant Moses is gone. It's your turn now. Get up and cross the Jordan River, you and this whole crew. You're heading to the land I'm giving the people of Israel. For real, every single place you step, it's yours—I already promised this to Moses. From the desert and Lebanon all the way east to the big Euphrates River—the whole Hittite area—and then west to the Mediterranean Sea. It's all for you. All your life, no one's gonna be able to stand against you, like, ever. Just like I had Moses's back, I've got yours. I'm not gonna bail on you or leave you hanging. Be strong. Be brave. You're the one who's gonna lead these people to get the land I swore to their ancestors I'd give them. So go all in, heart and soul. Make sure you follow every single rule Moses gave you from me. Don't get sidetracked, not even a little, so you can actually get where you're going. And don't let this Book of the Law out of your sight for a second. Think about it 24/7, and actually do what it says. Then you'll make it, for real. You'll be successful. Didn't I tell you? Be strong! Be brave! Don't be scared or freaked out. Your God is with you literally every step of the way."

Then Joshua told the leaders of the people, "Go through the camp and tell everyone to pack their stuff. In three days, we're crossing the Jordan River to go in and take the land our God is giving us."

Then Joshua talked to the guys from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. He said, "Remember what Moses, God's servant, told you: Your God is giving you a place to chill, and he's giving you this land. Your wives, kids, and animals can stay here east of the Jordan, the land Moses gave you. But all you soldiers have to cross the river ready for a fight, leading your brothers to help them out. You gotta help them until their God gives them a place to rest just like he did for you. They'll also take over the land their God is giving them. After that, you can come back to your own land that Moses, God's servant, gave you over here east of the Jordan."

They answered Joshua, "Whatever you say, we'll do. Wherever you send us, we'll go. We followed Moses completely, and we'll follow you too. We just pray that your God will be with you like he was with Moses. Anyone who questions you or refuses to do what you say will be put to death. So be strong and brave!"

Joshua.title: Two Spies & A Secret Promise
paragraphs: So, Joshua, Nun's son, lowkey sent two dudes out from Shittim as spies. He was like, "Go check out the land, especially Jericho." So they bounced and ended up at the house of a prostitute named Rahab and crashed there for the night.
Word got to the king of Jericho, like, "Yo, some Israelite guys just showed up tonight to spy on our land."
The king of Jericho hit up Rahab, saying, "Bring out the men who came to your house tonight. They're spies, here to scope out the whole country."

But the woman had already taken the two men and hidden them. She was like, "Yeah, two guys came by, but I didn't know where they were from. They left around dusk, right when the gate was about to close. I have no idea where they went. But if you hurry, you might still catch them!" (Plot twist: she had actually taken them up to the roof and hidden them under a pile of flax she had laid out.) So the king's men chased them down the road toward the Jordan River fords. As soon as the pursuers left, they shut the gate.

Before the spies were even asleep, the woman went up to the roof and said to them, "Look, I know God has given you this land. We're all terrified of you. Everyone in this country is losing their nerve. We heard how God totally dried up the Red Sea for you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to those two Amorite kings east of the Jordan, Sihon and Og—you completely destroyed them. When we heard about it, our hearts just melted. None of us have any courage left because of you. For real, your God is God in the heavens above and on the earth below.

"So now, please, swear to me by God. Since I've shown you kindness, promise you'll show kindness to my family. Give me a real sign that you'll spare my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and everyone connected to them. Save us from death!"
"Our lives for yours!" the men said. "As long as you don't tell anyone about our mission. When God gives us the land, we'll treat you with loyal kindness."

So she lowered them down from a window with a rope, because her house was built right into the city wall. She told them, "Head for the hills so your pursuers don't find you. Hide out there for three days until they get back. Then you can go on your way."

The men told her, "To make this oath you made us swear legit, you have to do this: hang this red rope from the window you let us down through. Then gather your entire family—father, mother, brothers, and all your relatives—into your house with you. If anyone goes out the doors of your house into the street, their fate is on them; we're not responsible. But if a hand is laid on anyone inside the house with you, it's on us. But if you spill the beans about our business, then we're off the hook from the oath you made us swear."
She said, "Sounds like a plan," and sent them off. They left, and she immediately hung the red rope in the window.
They made their way to the hills and stayed there for three days, until the guys chasing them had returned. The pursuers had looked all over the road but didn't find them.

Then the two men started back. They came down from the hills, crossed the river, and returned to Joshua son of Nun and told him everything that had happened. They told Joshua, "No cap, God has given the whole land over to us. Everyone there is literally shaking in their boots because of us."

Joshua.title: God Parts the Waters, AGAIN?!
paragraphs: So, Joshua gets everyone up super early, and they all head out from Shittim. The whole crew of Israel is with him. They get to the Jordan River and set up camp, waiting to cross. Three days later, the leaders go around telling everyone the plan: 'Alright, listen up. When you see the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant, that's our cue to move out. Follow them, but don't get too close—stay back like half a mile. Seriously, keep your distance. That way, you'll see the exact path to take. This is a brand new road for us, so no messing around.'
Then Joshua tells the people, 'Get yourselves ready and be respectful. Tomorrow, God's gonna do some mind-blowing things among us.'
Joshua told the priests, 'Go ahead and pick up the Ark of the Covenant and lead the people.' So, they did just that and walked out in front of everyone.

God then says to Joshua, 'Today, I'm gonna start making you look like a big deal to all of Israel. They're gonna see for themselves that I'm with you, just like I was with Moses. Now, you tell the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant this: 'When you get to the edge of the Jordan River, just stand there on the bank.''

Then Joshua gathered the Israelites and said, 'Yo, listen up! Pay attention to what God, your God, is saying. This is how you'll know for sure that the living God is with us—he's going to totally kick out the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites for you. Check it out: the Ark of the Covenant is right in front of you. And get this—the Master of the whole earth is about to cross the Jordan right before your eyes. Now, pick twelve guys from the tribes of Israel, one from each tribe. When the priests carrying the Ark of God, the Master of all the earth, step into the Jordan's water, the river's flow is gonna stop. The water coming from upstream will just pile up in a huge heap.'

And that's exactly what went down. The people packed up and left their tents to cross the Jordan, with the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant leading the way. The moment the priests reached the Jordan and their feet touched the water's edge (the Jordan was totally overflowing its banks because it was harvest season), the water just stopped flowing. It piled up in a massive heap way, way off at a town called Adam, which is near Zarethan. The riverbed went completely dry all the way down to the Dead Sea. So the people crossed over, right opposite Jericho.

And there they were; the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant stood on solid, dry ground right in the middle of the Jordan while every single Israelite crossed over on dry land. The whole nation made it across without even getting their feet wet. Wild.

Joshua.title: Jordan River Crossing: The Ultimate Flex
paragraphs: So, once everyone in Israel finally made it across the river, God hit up Joshua and was like, "Yo, pick twelve dudes, one from each tribe. Tell them to go to the exact spot in the middle of the Jordan where the priests are standing firm. They need to grab twelve big rocks from there, carry 'em over, and drop 'em at the spot where you guys are camping tonight."

Joshua called out the twelve guys he'd selected from the People of Israel, one from every tribe. He gave them the game plan: "Alright, head out to the middle of the Jordan and post up in front of the Ark of God, your God. Each of you needs to haul a stone onto your shoulder—one for each of the tribes of Israel. This is so you'll have something to remember this moment. Down the road, when your kids ask you, 'Yo, what's the deal with these rocks?' you'll tell them, 'The Jordan River literally stopped flowing right in front of the Ark of the Covenant when it crossed. It just stopped cold. These stones are a permanent reminder for the people of Israel.'"

The people of Israel did exactly what Joshua commanded. They took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan—one for each of the twelve tribes, just as God had told Joshua—carried them over to the camp, and set them down there. Joshua also set up another twelve stones right in the middle of the Jordan, at the exact spot where the priests who carried the Ark of the Covenant had stood. They're actually still there today.

The priests carrying the Ark kept standing in the middle of the Jordan until everything God had ordered Joshua to tell the people was done (which was also what Moses had told Joshua to do). The people hustled across; nobody was messing around. When every single person was safely across, they all watched as the Ark of the Covenant and the priests finally crossed over.

The soldiers from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had already crossed over in battle formation ahead of the rest of Israel, just like Moses had instructed. All in all, about forty thousand armed soldiers crossed over in God's presence, ready for battle on the plains of Jericho.
That day, God made Joshua look like a total legend in front of all of Israel. They had major respect for him, just like they had for Moses his whole life.
Then God told Joshua, "Command the priests carrying the Ark of the Testimony to come up out of the Jordan."
So Joshua commanded the priests, "Come on up out of the Jordan."

And they did it. The priests carrying God's Ark of the Covenant came up from the middle of the Jordan. The second their feet hit dry land, the Jordan's waters started flowing again, right back to normal like nothing happened.

The people came up from the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month. They set up their camp at a place called Gilgal, just east of Jericho. Joshua then took the twelve stones they had grabbed from the Jordan and set them up as a monument at Gilgal. Then he told the Israelites, "In the future, when your kids ask their parents, 'What are these stones for?' tell them this: 'Israel crossed this Jordan river on dry ground.'

"Yeah, for real. God, your God, dried up the Jordan's waters for you until you had crossed, just like He did at the Red Sea, which he dried up for us until we crossed. This happened so that everyone on earth would know how strong God's power is, and so that you would always have a healthy respect for God."

Joshua.title: The Ultimate Glow-Up
paragraphs: So, get this: all the Amorite kings on the west side of the Jordan and the Canaanite kings on the coast heard that God literally stopped the Jordan River so the Israelites could cross. They were totally shook. Like, their courage just went *poof* and they were seriously scared of the Israelites.
Then God told Joshua, "Make some stone knives and circumcise the Israelites again." So, Joshua did just that. He made the knives and they did the circumcisions at a place they called Foreskins Hill.

Here's the deal with the circumcision. All the guys who were soldiers when they left Egypt had died in the desert on the way. The people who came out of Egypt were all circumcised, but the kids born in the desert on the journey hadn't been. The Israelites wandered in the desert for 40 years until that whole generation of soldiers who had disobeyed God died off. God promised they'd never see the awesome land He'd promised their ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey. But their kids took their place. These were the ones Joshua circumcised.
