The tribes of Joseph also went up to attack Bethel, and God was with them. They sent spies to check out the area. (Bethel’s old name was Luz.) The spies saw a man coming out of the city and told him, “Show us how to get into the city, and we’ll make sure you’re safe.” So the man showed them the way in. They wiped out everyone in the city but let that man and his whole family go free. The man later went to the land of the Hittites, built a city, and named it Luz, and that’s still its name.

But the tribe of Manasseh never drove out the people of Beth Shan, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, or Megiddo and their surrounding villages. The Canaanites were stubborn and just refused to leave. When the Israelites got stronger, they made the Canaanites do forced labor, but they never fully kicked them out.
Ephraim didn’t drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer, either. The Canaanites just kept on living there among them.
Zebulun didn’t drive out the Canaanites in Kitron or Nahalol. They stayed and lived there too, but they were put to forced labor.
Asher didn’t drive out the people of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Aczib, Helbah, Aphek, or Rehob. The Asherites just settled in and lived among the Canaanites since they couldn’t get rid of them.
Naphtali had the same problem. They couldn’t drive out the people of Beth Shemesh or Beth Anath, so they just moved in with them. They did, however, make them do forced labor.

The Amorites pushed the tribe of Dan back into the hill country and wouldn’t let them come down to the plains. The Amorites stubbornly held on to Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim. But when the tribes of Joseph got stronger, they put them to forced labor too.
The border of the Amorites started from the Scorpion Pass, went up from Sela, and continued onward.

Judges.title: The Generation That Forgot God
paragraphs: So, God's angel shows up at this place called Bokim, coming from Gilgal, and he's like, 'Yo, I'm the one who got you out of Egypt. I brought you to this land I promised your ancestors. I even said I'd never, ever break my promise to you. And what did I ask? Just one thing: don't team up with the people living here. Wreck their altars!' But you guys didn't listen. Seriously, what's up with that?
So now, here's the deal: I'm not gonna kick out the people who are already here. They're gonna be a major problem for you, and you'll get caught up in their fake gods.

When the angel of God said all this to the Israelites, they just lost it. Like, full-on ugly crying. They even named the place 'Bokim,' which means 'the weepers.' Then they offered sacrifices to God right there.

After Joshua sent everyone off, the Israelites went to claim their new land. And for a while, things were good. They worshiped God as long as Joshua was alive, and even while the leaders who outlived him were around—the ones who saw all the amazing things God did for Israel. Then Joshua, God's servant, died at 110 years old. They buried him in his own land at Timnath Heres.
But then, that whole generation passed away. A new generation came up, and they were totally clueless about God and all the incredible stuff He'd done for Israel.

The Israelites started doing some seriously messed-up stuff in God's eyes. They started worshiping these Baal gods, totally ditching the God of their ancestors who brought them out of Egypt. They started following the gods of the people around them. They actually bowed down to them! And man, did that make God angry. He was so mad at Israel that He let raiders come and take all their stuff. He basically sold them to their enemies, and they were completely helpless. Every time they tried to do something, God was against them, just like He warned them He would be. They were in a really bad spot.

But then God would raise up judges to save them from the people who were robbing them. But would they listen to the judges? Nope. They just kept chasing after other gods, worshiping them. They were quick to leave the path their ancestors had walked, the path of obeying God's commands. They wanted nothing to do with it.

Whenever God gave them a judge, He would be with that judge and save them from their enemies as long as the judge was alive. God felt bad for them when He heard them crying out because of how they were being treated. But as soon as the judge died, they went right back to their old ways, and were even worse than their parents! They were chasing other gods, serving and worshiping them. They were so stubborn, they wouldn't stop any of their evil habits.

So God's anger just blazed against Israel. He said, 'Because these people broke the covenant I made with their ancestors and haven't listened to me, I'm not going to drive out any more of the nations that Joshua left behind when he died. I'm going to use them to test Israel and see if they'll stay on God's path like their ancestors did.'
And that's why God left those nations there. He didn't drive them out right away or let Joshua finish the job.

Judges.title: The Left-Handed Assassin & The Cattle Prod Champ
paragraphs: So, here's the deal. God left some nations hanging around to test the Israelites who were total noobs when it came to the Canaanite wars. He basically wanted to put the next generation of Israelites, who'd never seen a real battle, through a training montage in the art of war. He left the five big-shot Philistine bosses, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who were chilling on Mount Lebanon from Mount Baal Hermon to Hamath’s Pass. They were there as a pop quiz for Israel, to see if they'd actually listen to the commands God gave their ancestors through Moses.

But, of course, the Israelites got way too comfortable. They started living like locals among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. They married their daughters and letting their sons marry their daughters. And then, the biggest L, they started worshiping their gods.

The people of Israel did some seriously messed up stuff in God's eyes. They totally forgot their own God and started worshiping the Baal and Asherah gods. God's anger flared up against Israel, like, for real. He basically sold them to Cushan-Rishathaim, the king of Aram Naharaim. The Israelites were stuck serving this dude for eight years.

The people of Israel cried out to God, and God sent a hero to save them: Othniel, who was Caleb's nephew. The Spirit of God came over him, and he got Israel hyped up. He went to war, and God handed him the win against King Cushan-Rishathaim. Othniel totally owned him.
The land was chill for forty years. Then Othniel died.

But the Israelites went right back to their old habits, doing evil in God's sight. So God powered up Eglon, king of Moab, to go against Israel because they were messing up again. Eglon teamed up with the Ammonites and Amalekites, attacked Israel, and they took over the City of Palms. The Israelites were stuck serving Eglon for fourteen years.

The people of Israel cried out to God, and God raised up another hero for them, a guy named Ehud. He was a Benjaminite and, plot twist, he was left-handed. The Israelites sent him with tribute money to King Eglon of Moab. Ehud made himself a short, two-edged sword and strapped it to his right thigh, hidden under his clothes. He went to present the tribute to King Eglon, who was a super fat dude. After Ehud gave him the tribute, he walked a little way with the guys who carried it. But when he got to the stone idols near Gilgal, he turned back and said, 'I have a secret message for you, O King.'
The king told his servants, 'Peace out.' So they all left.

Ehud went up to him—the king was all alone in his cool rooftop room—and said, 'I have a word from God for you.' Eglon stood up from his throne. Ehud, with his left hand, grabbed the sword from his right thigh and plunged it right into the king's massive belly. The blade went in so deep, the hilt went in too. The fat just swallowed it up, and he couldn't even pull it out. Ehud slipped out through the porch, locked the doors of the rooftop room behind him, and bounced.
When the servants came back, they were surprised to see the doors to the rooftop room were locked. They were like, 'He's probably just using the bathroom.'
They waited. And waited. Then they started to get worried—why wasn't anyone coming out? Finally, they grabbed a key and unlocked the doors. And there was their master, dead on the floor!

While they were all freaking out, Ehud was long gone. He got past the stone idols and escaped to Seirah. When he got there, he blew a trumpet on Mount Ephraim. The Israelites came down from the hills and joined him, and he became their leader.

He told them, 'Follow me! God has given us our enemies—yep, Moab!—on a silver platter.' They followed him down, secured the river crossings of the Jordan against the Moabites, and didn't let a single person cross.
That day, they took down about ten thousand Moabite soldiers, all of them strong and well-fed. Not a single one got away. On that day, Moab was officially pwned by Israel.
The land was quiet for eighty years.
After Ehud, there was Shamgar son of Anath. This dude, with just a cattle prod, took out six hundred Philistines all by himself. He saved Israel too. What a legend.

Judges.title: This Woman is GOATED (God's secret weapon)
paragraphs: After the last judge, Ehud, died, the Israelites started messing up again, doing things God totally hated. So God let them get taken over by Jabin, a Canaanite king. This king's top general was a dude named Sisera, and he was a real piece of work. For twenty years, he made life miserable for the Israelites with his 900 iron chariots. Finally, the Israelites couldn't take it anymore and cried out to God for help.

At that time, a prophet named Deborah was leading Israel. She was super wise and would hold court under a palm tree, and people would come to her to settle their arguments. One day, she sent for a guy named Barak and told him, "God is commanding you to gather 10,000 soldiers and go to Mount Tabor. I'll make sure Sisera and his army meet you there, and I promise you'll win."
Barak was a little scared and said, "I'll only go if you come with me. If you don't, I'm not going."
Deborah replied, "Okay, I'll go with you. But because you're being so hesitant, you won't get the glory for the victory. A woman will defeat Sisera."
So Deborah went with Barak, and he gathered his army. When Sisera heard that Barak was at Mount Tabor, he brought all his chariots and soldiers to the Kishon River to fight.
Deborah told Barak, "Go! Today is the day God will give you victory!" So Barak and his army charged down the mountain.

And just as Deborah had said, God totally routed Sisera's army. Sisera himself had to abandon his chariot and run for his life. Barak's army chased after the enemy and wiped them all out. Not a single one of Sisera's soldiers survived.

Meanwhile, Sisera ran to the tent of a woman named Jael. He thought he would be safe there because her husband was on good terms with his king. Jael invited him in, gave him a drink of milk, and covered him with a blanket. Sisera told her to stand guard and lie if anyone came looking for him. Then, completely exhausted, he fell fast asleep.

While he was sleeping, Jael took a tent peg and a hammer, snuck up to him, and drove the peg right through his temple and into the ground. It was a brutal but effective way to take him out. He convulsed and died.

Just then, Barak showed up, still chasing Sisera. Jael went out to meet him and said, "Come, I'll show you the man you're looking for." She took him into her tent, and there was Sisera, dead on the ground with a tent peg in his head.
That day, God gave the Israelites a huge victory over the Canaanites. They kept fighting until King Jabin and his kingdom were completely destroyed.

Judges.title: Deborah's Victory Anthem is FIRE
paragraphs: So that day, Deborah and Barak dropped a victory anthem. It went something like this:
When Israel let its hair down and just went for it, when the people signed up to fight without even being asked—props to God for that!
Yo, kings, listen up! Rulers, pay attention! I'm singing to God, yeah, to God himself. Making a track for the God of Israel.

God, when you rolled out from Seir, and marched through Edom, the whole earth shook. The sky literally started crying, like, full-on ugly crying, making rivers. Even the mountains were jumping around for God, the God of Sinai, the one and only God of Israel.

Back in the day, during Shamgar's and Jael's time, things were sketchy. Nobody used the main roads; everyone took the backstreets to stay safe. The so-called 'warriors' got lazy and out of shape, with zero fight in them. But then you, Deborah, you stepped up. You became like the mom of Israel, getting everyone in line. God picked some new leaders, and they actually fought back at the city gates. And get this—they did it without a single shield or spear in sight for, like, 40 whole squads of dudes.
Let's go, Israel! Get hyped! Big shoutout to everyone who volunteered to help out—God sees you!

All you people riding your fancy donkeys with the comfy seats, and you walking down the street, stop and think about this. Get together at the town well and listen to the victory songs, the stories of how God came through for Israel.
Then God's people went down to the city gates.
Wake up, Deborah! Let's hear you sing! Get up, Barak! Go grab your prisoners!

Then the ones who were left went down to meet the brave ones. God's people linked up with the strong. The leaders from Ephraim came down to the valley, and Benjamin was right behind you with his crew. Captains from Makir and high-level leaders from Zebulun marched down. Issachar's princes were with Deborah, and Issachar stuck with Barak, having his back on the battlefield. But Reuben's crew? They were lowkey having second thoughts. Like, why were they just sitting around talking? They got distracted and couldn't decide what to do. Gilead played it safe on the other side of the Jordan, and Dan? He just dipped and went sailing. Asher stayed by the coast, chilling in his safe harbors. But Zebulun and Naphtali? They were the real ones, risking it all on the front lines.

The kings showed up and fought, the kings of Canaan fought. They battled at Taanach, by the Megiddo stream, but they didn't get any money or loot. Even the stars in the sky joined the fight against Sisera. The Kishon river just swept them away. It was wild. We're gonna stomp on the necks of the strong! You could hear the horses' hooves pounding, the stallions charging and stampeding. But God's angel said, 'Curse Meroz. Double curse its people, because they didn't show up when God needed them. They didn't roll with God's crew of fighters.'

But the most blessed woman of all is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite. The most blessed of all the homemakers. Sisera asked for water, and she brought him milk. She served him cream in a nice bowl. Then she grabbed a tent peg with her left hand and a hammer with her right. She went to work on Sisera, smashed his head, and put a hole right through his temple. He just slumped at her feet and fell. He was sprawled out. He slumped, he fell. Slumped. Fallen. Dead.

Meanwhile, Sisera's mom was waiting at the window, getting super anxious. 'Why is his chariot so late? What's the hold-up?' The wisest of her friends tried to calm her down, saying, 'They're probably just dividing up all the stuff they took, right? A girl, maybe two, for each guy. And for Sisera, a sick silk shirt, a prize for sure! And a cool scarf—no, two scarves—for the neck of the winner.'
So this is how all of God's enemies should go down, while the people who love him should shine like the sun on a clear day.
And the land was chill for forty years.

Judges.title: God's Lowkey Recruit & The Wet Fleece Test
paragraphs: So, the Israelites started messing up again, doing stuff God wasn't happy with. As a result, God let the Midianites totally dominate them for seven years. Midian was way too strong for Israel. Because they were so scared of the Midianites, the Israelites had to hide out in mountain caves and secret forts. Whenever the Israelites would plant their crops, the Midianites and their allies from the east would roll in, set up camp, and just wreck everything all the way to Gaza. They didn't leave a single thing for the Israelites to survive on—no sheep, no cows, no donkeys. They'd show up with all their own animals and tents, like a massive swarm of locusts, and their camels were literally too many to count. They just marched in and trashed the whole place. The Israelites ended up super poor because of Midian, so they finally cried out to God for help.

So when the Israelites were at their breaking point and finally called out to God, He sent a prophet with a message. It was like, 'This is what God, the God of Israel, is saying: I'm the one who got you out of Egypt. I freed you from being slaves. I saved you from the Egyptians when they were being brutal, and then I saved you from everyone else who tried to mess with you. I cleared them out and gave you their land. And I told you, "I am your God. Don't be scared of the fake gods of the people whose land you're living in now." But you guys just didn't listen.'

Then one day, an angel from God showed up and just chilled under an oak tree in a place called Ophrah. The tree belonged to this guy Joash, and his son, Gideon, was secretly threshing wheat in a winepress so the Midianites wouldn't see him. The angel appeared to Gideon and said, 'What's up, mighty warrior! God is with you.'

Gideon shot back, 'With me, sir? Lowkey, if God is with us, why is all this bad stuff happening? Where are all the insane miracles our parents told us about, like when they said, "Didn't God get us out of Egypt?" The reality is, God has completely ghosted us—he just handed us over to Midian.'
But God looked him right in the eye and said, 'Go with the strength you have. You're the one who's going to save Israel from Midian. Didn't I just tell you to go?'
Gideon was like, 'Me, sir? How am I supposed to save Israel? My family is the weakest in our whole tribe, and I'm basically the nobody of the family.'
God told him, 'I'll be with you. Trust me, you'll crush the Midianites like you're fighting just one guy.'
Gideon said, 'Okay, if you're for real, give me a sign to prove what you're saying is legit. Don't leave until I come back with a gift for you.'
The angel said, 'I'll wait here 'til you get back.'

So Gideon went and cooked up a young goat and made a massive batch of bread without yeast (he used like, a ton of flour). He put the meat in a basket and the soup in a pot and brought them back to the angel under the oak tree for a sacred meal.
The angel of God told him, 'Put the meat and the bread on that rock over there, and pour the soup over them.' Gideon did it.

Then the angel of God reached out the stick he was holding and touched the meat and bread. A fire just burst out of the rock and burned everything up, and then the angel just vanished. That's when Gideon knew it was a real angel from God!
Gideon freaked out, 'Oh no! Master, God! I've seen an angel of God face-to-face!'
But God calmed him down, 'Chill. Don't panic. You're not going to die.'
So Gideon built an altar to God right there and named it 'God's Peace.' It's still there in Ophrah of Abiezer today.

That very night, God told him, 'Take your dad's best seven-year-old bull. Tear down your father's altar to the fake god Baal and chop down the Asherah pole next to it. Then, build a proper altar to your God on top of this hill. Take the bull and offer it as a sacrifice, using the wood from the Asherah pole you chopped down.'
Gideon got ten of his servants and did exactly what God told him. But he was too scared of his family and the neighbors to do it during the day, so he did it at night.
When everyone in town woke up the next morning, they were shocked. Baal's altar was destroyed, the Asherah pole was chopped down, and the best bull was being burned on a new altar.
They were all asking each other, 'Who did this?'
After a bunch of questions, someone finally figured it out: 'Gideon, Joash's son, did it.'
The townspeople went to Joash and demanded, 'Bring out your son! He has to die! He tore down Baal's altar and chopped down the Asherah tree!'

But Joash stood up to the angry mob and said, 'Are you guys seriously going to fight Baal's battles for him? Are you going to save him? Anyone who defends Baal will be dead by morning. If Baal is really a god, let him fight his own battles and defend his own altar.'
From that day on, they called Gideon 'Jerub-Baal,' which means 'Let Baal fight his own battles,' because he had torn down Baal's altar.

Then all the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern armies teamed up, crossed the river, and set up camp in the Jezreel Valley. The Spirit of God came over Gideon in a big way. He blew a ram's horn, and his own clan, the Abiezrites, came out ready to fight with him. He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they all came to join him.

Gideon said to God, 'Okay, if you're really going to use me to save Israel like you said, then check this out: I'm putting a piece of wool on the ground. If there's dew only on the wool but the ground is dry, then I'll know you're going to use me to save Israel, just like you said.'
And that's exactly what happened. When Gideon got up early the next morning, he squeezed the wool and a whole bowlful of water came out!

Then Gideon said to God, 'Don't get mad at me, but let me just ask one more thing. I want to try this one more time with the wool. But this time, let the wool stay dry and let the ground be covered in dew.'
And God did it that night. The wool was completely dry, but the ground was soaking wet with dew.

Judges.title: God's 300 vs. a Whole Army?!
paragraphs: So, Gideon (aka Jerub-Baal) was up super early the next day with his whole crew. They posted up at Harod's Spring. Meanwhile, the Midianite camp was down in the valley, just north of them by the Hill of Moreh.

Then God hit Gideon up and said, 'Yo, your army is way too big. I can't just hand Midian over to you guys like this, or you'll all be like, 'We did it ourselves!' and totally forget about me. So, make an announcement: 'If you're scared or having second thoughts, you can bounce. Head home from Mount Gilead.' And just like that, 22,000 soldiers dipped. Only 10,000 were left.

But God was like, 'Still too many. Take them down to the river, and I'll make the final cut there. If I say someone's in, they're in. If I say they're out, they're out.' So Gideon marched his guys down to the river.

God told Gideon, 'Separate the guys who lap water with their tongues like a dog from the ones who kneel down to drink.' It was wild, but only 300 guys lapped water from their hands. The rest all knelt.
Then God said, 'I'm gonna use these 300 guys who lapped the water to save you and give you the win over Midian. Everyone else can go home.'
So Gideon took their supplies and trumpets and sent the rest of the Israelites home. He stayed with his 300 men, and the Midianite camp was spread out in the valley below them.

That night, God told Gideon, 'Get up and go down to their camp. I've already given it to you. But if you're feeling a little shaky, take your boy Purah with you. When you hear what they're saying, you'll be hyped and ready to go.' So he and Purah snuck down to the edge of the enemy camp. The Midianites, Amalekites, and all the easterners were everywhere, like a massive swarm of locusts. And their camels? You couldn't even count them, like sand on a beach.

Gideon got there just in time to overhear a guy telling his friend about a dream he had. He was like, 'Bro, I had this crazy dream. A loaf of barley bread just rolled into our camp, hit a tent so hard it just collapsed. The whole thing just fell flat!'
His friend was like, 'Dude, that's gotta be the sword of Gideon, the Israelite! God has handed Midian—our whole camp!—over to him.'
When Gideon heard the dream and what it meant, he dropped to his knees and prayed. Then he went back to his camp and said, 'Let's go, boys! God just gave us the whole Midianite army!'

He split the 300 men into three groups. He gave each guy a trumpet and an empty jar with a torch inside. He told them, 'Watch me and do exactly what I do. When I get to the edge of their camp, copy me. When I and my group blow our trumpets, you guys blow your trumpets all around the camp and shout, 'For God and for Gideon!''

Gideon and his 100 men reached the edge of the camp right at the beginning of the middle watch, just after they had changed guards. They blew their trumpets and smashed the jars they were holding. All three groups blew their trumpets and broke their jars. They held the torches in their left hands and the trumpets in their right, ready to blow, and shouted, 'A sword for God and for Gideon!' They were positioned all around the camp, each man at his post. The whole Midianite camp freaked out. They started yelling and running away. When the 300 blew their trumpets, God made the Midianites turn on each other with their swords, all over the camp. They ran for their lives—to Beth Shittah, toward Zererah, and to the border of Abel Meholah near Tabbath.
The Israelites from Naphtali, Asher, and all over Manasseh rallied and chased after the Midianites.
Gideon then sent messengers all over the hill country of Ephraim, saying, 'Come down and cut off the Midianites! Take control of the Jordan River crossings at Beth Barah.'

So all the men of Ephraim gathered and took control of the Jordan crossings at Beth Barah. They also captured the two Midianite commanders, Oreb (which means Raven) and Zeeb (which means Wolf). They killed Oreb at a place called Raven Rock and Zeeb at a place called Wolf Winepress. And they kept chasing the Midianites. They brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan.

Judges.title: Gideon's Epic Chase and Major Fail
paragraphs: Then the guys from Ephraim came to Gideon and were like, "Yo, why did you do us dirty like that, not calling us when you went to fight Midian?" They were seriously mad and totally called him out.

But Gideon smoothed it over, saying, "Chill, what have I really done compared to you all? Lowkey, even Ephraim's leftovers are better than the best my family, Abiezer, can do. God handed you Midian's top guys, Oreb and Zeeb. What have I done that even comes close to that?"
When they heard that, they calmed down.

Gideon and his 300 guys got to the Jordan River and crossed it. They were dead tired but still kept chasing the enemy. He asked the men of Succoth, "Please, can you give my crew some bread? They're exhausted, and I'm right on the heels of Zebah and Zalmunna, the Midianite kings."
But the leaders of Succoth were like, "LOL, why should we give your army food? You haven't even caught Zebah and Zalmunna yet. We're not helping you on some wild goose chase."
Gideon shot back, "Alright, bet. But when God hands Zebah and Zalmunna over to me, I'm coming back to tear you up. I'll literally whip your bare skin with desert thorns and thistles!"

He left and went to Peniel and asked for the same thing. The men of Peniel gave him the same answer as the men of Succoth. So Gideon told them, "When I come back victorious, I'm tearing this tower down."
Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their army, about 15,000 men. It was all that was left of the eastern armies—they had already lost 120,000 soldiers.

Gideon went up a back road, the caravan trail east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and surprise-attacked the camp when they weren't expecting it. Zebah and Zalmunna bounced, but Gideon chased them and captured the two Midianite kings. The whole camp was in total chaos.

Gideon, son of Joash, returned from the battle through the Heres Pass. He caught a young guy from Succoth and started questioning him. The kid wrote down the names of all the officials and leaders of Succoth, seventy-seven men in total. Then Gideon went to the men of Succoth and said, "Hey, remember those 'wild geese' Zebah and Zalmunna you said I'd never catch? Here they are. You wouldn't even give a piece of bread to my exhausted men and mocked us for being on a 'fool's errand.'"
Then he grabbed the seventy-seven leaders of Succoth and taught them a lesson with desert thorns and thistles. He also tore down the tower of Peniel and killed the men of that city.
Then he turned to Zebah and Zalmunna, "Tell me about the men you killed at Tabor."
They answered, "They looked a lot like you, actually. Each one looked like a prince."
Gideon said, "They were my brothers, my own mother's sons. I swear, if you had let them live, I would let you live now."
Then he said to his oldest son, Jether, "Get up and kill them." But Jether was too scared to draw his sword. He was still just a kid.
Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Do it yourself if you're man enough." So Gideon got up, killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and took the crescent-shaped ornaments that were on their camels' necks.
The Israelites told Gideon, "You should be our ruler! You, your son, and your grandson after you. You saved us from Midian!"
But Gideon said, "Nah, I'm not gonna rule over you, and neither is my son. God will be your ruler."
Then Gideon said, "But I do have one request. Can each of you give me an earring from the loot you took?" (The Ishmaelites all wore gold earrings, so the Israelites had a ton of them).
They were all for it. "Of course! Take them!"

They spread out a cloak, and every man threw the earrings he had plundered onto it. The gold earrings Gideon asked for weighed about 43 pounds! And that wasn't even counting the other bling—the crescents, pendants, the purple robes the Midianite kings wore, and the ornaments from their camels' necks.

Gideon melted all that gold and made a sacred ephod, which is like a priestly vestment. He put it on display in his hometown, Ophrah. But this was a big mistake. All of Israel started worshipping it, basically cheating on God. Even Gideon and his family got caught up in it.
And that's how Midian was finally defeated by the Israelites. They never caused trouble again. The land was peaceful for 40 years, all during Gideon's time.

Jerub-Baal (that's Gideon) son of Joash went back to his own house to live. Gideon had seventy sons of his own—he had a lot of wives! He also had a concubine in Shechem who had a son for him, and he named him Abimelech.
Gideon, son of Joash, died at a ripe old age. He was buried in his father Joash's tomb in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

But Gideon was barely cold in his grave when the Israelites went off the rails again. They started chasing after other gods, the Baals, and even made a pact with a god named Baal-of-the-Covenant. The people of Israel completely forgot about their God, who had saved them from all the enemies surrounding them. And they showed no loyalty to the family of Jerub-Baal (Gideon), completely dissing all the good things he had done for Israel.

Judges.title: Abimelech's Power Trip Ends in Epic Fail
paragraphs: Abimelech, son of Jerub-Baal, rolled up to Shechem to chat with his uncles and his mom's whole fam. He was like, "Yo, ask the leaders of Shechem, 'What's the move? You want seventy dudes—all of Jerub-Baal's sons—running things, or just one guy?' Don't forget, I'm your boy, your own flesh and blood."
His mom's relatives pitched the idea to the Shechem bosses. They were kinda feeling it, saying, "Yeah, he's one of us, for real."

So they hooked him up with seventy silver coins from the temple of Baal-of-the-Covenant. With that cash, he hired a bunch of reckless, broke guys to be his crew. He then dipped to his dad's house in Ophrah and straight-up murdered his seventy half-brothers, all on a single stone. It was brutal. Only the youngest, Jotham, son of Jerub-Baal, managed to hide and survive.
Then all the big shots from Shechem and Beth Millo met up at the big oak tree by the stone pillar in Shechem and crowned Abimelech king.
When Jotham heard about all this, he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim and yelled out to them:

"Listen up, leaders of Shechem! And let God hear you too! One day, the trees decided they wanted a king. They went to the Olive Tree and said, 'Rule over us.' But the Olive Tree was like, 'Nah, I'm good. Should I quit making this awesome oil that honors gods and people, just to wave over you guys? Hard pass.'

Then the trees asked the Fig Tree, 'You come and rule over us.' But the Fig Tree said, 'Seriously? I should stop making my super sweet, delicious fruit just to get demoted to waving over trees? No thanks.'
Then the trees hit up the Vine, 'You come and rule over us.' But the Vine was like, 'Get demoted from making wine that makes gods and people happy, just to wave over trees? You're buggin'.'

Finally, all the trees went to the Tumbleweed. 'You come and be our king.' And the Tumbleweed said, 'Aight, bet. If you're for real about making me king, then come chill in my shade. But if you're playing me, I'll spit fire and burn down the huge cedars of Lebanon!'

So, for real, do you think you did the right thing making Abimelech king? Did you treat Jerub-Baal and his family right? My dad fought for you, risked his life, and saved you from Midian. And what do you do? You turn on him. You massacred his sons—seventy guys on one stone! You made Abimelech, the son of his servant girl, king over Shechem just 'cause he's your relative. If you think that's cool, then enjoy your new king. But if not, let fire come from Abimelech and burn you all down. And let fire come from you and burn him up."
And with that, Jotham bounced. He ran for his life to a place called Beer and stayed there, terrified of his brother Abimelech.

Abimelech ruled Israel for three years. Then God stirred up some major drama between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem. They started plotting against him behind his back. The violence came back around like a boomerang. The murder of the seventy brothers was now haunting Abimelech and the Shechem leaders who helped him do it.
The Shechem leaders set up ambushes in the mountains to rob people on the roads, just to mess with Abimelech. And someone snitched to him about it.

Around that time, this guy Gaal, son of Ebed, moved to Shechem with his crew. The leaders of Shechem started trusting him. One day, they were out in the vineyards, picking grapes and making wine. They threw a huge party at their god's temple, eating and drinking, and then they started trash-talking Abimelech.

Gaal stood up and said, "Who even is this Abimelech? And who are we to take orders from him? Isn't he just Jerub-Baal's son, and Zebul is his little henchman? We're from the line of Hamor, the OG of Shechem. Why should we be his servants? If I were in charge, I'd get rid of Abimelech ASAP! I'd tell him, 'Let's see what you got, bro! Let's see who's the real boss!'"

Zebul, the governor of the city, heard all this and was furious. He secretly sent a message to Abimelech: "Gaal and his boys are in Shechem, stirring up trouble. Here's the plan: tonight, bring your army and hide in the fields. In the morning, as soon as the sun's up, rush the city. Gaal and his crew will come out to fight, and you'll know what to do."

So Abimelech and his four companies of soldiers went up that night and set an ambush near Shechem. Gaal was standing at the city gate in the morning when Abimelech and his troops came out of hiding. When Gaal saw them, he said to Zebul, "Look, there are people coming down from the mountains!"
Zebul said, "Nah, you're just seeing mountain shadows that look like people." But Gaal kept insisting.
Then he said, "Look! Troops are coming down from the center of the land, and another group is coming from the Oracle Oak tree."
Zebul shot back, "Where's your big talk now? You were the one saying, 'Who is Abimelech that we should obey him?' Well, there he is with his army you were dissing. Now's your chance. Go fight!"
Gaal went out with the leaders of Shechem and fought Abimelech. But Abimelech chased him down, and Gaal had to run for it. A lot of his men were wounded, all the way up to the city gate.
Abimelech set up his base at Arumah, and Zebul kicked Gaal and his relatives out of Shechem.

The next day, the people of Shechem went out to the fields, and someone told Abimelech. He split his army into three groups and ambushed them. When he saw the people out in the open, he attacked. Abimelech and his company charged and took control of the city gate, while the other two companies chased down and killed the people in the fields. Abimelech fought the city all day, captured it, and killed everyone inside. He then tore the city down and threw salt all over the ground.

When the leaders of the Tower of Shechem heard this, they ran to the fortified temple of their god. Someone told Abimelech they were all gathered there. So he and his troops climbed Mount Zalmon. Abimelech grabbed an ax, chopped a bunch of wood, and put it on his shoulder. He told his men, "Do what I do, and do it fast." So they all cut their own bundles of wood, followed Abimelech, piled the wood against the tower, and set it on fire. Everyone in the Tower of Shechem died, about a thousand men and women.

Then Abimelech went to Thebez, camped there, and captured it. In the middle of the city was a strong tower, and all the men and women of the city, including the leaders, had locked themselves inside on the roof. Abimelech got to the tower and tried to attack it. He went up to the door to set it on fire. But then, a woman on the roof dropped a millstone on his head and cracked his skull. He quickly called his young armor-bearer and said, "Pull out your sword and kill me. I don't want people saying, 'A woman killed him.'" So the young man stabbed him, and he died.
When the Israelites saw that Abimelech was dead, they all just went home.

And that's how God paid back the evil Abimelech did to his father by murdering his seventy brothers. God also brought down all the evil the men of Shechem had done, fulfilling the curse of Jotham, son of Jerub-Baal.

Judges.title: Israel Hits Rock Bottom (Again)
paragraphs: After Abimelech, the next guy to step up and save Israel was Tola, son of Puah, who was the son of Dodo. He was from the tribe of Issachar and lived in Shamir, up in the hill country of Ephraim. He led Israel for 23 years, then he died and was buried right there in Shamir.

Next up was Jair the Gileadite. He was in charge of Israel for 22 years. This guy had 30 sons, and they each had their own donkey and their own town in Gilead. To this day, those towns are still called Jair’s Villages. Then Jair died and was buried in Kamon.

And then, big surprise, the people of Israel went right back to doing what they knew was wrong in God's eyes. They started worshipping the Baal and Ashtoreth gods, plus a bunch of others from all over—Aram, Sidon, Moab, Ammon, and Philistia. They basically just walked away from God and stopped worshipping him altogether. So, God got super angry with Israel and was like, "Fine, deal with it yourselves." He let the Philistines and Ammonites take over. Starting that year, they totally bullied and beat down the Israelites. For 18 long years, all the Israelites living east of the Jordan in Gilead were crushed under their rule.
Then the Ammonites decided to cross the Jordan River to start beef with Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim too. Israel was in a seriously bad spot.
The Israelites finally cried out to God for help, saying, "We messed up! We sinned against you! We abandoned our God and started worshipping the Baals!"

God shot back, "Remember when the Egyptians, Amorites, Ammonites, Philistines, Sidonians, Amalekites, and Midianites were all oppressing you? You cried out to me, and I saved you from all of them. But what did you do? You turned your backs on me and started worshipping other gods. I'm done saving you. Go on, cry out to the gods you chose! Let's see if they can get you out of this mess you're in!"
The Israelites pleaded with God, "We have sinned. Do whatever you want to us, but please, just save us this one time!"
Then they actually did something about it. They got rid of all the foreign gods and started worshipping only God again. And seeing that, God started to feel for them and their suffering.

The Ammonite army got ready for war and set up their camp in Gilead. The Israelites gathered their own army and set up a camp across from them in Mizpah. The leaders in Gilead were talking amongst themselves, saying, "Whoever steps up to lead the fight against the Ammonites, we'll make him the head of everyone in Gilead!"

Judges.title: He Made a Promise He Couldn't Keep...
paragraphs: So, there was this guy Jephthah from Gilead, a total beast in a fight. Here's the tea: his dad was Gilead, but his mom was a prostitute. Gilead's actual wife had other sons, and when they got older, they kicked Jephthah out. They were like, 'You're not getting any of our dad's money, you're the son of some other lady.' So Jephthah bounced, moved to a place called Tob, and linked up with a crew of outcasts.

A while later, the Ammonites decided to throw hands with Israel. With a war kicking off, the leaders of Gilead went to find Jephthah in Tob. They told him, 'Yo, come be our commander, and we'll take on the Ammonites.'
But Jephthah was like, 'Hold up. Y'all hate me. You threw me out of my own house. Why are you crawling back to me now? Oh, right, 'cause you're in deep trouble.'
The Gilead leaders were straight up: 'You're right. That's why we're here. We need you to come with us and fight the Ammonites. You'll be the leader of all of us, all the Gileadites.'
Jephthah laid it out for them: 'So if you bring me back to fight the Ammonites and God lets me win, I'll be your leader for real? Is that the deal?'

They promised, 'God is our witness. Whatever you say, we'll do.' So Jephthah went with the Gilead leaders. The people made him their top dog and commander. And Jephthah repeated his terms before God at a place called Mizpah.
Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites with a message: 'What's your problem? Why are you coming into my country trying to start a fight?'

The Ammonite king shot back to Jephthah's messengers: 'Because Israel jacked my land when they came out of Egypt—from the Arnon river all the way to the Jabbok and the Jordan. Give it back peacefully and I'll leave.'

Jephthah sent messengers again to the Ammonite king, basically saying: 'Here's the history, my dude. Israel didn't take any Moabite or Ammonite land. When they came up from Egypt, Israel went through the desert to the Red Sea and got to Kadesh. There, Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom saying, 'Please let us pass through your land.' But the king of Edom was like, 'Nah.' Israel asked the king of Moab for permission too, but he also said no. They were stuck at Kadesh. So they went the long way around the lands of Edom and Moab. They came out east of Moab and camped on the other side of the Arnon river—they didn't even step foot in Moabite territory, because the Arnon was the border. Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorites, and asked, 'Can we please pass through your land to get to our country?' But Sihon didn't trust Israel. He got his whole army together, camped at Jahaz, and fought Israel. But God, the God of Israel, handed Sihon and his army over to Israel. Israel defeated them and took all the Amorite land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the desert to the Jordan. It was God, the God of Israel, who kicked out the Amorites for Israel; so who do you think you are trying to take it back? Why don't you just be happy with what your god Chemosh gives you, and we'll keep what our God gives us? You think you're better than Balak, the king of Moab? Did he ever mess with Israel? Did he start a war? Israel has been living in Heshbon and its villages, in Aroer and its villages, and in all the towns along the Arnon for 300 years! Why didn't you try to take them back then? Look, I haven't done anything wrong to you. But you're the one being shady by starting a fight. Today, God the Judge will decide who's right between the people of Israel and the people of Ammon.'
But the king of the Ammonites completely ignored the message Jephthah sent.

Then God's Spirit came on Jephthah. He went through Gilead and Manasseh, passed through Mizpah of Gilead, and from there went to face the Ammonites. Jephthah made a wild vow to God: 'If you give me a clear win over the Ammonites, then whatever comes out of my house to meet me when I get back safely, I'll offer it to God as a burnt offering.'

Then Jephthah went off to fight the Ammonites. And God gave him the victory. He totally wrecked them, from Aroer all the way to the area around Minnith, as far as Abel Keramim—twenty cities! It was a massacre. The Ammonites were completely humbled by the people of Israel.

Jephthah came home to Mizpah. And who runs out of the house to greet him? His daughter, dancing with tambourines! She was his one and only child. He had no other sons or daughters. When he saw it was her, he ripped his clothes in despair, crying, 'Oh no, my sweet daughter—you've destroyed me. I'm a wreck. My heart is shattered. I made a vow to God and I can't take it back!'
She said, 'Dad, if you made a vow to God, you have to do what you promised. God did his part and saved you from your enemies, the Ammonites.'
Then she said to her father, 'But just do this one thing for me. Give me two months to go up into the hills and mourn with my friends that I'll never get married.'

'Okay, go,' he said. He sent her away for two months. She and her friends went into the hills, grieving that she would never get married. At the end of the two months, she came back to her father. And he did what he had vowed to do with her. She had never been with a man.
And it became a tradition in Israel that for four days every year, the young women of Israel would go out to mourn for the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite.

Judges.title: The Password Is 'Shibboleth'
paragraphs: The guys from Ephraim got their whole squad together, crossed over to Zaphon, and rolled up on Jephthah like, 'Yo, why'd you go fight the Ammonites and not even invite us? We're about to burn your house down with you in it.'

Jephthah was like, 'Me and my people were in a seriously tough spot trying to deal with the Ammonites. I actually hit you guys up for help, but you totally ghosted me. When I saw you weren't showing, I basically put my life on the line and went at the Ammonites myself. And God came through and gave me the W! So why are you even here now? You trying to start something?'

So Jephthah rounded up his Gilead crew and went to battle with Ephraim. And the Gileadites wrecked them because the Ephraimites were trash-talking, saying stuff like, 'Gileadites are just a bunch of wannabe rejects from Ephraim and Manasseh.'

The Gileadites took control of the river crossings of the Jordan that led to Ephraim. If some dude from Ephraim who was on the run was like, 'Let me cross,' the Gileadite soldiers would ask, 'You from Ephraim?' and he'd be like, 'Nah.' Then they'd say, 'Alright, say "Shibboleth."' But he'd always mess it up and say 'Sibboleth'—he just couldn't pronounce it right. So they'd grab him and take him out right there at the Jordan crossings. A wild 42,000 Ephraimite soldiers died that day.
Jephthah was Israel's leader for six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in his hometown, Mizpah of Gilead.

After him, Ibzan from Bethlehem became the leader of Israel. He had thirty sons and thirty daughters. He had his daughters marry guys from outside his clan and brought in thirty girls from outside the clan for his sons to marry.
He was Israel's leader for seven years. Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
After him, Elon the Zebulunite was Israel's leader. He led Israel for ten years. Then Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried at Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.

After him, Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite was Israel's leader. He had forty sons and thirty grandsons who all rode on seventy donkeys. He was Israel's leader for eight years. Then Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried at Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the Amalekite hill country.

Judges.title: An Angel Announces a Super-Baby!
paragraphs: So, the people of Israel were at it again, doing what they knew was wrong in God's eyes. Because of this, God let the Philistines rule over them for forty years.

During this time, there was a guy named Manoah from Zorah, part of the Dan tribe. His wife couldn't have kids, which was a big deal back then. One day, an angel of God showed up and told her, "Hey, I know you haven't been able to have children, but you're about to get pregnant and have a son. But listen up, this is important: Don't drink any wine or beer, and don't eat any food that's considered unclean. You're actually pregnant right now with a son. A razor is never to touch his head because this boy will be a Nazirite—set apart for God—from the day he's born. He's the one who will start the process of freeing Israel from the Philistines."

The woman rushed to her husband and said, "A man of God just came to me! He looked like an angel of God—it was lowkey terrifying but also glorious. I didn't even think to ask where he was from, and he didn't tell me his name. But he told me, 'You're pregnant and you're going to have a son. Don't drink any wine or beer, and don't eat anything unclean. This boy will be a Nazirite for God from his birth until the day he dies.'"
Manoah prayed to God, saying, "Lord, please let the man of God you sent come back to us and teach us how we're supposed to raise this boy who is going to be born."

God heard Manoah's prayer. The angel of God came back to the woman while she was sitting out in a field; her husband, Manoah, wasn't with her. She immediately jumped up, ran, and told her husband, "He's back! The man who came to me the other day is here!"
Manoah got up, followed his wife, and went to the man. He asked him, "Are you the man who spoke to my wife?"
He replied, "I am."
Manoah then said, "Okay, so when everything you've said happens, what are the rules for the boy? What's his life's work going to be?"

The angel of God told Manoah, "Just make sure your wife follows all the instructions I gave her. She shouldn't eat anything that comes from a grapevine, drink no wine or beer, and eat no unclean foods. She has to do everything I commanded."
Manoah then said to the angel of God, "Please, stay a bit longer. We want to prepare a meal for you, like a young goat."

The angel of God said to Manoah, "Even if I stay, I won't eat your food. But if you want to prepare a burnt offering, offer it to God." Manoah still had no idea he was talking to an actual angel of God.
Then Manoah asked the angel of God, "What's your name? We want to honor you when your prediction comes true."
The angel of God replied, "Why are you asking for my name? It's too wonderful for you to understand—it's a total mystery."

So Manoah took the young goat and a grain offering and sacrificed them on a rock as an altar to the God who does amazing things. As the fire from the altar blazed up toward the sky, the angel of God went up in the flames. When Manoah and his wife saw this, they fell flat on their faces on the ground. They never saw the angel of God again.
It was only then that Manoah finally realized it was the angel of God. He said to his wife, "We're dead. We've seen God!"

But his wife replied, "Chill out. If God wanted to kill us, he wouldn't have accepted our burnt offering and grain offering. And he wouldn't have revealed all these things to us or given us this birth announcement."

The woman gave birth to a son, and they named him Samson. The boy grew up, and God blessed him. The Spirit of God started to stir in him while he was living at the Danite camp between Zorah and Eshtaol.

Judges.title: Samson's Riddle Goes Terribly Wrong
paragraphs: So Samson heads down to Timnah and, boom, this Philistine girl totally catches his eye. He gets back and tells his parents, 'Yo, I saw this girl in Timnah, she's a Philistine, but you gotta get her for me. I want to marry her.'
His parents were like, 'Seriously? Are there zero girls from our own people good enough for you? You really have to go marry some girl from the uncircumcised Philistines?'
But Samson just told his dad, 'Get her for me. She's the one. No cap.'
(Plot twist: his parents had no clue that God was orchestrating this whole thing. He was setting up a chance to mess with the Philistines, who were basically controlling Israel back then.)

So Samson goes down to Timnah with his mom and dad. As he's getting to the vineyards there, a young lion straight up charges him, roaring like crazy. The Spirit of God just floods him with power, and he literally rips the lion apart with his bare hands, like tearing a baby goat. But he kept it lowkey and didn't tell his parents what he'd done.
Then he went and talked to the girl. And yeah, in his mind, she was definitely the one.

A few days later, when he was heading back to marry her, he took a detour to check out the dead lion. And get this—it was wild. There was a swarm of bees and honey inside the lion's carcass! He scooped a bunch of it into his hands and kept walking, eating it as he went. When he met up with his parents, he gave them some and they ate it. But he never told them he got the honey from the dead lion.

His dad went down to the girl's place to finalize the wedding plans, and Samson threw a huge feast, which was the custom for young guys back then. The local people were kind of sketched out by him, so they sent thirty dudes to be his 'buddies' at the party.

Samson says to them, 'Alright, I've got a riddle for you. If you can solve it during the seven days of this feast, I'll give each of you a fresh set of nice clothes. But if you can't figure it out, you guys owe me thirty sets of clothes.'
They were like, 'Okay, bet. Tell us the riddle.' So he said,
'From the eater came something to eat, From the strong came something sweet.'

They could not figure it out. Three days went by and they were still clueless. On the fourth day, they went to Samson's new wife and said, 'You better trick your husband into telling you the answer, or we're gonna burn you and your father's house down. Did you invite us here just to make us go broke or what?'
So Samson's wife starts bawling to him, 'You hate me! You don't really love me! You told my people a riddle, but you won't even tell me the answer?'
He was like, 'Look, I haven't even told my own parents. Why would I tell you?'

But she just kept crying and nagging him for the whole seven-day feast. Finally, on the seventh day, he was so worn out from her whining that he told her the answer. And of course, she immediately went and told her people.
So, on the seventh day, right before sunset, the men of the town came to him and said,
'What's sweeter than honey? What's stronger than a lion?'
And Samson said,
'If you hadn't plowed with my heifer, you wouldn't have solved my riddle.'

Then the Spirit of God came over him with power. He went down to the town of Ashkelon, killed thirty of their men, took their clothes, and gave them to the guys who solved the riddle. He was absolutely fuming. He stormed off and went back to his father's house. And his wife? She ended up getting married to the guy who was his best man.

Judges.title: Samson's Jawbone Rampage
paragraphs: A little while later, during the wheat harvest, Samson went to see his wife. He brought a young goat as a gift and was like, "I'm here to see my wife, let me into her room."

But her dad straight up blocked him. He said, "Look, I honestly thought you hated her, so I gave her to your best man. But hey, her younger sister is even prettier. You should totally take her instead."
Samson was like, "Oh, it's on. After this, when I totally wreck the Philistines, no one can blame me."

So Samson went out and caught 300 jackals. This is wild—he tied their tails together in pairs and stuck a torch in each knot. Then he lit the torches and sent the jackals running through the Philistines' grain fields. Everything got torched—the harvested grain, the standing grain, and even the vineyards and olive groves.
The Philistines were freaking out, asking, "Who did this?!"
Someone told them, "It was Samson, the Timnite's son-in-law. The one whose wife was given to his best man."
So the Philistines went and, no cap, burned both the woman and her father to death.
When Samson heard, he said, "If that's how you're gonna play, I swear I'm getting you back for this. And I'm not stopping until I'm done!"
And then he just went off on them, a total rampage. It was a huge slaughter. After that, he went to chill in a cave at Etam Rock.

The Philistines gathered their army and set up camp in Judah, getting ready to attack a place called Lehi (which means Jawbone). The men of Judah were like, "Yo, why are you guys coming after us?" and they replied, "We're here for Samson. We're gonna do to him what he did to us."
So, 3,000 guys from Judah went down to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, "Dude, don't you get it? The Philistines are in charge of us. What are you doing making them even angrier?"
He was just like, "It was payback. I only did to them what they did to me."
They said, "Well, we're here to tie you up and hand you over to the Philistines."
Samson said, "Just swear you won't kill me yourselves."
"We swear," they said. "We'll just tie you up and give you to them. We promise we won't kill you." So they tied him up with brand new ropes and led him away from the rock.

As he got near Lehi, the Philistines came out to meet him, all shouting and celebrating. But then the Spirit of God came over Samson with some serious power. The ropes on his arms just melted off like they were nothing, and the bindings on his hands slipped right off. He saw a fresh donkey jawbone on the ground, picked it up, and killed a thousand men with it. Then Samson said,
"With a donkey's jawbone, I made donkeys out of them. With a donkey's jawbone, I killed a thousand men."
When he was done, he threw the jawbone away. And he named that place Ramath Lehi, which means "Jawbone Hill."

But then he was suddenly super thirsty. He cried out to God, "You just gave me this huge win. Are you really gonna let me die of thirst now and get captured by these guys?" So God split open a rock, and water gushed out. Samson drank it and felt his energy come back—he was alive! That's why the spring is called En Hakkore (which means "Caller's Spring"), and it's still there in Lehi today.
Samson was Israel's leader for twenty years, all during the time of the Philistines.

Judges.title: Samson's Final Betrayal & Revenge
paragraphs: So, Samson went to Gaza, saw a prostitute, and went to her place. The news spread like wildfire: “Samson’s here.” So people gathered and hid, waiting all night for him at the city gate, being super quiet. They were thinking, “At sunrise, we’ll kill him.”

Samson was in bed with the woman until midnight. Then he got up, grabbed the doors of the city gate and the two gateposts, bolts and all, put them on his shoulder, and carried them to the top of the hill that faces Hebron. What a legend.

Some time later, he fell in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah. The Philistine leaders went to her and said, “Seduce him. Find out what’s behind his great strength and how we can tie him up and humble him. Each of us will give you a hundred shekels of silver.”
So Delilah said to Samson, “Tell me, dear, the secret of your great strength, and how you can be tied up and humbled.”
Samson told her, “If they were to tie me up with seven fresh bowstrings—the kind made from fresh animal tendons, not dried out—then I would become weak, just like anyone else.”

The Philistine leaders brought her seven fresh bowstrings, and she tied him up with them. The men were waiting in ambush in her room. Then she said, “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” He snapped the cords as though they were just threads. The secret of his strength was still a secret.
Delilah said, “Come on, Samson—you’re playing with me, making up stories. Be serious; tell me how you can be tied up.”
He told her, “If you were to tie me up tight with new ropes, ropes never used for work, then I would be helpless, just like anybody else.”
So Delilah got some new ropes and tied him up. She said, “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” The men were hidden in the next room. He snapped the ropes from his arms like threads.
Delilah said to Samson, “You’re still playing games with me, teasing me with lies. Tell me how you can be tied up.”
He said to her, “If you wove the seven braids of my hair into the fabric on the loom and drew it tight, then I would be as helpless as any other mortal.”

When she had him fast asleep, Delilah took the seven braids of his hair and wove them into the fabric on the loom and drew it tight. Then she said, “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” He woke from his sleep and ripped loose from both the loom and fabric!
She said, “How can you say ‘I love you’ when you won’t even trust me? Three times now you’ve toyed with me, like a cat with a mouse, refusing to tell me the secret of your great strength.”
She kept at it day after day, nagging and tormenting him. Finally, he was fed up—he couldn’t take another minute of it. He spilled it.
He told her, “A razor has never touched my head. I’ve been God’s Nazirite from conception. If I were shaved, my strength would leave me; I would be as helpless as any other mortal.”
When Delilah realized that he had told her his secret, she sent for the Philistine leaders, telling them, “Come quickly—this time he’s told me the truth.” They came, bringing the bribe money.
When she got him to sleep, his head on her lap, she motioned to a man to cut off the seven braids of his hair. Immediately he began to grow weak. His strength drained from him.
Then she said, “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” He woke up, thinking, “I’ll go out, like always, and shake free.” He didn’t realize that God had abandoned him.

The Philistines grabbed him, gouged out his eyes, and took him down to Gaza. They shackled him in irons and put him to the work of grinding in the prison. But his hair, though cut off, began to grow again.
The Philistine leaders got together to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon. They celebrated, saying,
Our god has given us Samson our enemy!
And when the people saw him, they joined in, cheering their god,
Our god has given Our enemy to us, The one who ravaged our country, Piling high the corpses among us.
Then this: Everyone was feeling high and someone said, “Get Samson! Let him show us his stuff!” They got Samson from the prison and he put on a show for them.

They had him standing between the pillars. Samson said to the young man who was acting as his guide, “Put me where I can touch the pillars that hold up the temple so I can rest against them.” The building was packed with men and women, including all the Philistine leaders. And there were at least three thousand in the stands watching Samson’s performance.
And Samson cried out to God:
Master, God! Oh, please, look on me again, Oh, please, give strength yet once more.
God! With one avenging blow let me be avenged On the Philistines for my two eyes!

Then Samson reached out to the two central pillars that held up the building and pushed against them, one with his right arm, the other with his left. Saying, “Let me die with the Philistines,” Samson pushed hard with all his might. The building crashed on the leaders and all the people in it. He killed more people in his death than he had killed in his life.
His brothers and all his relatives went down to get his body. They carried him back and buried him in the tomb of Manoah his father, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
He judged Israel for twenty years.

Judges.title: My Mom's Stolen Money & My DIY Religion
paragraphs: So there was this guy named Micah from the hill country of Ephraim. He went to his mom and was like, “Hey, you know that 1,100 silver pieces that went missing? I heard you putting a curse on whoever took them. Well… surprise, it was me. I have the money. I stole it, but I’m giving it back to you now.”
His mom said, “Oh, God bless you, my son!”

When he handed the 1,100 silver pieces back, his mom said, “I had actually set this money aside for God, for you to make a sick statue, a cast idol.” Then she took 200 of the silver pieces, gave them to a sculptor, and he made it into a god-statue for them.
This dude Micah had his own personal chapel. He had made a special priest vest and some other little idols, and he even appointed one of his own sons to be his priest.
This was back in the day when Israel had no king. It was lowkey chaotic; everyone just did whatever they wanted.

Meanwhile, there was this young Levite guy from Bethlehem in Judah. He was just passing through, trying to find a place to live and work. He left his hometown of Bethlehem and was just wandering, and his journey took him to the hill country of Ephraim, right to Micah’s house.
Micah asked him, “Yo, where you from?”
He answered, “I’m a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah. I’m just looking for a place to crash and maybe find some work.”
Micah was like, “Bet. Why don’t you stay with me? You can be like a father and a priest to me. I’ll pay you ten silver pieces a year, give you a fresh set of clothes, and cover all your meals.”

The Levite was down for it and decided to stay. The young guy fit in perfectly and basically became part of the family. Micah officially made the young Levite his priest, and he lived right there in Micah’s house.
Micah was stoked. He said, “Now I know for sure God’s gonna bless me. No cap, I’ve got an actual Levite as my priest!”

Judges.title: The Great God Heist & Priest Poaching
paragraphs: So, back in the day, Israel didn't have a king, which was kinda chaotic. And the tribe of Dan was basically looking for a place to call home because they hadn't locked down their own territory yet among the other Israelite tribes.
The Danites picked five of their strongest dudes from Zorah and Eshtaol and sent them to scout out the land and find a good spot for their families. The mission was simple: "Go explore the land."

They traveled up to the hill country of Ephraim and ended up near some guy named Micah's house. They decided to crash there for the night. As they got closer, they heard a voice they recognized—it was the young Levite guy. They went over to him and were like, "Whoa, how did you end up here? What’s the story? What are you even doing?"
He explained, "Well, one thing led to another... Micah hired me, and now I'm his personal priest."
They were like, "Oh, perfect! Can you ask God for us if our mission's gonna be a success?"
The priest told them, "Yeah, for sure. Go for it. God's watching out for you the whole way."

The five guys left and went north to a town called Laish. They saw the people there were living super chill and safe, protected by the Sidonians, not suspecting a thing. They were living the good life. But, they were super far from the Sidonians and had no alliances with anyone else.
When the scouts got back to their people in Zorah and Eshtaol, their brothers asked, "So? What's the verdict?"

They said, "Let's GO! We have to attack. We saw the land, and it's seriously amazing. Are you guys just gonna sit around? Don't wait! Let's go invade and take it! When you get there, you'll see they're total sitting ducks, completely clueless. It's wide-open land, and God is basically handing it to you on a silver platter—everything you could ever want."

So, six hundred men from the tribe of Dan, armed to the teeth, set out from Zorah and Eshtaol. On their way, they camped at Kiriath Jearim in Judah. That's why the place is still called Dan's Camp today. From there, they continued into the hill country of Ephraim and showed up at Micah's house.

The five guys who had scouted Laish told the others, "Yo, quick heads up. In these buildings, there's a sacred ephod, some household idols, and a cast metal god statue. You know what that means, right? Should we... do something about it?"

So they took a detour, went to the young Levite's house at Micah's place, and asked him how he was doing. While they were chatting, the six hundred armed Danite soldiers stood guard at the gate. The five scouts then went inside and just took everything: the carved idol, the ephod, the other idols, and the metal god statue. The priest, who was standing at the gate with the soldiers, saw them and was like, "Umm, what do you think you're doing?"
They told him, "Shhh! Keep it down. Come with us. Be our father and our priest. What's better: being a priest for one guy, or being the priest for a whole tribe and clan in Israel?"
The priest was totally sold. He grabbed the ephod, the idols, and the main idol and joined up with them.

They all turned and left, putting the kids, the livestock, and all their stuff in the front for protection. They were a good distance from Micah's house before Micah and his neighbors finally got their act together and chased after them. They started shouting at the Danites. The Danites turned around and said, "What's with all the noise? What's your problem?"
Micah yelled back, "You stole my god, the one I made! And you took my priest! And just left! What do I have left? And you have the nerve to ask, 'What's your problem?'"
But the Danites just said, "You better stop yelling at us, or you might tick off some of these fierce, short-tempered guys, and you and your whole crew will end up dead."
The Danites just kept on walking. Micah realized he was seriously outmatched and had no chance against them. He turned around and went home, defeated.

So the Danites took the stuff Micah had made, and his priest, and they got to Laish, that city of quiet, unsuspecting people. They went in, massacred everyone, and burned the whole city to the ground.

There was no one to save them. They were too far from Sidon, and they didn't have a treaty with anyone else. The city was in the valley of Beth Rehob. The Danites rebuilt the city and renamed it Dan, after their ancestor, who was one of Israel's sons. Its original name was Laish.

The Danites set up the idol for themselves. And Jonathan, son of Gershom, who was the son of Moses, and his descendants became the priests for the tribe of Dan, and they stayed in that role until the whole land was taken into captivity. They kept and used the idol that Micah had made for their own private worship the entire time the official sanctuary of God was in Shiloh.

Judges.title: A Road Trip Goes Horribly Wrong
paragraphs: So, back in the day when Israel didn't have a king, there was this Levite dude living way out in the Ephraim hills. He had a side-chick, a concubine, from Bethlehem in Judah. But they got into a massive fight, and she just up and left, going back to her dad's place in Bethlehem. She was there for four months.

Finally, her husband decided to go get her and try to smooth things over. He brought a servant and a couple of donkeys with him. When he showed up at her dad's house, the dad was super welcoming and made him feel right at home. His father-in-law was all like, 'You gotta stay!' So he ended up staying for three days, just eating, drinking, and crashing there.
On the fourth day, they were up super early, ready to leave. But the girl's dad said to him, 'Yo, you need a good breakfast before you go.' So they sat down and ate together again.
Then the dad was like, 'C'mon, just stay the night. Make it a whole thing.' The guy got up to leave, but his father-in-law was so persistent that he caved and stayed another night.

On the fifth day, he was up early again, ready to hit the road. The girl's dad said, 'You need some breakfast.' They went back and forth, and before they knew it, the day was slipping away as they ate and drank. But the man and his concubine were finally, for real, ready to go. Then his father-in-law said, 'Look, the sun's almost down—why not just stay one more night? There's barely any daylight left. Stay and chill. You can get an early start tomorrow and head home.'

But this time, the guy was done. He was not about to spend another night there. He packed up, left, and made it as far as Jebus (which is now Jerusalem) with his two donkeys, his concubine, and his servant. By the time they got to Jebus, though, it was almost dark. The servant said to his master, 'It's late, let's just crash in this Jebusite city for the night.'

But his master was like, 'Nah, we're not staying in some city full of foreigners. We'll push on to Gibeah.' He told his servant, 'Keep going. Let's just get ahead. We'll find a place in either Gibeah or Ramah.'
So they kept going. As they pushed on, the sun finally set on them when they were near Gibeah, which was in Benjamin's territory. They got off the main road to find a place to stay in Gibeah.

The Levite went and sat in the town square, but legit no one invited them in for the night. Then, late in the evening, an old man came in from working in his fields. He was from the Ephraim hills too, just temporarily living in Gibeah where everyone else was a Benjaminite. The old man saw the traveler in the square and asked, 'Where are you headed? And where are you from?'

The Levite said, 'We're just passing through. We came from Bethlehem and we're heading to our home way out in the Ephraim hills. I'm from there. I just went to Bethlehem in Judah and now I'm on my way home, but nobody's offered us a place to stay. We wouldn't be any trouble, though. We have our own food and straw for the donkeys, and bread and wine for me, the woman, and the young man—we're all set.'
The old man said, 'It's all good, I'll take care of you. You are not spending the night in the town square.' He took them to his house and fed their donkeys. They all washed up and had a good meal.

They were just chilling and having a good time when the men of the city, a whole gang of local troublemakers, surrounded the house and started banging on the door. They yelled at the old man who owned the house, 'Bring out the guy who came to your house! We want to have sex with him.'

The owner went out and was like, 'No, my dudes! Don't be disgusting—this man is my guest. Don't do this horrible thing. Look, I have my virgin daughter and his concubine here. I'll bring them out. You can abuse them if you have to, but don't do something so messed up to this man.'

But the men wouldn't listen. So, the Levite pushed his concubine out the door to them. They raped her over and over, all night long. They finally let her go just before dawn. The woman stumbled back and collapsed at the door of the house where her master was. When the sun came up, she was still there.
It was morning. Her master got up, opened the door to leave, and there she was—his concubine, crumpled in a heap at the door, with her hands on the threshold.
'Get up,' he said. 'Let's go.' But there was no answer.

He lifted her onto his donkey and headed home. When he got there, he took a knife and... he dismembered his concubine. He cut her into twelve pieces. He sent a piece to every part of Israel. And he told the men he sent, 'Go say to every man in Israel: 'Has anything like this ever happened since the Israelites came up from Egypt until now? Think about it. Talk about it. And then do something!''

Judges.title: The Entire Nation vs. One Tribe: Civil War Goes Wild
paragraphs: So, basically all of Israel showed up. The whole crew gathered before God at a place called Mizpah. We're talking everyone, from the northern border to the southern one, all united as one. The leaders from every single tribe of Israel were there, taking their spots in the assembly. They brought an army of 400,000 infantry guys with swords.
Meanwhile, the tribe of Benjamin heard that the Israelites were all meeting up at Mizpah.
The Israelites were like, "Alright, spill the tea. How did this messed-up situation even happen?"

The Levite guy, the husband of the woman who was murdered, stood up and told his story: "My concubine and I were just looking for a place to crash for the night in Gibeah, which is in Benjamin's territory. That night, the guys from Gibeah came after me. They surrounded the house, and they were planning to kill me. They gang-raped my concubine, and she died. So I took her body, cut it into twelve pieces, and sent a piece to every single part of Israel. A truly vile and disgusting crime happened in Israel! So, fellow Israelites, you gotta decide what to do. It's time for action!"

Instantly, everyone was on their feet, totally unified. "None of us are going home. Not a single one. Here's the plan for Gibeah: we'll draw lots to see who goes against it. We'll have ten guys out of every hundred from all the tribes—that's a hundred out of every thousand, and a thousand out of every ten thousand—to carry supplies for the army. When our troops get to Gibeah, they're going to make them pay for the disgusting and evil thing they did in Israel." So, all the men of Israel gathered to attack the city, completely united.

The Israelite tribes sent messengers to the whole tribe of Benjamin, saying, "What is up with this disgusting thing that happened among you? Hand over those scumbags from Gibeah right now. We're going to execute them and get rid of this evil from Israel."

But they totally refused. The Benjaminites wouldn't listen to their own brothers, the people of Israel. Instead, they rounded up an army from all their cities and gathered at Gibeah to fight against the Israelites. In no time, they had 26 divisions of infantry with swords. From Gibeah itself, they had 700 elite, hand-picked fighters. On top of that, there were another 700 super-skilled guys who were ambidextrous—they could sling a stone at a single hair and not miss. Wild.
The Israelite army, not including Benjamin, had 400 divisions of fighting men with swords.
They headed out and went to Bethel to ask God for guidance. The Israelites asked, "Who should go first to fight the Benjaminites?"
God said, "Judah goes first."

The next morning, the Israelites got up and set up camp outside Gibeah. The Israelite army marched out against Benjamin and got into their battle positions, ready to attack Gibeah. But the Benjaminites charged out of Gibeah and absolutely wrecked twenty-two Israelite divisions.
The Israelites went back to the sanctuary and cried before God until evening. They asked God again, "Should we go back and fight our brothers, the Benjaminites?"
God said, "Yeah. Attack."
The army felt more confident. The men of Israel went back to the same positions they had on the first day.
On the second day, the Israelites went up against Benjamin again. But when the Benjaminites came out of the city this time, they wrecked another eighteen Israelite divisions, all of them swordsmen.
All the people of Israel, the entire army, went back to Bethel, crying and sitting in God's presence. They fasted all day until evening and offered up sacrifices to God.

And they asked God for guidance again. The Ark of the Covenant was there at the time, and Phinehas, the son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron, was the priest. They asked, "Should we go out and fight our brothers, the Benjaminites, again? Or should we just give up?"
And God said, "Attack. Tomorrow, I'll give you the win."
