At that exact moment, the Spirit of God left Saul, and instead, this dark mood sent by God just settled over him. He was totally freaked out.

Saul’s advisors were like, “This awful, tormenting depression from God is making your life a nightmare. Sir, let us help. We can find someone who can play the harp. When that dark mood from God comes over you, he’ll play his music, and you’ll feel better.”
Saul told his servants, “Alright, do it. Find me someone who’s a good musician and bring him to me.”

One of the young guys spoke up, “I know a guy. I’ve seen him myself: he’s the son of Jesse from Bethlehem, and he’s an amazing musician. He’s also brave, old enough, speaks well, and is good-looking. Plus, God is with him.”
So Saul sent messengers to Jesse, saying, “Send me your son David, the one who takes care of the sheep.”

Jesse got a donkey, loaded it up with some bread, a flask of wine, and a young goat, and sent his son David with it to Saul. David came to Saul and stood before him. Saul instantly liked him and made him his right-hand man.
Saul sent a message back to Jesse: “Thanks. David’s staying here. He’s exactly who I was looking for. I’m super impressed by him.”
After that, whenever the bad depression from God would hit Saul, David would take out his harp and play. It would calm Saul down, and he’d feel better as the bad mood went away.

1 Samuel.title: David vs. Goliath: The Ultimate Showdown
paragraphs: So the Philistines got their squad ready for a fight. They set up at Socoh in Judah, camping between Socoh and Azekah at a place called Ephes Dammim. Saul and the Israelites linked up, made camp in Oak Valley, and got in formation, ready to take on the Philistines. The Philistines were on one hill, the Israelites on the hill across from them, with a whole valley in between.

Then this absolute unit, a giant who was almost ten feet tall, stepped out from the Philistine line. It was Goliath from Gath. He had a bronze helmet on and was decked out in armor that weighed, like, 126 pounds! He had on bronze shin guards and was carrying a bronze sword. His spear was massive, like a fence rail, and the spearhead alone was over fifteen pounds. He even had a guy walking in front of him just to carry his shield.

Goliath just stood there and yelled over to the Israelite army, “Why are you even bothering to bring out your whole army? Aren't I enough? And you're all Team Saul, right? So just pick your best fighter and let him fight me. If he wins and takes me out, we Philistines will be your slaves. But if I win and take him out, you'll all be our slaves and work for us. I'm calling out the army of Israel today. Send me a man. Let's settle this one-on-one!”
When Saul and his troops heard what the Philistine said, they were seriously freaked out and felt totally hopeless.

But then, David shows up. He was the son of Jesse, an Ephrathite from Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons and was too old to join Saul's army himself. His three oldest sons had gone off to war with Saul. The three who went were Eliab, the oldest; Abinadab, the second; and Shammah, the third. David was the youngest. While his three older brothers were with Saul at the war, David was going back and forth between helping Saul and taking care of his dad's sheep in Bethlehem.
For forty days, Goliath would come out every morning and evening and give his little speech.

One day, Jesse told his son David, “Take this bag of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread and run them over to your brothers at the camp. And take these ten blocks of cheese to their captain. See how your brothers are doing, and bring me back some kind of proof that they're okay. You know, with Saul and your brothers and all the Israelites fighting the Philistines in Oak Valley.”

David got up super early, found someone to watch the sheep, grabbed the food, and headed out just like Jesse told him. He got to the camp right as the army was moving into their battle lines, shouting their war cry. Israel and the Philistines were getting into position, facing off, ready to fight. David left his stuff with a guard, ran to the battle lines, and said hi to his brothers. While they were catching up, the Philistine champion, Goliath of Gath, stepped out from the Philistine lines and made his usual challenge. David heard it all.

The Israelite soldiers, every single one of them, backed away as soon as they saw the giant. They were completely terrified. The buzz among the soldiers was, “Can you believe this guy, openly dissing Israel like this? Whoever kills this giant is gonna be set for life. The king will give him a massive reward, his daughter's hand in marriage, and his whole family will be tax-free.”

David, talking to the guys standing around, asked, “So, what’s the prize for the guy who takes out that Philistine and ends this major embarrassment for Israel? I mean, who does this uncircumcised Philistine think he is, taunting the armies of the living God?”
They just repeated what everyone else was saying about the king's reward for the guy who kills him.

Eliab, his older brother, heard David chatting with the soldiers and got super mad. “What are you even doing here? Why aren't you at home watching those few sheep of yours? I know your game. You just came down here to watch the action, hoping to get a front-row seat to a bloody fight!”
“Whoa, what's your problem?” David shot back. “I just asked a question.” He ignored his brother, turned to someone else, asked the same thing, and got the same story.
Word got back to Saul about what David was saying, so Saul sent for him.
“Don't lose hope, sir,” David said. “I'm ready to go fight this Philistine.”
Saul replied, “You can't go fight him. You're just a kid, you've got no experience. This guy has been a warrior since he was young.”

David said, “I've been a shepherd for my father. Whenever a lion or a bear came and tried to snatch a lamb from the flock, I'd go after it, beat it up, and rescue the lamb. If it turned on me, I'd grab it by the jaw, and finish it off. Lion or bear, didn't matter—I killed it. And I'll do the same thing to this pagan Philistine who's been dissing the armies of the living God. The same God who saved me from the lion's teeth and the bear's claws will save me from this Philistine.”
Saul said, “Go. And may God be with you.”
Then Saul tried to suit David up in his own armor. He put a bronze helmet on his head and strapped his sword on him over the armor. David tried to walk, but he could barely even move.
David told Saul, “I can't move with all this gear on. I'm not used to it.” So he took it all off.
Then David grabbed his shepherd's staff, picked out five smooth stones from a stream, put them in his shepherd's bag, and with his sling in his hand, he went to face Goliath.
As the Philistine, with his shield-carrier in front, walked back and forth, he saw David. He looked down at him and just scoffed—a young, fresh-faced kid.
The Philistine dissed David, “Am I a dog, that you’re coming at me with a stick?” And he cursed him in the name of his gods.
“Come on over here,” said the Philistine. “I’ll feed you to the birds and the wild animals.”

David shot back, “You come at me with a sword and a spear and a javelin, but I come at you in the name of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, who you've been mocking. Today, God is going to hand you over to me. I'm going to kill you, cut off your head, and feed your dead body and the bodies of your Philistine buddies to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know there's a God in Israel. And everyone here will see that God doesn't need a sword or a spear to save people. The battle is the Lord's, and he's about to hand you over to us.”

That got the Philistine moving, and he started coming toward David. David ran from the front line to meet him. He reached into his bag for a stone, put it in his sling, and slung it right at the Philistine's forehead. The stone sank deep into his forehead, and the Philistine fell flat on his face.
And that's how David beat the Philistine—with a sling and a stone. He struck him down and killed him. David didn't even have a sword!

Then David ran over, stood over the Philistine, took the giant's own sword from its sheath, and finished him off by cutting off his head. When the Philistines saw that their hero was dead, they freaked out and ran for it.

The men of Israel and Judah jumped up, shouting, and chased the Philistines all the way to the edge of Gath and the gates of Ekron. The road to Shaaraim was littered with wounded Philistines all the way to Gath and Ekron. After chasing them, the Israelites came back and took all the stuff from their camp. David took the Philistine's head to Jerusalem, but he put the giant's weapons in his own tent.
When Saul saw David going out to fight the Philistine, he asked Abner, the commander of his army, “Hey, who's this kid's dad?”
Abner said, “I swear, Your Majesty, I have no idea.”
The king said, “Well, find out who this young guy's family is.”
As soon as David came back from killing the Philistine, Abner brought him straight to Saul. David was still holding the Philistine's head.
Saul asked him, “Young man, who's your father?”
And David answered, “I'm the son of your servant Jesse, from Bethlehem.”

1 Samuel.title: From Best Bro to Worst Enemy
paragraphs: By the time David was done talking to Saul, Jonathan was totally blown away by him—they had this instant connection. He was all in on David, becoming his number one supporter and friend from that moment on.
That same day, Saul brought David into his own house, and he didn't go back to his dad's place anymore.
Jonathan, because he cared for David so much, made a serious promise with him. He made it official by giving him some big-deal gifts: his own royal robe and all his gear—armor, sword, bow, and belt.

Whatever Saul asked David to do, he crushed it. He was so good that Saul put him in charge of the army. Everyone, from the regular folks to Saul's own officials, thought David was an awesome leader and totally respected him.

On their way back home after David took down the Philistine, women came out from all the towns in Israel, singing and dancing to welcome King Saul with tambourines, party songs, and lutes. The women were joking around and sang,
'Saul takes down thousands, but David takes down ten thousands!'

This made Saul furious—like, really mad. He felt like they were dissing him personally. He was like, “They’re giving David credit for ‘ten thousands’ and I only get ‘thousands.’ Next thing you know, they’ll be making him the king!” From that day on, Saul was super suspicious of David.

The next day, God sent this nasty mood to mess with Saul, and he totally lost it, just raving like a madman. David started playing his harp, like he usually did when Saul got like this. Saul was holding a spear, and then all of a sudden, he threw it, thinking, “I’m gonna pin David to the wall.” But David dodged it, and the spear missed. This happened two times.

After that, Saul was scared of David. It was obvious that God was with David and had bounced on Saul. So, Saul got David out of his face by making him an officer in the army. David was out fighting all the time. Everything David did was a success. For real, God was with him. The more Saul saw David winning, the more scared he got. He knew it was over for him. But everyone else in Israel and Judah loved David. They loved seeing him in action.

One day Saul said to David, “Check it out, here’s Merab, my oldest daughter. I want to give her to you as your wife. Just be a beast for me and fight God’s battles!” But really, Saul was thinking, “The Philistines will take him out for me. I won’t even have to do anything.”
David was super humbled and was like, “Are you for real? My family is a bunch of nobodies! I can’t be the king’s son-in-law.”
The wedding day was all set, but when it was almost time for Merab and David to get married, Saul bailed and married her off to some other guy, Adriel the Meholathite.

But get this, Saul’s other daughter, Michal, had a major crush on David. When Saul heard about it, he was totally scheming. “Yes, a second chance. I’ll use Michal as bait to get David right where the Philistines can finish him off.” So he said to David again, “You’re gonna be my son-in-law after all.”
Saul told his servants, “Go talk to David privately and tell him, ‘The king is a big fan of yours, and everyone at court thinks you’re great. Just do it, become the king’s son-in-law!’”
The king’s servants told David all this, but David was still hesitant. “What are you guys talking about? I can’t do that. I’m a nobody; I’ve got nothing to bring to the table.”

When the servants told Saul what David said, he told them to tell David this: “The king doesn’t want any cash from you; just this: Go kill a hundred Philistines and bring back the proof. Get revenge for the king on his enemies.” (Saul was pretty sure David would get killed trying to do this.)

When David got this message, he was actually stoked. There was finally something he could do for the king that would make him worthy of being his son-in-law! He didn’t waste any time. He and his guys went right out, killed a hundred Philistines, brought back the evidence in a bag, and counted it all out for the king—mission accomplished! So Saul gave his daughter Michal to David as his wife.
As Saul started to realize more and more that God was with David, and saw how much his own daughter, Michal, loved him, his fear of David grew and turned into straight-up hate. Saul hated David.
Whenever the Philistine bosses came out for a fight, David was there to shut them down, totally showing up Saul’s own guys. David’s name was literally on everyone’s lips.

1 Samuel.title: David's Wild Escape from a Psycho King
paragraphs: Saul told his son Jonathan and all his officials to straight up kill David. But Jonathan was tight with David, so he went and gave him a heads-up: “My dad is literally trying to find a way to kill you. So here’s the plan. Tomorrow morning, you need to disappear and stay completely hidden. I’ll go out with my dad to the field where you’re hiding. I’ll bring you up in conversation and see what he says. Then I’ll tell you everything.”

Jonathan went to his dad and talked David up, saying, “Dad, please don’t do David dirty like that. He’s never done anything to you, has he? And look at all the awesome stuff he’s done! He put his life on the line to kill that Philistine. God gave Israel a huge win that day! You were there. You saw it and you were cheering louder than anyone. So why would you even think about sinning against an innocent guy and killing David for no reason?”
Saul actually listened to Jonathan and said, “You’re right. As God is real, David will live. He will not be killed.”
So Jonathan called David and told him everything they said. Then he brought David back to Saul, and things were cool again, just like before.
But then war broke out again, and David went to fight the Philistines. He totally wrecked them, and they all ran away scared.

Then, this dark vibe from God came over Saul and just took over. He was just sitting at home, holding his spear, while David was playing some music. Suddenly, Saul tried to pin David to the wall with his spear, but David ducked. The spear got stuck in the wall, and David bounced. This all went down at night.

Saul sent guys to David’s house to watch it and then kill him first thing in the morning. But Michal, David’s wife, told him what was up. “You have to escape tonight. If you don’t, you’ll be dead by morning!” She let him down from a window, and he got away. Then Michal grabbed a household idol, put it in the bed, put a wig made of goat’s hair on its head, and threw a blanket over it. When Saul’s guys showed up to grab David, she said, “He’s sick in bed.”
Saul sent his guys back, ordering them, “Bring him to me, bed and all, so I can kill him myself.” When the men went into the room, all they found in the bed was the idol with the goat-hair wig!
Saul was so mad at Michal: “How could you trick me like this? You took my enemy’s side, and now he’s gone!”
Michal shot back, “He threatened me. He said, ‘Help me get out of here or I’ll kill you.’”
David got away and went to Samuel at Ramah and told him everything Saul had done. Then he and Samuel bounced to a private place called Naioth.

Someone told Saul, “David’s at Naioth in Ramah.” He immediately sent his men to capture him. But when they got there, they saw a group of prophets prophesying, with Samuel leading them. Before they knew it, the Spirit of God came on them too, and they started prophesying and going wild right along with them!
Someone told Saul what happened, so he sent more men. They also started prophesying. So Saul tried a third time with a third group of men—and they ended up doing the same thing!
Saul was so over it, he went to Ramah himself. He got to the big well at Secu and asked, “Where are Samuel and David?”
A random person said, “Over at Naioth in Ramah.”

As he was heading to Naioth, the Spirit of God came on him, too. The whole way there, he was in some kind of trance, just babbling. He ripped off his clothes and lay there talking nonsense in front of Samuel for a whole day and a night, completely naked. People still talk about it, saying, “Is Saul a prophet now too? Who would’ve thought?”

1 Samuel.title: My Best Friend's Dad Wants Me Dead
paragraphs: David managed to get out of Naioth in Ramah and went straight to Jonathan, asking, "Yo, what do I do? What did I do to your dad that has him so set on killing me?"

"Nothing," Jonathan replied. "You've done zero wrong. And you're not going to die, for real. My dad tells me everything, big or small, he doesn't do anything without telling me. So why would he keep this from me? No way."

But David was like, "Look, your dad knows we're best friends. So he's probably thinking, 'Jonathan can't know about this, or he'll take David's side.' But I'm telling you, as sure as God is real and you're standing here, he's dead serious about killing me."
Jonathan said, "Just tell me what you're thinking. I'll do anything for you."

David laid out the plan: "Okay, so tomorrow is the New Moon festival, and I'm supposed to have dinner with the king. But instead, I'm gonna go hide in a field until the third evening. If your dad even notices I'm gone, just say, 'David really wanted to go back to his hometown, Bethlehem, for a family thing.' If he's cool with it and says, 'Good!' then I know I'm safe. But if he gets mad, you'll know for sure he's planning to kill me. Please, stick with me on this. We made a pact before God, remember? If I'm the one who's wrong, then you can just kill me yourself. Why would you even hand me over to your father?"
"Never!" Jonathan exclaimed. "I would never do that! If I get even the slightest hint that my dad is serious about killing you, I'll tell you right away."
David then asked, "But who's gonna tell me if your dad gives a harsh answer?"

"Come on, let's go to the field," Jonathan said. Once they were outside, Jonathan declared, "I swear on God, the God of Israel, that by this time tomorrow, I'll figure out how my dad feels about you. Then I'll let you know what I find out. May God strike me down if I let you down! If my dad still wants to kill you, I'll tell you and get you out of here safely. And may God be with you, just like he was with my father. If I survive this, promise you'll always be my friend. And if I die, promise you'll be friends with my family forever. And when God finally gets rid of all your enemies, stay loyal to me!" Jonathan made his promise to David again, because he loved him more than his own life.

Jonathan then explained his plan: "Tomorrow is the New Moon, and you'll be missed when you don't show up for dinner. On the third day, when they've stopped looking for you, go to the place where you hid before, and wait by that big rock. I'll shoot three arrows toward the rock. Then I'll send my servant to 'Go find the arrows.' If I yell to him, 'The arrows are on this side! Get them!' that's the signal that you can come back safely—I swear, there's nothing to worry about! But if I yell, 'The arrows are farther out!' then you need to run for it—God wants you to get out of here! And about everything we've talked about, just remember that God is in on this with us until the end!"

So David hid in the field. When the New Moon holiday came, the king sat down to eat. He sat in his usual spot against the wall, with Jonathan across from him and Abner next to him. But David's seat was empty. Saul didn't say anything at the time, thinking, "Something must have happened to make him unclean. Yeah, he's probably not clean enough for the holy meal."
But the next day, the second day of the holiday, David's seat was still empty. Saul asked his son Jonathan, "So where's that son of Jesse? He hasn't eaten with us yesterday or today."

Jonathan replied, "David asked for my permission to go to Bethlehem. He said, 'Please let me go to a family reunion back home. My brothers told me I had to be there. If it's cool with you, let me go see my brothers.' That's why he's not at the king's table."

Saul completely lost it and yelled at Jonathan: "You son of a snake! You think I don't know you're on Jesse's son's side, embarrassing both me and your mother? As long as that son of Jesse is alive, you have no future in this kingdom. Now go get him. Bring him here. He's as good as dead!"
Jonathan stood up to his father, asking, "Why should he be dead? What did he do?"
Saul threw his spear at him, trying to kill him. That's when Jonathan knew for sure that his father was determined to kill David.
Jonathan stormed away from the table, super angry, and didn't eat anything for the rest of the day. He was upset for David and hurt by his father's humiliating actions.

In the morning, Jonathan went to the field for his meeting with David, bringing his young servant with him. He told the servant, "Run and get the arrows I'm about to shoot." The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow way past him. When the boy got to where the arrow had landed, Jonathan yelled, "Isn't the arrow farther out?" He yelled again, "Hurry up! Don't just stand there!" The servant then picked up the arrow and brought it to his master. The boy, of course, had no idea what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.

Jonathan gave his bow and arrows to the boy and sent him back to town. After the servant left, David came out from his hiding spot by the rock and bowed down to the ground three times. Then they kissed each other and cried, friend with friend, with David crying the hardest.
Jonathan said, "Go in peace! We made a promise of friendship in God's name, saying, 'God will be the bond between us, and between our kids and their kids forever!'"

1 Samuel.title: David's Crazy Escape Plan
paragraphs: So David bounced, and Jonathan headed back to the city.
David rolled up to Nob to see Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech was shook when he saw David and was like, 'Yo, why are you here all solo? Where's your crew?'

David told the priest, 'The king sent me on a secret mission, like, super hush-hush. He was like, ‘Don’t tell anyone.’ I’m meeting my guys at a secret spot. Anyway, I’m starving. You got any food? Like five loaves of bread? I’ll take whatever you’ve got.'
'Nah, I don’t have any normal bread,' the priest said. 'Only the holy bread. But if you and your guys haven't been with any girls lately, you can have it.'
David was like, 'Nah, we're good. We haven't been with any women. We always keep it clean on missions. Even on regular ones, so for sure on this holy one.'
So the priest gave him the holy bread. It was all he had. It was the special bread that was put out before God and then swapped out for fresh bread.
One of Saul's guys, this dude named Doeg the Edomite, was there that day doing some religious thing. He was the head of Saul's shepherds.
Then David asked Ahimelech, 'Yo, you got a spear or a sword I can borrow? I had to leave in a rush for the king's mission and didn't have time to grab my weapons.'
The priest said, 'Goliath's sword, the one from the Philistine you killed at Oak Valley—that’s here! It’s behind the Ephod, wrapped in a cloth. If you want it, take it. There’s nothing else here.'
'Oh, sick!' David said. 'There’s no sword like that! Give it to me!'

And just like that, David was out of there, running for his life from Saul. He went to Achish, king of Gath. When Achish's servants saw him, they were like, 'Isn't that David, the famous one? The one they sing about in their dances?'
'Saul kills by the thousand, David by the ten thousand!'

When David realized they knew who he was, he freaked out, scared of what Achish, the king of Gath, would do. So right then and there, while they were all watching, he pretended to be crazy. He started banging his head on the city gate and drooling, with spit dripping down his beard. Achish took one look at him and said to his servants, 'Are you blind? The dude's insane! Why'd you let him in here? You think I don't have enough crazy people to deal with already? Get him out of here!'

1 Samuel.title: David's Fugitive Squad & A Royal Meltdown
paragraphs: So David bounced and escaped to the Cave of Adullam. When his brothers and the rest of his family heard where he was, they came down and linked up with him. On top of that, everyone who was going through it—people who were broke, in debt, or just fed up—all flocked to him. David became their leader, and he had a crew of about four hundred guys.

From there, David went to Mizpah in Moab and hit up the king, like, 'Yo, can you let my mom and dad crash here with you until I figure out what God's plan is for me?' So he left his parents with the king of Moab, and they stayed there the whole time David was hiding out.
Then the prophet Gad told David, 'Don't stay in the hideout. Get back to the land of Judah.' So David did what he said and went to the forest of Hereth.

Saul got the news that David and his men had been spotted. At the time, Saul was sitting under a big tree on the hill at Gibeah, spear in hand, holding a meeting with his officials. He said, 'Listen up, you Benjaminites! Do you seriously think this son of Jesse is gonna hook you up with fields and vineyards or make you all commanders? You're all plotting against me, and not one of you had the guts to tell me that my own son made a pact with him. None of you care enough to let me know that my son has stirred up my own servant to be an outlaw, waiting to ambush me, which is what's happening now.'

Then Doeg the Edomite, who was standing there with Saul's officials, spoke up, 'I saw the son of Jesse go to Nob, to Ahimelech son of Ahitub. Ahimelech prayed for him, gave him supplies, and even handed him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.'
So Saul sent for the priest Ahimelech and his whole family, who were all priests at Nob. And they all came to the king.
Saul said, 'Listen here, son of Ahitub!'
'Yes, my king,' he answered.

Saul went off, 'Why did you conspire against me with the son of Jesse? You gave him bread and a sword, and you prayed to God for him, setting him up as an outlaw to ambush me, just like he's doing now!'

Ahimelech replied to the king, 'Literally who among all your servants is as loyal as David? He's the king's son-in-law, captain of your bodyguard, and is crazy respected in your own house. Was this the first time I prayed to God for him? No way. Don't blame me or my family for anything, my king, because your servant has no clue what's going on with all this.'
But the king said, 'You're gonna die, Ahimelech! You and your entire family.'

Then the king ordered the guards at his side, 'Turn and kill the priests of the LORD! They're in on it with David. They knew he was on the run and they didn't tell me.' But the king's officials refused to raise a hand to strike down the LORD's priests.

So the king said to Doeg, 'You do it. Go kill the priests.' So Doeg the Edomite turned and slaughtered them. That day he killed eighty-five men who wore the priest's uniform. He went on to Nob, the city of priests, and wiped it out with the sword—men and women, children and infants, cattle, donkeys, and sheep. A total massacre.
Only one of Ahimelech's sons, Abiathar, managed to escape and fled to join David. He told David that Saul had murdered the LORD's priests.

David said to Abiathar, 'I knew it that day. When I saw Doeg the Edomite there, I just knew he would snitch to Saul. I'm the one responsible for the deaths of your whole family. Stay with me. Don't be scared. The same person who wants to kill you wants to kill me too. You'll be safe with me.'

1 Samuel.title: Narrow Escape
paragraphs: So, word got to David that the Philistines were raiding Keilah and stealing all their grain. David hit up God in prayer, asking, "Yo, should I go after these Philistines and teach them a lesson?"
God was like, "Go. Attack the Philistines and save Keilah."
But David's crew was lowkey shook. They said, "Bro, we're already scared for our lives right here in Judah. How can you even think about going to Keilah where it's crawling with Philistines?"
So David went back to God to pray again. God said, "Get going. Head to Keilah. I'm literally placing the Philistines in your hands."

David and his guys went to Keilah and battled the Philistines. He jacked their cattle, totally crushed them, and saved the people of Keilah. After Abiathar bounced to join David, he went with him on the raid, and he even brought the Ephod.

Saul found out that David was in Keilah and immediately thought, "Let's go! God has handed him to me on a silver platter! He's trapped in a walled city with locked gates." Saul gathered his army for battle and headed to Keilah to corner David and his men.

But David got wind of Saul's plan to destroy him and said to Abiathar the priest, "Get the Ephod." Then David prayed to God, "God of Israel, I just heard that Saul is planning to come to Keilah and wreck the city just because of me. Are the city leaders of Keilah gonna turn me over to him? Is Saul really gonna come down and do what I've heard? Oh God, God of Israel, tell me!"
God replied, "He's coming down."
"And are the leaders of Keilah gonna hand me and my men over to Saul?"
And God said, "They'll turn you over."
So David and his men, all 600 of them, got out of there. They left Keilah and just kept it moving, going here, there, wherever—always on the run.
When Saul was told that David had dipped from Keilah, he called off the whole raid.

David kept living in desert hideouts and the wild hills of Ziph. Saul was out looking for him day after day, but God never handed David over to him. David kept a low profile in the wilderness of Ziph, hiding out at Horesh, since it was super obvious that Saul was determined to hunt him down.

Jonathan, Saul's son, visited David at Horesh and gassed him up in God. He said, "Don't even trip. My father, Saul, can't lay a hand on you. You're gonna be Israel's king and I'll be right there by your side to help. And my father knows it, no cap." Then the two of them made a pact before God. David stayed at Horesh and Jonathan went home.

Some dudes from Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Yo, did you know that David is hiding out near us in the caves and canyons of Horesh? Right now he's at Hakilah Hill just south of Jeshimon. So whenever you're ready to come down, we'd be honored to hand him over to the king."

Saul said, "God bless you for thinking about me! Now go back and check everything out. Learn his whole routine. Watch his movements—where he goes, who he's with. He's super sneaky, you know. Scout out all his hiding spots. Then meet me at Nacon and I'll go with you. If he is anywhere to be found in all of Judah, I'll track him down!"
So the Ziphites set out on their spy mission for Saul.

Meanwhile, David and his men were in the Maon wilderness, in the desert south of Jeshimon. Saul and his men showed up and started their search. When David heard about it, he went south to Rock Mountain and camped out in the Maon wilderness. Saul heard where he was and took off for the Maon wilderness to chase him. Saul was on one side of the mountain, and David and his men were on the other. David was in full retreat, running for his life, with Saul and his men closing in, about to catch him. But just then, a messenger came to Saul and said, "Hurry! Come back! The Philistines just attacked the country!"

So Saul called off his chase of David and went back to deal with the Philistines. That's how that place got the name 'Narrow Escape.' David left there and camped out in the caves and canyons of En Gedi.

1 Samuel.title: Cave Showdown: David's Big Mercy Play
paragraphs: So, Saul gets back from fighting the Philistines, and someone's like, "Yo, David's hiding out in the En Gedi wilderness." Saul grabs 3,000 of his best soldiers—the absolute top tier in Israel—and heads out to the Wild Goat Rocks area to find David and his crew.

He gets to these sheep pens on the side of the road, and there's a cave. Saul goes inside for a bathroom break. And guess what? David and his guys were hiding way in the back of that exact same cave. David's men were whispering to him, "Bro, no way. This is the day God was talking about. He promised He'd put your enemy in your hands and you could do whatever you want with him." So David, quiet as a ninja, creeps up and snips off a corner of Saul's royal robe.

But instantly, he felt super guilty about it. He told his men, "God forbid I would do something like this to my king, the one God himself chose. I can't even lift a finger against him. He's God's anointed!" David shut his men down with that and stopped them from attacking Saul. Saul got up, walked out of the cave, and went on his way.

Then David went to the entrance of the cave and shouted after Saul, "My king! My master!" Saul looked back, and David dropped to his knees and bowed down. He yelled out, "Why do you even listen to people who say I'm out to get you? Today, you saw it with your own eyes. God literally handed you to me in that cave. My guys wanted to kill you, but I said no. I told them I wouldn't touch my king—because he's the one God anointed. Look, my father, look at this piece of your robe in my hand. I cut this off instead of killing you! See the proof? I'm not trying to overthrow you. I'm not a traitor. I haven't done anything wrong to you, but you're still hunting me down to kill me. Let God decide who's right here. God can get revenge for me, but I'm not going to do it myself. There's an old saying, 'Evil deeds come from evil people,' so you can be sure I'll never lay a hand on you.

"Who is the king of Israel even chasing? A dead dog? A single flea? God is the judge. He'll see the situation and decide what's right. I just pray He'll look at my case and get me out of this mess with you!"

When David finished his speech, Saul started sobbing and said, "Is that really your voice, my son David?" He cried his eyes out. "You are way more in the right than I am," he said. "You've been good to me while I've been awful to you. And you just proved it again—you were so generous. God put me in your hands, and you didn't kill me. I mean, who finds their enemy and just sends them off with a blessing? May God bless you like crazy for what you did for me today! Now I know, for real, that you're going to be the king. The kingdom of Israel is basically yours already. Just promise me, swear to God, that you won't wipe out my family or erase my name from history."
David made the promise to Saul. Then Saul went home, and David and his men went back up to their hideout.

1 Samuel.title: David vs. The Rich Fool: How One Woman Prevented a Bloodbath
paragraphs: So, Samuel died. Literally the whole country showed up for his funeral to pay their respects. He was buried in his hometown, Ramah. After that, David dipped and moved out to the Maon wilderness.

There was this super-rich guy in Maon who did business around Carmel. He had 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats—dude was loaded. It was sheep-shearing season, which was a big deal. The guy's name was Nabal, which basically means 'Fool,' and his wife's name was Abigail. She was super smart and beautiful, but he was a total jerk and just plain mean.

David, out in the middle of nowhere, heard Nabal was shearing his sheep. He sent ten of his guys with a message: "Go find Nabal in Carmel. Greet him for me and say, 'Hope you're doing great! Peace to you, your family, and everyone with you. I heard it's shearing time. Just so you know, when your shepherds were near us, we were cool to them. They didn't lose a single thing the whole time they were in Carmel. Ask your own guys, they'll back me up. So, what I'm asking is if you could be generous with my crew—it's a party, right? Just give whatever you feel like giving to us, your servants and your boy David.'"

David's guys went and gave Nabal the message, word for word. Nabal just blew up at them, yelling, "Who even IS this David? Who does Jesse's son think he is? The whole country is full of runaway servants these days. You think I'm gonna take the bread, wine, and meat I prepped for my own workers and just give it to some random dudes I've never even seen? I don't know where they're from!"

David's men just got out of there, went back, and told David exactly what Nabal said. David's response? "Swords on. Now." Everyone strapped on their swords, and David led 400 of his men to go handle it. The other 200 stayed behind to guard their camp.

Meanwhile, one of Nabal's own workers went straight to Abigail, Nabal's wife, and told her everything. "David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, but he just insulted them and screamed at them. But for real, those guys were so good to us. They never stole anything, never messed with us the whole time we were out in the fields with them. They were like a human wall, protecting us 24/7 while we were watching the sheep. You gotta do something, and fast, because some serious trouble is coming for our master and all of us. You know you can't even talk to him. He's impossible—a legit monster!"

Abigail didn't waste a second. She got 200 loaves of bread, two big skins of wine, five sheep already prepped for cooking, a ton of roasted grain, 100 raisin cakes, and 200 fig cakes, and loaded it all onto donkeys. She told her servants, "You guys go on ahead. I'll be right behind you." But she didn't say a word to her husband, Nabal.

So, as she was riding her donkey down into a ravine, she ran right into David and his men coming down from the other side. David had just been ranting, "This is just great. I wasted my time protecting everything this guy owned out in the wild so nothing got lost, and what do I get? Insults. A total slap in the face! I swear to God, if Nabal and every single guy in his crew isn't dead by morning, then let the worst happen to me!"

As soon as Abigail saw David, she jumped off her donkey, fell to her knees, and bowed with her face to the ground. She said, "Sir, please, let this all be on me! Just let me talk to you for a sec. Listen to what I have to say. Don't even think about that awful Nabal. He's literally living up to his name: Nabal, the Fool. Foolishness just pours out of him.

I wasn't there when your men arrived, I didn't even see them. But now, sir, as sure as God lives and you live, God has stopped you from taking revenge and murdering someone. May all your enemies, and anyone who wants to hurt you, end up just like Nabal! Please, take this gift that I, your servant, have brought for you, and give it to the young men who follow you.
Forgive me for being so bold! But God is working with you, my master, building you up to be a strong and solid ruler. You fight God's battles! As long as you're alive, no evil is gonna touch you.

And if anyone tries to stop you or get you out of the picture, just know this: Your life is precious to God, wrapped up safe with Him. But the lives of your enemies? He's gonna yeet them away like a rock from a slingshot.

When God comes through on all the good things he's promised you and makes you the leader of Israel, you don't want this on your conscience—the heavy guilt of taking revenge and killing someone for no good reason. And when God does amazing things for you, please, remember me."

And David said to her, "Wow. Praise God, the God of Israel. He's the one who sent you to meet me today! And thank God for your good sense! You are a blessing for stopping me from committing murder and taking matters into my own hands. That was a close one! As God lives, the God of Israel who kept me from hurting you, if you hadn't gotten here so fast and stopped me, I swear there wouldn't have been a single one of Nabal's guys left alive by morning."
Then David accepted her gift and told her, "Go home in peace. I've heard you, and I'll do what you asked."

When Abigail got home, Nabal was in the middle of a huge feast, like a king's party. He was in a great mood—and completely wasted. So she didn't tell him anything about what she'd done until the next morning. But in the morning, after Nabal sobered up, she told him the whole story. He had a heart attack right then and there and basically fell into a coma. About ten days later, God took him out, and he died.
When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, "Praise God! He stood up for me against Nabal's insults, kept me from doing something evil, and made Nabal's own evil come right back and hit him."
Then David sent a message to Abigail, asking her to be his wife. His servants went to her in Carmel and said, "David sent us to bring you to him to get married."
She got up, bowed with her face to the ground, and said, "I'm your servant, ready to do whatever you need. I'd even wash the feet of my master's servants!"
Abigail didn't wait around. She got on her donkey, and with her five maids, she followed David's messengers and became his wife.
David also married a woman named Ahinoam from Jezreel. So now they were both his wives. Meanwhile, Saul had married off David's first wife, Michal, to a guy named Palti, who was from Gallim.

1 Samuel.title: Sneaking into the Enemy Camp: The Ultimate Glow-Up
paragraphs: Some guys from Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and were like, “Yo, just so you know, David’s hiding out on Hakilah Hill, right across from Jeshimon.” Saul immediately got up and went to the Ziph wilderness with 3,000 of his best soldiers to hunt for David. He set up camp just off the road at Hakilah Hill.

David, who was still out in the country, heard that Saul was after him. He sent out spies to find out exactly where Saul was. Then David went to Saul’s camp and saw where Saul and his general, Abner, were staying. Saul was sleeping inside the camp, surrounded by his army.
David, taking charge, talked to Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai, Joab’s brother, and asked, “Who’s down to go with me into Saul’s camp?”
Abishai whispered back, “I’m with you.”

So David and Abishai snuck into the camp at night. And there was Saul, passed out in the middle of the camp, with his spear stuck in the ground by his head. Abner and the soldiers were all sound asleep around him.
Abishai was like, “This is it! God has delivered your enemy to you. Let me pin him to the ground with his own spear. One shot is all I need, for real. I won’t have to hit him twice.”
But David told Abishai, “No way, don’t hurt him! Who can attack God’s chosen king and get away with it?”

He continued, “As God is my witness, either God will take him out, or he’ll die of old age, or he’ll get killed in battle. But I’m not going to be the one to lay a hand on God’s anointed. Now, let’s just grab the spear and the water jug from his bedside and bounce.”
David took the spear and water jug from right next to Saul’s head, and they dipped. Nobody saw them. Nobody knew. Nobody even woke up! They were all in a deep sleep, like God had put a spell on them.

David then crossed over to the opposite hill and stood on top of the mountain, a safe distance away. He yelled over to the army and to Abner, “Hey, Abner! Are you ever going to wake up and answer me?”
Abner yelled back, “Who’s that calling?”

David replied, “Aren’t you the one in charge? Why aren’t you doing your job? Why weren’t you protecting your king when someone came to kill him? That’s some bad leadership. Seriously, you and the whole bodyguard should be ashamed. And look what I’ve got—the king’s spear and water jug that were right by his head!”
By then, Saul had recognized David’s voice and said, “Is that you, my son David?”

David said, “Yeah, it’s me, my king. Why are you chasing me? What did I do? What crime have I committed? My king, listen to me. If God is the one who turned you against me, then I’ll offer my life as a sacrifice. But if it’s just some people who did it, then they should be cursed. They kicked me out of my home and told me to go serve other gods. But you’re not getting rid of me that easily. You won’t separate me from God, not in life or death. This is absurd! The king of Israel is obsessed with a single flea! Hunting me down like a partridge in the hills!”
Saul confessed, “I messed up. Come back, my dear son David. I won’t hurt you anymore. You showed me respect today by sparing my life. I’ve been a fool—a total idiot.”

David answered, “Look, I have the king’s spear. Let one of your servants come and get it. God will judge us based on what’s right and who’s loyal. God put you in my hands today, but I wasn’t going to touch his anointed king. Just like I valued your life today, I hope God values my life and saves me from all my troubles.”
Saul said to David, “Bless you, my dear son David! Yes, do what you have to do! And you will succeed in everything you try!”
Then David went his way, and Saul went home.

1 Samuel.title: Faking Out the Enemy King (for a YEAR!)
paragraphs: David was stressing, thinking to himself, "Man, sooner or later, Saul's gonna get me. The smartest move is probably to just bounce and hide out in Philistine territory. Saul will finally write me off and stop hunting me all over Israel. I'll be totally off his radar."

So David packed up and left with his six hundred guys, and they went straight to Achish, the king of Gath. They all settled down there with the king. Each guy brought his whole family, and David brought his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. As soon as Saul heard that David had escaped to Gath, he finally called off the manhunt.

After a bit, David said to King Achish, "Hey, if it's cool with you, could you maybe give me a spot in one of the smaller towns out in the country? It feels a little extra for me, your servant, to be living it up in the royal capital city."
So Achish gave him a town called Ziklag. (That's actually how Ziklag ended up belonging to the kings of Judah). David lived in Philistine country for a whole year and four months.

During that time, David and his guys would go out and raid the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites—these were the OG residents of the land stretching down toward Egypt. But when David raided a place, he went hard. He left no one alive, not a single man or woman. He just took all their stuff: sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, clothes—everything. Then he'd go back to Achish.
Achish would always ask, "So, who'd you raid today?"

And David would lie, saying something like, "Oh, you know, the southern part of Judah," or "The area where the Jerahmeelites live," or "The Kenite territory." He never left anyone alive to tell the real story, in case they showed up in Gath and exposed what he was actually doing. This was his whole strategy the entire time he lived with the Philistines.
Achish started to lowkey trust David completely. He thought, "This guy has made his own people hate him so much, he's never going to leave my side. He's stuck with me for good."

1 Samuel.title: Saul's Ghost-Summoning Stunt Goes Horribly Wrong
paragraphs: So, around this time, the Philistines were getting their army together to go to war with Israel. Achish, the Philistine king, tells David, "Yo, just so you know, you and your guys are rolling with my army."
And David was like, "Bet. Now you'll get to see what I'm really made of."
"Awesome!" said Achish. "I'm making you my personal bodyguard—for life!"

Okay, quick backstory: Samuel was dead by now. All of Israel had a huge funeral for him and buried him in his hometown, Ramah. And way before this, Saul had kicked out all the psychics and people who claimed to talk to the dead.

The Philistines got their troops together and camped at Shunem. Saul gathered all of Israel and camped at Gilboa. But when Saul saw the massive Philistine army, he was shaking in his boots, scared to death.
Saul prayed to God, but God left him on read—no answer, not in a dream, not through a sign, not from a prophet.
So Saul told his officials, "Find me someone who can summon spirits. I need to go ask them for advice."
His servants were like, "Well, there's a witch at Endor."

Saul went full-on disguise mode, changing his clothes and everything. He took two guys with him and went to the woman's house at night. He said, "I need you to do a séance for me. Call up the spirit of the person I name."
The woman was like, "Hold up. You know what Saul did, right? How he got rid of all the mediums in the country. Are you trying to set me up and get me killed?"
Saul swore a super serious oath, "As God is my witness, you won't get in any trouble for this."
The woman finally asked, "Alright, so who do you want me to bring up?"
"Samuel. Bring up Samuel for me."
When the woman saw Samuel's spirit, she screamed at the top of her lungs and yelled at Saul, "Why did you lie to me?! You're King Saul!"
The king told her, "It's cool, you have nothing to be scared of... but what do you see?"
"I see a spirit coming up from the ground."
"And what's he look like?" Saul asked.
"An old man, coming up, and he's wearing a priest's robe."
Saul knew it was Samuel. He immediately dropped to the ground, face down, and worshiped.
Samuel said to Saul, "Why did you bother me by calling me up?"

"Because I'm in huge trouble," Saul said. "The Philistines are about to attack, and God has ghosted me—He won't answer me anymore, not by prophet or by dream. So I'm calling you to tell me what I should do."

"Why are you asking me?" Samuel shot back. "God has literally left you and is on your neighbor's side now. God did exactly what He told you through me—He's ripping the kingdom out of your hands and giving it to your neighbor. This is all happening because you didn't obey God and refused to carry out His fierce anger on the Amalekites. That's why God is doing this to you today. And it gets worse. God is going to hand over Israel, and you with it, to the Philistines. Tomorrow, you and your sons will be with me. And yeah, God is totally giving Israel's army to the Philistines."

Saul just collapsed on the ground, like a tree getting chopped down, completely terrified by what Samuel said. He had zero strength left—he hadn't eaten anything all day and all night. The woman saw he was in deep shock and said to him, "Look, I did what you asked. I risked my life for you and followed your orders exactly. Now it's your turn to listen to me. Let me get you some food. Eat it. It'll give you strength so you can get going."
He refused, "I'm not eating."

But his servants and the woman kept insisting, so he finally gave in. He got up from the floor and sat on the bed. The woman quickly went to work. She had a calf that was well-fed, and she butchered it. Then she took some flour, kneaded it, and baked some flatbread. She served it all to Saul and his servants. After they had a pretty decent meal, they got up and left that same night.

1 Samuel.title: Kicked Out Before the Battle Even Starts?!
paragraphs: So the Philistines gathered all their troops at Aphek, while Israel was camped by the spring in Jezreel. The Philistine leaders were marching on with their units, and David and his guys were at the very back with King Achish.
The Philistine commanders were like, 'Yo, what are these Hebrews even doing here?'

Achish shot back, 'Chill, you guys know David, right? He used to work for King Saul of Israel. He's been with me for a while now, and I've got zero complaints. He's been a solid dude since the day he bounced from Saul.'

But the Philistine officers were ticked off at Achish. 'Send this guy back to his post!' they demanded. 'He's not fighting with us. He'll probably just turn on us mid-battle to get back on his master's good side. What better way to do that than by betraying us? Isn't this the same David they sing songs about?'
'Saul took down thousands, but David took down tens of thousands!'

So Achish had to call David over. 'Look, man,' he said, 'as God is my witness, you've been a loyal friend. You've been awesome to work with, and I have nothing but good things to say about you. But the other leaders just aren't having it. It's probably best if you just head out peacefully. It's not worth making them angry.'
David was like, 'But what did I do? Have you had a single problem with me since I joined you? Why can't I fight my master the king's enemies?'

'I know, I know,' Achish said. 'You're a good guy, like an angel from God in my book. But the Philistine officers were super clear: 'He's not going into battle with us.' So, just get an early start tomorrow with your men. As soon as it's light enough, just go.'
So David and his men got up early and were on their way back to Philistine territory by sunrise. The Philistines continued on to Jezreel.

1 Samuel.title: David's Epic Comeback: The Ultimate Rescue Mission
paragraphs: So, three days later, David and his crew finally roll back into Ziklag, and it's a complete disaster. The Amalekites had raided the Negev and Ziklag, totally trashing the town and burning it to the ground. They captured all the women, young and old. They didn't kill anyone, but basically herded them off like cattle. By the time David and his men got to the village, it was already a smoldering wreck, and their wives, sons, and daughters were all gone.

David and his guys just broke down, wailing and crying until they had nothing left. David’s two wives, Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, Nabal's widow from Carmel, were also taken. And then, things got even worse for David. His own men, bitter and heartbroken over losing their families, started talking about stoning him. It was a lowkey mutiny.
But David found his strength by trusting in his God. He told Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech's son, 'Bring me the Ephod so I can ask God what to do.' Abiathar brought it to him.
Then David prayed to God, 'Should I go after these raiders? Can I catch them?'
The answer came back: 'Go after them! You'll definitely catch them! And you'll rescue everyone!'

So David took off with his six hundred men. They got to the Brook Besor, but some of them were too wiped to go on. David and four hundred men kept pushing forward, but two hundred of them were just too exhausted to cross the brook and had to stay behind.

Some of the guys who continued on found an Egyptian dude in a field and brought him to David. They gave him some bread and water, and he ate. They also gave him a piece of a fig cake and a couple of raisin muffins. He started to come back to life. Turns out, he hadn't eaten or drunk anything for three whole days and nights!
David asked him, 'Who's your boss? Where are you from?'

'I'm an Egyptian, a slave to an Amalekite,' he said. 'My master just left me for dead when I got sick three days ago. We had just raided the Negev of the Kerethites, Judah, and Caleb. And yeah, we're the ones who burned Ziklag.'
David asked him, 'Can you lead us to this raiding party?'
'Swear to me by God,' the guy said, 'that you won't kill me or hand me back to my old master, and I'll take you right to them.'
He led David straight to them. The Amalekites were scattered everywhere, partying it up, eating and drinking, and enjoying all the stuff they had plundered from Philistia and Judah.

David and his men attacked. They fought from sunrise until the evening of the next day. No one got away except for four hundred younger guys who escaped on camels. David rescued everything the Amalekites had taken. And he got his two wives back! Nothing and no one was missing—not the young, not the old, not a single son or daughter, and none of the loot. David recovered it all. He gathered all the sheep and cattle, and everyone was shouting, 'This is all David's loot!'

Then David went back to the two hundred men who had been too tired to continue and had stayed at the Brook Besor. They came out to welcome David and his crew. As he got closer, he shouted, 'We did it!'

But some of the selfish, rotten guys who had marched with David started complaining: 'They didn't help with the rescue, so they shouldn't get any of the plunder we recovered. They can take their wives and kids, but that's it. Tell them to take their families and leave!'

'No way, my brothers! We're a team, we don't do that,' David said, shutting down the argument. 'You can't act like this with what God has given us! God protected us. He handed over the raiders who attacked us. Who would even listen to such nonsense? The guy who stays behind with the gear gets the same share as the guy who goes out to fight—equal shares for everyone. Share and share alike!' From that day on, David made that a rule in Israel—and it's still the rule today.

When he got back to Ziklag, David sent parts of the plunder to the elders of Judah, his neighbors, with a note that said, 'Here’s a gift for you from the stuff we took from God’s enemies!' He sent gifts to the elders in Bethel, Ramoth Negev, Jattir, Aroer, Siphmoth, Eshtemoa, Racal, the Jerahmeelite cities, the Kenite cities, Hormah, Bor Ashan, Athach, and Hebron, and a bunch of other places where he and his men had been.

1 Samuel.title: The King's Tragic Last Stand
paragraphs: The Philistines declared war on Israel, and the Israelite soldiers were in a full-blown retreat, getting absolutely wrecked on Mount Gilboa. The Philistines zeroed in on Saul and his sons, and they ended up killing Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malki-Shua—Saul's boys.

The fighting got super intense right around Saul. The archers found their mark and he was seriously wounded. Saul told his weapon guy, “Yo, pull out your sword and just end me. I can't let these pagans come and make a whole spectacle out of killing me.”

But his weapon guy was too freaked out and wouldn't do it. So Saul just took his own sword and fell on it. When the weapon guy saw that Saul was dead, he did the exact same thing and died with him. So Saul, his three sons, and his right-hand man—they all died together that day.

When the Israelites living in the nearby valley and across the Jordan River saw that their army was bailing and that Saul and his sons were dead, they straight up abandoned their cities and ran. The Philistines just moved in and took over their homes.

The next day, when the Philistines were looting the dead, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa. They cut off Saul's head and stripped his armor. Then they paraded the news all over Philistine territory, showing it off in their idol shrines and to all the people. They put his armor on display in the temple of their goddess Ashtoreth and nailed his body to the wall at Beth Shan.

The people of Jabesh Gilead heard what the Philistines did to Saul. Their most courageous men immediately jumped into action. They traveled all night, snatched the bodies of Saul and his three sons from the wall at Beth Shan, and brought them back to Jabesh where they performed a cremation. Then they buried their bones under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh and fasted for seven days as a sign of mourning.

2 Samuel.title: David Hears Some Crazy News
paragraphs: So, right after Saul died, David got back to Ziklag from totally crushing the Amalekites. Then, three days later, this random guy shows up from Saul’s army camp.
Dude was a mess, obviously mourning, and he got on his knees to show respect to David. David’s like, “What brings you here?”
He answered, “I literally just escaped from the Israelite camp.”
“So what happened?” David asked. “Spill the tea.”
He said, “The Israelite army dipped from the battle, leaving a bunch of their dead friends behind. And get this—Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
David pressed the young soldier for the deets: “How are you so sure Saul and Jonathan are dead?”

“I just happened to be on Mount Gilboa and saw Saul, super messed up and leaning on his spear, with enemy chariots and horsemen closing in on him, for real. He looked back, saw me, and called me over. I was like, ‘Yes sir, at your service.’ He asked who I was, and I told him, ‘I’m an Amalekite.’”
“‘Come here,’ he said, ‘and put me out of my misery. I’m lowkey already dead, just hanging on.’”
“So I did what he asked—I killed him. I knew he wasn’t going to last much longer anyway. I took his royal headband and bracelet and brought them to my master. Here they are.”

David was so wrecked he ripped his clothes to shreds. All the men with him did the same. They cried and fasted for the rest of the day, grieving for Saul and his son Jonathan, and also for God’s army and the nation of Israel, all victims in a failed battle.
Then David looked at the young soldier who brought the report: “Who are you, for real?”
“I’m from an immigrant family—an Amalekite.”
“Are you serious?” said David. “You weren’t afraid to just up and kill God’s anointed king?” He immediately ordered one of his soldiers, “Strike him dead!” The soldier struck him, and he died.
“You asked for it,” David told him. “You sealed your own death sentence when you said you killed God’s anointed king.”
Then David sang this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan, and ordered that everyone in Judah learn it by heart. Yeah, it’s even written in The Book of Jashar.

Oh, the gazelles of Israel, struck down on your hills, the mighty warriors—fallen, just fallen! Don’t talk about it in the city of Gath, don’t post the news in the streets of Ashkelon. Don’t give those Philistine girls another reason to party. No more dew or rain for you, hills of Gilboa, not a drop from the springs, because that’s where the warriors’ shields were dragged through the mud, Saul’s shield left there to rot.
Jonathan’s bow was goated—the bigger they were, the harder they fell. Saul’s sword was fearless—once it was out, nothing could stop it.
Saul and Jonathan—so loved, so awesome! Together in life, together in death. Faster than eagles, stronger than lions.

Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He dressed you in the finest clothes and silks, spared no expense to make you look good. The mighty warriors—fallen, fallen in the middle of the fight! Jonathan—struck down on your hills!
Oh my dear brother Jonathan, I’m crushed by your death. Your friendship was a miracle, for real—a love way beyond anything I’ve ever known, or ever hope to know.
The mighty warriors—fallen, fallen. And their weapons of war, broken to pieces.

2 Samuel.title: Civil War STARTS! David vs. Saul's Son
paragraphs: So after all that went down, David hit up God. He was like, 'Yo, should I roll out to one of the cities in Judah?' And God was straight up, 'Yep, time to move.' David asked, 'Aight, which one?' God said, 'Hebron.'

So David packed up and moved to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, who used to be married to Nabal from Carmel. All of David's crew and their families came with and they all settled down in and around Hebron.
The people of Judah showed up in Hebron and, right then and there, they crowned David king over all the clans of Judah. It was official.

Then David got word that the guys from Jabesh Gilead had given Saul a proper funeral. David sent messengers to them, saying, 'God bless you guys for honoring your old leader, Saul, like that. Seriously, may God be good to you, and I'll do the same. I'll match that kindness you showed. Now, be strong and ready for what's next. Your master Saul is dead, and the people of Judah have made me their king.'

Meanwhile, Abner, the commander of Saul’s army, took Saul’s son Ish-Bosheth to Mahanaim and made him king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin—basically, he tried to make him king over all of Israel. Ish-Bosheth was 40 when this happened, but his reign only lasted two years. The tribe of Judah, though, was loyal to David. David ruled Judah from Hebron for seven and a half years.

One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ish-Bosheth marched out from Mahanaim to Gibeon. Joab, with David’s soldiers, also set out. The two groups met at the Pool of Gibeon and faced off, one on each side of the pool.
Abner trash-talked Joab, 'Let's have your best guys fight. Let's see what they've got.'
Joab shot back, 'You're on! Let's do it!'

So they got ready to throw down. Twelve guys from Benjamin for Ish-Bosheth, and twelve of David's soldiers. It was wild—each guy grabbed his opponent's head and shanked him with a dagger. They all died right there, the whole group together. So they named the place 'Slaughter Park,' and it's right there in Gibeon.

The battle got super intense after that. Abner and the men of Israel got totally wrecked by David's crew. Joab and his two brothers, Abishai and Asahel, were there. Asahel was crazy fast, like a gazelle, and he started chasing Abner, sticking right on his tail.
Abner looked back and yelled, 'Asahel, is that you?'
'You know it!' Asahel yelled back.
Abner warned him, 'Back off, dude. Go pick a fight with someone you can actually beat and take their stuff!' But Asahel was relentless and wouldn't stop.
Abner tried again, 'Seriously, turn back! Don't make me kill you. How could I ever face your brother Joab if I did?'

But he wouldn't quit, so Abner jabbed him in the stomach with the butt end of his spear. He hit him so hard it went right through his back. Asahel dropped and died right there. Everyone who came to that spot just stopped and stared at his body.

But Joab and Abishai didn't stop; they kept chasing Abner. As the sun was setting, they got to the hill of Ammah. The soldiers of Benjamin had regrouped with Abner there, setting up a defensive position on the hill.
Abner yelled out to Joab, 'Are we just gonna keep fighting forever? Don't you get that this will only end badly for everyone? How long are you gonna keep chasing your own brothers?'

Joab replied, 'As God is my witness, if you hadn't said something, we would've kept this chase going all night!' Then Joab blew the trumpet, and the whole army stopped. They quit chasing the Israelites and the fighting was over.
Abner and his soldiers marched all night through the Arabah Valley. They crossed the Jordan River and, after a long march, finally got back to Mahanaim.

When Joab got back from chasing Abner, he did a headcount. Nineteen of David's men were missing, not including Asahel. But they had taken down 360 of Abner's men, all from the tribe of Benjamin—all dead. They took Asahel's body and buried him in his family's tomb in Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men marched through the night, arriving back in Hebron just as the sun came up.

2 Samuel.title: The OG Beef: Betrayal and Revenge
paragraphs: The beef between Saul's crew and David's crew just kept going. But the longer it went, the stronger David's side got, while Saul's team was getting weaker and weaker.
While he was in Hebron, David had a bunch of sons:
Amnon was his first, from Ahinoam of Jezreel.
Kileab was his second, from Abigail of Carmel, who used to be married to Nabal.
Absalom was his third, from Maacah, who was the daughter of Talmai, the king of Geshur.
Adonijah was his fourth, from Haggith.
Shephatiah was his fifth, from Abital.
Ithream was his sixth, from Eglah.
So yeah, these six sons were all born in Hebron.

Abner, who was on Saul's side, was using the war to get more power for himself. Saul had a side-chick named Rizpah, and one day Saul's son Ish-Bosheth went off on Abner, like, "Why are you sleeping with my dad's girl?"

Abner totally lost it at Ish-Bosheth. "You think I'm some kind of dog? This is the thanks I get for being loyal to your dad's family and friends? I literally saved you from being captured by David, and you're gonna get mad at me for hooking up with a woman? You know what, I'm gonna help God make his promise to David come true. I'm gonna take the kingdom from Saul's family and make David the king of everyone, Israel and Judah. If I don't, I hope God messes me up."
Ish-Bosheth was so scared by Abner's rant that he couldn't even say anything back.
So Abner sent messengers to David, saying, "Make a deal with me, and I'll get all of Israel on your side."
David was like, "Awesome, it's a deal. But on one condition: you have to bring back my wife Michal, Saul's daughter, when you come to see me."
Then David sent messengers to Ish-Bosheth, saying, "Give me back my wife Michal. I paid for her with a hundred Philistine foreskins."
Ish-Bosheth made her leave her husband, Paltiel. But Paltiel followed her, crying the whole way, until they got to Bahurim. Then Abner told him, "Go home," and he did.

Abner got all the leaders of Israel together and said, "You guys were already trying to make David your king, right? Well, now's the time to do it! God even said he'd save Israel from the Philistines and all their enemies through David."
Abner also talked to the Benjaminites privately. Then he went to Hebron to talk to David and tell him everything Israel and Benjamin were planning.
When Abner and his twenty guys met David in Hebron, David threw a big party for them.

Then Abner said, "Alright, I'm ready. I'm gonna go rally everyone in Israel for you, my king. They'll make a deal with you, and you can rule them however you want." David sent him off with his blessing.

Right after that, David's men, led by Joab, came back from a mission. Abner was already gone. When Joab and his crew got there, they were told that Abner had been there with David and had left on good terms.

Joab went straight to the king and was like, "What did you just do? Abner shows up, and you just let him go? You know what he's like. He wasn't here to be friends. He was here to spy on you and figure out what you're up to."

Joab left David and immediately sent messengers after Abner. They caught up with him at a well and brought him back. David had no idea. When Abner got back to Hebron, Joab pulled him aside at the gate to talk privately. And then he stabbed him in the stomach and killed him, to get revenge for his brother Asahel's death.

When David heard what happened, he said, "God knows that my kingdom and I are innocent of Abner's murder. Joab and his whole family will be cursed for this. I hope they're always dealing with sickness, violence, and hunger." (Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in a battle.)

David told Joab and all his men, "Tear your clothes, wear mourning clothes, and lead Abner's funeral, crying loudly." King David even followed the coffin. They buried Abner in Hebron, and the king cried super loudly at his grave. Everyone else was crying too.
Then the king sang this song for Abner:
"How can this be? Abner's dead like some random dude? You were a free man, you could do whatever you wanted—but you got taken out in a street fight."
And everyone started crying even harder.

Then they all tried to get David to eat something before it got dark. But David swore, "I swear to God, I won't eat anything, not even a piece of bread, before the sun sets." Everyone there saw it and was impressed. Actually, everything the king did, the people loved. It was obvious to everyone that day that the king had nothing to do with Abner's death.

The king said to his servants, "You guys realize that a prince and a hero was killed today, right? And even though I'm the king, I was powerless to stop it. These sons of Zeruiah are too much for me. God will pay back the criminal for his crime!"

2 Samuel.title: Two Bros Betray Their King & Get What They Deserve
paragraphs: When Saul's son, Ish-Bosheth, heard that Abner was dead, he was devastated. His courage just evaporated, and the whole country was shook.

Now, Ish-Bosheth had these two guys, Baanah and Recab, who were captains of his raiding parties. They were sons of a dude named Rimmon from Beeroth, from the tribe of Benjamin. (A little backstory: the people of Beeroth had to dip and ended up in Gittaim, where they still live as foreigners).

Also, quick side note: Saul's son, Jonathan, had a son who couldn't use his feet. When he was five, the news about Saul and Jonathan's death came from Jezreel. His nanny grabbed him and ran, but in her panic, she dropped him, and he was injured permanently. His name was Mephibosheth.

So one day, Baanah and Recab, the sons of Rimmon, headed over to Ish-Bosheth's house. They got there during the hottest part of the day, right when he was taking his afternoon nap. They got in by pretending they were there on official business. The guard at his bedroom door had dozed off, so they slipped right past her and went into the room where Ish-Bosheth was sleeping. They killed him, cut off his head, and took it as a trophy. They traveled all night through the Arabah Valley.

They brought Ish-Bosheth's head to David in Hebron and said, "Here's the head of Ish-Bosheth, son of your enemy Saul. He wanted to kill you, but today God has given you revenge on Saul and his family!"

David looked at the brothers, Recab and Baanah, and said, "As surely as God lives—the God who has saved me from all my troubles—when a guy brought me the news that Saul was dead, thinking I'd be thrilled, I had him arrested and killed right there in Ziklag. That was his reward for the 'good news.' And now you two, a couple of evil men, have murdered an innocent man in his own bed. You really think I won't hold you accountable for this murder and get rid of you?"

Then David gave the order to his soldiers. They killed the two brothers, chopped off their hands and feet, and hung their bodies up by the pool in Hebron. But they took Ish-Bosheth's head and buried it in Abner's tomb in Hebron.

2 Samuel.title: David's Ultimate Glow-Up: Finally King of ALL Israel!
paragraphs: So after a bit, all the tribes of Israel went to David over in Hebron and were like, “Yo, look at us—we’re your own flesh and blood! Back when Saul was our king, you were the one actually leading us. And God even told you, ‘You’re gonna shepherd my people Israel and be their leader.’”
All the elders of Israel came to King David at Hebron, and the king made a deal with them before God. Then they anointed David and made him king over all of Israel.

David was thirty years old when he started his reign, and he ruled for forty years. He was king of Judah in Hebron for seven and a half years, and then he ruled all of Israel and Judah from Jerusalem for thirty-three years.

David and his crew immediately headed to Jerusalem to take on the Jebusites who lived there. But the Jebusites were cocky and said, “You can’t get in here! Even our blind and lame citizens could keep you out.” They seriously thought David had no chance.

But David went for it anyway and captured the fortress of Zion, which is now known as the City of David. That day, David said, “To beat these Jebusites, you gotta go for their water supply. And forget this ‘lame and blind’ crew that I’m so sick of.” He was so over it that it became a saying: “No lame and blind people allowed in the palace.”

David moved into the fortress and called it the “City of David.” He built up the city from the terraces inward. David just kept getting stronger and more successful because the God of Angel Armies was with him.

Around this time, Hiram, the king of Tyre, sent messengers to David with cedar logs. He also sent carpenters and stonemasons to build a palace for David. David saw this as a sign that God had officially made him king of Israel and was making his kingdom a big deal for the sake of his people, Israel.
After he left Hebron, David got more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, and had more sons and daughters. These are the names of the kids he had in Jerusalem:
Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
Shammua,
Shobab,
Nathan,
Solomon,
Ibhar,
Elishua,
Nepheg,
Japhia,
Elishama,
Eliada,
Eliphelet.

When the Philistines heard that David had been made king over all of Israel, they came looking for him. David found out and went down to his stronghold. When the Philistines showed up, they spread out their troops in the Rephaim Valley.
Then David asked God, “Should I go fight the Philistines? Will you help me win?”
“Go for it,” God said. “I got you. I’ll help you beat them.”

So David went to a place called Baal Perazim and totally crushed them. Afterward, David said, “God just burst through my enemies like a flood of water.” That’s why he named the place Baal Perazim (which means “The Master Who Bursts Through”). The Philistines ran off and left their idols behind, so David and his soldiers picked them up.
Later, it was like a sequel. The Philistines came back and set up their troops in the Rephaim Valley again. David prayed to God again.

This time God said, “Don’t attack them from the front. Go around behind them and ambush them from the grove of sacred trees. When you hear a rustling sound in the trees, that’s your cue to move out. It means I’m going ahead of you to wreck the Philistine camp.”
David did exactly what God told him to do. He chased the Philistines all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.

2 Samuel.title: God's Ark is WILD, David's Dance Moves are WILDER
paragraphs: So David got all of Israel's best troops together—like, thirty whole divisions of them. He and his soldiers went to Baalah to bring back the Ark of God. You know, the one that's called by the Name of God-of-the-Angel-Armies, who sits enthroned over the angels on the Ark itself.

They put the Ark of God on a brand-new oxcart and rolled it out of Abinadab's house on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, Abinadab's sons, were driving the new cart with the Ark. Ahio was out front, and Uzzah was right there next to the Ark. David and the whole crew from Israel were basically having a huge parade. They were singing like crazy and playing all sorts of instruments—mandolins, harps, tambourines, you name it. But when they got to Nacon's threshing floor, the oxen stumbled. Uzzah reached out and grabbed the Ark to steady it. And then, bam. God got super angry with Uzzah and struck him down right there because he'd disrespected the Ark. Uzzah died on the spot, right next to it. It was intense.

David was actually pretty ticked off that God had lashed out at Uzzah like that. They even named that place Perez Uzzah, which means 'The-Explosion-Against-Uzzah.' After that, David was lowkey scared of God and was like, 'This Ark is way too intense. How am I ever gonna get it back to the City of David?' So he decided not to move the Ark any farther. Instead, he took it to the house of a guy named Obed-Edom. The Ark of God stayed with Obed-Edom's family for three months, and God totally blessed him and his entire household. No cap.

When King David heard that God had blessed Obed-Edom and his whole family because of the Ark, he was like, 'Okay, bet. I want in on that blessing.' So he went and brought the Ark of God up from Obed-Edom's house to the City of David, and this time it was a full-on party. They were making sacrifices of the best bulls all along the way.
