Because this is what the God of Israel says: ‘The flour jar won’t run out and the oil bottle won’t be empty until the day God sends rain and ends this drought.’”

And she just went and did it, exactly what Elijah asked. And it turned out just like he said—they had food to eat every single day. The flour jar never ran out and the oil bottle never became empty. It was God’s promise, delivered by Elijah, coming true down to the last letter.
Sometime later, the woman’s son got really sick. It got worse and worse, and then he just stopped breathing.
The woman said to Elijah, “Why did you even come here? You, a holy man, just had to show up, point out all my past mistakes, and get my son killed?”
Elijah just said, “Give me your son.”

He took the boy from her arms, carried him up to the room where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed. Then he prayed, “Oh God, my God, why would you do something so terrible to this widow who’s been so good to me? Why would you take her son’s life?”

Three times, he stretched himself out on top of the boy, praying with everything he had, “God, my God, please bring this boy back to life!” And God heard Elijah’s prayer. He put breath back into the boy’s body—he was alive! Elijah picked him up, carried him downstairs, and gave him back to his mother. “Look,” Elijah said, “your son is alive!”
The woman said to Elijah, “Okay, now I get it. You’re for real a man of God. When you speak, it’s God speaking—it’s the real deal, no cap!”

1 Kings.title: Elijah vs. Team Baal: The Ultimate God-Off
paragraphs: A super long time went by. Then God's word came to Elijah. The drought was in its third year, which was wild. The message was: "Go show yourself to Ahab; I'm about to make it rain." So Elijah went to go see Ahab. The drought in Samaria was no joke, like, it was severe.

Ahab called for Obadiah, the guy in charge of the palace. Obadiah was a real one, he truly feared God. Back when Jezebel was trying to cancel all of God's prophets, Obadiah hid a hundred of them in two caves, fifty in each, and made sure they had food and water.

Ahab told Obadiah, "Go search the whole country, check every spring and stream. We gotta see if we can find enough grass to keep our horses and mules from literally dying." So they split up the country to search—Ahab went one way, and Obadiah went the other.
Obadiah was on his way when, boom, there was Elijah! Obadiah dropped to his knees, totally bowing down, and was like, "Is that really you, my master Elijah?"
"Yep," said Elijah, "it's me, for real. Now go tell your boss, 'Elijah's here.'"

Obadiah was shook. "What did I do to deserve this? Ahab's gonna kill me. I swear on your God, there isn't a single country my master hasn't sent people to find you. And if they said, 'He's not here,' he'd make them swear they couldn't find you. And now you're telling me to go tell him you've been found? The second I leave, God's Spirit will probably teleport you to who-knows-where. Then when I tell Ahab, you'll be gone, and he'll kill me. I've been serving God since I was a kid! Hasn't anyone told you what I did when Jezebel was hunting God's prophets? I risked my neck hiding a hundred of them and feeding them. And now you want me to tell my master, 'Elijah's been found'? He'll kill me for sure!"
Elijah said, "As surely as the God of Angel Armies lives, the one I serve, I will 100% meet your master face-to-face today."
So Obadiah went straight to Ahab and told him. And Ahab went out to meet Elijah.
The second Ahab saw Elijah, he said, "So it's you, the guy who's been causing all this trouble in Israel!"

"It's not me who's been causing trouble," Elijah shot back, "it's you and your family. You've ghosted God's commands and started chasing after the local gods, the Baals. So here's the plan: Get everyone in Israel to Mount Carmel. And make sure you bring Jezebel's crew—the 450 prophets of Baal and the 400 prophets of the goddess Asherah."
So Ahab got everyone in Israel, especially the prophets, to go to Mount Carmel.
Elijah stood up and called out the people: "How long are you gonna play both sides? If God is the real God, then follow him. If it's Baal, then follow him. Just pick one!"
No one said a thing. Crickets.

Then Elijah said, "I'm the only prophet of God left here, and there are 450 prophets of Baal. So let's do this: they bring two bulls. They can pick one, cut it up, and put it on an altar with wood—but no fire. I'll do the same with the other bull. Then, you pray to your god, and I'll pray to my God. The god who answers with fire? That's the real God."
Everyone was like, "Good plan, let's do it!"
Elijah told the Baal prophets, "You guys go first, there are more of you. Pick your bull, get it ready, and pray to your god, but don't light the fire."

So they took the bull, prepped it, and prayed to Baal all morning, shouting, "O Baal, answer us!" But nothing. Not even a whisper. They got so desperate they were jumping and dancing all over the altar they made.

By noon, Elijah started trolling them. "Maybe you should shout louder! He's a god, right? Maybe he's meditating, or busy with a project, or on vacation. You don't think he overslept and needs a wake-up call, do you?" So they yelled even louder and started cutting themselves with swords and knives, which was their ritual, until they were covered in blood.
This went on all afternoon. They tried every religious trick in the book to get something to happen, but still nothing. Not a sound, not a flicker.

Then Elijah told the people, "Okay, that's enough. My turn. Everyone, come here." So they all gathered around. He rebuilt God's altar, which was a wreck. He took twelve stones, one for each of the tribes of Jacob (the same Jacob God renamed Israel). He built the altar in God's name and then dug a big trench around it. He put the wood on the altar, cut up the bull, put it on the wood, and said, "Fill four big jars with water and pour it all over the bull and the wood." Then he said, "Do it again," and they did. "Do it a third time," and they did. The whole altar was soaked, and the trench was full of water.

When it was time for the evening sacrifice, Elijah the prophet went up and prayed, "O God, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, show them right now that you are God in Israel and that I'm your servant, doing all this because you told me to. Answer me, God, answer me and show these people that you are the one true God, and that you're giving them another chance to come back to you."
Instantly, fire from God fell from the sky and burned up the offering, the wood, the stones, the dirt, and even all the water in the trench.
When all the people saw it, they fell on their faces and started worshiping, yelling, "God is the true God! God is the true God!"
Elijah commanded them, "Grab the prophets of Baal! Don't let a single one get away!"
They grabbed them all. Elijah took them down to the Kishon Brook and had them all executed.
Then Elijah said to Ahab, "Go on, get up, eat and drink. Celebrate! Rain is coming. I can hear it."
Ahab went and ate and drank. Meanwhile, Elijah climbed to the top of Mount Carmel, bowed down low in prayer with his face between his knees. Then he told his servant, "Go look toward the sea."
He went, looked, and came back, "I don't see anything."
"Keep looking," Elijah said, "seven times if you have to."
And on the seventh time, the servant said, "Oh, wait, I see a cloud! But it's tiny, like the size of a hand, coming up from the sea."
"Quick!" Elijah said. "Go tell Ahab, 'Get in your chariot and get down the mountain before the rain traps you.'"

And then everything happened super fast. The sky turned black with clouds and wind, and then a massive downpour started. Ahab was racing his chariot back to Jezreel. And God gave Elijah a huge boost of strength. He tucked his robe into his belt and ran ahead of Ahab's chariot all the way to Jezreel.

1 Kings.title: Elijah's Burnout & God's Whisper
paragraphs: So Ahab went and told Jezebel everything Elijah had done, including how he totally wrecked her prophets. Jezebel was livid and sent a messenger to Elijah with a threat: “The gods are gonna get you for this, and I'm gonna get you. By this time tomorrow, you'll be just as dead as every one of those prophets.”

When Elijah heard this, he freaked out and ran for his life to Beersheba, way down in the south of Judah. He left his young assistant there and then walked for a whole day into the desert. He found a random broom bush, collapsed in its shade, and was just so done with everything. He wanted to die. “I’ve had enough, God! Just take my life—I’m ready to join my ancestors.” Totally exhausted, he fell asleep right there under the bush.
Suddenly, an angel shook him awake and said, “Get up and eat!”
He looked around and, what do you know, right by his head was a loaf of bread baked on some coals and a jug of water. He ate and drank, then went back to sleep.
The angel of God came back, shook him awake again, and said, “Get up and eat some more—you’ve got a long trip ahead of you.”

So he got up, ate and drank until he was full, and then started walking. That one meal gave him enough energy to walk for forty days and forty nights, all the way to Horeb, the mountain of God. When he got there, he crawled into a cave and fell asleep.
Then the word of God came to him: “So, Elijah, what are you doing here?”

“I’ve been going all out for the God-of-the-Angel-Armies,” Elijah said. “The people of Israel have ditched your covenant, wrecked the places of worship, and murdered your prophets. I’m the only one left, and now they’re trying to kill me too.”
Then he was told, “Go, stand on the mountain and wait for God. God is about to pass by.”

A crazy hurricane-level wind ripped through the mountains and shattered rocks in front of God, but God wasn't in the wind. After the wind, there was an earthquake, but God wasn't in the earthquake. And after the earthquake, there was a fire, but God wasn't in the fire. And after the fire, there was a gentle, quiet whisper.

When Elijah heard that quiet voice, he pulled his cloak over his face, went to the entrance of the cave, and just stood there. A quiet voice asked, “So Elijah, for real, what are you doing here?” Elijah repeated himself, “I’ve been working my heart out for God, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, because the people of Israel have abandoned your covenant, destroyed your places of worship, and murdered your prophets. I’m the only one left, and now they’re trying to kill me.”

God said, “Go back the way you came, through the desert to Damascus. When you get there, anoint Hazael as the new king of Aram. Then anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king of Israel. And finally, anoint Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel Meholah to take over for you as prophet. Anyone who escapes from Hazael will be killed by Jehu, and anyone who escapes from Jehu will be killed by Elisha. But listen, I’m keeping seven thousand people for myself—all the knees that haven’t bowed down to the god Baal and all the mouths that haven’t kissed his idol.”

Elijah left right away and found Elisha son of Shaphat. He was out in a field plowing with twelve teams of oxen, and Elisha was with the twelfth team. Elijah went up to him and threw his cloak over him.
Elisha just left the oxen, ran after Elijah, and said, “Please! Let me just kiss my mom and dad goodbye—then I’ll follow you.”
“Go ahead,” said Elijah, “but don't forget what I just did to you.”

So Elisha went back, took his team of oxen, and butchered them. He used the plowing equipment to make a fire and cooked the meat—a real farewell feast for his family. Then he left and followed Elijah, becoming his right-hand man.

1 Kings.title: My Enemy is My Brother?? King Ahab's Big Mistake
paragraphs: So, around this time, King Ben-Hadad of Aram got his army together. He also roped in 32 local chiefs with their horses and chariots. They rolled up to Samaria and surrounded it, ready for war. He sent a messenger to King Ahab of Israel with a message: 'Yo, Ben-Hadad says your silver, gold, and the best of your wives and kids are his now.'
The king of Israel was like, 'Okay, whatever you say, my lord; I and everything I have is yours.'

But then the messenger came back a second time and was like, 'Actually, on second thought, I want *everything*. Your silver, your gold, all your wives, all your kids. Hand it all over. You've got 24 hours. Then my guys are coming to search your palace and your officials' houses and take whatever they think is cool.'

King Ahab called all his elders and was like, 'Can you believe this guy? He's just trying to start something. He wants to completely clean me out, demanding all my wives and children, even after I already agreed to pay him a ton!'
The elders and the people were all, 'Don't do it! Don't give him anything.'
So he told Ben-Hadad's messenger, 'Tell my lord, I was cool with the first deal, but this new one? I can't. I won't do it.'
The messenger went back and delivered the answer.
Ben-Hadad shot back his response: 'I swear to God, there won't be anything left of Samaria but dust by the time I'm done.'
King Ahab shot back, 'You know, it's a lot easier to talk tough than to actually win a fight.'
It turned out, when Ben-Hadad heard this comeback, he was already day-drinking with his chiefs in their tents. Super drunk, he just yelled, 'Get 'em!' and they attacked the city.
Just then, a random prophet shows up to King Ahab and says, 'God's message: See this huge army? Well, guess what? I'm handing them over to you today. And you'll know for sure that I am God.'
Ahab was like, 'For real? And who's gonna make this happen?'
God said, 'The young soldiers of the regional chiefs.'
'And who,' asked Ahab, 'gets to start the fight?'
God said, 'You do.'
Ahab checked out the young soldiers of the regional chiefs; he counted 232 of them. Then he checked his whole army—7,000 troops.
At noon they marched out after Ben-Hadad who, with his 32 allied chiefs, was busy getting wasted in their tents. The young soldiers led the charge.
A report came to Ben-Hadad: 'Uh, there are guys coming from Samaria.'
He said, 'If they're coming in peace, take them hostage. If they're coming to fight, do the same thing—take them hostage.'

The young soldiers poured out of the city with the whole army right behind them. They went hard in hand-to-hand combat. The Arameans bailed, with Israel right on their tail. But King Ben-Hadad of Aram escaped on a horse with his cavalry.
The king of Israel wrecked their horses and chariots—it was a huge loss for Aram.

A bit later, the prophet came to the king of Israel and said, 'Stay sharp—build up your army, figure out what you're capable of, and see what needs to be done. Before the year is over, the king of Aram will be back and he'll be strong.'

Meanwhile, the advisors to the king of Aram said, 'Their god is a god of the mountains—we have no chance against them there. So let's fight them on the flat plains where we'll have the upper hand. Here's the plan: replace every chief with a pro officer. Then get an army the same size as the one that bailed—horse for horse, chariot for chariot. And we'll fight them on the plains—we're sure to be stronger than them.'
The king thought it sounded like a good plan, so he did it.

When the new year came, Ben-Hadad gathered his army and they went up to Aphek to fight Israel. The Israelite army got ready and went to meet them. They set up in two camps, looking like two small flocks of goats. The whole plain was crawling with Arameans.

Just then a holy man came to the king of Israel and said, 'This is God's word: Because Aram said, "God is a god of the mountains and not a god of the valleys," I'll hand over this massive army to you. Then you'll know that I am God.'

The two armies just stared each other down for seven days. On the seventh day, the fight broke out. The Israelites took out 100,000 of the Aramean foot soldiers in one day. The rest of the army ran for their lives back to the city, Aphek, but then the city wall fell on 27,000 of the survivors.

Ben-Hadad escaped into the city and hid in a closet. Then his advisors told him, 'Look, we've heard the kings of Israel are pretty fair. Let's wear old rags, carry a white flag, and go to the king of Israel. Maybe he'll let you live.'
So that's what they did. They dressed in old rags, carried a white flag, and came to the king of Israel saying, 'Your servant Ben-Hadad said, "Please let me live."'
Ahab said, 'You're telling me he's still alive? If he's alive, he's my brother.'
The men saw this as a good sign and figured everything would be okay: 'Ben-Hadad is definitely your brother!'
The king said, 'Go get him.' They went and brought him back in a chariot.

Ahab said, 'I'm willing to give back the cities my father took from your father. And you can set up your own business area in Damascus just like my father did in Samaria. I'll send you home safely.' Then he made a treaty with him and let him go.
A man who was one of the prophets said to a random guy, 'Hit me; hurt me. Do it for God—it's his command. Hit me; hurt me.' But the guy wouldn't do it.
So he told him, 'Because you didn't obey God's orders, a lion is going to attack you as soon as you leave.' And no sooner had the man left, a lion met him and attacked.
He then found another man and said, 'Hit me; hurt me.' That man did it—hit him hard in the face, and he started bleeding.

Then the prophet went and waited on the road for the king, with a bandage over his eyes to disguise himself. It wasn't long before the king came by. The man yelled out to the king, 'Your servant was in the middle of the battle when a guy showed up and gave me a prisoner, saying, "Guard this man with your life; if he goes missing you'll pay big time." But I got busy with other stuff and the next thing I knew, he was gone.'
The king of Israel said, 'You just decided your own punishment.'
At that, the man tore the bandage off his eyes and the king recognized who he was—one of the prophets!
The man said to the king, 'God's word: Because you let a man go who God had sentenced to die, it's now your life for his, and your people for his.'
The king of Israel went home super annoyed. He got back to Samaria in a really bad mood.

1 Kings.title: The King Who Got CANCELLED for Stealing a Vineyard
paragraphs: So, get this. On top of everything else, this happened: Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel right next to King Ahab's palace. One day, Ahab hits up Naboth and says, “Yo, let me get that vineyard. I wanna turn it into a vegetable garden since it’s right next to my house—super convenient. I’ll trade you for a way better vineyard, or if you want, I’ll just pay you cash for it.”

But Naboth was like, “Not a chance. I swear to God, I would never sell you my family’s land.” Ahab went home in a total mood, sulking over what Naboth said: “I’ll never hand over my family’s inheritance to you.” He went to bed, shoved his face in his pillow, and refused to eat.
His wife Jezebel came to him and was like, “What’s going on? Why are you so salty and refusing to eat?”

He told her, “Because I talked to Naboth the Jezreelite. I said, ‘Give me your vineyard—I’ll pay you for it or, if you’d rather, I’ll give you another vineyard in exchange.’ And he said, ‘I’ll never give you my vineyard.’”

Jezebel was like, “Is this seriously how a king of Israel acts? Aren't you the one in charge? Get up! Eat something! Cheer up! I’ll handle this. I’ll get you that vineyard from Naboth the Jezreelite.”

She wrote letters using Ahab’s name, stamped them with his official seal, and sent them to the elders and leaders in Naboth’s city. She wrote, “Announce a fast day and give Naboth the seat of honor. Then get a couple of phonies to sit across from him and publicly accuse him, saying, ‘You! You cursed God and the king!’ Then they’ll drag him out and stone him to death.”

And they actually did it. The men of the city—the elders and leaders—followed the instructions Jezebel wrote in the letters. They called for a fast day and sat Naboth at the head table. Then they brought in two liars and sat them across from Naboth. In front of everyone, the two degenerates accused him, “He cursed God and the king!” So the crowd dragged him out into the street, stoned him without mercy, and he died.

When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned to death, she told Ahab, “Go for it, Ahab—take Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard for yourself, the one he refused to sell you. Naboth is gone. Naboth is dead.”
The second Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he went down to Naboth’s vineyard and claimed it as his own.

Then God stepped in and spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, “Get up, go down and confront Ahab, king of Israel, in Samaria. You’ll find him in Naboth’s vineyard; he’s gone there to claim it. Say this to him: ‘This is God’s word: What’s going on here? First murder, then theft?’ Then tell him, ‘This is God’s verdict: In the exact spot where the dogs licked up Naboth’s blood, they’ll lick up your blood—that’s right, your blood.’”
Ahab shot back at Elijah, “My enemy! So, you’ve found me.”

“Yeah, I’ve found you out,” said Elijah. “And because you’ve sold yourself out to do evil, defying God, ‘I’m definitely bringing disaster on you, I’ll destroy your descendants, and I’ll get rid of every single guy even remotely connected to your family. I’ll bring the same fate on you that happened to Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah—you’ve made me that angry by leading Israel into sin.’”

And about Jezebel, God said, “Dogs will fight over Jezebel’s body all over Jezreel. Any of Ahab’s family who dies in the city will be eaten by stray dogs; and if they die in the country, they’ll be eaten by vultures.”

Ahab, egged on by his wife Jezebel and in total defiance of God, set a new record for making a business out of evil. He got into some seriously messed up stuff with idols, just like the Amorites who God had kicked out of Israelite territory before.

When Ahab heard what Elijah said, he tore his clothes, put on rough burlap to show he was sorry, and fasted. He even slept in coarse burlap pajamas. He started walking around super quietly, like a mouse.
Then God spoke to Elijah the Tishbite: “Do you see how sorry Ahab is acting? Because he’s repenting, I won’t bring the disaster while he’s alive; but his son will get it.”

1 Kings.title: King Goes Undercover & It Ends BADLY
paragraphs: So for three years, everything was chill—no beef between Aram and Israel. Then, in the third year, King Jehoshaphat of Judah went to meet up with the king of Israel. The king of Israel said to his crew, "Yo, do you guys realize Ramoth Gilead is actually ours, and we're just sitting here doing nothing instead of taking it back from the king of Aram?"
He turned to Jehoshaphat and was like, "You down to roll with me and fight for Ramoth Gilead?"
Jehoshaphat said, "For sure. I'm with you 100%—my squad is your squad, my horses are your horses." Then he added, "But hold up, before we do anything, let's ask God for some guidance."
So the king of Israel got all his prophets together—all 400 of them—and asked, "Should I go attack Ramoth Gilead? Or should I chill?"
They all shouted, "Go for it! God will totally hand it over to you."
But Jehoshaphat was hesitant. "Is there maybe another prophet of God around here we can check with?"
The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "Well, there is one more guy, Micaiah son of Imlah. But lowkey, I hate him. He never says anything good about me, only bad news, doom and gloom."
"Bro, a king shouldn't talk like that about a prophet," said Jehoshaphat.
So the king of Israel told one of his guys, "Go get Micaiah son of Imlah, and be quick about it."

Meanwhile, the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat were sitting on their thrones, decked out in their royal robes, right in front of the Samaria city gates. All the prophets were putting on a big show for them. This one dude, Zedekiah, even made some iron horns and was waving them around yelling, "God's word! With these, you're gonna wreck Aram until they're completely gone!" And all the other prophets were hyping him up, like, "Yeah! Go attack Ramoth Gilead! It's an easy win! God's giving it to you!"
The messenger who went to get Micaiah told him, "Listen, all the other prophets are saying the king will win. You should just agree with them and say yes too."
But Micaiah was like, "As God is my witness, I'm only gonna say what God tells me to say. No cap."
When Micaiah showed up, the king asked him, "So, Micaiah—should we attack Ramoth Gilead, or nah?"
He replied sarcastically, "Oh yeah, go for it. It'll be an easy win. God's gift to the king."
The king shot back, "Cut the crap. How many times do I have to make you swear you'll only tell me the truth from God?"

"Alright, fine," Micaiah said, "since you're insisting. I had a vision of all of Israel scattered across the hills, like sheep without a shepherd. And God said, 'These poor people have no leader. Let them just go home and try to survive.'"
The king of Israel turned to Jehoshaphat and said, "See! What did I tell you? He never has anything good to say about me from God, only doom."

Micaiah wasn't finished. "I'm not done yet; listen to God's word: I saw God on his throne, and the entire army of heaven was standing by his side. And God asked, 'Who can trick Ahab into attacking Ramoth Gilead so he'll die?' They all had different ideas. Then one spirit stepped up and said, 'I'll do it.' 'How?' God asked. 'Easy,' the spirit said, 'I'll go and make all his prophets lie.' And God said, 'That'll work. Go on, trick him.'"
"So that's what's happening right now. God has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all your prophets. God has declared your doom."
Just then, Zedekiah son of Kenaanah walked up and punched Micaiah in the face, saying, "Oh really? Since when did the Spirit of God leave me to go talk to you?"
Micaiah shot back, "You'll find out soon enough, when you're desperately looking for a place to hide and can't find one."

The king of Israel was furious. "Get Micaiah out of here! Hand him over to the city officials with this message: 'King's orders: Throw him in jail and only give him bread and water until I get back safely.'"
Micaiah said, "If you actually get back safely, then I'm not a real prophet of God."
He then yelled to the crowd, "When it all goes down, people, remember you heard it here first!"

So the king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah went to attack Ramoth Gilead. The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "You wear my royal robes; I'm gonna go into battle in disguise." So the king of Israel went into the fight undercover.
Meanwhile, the king of Aram had given his 32 chariot commanders one order: "Don't waste your time with anyone else, big or small; go after the king of Israel and only him."

When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat in the king's robes, they thought, "There he is! The king of Israel!" and they went straight for him. Jehoshaphat screamed, and the commanders realized they had the wrong guy—it wasn't the king of Israel. So they left him alone.

But then, some random soldier just shot an arrow into the air without aiming, and it hit the king of Israel right in a gap in his armor. The king told his chariot driver, "Turn around! Get me out of here—I'm hit."

The battle raged all day. The king, propped up in his chariot, had to watch from the sidelines. He died that evening, and his blood pooled in the chariot. As the sun set, a shout went through the army: "Everyone go home! The king is dead!"

They brought the king's body to Samaria and buried him there. They washed his chariot at the pool of Samaria, where the town prostitutes bathed, and dogs licked up his blood, just like God had said would happen.

The rest of Ahab's story—everything he did, the fancy ivory palace he built, the towns he founded—it's all written down in the official records of the kings of Israel. He was buried with his ancestors, and his son Ahaziah became the next king.

Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in the fourth year of Ahab's reign in Israel. Jehoshaphat was 35 when he started his 25-year rule in Jerusalem. His mom was Azubah. He basically followed in his dad Asa's footsteps, living a life that pleased God. But he messed up by not getting rid of the local shrines where people worshiped other gods. And he stayed on good terms with the king of Israel.

The rest of Jehoshaphat's life, his accomplishments and his wars, are all in the official records of the kings of Judah. He also got rid of the male shrine prostitutes that were still around from his father Asa's time.
During his reign, Edom didn't have a king; a governor was in charge.

Jehoshaphat built some big ships to go get gold from Ophir. But they never even made it out of the harbor; they wrecked at Ezion Geber. Around that time, Ahaziah, Ahab's son, suggested they team up on a shipping business, but Jehoshaphat turned him down.
Then Jehoshaphat died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Jehoram became the next king.

Ahaziah, son of Ahab, became king of Israel in Samaria during the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah. He was king for two years. And in God's eyes, he was a total failure, just living the same evil life as his parents and repeating the sinful patterns set by Jeroboam, who first led Israel into sin. By worshiping Baal, he made God, the God of Israel, super angry. If anything, he was even worse than his dad.

2 Kings.title: King Asks Wrong 'God', Gets Literally Roasted
paragraphs: Alright, so after King Ahab died, the whole nation of Moab decided they were done with Israel and started a rebellion.

So, the new king, Ahaziah, was hanging out at his palace in Samaria when he totally wiped out and fell through the balcony railing on his roof. It was a pretty bad injury. Instead of asking God for help, he sent his messengers to go ask this idol, Baal-Zebub, the god of a town called Ekron, 'Yo, am I gonna pull through this?'

But an angel of God hit up the prophet Elijah and was like, 'Hey, get up and go intercept the king's messengers.' The angel told him to give them this message: 'What's the deal? Is it because there's no God in Israel that you guys are running off to consult some idol? Here's the real message from the God you're trying to ignore: You're not getting out of that bed. You're as good as dead.' So Elijah delivered the message and bounced.
The messengers went straight back to the king. He was like, 'Wait, why are you back so soon? What happened?'

They told him, 'This random guy met us and told us to turn back and tell you a message from God. He said, "Is it because there's no God in Israel that you're sending people to consult an idol? Well, don't bother. You're not getting out of that bed you're in—you're toast."'
The king asked, 'Hold on, describe this guy who met you and said all this. What did he look like?'
'He was a pretty rugged dude,' they said, 'all hairy and wearing a leather belt.'
'Yup, that's Elijah the Tishbite,' the king said. He knew exactly who it was.
So the king sent a captain with fifty soldiers to get Elijah. Elijah was just chilling on top of a hill. The captain went up and said, 'O Holy Man! The king orders you to come down!'
Elijah shot back, 'If I'm really a 'holy man,' then let fire come down from the sky and burn you and your fifty men.' And BAM! Lightning zapped the captain and his whole crew.
The king, not getting the hint, sent another captain with another fifty men. This guy also went up and said, 'O Holy Man! The king's orders are for you to come down, like, right now!'
Elijah replied, 'If I'm a 'holy man,' let fire come down and get you and your fifty men.' And boom, another lightning strike from God toasted that captain and his guys too.

Seriously, the king sent a THIRD captain with fifty more men. But this captain was smart. He went up, fell on his knees, and begged, 'O Holy Man, please, have mercy on me and my men! I know lightning has already fried two other captains and their crews. Please, I'm begging you, spare my life!'
Then the angel of God told Elijah, 'It's cool, go with him. Don't be afraid.' So Elijah got up and went with the captain to see the king.

Elijah went right up to the king and said, 'Here's God's word: Because you sent messengers to ask an idol for help, as if there's no God in Israel to pray to, you will never get out of that bed. You're already as good as dead.'
And just like that, he died, exactly as God had said through Elijah.
Since Ahaziah didn't have a son, his brother Joram became the next king. This all happened in the second year that Jehoram, son of Jehoshaphat, was king of Judah.
And that's the tea on Ahaziah. The rest of his story is written down in the official records of the kings of Israel.

2 Kings.title: Elijah's Epic Exit & Elisha's Wild First Day
paragraphs: Just before God yeeted Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha were walking from Gilgal. Elijah told Elisha, “Hey, you should probably stay here. God’s sending me to Bethel on an errand.”
But Elisha was like, “No cap, as long as God lives and you live, I’m not leaving you.” So they went to Bethel together.
The squad of prophets at Bethel came up to Elisha and asked, “Bro, did you know God is taking your master from you today?”
He was like, “Yeah, I know. But let’s keep it lowkey.”
Then Elijah said, “For real, stay here. God’s sending me to Jericho.”
Elisha shot back, “Not a chance. As God lives and you live, I’m not leaving you.” So they went to Jericho together.
The prophet squad at Jericho came to Elisha and said, “You know God’s about to take your master from you today, right?”
He said, “Yeah, I know. Just be cool about it.”
Then Elijah said, “Okay, for real this time, stay here. God’s sending me to the Jordan River.”
Elisha said, “Nope. As God lives and you live, I’m not leaving.” So the two of them kept going.
Meanwhile, fifty guys from the prophet squad were watching from a distance as the two of them stood by the Jordan.
Elijah took off his cloak, rolled it up, and smacked the water with it. The water split down the middle, and they walked across on dry ground. It was wild.
When they got to the other side, Elijah asked Elisha, “Alright, what can I do for you before I’m taken away? Ask for anything.”
Elisha said, “I want a double portion of your spirit. I want to be a man of God just like you.”
Elijah was like, “Dang, that’s a big ask. But if you see me when I’m taken from you, you’ll get it. But only if you’re watching.”

And then it happened. As they were walking and talking, a chariot of fire with horses of fire suddenly appeared between them, and Elijah went up to heaven in a whirlwind. Elisha saw it all and screamed, “My father, my father! The chariot and horsemen of Israel!” And then he couldn’t see him anymore. He grabbed his own clothes and ripped them in two.
Then he picked up Elijah’s cloak that had fallen, went back to the bank of the Jordan, and stood there. He took the cloak and hit the water with it, saying, “Where is the God of Elijah now?”
When he hit the water, it divided, and Elisha walked across.
The prophet squad from Jericho saw the whole thing from a distance and said, “Whoa, the spirit of Elijah is on Elisha now!” They came to meet him and bowed down.
They said to him, “Look, we’ve got fifty strong guys here. Let us go and search for your master. Maybe the Spirit of God dropped him on a mountain or in a valley somewhere.”
Elisha was like, “Nah, don’t send them.”
But they kept bugging him until he was like, “Ugh, fine. Go ahead.”
So they sent the fifty men, and they searched for three days but found nothing.
When they came back to Elisha in Jericho, he said, “See? Told you so.”
The men of the city came to Elisha and said, “Master, this city is in a nice spot, but the water is bad, and it’s causing our crops to fail.”
He said, “Bring me a new bowl and put some salt in it.” So they did.

He went to the spring, threw the salt in, and said, “This is what God says: ‘I have healed this water. It won’t cause death or make the land unproductive anymore.’” And the water has been pure ever since, just like Elisha said.
Another time, Elisha was walking up to Bethel, and a bunch of kids from the town came out and started making fun of him, yelling, “Go on up, baldy! Go on up, baldy!”
He turned around, looked at them, and cursed them in the name of God. Then two bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of them.
Elisha then went on to Mount Carmel and later returned to Samaria.

2 Kings.title: The Time God Sent a Flood Without Rain
paragraphs: So, Joram, Ahab's son, became the king of Israel in Samaria. This was during the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah. He was king for twelve years, and honestly, he was a pretty bad king in God's eyes. But, lowkey, he wasn't as bad as his mom and dad. To his credit, he did get rid of the messed-up Baal statue his dad had made. But he was still into the same sinful stuff as Jeroboam, the guy who had messed up Israel for a long time. He just wouldn't quit.

Now, King Mesha of Moab was a sheep guy. He was forced to give the king of Israel 100,000 lambs and 100,000 rams. But when Ahab died, the king of Moab was like, 'I'm out,' and rebelled against the king of Israel. So King Joram got his army ready for war. First thing he did was send a message to Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, saying, 'The king of Moab is rebelling against me. You wanna join me and fight him?'
Jehoshaphat was all in. 'I'm with you, man. My soldiers are your soldiers, my horses are your horses. Which way are we going?'
'Through the desert of Edom.'
So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom started out on this crazy, long detour. After seven days, they ran out of water for both the army and the animals.
The king of Israel was like, 'This is bad. God brought us three kings out here just to let Moab destroy us.'
But Jehoshaphat asked, 'Isn't there a prophet of God around here we can ask?'
One of the king of Israel's servants said, 'Elisha son of Shaphat is somewhere around here—he was Elijah's right-hand man.'
Jehoshaphat said, 'Perfect! A guy we can trust!' So the three kings—Israel, Jehoshaphat, and Edom—went to find him.
Elisha looked at the king of Israel and said, 'What do you want from me? Go ask the fake prophets your parents listened to.'
'No way!' said the king of Israel. 'It's God who got us into this mess, and now he's going to let Moab defeat all three of us.'

Elisha said, 'As the God of Angel Armies lives, the one I serve, if it wasn't for the respect I have for King Jehoshaphat of Judah, I wouldn't even be talking to you. But since you're here, bring me a musician.' (When the musician played, the power of God came on Elisha.)

Then he said, 'God's word: Dig ditches all over this valley. And here's what's gonna happen—you won't hear any wind, you won't see any rain, but this valley is going to fill up with water, and your army and animals will have plenty to drink. This is easy for God to do; he's also going to give you victory over Moab. You're going to destroy their country: tear down their forts, flatten their main villages, cut down their orchards, block their springs, and cover their fields with rocks.'
In the morning, around the time of the morning sacrifice, water started pouring in from the west, from Edom. It was a flash flood that filled the whole valley.

By this time, everyone in Moab had heard that the kings were coming to fight them. Every guy who could hold a sword was called up and they all stood at the border. They were up early in the morning when the sun rose over the water. From where the Moabites were standing, the water looked red, like blood.
'Blood! Look at the blood!' they said. 'The kings must have fought each other—a total massacre! Let's go get the loot, Moab!'

When the Moabites entered the Israelite camp, the Israelites jumped up and started attacking them. The Moabites ran for their lives, but the Israelites were relentless—it was a slaughter. They destroyed the towns, covered the fields with rocks, blocked the springs, and cut down the orchards. Only the capital city, Kir Hareseth, was left, and not for long. It was surrounded and attacked with slingshots and rocks.

When the king of Moab saw that he was losing, he took seven hundred swordsmen to try and break through the king of Edom's line, but they failed. Then he took his oldest son, the one who was supposed to be the next king, and sacrificed him on the city wall. This made God furious with Israel. So Israel pulled back and went home.

2 Kings.title: Prophet's Miracles Go VIRAL
paragraphs: So, the wife of a guy from the prophet squad went to Elisha and was like, “My husband, your student, is dead. You know he was a solid dude who was all in for God. But now, the guy he owed money to is coming to take my two sons as slaves to settle the debt.”
Elisha said, “Okay, how can I help? Tell me, what do you have in your house?”
“Literally nothing,” she said. “Well, except for a tiny bit of oil.”

“Alright, here’s the game plan,” Elisha said. “Go hit up all your neighbors and borrow every empty jar and container you can find. And I mean a LOT—get as many as possible. Then go home, lock the door with you and your sons inside. Start pouring that little bit of oil into every container. When one’s full, put it to the side and grab the next one.”

She did exactly what he said. She locked the door with her and her sons inside. They kept bringing her containers, and she kept filling them up. When every single jar and bowl was full, she asked one of her sons, “Hey, pass me another jar.”
He replied, “That’s it. There are no more.”
And just like that, the oil stopped flowing.
She went and told the man of God what happened. He said, “Go sell all that oil and pay off your debts. You and your sons can live on the money that’s left over.”

Another time, Elisha was passing through a town called Shunem. A really important woman in the town convinced him to stop and have a meal. After that, it became a thing: whenever he was in the area, he’d stop by her place to eat.

The woman told her husband, “I’m lowkey sure this guy who always stops by is a holy man of God. What if we build a small room for him on the roof? We can put a bed, a desk, a chair, and a lamp in it. That way, whenever he comes, he has his own space to crash.”
So, it happened. The next time Elisha came, he went up to his new room and took a nap.
He told his servant, Gehazi, “Go tell the Shunammite woman I want to talk to her.” So Gehazi called her, and she came up.
Elisha had Gehazi tell her, “You’ve done so much for us, way more than you had to. What can we do for you? You want us to put in a good word for you with the king or the army commander?”
She was like, “Nah, I’m good. I’ve got my family, I’m content.”
Elisha talked it over with Gehazi, “There has to be something we can do for her. But what?”
Gehazi said, “Well, she doesn’t have a son, and her husband is pretty old.”
“Call her back,” Elisha said. He called her, and she stood at the doorway.
Elisha told her, “A year from now, you’re going to be holding your own baby boy.”
She was like, “Whoa, master, man of God, for real? Don’t play with me like that. Don’t get my hopes up with some fantasy.”
But the woman got pregnant. A year later, just like Elisha had promised, she had a son.
The kid grew up. One day, he went out to his dad, who was working with the harvest crew, and started yelling, “My head, my head!”
His dad told a servant, “Carry him to his mother.”
The servant picked him up and brought him to his mom. The boy just lay on her lap until noon, and then he died.
She carried him upstairs and laid him on the bed that belonged to the man of God. She shut the door, leaving him there alone, and then she left.
She called to her husband, “Quick, get me a servant and a donkey. I have to go see the man of God. I’ll be back as fast as I can.”
He was like, “But why today? It’s not a special holiday or anything.”
She just said, “Don’t ask. I have to go. Now. Trust me.”
She saddled up the donkey and told her servant, “You lead the way, and go as fast as you can. I’ll let you know if you’re going too fast.” And off she went. She found the man of God on Mount Carmel.

The man of God saw her coming from a distance and said to his servant Gehazi, “Yo, look! It’s the Shunammite woman! Run over there and ask her, ‘Is everything okay? Are you good? Is your husband okay? Your kid okay?’”
She just said, “Everything’s fine.”
But when she got to the man of God on the mountain, she fell at his feet and just clung to him.
Gehazi tried to pull her off, but the man of God said, “Leave her alone. Can’t you see she’s in major distress? God hasn’t told me what’s wrong; I’m totally in the dark here.”
Then she finally said it: “Did I even ask you for a son, master? Didn’t I tell you not to mess with me and give me false hope?”
He immediately ordered Gehazi, “No time to waste. Grab my staff and run. Don’t stop to say hi to anyone. If someone says hi to you, just ignore them. Lay my staff on the boy’s face.”
The boy’s mom said, “As surely as God is real and you are real, you are not leaving me here.” So Elisha let her go first and followed her.
Gehazi got there first and laid the staff on the boy’s face. But there was nothing. No sound, no sign of life. Gehazi went back to meet Elisha and told him, “The boy didn’t even move.”

Elisha went into the house and saw the boy lying dead on the bed. He went into the room, locked the door so it was just the two of them, and prayed to God. Then he got on the bed and lay on top of the boy, covering him with his own body—mouth to mouth, eyes to eyes, hands to hands. As he was stretched out over him, the boy’s body started to get warm. Elisha got up and walked around the room for a bit. Then he went back and stretched out on the boy again. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
He called Gehazi and said, “Get the Shunammite woman in here!” He called her and she came in.
Elisha said, “Go hug your son.”
She fell at Elisha’s feet, face on the ground, totally in awe. Then she hugged her son and walked out with him.
Elisha went back to Gilgal, where there was a huge famine. While he was meeting with the group of prophets, he told his servant, “Put a big pot on the fire and cook some stew for everyone.”

One of the guys went out to a field to find some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked a bunch of gourds from it, filling his bag. He brought them back, chopped them up, and threw them in the stew, even though nobody knew what they were. The stew was served, and the men started to eat. But then they all screamed, “Dude, there’s death in this pot! Death in the pot!” No one could eat it.
Elisha said, “Bring me some flour.” He sprinkled it into the pot.
“Okay, serve it to the men now,” he said. They ate it, and it was totally fine—nothing wrong with the stew at all.
Another day, a man came from a place called Baal Shalishah. He brought the man of God twenty loaves of fresh bread from the first harvest, and some apples from his orchard.
Elisha said, “Pass it out for everyone to eat.”
His servant was like, “For a hundred guys? No way, this is not nearly enough!”
Elisha just said, “Do it. God says there’s more than enough.”
And for real, there was. He passed out what he had, and not only did everyone eat, but there were leftovers.

2 Kings.title: This General's Wild Skin Transformation
paragraphs: So, there was this guy Naaman, the top general for the king of Aram. He was a big deal, super respected by his boss because God had used him to win battles for Aram. A total legend, but he had this really bad skin problem. Anyway, during a raid on Israel, they captured this young girl who ended up working for Naaman's wife. One day, she told her mistress, "Yo, if my master could just meet the prophet in Samaria, he'd totally get healed from his skin thing."
Naaman went straight to his master and told him what the girl from Israel had said.
"Alright, bet," said the king of Aram. "I'll even write you a letter to the king of Israel so he knows you're coming."
So Naaman took off with a ton of silver, a bunch of gold, and ten fresh outfits.
Naaman gave the letter to the king of Israel. It was like, "When you get this, know that I'm sending my guy Naaman to you. Heal his skin condition."

When the king of Israel read the letter, he freaked out and ripped his clothes. He was like, "Am I a god? Can I kill people and bring them back to life? Why is he sending this guy to me to be healed? This is sus. He's just trying to start a fight, for real!"

Elisha, the man of God, heard that the king of Israel was so stressed he ripped his clothes. He sent a message to the king, saying, "Why are you bugging out and ripping your clothes? Send him to me, and he'll find out there's a real prophet in Israel."
So Naaman rolled up with his horses and chariots and pulled up to Elisha's front door.
Elisha didn't even come out. He just sent a servant with a message: "Go wash yourself in the Jordan River seven times. Your skin will be all better, good as new."

Naaman was so mad. He turned around and was like, "I thought he'd at least come out and see me, pray to his God, wave his hand over my skin, and heal me. The rivers in Damascus, the Abana and Pharpar, are way cleaner than any river in Israel. Why can't I just wash in them and get clean?" He stormed off, super ticked.
But his servants ran after him and said, "Sir, if the prophet had asked you to do something crazy and heroic, you would've done it, right? So why not just do this simple thing, 'wash and be clean'?"
So he did it. He went down to the Jordan and dipped himself in seven times, just like the man of God said. And his skin was totally healed, smooth like a baby's. He was brand new.

Then he went back to the man of God with his whole crew, stood in front of him, and said, "Okay, now I know for sure that there's no other God on earth but the God of Israel. For real. As a thank you, please take this gift."
"As God lives," Elisha said, "the God I serve, I'm not taking anything from you." Naaman tried to get him to take it, but he wouldn't.

"If you won't take it," Naaman said, "then let me ask for something. Can I get some dirt, like, as much as two donkeys can carry? Because I'm never going to worship any other god but God again. But, uh, there's one thing I need God to forgive me for. When my master leans on my arm and goes into the temple of Rimmon to worship, and I'm there with him, bowing down too, I hope God will forgive me for that."
Elisha said, "It's all good. Go in peace."

But he hadn't gone far when Gehazi, Elisha's servant, thought to himself, "My master just let this Naaman guy go without even a thank you. As God is alive, I'm gonna go after him and get something." And Gehazi ran after Naaman.
Naaman saw him running and jumped down from his chariot to meet him. "Is everything okay?"

"Yeah, everything's fine, but something came up. My master sent me to tell you that two young prophets just showed up from the hill country of Ephraim. He said to give them some silver and a couple of new outfits."

Naaman was like, "Of course, how about double the silver?" He insisted, tied up the money in two bags, gave him the two sets of clothes, and even sent two of his own servants to carry the stuff back for him.
When they got to the hill, Gehazi took the gifts from the servants, hid them inside, and sent the servants away.
He went back and stood before his master. Elisha asked, "So, what were you up to, Gehazi?"
"Nothing much," he said.

Elisha said, "Didn't you know I was with you in spirit when that man got down from his chariot to meet you? Seriously, is this the time to be lining your own pockets with gifts? Naaman's skin disease is now going to be on you and your family, forever." Gehazi walked away, and his skin was all white and flaky, like snow.

2 Kings.title: Floating Axe Heads & Invisible Armies?!
paragraphs: One day, the crew of prophets went to Elisha and were like, "Look, this place we're living in with you is getting seriously cramped. We have no elbow room."
They said, "Can we get permission to go down to the Jordan River? Each of us can grab a log and we'll build a bigger place."
Elisha was cool with it. "Go ahead," he said.
Then one of them was like, "Please! You should totally come with us!"
"For sure," Elisha replied.
So he went with them. They got to the Jordan and started chopping down trees. As one of the guys was cutting down a big piece of timber, his axe head flew right off and sank in the river.
"Oh no, master!" he yelled. "And it was borrowed!"
The Holy Man asked, "Where did it sink?"
The guy showed him the spot.
Elisha cut a branch off a tree and tossed it right where the axe head fell. And you won't believe this—the axe head floated to the surface.
"Go grab it," he said. The man reached out and took it.
Another time, the king of Aram was at war with Israel. He had a meeting with his officers and said, "I want to set up an ambush at this specific spot."
But the Holy Man sent a message to the king of Israel: "Watch out when you pass by this place, because the Arameans have set up a trap there."
So the king of Israel sent a warning to the people at the place the Holy Man had told him about.
This kind of thing happened all the time.
The king of Aram was absolutely furious about this. He got his officers together and demanded, "Tell me, who is leaking information to the king of Israel? Who is the spy in our group?"
But one of his officers said, "It's not us, my king. It's Elisha, the prophet in Israel. He tells the king of Israel literally everything you say, even the stuff you whisper in your bedroom."
The king ordered, "Go find out where he is. I'll send people to capture him."
The report came back: "He's in Dothan."
So the king sent out horses and chariots—a huge, impressive army. They traveled by night and surrounded the city.
Early the next morning, a servant of the Holy Man got up and went outside. Surprise! The city was surrounded by horses and chariots. The young man freaked out, "Oh, master! What are we going to do?"
Elisha told him, "Don't even worry about it. There are more on our side than on their side."
Then Elisha prayed, "O God, open his eyes and let him see."
And God opened the young man's eyes. He looked, and it was a wonder. The entire mountainside was filled with horses and chariots of fire, all surrounding Elisha.
When the Arameans started to attack, Elisha prayed to God, "Strike these people blind!" And God struck them blind, just as Elisha had asked.
Then Elisha called out to the blind army, "You're going the wrong way! This isn't the right city! Follow me, and I'll lead you to the man you're looking for." And he led them all the way to Samaria.
As they entered the city, Elisha prayed, "O God, open their eyes so they can see where they are." God opened their eyes, and they looked around—they were trapped inside Samaria!
When the king of Israel saw them, he asked Elisha, "Father, should I just massacre them all?"
"Not a chance!" said Elisha. "You didn't do anything to capture them, so why would you kill them? No way. Make a big feast for them and then send them back to their master."
So the king prepared a huge feast for them. After they had eaten and drunk as much as they wanted, he sent them home. After that, the raiding parties from Aram stopped bothering Israel for a while.

But later, King Ben-Hadad of Aram gathered his entire army and attacked Samaria, laying siege to it. This caused a terrible famine, so bad that food prices went through the roof. A donkey's head cost eighty shekels of silver, and a small bowl of field greens cost five shekels!
One day, the king of Israel was walking along the city wall when a woman cried out to him, "Help me, your majesty!"
He answered, "If God won't help you, how can I? Should I get you grain from the granary? Or wine from the dairy?"
The king then said, "Tell me what's wrong."

She said, "This woman came to me and said, 'Give me your son, and we'll eat him today. Tomorrow, we'll eat my son.' So we cooked my son and ate him. The next day, I told her, 'It's your turn—bring your son so we can eat him.' But she had hidden her son away."

When the king heard the woman's story, he tore his robes in grief. Since he was on the city wall, everyone saw that he was wearing coarse burlap under his clothes as a sign of mourning. And he shouted, "May God strike me down if Elisha son of Shaphat still has his head on his shoulders by the end of today!"

Elisha was at home, sitting with the elders. The king had already sent an executioner, but before the man arrived, Elisha said to the elders, "Do you know that this murderer has just sent a man to cut off my head? Look, when the executioner gets here, shut the door and lock it. Don't I hear the footsteps of his master right behind him?"
While he was still talking, the king himself showed up and accused him, saying, "This disaster is from God! What's next? I'm so done with God!"

2 Kings.title: From Starving to Feasting, Like, Overnight
paragraphs: Elisha was like, “Yo, listen up! God’s got something to say. The famine is officially over. By this time tomorrow, food will be super cheap and everywhere—a bunch of flour for a single coin, two big scoops of grain for a single coin. The market at the city gate is gonna be popping.”
But the official who was always with the king just scoffed at the prophet, saying, “Yeah, right. You expect us to believe that? Like food is just gonna magically fall out of the sky?”
Elisha shot back, “Oh, you’ll see it happen with your own eyes, but you won’t get to eat a single bite.”

Meanwhile, there were four guys with leprosy just chilling outside the city gate. They said to each other, “Bro, what are we doing just sitting here waiting to die? If we go into the city, we’ll starve to death with everyone else. If we stay here, we’ll die too. So, let's just take a chance and sneak over to the Aramean camp. If they let us live, cool. If they kill us, well, we were gonna die anyway. We’ve got nothing to lose.”

So when the sun went down, they got up and headed to the Aramean camp. But when they got to the edge of it, plot twist! There was literally no one there. Turns out, the Lord had made the whole Aramean army hear what sounded like a massive army with chariots and horses charging at them. They all freaked out and said, “The king of Israel must have hired Egyptian and Hittite armies to attack us!” They totally panicked and ran for their lives in the middle of the night, leaving everything behind—tents, horses, donkeys, the whole camp was just left as is. Those four lepers walked into the camp, went into a tent, and had a feast. Then they grabbed a bunch of silver, gold, and clothes, and went and hid it all. They came back, looted another tent, and hid that stuff too.

Finally, they looked at each other and were like, “Okay, we probably shouldn’t be doing this. This is a day of amazing news, and we’re just keeping it to ourselves. That's lowkey selfish. If we wait until morning, we’re gonna get in trouble. Let’s go tell the king’s palace right now.”

So they went back to the city gate and shouted the news, “We went to the Aramean camp and—you’re not gonna believe this—it’s completely empty. Not a single person, not a sound! The horses and donkeys are still tied up, and the tents are just sitting there.”

The gatekeepers passed the message all the way to the king's palace. The king, woken up in the middle of the night, told his servants, “I know what’s going on. The Arameans know we’re starving. They’ve left their camp and are hiding in the fields. They’re thinking, ‘When the Israelites come out, we’ll capture them and take over the city.’”

But one of his advisors said, “Hold up, let’s send some guys with five of the remaining horses. I mean, the worst that can happen to them is the same thing that could happen to any of us left in the city. Let’s just send them to see what’s up.”
So they sent out two chariots with horses. The king ordered them, “Go follow the Aramean army and find out what happened.”

They followed the trail all the way to the Jordan River, and the whole path was littered with clothes and gear that the Arameans had ditched in their rush to escape. The scouts came back and told the king everything.

Then the people rushed out and looted the entire Aramean camp. Just like God said, food prices crashed overnight. You could get a ton of flour for one coin, and two tons of grain for one coin. It was wild.

The king had put his right-hand man, the official he always leaned on, in charge of the gate. But the starving people were like a mob and just poured through the gate, trampling the official to death in the chaos. It happened exactly like the prophet had said it would when the king visited him.

Every single thing the prophet told the king came true. He said, “A bunch of flour for a coin, two big scoops of grain for a coin, this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria.” And when the official had replied with a sarcastic, “Yeah right, like food’s gonna fall from the sky?” the prophet had said, “You’ll see it with your own eyes, but you won’t eat a single bite.” And that’s exactly what happened. The final detail was the people trampling him to death at the gate.

2 Kings.title: Prophecies, Betrayal, and a Wild Ride for the Throne
paragraphs: So, like, 8 years ago, Elisha told this lady whose son he'd brought back from the dead, "Yo, you and your fam need to dip. God's calling a seven-year famine on this place." The woman actually listened to the prophet and bounced. She and her family were basically refugees in Philistia for seven years. When the seven years were over, they came back and she went straight to the king to get her house and land back.

At that exact moment, the king was chatting with Gehazi, Elisha's assistant, and was like, "Bro, tell me some of the wild stuff Elisha has done." And no cap, right as Gehazi was telling the king about how Elisha brought a dead person back to life, the *actual* woman whose son was resurrected showed up, asking for her property back. The timing was insane.
Gehazi was like, "My king, no way! This is her! This is the lady, and that's her son who Elisha brought back from the dead!"

The king was shook and wanted the whole story, so she told him everything. Then the king put an official on the case and said, "Make sure she gets all her stuff back, plus all the money her farm made while she was gone."
Later, Elisha went to Damascus. The king of Aram, Ben-Hadad, was super sick. Someone told him, "The prophet is in town."
The king told his official, Hazael, "Go meet the prophet and bring a gift. Ask God through him if I'm gonna get better from this sickness."

Hazael went to meet Elisha with a ton of gifts from Damascus—like, 40 camel-loads of the best stuff! He stood in front of Elisha and said, "Your son, King Ben-Hadad of Aram, sent me to ask you: 'Am I going to recover from this sickness?'"

Elisha was like, "Go tell him, 'Don't trip, you'll live.' But lowkey, God showed me he's actually gonna die." Then Elisha just stared at Hazael, like he was reading his soul. Hazael got all awkward and looked away. Then the prophet started crying.
Hazael asked, "My lord, why are you crying?"

Elisha said, "Because I know the terrible things you're going to do to the people of Israel. You're gonna burn down their fortresses, murder their young men, smash their babies, and rip open their pregnant women."
Hazael was like, "Whoa, am I some kind of dog that I would do something that messed up?"
Elisha just said, "God showed me that you will be the king of Aram."
Hazael left and went back to his king, who asked, "So, what did Elisha say?"
He said, "He told me, 'Don't worry, you'll live.'"
But the very next day, Hazael took a thick blanket, soaked it in water, and held it over the king's face until he suffocated. And just like that, Hazael became king.

In the fifth year that Joram, son of Ahab, was king of Israel, Jehoram, son of Jehoshaphat, became king of Judah. He was 32 when he started his reign, and he was king in Jerusalem for eight years. He totally copied the lifestyle of the kings of Israel, even marrying into Ahab's messed-up family. From God's POV, he was just another evil dude living an evil life. But because of his promise to David, God wasn't ready to destroy Judah yet. He had promised to keep a light shining for David's descendants.
During Jehoram's rule, Edom rebelled against Judah and got their own king. Jehoram took his army and chariots to a place called Zair to deal with it.
The Edomites surrounded him, but in the middle of the night, he and his chariot commanders broke through their lines and wrecked them. But then his own soldiers bailed on him.
Edom is still in rebellion against Judah to this day. Even the small town of Libnah rebelled at that time.

The rest of the story of Jehoram's life and his rule is written in *The Chronicles of the Kings of Judah*. Jehoram died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Ahaziah took over as king.

In the twelfth year that Joram, son of Ahab, was king of Israel, Ahaziah, son of Jehoram, became king of Judah. Ahaziah was 22 when he started his reign, and he only ruled for a year in Jerusalem. His mom was Athaliah, the granddaughter of King Omri of Israel. He lived and ruled just like the Ahab family, continuing their legacy of doing evil in God's eyes. He was connected to the Ahab family by marriage and by sin.

He teamed up with Joram, son of Ahab, to fight against King Hazael of Aram at Ramoth Gilead. Joram got wounded by archers and had to go back to Jezreel to recover. Ahaziah, king of Judah, went to visit Joram while he was on his sickbed in Jezreel.

2 Kings.title: Jehu's Purge Goes Viral
paragraphs: So, Ahab had like, seventy sons still hanging out in Samaria. Jehu shot off some letters to the big shots in Jezreel—the city elders and the guys looking after Ahab’s sons. He basically wrote:

This is your heads-up. You've got your master's kids, all the chariots, horses, a fortified city, and weapons. So pick the best and most qualified of your master's sons, put him on the throne, and get ready to fight for your old boss's dynasty.
They were totally shook by the letter. They were like, “Dude, he already took out two kings. What chance do we have?”

So, the palace manager, the mayor, the elders, and the guardians all sent a message back to Jehu saying, “We’re your servants now. We'll do whatever you say. We're not picking a new king. You're the boss—do what you think is best.”
Then Jehu sent a second letter:
If you're really on my team and ready to follow orders, here's the deal: chop off all of your master's sons' heads and bring them to me in Jezreel by this time tomorrow.

The king's sons, all seventy of them, were being raised by the city's leaders. When they got that letter, they grabbed all seventy sons and killed them. Then they put their heads in baskets and shipped them off to Jehu in Jezreel.
A messenger came to Jehu and said, “They’ve delivered the heads of the king’s sons.”
He was like, “Stack them in two piles at the city gate and leave them there till morning.”

In the morning, Jehu went out, stood in front of everyone, and gave a speech: “You guys are actually part of God’s righteous plan today. Yeah, I'm the one who conspired against my master and killed him. But who do you think is responsible for this pile of heads? Know this for sure: not a single word God spoke against Ahab's family has been canceled. You're seeing it happen right now—God doing exactly what he said he'd do through Elijah.”
Then Jehu went on a spree and killed everyone even remotely connected to Ahab's family in Jezreel—leaders, friends, priests. He wiped them all out.
After that, he dusted himself off and headed to Samaria. On the way, at a place called Beth Eked of the Shepherds, he ran into some relatives of King Ahaziah of Judah.
Jehu asked, “Who are you?”
They said, “We’re Ahaziah’s relatives, and we're heading down for a royal family reunion.”
“Grab them!” Jehu ordered. His men captured them and then slaughtered all forty-two of them at the well of Beth Eked. There were no survivors.
He kept going and then ran into Jehonadab the Recabite, who was on his way to meet him. Jehu greeted him and said, “Are we on the same page here? Are you with me on this?”
Jehonadab said, “Totally. You can count on me.”
“Then give me your hand,” said Jehu.
They shook on it, and Jehonadab hopped into the chariot with Jehu.
“Come with me,” Jehu said, “and see how passionate I am for God.” So they rode off together in the chariot.
When they got to Samaria, Jehu killed everyone left in the city who had any connection to Ahab. It was a total wipeout, just like God had told Elijah would happen.
Next, Jehu gathered all the people and made an announcement:
Ahab was a part-time Baal worshiper; I'm going to be a full-time, hardcore one.

“Get all the prophets of Baal here—every single servant and priest. Don't leave anyone out. I’m about to throw a huge sacrifice for Baal. If you don't show up, you're dead.” (This was a total lie, of course. Jehu was planning to destroy all of Baal's worshipers.)
Jehu ordered, “Set up a special holy event for Baal.” So they did, and they announced the date.
Jehu then sent word to everyone in Israel. They all came—every single Baal worshiper in the country. No one stayed home. They flooded into Baal's temple until it was packed.
Jehu told the guy in charge of the wardrobe, “Get robes for all the servants of Baal.” And he brought them out.

Then Jehu and Jehonadab the Recabite went into the temple of Baal and said, “Double-check and make sure there are no worshipers of God in here. Only Baal worshipers allowed.” Then they started the worship service with sacrifices and burnt offerings.
Meanwhile, Jehu had eighty of his men waiting outside with these orders: “Don’t let a single person escape. If you do, you'll pay with your own life.”
As soon as Jehu finished the sacrificial ceremony, he gave the signal to his officers and guards: “Go in and kill them all! No survivors!”

And the massacre began. The officers and guards threw the bodies outside and cleared a path to the inner shrine of Baal. They dragged out the sacred stone pillar from Baal's temple and smashed it to pieces. They destroyed the Baal altars and tore down the temple. It’s been a public toilet ever since.
And that’s the story of how Jehu got rid of Baal worship in Israel.

But even after all that, Jehu didn't stop committing the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, the sins that had dragged Israel into a sinful lifestyle—the golden calves in Bethel and Dan were left untouched.
God told Jehu, “You did a good job doing what I wanted. You followed my orders against Ahab's family. As a reward, your sons will sit on the throne of Israel for four generations.”
Even so, Jehu wasn't careful to follow God's ways with his whole heart. He didn't turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, who had led Israel into a life of sin.

It was around this time that God started to shrink Israel's territory. Hazael started chipping away at the borders of Israel east of the Jordan—all the land of Gilead, Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh, from Aroer near the Arnon Gorge. Basically, all of Gilead and Bashan.

The rest of Jehu's life story, all his accomplishments and his fame, are written in The Chronicles of the Kings of Israel. Jehu died and was buried with his ancestors in Samaria. His son Jehoahaz became the next king. Jehu ruled Israel from Samaria for twenty-eight years.

2 Kings.title: The Hidden King's Epic Comeback
paragraphs: So, Ahaziah's mom, Athaliah, found out her son was dead and went full-on power hungry. She decided to wipe out the entire royal family to secure her spot on the throne. But plot twist! Jehosheba, who was King Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's sister, snatched Ahaziah's baby son, Joash, right before he was about to get axed with the other princes. She stashed him and his nanny in a secret room, totally off Athaliah's radar. He survived, and they stayed hidden in God's Temple for six whole years. Meanwhile, Athaliah was running the country, completely clueless that the real heir was still alive.

Okay, so seven years later, this priest named Jehoiada calls a secret meeting with the top security guys—the captains of the bodyguards and the palace guards. They all meet up at the Temple. He makes them swear a super serious oath of secrecy, and then, boom, he reveals the hidden prince, Joash.

Then he lays down the plan: 'Alright, listen up. All of you, the guys starting your shift at the palace and the guys finishing up at the Temple, you're gonna team up during the guard change. Form a human shield around the new king, and be ready to fight. If anyone even *tries* to get through, take them out. Your one and only job is to protect the king, 24/7, wherever he goes.'

The captains were all in. They gathered their squads—both the on-duty and off-duty guys—and reported to Jehoiada. The priest then hooks them up with some legendary gear: spears and shields that used to belong to King David himself, which had been kept in the Temple. Now fully kitted out, the guards got into position, making a protective circle around the Altar and the Temple, ready to defend the king.

The priest then brought out the prince, put the crown on his head, gave him the official scroll of God's laws, and officially made him king. They anointed him with oil, and everyone just went wild, cheering and shouting, 'Long live the king!'

Athaliah heard all the noise from the guards and the crowd and rushed over to the Temple to see what was up. She was shook. There was the new king, standing by the royal pillar, surrounded by his captains and trumpeters, and the whole crowd was celebrating like crazy with trumpets blasting. Athaliah freaked out, tore her clothes, and started screaming, 'Treason! This is a coup!'

Jehoiada the priest ordered the army officers, 'Get her out of here! And if anyone tries to help her, kill them on the spot!' He had already told them not to kill her inside the Temple. So they grabbed her and dragged her out to the palace's horse entrance, and that's where they finished her.
Then Jehoiada made a covenant, a solemn promise, between God, the king, and the people, that they would be God's people. He also made a pact between the king and the people.
The people then stormed the temple of Baal and completely wrecked it. They smashed the altars and idols into a million pieces and killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, right in front of his own altar.

Jehoiada then set up guards for God's Temple. He had the bodyguard officers, the palace security, and all the people escort the king from the Temple, through the main Guard's Gate, and into the royal palace. There, he sat on the king's throne. The whole city celebrated, and everything was finally chill and peaceful. And as for Athaliah, she was taken care of with the royal sword.
Joash was only seven years old when he became king.

2 Kings.title: Temple Flip Turns Deadly
paragraphs: So, in Jehu's seventh year as king, this dude Joash steps up and starts his own reign. He was king in Jerusalem for a solid 40 years. His mom was a woman named Gazelle from Beersheba.

Basically, for as long as the priest Jehoiada was teaching and training him, Joash did what was right in God's eyes. (But, lowkey, he never got around to tearing down the sketchy hilltop shrines—people were still going there all the time, making sacrifices and burning incense.)

Joash told the priests, "Yo, all the money that comes into God's Temple for offerings—whether it's the required stuff or people just giving it freely—let's use it to fix up the Temple wherever it's falling apart. Just make sure you keep track of it all."
But fast-forward 23 years into Joash's rule, and the priests hadn't done a single thing. The Temple was still a total wreck.

So King Joash calls in Jehoiada the priest and his whole crew and is like, "Uh, why haven't you renovated this beat-up Temple? You're cut off. No more taking money for Temple repairs. From now on, hand over every single coin you get."
The priests had to agree to stop taking the money and to stay out of the renovation project.

Then Jehoiada got this idea. He took a chest, cut a hole in the lid, and put it right by the main entrance of God's Temple. All the offerings people brought were dropped into that chest by the priests guarding the door. Whenever they saw the chest was getting full, the king's secretary and the head priest would come, empty it out, and count all the money. They'd give the counted cash to the project managers, who then paid the carpenters, builders, masons, and stonecutters. They also used it to buy timber and stone for the repairs—basically, any expense for fixing up God's Temple. But none of that money was used for the fancy extras, like silver cups, candle snuffers, or gold and silver instruments. It all went to the workers fixing the Temple. And get this—they trusted the guys handling the money so much that they didn't even need to audit them. They were just straight-up honest dudes. The only money that didn't go into the building fund was from the special offerings for guilt and sin—that money went directly to the priests.

Around this time, King Hazael of Aram went and attacked Gath, and he actually captured it. Then he got ambitious and set his sights on Jerusalem. Joash, the king of Judah, countered by gathering up all the sacred stuff his ancestors—kings Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah—had dedicated, plus his own holy gifts. He also grabbed all the gold he could find in the temple and palace storerooms and sent it all as a massive bribe to King Hazael. That did the trick. Hazael was satisfied, bounced, and left Jerusalem alone.

The rest of the story of Joash, and everything he did, is all written down in the official records of the kings of Judah. But it ends pretty badly for him. His own palace staff plotted against him and assassinated him while he was taking a walk on the ramp of the city's outer wall. The assassins were Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer. And that's how Joash died. He was buried in the royal tombs in the City of David, and his son Amaziah became the next king.

2 Kings.title: Elisha's Last Prophecy & a Dude Comes Back to Life?!
paragraphs: Alright, so in the 23rd year that Joash was king of Judah, this dude Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, became the king of Israel in Samaria. He was in charge for seventeen years, and honestly, he was kinda trash. He was doing all sorts of evil stuff in God's eyes, basically just copying the terrible example of Jeroboam, the guy who got Israel into sin in the first place. He didn't even try to be better. God was so over it and furious with Israel, so He let King Hazael of Aram and his son Ben-Hadad just walk all over them. This went on for a super long time.

Then Jehoahaz finally prayed for God to chill out, and God actually listened. He saw how messed up life was for the Israelites because of the king of Aram's cruelty. So God sent a savior for Israel who got them out from under Aram's thumb. The Israelites could finally live in peace in their own homes again. But it was lowkey pointless: they didn't change their lives at all, didn't stop the whole Jeroboam-sin lifestyle that was basically Israel's brand at this point. Plus, those weird sex-and-religion Asherah shrines were still going strong in Samaria.
