It covers his entire rule, all his epic adventures, and everything that happened with him, Israel, and the kingdoms around them.

2 Chronicles.title: Solomon's GOATED Wish
paragraphs: So, Solomon, David's son, was now in charge, and he was killing it. God had his back and was helping him out big time. Solomon got on the mic and called a meeting with everyone in Israel - all the big shots, the military guys, the judges, and the leaders of the families. Then, he and the whole crew went to this place called Gibeon to worship. That's where the OG Tent of Meeting was, the one Moses built back in the day. The Ark of the Covenant, though, was in Jerusalem because David had moved it there and set up a special tent for it. But the Bronze Altar, made by this dude Bezalel, was still at Gibeon, right in front of the Tabernacle. So that's where Solomon and everyone went to pray. Solomon went all out and sacrificed a thousand burnt offerings on that altar. It was lit.
That night, God slid into Solomon's DMs. He was like, 'Yo, what do you want? Name it.'

Solomon was like, 'You were so good to my dad, David, and now you've made me king. So, God, please keep your promises to my dad. You've given me this crazy huge job of leading all these people. So, for real, I need wisdom and knowledge to lead them. Who can do this on their own? It's impossible without you.'

God replied, 'I see what's in your heart. You didn't ask for money, or to be famous, or for your enemies to be destroyed. You didn't even ask for a long life. You asked for wisdom and knowledge to rule my people. Because you asked for that, you'll get it. And I'm gonna throw in a bonus - more money, wealth, and fame than any king before or after you will ever have.'
Then Solomon bounced from Gibeon and the Tent of Meeting and went back to Jerusalem. He got to work as the king of Israel.

Solomon started collecting a ton of chariots and horses - like, 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses! He kept them in special cities and also in Jerusalem. The king made silver and gold as common as rocks, and cedar wood as common as fig trees. He imported his horses from Egypt and Cilicia, and his agents had a special hookup. Chariots from Egypt cost about 15 pounds of silver, and a horse was about 3.75 pounds of silver. Solomon was basically running a huge horse-trading business with the Hittite and Aramean kings.

2 Chronicles.title: Solomon's Temple Build: The Ultimate Collab
paragraphs: Solomon decided it was go-time for building a huge temple to honor God, and a sick palace for himself too.
He put together a massive crew: 70,000 guys for general labor, 80,000 to cut stone in the mountains, and 3,600 foremen to manage the whole operation.

Then Solomon slid into King Hiram of Tyre's DMs with a message: “Yo, could you send me some cedar logs, the same kind you sent my dad David for his palace? I'm about to build a temple for my God, a holy place for burning fragrant incense, setting out the holy bread, and making the big morning and evening sacrifices, plus all the services for the Sabbath, New Moon, and other holy days—all the stuff Israel is required to do.

“The temple I’m building has to be absolutely epic, because our God is the greatest, way better than any other gods. But for real, who could possibly build a house big enough for him? I mean, the entire universe can’t even contain him. And who am I to think I can build a house worthy of God? About all I'm good for is burning incense for him! So I need your help. Send me a master craftsman who's skilled in working with gold, silver, bronze, iron, and all kinds of colored fabrics, and who's also a master engraver. He'll oversee the skilled workers in Judah and Jerusalem that my father David already set up. Also, send me cedar, cypress, and algum logs from Lebanon; I know you have expert lumberjacks there. I'll send my own guys to help your crews cut a ton of timber—I'm going to need a crazy amount, because this temple I'm building is going to be absolutely stunning, a total showpiece! I'll supply all the food for your crew of lumberjacks: 130,000 bushels of wheat, 120,000 gallons of wine, and 120,000 gallons of olive oil.”
Hiram, the king of Tyre, wrote back to Solomon: “It’s obvious that God loves his people—that’s why he made you their king!”

He continued, “Shoutout to the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth! He gave King David a son who is super wise, knowledgeable, and sharp, to build a temple for God and a palace for himself. I’m sending you Huram-Abi—he's already on his way. The guy is a legend in the construction game. His mom is from Dan and his dad is from Tyre. He's a pro with gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood, and with all kinds of fabrics. He's also an expert engraver and can come up with amazing designs, working with your artists and the ones who worked for your dad, David.

“Go ahead and send the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine you promised for my work crews. We’ll cut all the trees you need from the Lebanon forests and float them down to Joppa as rafts. You’ll just have to handle getting the timber up to Jerusalem yourself.”

Solomon then counted all the foreigners living in Israel, just like his dad David had done. There were 153,600 of them. He made 70,000 of them do the heavy lifting, 80,000 work in the mountain quarries, and put 3,600 in charge as foremen to keep the work going.

2 Chronicles.title: Solomon's GOATED Temple Build!
paragraphs: Alright, so Solomon finally got started on building God's house in Jerusalem. He picked Mount Moriah, the exact spot where God had shown up for his dad, David. It was this place David had already picked out, where some guy named Araunah the Jebusite used to thresh his wheat. Solomon kicked things off on the second day of the second month, four years after he became king. The temple's blueprint was pretty legit: 90 feet long and 30 feet wide. The front porch was also 30 feet across and 30 feet high.

Inside, it was basically dripping in gold. The main room was lined with cypress wood, but then covered in a thin layer of pure gold that had these cool palm tree and chain patterns carved into it. He threw in some precious gems and more gold from a place called Parvaim to make it look extra fancy. Seriously, everything was covered in gold—the beams, the doorframes, the walls, the doors. And to top it off, they carved angels, or cherubim, all over the walls.

Then there was the Holy of Holies, which was a perfect cube—30 feet in every direction. And get this: it was covered in over 22 *tons* of gold. Even the nails were made of gold and weighed over a pound. The rooms upstairs were decked out in gold too. Wild.

He had these two huge, angel-like statues called cherubim made for the Holy of Holies, and of course, they were covered in gold too. Their wings were so big that when they stood side-by-side, their wings stretched all the way across the room, a full 30 feet. They were standing up straight, facing the main hall.
He also had this curtain made from super expensive purple and crimson fabric, and it had an angel design woven into it.

And for the front of the temple, he put up two massive pillars, each one 52 feet tall with a fancy top part that added another 7.5 feet. The tops had these crazy chain designs, like necklaces, with a hundred pomegranates hanging off them. He set them up in front of the Temple, one on the right and one on the left. He named the right one Jakin, which means 'Security,' and the left one Boaz, which means 'Stability.' Lowkey, that's a pretty cool move.

2 Chronicles.title: Solomon's Temple Bling: Gold Everything!
paragraphs: First, he built the Bronze Altar—a massive 30 feet long, 30 feet wide, and 10 feet high.

Then, he made a giant metal bowl called the Sea. It was 15 feet across, 7.5 feet high, and 45 feet around. Under the rim, it had two rows of bull decorations, ten for every 1.5 feet, all cast as one piece with the bowl. The whole thing was propped up on twelve bronze bulls, three facing each direction (north, west, south, east), holding the Sea on their backs. The bowl was three inches thick and the rim flared out like a lily flower. It could hold a whopping 18,000 gallons.
He also made ten washbasins, five for each side, to rinse the stuff for the burnt offerings. The priests washed themselves in the Sea.
He made ten gold lampstands, just like the design specified, and put five on the right and five on the left.
He made ten tables, five on each side, and a hundred gold bowls.
He built a special courtyard for the priests, and then the main courtyard with bronze-covered doors.
The Sea was placed on the right side of the Temple, at the southeast corner.
He also made all the tools: ash buckets, shovels, and bowls.

So yeah, a guy named Huram basically finished all the contract work for King Solomon's Temple. Here's the rundown of what he made: two pillars, two big bowl-shaped tops for the pillars, two fancy chain designs for the tops, four hundred pomegranates for the chains (two rows for each), ten washstands with their basins, the one Sea with the twelve bulls under it, and all the other buckets, forks, shovels, and bowls.
To be super clear, that's:
two pillars;
two bowl-shaped capitals for the tops of the pillars;
two decorative filigrees for the capitals;
four hundred pomegranates for the filigrees (a double row of pomegranates for each filigree);
ten washstands with their basins;
one Sea and the twelve bulls under it;
miscellaneous buckets, forks, shovels, and bowls.

All this stuff that Huram-Abi made for King Solomon for God's Temple was made of polished bronze. The king had it all cast in clay molds down in the Jordan Valley, between Succoth and Zarethan. There was so much stuff they didn't even bother to weigh it. Nobody knows how much bronze was actually used. It was a crazy amount.
Solomon also took care of all the furniture and accessories inside the Temple:

the gold altar, the tables for the special Bread of the Presence, the pure gold lampstands with their lamps that were lit in front of the Most Holy Place, the gold flowers, lamps, and tongs (all solid gold), the gold wick trimmers, bowls, ladles, and incense burners, and the gold doors for the Temple, both for the Most Holy Place and the main sanctuary.
Just to list it out again:
the gold Altar;
the tables that held the Bread of the Presence;
the Lampstands of pure gold with their lamps, to be lighted before the Inner Sanctuary, the Holy of Holies;
the gold flowers, lamps, and tongs (all solid gold);
the gold wick trimmers, bowls, ladles, and censers;
the gold doors of The Temple, doors to the Holy of Holies, and the doors to the main sanctuary.

2 Chronicles.title: God's Glory Cloud Fills the Temple!
paragraphs: So, King Solomon finally finished building God's Temple, which was a huge deal. Then he brought in all the special stuff his dad, King David, had set aside for God—tons of silver, gold, and other cool artifacts. He put everything safely in the Temple's treasury.

To top it all off, Solomon gathered all the important people in Jerusalem—the tribal chiefs and family leaders—to move the Ark of the Covenant from its old spot in Zion to its new home in the Temple. Every guy in Israel showed up for this big event, which happened during the Feast of Booths in the seventh month.

Once all the leaders were good to go, the Levites carefully picked up the Ark. They also carried the Tent of Meeting and all the holy items used for worship. The priests, who were also Levites, did the heavy lifting. King Solomon and basically everyone in Israel were there, right in front of the Ark, worshiping and sacrificing a crazy number of sheep and cattle—like, so many you couldn't even count them all.

The priests carried the Ark of the Covenant into its designated spot in the Inner Sanctuary, the most holy place, right under the wings of the cherubim statues. The cherubim's wings spread out over the Ark and its carrying poles, making a sort of canopy. The poles were so long that you could see their tips from just outside the Inner Sanctuary, but not from any farther away. Fun fact: they're still there. Inside the Ark, there was nothing but the two stone tablets that Moses put there back at Mount Horeb, where God made a promise with the Israelites after they escaped from Egypt.

The priests then left the Holy Place. All the priests who were there were officially ready for service, no matter their rank or job. And all the Levite musicians were there too—Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their families, all decked out in their worship clothes. The choir and orchestra got together on the east side of the altar, and 120 priests with trumpets joined them. The choir and trumpets all sounded like one voice, praising and thanking God. The orchestra and choir were in perfect sync, singing and playing praises to God:
'Yes! God is good! His loyal love goes on forever!'
Then, a massive cloud filled God's Temple. It was so thick that the priests couldn't even do their jobs because of it. It was the glory of God, for real, filling the entire Temple.

2 Chronicles.title: Solomon's Epic Temple Dedication Prayer
paragraphs: Then Solomon said,
“God, you said you’d hang out in a thick cloud, but check it out, I’ve built this incredible house for you, a place for you to live forever.”
The king then turned to the whole crowd of Israel that had gathered and gave them his blessing:

“Shoutout to God, the God of Israel! He personally told my dad David what he was going to do, and now he’s actually done it. He said, ‘Ever since I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I never picked one city from all the tribes of Israel to build a temple for my Name, and I never chose one guy to be the leader. But now, I’ve chosen both: Jerusalem to honor my Name, and David to lead my people Israel.’

“My dad, David, was super passionate about building a temple for the Name of God, the God of Israel. But God told him, ‘It’s awesome that you wanted to build a temple for me—major props for that! But you’re not the one who’s gonna build it. Your son, the one who comes after you, he’s the one who will build it for my Name.’

“And now, you can see the promise is a done deal. God did exactly what he said. I took over from my dad David and now I’m ruling Israel. I’ve built the temple for the Name of God, the God of Israel, and I’ve made a special place for the Chest that holds God’s Covenant, the deal he made with the people of Israel.”

Standing in front of the whole Israelite crowd, Solomon went up to God’s Altar and stretched out his hands. He had made this bronze platform that was about seven and a half feet square and four and a half feet high, and put it in the courtyard. That’s where he stood. Then he got on his knees where everyone could see him, stretched his hands up to the sky, and prayed:

“God, O God of Israel, there is literally no god like you in heaven or on earth. You’re the one who always keeps your promises and shows crazy love to your people when they’re trying to live right and follow you. You kept your promise to my dad David. You did exactly what you said you would—every single detail. And the proof is right here, right now!

“So please, God of Israel, keep it going! Keep the other promises you made to my dad David when you said, ‘You’ll always have someone from your family line to rule Israel, but only if your sons are careful to live my way, just like you did.’
“O God, God of Israel, please make it all happen—make it official!

“But for real, is God actually going to move into our neighborhood? I mean, the entire universe isn’t big enough for you, let alone this Temple I built. Still, I’m gonna be bold and ask: please pay attention to my prayers, the ones for everyone and the ones just from me, O God, my God. Listen to the passionate prayers I’m throwing up to you right now. Keep your eyes on this Temple 24/7, this place you promised to make special with your Name. And listen to the prayers I pray here. And listen to your people Israel when they pray here.
“Listen from your home in heaven, and when you hear us, please forgive us.
“If someone messes up and hurts their neighbor but then promises to fix it, and they come and say that same promise in front of your Altar in this Temple,
“Listen from heaven and do something. Judge your people. Make the person who did wrong pay for it, and let the person who was wronged go free, dropping all the charges.
“When your people Israel get defeated by an enemy because they sinned against you, but then they turn back to you, admit you’re in charge, and pray like crazy in this Temple,
“Listen from your home in heaven, forgive your people’s sin, and bring them back to the land you gave them and their ancestors.
“When it stops raining because your people have sinned against you, but then they pray here, acknowledge you’re the boss, and stop sinning because you disciplined them,
“Listen from your home in heaven, and forgive the sins of your people Israel. Then show them the right way to live, and send rain on the land you gave them.

“When disasters happen—like famine, disease, plagues of locusts, or when enemies attack our cities—whatever the problem is, if anyone from your people Israel prays, their heart totally broken, and they lift their hands to you in this Temple,

“Listen from your home in heaven, forgive them, and help them out. You know what’s really going on inside each person—you’re the only one who does! So treat them right, so they’ll respect you and live obediently on this land you gave our ancestors.

“And don’t forget about the foreigners who aren’t part of Israel but came from far away because they heard about you—because people are gonna hear about your great name and your awesome power—and they come and pray at this Temple.

“Listen from your home in heaven and answer that foreigner’s prayer. Do it so that everyone all over the world will know who you are, and respect you just like your own people Israel do. Then they’ll know that this Temple I built is truly connected to you.
“When your people go out to fight their enemies wherever you send them, and they pray to you facing this city you chose and this Temple I built for your Name,
“Listen from heaven to their prayer and what they’re asking for, and fight for them.

“When they sin against you—and let’s be real, they will, ’cause no one’s perfect—and you get angry and let their enemies capture them and take them to another country, far or near, but then they have a change of heart in that country and pray, saying, ‘We messed up, we did wrong, we’ve been so bad,’ and they turn back to you with their whole heart in the land of their enemies, and they pray facing their homeland that you gave their ancestors, toward the city you chose, and this Temple I built for your Name,
“Listen from your home in heaven to their desperate prayers. Do what’s best for them. Forgive your people who sinned against you.
“And now, dear God, please be alert and pay attention to every prayer offered in this place.

“Let’s go, God! Come to your new resting place, you and your powerful Covenant Chest. Let your priests be clothed in salvation, and let your faithful people celebrate all the good things. And God, please don’t turn your back on your chosen one. Remember the loyal love you promised to your servant David.”

2 Chronicles.title: God's GLORY Fills the Temple (ft. Lightning & a HUGE Party)
paragraphs: The second Solomon wrapped up his prayer, BAM! Lightning zapped down from the sky and torched the big offering. Then, God's glory, like this super thick, amazing presence, just flooded the entire Temple. It was so intense the priests couldn't even get inside. God's presence was so real, there was literally no room for them! When everyone in Israel saw the fire come down and God's glory fill the place, they all dropped to their knees, bowed down, and started worshiping, thanking God, like:
Yeah! God is so good! His love is, like, forever!

Then the king and everyone in Israel started worshiping by giving a ton of sacrifices to God. King Solomon went all out, sacrificing 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep for the Temple's opening party. The priests were all doing their thing, the choir and orchestra that David had set up were playing and singing praises to God, and across the courtyard, priests were blasting on their trumpets. Every single person was on their feet, totally into it.

Solomon made the middle of the courtyard in front of the Temple a holy space and used it to sacrifice even more offerings, because the bronze altar was way too small for everything. That's how Solomon celebrated the big fall festival. For a whole week, people came from all over the place, from the far northeast to the far southwest—it was a massive crowd. They partied for seven days straight, and then they did it for another seven days. A whole week for dedicating the altar and another week for the festival itself—two full weeks of celebrating! On the 23rd day of the seventh month, Solomon sent everyone home. They left super happy, just buzzing about all the awesome things God had done for David, Solomon, and his people, Israel.
So, Solomon finished building God's Temple and his own palace—the projects he was super passionate about. Everything was done, and it was a total success. So satisfying!

That very night, God showed up to Solomon and said, 'I heard your prayer, and for real, I've chosen this place as a temple for sacrifices, a house to be worshiped in. If I ever stop the rain, or tell locusts to destroy the crops, or send a plague on my people, and my people, who are called by my name, humble themselves, pray, look for me, and turn away from their messed-up lives, I'll be there for you. I'll listen from heaven, forgive their sins, and heal their land. From now on, I'm watching this place 24/7, listening to the prayers offered here. Trust me, I've chosen and made this Temple you built holy. My Name is on it forever; my eyes and my heart are always in it. As for you, if you live your life for me like your dad David did, with a pure heart and good actions, living the way I've told you to, and paying attention to my rules and commands, then I'll make sure your kingdom in Israel is solid. The same promise I gave your dad David, I'm giving to you: You'll always have a descendant on Israel's throne.'

'But if you or your sons ditch me, ignore my rules and commands, and start following other gods by serving and worshiping them, then the deal is off. I'll kick Israel right off the map and reject this Temple that I just made holy for my Name. And Israel will become a total joke to everyone. And this Temple, as amazing as it is now, will be looked at with disgust. Tourists will shake their heads and be like, 'What happened here? What's the story with these ruins?' Then they'll be told, 'The people who used to live here betrayed their God, the same God who saved their ancestors from Egypt. They started following other gods, worshiping and serving them. That's why God brought all this destruction on them.'

2 Chronicles.title: Solomon's Epic 20-Year Building Spree
paragraphs: So, after a solid 20 years, Solomon had a pretty wild list of accomplishments. He built God's Temple and his own palace, which is a major flex. He also rebuilt the cities King Hiram had given him and had Israelites move in to colonize them. He went and took over Hamath Zobah, fortified Tadmor out in the desert, and all the supply cities he'd started in Hamath. He built up Upper and Lower Beth Horon as fortress cities, decking them out with walls, gates, and bars. On top of that, he built Baalath and a bunch of other cities just for storage and for his chariot horses.
Solomon was lowkey an impulsive builder, just going all out whenever he got an idea. In Jerusalem, in Lebanon—basically anywhere he felt like it.

The people who were left from the original tribes in the land (the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—all non-Israelites) who had survived the big wars, Solomon rounded them up for his slave labor crews. And that's how it stayed. But he didn't do that to the actual Israelites. They were in his army and government, serving as leaders and commanders for his chariots and horsemen. They were also the project managers for all his building stuff—250 of them were in charge of all the workers.

Solomon also moved Pharaoh's daughter from the City of David to a house he built just for her. He was like, "My wife can't live in the house of King David of Israel, because any place the Ark of God has been is sacred ground."

Then Solomon started offering up burnt offerings to God on the altar he had built in front of the Temple's porch. He stuck to the regular worship schedule that Moses had laid out: Sabbaths, New Moons, and the three big annual festivals—the Feast of Unleavened Bread (Passover), the Feast of Weeks (Pentecost), and the Feast of Booths.

He copied what his dad David did and set up groups of priests to handle the worship services. The Levites were in charge of leading the music for praising God and helping the priests with the daily stuff. He also posted security guards at every gate—that's what David, the man of God, had ordered. The king's instructions for the priests, Levites, and the finance guys were followed down to the last detail, no cap. That included how the treasuries were managed.
Everything Solomon had planned, from the day they broke ground on God's Temple to the day it was finished, was now totally done.

Then Solomon went to Ezion Geber and Elath on the coast of Edom. King Hiram sent him ships and some veteran sailors. They teamed up with Solomon's guys and sailed to Ophir, loaded up fifteen tons of gold, and brought it all back to King Solomon. Wild.

2 Chronicles.title: Queen of Sheba Tests Solomon's Legendary Swag
paragraphs: So, the Queen of Sheba heard about Solomon's legendary reputation and decided to see for herself. She rolled up to Jerusalem to quiz him with all her toughest questions. She made a huge entrance with a massive crew and camels loaded with perfumes, a ton of gold, and precious gems. She basically poured out her heart to Solomon, talking about everything she was into. And Solomon? He aced every question she threw at him—nothing was too hard for him. When the Queen of Sheba saw Solomon's wisdom firsthand, checked out the palace he built, the fancy meals, his sharp-looking officials, the well-dressed waiters, the cupbearers, and the insane amount of offerings he gave at God's Temple, she was totally blown away.

She told the king, "Wow, the rumors are true! Everything I heard back home about your success and wisdom is legit. I wouldn't have believed it if I hadn't seen it with my own eyes. They didn't even tell me the half of it! Your wisdom and style are way beyond what I could've imagined. Your crew is so lucky—they get to be around you every day and soak up all your wisdom. And shoutout to your God who's so into you that He made you king. It's clear God loves Israel, putting you in charge to keep things fair and build a nation that honors Him."

Then she gave the king a wild gift: four and a half tons of gold, tons of spices, and precious stones. Seriously, there's never been a spice shipment like the one the Queen of Sheba brought to King Solomon. Hiram's ships also brought in gold from Ophir, plus fragrant sandalwood and expensive gems. The king used the sandalwood to make cool cabinets for the Temple and his palace, and even made harps and other instruments for the musicians. They'd never seen wood like that before.

King Solomon, in return, gave the Queen of Sheba everything she wanted—whatever she asked for. She ended up leaving with more stuff than she brought. Super happy, she headed back home with her whole squad.

Solomon was raking in about twenty-five tons of gold every year. And that wasn't even counting the money from taxes and trade with merchants. All the kings in Arabia and the local governors also brought him silver and gold.

King Solomon made 200 massive shields out of hammered gold—each one had like fifteen pounds of gold in it—and another 300 smaller shields that were about half that size. He kept them all in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.

The king also had this epic throne made of ivory and covered in gold. It had six steps leading up to it with a gold footstool attached. There were lions on both sides of the armrests. And get this: twelve more lions were placed on the ends of the six steps. No other kingdom had a throne that cool.
All of King Solomon's cups and dishes were made of pure gold. Even the stuff in the House of the Forest of Lebanon was all pure gold. Nobody used silver; it was considered basic and cheap back then.
The king's ships, sailed by Hiram's crew, went on a three-year trip to Tarshish and came back with gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks. Wild.

King Solomon was richer and wiser than any other king on the planet—he was just on another level. Kings from all over came to hang with Solomon and learn from the wisdom God gave him. And everyone who visited brought gifts: gold and silver things, cool clothes, the newest weapons, exotic spices, horses, and mules. It was a parade of visitors, year after year.

Solomon started collecting horses and chariots. He had 4,000 stalls for them and 12,000 horsemen stationed in special chariot cities and in Jerusalem. He ruled over all the kings from the Euphrates River all the way to the border of Egypt. The king made silver so common it was like finding rocks, and cedar wood was as common as fig trees. He also had a big horse-trading business going with Egypt and other places.

If you want to read the rest of Solomon's story, from beginning to end, you can check out the records of Nathan the prophet, the prophecy of Ahijah of Shiloh, and the visions of Iddo the seer about Jeroboam son of Nebat. Solomon ruled over all of Israel from Jerusalem for forty years. Then he died and was buried in the City of David, his father's town. His son Rehoboam took over as the next king.

2 Chronicles.title: How to Lose a Kingdom in 3 Days
paragraphs: Rehoboam bounced to Shechem where all of Israel was gathered to make him the new king. Meanwhile, Jeroboam, who had dipped to Egypt to get away from King Solomon, heard Solomon was dead and came back.
Israel sent for Jeroboam, and he and all of Israel went to Rehoboam and were like, “Yo, your dad worked us to the bone. Give us a break, lighten up the load, and we’ll totally serve you.”
Rehoboam said, “Give me three days to think it over, then come back.” So the people peaced out.
King Rehoboam hit up the elders who used to advise his dad, Solomon. “What’s your advice? How should I answer these people?”
They told him, “If you serve these people and are cool with them, responding with some compassion, they’ll be loyal to you forever. No cap.”

But he totally ghosted the elders' advice and asked the young guys he grew up with, who were now his yes-men. “What do you guys think? What should I tell these people who are saying, ‘Give us a break from your father’s harsh ways—lighten up’?”

The young crew he grew up with said, “These people complaining that your dad was too hard? Tell them this: ‘My pinky is thicker than my father’s waist. You think my dad was tough? You haven’t seen anything yet. My dad disciplined you with whips; I’ll beat you bloody with chains!’” It was pretty wild.

Three days later, Jeroboam and the people showed up, just like Rehoboam said. The king’s answer was super harsh. He dissed the elders' advice and went with what the young guns said: “You think my dad was tough? You’ve seen nothing. My dad whipped you; I’ll beat you bloody with chains!”
Rehoboam straight up ignored the people. But this was all lowkey God's plan, to make good on the message he gave to Jeroboam through Ahijah of Shiloh.
When all of Israel realized the king wasn’t listening to a word they said, they stood up to him and said,
“We’re out, David! We’ve had it with you, son of Jesse! Let’s dip, Israel! From now on, David, you do you.”
And with that, they left. Rehoboam was left ruling only the people who lived in the towns of Judah.

When King Rehoboam sent Adoniram, the head of the workforce, the Israelites ganged up on him, threw stones at him, and killed him. King Rehoboam had to jump in his chariot and escape to Jerusalem ASAP. Israel has been beefing with the house of David ever since.

2 Chronicles.title: Kingdom Divided & A King's Wild Family Life
paragraphs: So when King Rehoboam rolled back into Jerusalem, he immediately rounded up 180,000 of his best soldiers from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin. His plan? Go to war with Israel and take his kingdom back.

But right then, God sent a message to this holy guy named Shemaiah. He was told to tell Rehoboam and all the people in Judah and Benjamin, "This is God's word: Don't you dare go fight your own relatives, the Israelites. Every single one of you, go home. I'm the one calling the shots here." And you know what? They actually listened. They obeyed God and went home.

Rehoboam stayed in Jerusalem and started seriously beefing up Judah's defenses. He fortified a bunch of cities: Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa, Beth Zur, Soco, Adullam, Gath, Mareshah, Ziph, Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah, Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron. It was like a whole defensive line protecting Judah and Benjamin. He made the forts extra strong, put commanders in charge, and stocked them with food, olive oil, and wine. He also loaded them up with weapons—big shields and spears. He made those forts basically impenetrable. So, for a while, Judah and Benjamin were pretty secure.

Then, all the priests and Levites from all over Israel started showing up to support Rehoboam. The Levites literally abandoned their homes and property and moved to Judah and Jerusalem. Why? Because King Jeroboam and his sons had fired them from serving as God's priests. Jeroboam had even set up his own priests for his fake worship centers, complete with goat and calf idols—super sketchy. Everyone from all the tribes of Israel who was serious about following the real God of Israel packed up and moved to Jerusalem with the priests and Levites to worship properly, sacrificing to the God of their ancestors. This gave the kingdom of Judah a huge boost. They stuck with Rehoboam for three years, and for that time, they were loyal to the ways of David and Solomon.

On the personal side, Rehoboam married Mahalath, who was the daughter of David's son Jerimoth and Abihail, the daughter of Jesse's son Eliab. Mahalath had three sons for him: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham. Then he married Maacah, Absalom's daughter, and she had four kids: Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith. Lowkey, Maacah was his favorite wife. He loved her more than all his other wives and concubines combined—and dude had a lot: eighteen wives and sixty concubines, who produced twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters! It was wild.

Rehoboam was pretty smart, though. He made Abijah, Maacah's son, the head honcho among the brothers, basically making it clear he was next in line to be king. He strategically placed his other sons in charge of all the fortress cities throughout Judah and Benjamin, keeping them well-fed and with plenty of wives to keep them happy.

2 Chronicles.title: He Ditched God, Then Got Wrecked
paragraphs: Alright, so check it. By the time Rehoboam had his kingdom on lock and was feeling himself, he and pretty much all of Israel just dipped on God and his ways. Total ghosting.

So in Rehoboam’s fifth year as king, because he and the people were being unfaithful to God, this dude Shishak, the king of Egypt, rolls up and invades all the way to Jerusalem. He came through with 1,200 chariots and 60,000 cavalry, plus a massive army of Libyans, Sukkites, and Ethiopians. They started capping the fortress cities in Judah and pushed all the way to Jerusalem itself.

Then the prophet Shemaiah, along with the leaders of Judah who had bailed and retreated to Jerusalem because of Shishak, came to Rehoboam and dropped this message: “God’s word is this: You abandoned me, so now I’m abandoning you to Shishak.”
The leaders of Israel and the king actually felt that. They were like, “You know what, God is right. Our bad.”

When God saw that they were genuinely sorry and humbled themselves, He sent another message to Shemaiah: “Because they’re being humble, I’m not gonna completely destroy them. I’ll give them a break. I won’t use Shishak to pour out my anger on Jerusalem. But, here’s the catch: I’m gonna make them Shishak’s subjects. That way, they’ll learn the real difference between serving me and serving some human king.”

So Shishak, king of Egypt, attacked Jerusalem. He plundered the treasury of God's Temple and the royal palace—like, he took everything he could get his hands on. He even snagged the gold shields that Solomon had made.

King Rehoboam had to replace those gold shields with bronze ones and gave them to the guards posted at the palace entrance. Whenever the king went to God’s Temple, the guards would roll with him carrying the shields, but they always had to return them to the guardroom right after.
Because Rehoboam repented, God’s anger cooled off, so he wasn’t totally destroyed. The situation wasn't a complete disaster—there were still some good things happening in Judah.

King Rehoboam managed to regroup and get his rule in Jerusalem back on solid ground. He was 41 when he became king and reigned for 17 years in Jerusalem, the city God chose out of all the tribes of Israel for His name to be present. His mom was Naamah from Ammon. But the final verdict on Rehoboam? He was a bad king. God just wasn't important to him; his heart wasn't in it to seek or care for God.

The whole story of Rehoboam, from start to finish, is written down in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and Iddo the seer, which also include the family trees. Also, there was constant beef between Rehoboam and Jeroboam. Eventually, Rehoboam died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Abijah took over as king after him.

2 Chronicles.title: God's King vs. a Rebel with Golden Calves
paragraphs: So, in the 18th year that King Jeroboam was in charge, Abijah became the new king of Judah. He ruled from Jerusalem for three years. His mom was Maacah, who was Uriel of Gibeah's daughter.
A war totally broke out between Abijah and Jeroboam. Abijah rolled up with 400,000 of his best soldiers, but Jeroboam came back with a massive 800,000 of his own top guys.

Abijah found a high spot on Mount Zemaraim in the Ephraim hills and just started shouting, 'Yo, Jeroboam and all of Israel, listen up! Don't you get it? God, the one and only God of Israel, made a promise—a super serious, unbreakable promise—that David and his family would rule Israel forever. It's God's kingdom, led by God's chosen king! But what happened? Jeroboam, whose dad was just a servant to Solomon, decided to rebel against his boss. Then all the troublemakers and losers joined him, and they were too much for Rehoboam, Solomon's actual son and heir. Rehoboam was young and kinda clueless, a total wimp, really. He couldn't handle them.'

'And now, you're using that past weakness to go against God's chosen rulers, the descendants of David. You think you're so tough with your giant army and those golden calves Jeroboam made for you to worship. But look at what you've actually done—you kicked out God's real priests, the sons of Aaron and the Levites, and just made up your own. It's like those pagan nations do! Now, anyone with enough cash can just buy their way into being a priest. A priest for a god that isn't even real!'

'But us? The people of Judah? We're sticking with God. We haven't ditched him for some new, flashy thing. We've kept the real-deal priests of Aaron to guide us and the Levites to lead our worship. They offer up sacrifices and burn incense to God every single morning and evening. They put out the holy bread on a clean table and light the lamps on the golden lampstand every night. We're still doing what God told us to do, the way he said to do it. You guys are the ones who got rid of him.'

'Isn't it obvious? God is on our side; he's our leader. And his priests are right here with trumpets, ready to sound the call for battle. So, people of Israel, don't fight against God, the God of your ancestors. You are not going to win this.'

While Abijah was giving this big speech, Jeroboam was sneakily sending troops around to ambush them from behind. So Judah had Jeroboam's main army in front and the ambush squad behind them. When they realized they were trapped, they freaked out and prayed to God like crazy. The priests blew the trumpets, and the soldiers of Judah let out a massive battle cry. The second they shouted, God totally wrecked Jeroboam and his whole army. The Israelite army just scattered, and God gave Judah the victory. Abijah and his soldiers went on a rampage and took down 500,000 of Israel's best fighters that day. It was a humiliating defeat for Israel. Judah won, big time, because they trusted in God, the God of their ancestors.

Abijah kept the pressure on, chasing after Jeroboam and capturing the towns of Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, plus all the villages around them. Jeroboam never really got back on his feet as long as Abijah was alive. Eventually, God struck him down, and he died. Meanwhile, Abijah was thriving. He married fourteen wives and had a huge family with twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
The rest of Abijah's story, everything he did and said, is all written down in the records of the prophet Iddo.

2 Chronicles.title: King Asa's GOD TIER Battle Royale
paragraphs: So, King Abijah passed away and was buried in the family plot in David's City. His son, Asa, took over the throne. And for the first ten years he was king, things were super chill—no drama.

Asa was actually a solid king. He was all about doing what God wanted. He basically did a total spiritual cleanup—tore down all the fake god altars and shrines, smashed the weird stone pillars, and got rid of those creepy sex-and-religion groves. He told everyone in Judah to get their priorities straight and focus on the real God, the one their ancestors followed. He was like, 'Yo, let's actually follow the rules and commandments.' And because he got rid of all that pagan junk from the cities, the whole kingdom was at peace. Since everything was quiet and there were no wars, he beefed up their defenses. God was basically holding it down for them, keeping everything peaceful.

Asa told his people, 'Look, while things are calm and we have this quiet, let's build up some serious defenses. Let's fortify our cities with walls, towers, gates, and bars. We've got this peace because we actually tried to follow God, and he's given us a break from all our problems.' So they got to building and were living the good life.
Asa had a pretty stacked army: 300,000 guys from Judah with shields and spears, plus another 280,000 from Benjamin who were shield-bearers and archers. They were all legit warriors.

Then this guy, Zerah the Ethiopian, rolled up on Asa with a wild army of a million soldiers and 300 chariots, making it all the way to Mareshah. Asa met him there and got ready to throw down in the Valley of Zephathah. Then Asa prayed to God, saying, 'Yo God, you're not scared of big numbers or a show of force when you decide to help. So, help us, God! We're facing this massive army because we trust you and what you're about. Don't let these mere humans win against you!'

And boom, God wrecked the Ethiopians right in front of Asa and the army of Judah. The Ethiopians dipped and ran for their lives. Asa and his crew chased them all the way to Gerar. So many Ethiopians got taken out that they had zero fight left in them—it was a total massacre, courtesy of God and his squad. The soldiers from Judah walked away with tons of loot. They wrecked all the towns around Gerar, where the people were basically paralyzed with fear because of God, and they just plundered the whole area. They also jacked the herdsmen's animals and brought back a crazy amount of sheep and camels to Jerusalem.

2 Chronicles.title: King Asa's Kingdom Cleanup Was WILD
paragraphs: So, this prophet Azariah, son of Oded, gets this major download from God's Spirit and goes to meet King Asa. He's like, 'Yo, Asa, and everyone in Judah and Benjamin, listen up! God's got your back as long as you have His. If you're actually looking for Him, you'll find Him. But if you ghost Him, He'll ghost you. For ages, Israel was basically running on empty, without the real God, no spiritual leaders, no instruction manual. But when things got rough and they finally got real about finding God, He was right there. Back then, it was total chaos, a real dog-eat-dog situation. Life was a mess, nobody knew what was coming next. Countries were fighting countries, cities were at war with each other. God basically let all kinds of trouble loose on them.'
'But for you guys, it's a different story. So, be strong, don't lose hope. Your hard work is about to pay off, big time!'

When Asa heard what Azariah the prophet said, he took a deep breath, rolled up his sleeves, and got down to business. He went on a massive cleanup mission, getting rid of all the gross, fake shrines all over Judah, Benjamin, and the towns he'd captured in the Ephraim hills. He even gave the Altar of God outside the Temple a serious makeover. Then he got everyone from Judah and Benjamin together, plus all the people from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who had moved over because they saw God was team Asa.

They all showed up in Jerusalem in the third month of Asa's fifteenth year as king for this huge worship festival. They sacrificed 700 oxen and 7,000 sheep from the stuff they'd captured. Then they all made a super serious promise to go all-in for God, the God of their ancestors, holding nothing back. They even agreed that anyone who bailed on seeking God should be executed, no matter who they were—young, old, guy, or girl. They shouted out their promise to God, making a ton of noise with trumpets and horns. The whole country was stoked about this promise because they meant it, for real. They were hyped to find God, and He showed up for them. God gave them peace on all fronts—it was a super chill kingdom.

Asa's cleanup was so intense, he even kicked his own mom, Queen Maacah, off the throne because she'd made this super inappropriate statue of the goddess Asherah. Asa tore it down, smashed it to pieces, and burned it in the Kidron Valley. He didn't manage to get rid of all the local hookup spots that were mixed with religion, which was a bummer. But his heart was in the right place; he was loyal to God, no cap. He took all the gold and silver stuff that he and his dad had dedicated to God and put it back in the Temple. And get this—there was zero war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.

2 Chronicles.title: King Asa's Epic Fail: Trusts Humans, Gets Burned
paragraphs: So, in the 36th year of King Asa's reign, things got real. Baasha, the king of Israel, decided to throw down and started by building a fort at Ramah. He basically put up a blockade, trapping King Asa and his people in Judah.

Asa's move? He took a bunch of silver and gold from God's Temple and his own palace and sent it to Ben-Hadad, the king of Aram, with a message: 'Yo, let's make a deal like our dads did. Here's a gift to prove I'm serious. Break your treaty with Baasha, and get him off my back.'

And what do you know, Ben-Hadad was all for it. He sent his army to attack Israel's towns, and they wrecked Ijon, Dan, Abel Maim, and all of Naphtali's supply cities. When Baasha heard about it, he bailed on building his fort at Ramah.
Then King Asa had all the people of Judah haul away the stones and timber Baasha had been using for his fort, and used them to build up his own cities, Geba and Mizpah. Total power move.

But right after that, Hanani the prophet came to Asa and was like, 'Bro, you messed up. You relied on the king of Aram instead of asking God for help, so now you've missed the chance to defeat Aram's army. Don't you remember when the Ethiopians and Libyans came at you with a huge army, way more chariots and horsemen? You cried out to God, and He saved you. God is always looking for people who are 100% committed to Him. You were foolish to trust a human for help when you could've had God on your side. Now you're in for a whole lot of trouble and non-stop wars.'
Asa totally lost it. He got so mad that he threw Hanani in jail. And at the same time, he started being a real jerk to some of his own people.

The rest of Asa's story is all written down in the official records of Judah's kings. In the 39th year of his rule, he got a nasty foot disease. But even then, he didn't ask God for help; he went to the doctors instead. Asa died in the 41st year of his reign. They buried him in a fancy tomb he had built for himself in the City of David, laid him in a crypt filled with perfumes and spices, and had a massive bonfire in his honor.

2 Chronicles.title: Jehoshaphat's GOATED Reign Begins!
paragraphs: Alright, so after King Asa, his son Jehoshaphat took the throne. First thing he did? Beef up the security against Israel. He put soldiers in all the major fortified cities in Judah and set up garrisons all over, including the towns his dad Asa had taken back from Ephraim. God was totally on Jehoshaphat's team because he followed the good example his dad set in his early days. He didn't get sidetracked by the trendy Baal worship stuff everyone else was into. Nah, he was all in for the God of his ancestors and actually obeyed His commands, not like the mess Israel was in. Because of this, God made his kingdom super stable and gave him solid control. The people of Judah were so stoked about it, they brought him a bunch of presents. Jehoshaphat got seriously rich and respected. He was laser-focused on following God and even tore down all those sketchy local shrines where people were mixing worship with wild stuff.

In his third year as king, he sent out his top officials—Ben-Hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah, all total stand-up guys—on a teaching tour through the cities of Judah. A bunch of Levites went with them—Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah—plus the priests Elishama and Jehoram. They went all around Judah, teaching the people directly from the Book of God's Law.

God's presence was felt so strongly that all the kingdoms around Judah were lowkey terrified—they didn't even think about starting a war with Jehoshaphat. Some Philistines even brought him gifts and a ton of silver, and the nomads from the desert brought him flocks of 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats. So yeah, Jehoshaphat just kept getting more and more powerful, building more forts and supply cities. It was a golden age for Judah!

He also had a seriously goated army stationed in Jerusalem. The commanders of the Judah military units, organized by family, were: Captain Adnah with 300,000 soldiers; his second-in-command Captain Jehohanan with 280,000; and his other associate Amasiah son of Zicri, who was a full-on volunteer for God, with 200,000. From the tribe of Benjamin, there was Officer Eliada with 200,000 soldiers armed with bows and shields; and his second was Jehozabad with 180,000 troops ready to fight. These guys were all under the king's direct command, and on top of that, there were all the troops stationed in the fortress cities all over Judah.

2 Chronicles.title: Prophet Spits Facts, Gets Slapped, King Dies Anyway
paragraphs: So, King Jehoshaphat was crazy rich and super respected, but he made a deal to have his family marry into King Ahab of Israel's family. A while later, he dropped by to visit Ahab in Samaria. Ahab went all out for his visit with a huge feast—we're talking a massive barbecue with all the lamb and beef you could imagine. But Ahab was being kinda shady; he really wanted Jehoshaphat to help him attack Ramoth Gilead. Then Ahab just put it all out there: “So, you gonna join me in attacking Ramoth Gilead?” Jehoshaphat was like, “You know it. I’m with you all the way; you can count on me and my squad.”
Then Jehoshaphat was like, “But wait, before we do anything, we should probably ask God for his opinion.”
The king of Israel gathered all his prophets—like, all 400 of them—and asked, “Should I go attack Ramoth Gilead or just chill?”
They all chanted, “Go for it! God will totally give it to you, king.”
But Jehoshaphat was hesitant. “Isn't there, like, another prophet of God we can ask? Let's get a second opinion.”
The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, “Well, there is one other guy. But I can't stand him. He never says anything good about me, it's always doom and gloom. His name is Micaiah, son of Imlah.”
“Whoa, a king shouldn't talk about a prophet like that!” said Jehoshaphat.
So the king of Israel told one of his guys, “Go get Micaiah, son of Imlah. And hurry.”

Meanwhile, the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat were sitting on their thrones, decked out in their royal robes, looking all majestic in front of the Samaria city gates. All the prophets were putting on a big show for them. One of them, Zedekiah son of Kenaanah, even made some iron horns and was waving them around, yelling, “This is what God says! With these horns, you’ll totally destroy Aram until they're all gone!” All the other prophets chimed in, “Yeah! Go attack Ramoth Gilead! It'll be an easy win! God's giving you this victory!”
The messenger who went to get Micaiah told him, “Look, all the other prophets are telling the king he's going to win. You should just agree with them and say yes too.”
But Micaiah said, “As God is my witness, I'm only going to say what God tells me to say.”
When Micaiah stood before him, the king asked, “So, Micaiah—should we attack Ramoth Gilead or not?”
He replied, “Go for it. It'll be an easy win. God's gift to the king.”
“Not so fast,” the king shot back. “How many times do I have to make you swear you'll tell me the truth and nothing but the truth from God?”
“Alright, fine,” said Micaiah, “since you're pushing it...
I saw a vision of all of Israel scattered across the hills, like sheep without a shepherd. Then God said, ‘These poor people have no leader. Let them just go home and try to survive.’”
The king of Israel turned to Jehoshaphat and said, “See! What did I tell you? He never has anything good to say about me from God, only bad news.”
Micaiah wasn't finished. “Hold on, I have more to say. Listen to God's word:

I saw God sitting on his throne, with all the angels of heaven lined up on his right and his left. And God asked, ‘How can we trick Ahab into attacking Ramoth Gilead so he'll be defeated?’ Some angels said one thing, and some said another. Then one bold angel stepped up to God and said, ‘I’ll trick him.’ ‘How are you going to do that?’ God asked. ‘Easy,’ the angel said, ‘I’ll make all his prophets lie.’ God said, ‘That'll work. Go on, trick him!’
“And that's what's happening right now. God has made your puppet prophets tell you a bunch of convincing lies. God has already decided you're doomed.”
Just then, Zedekiah son of Kenaanah walked up and slapped Micaiah across the face. “Since when did the Spirit of God leave me to go talk to you?” he sneered.
Micaiah shot back, “You'll find out soon enough, when you're desperately trying to find a place to hide and can't.”

The king of Israel had heard enough. “Get Micaiah out of here! Take him to Amon, the city governor, and to Joash, the king's son, with this message: ‘The king orders you to throw this man in jail! Give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.’”
Micaiah said,
“If you actually come back safely, then I'm not a real prophet of God.”
He then added,
“And when it happens, everyone, remember who told you first!”

So, the king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah went ahead and attacked Ramoth Gilead. The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, “You wear my royal robes; I’m going into battle disguised.” So the king of Israel went into the fight in a disguise.
Meanwhile, the king of Aram had given his 32 chariot commanders one order: “Don’t waste your time with anyone else, big or small; go after the king of Israel and only him.”

When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they thought, “There he is! The king of Israel!” and they went straight for him. Jehoshaphat screamed, and the commanders realized they had the wrong guy—it wasn't the king of Israel after all. God stepped in, and they backed off.

Just then, some guy randomly shot an arrow into the air, not even aiming, and it hit the king of Israel right in a gap in his armor. The king yelled to his chariot driver, “Turn around! Get me out of here—I’m hit!”
The battle raged on all day, super intense. The king, propped up in his chariot, had to watch from the sidelines. He died that evening.

2 Chronicles.title: Level Up Your Leadership: The No-Bribe Zone
paragraphs: But King Jehoshaphat of Judah made it back home, safe and sound. Then Jehu, the son of Hanani the seer, went to confront him, saying, "Seriously? You're going to help out evil people and get cozy with those who hate God? Because of that, God is lowkey really mad at you. But you're not a total lost cause—you did get rid of all those gross sex-and-religion shrines, and you were all-in on seeking God."
Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem but he'd go on these tours to visit his people, from Beersheba all the way up to Mount Ephraim, trying to get them to come back to God, the God of their ancestors.

And he was super serious about setting up judges all over the land—every single fortress city got one. He told the judges, "Listen up, this is a huge deal, so take it seriously. You're not just settling fights between people; you're delivering God's judgments. You need to live in awe of God and be super careful, because God is not about dishonesty, playing favorites, or taking bribes."

In Jerusalem, Jehoshaphat also appointed some Levites, priests, and family heads to handle all the stuff related to worship and to settle local arguments. He charged them, saying, "Do your job with a healthy fear of God; be reliable and totally honest. Whenever a case comes to you from your fellow citizens, whether it's something huge like a murder or something smaller like figuring out what a law means, you have to warn them that they're dealing with God. Make it crystal clear. Otherwise, both you and them will have to face God's anger. Do your job right, or you'll end up just as guilty as they are.

"Amariah, the head priest, is in charge of all the cases about worshipping God. Zebadiah, son of Ishmael, who's the leader of the Judah tribe, is in charge of all the regular legal cases. And the Levites will be like the bailiffs, keeping order. So be bold and get it done. And may God be with you as you do your best."

2 Chronicles.title: God's Ultimate Battle Plan: No Cap
paragraphs: So, a little while later, the Moabites, Ammonites, and some Meunites teamed up to start a war with Jehoshaphat. He got a message saying, "Yo, a massive army is coming at you from across the Dead Sea. They're already at Hazazon Tamar, which is En Gedi. No time to waste."

Jehoshaphat was shook, so he started praying hard. He hit up God for help and told the whole country to fast. All of Judah came together to ask God for guidance, with people showing up from every city.

Then Jehoshaphat stood up in front of everyone from Judah and Jerusalem at God's Temple, right by the new courtyard. He said, "O God, the God of our ancestors, aren't you the God in heaven who rules over all the kingdoms down here? You've got all the power and might—no one can even touch you! And didn't you kick out the people who used to live here when you brought Israel in, giving this land to them forever, to the descendants of your boy Abraham? They've lived here and built this holy Temple to honor you, saying, 'When things get bad—like war, floods, sickness, or famine—and we stand in front of this Temple (because we know you're here) and cry out about our problems, we know you'll hear us and give us the W.'

"And now, for real, guys from Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir are here. You told Israel not to mess with them when we first got here, so we went around them and didn't touch them. And now they're trying to kick us out of the land you gave us. O dear God, can you please handle them? We're totally helpless against this huge crew about to attack us. We have no idea what to do; we're just looking at you."
Everyone in Judah was there—even the little kids, wives, and sons—all paying attention to God.

Then the Spirit of God came over Jahaziel, and he spoke up from the middle of the crowd. (Jahaziel was from the Asaph clan, a Levite). He said, "Listen up, everyone—all you from out of town, all you from Jerusalem, and you, King Jehoshaphat! God's word is this: Don't be scared; don't even worry about this huge army. This is God's fight, not yours. Tomorrow, you'll go after them. Look, they're already coming up the slopes of Ziz, and you'll find them at the end of the ravine near the Jeruel wilderness. You won't even have to do anything in this battle; just stand strong, Judah and Jerusalem, and watch God save you. Don't be afraid, don't hesitate. Go out there boldly tomorrow—God's got your back."

Then Jehoshaphat bowed down with his face to the ground, and everyone from Judah and Jerusalem did the same, worshiping God. The Levites (both Kohathites and Korahites) got up to praise God, the God of Israel, and they were shouting their praises at the top of their lungs!

They got up super early the next morning, ready to head into the Tekoa wilderness. As they were leaving, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, "Listen up, Judah and Jerusalem! Hear me out! Trust in God, your God, and you'll be solid! Believe in his prophets, and you'll win!"

After chatting with the people, Jehoshaphat picked out a choir for God. They were dressed in holy robes and were supposed to march in front of the army, singing, "Give thanks to God, His love is forever."

As soon as they started singing and praising, God set up ambushes for the guys from Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir who were attacking Judah, and they all got wrecked. The Ammonites and Moabites accidentally attacked the guys from Mount Seir and wiped them out. Then, they got even more confused and started fighting each other until everyone was dead.
When Judah got to the top of the hill and looked out into the wilderness for the army, all they saw was a field of dead bodies—not a single person was left alive.

When Jehoshaphat and his people came to take the loot, they found more stuff than they could even carry—equipment, clothes, and other valuables. It took them three whole days to haul it all away! On the fourth day, they all met up at the Valley of Beracah (which means 'Blessing') and blessed God. That's how the valley got its name.

Jehoshaphat then led all the men of Judah and Jerusalem back to Jerusalem in a massive, hype parade. God had given them a huge win over their enemies! They went into Jerusalem and to God's Temple with the whole band playing.

When the kingdoms nearby heard that God had fought Israel's enemies for them, they were all terrified of God. Jehoshaphat didn't have any more trouble from them; as long as he was king, there was peace.

So, that's basically the story of Jehoshaphat's rule over Judah. He was 35 when he became king and ruled in Jerusalem for 25 years. His mom was Azubah. He lived a life like his dad Asa—no messing around, just trying to please God. But he didn't get rid of the local shrines where people worshiped other gods, so people kept going to those places.
The rest of Jehoshaphat's life, from beginning to end, is written down in the records of Jehu son of Hanani, which are in the official history of Israel's kings.

Late in his life, Jehoshaphat made a business deal with King Ahaziah of Israel, which was a big mistake. He partnered with him to build ships at Ezion Geber to trade with Tarshish. But Eliezer son of Dodavahu preached against it, saying, "Because you teamed up with Ahaziah, God has wrecked your plans." The ships were destroyed, and the business deal totally failed.

2 Chronicles.title: The King Who Killed His Bros & Got Wrecked
paragraphs: So, King Jehoshaphat died and was buried with his family in the City of David. His son Jehoram took over as the new king.

Jehoram had a bunch of brothers: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael, and Shephatiah. Their dad, King Jehoshaphat of Judah, had hooked them up with tons of gifts—silver, gold, and other expensive stuff, plus their own fortified cities. But since Jehoram was the oldest, he got the kingdom. And as soon as he felt secure on the throne, he went and killed all his brothers. Lowkey savage. He also took out some of the government officials.

Jehoram was 32 when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eight years. He started acting just like the kings of Israel and even married into Ahab's messed-up family. God saw him as a seriously bad dude. But even so, because of the promise He made to David, God wasn't ready to completely cancel David's family line. He had promised to always keep a light shining for David and his kids, after all.

During Jehoram's rule, the country of Edom rebelled against Judah and set up their own king. Jehoram rolled out with his officers and chariots to deal with it. The Edomites surrounded him, but in the middle of the night, he and his chariot squad broke through their lines and hit them hard.

But Edom is still in rebellion against Judah to this day. Even the small town of Libnah revolted back then. The evidence was piling up: Jehoram had ditched the God of his ancestors, so God was starting to ditch him. He even built pagan shrines up in the mountains of Judah and straight-up led Jerusalem and the whole country away from God.

Then one day, he gets a letter from the prophet Elijah. It was basically a message from God, the God of his ancestor David, saying: 'Yo, you haven't followed the good examples of your dad Jehoshaphat or your grandpa Asa. Instead, you're acting like the kings of Israel, leading Judah and Jerusalem down the same bad path as Ahab and his crew. You even murdered your own brothers, who were way better men than you! Because of all this, God's about to hit your people, your wives, your sons, and everything you own with a massive plague. And you? You're going to get a nasty, painful, and super embarrassing intestinal disease.'

The trouble kicked off with an invasion. God stirred up the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Ethiopians to attack Jehoram. They broke into Judah, plundered the place, and looted the royal palace, taking everything, including his wives and sons. The only son left was Ahaziah, the youngest. After that, the horrible and deadly disease in his gut started. After about two years, he lost all control of his bowels and died in agonizing pain. His people didn't even give him a big funeral bonfire like they did for his ancestors. He was 32 when he became king and ruled for eight years in Jerusalem. No one cried when he died—it was good riddance. They buried him in the City of David, but not in the royal tombs.

2 Chronicles.title: The Queen Who Killed Her Own Grandkids?!
paragraphs: So, the people in Jerusalem picked Ahaziah, Jehoram's youngest son, to be their new king. Why the youngest? Because some desert raiders, teamed up with the Arabs, had already taken out all his older brothers. So, boom, Ahaziah, son of Jehoram, is now king of Judah. He was 22 when he started, but his reign in Jerusalem only lasted a year. His mom was Athaliah, who was Omri's granddaughter, and let's just say she was a bad influence. He basically copied the playbook of the evil Ahab family, with his mom coaching him on how to be shady. God was not a fan, seeing him as part of the corrupt Ahab crew through both family ties and his own bad choices. After his dad died, he basically enrolled in 'Ahab's School for Sinners' and, no surprise, it led to his downfall. He did everything they taught him, even rolling with King Joram of Israel to fight against King Hazael of Aram. Joram got injured and had to fall back to Jezreel to heal up. So Ahaziah went to visit him while he was recovering.

But this little road trip to visit Joram? It was a setup by God, and not in a good way for Ahaziah. When he got to Jezreel, he and Joram ran into this guy Jehu. God had already given Jehu the green light to wipe out Ahab's entire family line. Jehu was already on a rampage, taking down Ahab's house, when he stumbled upon Ahaziah's crew—his officials and even his nephews. He killed them all on the spot. Then he was like, 'Where's Ahaziah?' and sent people to find him. They found him trying to lay low in Samaria, dragged him back to Jehu, and Jehu finished the job.

They didn't just leave his body, though. They actually gave him a proper burial, but only because his grandpa, Jehoshaphat, was known for being a real one who genuinely sought God. Still, with him gone, there was literally no one left in Ahaziah's family who could take over and run the kingdom.

When Ahaziah's mom, Athaliah, found out her son was dead, she went full-on villain mode. She decided to take power for herself and started by trying to kill off the entire royal family. But Jehosheba, who was King Jehoram's daughter, snatched Ahaziah's baby son, Joash, from the group of princes about to be executed. She hid him and his nanny in a secret room, safe from Athaliah. So Jehosheba, who was not only King Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's sister but also married to the priest Jehoiada, saved little Joash from his psycho grandma Athaliah. He stayed hidden with her in the Temple of God for six years, while Athaliah ruled the country, totally clueless that he even existed.

2 Chronicles.title: The Secret Coup to Dethrone the Evil Queen
paragraphs: Okay, so in the seventh year, the priest Jehoiada decided it was go-time. He got a bunch of important army officers on his side, guys like Azariah, Ishmael, and a few other dudes with hard-to-pronounce names. They went all over Judah and gathered up the Levites and the heads of the families for a big meeting in Jerusalem. They all met up at God's Temple and made a secret pact.

Jehoiada then showed them the young prince and said, "Here he is—the king's son! He's going to rule, just like God promised for David's family. Now, here's the plan: one-third of you priests and Levites who are on duty this Saturday will guard the gates. Another third will guard the palace, and the last third will guard the foundation gate. All the people will just chill in the Temple courtyards. Nobody is allowed to go into the actual Temple except for the priests and the special Levites—they can go in because they're consecrated. Everyone else, just stick to your posts. The Levites need to form a human shield around the young king, and be ready to take down anyone who tries to break through. Your whole job is to stick with the king 24/7, wherever he goes."

So, the Levites and officers did exactly what Jehoiada told them. Every single one of them, whether they were starting their shift or ending it, took their positions because Jehoiada made it clear nobody was excused. Then the priest handed out the spears and shields that used to belong to King David, which were stored in the Temple. Fully armed, the guards got into formation to protect the king, making a perimeter from one side of the Temple to the other, surrounding the Altar and the main building.

Then they brought the prince out, put the crown on his head, handed him the official scroll of God's covenant, and officially made him king. As Jehoiada and his sons anointed him with oil, everyone started shouting, "Long live the king!"

When the evil queen Athaliah heard all the noise, with people running around and cheering for the new king, she rushed over to the Temple to see what was up. She was totally shocked to see the young king standing by the entrance, surrounded by captains and trumpeters, with everyone going absolutely wild with joy, trumpets blasting, and the choir and orchestra leading the celebration. Athaliah freaked out, ripped her clothes, and screamed, "This is a setup! A mutiny!"

Jehoiada the priest ordered the army officers, "Get her out of here! And if anyone tries to help her, take them out." He had already told them, "Don't kill her inside God's Temple." So they grabbed her, dragged her out to the palace's horse stables, and killed her there.
Jehoiada then made a new covenant between himself, the king, and the people, declaring that they would all be God's special people from now on.

The people then stormed the temple of the false god Baal and completely wrecked it. They smashed the altar and all the idols into a million pieces. They also killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, right in front of his own busted altar.

Jehoiada put the priests and Levites back in charge of God's Temple, just like David had originally set it up. Their job was to offer the proper sacrifices to God as laid out in the laws of Moses, and to lead worship with singing and praise as David had instructed. He also posted guards at the Temple gates so no one who wasn't supposed to be there could just wander in. Then he gathered all the officials and the people and personally escorted the new king down from the Temple, through the main gate, and sat him on the royal throne. The whole city celebrated. And for the first time in a long time, the city was peaceful and quiet—because the tyrant Athaliah was finally gone.

2 Chronicles.title: Good King Gone Bad: The Joash Story
paragraphs: So, this kid Joash was only seven when he became king, and he reigned for a solid 40 years in Jerusalem. His mom's name was Zibiah, and she was from Beersheba.
As long as the priest Jehoiada was alive to guide him, Joash actually did what was right in God's eyes. Jehoiada even hooked him up with two wives, and he started a family with sons and daughters.

After a while, Joash got this big idea to renovate God's Temple. He gathered the priests and Levites and was like, 'Alright team, fan out across Judah and collect money from everyone every year to fix up your God's Temple. Get on it.' But honestly, the Levites were dragging their feet and didn't do much.

This got the king heated, so he called in Jehoiada, the head priest, and said, 'Yo, why haven't you made the Levites collect the tax that Moses and the people decided on for the holy place? Can't you see how bad it is? That evil Queen Athaliah and her sons totally trashed God's Temple and used all the sacred items to worship their fake god, Baal.'

So, on the king's orders, they made a big chest and stuck it at the entrance of the Temple. Then they sent out a notice all over Judah and Jerusalem saying, 'Time to pay up the tax that Moses, God's servant, commanded back in the wilderness.'
And you know what? The leaders and the people were actually super into it. They cheerfully brought their money and filled that chest right up.

Whenever the Levites brought the chest for a royal audit and saw it was stuffed with cash, the king's secretary and the chief priest's official would empty it out and put it back. They did this day after day and stacked up a ton of money. The king and Jehoiada gave the funds to the Temple project managers, who then paid the masons and carpenters to restore God's Temple. The workers kept at it until the job was done, and the Temple was basically good as new. When they finished, they brought the extra money back to the king and Jehoiada. They used it to make all new sacred items for Temple worship—stuff for the daily rituals, for offerings, bowls, and other cool gold and silver gear.

They kept up the regular offerings in God's Temple for Jehoiada's entire life. He died when he was super old—like, 130! They buried him in the royal cemetery, which was a huge honor, because he had done so much good for Israel, for God, and for His Temple.

But the moment Jehoiada died, everything went south. The leaders of Judah came to the king, buttered him up, and he just went along with their terrible ideas. Things got bad, then worse. They straight up abandoned the Temple of God and started worshipping fake sex goddesses. God was seriously angry about this, and you could just feel the bad vibes over Judah and Jerusalem because of their sin. God sent prophets to try and get them back on track, warning them what would happen, but no one listened.

Then the Spirit of God came on Zechariah, who was the son of the priest Jehoiada. He stood up and called them out: 'This is God's word: Why are you ignoring God's commands? It's not going to end well for you! If you walk out on God, he's gonna walk out on you.'

But instead of listening, they plotted against him. And the king—get this—the king himself ordered it. They murdered Zechariah by stoning him, right there in the courtyard of God's Temple. That's how King Joash repaid the loyalty of Jehoiada, the guy who made him king. He murdered his son. Zechariah's last words were, 'God, you see this! Make them pay!'

About a year later, the Aramean army rolled in and attacked Joash. They invaded Judah and Jerusalem, killed all the leaders, and sent all their stuff back to their king in Damascus. The Aramean army was actually pretty small, but God used them to crush Joash's huge army. It was punishment for abandoning the God of their ancestors. The Arameans were basically carrying out God's judgment on Joash.

They left Joash badly wounded, and then his own servants finished the job. It was a whole palace conspiracy to get revenge for the murder of Jehoiada's son. They killed him in his own bed. They buried him in the City of David, but he didn't get the honor of being buried in the royal cemetery. The guys who conspired against him were Zabad and Jehozabad. The rest of the story about his sons, all the warnings he got, and the details about the Temple repair are all written down in the history books of the kings.
After him, his son Amaziah became the next king.

2 Chronicles.title: King Gets Cocky, Gets Wrecked
paragraphs: So, this dude Amaziah becomes king when he's 25 and rules for 29 years in Jerusalem. His mom was Jehoaddin, from Jerusalem. He was pretty decent in God's eyes, doing the right thing for the most part. But, lowkey, he wasn't 100% committed to God. Once he had the kingdom on lock, he executed the guards who had taken out his dad, the former king. But he didn't go after their kids—he actually followed God's law from the book of Moses, which says parents don't die for their kids' mistakes, and kids don't die for their parents'. Everyone pays for their own mess.

Amaziah got Judah organized, sorting everyone into families and military groups. All the guys 20 and up had to sign up, and they ended up with 300,000 soldiers ready to fight. On top of that, he hired 100,000 soldiers from Israel up north for about four and a half tons of silver.

Then a man of God shows up and is like, 'Yo, King, don't let those northern Israelite soldiers join your army. God isn't with them, or with any of those Ephraimite guys. You gotta go into this battle by yourself and be strong. Only God has the power to give you the W or the L.'
But Amaziah was like, 'But what about all this cash I already paid to hire them? That's a lot of silver.'
The holy man said, 'God's help is worth way more than that, my guy.'
So Amaziah sent the soldiers he hired from the north back home. They were super mad about losing the gig and went home totally fuming.
