Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai. That last guy had married one of Barzillai the Gileadite's daughters and took his name.

They searched everywhere for their family records but came up with nothing. So, they were basically banned from being priests because they were considered unclean. The governor made the call that they couldn't eat any of the holy food until a priest could figure out their status with the Urim and Thummim.

The grand total of everyone who came back was 42,360. That's not even counting their male and female slaves, which was another 7,337. They also had 200 male and female singers, plus 736 horses, 245 mules, 435 camels, and 6,720 donkeys.

When they got to God's Temple in Jerusalem, some of the family leaders made freewill offerings to help rebuild the Temple on its original spot. They gave what they could to the building fund: about 1,100 pounds of gold, around three tons of silver, and 100 robes for the priests.

The priests, Levites, and some of the other people settled down in Jerusalem. The singers, security guards, and temple support staff found places in their hometowns. Basically, all the Israelites found a place to live.

Ezra.title: Rebuilding the Altar: The Comeback Gets REAL
paragraphs: So, by the seventh month, all the Israelites were basically settled in their new towns. Then, everyone had a massive meetup in Jerusalem. This dude Jeshua (son of Jozadak) and his brother priests, along with Zerubbabel (son of Shealtiel) and his family, got straight to work. They rebuilt the Altar for the God of Israel so they could make offerings on it, exactly like the rules from Moses, God's main guy, said to.

Even though they were lowkey terrified of what their non-Israelite neighbors might pull, they just went for it. They set up the Altar right where it used to be and started giving offerings on it every morning and evening. They also celebrated the Festival of Booths like they were supposed to, and did all the daily offerings for each day. On top of that, they gave the regular offerings for Sabbaths, New Moons, and all of God’s holy festivals, plus any voluntary offerings people wanted to give to God.
They started giving these offerings to God from the very first day of the seventh month, even though the foundation of God's Temple hadn't even been started yet.

They paid masons and carpenters, and gave food, drinks, and oil to the people from Sidon and Tyre. In exchange, those guys brought cedar logs by sea from Lebanon to Joppa. This whole trade deal was approved by Cyrus, the king of Persia, so it was all official.

Then, in the second month of the second year after they got back to God's Temple in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of their crew—priests, Levites, and everyone else who had returned from exile—finally got the big project started. They put the Levites who were twenty or older in charge of supervising the rebuilding of God's Temple. Jeshua and his family teamed up with Kadmiel, Binnui, and Hodaviah, and the whole Henadad family clan—all Levites—to manage the construction crew working on God's Temple.

When the builders laid the foundation for God's Temple, it was a huge moment. The priests put on their official robes and stood with trumpets, and the Levites from Asaph's family line were there with cymbals, all to praise God just like King David of Israel had set up ages ago. They sang back and forth, a praise and thank-you song to God:
'Yes! God is good! Oh yes—he’ll never quit loving Israel!'

And all the people just erupted in a massive cheer, praising God because the foundation of His Temple was finally being laid. But while a ton of people were shouting for joy, a lot of the older priests, Levites, and family leaders who had seen the first Temple, started weeping loudly when they saw the foundation of this new one. It was a wild scene. You couldn't even tell the difference between the happy shouting and the loud crying. The sound of it all just echoed for miles.

Ezra.title: Haters Try to Stop the Temple Build
paragraphs: So, when the old enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the exiles were rebuilding the Temple for the God of Israel, they got seriously nosy. They went to Zerubbabel and the family leaders and were like, “Hey, let us help you build. We worship the same God as you. We’ve been making sacrifices to him ever since King Esarhaddon of Assyria brought us here.”

But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the other leaders of Israel were straight up: “Nah, not happening. Building the Temple for our God isn’t your project. We’re the only ones who are gonna build for the God of Israel. King Cyrus of Persia literally commanded us to do it.”

After that, those people started trying to kill the vibe for the people of Judah, messing with them while they were trying to build. They even paid people to spread lies and mess with their motivation. This went on for like fifteen years, all through King Cyrus’s reign and even into the time of King Darius.
For real, during the reign of Xerxes, right when he became king, they wrote a whole letter accusing the people living in Judah and Jerusalem.

And then later, when Artaxerxes was king, some guys named Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their crew wrote to him about what was happening in Jerusalem. The letter was in Aramaic and had to be translated. (So, what you're about to read was originally in Aramaic.)
The commanding officer Rehum and the secretary Shimshai wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes, and it went something like this:

From: Rehum the commanding officer, Shimshai the secretary, and all their boys—the judges, officials from Tripolis, Persia, Erech, and Babylon, the Elamites from Susa, and everyone else the GOAT Ashurbanipal deported and moved to Samaria and other spots across the Euphrates River.
(This is a copy of the letter they sent him.)
To: King Artaxerxes, from your loyal servants across the Euphrates.

Just wanted to let you know, King, that the Jews who came from you to us are now in Jerusalem, and they're rebuilding that rebellious, sketchy city. They're working hard on the walls and foundations. You need to know that as soon as that city is rebuilt and the wall is done, they’re gonna stop paying all taxes and tributes. The royal bank account is gonna take a major hit. We’re loyal to you, King, and we can’t just sit back and watch you get disrespected—that’s why we’re telling you this. We think you should check out your ancestors' records. You’ll see in those books that this city has a history of being rebellious and causing trouble for kings and provinces. It's always been a hotspot for revolts. That’s why it was destroyed in the first place. We're letting you know, if that city gets rebuilt and its walls are finished, you’ll basically lose control of everything in your province beyond the Euphrates.
The king sent his reply back to Rehum the commanding officer, Shimshai the secretary, and their crew living in Samaria and other places across the Euphrates.

'Sup. The letter you sent has been translated and read to me. I ordered a search of the records, and it's true—this city has a long history of rebelling against kings. It’s their whole thing. I also found out they’ve had some strong kings who ruled the whole area beyond the Euphrates and collected all sorts of taxes. So here’s the plan: Order these guys to stop working immediately. No more rebuilding in that city unless I say so. Get on it ASAP; they’ve already caused enough trouble for kings!
As soon as that letter from King Artaxerxes was read to Rehum, Shimshai, and their crew, they didn't waste any time. They went straight to the Jews in Jerusalem and forced them to stop working.
And just like that, the work on God's Temple in Jerusalem came to a dead stop. Nothing else got done until the second year of King Darius of Persia's reign.

Ezra.title: The Rebuild Gets Questioned
paragraphs: So, while all this was going down, the prophets Haggai and Zechariah were preaching to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem. They were speaking for the God of Israel, who was in charge. Their words got Zerubbabel and Jeshua so hyped that they decided to start rebuilding the Temple of God in Jerusalem all over again. And the prophets were right there with them, backing them up.

At that time, this dude Tattenai was the governor of the area. He, along with Shethar-Bozenai and their crew, rolled up on the Israelites and were like, “Yo, who gave you permission to rebuild this Temple?” So, the Israelites told them who was in charge of the construction.
But God was watching out for the Jewish leaders, so the construction didn't get shut down. They had to wait for a report to get to King Darius and for him to send back an official answer.
So Tattenai, the governor, and Shethar-Bozenai and his crew of officials sent a letter to King Darius. It basically said:
"To King Darius, hope you're doing good.
We're writing to let you know that we went to Judah and saw the Temple of the great God being rebuilt with huge stones and timbers. The work is going super fast and looking good.
We asked the leaders who gave them permission to rebuild the Temple. We also got their names to send to you, so you know who's in charge.

This is what they told us: 'We serve the God of heaven and earth. We're rebuilding the Temple that was built a long time ago by a great king of Israel. But our ancestors made God angry, so he let King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon destroy the Temple and take everyone to Babylon.'

'But in the first year of his reign, King Cyrus of Babylon gave us a permit to rebuild God's Temple. He even gave back the gold and silver stuff from the Temple that Nebuchadnezzar had taken. Cyrus gave them to a guy named Sheshbazzar, who he made governor. He told him to take everything back to the Temple in Jerusalem and rebuild it on its original spot. So Sheshbazzar laid the foundation, and it's been under construction ever since, but it's still not done.'

So, if you don't mind, could you check the royal records in Babylon to see if King Cyrus really did give them a permit to rebuild the Temple of God in Jerusalem? And then let us know what you decide."

Ezra.title: The King's Decree? No Cap, It's GOATED!
paragraphs: So, King Darius was like, "Yo, find me those records!" and had his people search the archives in Babylon. They finally found a scroll in the Ecbatana fortress over in Media, and this is what it said:
**MEMO**
Basically, back in his first year as king, Cyrus made it official about the Temple of God in Jerusalem. Here's the deal he laid out:

The Temple, you know, the one for sacrifices, needs to be rebuilt on some fresh foundations. It's gotta be 90 feet high and 90 feet wide. The structure should be three layers of big stones and then one layer of timber on top. And get this—the king's own bank is footing the bill. Oh, and all the gold and silver stuff from the Temple that Nebuchadnezzar yoinked and took to Babylon? Yeah, that all has to be returned to the Temple in Jerusalem, right back where it belongs.

Then Darius added his own two cents. He was like, "Listen up, Tattenai, you're the governor of the whole area across the Euphrates, and you and your crew need to back off. Just stay out of their way. Let the governor and the Jewish leaders do their thing and rebuild the Temple.
And I'm making it official: you guys are gonna help them out. Here's how:
First off, all the construction costs? The royal bank is paying for it, straight from the taxes collected in your area. And don't be slow about it, pay them on time.

Second, whatever they need for their worship services—bulls, rams, lambs for offerings to the God of Heaven, plus wheat, salt, wine, and oil for the priests in Jerusalem—you give it to them. Every single day, no excuses. This is so they can make their sacrifices and pray for me and my sons.

I'm also making a decree that if anyone messes with this order, you're to take a beam from their own house, sharpen it, and impale them on it. And their house? It becomes a public toilet. Seriously. And may the God who made that place special take down any king or person who tries to stop this and destroy the Temple in Jerusalem.
I, Darius, have spoken. So get it done. Now."
And you know what? Tattenai, the governor, and his buddies did exactly that. They followed Darius's orders perfectly and right away.

So the Jewish leaders kept on building, and things went super well, especially with the prophets Haggai and Zechariah cheering them on. They finished the whole thing, just like the God of Israel wanted, and with the official thumbs-up from Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes, the kings of Persia. The Temple was officially done on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of King Darius's reign.

Then it was time to party! The Israelites—the priests, the Levites, and everyone who had been in exile—had a massive celebration for the dedication of the Temple. They sacrificed 100 bulls, 200 rams, and 400 lambs. And to make things right with God for all of Israel, they offered 12 male goats, one for each of the 12 tribes. They also got all the priests and Levites organized for their duties at the Temple in Jerusalem, just like it says in the Book of Moses.

On the fourteenth day of the first month, the exiles celebrated Passover. The priests and Levites had all made sure they were spiritually clean, no exceptions. The Levites sacrificed the Passover lamb for everyone who had returned from exile, for their brother priests, and for themselves.

Then all the Israelites who were back from exile, plus anyone else who had left their old ways to follow the God of Israel, ate the Passover meal together. They were so happy, they celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven whole days. God had totally filled them with joy and even changed the mind of the king of Assyria to support them in rebuilding the Temple of their God, the God of Israel. Wild, right?

Ezra.title: King Gives Priest a Blank Check?!
paragraphs: So, after all that went down, this guy Ezra shows up. This was when Artaxerxes was king of Persia. Ezra's family tree was seriously stacked: he was the son of Seraiah, who was the son of Azariah, who was the son of Hilkiah, and on and on it goes, all the way back to Aaron, the OG high priest. Lowkey, his ancestry was goated.

So yeah, that's Ezra. He rolled up from Babylon, and he was a total pro when it came to the laws God gave Moses. And because God had his back, the king literally gave him whatever he wanted. A bunch of Israelites—priests, Levites, singers, the temple security crew, and temple workers—all decided to head to Jerusalem with him. This was all happening in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes's reign.

They made it to Jerusalem in the fifth month of the king's seventh year on the throne. Ezra had planned for them to leave Babylon on the first day of the first month, and they got to Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, all thanks to God's awesome guidance. Ezra was all in on studying God's laws, actually living them out, and teaching all of Israel how to do the same.
Here's the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra, the priest and scholar who was an expert on everything about God's rules for Israel:
Artaxerxes, the King of all Kings, to Ezra the priest, a scholar of the teachings of the God of Heaven.

What's up. I'm officially saying that any Israelite in my kingdom who wants to go to Jerusalem, including the priests and Levites, can totally go with you. The king and his seven advisors are sending you to check out how things are going in Judah and Jerusalem with your God's laws, which you've got with you. You can also take the silver and gold that the king and his advisors are giving to the God of Israel, whose home is in Jerusalem. Plus, you can take all the silver and gold that's been donated all over Babylon, including from the people and priests, for God's Temple in Jerusalem. Be smart with the money and buy bulls, rams, lambs, and all the stuff for offerings, and then offer them on the altar at your God's Temple in Jerusalem. Whatever money is left over, you and your crew can use it for whatever you think your God would want. Make sure you deliver the special items you were given for the temple services to the God of Jerusalem. And if you need anything else for the temple, you can just pay for it from the royal bank.

I, King Artaxerxes, have officially ordered all the treasurers in the land across the Euphrates River to give Ezra, the priest and scholar of the God of Heaven's teachings, whatever he asks for. That's up to 100 talents of silver, 650 bushels of wheat, and 607 gallons each of wine and olive oil. And there's no limit on the salt. No cap. Whatever the God of Heaven needs for His Temple has to be given right away. Why would the king and his sons want to make God angry?
Also, just to be clear, nobody is allowed to make any priest, Levite, singer, temple security guard, temple worker, or anyone else who works at the Temple of God pay any kind of tax or duty.

And you, Ezra, since you've got God's wisdom, I'm giving you the power to pick leaders and judges to bring justice to all the people across the Euphrates who follow your God's laws. And if anyone doesn't know the laws, you teach them.
Anyone who doesn't follow your God's laws and the king's laws has to be judged and sentenced immediately—whether it's death, being kicked out, a fine, or jail time, whatever fits.

Shout out to God, the God of our ancestors, who put it in the king's heart to make God's Temple in Jerusalem look amazing! And not only that, he made the king and all his advisors and important officials actually like me and support me. My God was on my side, so I was ready to roll. And I got all the leaders of Israel to go with me.

Ezra.title: The Ultimate Trust Fall: Road Trip Edition
paragraphs: Alright, so here's the rundown of the family heads and everyone who signed up to roll with me from Babylon back in the day when King Artaxerxes was in charge.

From Phinehas's crew: Gershom. From Ithamar's: Daniel. From David's: Hattush. From Shecaniah's, who was from Parosh's line: Zechariah, and he had 150 guys with him. From Pahath-Moab's line: Eliehoenai, son of Zerahiah, with 200 men. From Zattu's descendants: Shecaniah, son of Jahaziel, and 300 men. From Adin's crew: Ebed, son of Jonathan, with 50 men. From Elam's family: Jeshaiah, son of Athaliah, and 70 men. From Shephatiah's family: Zebadiah, son of Michael, and 80 men. From Joab's line: Obadiah, son of Jehiel, and 218 men. From Bani's descendants: Shelomith, son of Josiphiah, and 160 men. From Bebai's crew: Zechariah, son of Bebai, and 28 men. From Azgad's family: Johanan, son of Hakkatan, and 110 men. From Adonikam's family, who were the last to join: Eliphelet, Jeuel, and Shemaiah, with 60 men. And from Bigvai's crew: Uthai and Zaccur, with 70 men.

I got them all together at the canal that flows to Ahava, and we camped out there for three days. I was checking everyone out and realized we had a bunch of regular people and priests, but not a single Levite. Zero.

So I sent for the leaders—Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam—and also for the teachers Joiarib and Elnathan. I sent them to Iddo, the head guy in a town called Casiphia. I told them exactly what to say to Iddo and his relatives there: "Send us some ministers for God's Temple."

And what do you know, God was totally looking out for us. They sent back a super wise guy from the family of Mahli, who was a descendant of Levi, the son of Israel. His name was Sherebiah, and he came with his sons and brothers, making a group of eighteen. They also brought Hashabiah and Jeshaiah from the Merari family, along with their brothers and sons, which was another twenty guys. On top of that, we got 220 temple servants, who were descendants of the helpers King David and his officials had assigned to the Levites. Every single one of them was on the list.

Right there by the Ahava Canal, I announced a fast. We were all going to humble ourselves before God and pray for a safe journey for all of us and our stuff. I was honestly a little embarrassed to ask the king for an armed escort to protect us from bandits. We had just told the king, "Our God looks out for everyone who seeks him, but he turns his back on those who abandon him."
So we fasted and prayed hard about it. And He listened.

Then I chose twelve of the head priests—Sherebiah and Hashabiah, plus ten of their brothers. I weighed out all the silver, gold, and special items that the king, his advisors, and all the Israelites had donated for our God's Temple.

It was a wild amount: 25 tons of silver, 100 silver vessels worth another 3.75 tons, 20 gold bowls that weighed about 18.5 pounds, and 2 vessels made of a bright red copper that was as valuable as gold.

I told them, "You guys are holy to God, and these things are holy too. The silver and gold are gifts for the God of your ancestors. Guard them with your life until you can weigh them out safely in God's Temple for the priests, Levites, and family leaders in Jerusalem."
The priests and Levites took charge of everything that was weighed out and got ready to bring it all to the Temple of our God in Jerusalem.
We left the Ahava Canal on the twelfth day of the first month to head to Jerusalem. God was with us the whole trip and kept us safe from robbers and ambushes.

We got to Jerusalem and just chilled for three days. On the fourth day, all the silver, gold, and vessels were weighed inside God's Temple and handed over to Meremoth, a priest who was the son of Uriah. Eleazar son of Phinehas was with him, and so were the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui. Everything was counted and weighed, and the final totals were written down.

Once they arrived, the exiles who had returned from captivity gave a massive burnt offering to the God of Israel: 12 bulls for all of Israel, 96 rams, 77 lambs, and 12 male goats as an offering to be forgiven. All of it was sacrificed as a burnt offering to God.
They also delivered the king's official orders to his governors in the region west of the Euphrates. And those guys, in turn, supported the people and the work of God's Temple.

Ezra.title: We Messed Up, Big Time
paragraphs: So after everything was done, the leaders came to me and were like, “The people of Israel, including the priests and Levites, haven't kept themselves separate from the people around here with all their wild and nasty habits—we're talking Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites. They've been marrying their daughters and taking their daughters for our sons. The holy line is now all mixed in with these other people. And lowkey, our leaders were the ones who started this whole mess.”
When I heard this, I completely lost it. I ripped my shirt and my robe, pulled hair from my head and my beard, and just collapsed on the ground, totally appalled.

A lot of people who actually feared God's word about this betrayal by the exiles gathered around me. I just sat there, completely devastated, until it was time for the evening sacrifice. Then, at the evening sacrifice, I got up from my state of devastation, and still in my ripped clothes, I fell to my knees and stretched out my hands to my God. And I prayed:

“My God, I am so completely ashamed, I can't even look at you. Oh my God—our sins are piled up so high we can't see past them; our guilt is literally touching the sky. We've been stuck in this pit of guilt from our ancestors' time until right now. Because of our sins, we, our kings, and our priests have been handed over to foreign kings, to be killed, captured, looted, and publicly shamed—just like you see us now.

“But now, for a little while, our God has shown us grace. He let a few of us escape and gave us a solid place in His holy home. You, our God, have brightened our eyes and given us a little relief in the middle of our slavery. We were slaves, but even then, our God didn't ditch us. He made the kings of Persia like us and gave us the motivation to rebuild our God's Temple, fix its ruins, and build a protective wall in Judah and Jerusalem.

“And now, our God, after all this, what can we even say? We've ignored the commands you gave us through your servants the prophets. They told us, ‘The land you're about to take over is super polluted. It's filled from one end to the other with the disgusting, immoral stuff of the people who live there. So for real, don't let your daughters marry their sons, and don't let your sons marry their daughters. Don't even try to be friends with them or get on their good side. That's how you'll get strong, enjoy the good things in the land, and leave a solid inheritance for your kids.’

“And now, on top of everything we've already been through because of our evil actions and massive guilt—even though you, our God, punished us way less than we deserved and even gave us this escape—here we are, doing it all over again. We're breaking your commands by marrying people who do all this nasty stuff. Aren't you going to get angry enough to just wipe us out completely, with no one left, no way out? You are the righteous God of Israel. We're just a small group of escapees right now. Look at us, standing here totally guilty before you. No one can survive like this.”

Ezra.title: The Great Breakup: It's Complicated
paragraphs: Ezra was just completely wrecked, face down in front of God's Temple, crying his eyes out. While he was praying and spilling his guts about everything, a massive crowd of Israeli men, women, and even kids gathered around. And then everyone just started bawling, like, full-on ugly crying.

Then this dude Shecaniah, from the Elam family, stepped up and was like, 'Ezra, my guy, we messed up. We totally betrayed God by marrying girls from around here who don't follow him. But, look, it's not over. There's still a chance for Israel. Let's make a promise to God, like, right now. We'll send away all these wives and their kids, just like you and everyone who's serious about God's rules are saying. It's what the Book says, so let's just do it.'
'So get up, Ezra. You're in charge. We've got your back. Don't chicken out now.'
So Ezra got to his feet and made all the head priests, the Levites, and all the leaders of Israel swear a super serious oath to do what Shecaniah said. And they were all in.

After that, Ezra bounced from the Temple square and crashed at Jehohanan's place. He was still on a hunger strike, not eating or drinking anything, just mourning hard over how the exiles had been so unfaithful.

Then they sent out a blast to all of Judah and Jerusalem, telling all the exiles to get to Jerusalem, like, ASAP. And the message was clear: if you don't show up in three days, you're gonna lose all your stuff and get kicked out of the community. No joke.

And yo, everyone from Judah and Benjamin actually showed up in Jerusalem within the three days. It was the twentieth day of the ninth month, and they were all just sitting in the square in front of the Temple. They were all super antsy, partly because of the serious stuff they had to deal with, and partly 'cause it was pouring rain.

Ezra the priest stood up and said, 'You guys broke your promise. You married foreign women, and now you've made Israel look real bad. So, it's time to come clean to God, the God of our ancestors, and do what he wants. You gotta separate yourselves from the local people and from your foreign wives.'
The whole crowd shouted back, 'Yeah, okay! We'll do it, just like you said!'

But they also said, 'But dude, look how many of us there are! Plus, it's the rainy season, we can't just stand out here getting soaked. This is gonna take more than a day or two. A lot of us are in deep with this. How about our leaders handle it for everyone? Anyone who lives in the cities and married a foreign wife can come at a set time with the elders and judges from their city. We'll keep at it until God's not so mad at us anymore.'

Only a couple of guys, Jonathan and Jahzeiah, with Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite backing them up, were against this idea. So the exiles went ahead with the plan. Ezra the priest picked out some family heads, one by one, and they all sat down on the first day of the tenth month to get this sorted. By the first day of the first month, they had dealt with every single guy who had married a foreign wife.
Here's the list of the priests who were found to have married foreign wives:

From Jeshua's family (he was the son of Jozadak) and his brothers: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah. They all promised to divorce their wives and shook on it. To make up for their guilt, they brought a ram as a special offering.
From Immer's family: Hanani and Zebadiah.
From Harim's family: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
From Pashhur's family: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
From the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (also known as Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
From the singers: Eliashib.
From the temple security guards: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
And from the rest of the Israelites:
From Parosh's family: Ramiah, Izziah, Malkijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malkijah, and Benaiah.
From Elam's family: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
From Zattu's family: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
From Bebai's family: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
From Bani's family: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeremoth.
From Pahath-Moab's family: Adna, Kelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
From Harim's family: Eliezer, Ishijah, Malkijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon, Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah.
From Hashum's family: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
From Bani's family: Maadai, Amram, Uel, Benaiah, Bedeiah, Keluhi, Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Jaasu.
From Binnui's family: Shimei, Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah, Macnadebai, Shashai, Sharai, Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah, Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.
From Nebo's family: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah.
All these guys had married foreign wives, and some of them even had kids with them.

Nehemiah.title: My Hometown is WRECKED... So I Made a Plan
paragraphs: The journal of Nehemiah, son of Hacaliah.

So, it was December, in the twentieth year of the king's reign. I was hanging out at the palace in Susa when my bro Hanani showed up with some other guys from Judah. I was like, 'Yo, what's the situation with our people back home who made it through the exile? How's Jerusalem doing?'
And they were like, 'Bro, it's bad. The survivors are really struggling. The wall of Jerusalem is completely wrecked, and the gates are just ashes. It's a total mess.'
Hearing that just broke me. I literally sat down and cried. I was so torn up about it that I spent days fasting and praying to God about the whole situation.

I prayed, 'God, the God of heaven, you're so great and powerful. You're always loyal to your promises and faithful to people who love you and follow your rules. Please, just look at me and listen. I'm praying day and night for your people, the Israelites. I'm admitting that we've all messed up, including me and my family. We've sinned against you.'

'We've totally disrespected you. We didn't do what you told us, we ignored your commands, and we didn't follow the rules you gave to Moses. But you also promised Moses that if we messed up and you scattered us all over the world, that if we came back to you and started obeying you again, you'd bring us all back to the special place you chose for your Name.'

'Well, here they are—your people, the ones you saved with your incredible power. So please, Master, listen to my prayer, and the prayers of all your servants who actually enjoy honoring you. Help me out today and make the king be cool with what I'm about to ask.'
I was the king's cupbearer, so I had his ear.

Nehemiah.title: Nehemiah's Secret Mission to Rebuild Jerusalem
paragraphs: So, it was April, during the 20th year of King Artaxerxes's reign. I was on duty, serving the king his wine, and brought it over to him. I’d literally never looked sad in front of him before, so he was like, “Yo, why the long face? You’re not sick, are you? Or are you just feeling down?”

That question lowkey made me even more nervous. I said, “Long live the king! But for real, how can I not be sad when the city where my ancestors are buried is a total wreck, and its gates are just a pile of ashes?”
The king then asked me, “Okay, so what do you need?”

I shot a quick prayer up to the God of heaven, and then said, “If you’re cool with it, and if you think I’m a good dude, please send me to Judah, to the city where my family is buried, so I can rebuild it.”
The king, with the queen sitting right next to him, asked, “How long will you be gone, and when will you be back?”
I gave him a specific timeline, and the king was like, “Alright, bet,” and gave me his permission.

Then I added, “If it’s not too much to ask, could you also give me some official letters for the governors in the region across the Euphrates River, so they’ll let me pass through to Judah? And maybe an order for Asaph, the guy in charge of the king’s forest, to hook me up with timber for the beams for the Temple fortress, the city wall, and the house I’ll be staying in.”

God totally had my back on this, and the king gave me everything I asked for. When I got to the governors on the other side of the river, I showed them the king’s letters. The king even sent some of his cavalry with me as an escort, which was pretty sick.
But when Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah, that Ammonite official, heard about it, they were super salty. They were seriously mad that someone was actually there to help out the people of Israel.

So I finally made it to Jerusalem. After chilling for three days, I got up in the middle of the night with a few of my guys. I hadn't told a soul what God had put on my heart to do for the city. The only animal with us was the one I was riding.

I rode out in the dark, past the Valley Gate, toward the Dragon's Fountain, and over to the Dung Gate. I was checking out the city walls, which were all busted up, and the gates that had been torched. Then I went over to the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool, but it was so messy my donkey couldn't get through. So I just went up the valley in the dark, still checking out the wall. I came back in through the Valley Gate. The whole time, the local officials were clueless. They had no idea where I'd gone or what I was up to. I hadn't said a word to any of the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials, or anyone else who would be helping with the work.

Then I finally told them what was up: “Look, guys, we’re in a really bad spot here. Jerusalem is a disaster, and its gates are burned down. Let's get it together and rebuild the wall of Jerusalem so we don't have to live in this shame anymore.” I told them how God was backing me and how the king was on our side too.
They were immediately like, “We’re so in. Let’s do this.” They got ready to start the good work.

But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arab heard our plan, they just laughed at us and mocked us, saying, “Ha! What do you guys think you’re doing? You really think you can go against the king?”

I clapped back, “The God of heaven will make sure we succeed. We’re his servants, and we’re going to get to work and rebuild. You guys can stay out of it. You have no say, no claim, and no part in Jerusalem’s business!”

Nehemiah.title: The Great Wall Build of Jerusalem
paragraphs: First up, the head priest Eliashib and his crew of priests got right on it. They rebuilt the Sheep Gate, got the doors hung, and kept going all the way to the Tower of the Hundred and the Tower of Hananel. The guys from Jericho pitched in and worked next to them, and Zaccur son of Imri was on the other side.

The Hassenaah brothers took care of the Fish Gate. They fixed it up, hung the doors, and even installed all the bolts and bars. Meremoth, Uriah's son, worked next to them. Then there was Meshullam, and after him Zadok, and then the guys from Tekoa. But get this, their big-shot leaders were too cool for school and refused to get their hands dirty and help out their master.

The Jeshanah Gate was rebuilt by Joiada and Meshullam. They got it all set up with doors, bolts, and bars. Working with them were Melatiah from Gibeon, Jadon from Meronoth, and a bunch of other dudes from Gibeon and Mizpah, which was basically ruled by the governor from across the Euphrates. Uzziel, a goldsmith, worked on the next section, and then Hananiah, a perfume maker, was after him. They rebuilt the Jerusalem wall all the way to the Broad Wall.

Rephaiah, who was basically the mayor of half of Jerusalem, worked on the next part. Then Jedaiah son of Harumaph fixed up the wall right in front of his own house. Hattush son of Hashabneiah was next to him.

Malkijah and Hasshub rebuilt another section, which also included the Tower of the Furnaces. Shallum, the mayor of the other half of Jerusalem, worked next to them, and his daughters were even helping out—girl power!

The Valley Gate was handled by Hanun and the people from the village of Zanoah. They fixed it, hung the doors, and installed all the hardware. They were on a roll and repaired a whole 1,500 feet of wall, all the way to the Dung Gate.
Speaking of the Dung Gate, that was rebuilt by Malkijah, the mayor of the Beth Hakkerem district. He got it repaired, hung the doors, and put in the bolts and bars.

The Fountain Gate was Shallun's project. He was the mayor of the Mizpah district. He fixed it, put a roof on it, hung the doors, and installed all the hardware. He also rebuilt the wall of the Pool of Siloam by the King's Garden, all the way to the steps leading down from the City of David.
After him was Nehemiah son of Azbuk, the mayor of half the Beth Zur district. He worked on the section from in front of King David's tomb all the way to the Pool and the House of Heroes.

Next up were the Levites, led by Rehum son of Bani. Hashabiah, the mayor of half the Keilah district, was there representing his area. Then their relatives kept the work going under Binnui, the mayor of the other half of Keilah.

Ezer, the mayor of Mizpah, rebuilt the section from the Ascent to the Armory all the way to the Angle. Baruch son of Zabbai was super motivated and did the part from the Angle to the door of the high priest Eliashib's house. Meremoth took over from there and finished the wall to the end of Eliashib's property. Priests from the area took over from there. Benjamin and Hasshub worked on the wall in front of their own house, and Azariah did the same, working right next to his house.

Binnui son of Henadad rebuilt the section from Azariah's house to the Angle at the Corner. Palal son of Uzai worked on the part opposite the Angle and the tower that sticks out from the king's upper palace near the Court of the Guard. Next to him was Pedaiah, and the Temple staff who lived on Ophel hill worked up to the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower. The guys from Tekoa handled the section from that big tower to the wall of Ophel.

Above the Horse Gate, the priests were at it, each one fixing the wall in front of his own house. After them, Zadok son of Immer rebuilt the part in front of his house, and then Shemaiah, the keeper of the East Gate, did his part. Then came Hananiah and Hanun, and after them, Meshullam son of Berekiah rebuilt the wall in front of his own storage shed.

Malkijah the goldsmith repaired the wall all the way to where the Temple staff and merchants lived, up to the Inspection Gate and the Upper Room at the Corner. The goldsmiths and merchants teamed up to fix the last part between that Upper Room and the Sheep Gate.

Nehemiah.title: Building a Wall While Dodging Haters
paragraphs: So, when this guy Sanballat heard we were rebuilding the wall, he totally lost it and started trashing the Jews. He was with his Samaritan buddies and army dudes and was like, “What are these pathetic Jews even doing? You think they can just snap their fingers and fix everything overnight? Like they can magically turn rubble into real building stones?”
Then his sidekick, Tobiah the Ammonite, chimed in, “For real! What even is that wall they're building? I bet if a single fox climbed on it, the whole thing would crumble.”

Nehemiah just prayed through it, “God, please listen. We're getting so much hate. Make their insults bounce right back at them. Let their enemies drag them off to some other country. Don’t forgive them or forget their sin, because they’ve been dissing the builders to their faces!”
But we just kept going, fixing and rebuilding the wall. Pretty soon the whole wall was connected and halfway up to where it was supposed to be, because everyone was all in and super motivated.

But when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the Jerusalem wall repairs were going so well and the gaps were being closed, they were seriously ticked off. They all schemed together to come fight Jerusalem and just cause a ton of drama. We fought back by praying to our God and posting a 24/7 guard to watch out for them.
But then, rumors started spreading around Judah.
The construction crew is exhausted, and there's just so much rubble. We’re in way over our heads; there's no way we can finish this wall.

And the whole time, our enemies were whispering, “They'll never see us coming. Before they even know what’s up, we’ll be on them, killing them, and that’ll stop the work for good!” The Jews who lived near them kept telling us, like, ten times, “They’re all around us! They’re about to attack!”

So I posted armed guards at the weakest spots on the wall. I had families stand guard together with their swords, spears, and bows. After checking everything out, I got everyone together—the leaders, the officials, and all the people—and said, “Don’t be scared of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your families, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your homes.”

Eventually, our enemies found out that we knew their whole plan and that God had totally wrecked it. So we all went back to work on the wall. From that point on, half of my guys worked while the other half stood guard with spears, shields, bows, and armor. The army officers were there to back up everyone in Judah who was building. The guys hauling materials did it with one hand while holding a weapon in the other. Every builder had a sword strapped to his side while he worked. And I kept a guy with a trumpet right next to me to sound the alarm.

I told the nobles, officials, and everyone else, “This is a huge job, and we're spread out all along the wall, far from each other. If you hear the trumpet, run to that spot and group up with us. Our God will fight for us.”
So we kept at it, working from sunup to sundown, with half of us holding spears the whole time.
I also told everyone, “Every man and his helper needs to stay inside Jerusalem. That way, you can be guards at night and workers during the day.”
None of us even changed our clothes to sleep—not me, not my brothers, not my workers, not the guards with me. We all kept our weapons in hand, even when we went to get water.

Nehemiah.title: Nehemiah Goes OFF on the Rich Bullies
paragraphs: So, a bunch of people, including the wives, started a huge protest against their fellow Jews. Some were like, “We’ve got huge families, and we literally need food just to stay alive.”
Others were saying, “We’re having to put our fields, vineyards, and houses on the line just to get enough grain so we don’t starve.”

And then others said, “We’re having to borrow money just to pay the king’s tax on our fields and vineyards. Like, look at us. We’re the same as our brothers here; our kids are just as valuable as theirs. But here we are, having to sell our own kids as slaves—some of our daughters are already gone—and we can’t do a thing about it because other people own our fields and vineyards now.”
I got so mad when I heard all their protests and complaints. After thinking it over, I totally called out the nobles and officials. I said, “Every single one of you is ripping off your own people.”

Then I called a big meeting to deal with them. I told them, “We did everything we could to buy back our Jewish brothers who had to sell themselves as slaves to foreigners. And now you’re turning around and selling those same brothers back into slavery? Does that mean we have to buy them back all over again?”
They were dead silent. What could they even say?
“What you’re doing is so wrong. Do you not even fear God anymore? Don’t you care what the other nations, our enemies, think about you?

“Me, my brothers, and my crew have also loaned them money. But this whole thing of charging them crazy interest has to stop. Right now, give them back their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and homes that you took. And you need to cancel the debt they owe you—the money, the grain, the new wine, and the olive oil.”
They actually said, “Okay, we’ll give it all back. We won’t demand anything else from them. We’ll do everything you say.”

Then I got the priests together and made them swear an oath to keep their promise. After that, I emptied my pockets, turning them inside out, and said, “If you don’t keep this promise, may God do this to you—empty out your pockets and your house, just like this. Totally broke and empty.”
Everyone shouted a wholehearted “Yes, we’ll do it!” and praised God. And the people actually did what they promised.

And get this—from the time King Artaxerxes made me governor in Judah, from his 20th year to his 32nd year, for twelve whole years, neither I nor my brothers ever used the food allowance that came with the job. The governors before me were hard on the people, taxing them about a pound of silver a day for food and wine, and their staff were total bullies. But because I respected God, I didn't do any of that. I had a job to do: I worked on this wall. All my guys were on the job, working hard. We didn't have time to get rich on the side.

I fed 150 Jews and officials at my own table, not even counting the people who came from other countries. Every day, we cooked up one ox, six prime sheep, and a bunch of chickens for me, and every ten days, we got a huge shipment of wine. But even with all that, I never used the governor's food allowance—the people were already having a tough enough time.
So, my God, please remember all the good things I’ve done for these people.

Nehemiah.title: Finishing Strong Despite the Haters
paragraphs: So, get this. When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our haters heard that I’d rebuilt the wall and there were no gaps left—even though I hadn't put the gates in yet—Sanballat and Geshem hit me up with a message: “Yo, come meet us at Kephirim in the Ono valley.”

I was pretty sure they were just scheming to mess me up, so I sent my own messengers back saying: “I’m doing something really important right now; I can’t just leave. Why should this whole project stop just so I can come down and hang out with you?”
They sent me that same message four times, and every single time I gave them the same answer.
The fifth time, it was the same messenger with the same message, but this time Sanballat sent it as an unsealed letter for everyone to read. It said:

“So the word on the street is—and Geshem says it’s legit—that you and the Jews are planning to rebel. They’re saying that’s why you’re rebuilding the wall. The rumor is you want to make yourself king, and you’ve even got prophets in Jerusalem ready to announce, ‘Judah has a king!’ The actual king is gonna hear all this, so don’t you think we should probably sit down and talk?”
I sent him a message right back: “Literally none of what you’re saying is true. You completely made it all up.”
They were just trying to scare us into quitting. They were thinking, “They’ll get scared, give up, and never finish the job.”
I just prayed, “God, give me strength.”
Then I went to have a secret meeting with this guy Shemaiah. He was like:
“Let’s go meet at the house of God, like, inside the Temple. We can lock the doors and be safe because they’re coming to kill you. For real, they’re coming tonight to kill you.”
But I was like, “Dude, why would a guy in my position run and hide? And why would someone like me use the Temple as a hideout just to save my life? Nah, I’m not doing it.”

I had a gut feeling that God hadn't sent this guy. The so-called prophecy he was giving me was totally a setup by Tobiah and Sanballat; they had hired him. He was paid to scare me off and trick me, a regular person, into disrespecting the Temple. That way, they could ruin my reputation and have a reason to accuse me.
“My God, please don’t let Tobiah and Sanballat get away with this. And same for that prophetess Noadiah and the other prophets who were trying to mess with my head.”

The wall was officially finished on the twenty-fifth day of the month of Elul. The whole thing took fifty-two days. When all our enemies heard the news and all the nations around us saw it, they totally lost their confidence. They knew this had to be God’s work.

During this whole time, the nobles of Judah and Tobiah were basically pen pals, sending letters back and forth constantly. A lot of them were connected to him because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah, and his own son had married the daughter of Meshullam. They kept telling me all these ‘good things’ he was doing and then would snitch to him about everything I said. And then Tobiah would send me letters trying to intimidate me.

Nehemiah.title: Jerusalem's Got a New Vibe & We're Taking Names
paragraphs: Alright, so the wall was finally done, and I got the doors set up. I assigned the security crew, the worship team, and the Levites their jobs. Then I put my bro Hanani in charge of Jerusalem, along with Hananiah, the head of the main fortress. I picked Hanani 'cause he was a super solid dude who, no cap, respected God more than pretty much anyone.

I told them straight up: 'Don't even think about opening the city gates until the sun's high in the sky. And make sure you lock and bar them up tight while the guards are still on their shift. Your security team? They're gonna be regular citizens of Jerusalem, posted up right in front of their own houses.'
The city itself was huge, with tons of space, but there was hardly anyone living there yet, and most of the houses were still wrecked.

Then, I got this idea, and I'm pretty sure it was from God, to get all the important people, the leaders, and everyone else together for a big headcount. I managed to find the old family records of the first wave of people who came back from being exiled. This is what the list said:

These are the peeps from the province who came back from being held captive in exile. You know, the ones King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon dragged away? Well, they came back to Jerusalem and Judah, each to their own hometown. They rolled in with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah.
Here's the breakdown of the guys from Israel, based on their families:
From Parosh's family, 2,172.
From Shephatiah's family, 372.
From Arah's family, 652.
From Pahath-Moab's family (the descendants of Jeshua and Joab), 2,818.
From Elam's family, 1,254.
From Zattu's family, 845.
From Zaccai's family, 760.
From Binnui's family, 648.
From Bebai's family, 628.
From Azgad's family, 2,322.
From Adonikam's family, 667.
From Bigvai's family, 2,067.
From Adin's family, 655.
From Ater's family (Hezekiah's descendants), 98.
From Hashum's family, 328.
From Bezai's family, 324.
From Hariph's family, 112.
From Gibeon's crew, 95.
And here are the Israelites, listed by where they were from:
From Bethlehem and Netophah, 188 people.
From Anathoth, 128.
From Beth Azmaveth, 42.
From Kiriath Jearim, Kephirah, and Beeroth, 743.
From Ramah and Geba, 621.
From Micmash, 122.
From Bethel and Ai, 123.
From the other Nebo, 52.
From the other Elam, 1,254.
From Harim, 320.
From Jericho, 345.
From Lod, Hadid, and Ono, 721.
From Senaah, a whopping 3,930.
Now for the priest families:
From Jedaiah's family (Jeshua's descendants), 973.
From Immer's family, 1,052.
From Pashhur's family, 1,247.
From Harim's family, 1,017.
And the Levite families:
From Jeshua's family (descendants of Kadmiel and Hodaviah), only 74.
The singers:
From Asaph's family line, 148.
The security guard families:
Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai, adding up to 138.
The families of the support staff:
Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,
Keros, Sia, Padon,
Lebana, Hagaba, Shalmai,
Hanan, Giddel, Gahar,
Reaiah, Rezin, Nekoda,
Gazzam, Uzza, Paseah,
Besai, Meunim, Nephussim,
Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur,
Bazluth, Mehida, Harsha,
Barkos, Sisera, Temah,
Neziah, and Hatipha.
And the families of Solomon's servants:
Sotai, Sophereth, Perida,
Jaala, Darkon, Giddel,
Shephatiah, Hattil, Pokereth-Hazzebaim, and Amon.
All the Temple support staff and Solomon's servants together were 392 people.

Then there were these guys who came from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Kerub, Addon, and Immer. The problem was, they couldn't prove their family history, so we weren't sure if they were legit Israelites or not:
The descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda, 642 of them.
And the same thing happened with these priest families:
The descendants of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai (he was the one who married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite and took his name).

They searched everywhere for their family records but came up empty. So, they were kicked out of the priesthood because they were considered 'unclean.' The governor made a rule that they couldn't eat any of the holy food until a priest could figure out their status using the Urim and Thummim.

The grand total for the whole community was 42,360. That's not even counting the 7,337 male and female slaves. Plus, there were 245 male and female singers. And get this, they had 736 horses, 245 mules, 435 camels, and 6,720 donkeys.

Some of the family leaders gave money for the project out of their own pockets. The governor himself donated about 19 pounds of gold, 50 bowls, and 530 sets of clothes for the priests. Other family heads gave about 20,000 drachmas of gold and over a ton of silver. The rest of the people pitched in about 375 pounds of gold, 2,000 minas of silver, and 67 sets of priest clothes.
The priests, Levites, security guards, singers, Temple workers, and a bunch of other people, plus all the rest of the Israelites, all found places to live in their own towns.

Nehemiah.title: The Greatest Bible Study Session Ever
paragraphs: By the time the seventh month rolled around, all the Israelites were settled in their new towns. Then, everyone, and I mean *everyone*, gathered together in the square by the Water Gate. They were like, 'Yo, Ezra, my guy, bring out that Book of the Law of Moses that God gave us!'

So Ezra the priest brought the Law out for the whole assembly—men, women, and anyone old enough to get what was going on. It was the first day of the seventh month. He read it out loud, facing the square from dawn till noon. And you know what? The people were locked in. They were hanging on every word.

The scholar Ezra was standing on a wooden stage they built just for this. He had a whole crew with him. On his right were Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah. On his left were Pedaiah, Mishael, Malkijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.

Ezra opened the book, and everyone could see him because he was up high. As soon as he opened it, everyone stood up. Then Ezra gave a huge shout-out to God, the great God, and all the people raised their hands and yelled back, 'Amen! For real!' Then they all bowed down, faces to the ground, and worshipped God.

The Levites—Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, and the rest of the crew—went around explaining the Law to the people while they were standing there. They basically translated the Book of God's Law so everyone could understand what was being read.

Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scholar, and the Levites who were teaching, told everyone, 'This is a holy day for your God. Don't be sad and cry.' They had to say that because everyone was literally weeping as they heard the words of the Law.
He went on, 'Go home and have a feast! Eat good food, drink sweet drinks, and share with those who don't have anything. This day is special to God. Don't feel bad. The joy of God is your superpower!'
The Levites helped calm everyone down, saying, 'Quiet down, y'all. This is a holy day. No need to be upset.'

So the people went off and had a huge party, eating and drinking and making sure to include the poor. It was a massive celebration because they finally got it. They understood the words that had been read to them.

On the second day, all the family heads, the priests, and the Levites got together with Ezra the scholar to dive deeper into the Law's words. They found it written that God had commanded through Moses that the Israelites should live in temporary shelters, like booths, during the festival in the seventh month. So they sent out a notice everywhere, even in Jerusalem: 'Go up to the hills and grab some olive, pine, myrtle, palm, and other leafy branches to build booths, just like the scripture says.'

So the people went out, got the branches, and built themselves little shelters on their roofs, in their courtyards, in the Temple courtyards, and in the public squares by the Water Gate and the Ephraim Gate. The entire group that came back from exile built booths and lived in them. It was wild because the Israelites hadn't done this since the time of Joshua, son of Nun. It was an amazing day, full of incredible joy!
Ezra read from the Book of God's Law every single day of the seven-day festival. On the eighth day, they had a special final assembly, just as they were supposed to.

Nehemiah.title: Israel's Epic History Lesson & A Big 'We Messed Up'
paragraphs: So on the 24th day of the month, the Israelites all got together. They were fasting, wearing scratchy burlap clothes, and had dirt on their faces to show they were serious about saying sorry. They basically unfriended all the foreigners and then stood up to confess their own screw-ups and the messed-up things their ancestors had done. They just stood there for like a quarter of the day, reading from the rule book of their God. Then for another quarter of the day, they were confessing and worshipping their God.

A bunch of Levites—Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Kenani—got up on a platform and just yelled out to their God. Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah were like, “Get up! Praise your God, forever and ever!”

Your awesome name is blessed, way above any praise we could give! You're the one, God, you and only you. You made the skies, even the highest heavens, and all the angels. You made the earth and everything on it, the oceans and everything in them. You keep it all going, and all the angels in heaven worship you!

You're the God who picked Abram, brought him all the way from Ur of the Chaldees, and changed his name to Abraham. You saw that his heart was loyal to you, so you made a promise with him. A promise to give him the land of all those 'ites'—the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites—and to give it to his kids. And you actually kept your promise, because you're a good God.
