Nehemiah.title: We're All In This Together: The Official Pact
paragraphs: Alright, so everyone put their name on this super serious contract. The big boss, Governor Nehemiah, son of Hacaliah, signed it first.

Then came the priests: Zedekiah, Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah, Pashhur, Amariah, Malkijah, Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch, Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah, Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch, Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin, Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah. Yeah, that's the whole priest squad.

The Levites were next: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel, and their boys: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan, Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah, Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah, Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.

Then the leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani, Bunni, Azgad, Bebai, Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin, Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur, Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai, Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai, Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir, Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua, Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah, Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub, Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek, Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah, Ahiah, Hanan, Anan, Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.

The rest of the people—priests, Levites, security guards, singers, Temple staff, and everyone who had separated themselves from the local foreigners to follow God's Law, along with their wives and kids who were old enough to understand—all teamed up with their leaders. They made a binding promise, a legit oath, to follow God's Law that was given through Moses, God's servant. They promised to obey all the commands, rules, and laws of God our Master.
So basically, they promised:
We won't let our daughters marry the guys from around here, and we won't let our sons marry their daughters.
When the local people bring stuff to sell on the Sabbath, like food or whatever, we're not buying. Not on the Sabbath or any other holy day. Period.
Every seventh year, we'll give the land a break and cancel all debts. No cap.

We're also taking responsibility for the Temple of our God. We'll pay a yearly tax to cover the costs for the special bread, the regular grain offerings, the regular burnt offerings, the offerings for Sabbaths, New Moons, and other festivals, the sin offerings to make things right for Israel, and basically for all the work of the Temple of our God.
We—the priests, Levites, and the people—cast lots to figure out when each of our families has to bring wood for the fire on the altar of our God. It's a yearly thing, just like it says in the Law.

We also promise to bring the first part of our harvest from our fields and orchards to the Temple of God each year. And we'll bring our firstborn sons, our firstborn cattle, and the firstborn of our herds and flocks to the priests serving in the Temple, just like the Law says.

We'll bring the best of our dough, our offerings, the fruit from all our trees, and our new wine and oil to the priests at the storerooms of the Temple of our God. And we'll bring a tenth of our crops to the Levites, because they're the ones who collect the tithes in all the towns where we work. A priest from Aaron's family will be with the Levites when they collect the tithes, and the Levites will bring a tenth of those tithes to the treasury of the Temple of our God. The people of Israel and the Levites are to bring their contributions of grain, new wine, and oil to the storerooms where the Temple equipment is kept and where the priests, the gatekeepers, and the singers are.
We will not neglect the Temple of our God.

Nehemiah.title: Who's Who in Jerusalem? (The Official Roster)
paragraphs: So, the big shots were already posted up in Jerusalem. For everyone else, they basically drew straws, and one out of every ten people had to pack up and move to the holy city, Jerusalem. The other nine got to stay in their hometowns. And everyone gave a massive shout-out to the people who were like, 'Yo, I'll go!' and volunteered to live in Jerusalem.

Alright, here’s the rundown of the provincial leaders who were living in Jerusalem. Just so you know, a bunch of regular Israelites, priests, Levites, Temple workers, and even descendants of Solomon's servants were living out in the towns of Judah on their own land. But these specific peeps from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin were the ones living inside Jerusalem:
From Judah's crew, you had:

Athaiah (son of Uzziah, who was the son of Zechariah, who was the son of Amariah, who was the son of Shephatiah, who was the son of Mahalalel, from Perez's family line). Also, Maaseiah (son of Baruch, who was the son of Col-Hozeh, who was the son of Hazaiah, who was the son of Adaiah, who was the son of Joiarib, who was the son of Zechariah, the son of the Shilonite). All in all, the descendants of Perez living in Jerusalem were 468 seriously brave dudes.
And from Benjamin's squad:

Sallu (son of Meshullam, who was the son of Joed, who was the son of Pedaiah, who was the son of Kolaiah, who was the son of Maaseiah, who was the son of Ithiel, who was the son of Jeshaiah), and his bros Gabbai and Sallai, making it 928 guys. Their top dog was Joel son of Zicri, and Judah son of Hassenuah was his second-in-command for the city.
From the priests:

There was Jedaiah son of Joiarib; Jakin; Seraiah (son of Hilkiah, who was the son of Meshullam, who was the son of Zadok, who was the son of Meraioth, who was the son of Ahitub), who was the supervisor of God's Temple, along with his crew who did all the work in the Temple—that was 822 guys. Then there was Adaiah (son of Jeroham, who was the son of Pelaliah, who was the son of Amzi, who was the son of Zechariah, who was the son of Pashhur, who was the son of Malkijah), and his associates who were family heads—242 of them. And Amashsai (son of Azarel, who was the son of Ahzai, who was the son of Meshillemoth, who was the son of Immer), and his crew, all total legends: 128 men. Their commander was Zabdiel son of Haggedolim.
From the Levites:

Shemaiah (son of Hasshub, who was the son of Azrikam, who was the son of Hashabiah, who was the son of Bunni); Shabbethai and Jozabad, two of the Levite leaders who handled the Temple's external affairs; Mattaniah (son of Mica, who was the son of Zabdi, who was the son of Asaph), the director who led the thanksgiving and prayer time; Bakbukiah, who was second-in-command among his crew; and Abda (son of Shammua, who was the son of Galal, who was the son of Jeduthun). The total number of Levites in the holy city was 284.
From the security guards:
Akkub, Talmon, and their squad who guarded the gates: 172 dudes.
The rest of the Israelites, priests, and Levites were scattered across all the towns of Judah, each on their own family's land.
The Temple staff lived on a hill called Ophel. Ziha and Gishpa were in charge of them.

The head honcho of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi (son of Bani, who was the son of Hashabiah, who was the son of Mattaniah, who was the son of Mica). This Uzzi guy was from Asaph's family line, the singers who led worship in God's Temple. The singers had their own daily schedule set by the king himself.
Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, who was a descendant of Zerah son of Judah, was the guy who spoke to the king on behalf of the people.
Some of the people from Judah lived in villages near their farms:
Kiriath Arba (which is Hebron) and its suburbs
Dibon and its suburbs
Jekabzeel and its suburbs
Jeshua
Moladah
Beth Pelet
Beersheba and its suburbs
Ziklag
Meconah and its suburbs
En Rimmon
Jarmuth
Zanoah
Adullam and their towns
Lachish and its fields
Azekah and its suburbs.
They were living all over the place, from Beersheba all the way to the Valley of Hinnom.
The Benjaminites from Geba lived in:
Micmash
Bethel and its suburbs
Anathoth
Nob and Ananiah
Ramah and Gittaim
Hadid, Zeboim, and Neballat
Lod and Ono and the Valley of the Craftsmen.
Also, some of the Levite groups from Judah were assigned to live in Benjamin's territory.

Nehemiah.title: Jerusalem's Wall Party Was Epic
paragraphs: Alright, so here are the priests and Levites who came back with Zerubbabel (son of Shealtiel) and Jeshua:
Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Ginnethon, Abijah,
Mijamin, Moadiah, Bilgah,
Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah.
These guys were the top priests back in Jeshua's time.
And the Levites:
Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah;
Mattaniah and his crew were in charge of the praise and worship songs, and their bros Bakbukiah and Unni stood across from them during the services.
Jeshua was the father of Joiakim, Joiakim was the father of Eliashib, Eliashib was the father of Joiada, Joiada was the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan was the father of Jaddua.
Jeshua was the father of Joiakim,
Joiakim was the father of Eliashib,
Eliashib was the father of Joiada,
Joiada was the father of Jonathan,
and Jonathan was the father of Jaddua.
When Joiakim was around, these were the heads of the priestly families:
of Seraiah's family, Meraiah;
of Jeremiah's, Hananiah;
of Ezra's, Meshullam;
of Amariah's, Jehohanan;
of Malluch's, Jonathan;
of Shecaniah's, Joseph;
of Harim's, Adna;
of Meremoth's, Helkai;
of Iddo's, Zechariah;
of Ginnethon's, Meshullam;
of Abijah's, Zicri;
of Miniamin and Moadiah's, Piltai;
of Bilgah's, Shammua;
of Shemaiah's, Jehonathan;
of Joiarib's, Mattenai;
of Jedaiah's, Uzzi;
of Sallu's, Kallai;
of Amok's, Eber;
of Hilkiah's, Hashabiah;
and of Jedaiah's, Nethanel.
During the time of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, the Levites were registered as heads of families. The priests were also registered during the reign of Darius the Persian.
The Levites who were heads of families were written down in the Book of Chronicles until the time of Johanan, son of Eliashib. These were:
Hashabiah,
Sherebiah,
and Jeshua son of Kadmiel.
Their brothers stood across from them to praise and give thanks, with one side responding to the other, just like David, the man of God, had instructed.
The security guards included:
Mattaniah,
Bakbukiah,
Obadiah,
Meshullam,
Talmon,
and Akkub.

They guarded the storerooms at the gates. They were active during the time of Joiakim son of Jeshua (son of Jozadak), and also during the time of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scholar.

When it was time to dedicate the wall, they went and found all the Levites from their homes and brought them to Jerusalem to celebrate the dedication with some serious hype: thanksgiving hymns, songs, cymbals, harps, and lutes. The singers gathered from all around Jerusalem, from the villages of the Netophathites, from Beth Gilgal, and from the farms at Geba and Azmaveth—because the singers had built their own villages all around Jerusalem.
The priests and Levites first purified themselves, and then they purified the people, the gates, and the wall.

I had the leaders of Judah go up on the wall, and I set up two huge choirs. One went along the wall to the right, toward the Dung Gate. Hoshaiah and half of Judah's leaders followed them, along with Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam, Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah. Some of the younger priests had trumpets. Then came Zechariah (son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph) and his crew, playing the instruments of David, the man of God. Ezra the scholar led this group.
At the Fountain Gate, they went straight up the steps of the City of David, using the stairway on the wall above David's house, all the way to the Water Gate on the east.

The other choir went to the left. I followed them with the other half of the people on the wall, past the Tower of Furnaces to the Broad Wall, over the Ephraim Gate, the Jeshanah Gate, the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate, and we stopped at the Prison Gate.

Then the two choirs took their spots in God's Temple. I was there with half of the officials, and the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah with their trumpets. Also Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malkijah, Elam, and Ezer. The singers, led by Jezrahiah, were so loud they made the place shake.

That day, they offered huge sacrifices and had a massive party because God had made them so incredibly happy. The women and kids joined in, and the sound of Jerusalem's celebration could be heard from miles away.

On that same day, guys were put in charge of the storerooms for the offerings, firstfruits, and tithes. They made sure that the portions the Law required for the priests and Levites were brought in from the farms. Judah was super grateful for the priests and Levites and their service. They, along with the singers and security guards, did everything so well—worshipping their God and doing the purification rituals in a way that would have made David and his son Solomon proud. That's how they used to do it back in the day, in the time of David and Asaph, when they had choir directors for singing praise and thanksgiving songs to God.

So, during the time of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, all of Israel gave daily supplies for the singers and security guards. They also set aside the dedicated portion for the Levites, and the Levites did the same for the descendants of Aaron.

Nehemiah.title: Nehemiah Cleans House, No Cap
paragraphs: So, on the same day, they were reading out loud from the Book of Moses for everyone to hear. And get this, they found a rule that said no one from Ammon or Moab was ever allowed in God's crew. Why? Because way back, they didn't help out the Israelites with food and water. They were super shady and even hired a guy named Balaam to curse them. But God, being the GOAT, flipped the curse into a blessing. As soon as the people heard this, they were like, 'Aight, bet,' and kicked all the foreigners out of Israel.

Okay, so a little while before this, this priest named Eliashib was in charge of the Temple's storage rooms. He was boys with this dude Tobiah and gave him a huge room that was supposed to be for all the holy stuff—like offerings, incense, and all the supplies for the Levites and priests.

I wasn't even in Jerusalem when this was all going down. It was the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes of Babylon, and I had to go back to see him. But later, I got his permission to leave again. When I got back to Jerusalem, I found out about the messed-up thing Eliashib did, giving Tobiah a room right in the Temple courts. I was so mad, like, beyond angry. I literally threw all of Tobiah's stuff out into the street. Then I ordered them to do a deep clean of the room, and only then did I put all the Temple's sacred items back, along with the offerings and incense.

Then I found out that the Levites weren't getting their pay. So the Levites and the singers who led worship had all bounced and gone back to their farms. I called out the officials, like, 'Why is God's Temple being ghosted?' I got everyone to come back and put them back on their jobs. Then all of Judah started bringing in their tithes of grain, wine, and oil to the storerooms again. I put Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and a Levite named Pedaiah in charge of the storerooms. And I made Hanan, the son of Zaccur, their right-hand man. These guys had a rep for being honest and hardworking. They were in charge of giving out the supplies to their coworkers.
Remember me for this, my God. Don't ever forget the hard work I've put in for Your Temple and its worship.

During that time, back in Judah, I also saw people working on the Sabbath—stomping on grapes to make wine, bringing in grain, and loading up their donkeys. They were bringing wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of stuff to sell on the Sabbath. So I called them out and warned them about selling food on that day. And get this, people from Tyre who lived there were bringing in fish and other stuff, selling it to the people of Judah—in Jerusalem, of all places!—on the Sabbath.

I confronted the leaders of Judah and was like, 'What is going on here? This is so wrong! You're disrespecting the Sabbath! Isn't this exactly what your ancestors did? And because of that, didn't God bring all this disaster on us and this city? And now you're just making it worse, piling up more anger on Jerusalem by dissing the Sabbath.'

So, as the sun started to set on Friday, right before the Sabbath began, I ordered the city gates to be shut and not opened until the Sabbath was over. I even put some of my own guys at the gates to make sure no one could sneak in anything to sell on the Sabbath.

The merchants and sellers camped outside the gates once or twice. But I went off on them. I said, 'You have no business camping out here by the wall. If I catch you here again, I'm gonna have to get physical.'
And that was that; they didn't come back on the Sabbath.
Then I told the Levites to go through a cleansing ceremony and take over as guards at the gates to make sure the Sabbath day was kept holy.
Remember me for this too, my God. Show me mercy because of your great and never-ending love.

Also, during those days, I saw some Jewish guys who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. Half their kids couldn't even speak the language of Judah; all they knew was the language of Ashdod or some other language. So I confronted those men, gave them a piece of my mind, and even slapped some of them and pulled their hair. I made them swear to God: 'Don't let your daughters marry their sons, and don't let their daughters marry your sons—and don't you marry them either! Didn't King Solomon of Israel sin because of women just like these? Even though there was no king like him, and God loved him and made him king over all of Israel, foreign women were his downfall. Do you really think this is okay—doing this huge evil thing and being unfaithful to God by marrying foreign wives?'
One of the sons of Joiada, who was the son of the high priest Eliashib, was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite. I kicked him out of my sight.
Remember them, O my God, for how they trashed the priesthood and the promises of the priests and Levites.

So, all in all, I cleaned them up from everything foreign. I got the priests and Levites organized so that everyone knew their job. I also set up a regular supply of wood for the altar at the right times and for the first offerings of the harvest.
Remember me, O my God, for good.

Esther.title: King Throws Wild Party, Gets Ghosted By The Queen
paragraphs: So get this, this all went down back in the day with this king named Xerxes. This dude was the ruler of a massive empire that stretched all the way from India to Ethiopia—like, 127 different regions. King Xerxes was chilling on his throne in the capital city, Susa.
In his third year as king, he decided to throw a huge banquet for all his officials and ministers. The top military guys from Persia and Media were there, plus all the princes and governors.

For a solid six months, he was just flexing, showing off all the crazy rich stuff his kingdom had and how awesome his palace was. After that massive flex-fest, the king threw another party, this one for a whole week, for every single person living in the capital, Susa—didn't matter if you were a big shot or a nobody. The party was in the super fancy garden of the king's summer house. The whole place was decked out with white and blue curtains, tied up with fancy purple cords to silver rings on marble pillars. They had couches made of silver and gold set up on this insane mosaic floor made of all kinds of expensive stones. Drinks were served in solid gold cups, and get this—every single cup was unique. The royal wine was flowing like water, 'cause the king was being super generous.

Basically, you could drink as much as you wanted. The king ordered the waiters to just keep refilling everyone's cup. Meanwhile, Queen Vashti was having her own party for the women inside the main palace.

On the seventh and final day of the party, the king, who was pretty drunk by this point, told his seven personal servants to go get Queen Vashti. He wanted her to come out wearing her royal crown so he could show off to all his guests how beautiful she was. And yeah, she was a total smoke-show.

But Queen Vashti was like, 'Nah,' and straight up refused to come. She rejected the king's order that the servants delivered. The king completely lost it. He was absolutely fuming that she would disrespect him like that. So, he called in his advisors, who were all experts on the law. It was his thing to always ask his experts for advice. His inner circle included guys named Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan—the seven most powerful princes in the kingdom who could always talk to the king. He asked them what the law says he can do about Queen Vashti ignoring his direct order.

Then this guy Memucan spoke up in front of the king and all the other princes: “Look, Queen Vashti didn't just disrespect you, King. She dissed all of us, all the leaders and all the people in every single one of your provinces. The news is gonna spread like wildfire: ‘Yo, did you hear about Queen Vashti? The king told her to come, and she just said no!’ When other women hear this, they're all gonna start treating their own husbands with zero respect. The second the wives of all the important officials hear what the queen did, they'll go wild. Is that what we really want? A whole country full of angry women who don't know their place?”

“So, if you're cool with it, King, you should make a royal decree. Write it into the official laws of Persia and Media so it can never be changed. The law should say that Vashti is banned from ever being in your presence again. And then, you should give her royal title to a woman who's actually better and knows her place. When this new rule is announced all over your massive kingdom, every single woman, no matter if she's rich or poor, will have to show proper respect to her husband.”

The king and his princes were all like, 'Yeah, that's a great idea.' So the king did exactly what Memucan suggested. He sent out messages to every part of his kingdom, written in each province's own script and in their own language. The message was clear: “Every man is the boss in his own house, and whatever he says, goes. Period.”

Esther.title: The Royal Glow-Up: From Zero to Hero
paragraphs: So, after a while, King Xerxes wasn't as mad at Queen Vashti anymore. He was kinda rethinking the whole situation and what he'd ordered. His crew of young assistants saw their chance and were like, “Yo, let's find some amazing, beautiful young women for the king.” They suggested the king get officials in every part of his kingdom to bring all the beautiful, single ladies to the palace in Susa. They'd go to the harem, which was run by this guy Hegai, the king's eunuch in charge of the women. He'd get them all set up with spa treatments and everything. Then, the girl who the king vibes with the most would become the new queen instead of Vashti.
The king was totally on board with this plan and made it happen.

Now, there was this Jewish guy named Mordecai living in the palace complex at Susa. He was from the tribe of Benjamin, and his family had been exiled from Jerusalem way back when. Mordecai had raised his cousin, Hadassah, who everyone called Esther, because her parents had passed away. She was seriously stunning, with a great personality and a beautiful face. After her parents died, Mordecai basically adopted her.
When the king's new rule went public, a ton of young women were brought to the palace in Susa and handed over to Hegai. Esther was one of them.

Hegai thought Esther was awesome and took a real liking to her. He immediately started her on the best beauty treatments, got her special food, gave her seven personal maids from the palace, and put her and her maids in the best suite in the harem. But Esther kept her family and her Jewish background on the down-low, because Mordecai told her not to say anything.
Every single day, Mordecai would walk by the harem courtyard to check in and see how Esther was doing and what was going on with her.

Each girl had to go through a whole year of beauty prep before it was her turn to meet King Xerxes. It was six months of treatments with myrrh oil, and then six months with perfumes and other cosmetics. When a girl's time came to go to the king, she could take whatever she wanted with her from the harem. She'd go to his place in the evening and then in the morning, she'd move to a different harem, this one run by Shaashgaz, another one of the king's eunuchs who was in charge of the concubines. A girl would never see the king again unless he was super into her and specifically asked for her by name.

When it was Esther's turn to go see the king, she didn't ask for anything extra. She just went with what Hegai, the guy in charge of the harem, suggested. And just like that, Esther wowed everyone who saw her.
She was taken to King Xerxes in his royal palace in the tenth month, which was the seventh year of his reign.

The king was head over heels for Esther, way more than any of the other women. He was completely smitten. He put a royal crown on her head and made her the new queen, replacing Vashti. Then the king threw a huge party for all his important officials, calling it “Esther’s Banquet.” He even declared a public holiday for the whole kingdom and gave out tons of generous gifts.

One time, when the virgins were all being gathered, Mordecai was just chilling at the King's Gate. The whole time, Esther had kept her family background a secret, just like Mordecai told her to. She still listened to him, just like when she was a kid.

So on this particular day, while Mordecai was at the King's Gate, two of the king's eunuchs who guarded the entrance, Bigthana and Teresh, were plotting to kill King Xerxes. But Mordecai found out about their plan and told Queen Esther. She then went and told the king, making sure to give Mordecai the credit. The whole thing was investigated, and it turned out to be true, so the two guys were hanged. And this was all written down in the king's official records.

Esther.title: The King's Advisor Goes on a Power Trip
paragraphs: A little while later, King Xerxes gave a major promotion to this guy Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite. He basically made him the second most powerful person in the whole government. All the king's staff at the main gate would bow down and kneel whenever Haman came by—that was the king's direct order.

But Mordecai? Nah, he wasn't having it. He refused to bow down. The other royal staff were like, "Dude, why are you disobeying the king's command?" They bugged him about it every single day, but he just wouldn't listen. So, they snitched to Haman, thinking something had to be done. Mordecai had already told them he was a Jew.

When Haman saw with his own eyes that Mordecai wasn't bowing down, he was seriously ticked off. But then he found out Mordecai was a Jew, and suddenly, getting mad at just one guy felt like a waste of energy. He decided to go bigger—he started plotting how to get rid of not just Mordecai, but every single Jew in Xerxes' entire kingdom.

So, in the first month, Nisan, during Xerxes' twelfth year as king, Haman had them cast a "pur"—which is like drawing lots—to pick the perfect day and month for his evil plan. The lot fell on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is Adar.

Haman then went to King Xerxes and said, "Hey King, there's this weird group of people scattered all over your kingdom, and they just don't fit in. Their traditions are totally different from everyone else's. And what's worse, they totally ignore your laws. It's a disgrace, and you shouldn't let them get away with it. If you're cool with it, let's just issue an order to wipe them out. I'll even pay for the whole thing myself. I'll drop 375 tons of silver into the royal treasury to cover the costs."
The king just took off his special signet ring and handed it to Haman, the Agagite who was the number one enemy of the Jews.
"Go for it," the king told Haman. "It's your money. Do whatever you want with those people."

So on the thirteenth day of the first month, the king's secretaries were called in. They wrote down every single word of Haman's order, addressing it to all the king's satraps, governors, and officials of every single province and people group. It was written in their own languages and scripts, in King Xerxes' name, and sealed with his royal ring.

Official notices were sent out by messengers to every province in the kingdom. The orders were to massacre, kill, and completely wipe out all the Jews—young, old, women, and children—on one single day: the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, Adar. And, they were allowed to take all their stuff. Copies of the order were posted in public in every province, so everyone could get ready for that day.
At the king's command, the couriers took off; the order was also posted in the palace complex of Susa. The king and Haman sat back and had a drink while the city of Susa reeled from the news.

Esther.title: If I Die, I Die
paragraphs: When Mordecai found out what was going down, he totally lost it. He ripped his clothes, threw on some rough old burlap, and covered himself in ashes. Then he went through the city, wailing super loud and bitter. He could only go as far as the King’s Gate, though, because you weren’t allowed in wearing that kind of outfit. And as the king’s new rule got posted everywhere, all the Jewish people were in major mourning—they were fasting, crying, and just falling apart. Most of them were just lying on the ground in burlap and ashes.

Esther’s maids and personal assistants came and told her what was up. The queen was shook. She sent Mordecai some fresh clothes so he could change out of the burlap, but he was like, “Nah.” So Esther called for this guy Hathach, one of the king’s assistants assigned to her, and told him to go find out from Mordecai what was really going on. Hathach went to Mordecai in the town square right by the King’s Gate. Mordecai spilled everything that had happened to him. He even told him the exact amount of cash Haman had promised to pay the king to get all the Jews killed. Mordecai also gave him a copy of the official order for the massacre that was posted in Susa, so he could show it to Esther and tell her she had to go to the king and beg him to save her people.

Hathach went back and told Esther everything Mordecai said. Esther talked it over with Hathach and then sent him back to Mordecai with this message: “Look, everyone who works for the king, and even people out in the provinces, knows the deal. There’s one rule for any man or woman who just shows up to the king without an invite: they die. The only way out is if the king holds out his golden scepter to them; then they get to live. And it’s been a whole month since I was last called to see the king.”

When Hathach told Mordecai what Esther said, Mordecai sent this message back to her: “Don’t think for a second that just because you’re in the palace, you’re the one Jew who’s gonna make it out of this alive. If you stay quiet at a time like this, help will come for the Jews from somewhere else, but you and your whole family will be toast. Who knows? Maybe you were made queen for this exact moment.”

Esther sent her answer back to Mordecai: “Go get all the Jews in Susa together. Fast for me. Don’t eat or drink anything for three days and three nights. Me and my maids will do the same. After that, I’ll go to the king, even though it’s against the law. If I die, I die.”
Mordecai bounced and did everything Esther told him to do.

Esther.title: Esther's Risky Dinner Party
paragraphs: Three days later, Esther got all dressed up in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace, right in front of the king's throne room. The king was on his throne, facing the entrance. When he saw Queen Esther standing there, he was actually glad to see her and held out the golden scepter in his hand. Esther went up and touched the tip of it.
The king asked, "What's up, Queen Esther? What do you want? Just ask, and you'll get it—even if it's half of my kingdom!"
Esther said, "If it's cool with you, I'd like for you and Haman to come to a dinner I've made for you."
"Get Haman right away," the king said, "so we can go to dinner with Esther."
So the king and Haman went to the dinner Esther had set up. While they were drinking wine, the king said, "Okay, for real, what do you want? You can have up to half my kingdom. Just ask!"
Esther replied, "So, here's what I want. If you're really down to do this for me, please come with Haman to the dinner I'll make for you tomorrow. Then I'll tell you what I really want."

Haman left the palace that day feeling super happy. But then he saw Mordecai at the King's Gate, who completely ignored him. Haman was seriously mad at Mordecai, but he kept his cool and went home. He gathered his friends and his wife Zeresh and started flexing about how rich he was, his many sons, all the honors the king had given him, and how he was promoted to the top job in the government. "And get this," Haman went on, "Queen Esther invited me to a private dinner with the king, just the three of us. And she invited me again tomorrow. But none of that matters when I see that guy Mordecai the Jew sitting at the King's Gate."

His wife Zeresh and all his friends were like, "You should build a gallows that's 75 feet high. First thing in the morning, talk to the king and get him to hang Mordecai on it. Then you can go to dinner with the king and actually enjoy it."
Haman thought that was a great idea. So he had the gallows built.

Esther.title: The King's Sleepless Night Leads to Haman's Epic Fail
paragraphs: So that night, the king was tossing and turning and just could not sleep. He told his servants to bring the official records, like the kingdom's daily journal, and read it to him. They got to the part where Mordecai totally saved the day by exposing the assassination plot from Bigthana and Teresh, those two eunuchs who were supposed to be guarding the entrance.
The king stops them and asks, "Wait, what did we do for Mordecai for this? What kind of big reward did he get?"
His servants were like, "Uh, nothing. Literally nothing was done for him."
The king says, "Is anyone in the courtyard right now?"
And guess who just walked in? Haman. He was coming to the outer court to ask the king to hang Mordecai on the gallows he'd just built for him. Talk about awkward timing.
The servants go, "Yeah, Haman's out there waiting."
"Send him in," the king says.
When Haman comes in, the king asks him, "Hey, what should I do for someone I really, really want to honor?"

Haman's thinking to himself, "OMG, he's talking about me! Who else could it be?" So he goes all out and says, "For the guy the king wants to honor, you should totally do this: Get a royal robe the king himself has worn, and a horse the king has ridden, one with a royal crown on its head. Then, have one of the most noble princes put the robe on the guy, lead him on the horse through the main city square, and shout, 'This is what happens when the king wants to honor someone!'"

"Great idea!" the king says to Haman. "Go do that. Right now. Take the robe and the horse and do everything you just said for Mordecai the Jew, the one who hangs out at the King's Gate. And don't you dare skip a single detail."

So Haman had to take the robe and horse, dress up Mordecai, and lead him through the city square, yelling, "This is what is done for the man whom the king especially wants to honor!" The ultimate humiliation.

After the parade, Mordecai just went back to his post at the King's Gate like it was no big deal. But Haman? He sprinted home, completely mortified, hiding his face in shame. He told his wife Zeresh and all his friends what happened, and they were like, "Dude, if this Mordecai guy is a Jew, you're toast. Your bad luck is just getting started. You have zero chance against him—you're basically ruined."
And while they were still talking, the king's guys showed up to rush Haman to the dinner Esther had prepared. It was all happening so fast.

Esther.title: Haman's Epic Fail at the Dinner Party
paragraphs: So, the king and Haman rolled up to Queen Esther's dinner party. During the second dinner, while they were sipping on some wine, the king asked again, “Queen Esther, for real, what do you want? I'll give you half of my kingdom! Just say the word, and it's yours.”
Queen Esther answered, “If you're really cool with me, O King, and if you're down, please spare my life, and spare my people's lives.

“We've been sold out, me and my people, to be totally destroyed—like, massacred and eliminated. If we were just being sold as slaves, I wouldn't have even brought it up; our problems wouldn't have been a big enough deal to bother you with.”
King Xerxes totally lost it and was like, “Who? Where is this guy? This is messed up!”
“An enemy. A hater. This evil Haman,” said Esther.
Haman was shook, standing there in front of the king and queen.
The king was so mad he left his wine and stormed out into the palace garden.

Haman stayed behind, begging Queen Esther for his life—he knew the king was done with him and that he was toast. Just as the king was coming back from the garden into the banquet hall, Haman was basically throwing himself on the couch where Esther was chilling. The king yelled, “Are you seriously going to assault the queen while I'm right here?!”
The second the king said that, Haman went pale.

Harbona, one of the guys who worked for the king, spoke up: “Yo, check it out! There’s that huge gallows that Haman built for Mordecai, the guy who saved the king’s life. It’s right next to Haman’s house—like, 75 feet tall!”
The king said, “Hang him on it!”
So they hanged Haman on the very gallows he had built for Mordecai. And the king finally chilled out.

Esther.title: The Tables Have Turned: Payback Time!
paragraphs: On the very same day, King Xerxes handed over all of Haman's property to Queen Esther—you know, the guy who was the biggest hater of the Jewish people. And then Mordecai got to come before the king, because Esther finally told him that they were family. The king took off his special signet ring, the one he'd taken back from Haman, and gave it straight to Mordecai. To top it off, Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's entire estate. Talk about a major glow-up.

But Esther wasn't finished. She went back to the king, fell at his feet, and was literally in tears, begging him to undo the evil plan Haman had cooked up to destroy the Jews. The king held out his golden scepter to her, so she stood up and said, “Look, if you’re cool with it, and if you actually care about me and think this is the right thing to do, please, can you send out an official order to cancel Haman's plan to annihilate the Jews everywhere? I seriously can't handle watching my people get wiped out. How can I just stand by and see my own relatives get massacred?”

King Xerxes told Queen Esther and Mordecai the Jew, “Look, I’ve already given Haman’s estate to Esther, and he’s been executed because he tried to mess with the Jews. So now, you guys can write a new order for the Jews, whatever you think is best. Then seal it with my ring.” (Anything written in the king’s name and sealed with his ring was legit and couldn't be taken back.)

So on the 23rd day of the third month, Sivan, the king’s secretaries were called in. A new order was written exactly as Mordecai dictated. It was sent out to all the satraps, governors, and officials of the 127 provinces from India all the way to Ethiopia. They wrote it in each province's own script and language, and of course, for the Jews in their own script and language too.

He wrote it all under King Xerxes' name and sealed it with the royal signet ring. Then he sent out the official notices by messengers on super-fast horses, the best of the best from the king's own stables.

The king's new order gave the Jews in every city the green light to arm themselves and fight back. They could defend themselves to the death, kill anyone who threatened them, their women, or their children, and they could even take all the stuff their enemies owned. The day this was all supposed to go down was the 13th day of the twelfth month, Adar. The order was posted publicly in every province so everyone knew what was up, and the Jews could get ready to get their revenge on their enemies.
The messengers, hyped up by the king's command, took off on their royal horses like it was a race. At the same time, the new rule was posted all over the palace in Susa.

Mordecai walked out of the king's presence looking like a total boss in a royal robe of violet and white, a massive gold crown, and a fancy purple cape. The whole city of Susa just erupted with joy. For the Jews, it was a time for celebration, laughter, and being honored. It was like that everywhere, in every province and city where the king's order was announced. The Jews were partying in the streets, cheering and feasting. And get this—a lot of non-Jews even converted and became Jews, because suddenly it was pretty dangerous *not* to be one.

Esther.title: The Ultimate Payback: Purim Origin Story
paragraphs: On December 13th, the day the king's order was supposed to go live, everything got flipped. This was the day the Jews' enemies were planning to totally own them, but the tables turned, big time. The Jews ended up owning the people who hated them.

The Jews gathered in their cities all over King Xerxes' kingdom to take down anyone who was trying to ruin them. Literally no one could stand up to them—they were all shook. On top of that, all the government officials, the satraps, the governors—basically everyone working for the king—were lowkey helping the Jews because they were scared of Mordecai. By this point, Mordecai was a major player in the palace, and his reputation was growing everywhere.

So, the Jews absolutely wrecked their enemies with swords, just a complete slaughter, and did whatever they wanted to the people who hated them. In the capital city of Susa, the Jews took out five hundred men. They also killed the ten sons of Haman, the Jews' number one hater: Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha.

But here's the thing: they didn't take any of their stuff. That day, after it was all over, the king got the final body count from the capital. The king said to Queen Esther, "Just in Susa alone, the Jews have killed five hundred men, plus Haman's ten sons. It's wild to think about the numbers in the rest of the kingdom! So, what else do you want? Just say the word, and it's yours. Your wish is my command."

Queen Esther replied, "If it's cool with you, King, could you give the Jews in Susa permission to keep this going for one more day? Oh, and also, hang the bodies of Haman's ten sons on the gallows for everyone to see."
The king commanded it. The order was extended, and the bodies of Haman's ten sons were hung up in public.
The Jews in Susa went back at it. On the 14th of Adar, they killed another three hundred men in Susa. But again, they didn't take any loot.

Meanwhile, in the rest of the king's provinces, the Jews had teamed up to defend themselves and break free from their oppressors. On the 13th of Adar, they killed seventy-five thousand of their haters but, again, didn't take any of their stuff. The next day, the 14th, they chilled and had a huge party with tons of food and laughs. But in Susa, since the Jews had been fighting on both the 13th and 14th, they made the 15th their day to party. (This is why Jews who live out in the country celebrate on the 14th of Adar, making it a day for parties and giving gifts.)

Mordecai wrote all this down and sent letters to all the Jews in King Xerxes' provinces, no matter how far away. He told them to celebrate the 14th and 15th of Adar every year. This was to remember when the Jews got a break from their enemies, the month their sadness turned into joy, and their mourning turned into a holiday for parties, fun, laughter, and exchanging presents and giving gifts to the poor.
And they actually did it. What started then became a tradition, just like Mordecai had written to them.

Haman, son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the ultimate enemy of all Jews, had schemed to wipe them all out. He had cast the 'pur' (which means 'lot') to freak them out and destroy them. But when Queen Esther stepped in and talked to the king, he issued a written order that Haman's evil plan should totally backfire on him. He and his sons were hanged on the gallows. That's why these days are called 'Purim,' from the word 'pur' or 'lot.'

So, because of everything written in this letter and everything they had gone through, the Jews agreed to keep it going. It became a tradition for them, their kids, and anyone who joined them later to remember these two days every year on the exact dates written in the letter. These days are meant to be remembered and celebrated by every generation, every family, every province, and every city. These days of Purim must never be forgotten by the Jews; the memory of them must never fade away.

Esther.title: Mordecai's Epic Glow-Up
paragraphs: King Xerxes was basically taxing his entire empire, from one end to the other. And all the other stuff about his reign, like all his big achievements and the full story of Mordecai's glow-up after the king promoted him—it's all written down in the official history books of the kings of Media and Persia.

So yeah, Mordecai the Jew was basically the king's right-hand man, second only to King Xerxes himself. He was super popular with the Jewish people and they all looked up to him. He always worked hard for his people's best interests and made sure they were safe and thriving.

Job.title: Job's Life Goes From GOATED to Gutted... But He Keeps the Faith
paragraphs: So, there was this guy named Job who lived in a place called Uz. He was, like, a genuinely good dude—super honest, always kept his word, was all-in for God, and absolutely hated seeing bad stuff happen. He had a big family: seven sons and three daughters. And get this—he was loaded. We're talking 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 teams of oxen, 500 donkeys, and a ton of servants. Basically, he was the biggest deal in the entire East.

His sons were all about that party life. They'd take turns throwing these huge feasts at their houses and would always make sure their three sisters were there to hang out. After each round of parties, their dad, Job, would get up super early and offer a sacrifice for each of his kids. He was always thinking, "What if one of my kids messed up and secretly dissed God in their heart?" So, he made this a regular thing, just in case they'd sinned.
Then one day, all the angels went to check in with God, and Satan, who's basically the head accuser, tagged along. God called out Satan specifically, like, "So, what've you been up to?"
Satan shot back, "Just cruising around, you know, checking out what's happening on Earth."
God was like, "Oh yeah? Did you happen to see my boy Job? There's literally no one like him. He's the real deal—honest, a man of his word, totally devoted to me, and hates evil."

Satan just scoffed. "You really think he's that good for nothing? C'mon. The guy has it made! You treat him like a spoiled pet, making sure nothing ever goes wrong for him, his family, or any of his stuff. You bless everything he touches—he literally can't fail.
"But I bet if you actually took away all his stuff, he'd curse you straight to your face. Just watch."
God was like, "Alright, bet. You can do whatever you want with his things. Just don't lay a hand on him." And with that, Satan bounced from God's presence.

Not long after, while Job's kids were partying it up at the oldest brother's house, a messenger sprinted up to Job and said, "We were out in the field, the oxen were plowing and the donkeys were just chilling, when these Sabean raiders attacked! They jacked all the animals and killed all the workers. I'm the only one who made it out to tell you."

Before he could even finish, another messenger ran up, totally out of breath, and said, "Lightning just came out of nowhere and completely fried the sheep and the shepherds. They're all toast. I'm the only one who escaped to tell you."

And while HE was still talking, a third guy showed up and said, "A bunch of Chaldean raiders came at us from three different directions, stole all the camels, and killed all the drivers. I'm the only one who got away to tell you."

And if that wasn't enough, while that guy was still talking, a fourth messenger arrived, saying, "Your kids were all hanging out at your oldest son's place when a massive tornado just ripped in from the desert and wrecked the house. It collapsed right on top of them, and they're all… gone. I'm the only one who survived to tell you what happened."
Job just stood up, tore his robe, and shaved his head. Then he fell to the ground and just started worshiping, saying:
"I came into this world with nothing, and I'll leave with nothing. God gives, and God takes away. But God's name is still the GOAT."
Through all of this absolute chaos, Job didn't sin. Not once did he point a finger and blame God.

Job.title: Job's Ultimate Test: Round 2
paragraphs: So, one day, all the angels were reporting back to God, and guess who decided to show up again? Satan.
God immediately called him out, like, "And what have you been up to?"
Satan shot back, "Oh, you know, just cruising around, checking things out on earth."

Then God was like, "So, have you seen my boy Job? There's literally no one like him. He's honest, keeps his word, is totally devoted to me, and hates doing wrong. He's still holding on strong, even after you tried to get me to ruin him for no reason. Nice try, though."
Satan replied, "Yeah, but a person will give up anything just to save their own skin. What if you actually hurt him? Like, messed with his health? I bet he'd curse you to your face, for real."
God said, "Fine. Do whatever you want to him. Just don't kill him."

So Satan left God's presence and hit Job with some gnarly sores. Job was covered in painful ulcers and scabs from head to toe. They were so itchy and gross that he grabbed a piece of a broken pot to scrape himself and went to go sit in a pile of ashes on the trash heap.
His wife came to him and said, "Are you seriously still trying to be Mr. Perfect? Just curse God and let's be done with this!"
He told her, "You're talking like a fool. We take all the good stuff from God, why shouldn't we take the bad stuff too?"
And through all of this, Job didn't sin. He didn't say a single bad thing about God.

When Job's three best friends heard about all the terrible things that had happened to him, they decided to come and support him. Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar all traveled from their hometowns to comfort him. But when they saw him, they couldn't even recognize him. It was wild. They started wailing, tore their clothes, and threw dirt on their heads to show how sad they were. Then they just sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights without saying a word. They could see how completely wrecked he was and how much pain he was in.

Job.title: Job's Epic Rant About His Life
paragraphs: Then Job finally broke the silence and started cursing the day he was born.

“Just delete the day I was born. Erase the night I was conceived! Let it be a total black hole. May God just forget it ever happened. Wipe it from the history books! May my birthday be buried in deep darkness, covered by fog, and swallowed by the night. And the night I was conceived—let the devil take it! Rip that date off the calendar, delete it from every record. Oh, turn that night into pure nothingness—no happy sounds from that night, ever! Let the professional cursers curse that day. Unleash the sea monster, Leviathan, on it. May its morning stars turn black, waiting for a daylight that never shows up, never even seeing the first light of dawn. And why? Because it let me be born from my mother’s womb into a life with this much trouble.

“Why couldn’t I have just died at birth, my first breath being my last? Why were there arms to rock me and a chest to feed me? I could be chilling in peace right now, asleep forever, feeling no pain. I'd be with kings and politicians in their fancy tombs, or with princes surrounded by their gold and silver. Why wasn't I a stillborn baby, buried with all the others who never saw the light of day? A place where the wicked can't bother anyone and tired people finally get to rest. Prisoners sleep without being disturbed, never having to hear a guard yell again. The small and the great are all the same there, and slaves are finally free from their masters.

“Why does God even bother giving light to miserable people? Why keep bitter people alive? People who desperately want to die but can't, who think death is the best thing they could imagine. They'd consider the day they die and get buried the happiest day of their lives. What's the point of life when it makes no sense, when God has blocked every path to meaning?

“Instead of food, I get groans for dinner, and then I just vomit up my pain. My worst nightmare has literally come true; what I was most afraid of has happened. My peace is gone, my quiet is destroyed. There's no rest for me, ever—it feels like death has taken over my life.”

Job.title: Your Friend's Advice is... BRUTAL
paragraphs: Then Eliphaz from Teman spoke up:

“Yo, Job, mind if I say something? It’s kinda hard to stay quiet seeing all this. You’ve been the one dishing out advice, helping people see things clearly, and encouraging everyone who was about to quit. Your words have literally put stumbling people back on their feet and given hope to those about to collapse. But now you’re the one in deep trouble, and you’re totally bugging out. You got hit hard and you're reeling from it. But shouldn’t your faith give you some confidence now? Shouldn’t your good-guy life give you some hope?

“Think about it. Has a truly innocent person ever gotten completely wrecked? Do genuinely good people ever really lose in the end? From what I’ve seen, those who stir up trouble and plant seeds of evil get it all back in the end. One breath from God and they’re gone, one blast of his anger and there’s nothing left. The lion might be the king of the jungle, but if he loses his teeth, he’s useless. No teeth, no food, and his cubs are left to fend for themselves.

“I got this secret message, like a whisper, but I heard it crystal clear. It came in a wild dream one night when I was deep asleep. I was hit with this insane dread and terror. I was literally scared to death, shaking from head to toe. A spirit glided right in front of me—the hair on my head stood straight up. I couldn’t even tell what it was, just a blur… and then I heard this muffled voice:

“‘How can a regular person be more righteous than God? How can a human be purer than their own Creator? Look, God doesn’t even fully trust his own servants or give his angels a free pass. So how much less us, who are just made of dust and as fragile as moths? Our bodies are here today and gone tomorrow, and no one even notices—gone without a trace. When the tent stakes of our life are pulled up, the whole thing collapses—we die without ever getting any wiser.’”

Job.title: Why Bad Things Happen & How to Deal
paragraphs: “Go ahead, Job, call for help if you think anyone’s gonna answer. Which of the holy angels are you gonna hit up? A fool’s hot temper is what gets them in the end, and an idiot’s jealousy is basically a self-destruct button. I’ve seen it myself—I’ve seen fools putting down roots, looking all successful, and then boom, their whole setup is cursed. Their kids are left out in the cold, getting used and abused, with nobody to have their back. Random hungry people just roll up and steal their harvest, taking everything, even the thorny parts. They’re just insatiable for everything they own. Don’t blame fate when things go wrong—trouble doesn’t just appear out of thin air. It’s a human thing. Mortals are born for trouble, as sure as sparks fly up from a fire.

“If I were in your shoes, I’d go straight to God. I’d just throw myself on His mercy. I mean, He’s famous for doing awesome and unexpected stuff; His surprises are endless. For example, He sends rain all over the earth, watering the fields. He lifts up the people who are down and out and gives a solid footing to those who are drowning in sadness. He totally wrecks the plans of sneaky crooks, so none of their plots ever work out. He catches the know-it-alls in their own traps—all their complicated schemes get tossed in the trash. Suddenly they’re all confused, like they’re in total darkness; they can’t even see to walk straight. But God saves the oppressed from all the deadly plots and from the iron fist of the powerful. And that’s why the poor keep on hoping, while injustice gets shut down.

“So, it’s lowkey a blessing when God steps in and corrects you. For real, don’t hate on the discipline of Almighty God! It’s true, He wounds, but He also bandages the wound; the same hand that hurts you is the one that heals you. He’ll rescue you from one disaster after another; no matter what crazy thing happens, the evil can’t even touch you.

“When there’s a famine, He’ll keep you from starving. In a war, He’ll keep you from getting taken out by a sword. You’ll be protected from vicious gossip and you’ll be fearless through any catastrophe. You’ll just shrug off disaster and famine, and walk fearlessly among wild animals. You’ll be on good terms with the rocks and mountains; wild animals will become your friends. You’ll know that your place on earth is safe; you’ll check on all your stuff and find nothing missing. You’ll get to see your children grow up, your family as lovely and graceful as a field of green grass. You’ll live a long, good life and die at a ripe old age, like golden grain ready for harvest.
“Yeah, this is how it is—my word of honor. Take it to heart and you won’t go wrong.”

Job.title: Job Claps Back: My Suffering is Heavier Than All The Sand
paragraphs: Job answered:

“If you could actually weigh all my misery, if you could pile up this whole disaster on a scale, it would be heavier than all the sand in the sea! So is it any wonder I’m screaming like a cornered animal? God Almighty’s arrows are stuck in me, they’re poison arrows, and I’m poisoned through and through. God has just dumped his entire wrath on me. Donkeys and cows make noise when they run out of food—so don’t expect me to stay quiet through this. Do you see what God has served me? It’s enough to make anyone’s stomach turn. Everything inside me is repulsed by it—it makes me sick.

“All I want is for one prayer to be answered, a final request: let God just step on me—squash me like a bug, and be done with me for good. At least I’d have the satisfaction of knowing I didn’t blaspheme the Holy God, before being pushed past my breaking point. Where’s the strength to keep my hopes up? What future do I have to keep me going? Do you think I have nerves of steel? Do you think I’m made of iron? Do you think I can just fix this myself? Bro, I don’t even have the tools to start!

“When desperate people give up on God Almighty, their friends, at least, should stick with them. But you guys, my 'brothers,' are as unreliable as a desert stream—one day you’re overflowing with water from melting snow, but by summer you’re completely bone-dry, just a baked gully in the sun. Travelers who see you from a distance and detour for a drink end up in a waterless ditch and die of thirst. Merchant caravans from Tema see you and expect water, tourists from Sheba hope for a cool drink. They show up so confident—but what a letdown! They get there, and their faces just fall. And you, my so-called friends, are just like that—you’re useless! You take one look at a tough situation and you shrink back in fear. It’s not like I asked you for anything—I didn’t ask you for a single dime. Nor did I beg you to risk your necks for me. So why are you being so shady and evasive?

“Just hit me with the truth and I’ll shut up. Show me where I went wrong. Honest words never hurt, but what’s the point of all your preachy nonsense? You act like you're correcting me, but you treat my words of pure agony like they're just hot air. Are people just objects to you? Are friends just another item on your balance sheet?

“Look me in the eyes! Do you really think I’d lie to your face? Think about it—no more double-talk. Think carefully—my integrity is on the line here! Can you find anything fake in what I’m saying? Don’t you trust me to know the difference between right and wrong?”

Job.title: God, Just Let Me BREATHE
paragraphs: “Isn’t life just one big struggle? Like, we’re all sentenced to a life of hard work. It’s like being a field hand just waiting for the day to be over, or some worker who’s only got payday to look forward to. That’s my life right now, just pointless months and miserable nights. I go to bed thinking, ‘When is it morning already?’ I just toss and turn all night, and I’m so over it. I’m literally covered in gross stuff, my skin’s all messed up and nasty. My days are flying by faster than someone speed-knitting, and then suddenly the yarn’s gone—my life’s unfinished.

“God, seriously, don’t forget I’m just... temporary. Like a puff of smoke. My eyes have seen the last good thing they’re ever gonna see. And you’ve seen the last of me. Even as you’re looking, I’m fading away. Like a cloud that just disappears, people who die don’t come back. They don’t visit their families, their friends don’t just drop by for a chat anymore.

“So yeah, I’m not holding back. I’m putting it all out there. My complaining is bitter, but it’s real. Are you gonna try and shut me up, like you do with the sea and the storms? If I think, ‘Maybe if I just go to sleep, I’ll feel better,’ you just send me nightmares and freak me out with ghosts. Honestly, I’d rather just suffocate than keep living like this. I hate my life! Who needs this? Just leave me alone! My life is nothing, just smoke.

“Like, what even are humans that you care so much? That you even give us the time of day? You check on us every single morning, like ‘how’s it going down there?’ Just give me a break, will you? Can’t you let me even spit in peace? And even if I did sin, how does that even affect you? You’re in charge of everyone. Don’t you have better things to do than to pick on me? Why are you making such a big deal out of me? Why not just forgive me and let’s start over? At this rate, I’ll be dead soon. You’ll look for me, but I’ll be gone.”

Job.title: God Doesn't Mess Up, Bro
paragraphs: Bildad from Shuhah had to jump in next:

"Bro, how can you keep talking like that? You're just spouting nonsense, and it's loud nonsense too. You think God messes up? That the Almighty ever gets things backward? It's lowkey obvious your kids sinned against him—why else would God have punished them? So here's the move—and don't sleep on it: get on your knees and pray to God Almighty. If you're as innocent and good as you say you are, it's not too late. He'll pull up, make everything right again, and restore your life. Even though you're not doing so hot right now, you'll end up better than ever.

"Go ask your ancestors, for real. Study what they learned from their own ancestors. 'Cause we're new to this, with a lot to learn and not much time to learn it. So why not let the old-timers teach you, tell you what's real, and give you the wisdom they got from experience? Can huge pine trees grow without any dirt? Can you get juicy tomatoes without any water? Flowers look pretty before you pick them, but without soil or water, they die faster than grass. That's exactly what happens to people who forget God—all their dreams just crash and burn. They're basically hanging on by a single thread, trusting a spider web to save them. One little shake and the thread snaps, one poke and the whole web is gone. Or they're like weeds that pop up in the sun, taking over the whole garden, choking out the flowers, and even growing in the rocks. But when the gardener yanks them out, the garden doesn't even notice they're gone. The sooner the godless are out of the picture, the better, so that good things can grow in their place.

"There's no way God would ever ditch a good person, and no way he'd ever help a bad one. God's gonna let you laugh again; you'll be shouting with so much joy, while your enemies are totally owned, their whole world collapsing like a house of cards."

Job.title: God's on a Power Trip & I Can't Even
paragraphs: Job just kept going:

“Seriously, what else is new? I already know all this. The real question is, how can a regular person ever get on the right side of God? If we wanted to take him to court, we wouldn't have a shot—not even one in a thousand. God's wisdom is, like, crazy deep and his power is insane. Who could go up against him and come out okay? He moves mountains before they even know what hit them, just flips them upside down whenever he wants. He shakes the whole planet, rattling it to its core. He can tell the sun not to shine, and it listens. He literally puts the stars on lockdown. He stretched out the heavens all by himself and walks on the ocean waves. He's the one who designed the Big Dipper, Orion, the Pleiades, and all those stars in the southern sky. We can't even begin to get our heads around the awesome things he does; his miracles are just one surprise after another. It's wild because he can move right past me, and I don't even see him. He's working, quiet and steady, and I totally miss it. If he decides to take something from you, who's gonna stop him? Who's gonna be like, ‘Hey, what do you think you're doing?’ God doesn't pull his punches with his anger; even mythical monsters are terrified of him.

“So how could I possibly argue with him? How could I build a case that would actually get through to God? Even if I was completely innocent, I could never prove it. All I can do is beg the Judge for mercy. If I called out to God and he actually answered, that's the only way I'd believe he heard me. But right now, it feels like he's just messing with me, beating me up for no reason at all. He won't even let me catch my breath; it's just one bitter thing after another. If it's a contest of strength, he wins, no question. If it's about justice, who's gonna serve him a subpoena? Even if I'm innocent, anything I say just makes me look guilty. The more I defend myself, the worse I sound, even though I'm blameless.

“So how could I possibly argue with him? How could I build a case that would actually get through to God? Even if I was completely innocent, I could never prove it. All I can do is beg the Judge for mercy. If I called out to God and he actually answered, that's the only way I'd believe he heard me. But right now, it feels like he's just messing with me, beating me up for no reason at all. He won't even let me catch my breath; it's just one bitter thing after another. If it's a contest of strength, he wins, no question. If it's about justice, who's gonna serve him a subpoena? Even if I'm innocent, anything I say just makes me look guilty. The more I defend myself, the worse I sound, even though I'm blameless.

“Honestly, I know I'm blameless. I just don't get what’s happening. I'm so over my life. It feels like it doesn't matter if you're good or bad, it all ends the same. So I've gotta conclude that God just destroys good people right along with the bad ones. When some disaster hits and people die suddenly, he just folds his arms, like he's not even bothered by innocent people suffering. He lets messed-up people run the world and puts judges in charge who don't know right from wrong. If he's not the one doing it, then who is?

“My time is running out—what's left of my life is flying by so fast I can't even see any good in it. My life is like a speedboat at full throttle, or an eagle diving for its prey. Even if I try to just forget about it, put on a happy face, and force a smile, all this pain would still be twisting my gut because it's obvious you're not going to give me a break. The verdict is already in—‘Guilty!’—so what's the point of fighting it? Even if I scrubbed myself clean with the strongest soap out there, it wouldn't matter. You'd just shove me into a mud pit or something worse, and I'd stink so bad nobody could be near me.

“My time is running out—what's left of my life is flying by so fast I can't even see any good in it. My life is like a speedboat at full throttle, or an eagle diving for its prey. Even if I try to just forget about it, put on a happy face, and force a smile, all this pain would still be twisting my gut because it's obvious you're not going to give me a break. The verdict is already in—‘Guilty!’—so what's the point of fighting it? Even if I scrubbed myself clean with the strongest soap out there, it wouldn't matter. You'd just shove me into a mud pit or something worse, and I'd stink so bad nobody could be near me.

“God and I are not on the same level; I can't just sue him. We're never gonna be equals in a courtroom. Man, I wish there was a referee who could step in and help me get my life back on track—someone who could make God loosen his death grip on me, free me from this terror so I could just breathe. Then I'd speak my mind and tell him what's up, no holding back. But as it is now, there's just no way.”

Man, I wish there was a referee who could step in and help me get my life back on track—someone who could make God loosen his death grip on me, free me from this terror so I could just breathe. Then I'd speak my mind and tell him what's up, no holding back. But as it is now, there's just no way.”

Job.title: God, a few questions for you...
paragraphs: I'm so over my life, I seriously hate it. I'm just gonna lay it all out, all the bitter stuff, no holding back.
Job prayed:

'Okay, God, here's the deal. Don't just call me guilty without telling me what I supposedly did. How is this 'good'? You're giving me a hard time, rejecting me—the person you made with your own hands—and then you're blessing the plans of messed-up people? You don't see things like we do. You're not fooled by how things look, right? You're not on a deadline like us. You have forever to figure things out. So what's the deal with trying to dig up dirt on me, trying to find something wrong? You know I'm not guilty. And you know no one can save me.

'You made me like a custom work of art, and now you're just going to smash me? Don't you remember how carefully you made me? Are you really going to turn me back into a pile of mud? That whole miracle of life thing, mixing everything together to make me—skin, bones, muscles, and a brain! You gave me life and so much love. You watched over every single breath I took.

'You made me like a custom work of art, and now you're just going to smash me? Don't you remember how carefully you made me? Are you really going to turn me back into a pile of mud? That whole miracle of life thing, mixing everything together to make me—skin, bones, muscles, and a brain! You gave me life and so much love. You watched over every single breath I took.

'But you never told me about this part. I should've known there was a catch. Like, if I messed up even a little, you'd be on me, and wouldn't let it slide. If I'm actually guilty, I'm screwed. But even if I'm innocent, it's no better—I'm still screwed. I'm just full of bitterness. I'm drowning in this mess. I try to stay positive, to be brave, but you're just too much for me, like a lion that won't give up. You keep bringing new witnesses against me. Your anger just keeps growing, and you keep piling on the pain and sadness!

'So why did you even let me be born? I wish no one had ever seen me! I wish I'd never even existed—just a stillborn, buried without ever taking a breath. Isn't it time to just end my life? Can't you just let me be happy for a second before I die and get buried, before I'm stuck in a coffin, sealed in the ground, and sent away forever to the land of the dead, blind in the total darkness?'
