You think you’re so tough—strutting around all high and mighty, living in your fortress in the rocks, acting like you're king of the hill. You think you’re untouchable, right? Like an eagle in its nest? Well, you’re about to get knocked down. I’ll bring you crashing to the ground.” God’s decree.
“Edom will end up as straight-up garbage. Disgusting, nasty trash. A total train wreck. It’ll be just like Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors in the history books of failure.” God says so.
“No one will live there, not a single person will move in.

“Watch this: Like a lion creeping up from the Jordan jungle looking for a snack in the mountain pastures, I’ll jump Edom and pounce. I’ll take my pick of the flock—and who’s gonna stop me? The shepherds of Edom are helpless against me.”

“Watch this: Like a lion creeping up from the Jordan jungle looking for a snack in the mountain pastures, I’ll jump Edom and pounce. I’ll take my pick of the flock—and who’s gonna stop me? The shepherds of Edom are helpless against me.”
So, listen to the plan God has made against Edom, the blueprint he’s prepared for those who live in Teman:

“Believe it or not, even the young and weak—like little lambs and kids—will be dragged off. Believe it or not, the flock will be in shock, totally helpless, and just watch it happen. The whole earth will shake from their cries, cries of pain heard all the way at the Red Sea. Look! An eagle soars, swoops down, and spreads its wings over Bozrah. Even the toughest warriors will be doubled over in pain, totally helpless, like a woman giving birth.”
The message about Damascus:

“Hamath and Arpad will be shook when they hear the bad news. Their hearts will melt with fear as they pace around, worried sick. The color will drain from Damascus’s face as she tries to run. Panicking, she’ll fall apart, totally disabled, like a woman in labor. And now, how lonely—left behind, abandoned! The once-famous city, the once-happy city. Her bright young men are dead in the streets, her brave warriors silent as death. On that day”—decree of God-of-the-Angel-Armies—“I’m gonna light up the walls of Damascus and burn down all of Ben-hadad’s forts.”
The message about Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor that were attacked by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. This is God’s message:

“Get up! Attack Kedar! Go plunder the nomads from the east. Grab their blankets and pots and pans. Steal their camels. Freak them out, shouting, ‘Terror! Death! Doom! Danger everywhere!’ Oh, run for your lives, you nomads from Hazor.” God’s decree. “Find a safe place to hide. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has plans to wipe you out, to come after you with a vengeance: ‘Get ‘em,’ he says. ‘Go after these chill nomads who live free and easy in the desert, who live out in the open with no doors to lock, who live by themselves.’ Their camels are free for the taking, their herds and flocks, easy grabs. I’ll scatter them to the four winds, these defenseless nomads on the edge of the desert. I’ll bring terror from every direction. They won’t know what hit them.” God’s decree. “Jackals will take over the camps of Hazor, camps abandoned to the wind and sand. No one will live there, not a single person will move in.”
God’s message to the prophet Jeremiah about Elam at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah. This is what God-of-the-Angel-Armies says:

“Watch this! I’ll snap Elam’s bow, their favorite weapon, right over my knee. Then I’ll unleash four winds on Elam, winds from the four corners of the earth. I’ll blow them away in all directions, and homeless Elamites will end up in every country on earth. They’ll live in constant fear and terror among enemies who want to kill them. I’ll bring disaster on them, my anger-fueled disaster. I’ll send killer dogs after them until there’s nothing left. And then I’ll set up my throne in Elam, after kicking out their king and his cronies. But the time will come when I’ll make everything right for Elam again.” God’s decree.

Jeremiah.title: Babylon's Epic Fail
paragraphs: This is the tea God spilled through the prophet Jeremiah about Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans:

“Alright, listen up, world! Tell everyone, shout it from the rooftops: Babylon is DONE. Their god Bel is so embarrassed, and Marduk is exposed as a total fake. All their little statues are cringing, and their fake gods are looking like cheap knock-offs. Because a nation from the north is gonna roll up and wreck their cities. It's gonna be a ghost town—no people, no animals, not a single sound.

“When that day comes,” God says, “the people of Israel and Judah are gonna come back together. They’ll be crying, but they’ll be looking for me, their God. They’ll ask for the way to Zion and head straight there. They’re gonna stick with God, making a forever-promise they’ll never forget.

“My people were like lost sheep. Their own shepherds messed them up and left them to wander in the mountains. They got so lost they forgot where home was. Anyone who found them just took advantage. Their enemies were like, ‘Whatever, it’s fine. They’re the ones who ditched God, the true home their ancestors trusted.’

“But now, you gotta bounce from Babylon, like, ASAP. Get out of that country. Don't just follow, be a leader. Lead the way home! You see what I'm doing? I'm gathering a whole squad of nations against Babylon. They're coming from the north to take it all. These armies don't play; they never leave empty-handed. Babylon is basically free real estate. All the looters are gonna eat good!” God declares.

“You Babylonians really lived it up, huh? You had a blast taking advantage of my people, like happy little calves in a field or wild horses having fun. Well, your mom wouldn't be proud. The one who gave birth to you would be disappointed. Look at you now! You're a nobody nation, just trash and weeds. My anger is gonna leave you totally empty, a lifeless desert. Anyone who passes by will be shook, like, ‘Wow, what a glow-down.’ So, gang up on Babylon! Surround her! Unleash everything you've got. Don't hold back. Take her down. She messed up big time, against me! Let out a battle cry from all sides. She's got no fight left. Her defenses are toast, her walls are smashed. This is ‘Operation: God’s Payback.’ Get that revenge. Do to her what she did to others. Give her a taste of her own medicine! Wreck her farms, get rid of her farmers, and empty her barns. And for all you prisoners, while it's all going down, get out of there. Run for your lives and go home.
“Israel is like a scattered flock of sheep, hunted by lions. The king of Assyria started it, and then King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon finished the job, leaving nothing but bones.”

And now, the God of Angel Armies, the God of Israel, says this: “Watch out. I’m about to bring the same level of doom on the king of Babylon and his country that I brought on the king of Assyria. But I’ll bring Israel back home to good pastures. They’ll chill on the hills of Carmel and Bashan, and on the slopes of Ephraim and Gilead. They’ll eat until they’re totally full. When that time comes,” God says, “people will search for any dirt on Israel, but they won’t find a thing. They’ll look for any of Judah’s sins, but nothing. The people I saved will have a totally clean slate.
“Attack Merathaim, the land of rebels! Go after Pekod, the country of doom! Hunt them down and wipe them out,” God decrees. “These are my orders. Do exactly what I say.

“The sound of battle is shaking everything! The big bad ‘Hammer’ just got hammered, totally smashed. Babylon is wrecked beyond recognition. I set a trap for you, Babylon, and you walked right into it. You had no idea what was coming. Now you’re caught. That’s what you get for trying to fight God.

“I, God, opened up my armory. I brought out my weapons of anger. The Master, the God of Angel Armies, has a job to do in Babylon. Attack it from every angle! Break into their storage! Pile everything up and burn it. Leave nothing and no one! Get rid of all their young fighters. It’s their doomsday! Their time is up. And get this: the people who escape from Babylon will show up in Zion and tell everyone how God got his revenge, especially for his Temple.

“Send all the troops against Babylon, anyone who’s a good shot! Trap them completely, no escape routes! Pay her back for everything she did. Give her a taste of her own medicine! She was so arrogant and disrespectful to God, the Holy One of Israel. So now it’s payback time: her young men will be found dead in the streets, and all her soldiers will be silenced forever,” God decrees.

“You getting this, Mr. Pride? I’m coming for you!” says the Master, the God of Angel Armies. “Your time is up. It’s your doomsday. Mr. Pride is gonna fall flat on his face, and no one’s gonna help him up. I’m gonna set his towns on fire, and it’s gonna spread everywhere.”
And here’s more from the God of Angel Armies:

“The people of Israel and Judah are both oppressed. Their enemies have them in a death grip and won’t let go. But their Rescuer is strong: the God of Angel Armies. I’m gonna step in and save them. I’ll bring peace to their land, but for the people of Babylon, it’s gonna get rough.

“It’s an all-out war in Babylon,” God says. “A total war on its people, its leaders, and its so-called wise men! War on its fake prophets—they’re all fools! War on its soldiers—they’re all cowards! War on its hired fighters—they’re useless! War on its banks—they’re getting looted! War on its water—it’s drying up! This land of fake gods has gone nuts—just a bunch of creepy goblins! The whole place will be taken over by wild animals and creepy crawlies. No one will ever live there again. It’ll smell like death. It’s gonna be like Sodom and Gomorrah, those cities I completely destroyed,” God says. “No one will ever live there again. No one will even breathe the air in that land, ever.

“And now, check this out! A huge crowd is coming from the north, a massive army of kings from all over the world. They’ve got deadly weapons, and they’re savage and cruel. They roar like the ocean, riding on powerful horses, all lined up and ready to fight you, Babylon! The king of Babylon hears they’re coming and gets so scared he can’t even move. He’s terrified, doubled over in pain like a woman giving birth.

“And watch this: like a lion coming out of the jungle to hunt in the mountains, I’m gonna show up and attack. I’ll take whoever I want from the flock, and who’s gonna stop me? All those so-called shepherds are completely powerless against me.”
So, listen up. This is God’s master plan against Babylon, the blueprint for what he’s gonna do to Chaldea:

Believe it or not, even the weakest, most vulnerable ones—like little lambs—will be dragged away. And the rest of the flock will just watch in shock, totally helpless. When everyone shouts, “Babylon is down!” the whole world will feel it. The news will spread everywhere.

Jeremiah.title: Babylon's Epic Takedown
paragraphs: Alright, there's more. God's dropping another truth bomb:

"Yo, watch this. I'm about to unleash a crazy destructive hurricane on Babylon—let's call it 'Hurricane Persia'—against everyone living in that messed-up place. I'm sending in a cosmic cleanup crew, and they're gonna scrub Babylon clean. Seriously, when they're done, there'll be nothing left worth mentioning. They won't miss a single thing. It's the final, total Doomsday. Soldiers will go all out, no holding back. They're not sparing anyone or anything. It's the end of the line, a complete wipeout. Babylon's streets will be littered with wounded people, just piles of bodies. But guess what? It turns out Israel and Judah aren't left all alone. As their God, the God of Angel Armies, I'm still here, totally committed to them, even though their country was filled with sin against Israel's Holy God.

"Get out of Babylon, like, right now. Run for your lives, save yourselves! Don't stick around and get caught up in my revenge on her. I'm just paying her back for all her bad choices. Babylon was like this fancy gold cup I was holding, filled with my anger that made the whole world drunk. All the nations drank from it and went totally wild. Now Babylon herself is gonna stumble and fall, completely wasted. So tragic! Go find some healing ointment for her wounds. Who knows, maybe she can be fixed."

Babylon was like this fancy gold cup I was holding, filled with my anger that made the whole world drunk. All the nations drank from it and went totally wild. Now Babylon herself is gonna stumble and fall, completely wasted. So tragic! Go find some healing ointment for her wounds. Who knows, maybe she can be fixed."

"We tried our best, but she's a lost cause. Babylon is past the point of no return. Just leave her to her fate and go home. The judgment against her is gonna be massive, like a skyscraper-sized monument to my vengeance.
"God made everything right for us. Let's go! We've gotta tell everyone back in Zion the good news. Let's spill the tea on what our God did to fix things.

"Sharpen your arrows! Get your quivers full! God has hyped up the kings of the Medes, giving them a serious case of war fever. The mission: 'Destroy Babylon!' God is on the warpath, out to get revenge for his Temple. Give the signal to attack Babylon's walls. Post guards 24/7. Call for backup. Set up ambushes. God's gonna do exactly what he said he would to the people of Babylon. You guys have all the water and money you could ever want—but your time is up. Your lifeline's been cut."

With his power, he made the earth. His wisdom shaped the world. He's the master artist of the cosmos. When he thunders, rain pours down. He makes clouds soar, adds lightning to the storm for special effects, and unleashes the wind from his private stash. People who worship fake gods made of sticks look so dumb. The makers of these gods are just embarrassed by their own creations. Their gods are fakes, just dead pieces of wood—lame, tasteless jokes. They're nothing but smoke. When it clears, they're gone. But the God of Jacob is the real deal; he created the entire universe, and he gave special attention to Israel. His name? God-of-the-Angel-Armies!

God says, "You, Babylon, you're my hammer, my weapon of war. I'm gonna use you to smash godless nations and tear down kingdoms. I'll use you to wreck horse and rider, chariot and driver. I'll use you to take down man and woman, old man and boy. I'll use you to crush the young man and woman, the shepherd and his sheep. I'll use you to destroy the farmer and his oxen, and to take out governors and senators.
"Judeans, you're gonna see it all with your own eyes. I'll make Babylon and all the Chaldeans pay for the evil they did in Zion." That's a decree from God.

"I'm against you, Babylon, you 'Mount Destroyer,' you who wrecked the whole earth. I'm gonna reach out, grab you, and crush you until you're not a mountain anymore. I'll turn you into a gravel pit. No one will ever use your stones for important buildings again—no cornerstones, no foundation stones. You'll be nothing but gravel." That's God's decree.

"Raise a flag in the land, blow the trumpet for the nations. Get the nations ready for a holy war against her. Call the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz to fight. Appoint a commander, and bring in horses like a swarm of locusts! Get the nations ready for a holy war against her—the king of the Medes, his leaders, and all his people.

"The whole land is shaking in fear, terrified of my plans against Babylon. My plan is to turn Babylon into a lifeless wasteland, a total ghost town. Babylon's soldiers have just given up. They're hiding in caves like cowards who didn't even put up a fight. What a bunch of crybabies. Babylon's houses are on fire, its gates are busted. Messenger after messenger is running to the king of Babylon to tell him his city is totally done for. The river crossings are captured. Wildfires are burning through the swamps. Soldiers are deserting like crazy. I, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, told you this would happen: 'Daughter Babylon is like a threshing floor at harvest time. Soon, her own harvest will come, and the useless stuff will be blown away!'

People go way out of their way to avoid them. I'm gonna take down that glutton god, Bel, in Babylon. I'll make him puke up everything he swallowed. No more tourists will come to admire the 'wonders' of Babylon. The wonders are gone. Run for it, my people! Run and don't look back! Get out of this place while you still can, this place that's about to be torched by God's insane anger. Don't lose hope. Don't give up when you hear all the crazy rumors. One year it's this, the next it's that—rumors of violence and war. But trust me, the time is coming when I'll deal with Babylon's fake gods. I'll expose the whole country as a fraud, with dead bodies scattered everywhere. Heaven and earth, angels and people, will throw a massive victory party over Babylon when the avenging armies from the north come down on her." That's God's decree!

"Babylon has to fall—it's payback for all the people of Israel who died in the war. Babylonians will be killed because of all the killing they did. But you exiles who escaped being killed by Babylon, get out of there! Fast! Remember God, even though you're far from home. And don't forget Jerusalem."

"We've been so humiliated, mocked, and abused. We've been kicked around for so long we barely know who we are anymore. And we don't know what to think—our holy Temple, God's house, was desecrated by a bunch of strangers."

"Those massive walls of Babylon? They're gonna be completely flattened. And those huge city gates? They're gonna be set on fire. The harder you chase after this empty life, the less you have. All that ambition just turns to ashes."

Jeremiah the prophet gave a task to Seraiah, who was the son of Neriah and grandson of Mahseiah. This happened when Seraiah went with King Zedekiah of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of Zedekiah's reign. Seraiah was basically the trip coordinator.

Jeremiah had written down in a little book all the terrible things that were going to happen to Babylon. He told Seraiah, "When you get to Babylon, read this whole thing out loud in public. Read, 'You, O God, said you would destroy this place so that nothing could live here, not even people or animals—a total wasteland, an eternal nothing.'

"When you're done reading it, tie a rock to the book, throw it into the Euphrates River, and watch it sink. Then say, 'This is how Babylon will sink and never come back up after the disaster I'm bringing on her.'"

Jeremiah.title: The Final Days of Jerusalem: It Gets Real
paragraphs: So, this guy Zedekiah was 21 when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for 11 years. His mom was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah from a town called Libnah.
As far as God was concerned, Zedekiah was just another bad king, a total carbon copy of Jehoiakim.
Basically, all the terrible stuff that went down in Jerusalem and Judah was because God was just so angry. He pretty much turned his back on them as a final judgment.

Then Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. So, Nebuchadnezzar rolled up with his whole army. They set up camp and built siege ramps all around Jerusalem, completely sealing it off. This all started in the ninth year and tenth month of Zedekiah's rule. The city was under siege for a wild 19 months, all the way until Zedekiah's eleventh year as king.

By the fourth month of Zedekiah’s eleventh year, on the ninth day, the famine was insane. There wasn't a single crumb of bread for anyone. That's when the Babylonians finally broke through the city walls. In the middle of the night, the whole Judean army tried to escape through a gate between two walls near the King's Garden. They slipped past the Babylonian lines surrounding the city and made a run for the Jordan Valley. But the Babylonians were right on them. They caught up to Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, but by then his whole army had bailed on him and scattered.

The Babylonians captured Zedekiah and dragged him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, who put him on trial and sentenced him right there. The king of Babylon made Zedekiah watch as he killed his sons. That was the last thing Zedekiah ever saw, because they blinded him right after. Then the king of Babylon killed all of Judah's officials too. Zedekiah was put in chains and hauled off to Babylon, where he was thrown in prison and stayed there until he died.

In the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, on the seventh day of the fifth month, his top commander, Nebuzaradan, showed up in Jerusalem. He burned God's Temple to the ground, then the royal palace, and then the rest of the city. He torched the whole place. He had his Babylonian troops tear down the city walls. Finally, he rounded up everyone left in the city, including the people who had already surrendered, and shipped them off to exile. He only left a few of the poorest farmers to take care of the vineyards and fields.

The Babylonians smashed the bronze pillars, the bronze washing stands, and the giant bronze basin called 'the Sea' that were in God's Temple, and they carried all the bronze away to Babylon. They also took all the bronze tools, and the gold and silver bowls and censers used in the Temple services. The commander didn't miss a thing; he took every piece of precious metal he could find.

The amount of bronze they got was insane. The two pillars, the Sea, the twelve bronze bulls that held it up, and the ten washstands that Solomon had made for the Temple—it was too much to even weigh. Each pillar was 27 feet tall and 18 feet around. They were hollow, with the bronze being just under an inch thick. On top of each pillar was a fancy bronze capital with pomegranates and detailed metalwork, adding another seven and a half feet to the height. There were 96 pomegranates spaced out, with a total of 100 woven into the design.

The commander also took some high-profile prisoners: Seraiah the head priest, Zephaniah the priest under him, three important guards, the top army officer who was left, seven of the king's advisors found in the city, the army's main recruiter, and sixty other important guys who were still around. Nebuzaradan marched them all to the king of Babylon at Riblah. And right there in Riblah, the king of Babylon had them all executed in cold blood.
So Judah was forced into exile, kicked out of their own land.
In the seventh year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar took 3,023 people from Judah into exile.
In his eighteenth year, he took another 832 from Jerusalem.
Then in his twenty-third year, his commander Nebuzaradan took 745 more people from Judah.
The grand total of exiles was 4,600.

Thirty-seven years after King Jehoiachin of Judah was taken into exile, a new king, Evil-Merodach, came to power in Babylon. He let Jehoiachin out of prison on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. The king was super nice to him, giving him way better treatment than any of the other royal prisoners in Babylon. Jehoiachin got to change out of his prison clothes and ate at the king's table for the rest of his life. The king gave him everything he needed to live comfortably until he died.

Lamentations.title: Jerusalem's Epic Fail
paragraphs: Man, look at this city. It used to be so crowded, but now it's a ghost town. She was like the queen of all nations, and now she's basically a slave.
She's up all night crying, tears just pouring down her face. And out of all her so-called friends, not a single one is there for her. They all betrayed her and became her enemies.

Judah got dragged away into exile, totally defeated and forced into hard labor. Now she's living among foreigners with no place to even chill. Her enemies caught up to her and trapped her in a tight spot.

The roads to Zion are completely empty. No one's going to the festivals anymore. The city gates are deserted, the priests are all sighing, and the young women are grieving. It's a super bitter situation.
Her enemies are in charge now, living their best life while she's suffering. And it's because God brought this on her for all her screw-ups. Her own kids were captured and taken away by the enemy.
All the glamour of beautiful Zion is gone. Her leaders are like starving deer that can't find any grass. They're weak and running with no energy left, with the enemy hot on their trail.

Jerusalem can't stop thinking about the good old days, and how she lost it all. Her people were captured by the enemy, and there was no one to help. Her enemies just stared and laughed at her collapse.

Jerusalem seriously messed up, and now she's a total outcast. Everyone who used to look up to her now looks down on her because they've seen her dark side. She's just groaning and hiding her face in shame.

She was living wild and didn't care about the future, and now she's had a legendary crash. There's no one to give her a hand. She's crying out, "God, look at my pain! See how the enemy is flexing on me."
The enemy came in and snatched all her precious things. She had to watch as pagans, the very people you told to stay out, barged right into her holy Sanctuary.
All the people are groaning, desperate for a crumb of bread. They're trading their favorite things just to get a little food to stay alive. "God, just look at me! I'm completely worthless now."
"Yo, all you people walking by, pay attention! Have you ever seen pain like my pain? Have you seen what God did to me when he was furious?"
"He sent down fire from the sky that went straight through my bones. He set a trap for my feet and knocked me down. He left me totally wrecked and sick all day long."
"My sins were all bundled up and tied like a yoke on my neck. He made me so weak that I couldn't fight back when my enemies took over. The Lord handed me over to them."
"The Lord rejected all my best warriors. He sent an army to crush my young men. He stomped on the virgin daughter of Judah like she was a grape in a winepress."
"This is why I'm bawling my eyes out. Tears are streaming down my face. There's no one here to comfort me or give me strength. My children are ruined because the enemy was just too strong."
Zion is reaching out her hands, but there's no one to help her. God ordered enemies to surround Jacob's people. Now Jerusalem is like a filthy rag that everyone avoids.
"God is totally in the right; I'm the one who rebelled against his word. Listen up, everyone! Look at my suffering. My young men and women have all been dragged into exile."
"I called out to my friends, but they completely ghosted me. My priests and leaders were starving in the city, trying to find food just to stay alive, but they couldn't even save themselves."
"God, look at the mess I'm in! My stomach is in knots, and my heart is twisted because I've been such a rebel. Outside, there's violence in the streets, and inside, it feels like death."
"People hear me groaning, but no one comforts me. All my enemies heard about the disaster you sent, and they're actually happy about it. Bring on the day you promised! Let them get what I got!"
"Look at how evil they are. Do to them what you did to me because of all my sins. I'm groaning nonstop, and my heart is completely broken."

Every night, when the watch starts, get up and just pour out your heart in prayer. Talk to God like you're face to face. Lift up your hands and beg him to save your kids who are starving to death in the streets.

Lamentations.title: From Rock Bottom to Real Hope
paragraphs: I'm the guy who's seen some serious trouble, the kind that comes straight from God's anger. He literally led me into complete darkness. And yeah, He's been hitting me with setback after setback, non-stop.

He basically wasted me away to nothing but skin and bones, and then broke them. He cornered me, ganged up on me, and just dumped all this trouble and hardship on me. He locked me away in the deepest darkness, like I was already dead and buried.

He's boxed me in so I can't escape, like I'm in handcuffs and leg chains. Even when I scream and beg for help, it's like He just ignores my prayers, like He's locked them up and tossed the key. He's built walls around me with massive stones. I'm totally trapped.

He's like a bear stalking me, a lion hiding and ready to jump. He threw me off my path and tore me to shreds. When He was done, there was nothing left of me. He then used me for target practice with his bow and arrows.
He shot me right in the gut with his arrows. Everyone treats me like a joke, the main character in their diss tracks. He made me eat disgusting, rotten food and drink nasty stuff until I was bloated.

He smashed my face into the gravel and ground me into the dirt. I completely gave up on life. I can't even remember what being happy feels like. I told myself, "This is it. I'm done. Believing in God is pointless now."

I'll never forget the struggle, feeling so lost, the taste of ashes, the poison I had to swallow. I remember it all—man, I remember it so clearly—that feeling of hitting rock bottom. But there's this one other thing I remember, and holding onto that memory gives me hope:

God's love is loyal and it never runs out; His mercy never dries up. They are brand new every single morning. Your faithfulness is insane! I'm sticking with God (I'm telling you, for real). He's all I have left.

God is good to the person who waits for Him with everything they've got, to the one who seriously seeks Him out. It's a good thing to quietly hope, to quietly wait for help from God. It's also good to push through the hard times when you're young.

When life gets super heavy and hard to handle, just go be by yourself. Get into the quiet. Bow down and pray. Don't ask a bunch of questions: just wait for hope to show up. Don't run from your problems. Face them head-on. The "worst" thing that can happen is never actually the worst.

Why? Because the Lord will never just leave and not come back. If He's harsh, He's also gentle. His supply of loyal love is massive. He doesn't get any joy out of making life hard or putting obstacles in our way:
Stomping on helpless prisoners, denying justice to victims in God's own court, messing with the evidence—the Lord is not okay with any of that.

Who do you think just says something and it happens? It's the Lord who gives those orders. Doesn't the Most High God create everything, the good stuff and the hard stuff? And why would anyone who's been given life complain when they're punished for their own mistakes?

Let's take a hard look at how we're living and get our lives right with God. Let's lift up our hearts and our hands at the same time, praying to God in heaven: "We've been stubborn and rebellious, and you haven't forgiven us.

"You got angry with us and didn't hold back. You chased us down and killed us without any mercy. You wrapped yourself in a thick cloud so none of our prayers could get through. You treated us like trash, like dirty dishwater thrown out in the backyard for everyone to see.

"Our enemies are yelling insults at us, their mouths full of hate, just spitting venom. We've been through hell and back. We have nowhere to turn, nowhere to go. Rivers of tears are pouring from my eyes because my people are so broken.

"The tears just keep streaming from my eyes, like a non-stop fountain, until you, God, look down from heaven and see my pain. When I see what's happened to the young women in my city, my heart just breaks.

"Enemies who had no reason to hate me hunted me down like a bird. They threw me into a pit and then threw stones at me. Then the flood came and filled the pit. The water went over my head. I thought, 'It's all over.'

"I called out your name, O God, from the very bottom of that pit. You heard me when I cried out, 'Don't close your ears to me! Get me out of here! Save me!' You came close when I called. You said, 'It's going to be okay.'
"You took my side, Lord; you saved my life! God, you saw all the wrong they did to me. Now, give me justice! Yeah, you saw their evil plans, all their plots to destroy me.

"You heard them, God, their nasty gossip, their secret plots to ruin me. They never stop, these enemies of mine, just thinking up trouble, planning evil, day after day. Whether they're sitting or standing—just look at them!—they make fun of me with their vulgar songs.
"Make them pay for what they've done, God. Give them what they deserve. Break their miserable hearts! Curse them! Get really angry. Hunt them down. Completely destroy them from under your heavens!"

Lamentations.title: From Gold to Garbage: Jerusalem's Epic Fail
paragraphs: OMG, for real... How is gold now treated like dirt, the best gold just tossed out with the trash? Priceless jewels are scattered everywhere, just lying in the gutters.
The people of Zion, who used to be so highly valued, worth way more than gold, are now treated like cheap clay pots, the kind you can get anywhere.
Even wild animals like jackals feed their babies, you know? But my own people have become cruel to their kids, like ostriches that just abandon their eggs in the desert.
Babies are so thirsty their tongues are stuck to the roofs of their mouths. Little kids are begging for food, but nobody gives them even a single crumb.
People who used to eat at fancy restaurants are now scrounging for scraps in the streets. The ones who wore designer clothes are digging through trash piles for something to wear.
The messed-up things my people did were even worse than what Sodom did. That city was destroyed in an instant, with no one to even help them.

The leaders, who were once so healthy and looked so good, all strong and glowing, are now covered in soot. You wouldn't even recognize them on the street. They're just skin and bones, their skin all dry and leathery.
Honestly, it would've been better to die in a battle than to die of starvation. At least getting killed by a sword is quick, instead of slowly wasting away.
This is wild, but kind women actually boiled their own children for food. That was the only thing to eat when my people were completely broken.
God just let all His anger out, no holding back. He poured out all His fury and set a fire in Zion that burned the whole place to the ground.
Kings and rulers all over the world were shook. They couldn't believe it when they saw enemies just marching right into Jerusalem's gates like they owned the place.
This all happened because of the sins of the prophets and the evil of the priests. They totally took advantage of good people and basically ruined their lives.

Now those same prophets and priests are just stumbling around the streets, all grimy and stained from their own corruption. People yell at them, like, 'Get out of here, you're disgusting! Don't touch us!' They're total outcasts, and everyone knows they got kicked out of their own city.
God Himself scattered them. He's not looking out for them anymore. He's done with the priests and doesn't care about the elders.
We kept watching and watching for help, but got nothing. We were looking for someone to save us, but help never came.
They hunted us down. It wasn't even safe to walk in the streets. We knew our end was coming; our days were numbered. We were totally doomed.
They were faster than eagles, chasing us in the mountains and setting traps for us in the desert.
Our king, the one God chose, who was like our life-source, got caught in their traps. We always thought we'd be safe under his protection, but nope.
So go ahead and party, Edom. Live it up. Because your turn is coming. You're going to drink from the same cup of God's anger, get wasted on it, and wake up with nothing.
And that's a wrap for you, Zion. Your punishment is over. You won't have to go through this exile again. But Edom, your judgment is coming. God's gonna expose all your sin for everyone to see.

Lamentations.title: God, Are You Ghosting Us?!
paragraphs: God, seriously, look at what we've been through. Our reputation is totally wrecked. Our awesome land has been handed over to a bunch of strangers, and our homes to people we don't even know. We're basically orphans, with no dads around, and our moms are pretty much widows.

We literally have to pay for our own water. Even the wood for our fires has a price tag. We're getting pushed around and bossed like slaves, totally worn out with zero breaks. We had to make deals with Egypt and Assyria just to get some food on the table.
Our parents messed up and they're not here anymore, but now we're paying for all the wrong things they did. We're being ruled by our own former slaves, and there's no way to escape their control.
We have to risk our lives just to find food in the desert, which is crawling with bandits. The hunger has been so bad that our skin is as black as an oven and feels like old, dried-out leather.

The women in Zion were assaulted, and the young girls in the towns of Judah too. They hung our leaders by their hands and showed no respect to our elders. Strong young guys were forced to do humiliating work, and even little boys had to do heavy, back-breaking labor.

The wise elders don't hang out at the city gate anymore. The sound of young people making music is gone. All the joy has been sucked out of our lives. Our dance parties have turned into funeral marches.

The crown has fallen right off our heads. We're in deep trouble. Man, we really messed up by sinning. Because of all this, we're completely heartbroken; we can't even see straight through our tears. Mount Zion is a total ruin, just a hangout spot for jackals.

But look, God, you're still the King, right? Your throne is eternal. So why does it feel like you've forgotten us? Why would you just dump us and leave us hanging like this? Please, bring us back to you, God—we're so ready to come back. Give us a fresh start. Because right now, it feels like you've totally disowned us. You've been seriously angry with us.

Ezekiel.title: Ezekiel's Vision Was Lowkey Insane
paragraphs: So, when I was 30, I was living with the other exiles by the Kebar River. On the fifth day of the fourth month, the sky literally just opened up and I started seeing these wild visions of God.

(Just to be clear, it was the fifth day of the month, in the fifth year since King Jehoiachin got exiled. That's when God's word came straight to me, Ezekiel, son of Buzi the priest, right there on the banks of the Kebar River in Babylon. God's power just hit me that day, no cap.)

I looked up and saw this insane dust storm coming from the north—a massive cloud with lightning flashing everywhere, and a huge ball of fire that was glowing like shiny bronze. Inside the fire, there were these four living creatures that looked so alive. They basically had a human shape, but each one had four faces and four wings. Their legs were super sturdy and straight, like pillars, but their feet were like calf hooves that sparkled like polished bronze in the fire. They had human hands under their wings on all four sides. All four of them had these faces and wings, and their wings touched the creature next to them. They didn't turn or anything; they just moved straight forward.

Their faces were pretty wild: the front one was a human face, the one on the right was a lion's face, the one on the left was an ox's face, and the one in the back was an eagle's face. So yeah, that's the deal with the faces. Their wings were spread out, with one pair touching the wings of the creatures on either side, and the other pair covering their own bodies. Each one just went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit guided them, that's where they went, without even turning.

The four creatures themselves looked like a blazing fire, or maybe like torches. Flames were shooting back and forth between them, and lightning bolts were zapping out of the fire. The creatures were zipping around as fast as lightning strikes.

As I was watching these four creatures, I saw what looked like a wheel on the ground next to each of them. The wheels were all identical, sparkling like diamonds. It was like they were wheels inside of wheels, kind of like a gyroscope.

They could move in any of the four directions they were facing, but always straight, never swerving. The rims of the wheels were huge and were covered in eyes all the way around. When the living creatures moved, the wheels moved with them. When the creatures lifted off the ground, the wheels lifted off too. Wherever the spirit went, they went, and the wheels were right there with them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels. When the creatures moved, the wheels moved; when they stopped, the wheels stopped; and when they lifted off the ground, the wheels lifted off with them, because the spirit of the creatures was in the wheels.

Above the heads of the living creatures was this dome-like thing, shimmering like a sky made of crystal, stretched out over them. Under the dome, they each had one set of wings stretched out toward the others, and another set covering their bodies. When they moved, I heard their wings, and it sounded like a massive waterfall, like the voice of God Almighty, or like the noise of a whole army on a battlefield. When they stopped, they just folded their wings.

And then, while they were standing there with their wings folded, a voice came from above the dome over their heads. Above the dome was something that looked like a throne, the color of a sapphire, and on the throne was a figure that looked human, but was towering over it. From the waist up, he looked like glowing bronze, and from the waist down, he looked like a blazing fire. There was this incredible brightness all around him! It looked just like a rainbow on a rainy day. And then it hit me—it was the Glory of God!
When I saw all that, I just dropped to my knees and put my face on the ground. Then I heard a voice speaking.

Ezekiel.title: God's Super Intense Job Offer
paragraphs: Then a voice said, “Son of man, get up. I need to talk to you.”
The second that voice spoke, the Spirit just zapped into me and got me on my feet. I was actually listening as He talked to me.

He said, “Son of man, I’m sending you to the Israelites, who are lowkey the most rebellious crew ever. For real, they and their ancestors have been staging a rebellion right up to this very day. These people I’m sending you to are a tough crowd—super stubborn in their ways. You gotta tell them, ‘This is a message from the Lord GOD.’ They're a defiant bunch. So, whether they listen to you or not, at least they’ll know a real prophet was among them. But for real, don't be scared of them, son of man, and don't let their words get to you. Don't be afraid even if living with them feels like stepping on thorns or finding scorpions in your bed. Don't freak out over their mean words or their angry stares. They're just a bunch of rebels. Your job is to speak my words to them. It's not on you if they listen or not. They're just that stubborn.
“Just make sure, son of man, that you don’t start acting rebellious like them. Open your mouth and eat what I give you.”

And when I looked, His hand was stretched out to me, and in it was a scroll. He unrolled it, and on both sides, front and back, were written songs of sadness, mourning, and total doom. It was a major downer.

Ezekiel.title: I Ate a Book & Became God's Watchman
paragraphs: He told me, “Yo, son of man, eat what you see. Eat this scroll. Then go and speak to the family of Israel.”
As I opened my mouth, he gave me the scroll to eat, saying, “Son of man, eat this book that I am giving you. Make a full meal of it!”
So I ate it. It tasted so good—just like honey.

Then he told me, “Son of man, go to the family of Israel and speak my Message. Look, I’m not sending you to a people who speak a hard-to-learn language with words you can hardly pronounce. If I had sent you to such people, their ears would have perked up and they would have listened immediately.

“But it won’t work that way with the family of Israel. They won’t listen to you because they won’t listen to me. They are, as I said, a hard case, hardened in their sin. But I’ll make you as hard in your way as they are in theirs. I’ll make your face as hard as rock, harder than granite. Don’t let them intimidate you. Don’t be afraid of them, even though they’re a bunch of rebels.”

Then he said, “Son of man, get all these words that I’m giving you inside you. Listen to them obediently. Make them your own. And now go. Go to the exiles, your people, and speak. Tell them, ‘This is the Message of God, the Master.’ Speak your piece, whether they listen or not.”

Then the Spirit picked me up. Behind me I heard a great commotion—“Blessed be the Glory of God in his Sanctuary!”—the wings of the living creatures beating against each other, the whirling wheels, the rumble of a great earthquake.

The Spirit lifted me and took me away. I went bitterly and angrily. I didn’t want to go. But God had me in his grip. I arrived among the exiles who lived near the Kebar River at Tel Aviv. I came to where they were living and sat there for seven days, appalled.
At the end of the seven days, I received this Message from God:

“Son of man, I’ve made you a watchman for the family of Israel. Whenever you hear me say something, warn them for me. If I say to the wicked, ‘You are going to die,’ and you don’t sound the alarm warning them that it’s a matter of life or death, they will die and it will be your fault. I’ll hold you responsible. But if you warn the wicked and they keep right on sinning anyway, they’ll most certainly die for their sin, but you won’t die. You’ll have saved your life.

“And if the righteous turn back from living righteously and take up with evil when I step in and put them in a hard place, they’ll die. If you haven’t warned them, they’ll die because of their sins, and none of the right things they’ve done will count for anything—and I’ll hold you responsible. But if you warn these righteous people not to sin and they listen to you, they’ll live because they took the warning—and again, you’ll have saved your life.”
God grabbed me by the shoulder and said, “Get up. Go out on the plain. I want to talk with you.”
So I got up and went out on the plain. I couldn’t believe my eyes: the Glory of God! Right there! It was like the Glory I had seen at the Kebar River. I fell to the ground, prostrate.

Then the Spirit entered me and put me on my feet. He said, “Go home and shut the door behind you.” And then something odd: “Son of man: They’ll tie you hand and foot with ropes so you can’t leave the house. I’ll make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth so you won’t be able to talk and tell the people what they’re doing wrong, even though they are a bunch of rebels.

“But then when the time is ripe, I’ll free your tongue and you’ll say, ‘This is what God, the Master, says: . . .’ From then on it’s up to them. They can listen or not listen, whichever they like. They are a bunch of rebels!”

Ezekiel.title: Ezekiel's 430-Day Performance Art Was WILD
paragraphs: “Alright, son of man, grab a brick and put it in front of you. On this brick, I want you to draw a map of Jerusalem. Then, you’re gonna stage a whole siege against this brick-city. Build mini siege walls, a ramp, set up little army camps, and place tiny battering rams all around it. Next, grab an iron skillet and stand it up on its side between you and the city, like an iron wall. You need to face this model city. It’s under siege, and you’re the one leading the attack. This whole setup is a huge sign for the people of Israel.

“Next, you’re gonna lie down on your left side, and you’re going to place all the sin of the nation of Israel right on yourself. You have to bear their sin for the exact number of days you’re lying on that side. The number of days will match the years of their sin—that’s 390 years. So for 390 days, you will carry the sin of the nation of Israel.

“Then, once you’re done with that, you’re gonna flip over and lie on your right side to bear the sin of the nation of Judah. This time, your assignment is to lie there for forty days, one day for each year of their sin. You have to look straight at your siege of Jerusalem model. Roll up your sleeve, shake your fist at it, and preach against the city.
“I’m gonna tie you up with ropes, so tight that you can’t move or even turn over until you’ve completed all the days of this siege performance.

“Okay, now for your food. I want you to get some wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt. Mix them all together in a bowl to make a kind of flatbread. This is your food ration for the 390 days you’re lying on your side. You’ll measure out about half a pound for each day and eat it right on schedule. You’ll also get a daily ration of about a pint of water, and you have to drink that on schedule too. You’ll eat this bread like a muffin, but here’s the crazy part: you have to bake it out in public where everyone can see you, using dried human poop for fuel.”

God then said, “This is a picture of what the people of Israel are going to do. Among the foreign nations where I will send them, they will have to eat foods that are totally forbidden for a holy people.”

I immediately said, “No way, God, my Master! Never! I’ve never made myself unclean with food like that. Ever since I was a kid, I’ve never eaten anything the law forbids, nothing I found dead or that was attacked by wild animals. I have never taken a single bite of forbidden food.”
“Alright,” he said. “I’ll let you bake your bread over cow dung instead of human dung.”

Then he said to me, “Son of man, I’m about to cut off the entire food supply from Jerusalem. The people will be on starvation rations, constantly worrying where their next meal is coming from, and desperately searching for their next sip of water. It’s going to be a full-blown famine. People will just stare at each other, seeing nothing but skin and bones, and they’ll just be in despair. This is what sin leads to.”

Ezekiel.title: God's Judgment Goes Viral
paragraphs: “Alright, my guy, God says to take a sharp sword and use it like a razor to shave your head and your beard. Then, get some scales and divide the hair into three equal parts. When the siege is finally over, you’re gonna take one-third of the hair and burn it right in the middle of the city. Take the second third, chop it up with that sword, and sprinkle it all around the city. The last third, you’re just gonna throw it to the wind. And then I’m gonna come after them with a sword.

“But hold up, grab a few of those hairs and stick them in your pocket. Then take some of *those* hairs and toss them into the fire—burn ‘em up. From that fire, a new fire will spread to the whole family of Israel.

“This is what the Lord God is saying: This is Jerusalem we’re talking about. I put her at the center of the world, with all the nations surrounding her. But she rebelled against my laws and rules, and honestly, she was way worse than all the nations around her—just straight-up wicked. She refused my guidance and ignored my directions.

“So, the Lord God says: You’ve been more stubborn and rebellious than any of the nations around you, ignoring my rules and directions. You’ve actually sunk down to the low level of the people around you.

“So, the Lord God says this: I’m turning against you, Jerusalem. Yeah, you. I’m going to punish you right in front of all the other nations. Because of all your disgusting idols, I’m going to do something to you that I’ve never done before and will never do again: families are going to become cannibals. Parents will eat their own children, and children will eat their parents. That’s some serious punishment. And anyone who’s left, I’ll just scatter them to the winds.

“Therefore, as sure as I am the living God—this is a decree from the Lord God—because you’ve defiled my Holy Temple with your disgusting and obscene idols, I’m out. I won’t show you even an ounce of pity. A third of your people will die from disease or starvation inside the city, a third will be killed by the sword outside the city, and the last third will be scattered to the winds, chased by killers.
“Only after all that will my anger finally cool down. Then you’ll know that I, the Lord, was serious about all this, that I’m a jealous God who you don’t mess with.

“When I’m done with you, you’ll be nothing but a pile of ruins. The nations passing by will make jokes about you. When I’m finished with my angry punishment and harsh rebukes, you’ll be a total joke, a horror story that all the surrounding nations tell. I, the Lord, have said it.

“And when I start shooting my deadly arrows of famine at you, I’ll be shooting to kill. Then I’ll crank up the famine and cut off your food supply completely. Famine after famine—and then I’ll send wild animals to finish off your children. Sickness, murder, death—and I’ll be the one who sent it. I, the Lord, have spoken.”

Ezekiel.title: God's Final Warning: Idol Worship Canceled
paragraphs: Then God's word hit me. He was like, 'Yo, son of man, turn toward the mountains of Israel and call them out. Tell 'em: 'Hey, mountains of Israel, listen up to what the Lord GOD has to say.' The Master, GOD, is talking to all you mountains, hills, canyons, and valleys: I'm about to wreck your pagan shrines. I'm gonna tear down your altars, smash your sun-god statues, and your people are gonna drop dead right while they're bowing to your fake idols. I'll pile up the bodies of the Israelites right in front of those useless idols and scatter their bones all around your shrines. Every single town you live in will be left in ruins and the pagan spots will be totally demolished—altars wrecked, idols shattered, and all those custom sun-god pillars you love so much will be toast. Dead bodies everywhere. Then you'll finally get that I am the real GOD.

But I'll let a few of you survive the slaughter as you get scattered across other countries. In those foreign lands where they're taken as prisoners, they'll remember me. They'll finally realize how crushed I was by their cheating hearts, by their crazy lust for other gods. They'll be totally disgusted with themselves for all the evil, messed-up stuff they did. They'll know for sure that I am GOD. They'll get that my warning of judgment wasn't just some empty threat.

This is what the Lord GOD says: Clap your hands, stomp your feet, and scream, 'No, no, no!' because of all the disgusting, evil things happening in Israel. They're about to die by violence, by starvation, by sickness—death is coming for everyone. People far away will die, people nearby will be killed, and whoever is left in the city will starve. Why? Because I am so, so angry. They'll know I'm GOD when they see their own people's dead bodies scattered all around their busted sex-and-religion shrines, on every hill and under every green tree where they got into their weird rituals. I'm gonna bring my power down hard on them, completely destroy the country wherever they live, and turn it into a wasteland from the desert all the way to Riblah. Then they'll know that I am GOD!'

Ezekiel.title: It's Officially Over for Israel
paragraphs: God's Word hit me. He said, "Yo, son of man—God, the Boss, has a message for Israel:

"It's the end. Like, the end of normal life for everyone. It's all over. The end is coming for you. I'm unleashing my anger on you. I've made my decision based on how you've been living, and I'm gonna make you pay for all the nasty stuff you've done. I'm not gonna look away or feel bad for you. You're gonna get what you deserve for your lifestyle. All that gross stuff you did? It's gonna come right back at you, and then you'll know for real that I am God."

"I, God, the Boss, am telling you: Disaster after disaster! Look, it's coming! It's the end—the end is here. The end is ripe. Watch out, it's on its way! This is your destiny, all you people living in this land. Time's up. It's go-time. No more excuses, no more asking for extra time. I'm about to pour out my fury on you, let out all my anger, judge you for how you've lived, and make you pay for all your disgusting actions. I'm not gonna look the other way or feel sorry for you. I'm making you pay for your lifestyle. Your disgusting actions are gonna boomerang back on you. And then you'll realize that it's me, God, who's bringing the hammer down.

"I, God, the Boss, am telling you: Disaster after disaster! Look, it's coming! It's the end—the end is here. The end is ripe. Watch out, it's on its way! This is your destiny, all you people living in this land. Time's up. It's go-time. No more excuses, no more asking for extra time. I'm about to pour out my fury on you, let out all my anger, judge you for how you've lived, and make you pay for all your disgusting actions. I'm not gonna look the other way or feel sorry for you. I'm making you pay for your lifestyle. Your disgusting actions are gonna boomerang back on you. And then you'll realize that it's me, God, who's bringing the hammer down.

"'Judgment Day! Your fate is sealed. The leadership is way too full of itself, pride is off the charts, and violence is strutting around like it owns the place, waving its evil stick. But it's all for nothing, and nothing will be left of them. Time's up. The final countdown... The person buying stuff shouldn't be bragging, and the person selling shouldn't be stressing. Why? Because my judgment and anger have flipped the whole world upside down. The whole market has crashed. It's never going back to the way it was. And don't even think about the market bouncing back. The whole country is broke because of its sins, and it's not getting any better.

"'Judgment Day! Your fate is sealed. The leadership is way too full of itself, pride is off the charts, and violence is strutting around like it owns the place, waving its evil stick. But it's all for nothing, and nothing will be left of them. Time's up. The final countdown... The person buying stuff shouldn't be bragging, and the person selling shouldn't be stressing. Why? Because my judgment and anger have flipped the whole world upside down. The whole market has crashed. It's never going back to the way it was. And don't even think about the market bouncing back. The whole country is broke because of its sins, and it's not getting any better.

"'The trumpet sounds for battle: 'Get ready!' But nobody is actually going to fight. My anger has them all frozen! If you're on the roads, you get killed. If you go home, you die of starvation or sickness. You either get murdered out in the country or die from being sick or hungry in the city. The ones who survive will run for the hills. They'll be crying like doves in the valleys, each one crying over their own sins.

They literally tripped over their money and fell into sin. They were so proud and extra with their jewelry, using it to decorate their fake, gross idols. So I'm gonna make those disgusting idols stink. I'm gonna give away all their religious stuff—strangers will just take it for free, and godless people will spit on it and make fun of it. I'm gonna turn my face away so I don't have to see my special place and people get trashed, as violent strangers just walk in and wreck everything. It's gonna be a bloodbath, with crime and violence filling the city. I'll bring in the worst kinds of people to take over their houses. I'll shut down all the bragging and showing off from the rich and powerful, and I'll make sure there's nothing holy left in their holy places. It's a total disaster. They'll be looking for peace, but there's no peace anywhere. Just one disaster after another, and rumors spreading like crazy. They'll be begging the prophet to tell them what's going on, but nobody will know anything. The priests will be clueless, and the elders won't know what to say. The king will be in despair, and the prince will be totally wrecked. The regular people will be paralyzed with fear, unable to move. I'm gonna deal with them right where they are and judge them by their own standards. Then they'll know that I am God.'"

Ezekiel.title: God's Temple Got WEIRD...
paragraphs: So, picture this: It's the sixth year, sixth month, fifth day. I'm just chilling at my place, having a meeting with the leaders of Judah, when BAM! The hand of God just grabs me. I look up, and I'm shook. There's this figure that looks like a dude—fiery from the waist down and like super shiny bronze from the waist up. He reaches out a hand, grabs me by the hair (wild, right?), and the Spirit just yeets me into the air. Next thing I know, I'm in a vision, flying to Jerusalem. I land right at the north gate of the Temple's inner court, where they'd set up this statue of a sex goddess that totally ticks God off. And right there in front of me is the Glory of God, just like I saw it on the plain. It was insane.
He tells me, “Son of man, look north.” So I do, and there it is. Just north of the entrance, this altar for that sex goddess, Asherah, the one that makes God so mad.

Then he said, “Son of man, you seeing this? It's messed up. And they're doing it right here in my house! It's so bad it makes me want to just bounce from my own Temple. But trust me, you're about to see even crazier stuff.”
He took me to the entrance of the Temple court. I looked, and there was this big hole in the wall.
He said, “Son of man, dig through the wall.”
So I dug through the wall and found a door.
He said, “Alright, go through the door and see the messed-up things they're into.”

I went in and, no cap, I couldn't believe what I was seeing. The walls were covered in paintings of reptiles, animals, and monsters—basically the whole squad of Egyptian gods—and the Israelites were worshiping them. In the middle of the room were seventy of Israel's leaders, with this guy Jaazaniah son of Shaphan front and center. They were all holding these incense things, and the smoke was just rising up in a cloud.

He said, “Son of man, you see what your leaders are doing in the dark? Each one is bowing down to his favorite god-picture. They're telling themselves, ‘God can't see us. God has bailed on our country.’”
Then he said, “You're about to see something even worse.”

He took me to the north gate entrance of God's Temple. And I saw women just sitting there, crying for Tammuz, some Babylonian fertility god. He was like, “You getting a good look, son of man? Because you're about to see something even more messed up.”

Finally, he took me to the inner court of God's Temple. And there, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five guys. They had their backs to God's Temple, and they were facing east, bowing down and worshiping the sun.

He said, “You've seen enough, son of man? Isn't it bad enough that Judah is doing all this wild stuff? They've filled the country with violence, and now they're provoking me even more with these disrespectful gestures. That's it. They've got an angry God on their hands now. No more mercy. They can cry and shout all they want, but I'm not even listening.”

Ezekiel.title: Marked for Life or Death
paragraphs: Then I heard this booming voice shout, “Alright, executioners, get over here! And don’t forget your weapons.”

And just like that, six guys came down the road from the north gate, each one carrying a seriously deadly weapon. Another guy was with them, dressed in linen clothes and carrying a writer’s case. They all went inside and stood by the bronze altar.

The Glory of the God of Israel, which was usually chilling above the cherubim angels, moved to the entrance of the Temple. He called out to the guy in linen with the writer's case: “Go all through Jerusalem and put a mark on the forehead of everyone who is genuinely upset and grieving over all the terrible things happening in the city.”

Then I heard him tell the executioners, “Follow him through the city and start killing. Don’t feel sorry for anyone. Show zero mercy. Kill everyone—old men, women, young people, mothers, and children. But do not touch anyone who has the mark. Start right here at my Temple.”
So they started with the leaders who were right in front of the Temple.
He told the executioners, “Trash the Temple. Fill it up with dead bodies. Then go out and keep killing.” So they went out and started wrecking the city.

While this whole massacre was happening, I was the only one left. I just fell on my face and prayed, “Oh no, God, my Master! Are you really going to wipe out every single person left in Israel as you pour out your anger on Jerusalem?”

He replied, “The sin of Israel and Judah is off the charts. The whole country is full of murder, and the city is overflowing with injustice. They all keep saying, ‘God has bailed on us. He doesn’t see what we’re doing.’ Well, I do see, and I’m not feeling sorry for any of them. They’re about to get what they deserve for their actions.”
Just then, the man in linen with the writer’s case came back and said, “I did what you told me to do.”

Ezekiel.title: God's Glory is Leaving the Temple?!
paragraphs: So I looked up again, and whoa! Right above the heads of those cherubim-angel creatures, there was this thing that looked just like a throne, all sparkly and blue like a sapphire. It was wild.
Then God told the guy in the linen outfit, "Yo, go into the middle of those wheels under the cherubim. Grab a handful of burning coals from there and just toss 'em all over the city."

I saw him go in. The cherubim were just chilling on the south side of the Temple when he walked in. Suddenly, this massive cloud filled up the inner courtyard. Then, God's Glory, like this super bright presence, lifted up from the cherubim and moved to the entrance of the Temple. The whole place, the court and the Temple, were just lit up with God's blazing glory. And the sound was insane! You could hear the cherubim's wings all the way from the outer court—it sounded like God's powerful voice, like thunder.

When God ordered the guy in linen, "Get some fire from between the wheels, from the cherubim," he went and stood next to a wheel. One of the cherubim reached into the fire, grabbed some coals, and put them in the guy's hands. He took them and left. And get this, you could see something that looked like a human hand under the cherubim's wings.

Then I saw four wheels next to the cherubim, one for each of them. The wheels were sparkling like crazy, like diamonds in the sun. All four looked the same, and it was like a wheel inside another wheel. When they moved, they could go in any of the four directions but always in a straight line. Wherever the cherubim went, the wheels followed. The cherubim were covered in eyes—on their backs, hands, and wings. The wheels were full of eyes too. I heard someone call the wheels "wheels within wheels."
Each cherub had four faces: the first was an angel's face, the second a human's, the third a lion's, and the fourth an eagle's.

Then the cherubim flew up. They were the same living creatures I had seen before by the Kebar River. When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved with them. When they spread their wings to fly, the wheels stuck right by them. When they stopped, the wheels stopped. When they went up, the wheels went up, because the spirit of the creatures was in the wheels.

Then God's Glory left the Temple entrance and just hovered over the cherubim. I watched as the cherubim spread their wings and took off, with the wheels right there with them. They stopped at the entrance of the east gate of the Temple, and the Glory of the God of Israel was right there above them.

These were the exact same creatures I had seen under the God of Israel by the Kebar River. I knew they were cherubim. Each one had four faces and four wings, and under their wings, they had what looked like human hands. Their faces were identical to the ones I saw by the Kebar River. They all just moved straight ahead.

Ezekiel.title: You're NOT the Main Character
paragraphs: Then the Spirit just teleported me to the east gate of the Temple. Standing there were 25 dudes, and I totally recognized the leaders, Jaazaniah and Pelatiah.

God was like, "Son of man, these are the guys who are basically masterminds for sin, always cooking up some new evil scheme in the city. They’re out here saying, ‘We can do whatever we want. We're the VIPs, the best part of the soup.’"
"Go up against them, son of man. Preach the truth to them."

Then God's Spirit came on me and gave me the words to say: "This is what God's telling you: ‘That’s a nice little speech for the public, Israel, but I know what you’re really thinking. You’ve murdered so many people in this city. The streets are literally piled with bodies because of you.’

"So, here's the deal from the Master, God: ‘Those bodies you piled up in the streets? *They're* the meat in this soup pot of a city, and you're not even in it. I'm kicking you out! You're scared of war? Well, guess what's coming for you. I'm bringing war right to your doorstep. I'm kicking you out of this city, handing you over to your enemies, and you're gonna get punished, big time. You'll die in battle. I'll bring my judgment on you at the very border of Israel. Then you'll finally get that I am God. This city isn't your safe little soup pot, and you're definitely not the prime cuts of meat in it. Not even close. I'll judge you at Israel's border, and you'll realize that I am God, because you blew off all my rules and commands. Instead of following me, you just copied the messed-up ways of the nations around you.’"

While I was still preaching, Pelatiah son of Benaiah just dropped dead. I hit the ground, face down, and yelled out, "Oh, Master, GOD! Are you really going to wipe out every last person left in Israel?"

Then God's message came back to me: "Son of man, your family—and I mean all the people of Israel who are in exile with you—are the ones the people in Jerusalem are dissing. They're saying, ‘Ha, they're far away from God. This land is ours now.’

"So, tell them this: ‘Here’s a message from the Master, God. Yeah, it's true I sent you far away and scattered you. But even so, I've been like a temporary safe place for you in the lands where you've gone. I'm going to gather you back from all those countries and give you the land of Israel back. You'll come home and do a total clean-up, throwing out all the nasty idols and disgusting images. I'll give you a brand new heart and put a new spirit in you. I'll do surgery on you—take out that heart of stone and give you a real, living heart. Then you'll actually follow my rules and be careful to do what I say. You'll be my people, and I'll be your God!
"‘But for those who are stubborn and can't get enough of their gross idols? I'll make sure they get exactly what they deserve for what they've done.’ This is the decree of the Master, God."

Then the cherubim lifted their wings, the wheels right beside them, and the Glory of the God of Israel was shining over them. The Glory of God rose up from the city and stopped on the mountain east of it.

Then, still in this vision from God's Spirit, the Spirit picked me up and carried me all the way back to the exiles in Babylon. And just like that, the vision was over. I told the exiles everything God had shown me.

Ezekiel.title: My Life as a Meme: The Escape Plan
paragraphs: God's message hit my line: 'Yo, son of man, you're living with a crew that's straight-up rebellious. They've got eyes but are basically blind, and ears but they don't hear a thing. Total rebels. So, here's the plan: pack a duffel bag like you're getting kicked out. Do it in broad daylight so everyone sees you, and just walk away like you're being exiled. Maybe then they'll finally get what's happening, even though they're such rebels. Grab your stuff while they're all watching—just the essentials, like someone forced to leave home. When evening hits, head out like a real exile. While they're watching, I want you to dig a hole through the wall of your house and carry your bag through it. With everyone's eyes on you, throw the bag on your shoulder and walk off into the night. Cover your face so you don't have to see the place you'll never see again. I'm making you a living, breathing object lesson for the family of Israel.'

So, I did exactly what he told me to. I got my stuff, brought it out to the street for everyone to see, packed it up like an exile's go-bag, and then, when the sun started to set, I literally dug a hole through my house's wall with my bare hands. When it got dark, with everyone still staring, I bounced, throwing my bag over my shoulder.

The next morning, God hit me up again: 'Son of man, when someone from Israel, that rebellious crew, asks you, 'Bro, what are you even doing?' you tell them, 'The big boss, God, says this message is a direct @ to the prince in Jerusalem—we're talking about Zedekiah—but it's also for everyone in Israel.'
'Also, tell them, 'I'm literally acting out what's going to happen to you. What I'm doing now is a preview of what's coming for all the people of Israel. They're going into exile as prisoners.'

'The prince himself is gonna sling his bag over his shoulder in the dark and leave. He'll dig through the wall of his house, covering his face so he doesn't have to see the land he's leaving for good. But I'll make sure he gets caught and dragged to Babylon. He'll be blinded and will never see that land where he's gonna die. I'll scatter everyone who helped him escape, and his whole army, to the four winds, and tons of them will die in battle. They'll finally realize that I am God when I scatter them all over the world.'

'I'll let a few of them survive the fighting, the famine, and the plagues, but only so they can go and tell all the foreign nations about the disgusting stuff they've been up to. Then they will know that I am God.'

God's message came to me again: 'Son of man, when you eat, act like you're shaking with anxiety. When you drink, be all shaky and scared. Then tell the people of this land, everyone in Jerusalem and Israel, God's message: 'You're going to eat your food shaking with fear and drink your water in total terror, because your whole country is going to be wrecked as payback for all the messed-up stuff you've done. All the towns and cities will be ghost towns, and the fields will be destroyed. Then you'll realize that I am God.'
God's message came to me: 'Son of man, what's this little saying that's going around in Israel? 'Time keeps passing, but none of the prophecies ever come true.'?
'Tell them, 'God, the Master, says, That little saying is about to be canceled.'

'Tell them, 'Time's up. Every single warning is about to become reality. All the fake-deep prophecies and feel-good sermons are over for Israel. I, God, am speaking now. And what I say, goes. Nothing I say is getting delayed. What I say, I'll do—and it's happening soon, you rebels!' That's a decree from God, the Master.'

God's message came to me: 'Son of man, are you hearing what the people of Israel are saying? They're like, 'Oh, that prophet's warnings are for, like, way in the future.' Well, tell them, 'God, the Master, says, 'Nothing I say is on hold. What I say, happens. Period.' That's a decree from God, the Master.'

Ezekiel.title: Calling Out the FAKE Prophets
paragraphs: God's message hit me: 'Son of man, you gotta call out the prophets of Israel. They're just making stuff up and calling it prophecy.'

'Preach the real deal to them. Tell them, \'Listen to God's actual message!\' The big boss, God, is calling out these clueless prophets who are just doing their own thing and have no idea what's really going on. Your prophets, Israel, are like jackals picking through trash. They haven't done a single thing to fix the city's problems and haven't risked anything to help Israel when judgment day comes. All they do is sell comforting fantasies and preach straight-up lies. They say \'God says...\' when God hasn't even thought about them. And they're just standing there, thinking their words actually mean something.

'Haven't you been selling total nonsense? Aren't your sermons just a bunch of lies, saying \'God says...\' when I haven't said a thing? So, listen up—this is a message from the Master, God—I'm so done with prophets who pass off their own ideas as visions and use their sermons to lie. I'm kicking them out of my people's council, deleting them from Israel's contacts, and blocking them from the land of Israel. Then you'll know that I am the real deal, God, the Master.

'The truth is, they've lied to my people. They've been saying, \'No worries, everything's fine,\' when it's totally not fine. When people build a flimsy wall, these prophets are right there, slapping on a coat of paint to make it look good. So tell those painters, \'When a massive storm hits with hailstones and a hurricane, and the wall comes crashing down, what good was that paint job you were so proud of?\'

'And that's for real what's gonna happen. I, God, the Master, am saying it: \'I'm about to unleash a hurricane of my anger, a storm of hailstones. I'll demolish that wall you covered in paint. I'll knock it flat to the ground, leaving only the foundation. And you'll all be goners in the rubble. Then you'll finally get that I am God.

'I'm going to unleash my fury on that wall and on everyone who plastered it. I'll tell them, \'The wall is gone, and so are the people who painted it—those so-called prophets of Israel who preached to Jerusalem, promising everything was fine when it was all about to fall apart. That's a decree from God, the Master.\'

'And the women prophets—son of man, you need to confront them too. These women are also just making things up. Stand up to them. Tell them \'You're doomed!\'—these women who make magic bracelets and custom head scarves, trying to trap people's souls. Say to them, \'Are you really going to destroy my people's souls and use them just to get rich and famous? You've disrespected me among my own people just to get ahead, using my name to make yourselves look good—killing souls that should have lived and protecting souls that should have died. You've been lying to people who just love to hear lies.\'

'So God says, \'I'm against all your little tricks and schemes you use to hunt down souls. I'm going to snatch them right out of your hands. I'll set free the souls you're trying to trap. I'll tear your magic bracelets and scarves to pieces and rescue my people from your grip so they're not your victims anymore. That's how you'll learn that I am God.

'Because you've confused good, innocent people with your lies, and you've made it easy for bad people to keep doing wrong, so it wouldn't even cross their minds to turn to me so I could save them, you're done. No more selling delusions, no more lying sermons. I'm rescuing my people from your clutches. And you'll realize that I am God.\'

Ezekiel.title: God's Done Playing Games
paragraphs: So, some of Israel's leaders came to chill with me. Then, boom, God's message dropped: "Son of Man, these people have basically set up idols in their hearts. They're obsessed with stuff that's gonna totally ruin them. So why should I even listen to what they have to say? Tell them the Lord GOD's message is this: Any Israelite who's all about idols and into the sin that will wreck them, but still has the nerve to come to a prophet, needs to know this: I, GOD, will personally give them the answer they deserve, right along with their whole squad of idols. I'm about to get real with the hearts of the people of Israel, since they've all ditched me for their idols."

"So, tell the house of Israel: 'The Lord GOD says, Repent! Turn your back on your fake idols. Ditch all your gross habits.
