This goes for every single person in Israel, and even the foreigners living there—anyone who turns away from me, gets obsessed with idols, and puts wickedness on a pedestal in their life, and then still has the audacity to ask a prophet for my opinion—I, GOD, will step in and answer them myself. I'll go right up against them, make an example out of them—a total warning—and cut them off so you'll know that I am GOD.

"'And if a prophet gets tricked and gives these idol-lovers the fake news they want to hear, I, GOD, am the one who allowed that prophet to be deceived. But he's not getting away with it. I'll grab him and kick him out of my people. They'll both be guilty, the prophet and the person who asked him. This is so the house of Israel will never wander away from me again or get dirty with their rebellious ways. Instead, they'll be my people, and I will be their God. That's the deal from the Lord GOD.'"

God's message came to me again: "Son of Man, if a country sins against me by being unfaithful, and I have to step in and cut off their food supply with a famine, wiping out people and animals, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job—the ultimate big three—were there, it wouldn't save anyone else. Their own righteousness would only save themselves." This is the decree of the Lord GOD.

"Or, what if I sent wild animals to tear through the country, making it so deserted that no one would even dare to go through it? Even if those three guys were living there, as surely as I am the living God, they couldn't even save their own sons or daughters. Only the three of them would be saved, and the country would become a wasteland.

"Or, what if I brought war on that country and was like, 'Let the swords go crazy!' killing people and animals? Even if those three were there, as surely as I am the living God, they couldn't save their sons or daughters. Only they would be rescued.

"Or, if I sent a deadly plague on that country, pouring out my fury and killing both people and animals, and Noah, Daniel, and Job were alive, as surely as I am the living God, they couldn't save a single son or daughter. Only those three would be delivered because they were righteous.

"So here's the deal," says the Lord GOD, "when I send my four terrible judgments on Jerusalem—war, famine, wild animals, and disease—to wipe out people and animals. But check this out, believe it or not, there will be survivors. Some of their sons and daughters will make it out. When they come to you and you see the messed-up lives they were saved from, you'll get why I had to bring such a harsh judgment on Jerusalem. It was necessary. Yeah, when you see how they were living, you'll feel better about it. You'll understand the reason for everything I did in Jerusalem." This is the decree of the Lord GOD.

Ezekiel.title: Useless Vine Gets Burned
paragraphs: Ayo, listen up. God hit me with this message: "My guy, for real, how does a grapevine's wood stack up against any random tree branch in the forest? You ever see anyone build something with vine wood? Or use it to make a peg to hang stuff on?

Yeah, I didn't think so. It's basically only good for firewood. And get this: it's just a flimsy piece of vine, you toss it in the fire, and then pull it out. The ends are burnt to a crisp and the middle is all charred. Is it good for anything now?
Hardly. It wasn't good for anything when it was whole, and being half-burnt is definitely not an upgrade. So what's it even good for?

So here's the message from God, the Master: Just like I chose that vine wood from all the other trees in the forest just to use as fuel for the fire, that's exactly how I'm gonna treat the people living in Jerusalem. I'm dead set against them. Even though they escaped the fire once, all charred and messed up, the fire's gonna totally consume them this time. When I make my stand against them, you'll know without a doubt that I am God. I'm going to turn this country into a total wasteland because they've been so unfaithful." That's the final word from God, the Master.

Ezekiel.title: Jerusalem's Glow-Up & Ghosting God: A Wild Story
paragraphs: God's message hit me up. He said, "Yo, son of man, you need to call out Jerusalem for all the wild stuff she's been doing. Tell her this is what the LORD God has to say: 'Jerusalem, your roots are in Canaan. Your dad was an Amorite and your mom was a Hittite.'

'Back on the day you were born, nobody even bothered to cut your umbilical cord. You weren't washed, nobody rubbed you with salt—which was a thing back then—or even wrapped you in a blanket. Literally no one cared about you. Not a single person did anything to show you some love. You were just tossed out in a field, all dirty and unwanted—a literal newborn nobody wanted.

'Then I came walking by. I saw you there, a total mess, all bloody and helpless. And I said to you, lying there in your own filth, "Live! And grow up, like a flower in the field." And you did. You grew up, got tall, and became a woman, with a full chest and long hair. But you were still totally naked and vulnerable, just out there and exposed.

'So I came by again and saw you were ready for love. I took you under my wing, gave you clothes, and kept you safe. I promised to love you and we got married—a covenant. I, the LORD God, gave you my word. You became mine. I gave you a good bath, washed off all that old blood, and put some nice-smelling oils on you. I hooked you up with a colorful dress and some leather sandals. I gave you linen shirts and a whole wardrobe of expensive clothes. I decked you out in jewelry: bracelets, a necklace, emerald rings, sapphire earrings, and a diamond crown. You had all the best and most beautiful things: amazing clothes and gourmet food, with honey and oil. You were drop-dead gorgeous. A queen! You got famous worldwide, a legendary beauty, all because of the drip I gave you. That's a decree from the LORD God.

'But all that beauty went straight to your head. You used your fame to become a common prostitute, just grabbing any guy who walked by and sleeping with him. You took the nice clothes I gave you and made little hookup tents out of them, turning them into brothels. That kind of thing should never, ever happen.

'And then you took the beautiful jewelry I gave you, my gold and my silver, and you made these gross pornographic idols for your brothels. You decorated your beds with fancy silks and used my special oils and incense to make them smell good. Then you took the amazing food I gave you—the fresh bread, fruit, and all the good spices—and you served it up like a fancy meal in your whorehouses. That's what you did, says the LORD God.

'And then you took your own sons and daughters—the children you had for me—and you killed them. You sacrificed them to your idols. Like, wasn't being a whore bad enough? Now you're a murderer, too, killing my kids and offering them up to idols.
'Not one time during all these years of your disgusting, obscene cheating did you even think about where you came from—how you were a naked, bloody, abandoned newborn.

'And then, to top off all your evil, you built your flashy brothels in every single town square. You are so doomed! says the LORD God. You set up shop on every major street corner, selling your body and spreading your legs for anyone who passed by.

'Then you took your business international. You started sleeping with the Egyptians, joining in on their crazy sex parties. The more you slept around, the angrier I got. Finally, I had to step in. I shrank your territory and let your enemies walk all over you. Even the Philistine women—and this is wild—were shocked by how slutty you were acting.

'But you didn't stop there. You went after the Assyrians. Your appetite was just endless. But you still weren't satisfied. So you hooked up with the Babylonians, a whole country of traders, and you still weren't satisfied.

'Man, your soul is so sick! You did all this stuff—you're like the world champion of whores! You built your brothels on every corner and in every neighborhood, but you were different from a regular whore because you refused to get paid.

'Wives who cheat on their husbands get gifts from their lovers. And guys usually pay prostitutes. But you pay your lovers! You bribe guys from all over to come sleep with you! You're the total opposite of a normal prostitute who gets paid for sex. You're paying guys for it! You've somehow made being a whore even more messed up!

'So, you whore, listen to God's message: The LORD God says, because you were so shameless in your cheating, stripping down for every lover, and because of your gross idols and all the children you murdered for them, I'm going to get all your lovers together—the ones you liked and the ones you hated. I'm gonna gather them all around you like a jury. And I'm gonna strip you naked in front of them, so they can all see the real you. Then I'm gonna sentence you like an adulterous, murderous woman. I'm gonna give you a taste of my fury!

'I'm gonna hand you over to your lovers. They're gonna tear down your brothels and sex shrines. They'll rip your clothes off, steal your jewelry, and leave you naked and exposed. Then they'll call a big meeting, and a mob will stone you and chop you up with swords. They'll burn down your houses. It's gonna be a huge public judgment—with all the other women watching!
'And that's how I'll put a stop to your life of whoring. No more paying guys to sleep with you! By then, my anger will be gone. My jealousy will chill out.

'Because you forgot what it was like when you were young and just kept making me mad with all your behavior, I'm gonna make you pay for it. Didn't you just keep making your disgusting sins worse and worse with your slutty ways?

'You know that saying, "Like mother, like daughter"? Everyone's gonna use that about you. You're just like your mother, who couldn't stand her husband and kids. And you're just like your sisters, who couldn't stand their husbands and kids. Your mother was a Hittite and your father was an Amorite.

'Your older sister is Samaria, who lived north of you with her daughters. Your younger sister is Sodom, who lived south of you with her daughters. And didn't you act just like them? Didn't you do the same disgusting things they did? Actually, it didn't take you long to get even worse than them! As sure as I am the living God, says the LORD, your sister Sodom and her daughters never did anything close to as bad as what you and your daughters have done.

'Your sister Sodom's sin was this: She and her daughters were living in total luxury—they were proud, ate way too much, and were super lazy. They didn't care about the poor and oppressed. They were arrogant and lived disgusting lives. And you know what I did? I got rid of them.

'And Samaria? She didn't even sin half as much as you. You've done way more obscene things than she ever did. You make your two sisters look good by comparison! Seriously, they look like saints next to you. Because you've out-sinned them so badly, you've actually made them look righteous. Aren't you ashamed? Well, you're gonna have to live with it. You'll go down in history as the one who out-sinned her two sisters!

'But I'm going to turn their fortunes around—Sodom's and Samaria's. And guess what? I'll turn your fortune around right along with them! Still, you're going to have to live with your shame. And by accepting your shame, you'll actually make your two sisters feel a little better. Your sisters, Sodom and Samaria, will go back to how they were before, and you'll go back to how you were before. Remember when you were so arrogant, acting all high and mighty, looking down on your sister Sodom? That was before your own evil was exposed. Now you're the one everyone makes fun of—the Edomite women, the Philistine women, and everyone around. You just have to deal with it, accept the shame of your disgusting and vile life. That's a decree from the LORD God.

'The LORD God says, I'm going to do to you exactly what you did. You treated my promise like it was nothing and broke our covenant. But still, I'll remember the covenant I made with you when you were young, and I'll make a new, everlasting covenant with you. You'll remember your messed-up past and feel true regret when you get your sisters back, both the older and the younger one. I'll give them to you as daughters, but they won't be part of your covenant. I'll establish my covenant with you, and you'll know that I am God. You'll remember your past and be so ashamed, but when I forgive you for everything you've done, it will leave you speechless.' That's the decree of the LORD God."

Ezekiel.title: Two Eagles, One Vine, and a Whole Lotta Drama
paragraphs: God's message hit me up. He said, "Son of man, drop a riddle for the house of Israel. Tell them a story. Say, 'The Lord, the Master, says:

'A huge eagle, like, massive wingspan, crazy long feathers, super colorful and bright, flew over to Lebanon. It snapped the top right off a cedar tree, broke off the top branch, and carried it off to this land full of business people, dropping it in a city of shopkeepers. Then it took a cutting from the land and planted it in some really good, well-watered soil, like you'd plant a willow by a river. It sprouted and grew into this awesome vine, but it stayed low to the ground. Its branches reached up toward the eagle, and its roots got super established—a legit vine with shoots and branches popping out.

'Then another huge eagle showed up, also with a massive wingspan and thick feathers. And this vine, from where it was planted, started sending its roots out toward the new eagle. Its branches stretched out, trying to get water from him, even from far away. It was planted in good, rich soil, and it was supposed to grow branches, produce fruit, and become this noble, amazing vine.

'The Lord, the Master, asks, Is this thing really going to thrive? Won't the first eagle just rip it up by the roots, leave its fruit to rot, and all its branches to shrivel up into a dead, withered vine? It wouldn't even take much effort or a big crew to pull it up. And even if it gets moved, will it do well? When that hot east wind hits it, won't it just shrivel up? Won't it just dry up and blow away from the very spot where it was planted?'

'The Lord, the Master, says, Is it gonna thrive? Nah. Won't he just yank it up by the roots, let the grapes rot, and the branches wither? A dead, dried-up vine. It won't take a big army or much muscle to pull it up. Even if you transplant it, is it gonna make it? When that hot east wind blows, it's gonna shrivel up for sure. It'll dry up and blow away right from its own garden.'
God's message came to me again: "Go tell these rebels, 'Do you even get it? Do you have any clue what this means?'

"Tell them, 'The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, took its king and leaders, and brought them back to Babylon. He took a guy from the royal family, made a deal with him, and made him swear loyalty. The king of Babylon took all the top dogs into exile to make sure this kingdom stayed weak—so it wouldn't get any big ideas—and so it would keep the deal with him to even have a future.

"'But what did he do? He rebelled. He sent his people to Egypt to try and get horses and a huge army. You think that's gonna work? You think he's gonna get away with that? Does anyone just break a promise like that and get off scot-free?

"'As sure as I'm the living God, this king who broke his promise and his deal will die in that country, in Babylon. And Pharaoh, with his big army and all those soldiers, won't lift a finger to help him when Babylon attacks the city and wipes everyone out. Because he broke his word and the covenant, even after giving his solemn promise, and because he went and did all this stuff anyway, he's not getting away.

"'So, the Lord, the Master, says, As sure as I am the living God, because the king dissed my oath and broke my covenant, I'm gonna make the consequences crash down on his head. I'll send a search party for him and catch him. I'll take him to Babylon and put him on trial for completely disrespecting me. All his best soldiers and the rest of the army will be killed in battle, and anyone who's left will be scattered everywhere. Then you'll know that I, God, have spoken.

"'The Lord, the Master, says, But I'm personally going to take a shoot from the very top of that tall cedar, a cutting from the crown of the tree, and I'll plant it on a high and majestic mountain, on the high mountain of Israel. It will grow, putting out branches and fruit—a truly majestic cedar. All kinds of birds will come and live under it. They'll build nests in the shade of its branches. Then all the trees in the field will know that I, God, am the one who makes the big tree small and the small tree big, who makes the green tree dry up and the dry tree sprout green branches. I, God, said it—and I did it.'ll do it.' do it.' do it.'"

Ezekiel.title: Your Choices, Your Consequences
paragraphs: God's message came to me, and he was like, 'What's with this saying everyone keeps repeating all over the country? 'The parents ate sour grapes, and the kids are the ones with the stomachache.'

'For real, as I live and breathe,' says God, 'you're not going to be using that saying in Israel anymore. Every single person—man, woman, child—is mine. The parent and the kid, both belong to me. You die for your own screw-ups, not someone else's.'

'Picture this: a guy who lives a good life, treats people right, and keeps his relationships solid. He doesn't join in on pagan worship, doesn't get into all the idol stuff that's so popular in Israel, doesn't try to get with his neighbor's wife, doesn't sleep around, doesn't push people around, doesn't get into crazy debt, doesn't steal, always helps out the hungry and gives clothes to those who need them, doesn't take advantage of the poor, isn't driven by greed, and treats everyone the same. He follows my rules and sticks to my laws. This guy, who lives right, will have a full and real life. That's a promise from God, the boss.'

'But what if this guy has a kid who's a total mess—violent, a murderer, and does all the things the dad never did? He's all about the pagan shrines, goes after his neighbor's wife, bullies the weak, steals, racks up debt, is obsessed with idols, does some seriously messed-up stuff, and takes advantage of the poor. You think this kid is gonna live? No way. He's done all this terrible stuff, so he's going to die, and it'll be his own fault.'

'Now, let's say that kid has a son who sees all the messed-up things his dad did. He sees it, but he doesn't follow in his dad's footsteps. He doesn't get into pagan worship, doesn't care about the popular idols, doesn't try to get with his neighbor's wife, doesn't bully anyone, is willing to help people out, doesn't steal, always gives food to the hungry and clothes to those who need them, isn't greedy, and doesn't take advantage of the poor. He does what I say, follows my laws, and lives by my rules. This person won't die for his dad's mistakes; he'll live a good life. But the dad will die for what he did—for hurting the weak, robbing people, and doing what's totally wrong.'

'Are you seriously asking, 'So why doesn't the kid have to pay for his dad's mistakes?' Isn't it obvious? It's because the kid did what was right. Since he was careful to do what was right and fair, he'll live a good life. The person who messes up is the one who dies. The kid doesn't get blamed for the parent's mistakes, and the parent doesn't get blamed for the kid's. If you live a good life, you get the credit; if you live a bad life, you're the one who's guilty.'

'But if a bad person turns away from their messed-up life and starts following all my rules, living a good and fair life, they'll live. For real, they won't die. I'm not going to hold on to a list of all their past mistakes. They will live. Do you think I like it when bad people die? No, what I really want is for them to turn their lives around and start living right—really living.'

'The same goes for a good person who turns their back on a good life and starts messing up, doing the same terrible things that bad people do. You think they're going to live? I don't keep a record of all the good things they did, like a bank account they can just draw from. Because they turned their back on me and piled up all that bad stuff, they'll die.'

'Are you really saying, 'That's not fair! God's not fair!'? Listen up, Israel. You think I'm not fair? You're the ones who aren't being fair! If a good person turns away from their good life and starts doing bad things, they'll die for it. They'll die for their own mistakes. And if a bad person turns away from their bad life and starts living a good and fair life, they'll save their life. Because they owned up to all the wrong they did and left it behind, they will live. For real, they won't die.'
'And yet, Israel keeps complaining, 'That's not fair! God's not fair.' You think I'm not fair, Israel? You're the ones who aren't fair.'

'So here's the deal, Israel: I'm going to judge each of you based on how you live. So turn your life around! Stop being rebellious so your mistakes don't drag you down. Clean up your act. No more rebelling, please. Get a new heart! Get a new spirit! Why would you choose to die, Israel? I don't get any pleasure from anyone's death. That's a promise from God, the boss. So make a clean break! Live!'

Ezekiel.title: Royalty to Ruin: A Sad Song for Israel's Princes
paragraphs: Go ahead and sing a sad song for the leaders of Israel. It goes like this:

Man, your mom was like this total boss lioness. She hung out with a whole crew of lions, and her cubs got super strong. She raised one of them to be this absolute unit of a lion. He learned to hunt and, no cap, he started hunting people. Other countries freaked out and set a trap. They caught him, put hooks in him, and dragged him all the way to Egypt.

So when the momma lion realized her first son was a lost cause, she was like, 'Alright, bet.' She took her other cub and trained him up to be another beast. He rolled with the other lions, learned to hunt, and yeah, he hunted people too. This dude went on a rampage, wrecking their towns and leaving them in shambles. The whole country was shook by his roar. So, all the nations teamed up to take him down. They set traps and finally caught him. They slapped a wooden collar on him and shipped him off to the king of Babylon. You wouldn't hear his roar in the mountains of Israel ever again.

Okay, let me put it another way. Your mom was like a grapevine planted by a river, totally thriving with tons of branches and grapes because it had all the water it needed. It grew these super strong branches, the kind you could make a king's scepter from. It grew so tall it was basically touching the clouds. Its branches were everywhere, and everyone could see it. But then, someone got mad, ripped it out of the ground, and just threw it down. A hot wind came and dried it all up, stripping off all its fruit. Those strong branches got so dry they were only good for firewood. Now it's just a dead stick in the middle of a desert, totally useless except for starting a campfire. There's no trace of those awesome branches that could've been a royal scepter.
(This is a sad song, the kind you sing when you've got the blues.)

Ezekiel.title: God Spills the Tea on Israel's Messy History
paragraphs: So, get this. It was the seventh year, fifth month, tenth day. Some of Israel's leaders came to get some advice from God, and they were just sitting there in front of me.

Then God's message hit me: "Son of man, go talk to the leaders of Israel. Tell them, 'God, the Master, is saying this: You came to ask me questions? For real? As long as I'm alive, I'm not dealing with questions from you. That's a decree from God, the Master.'"
"Son of man, why don't you just do it? Yeah, go on. Call them out. Confront them with the totally messed-up stuff their ancestors did. Tell them that God, the Master, says:

"'The day I chose Israel, I revealed myself to them in Egypt. I made a huge, solemn promise to Jacob's descendants, saying, 'I am God, *your* personal God.' That same day, I swore I'd get them out of Egypt and bring them to a land I had scouted out just for them—a land flowing with milk and honey, like, the best place ever.
"'Back then, I told them, 'Get rid of all the gross things you're obsessed with. Don't get yourselves all dirty with those fake Egyptian gods. I'm the only God, your God.'

"'But they totally rebelled against me and wouldn't listen to a single thing I said. Nobody got rid of the nasty stuff they were addicted to. They clung to Egypt's fake gods like their lives depended on it. I was *this* close to unleashing my anger on them right there in Egypt. But then I chilled out. I acted based on who I am, not how I felt. I did it in a way that would get me respect, not hate, from the nations around them who saw me reveal myself by promising to lead my people out of Egypt. And then I did it: I led them out of Egypt and into the desert.

"'I gave them rules to live by, showed them how to live a good life by listening to me. I also gave them my weekly holy rest days, my 'Sabbaths,' which were like a sign between me and them to show them that I, God, am the one making them holy.

"'But Israel rebelled against me in the desert. They didn't follow my rules. They hated my laws for living a good and obedient life. And they completely disrespected my holy Sabbaths. I seriously thought about just letting all my anger out on them right there in the desert. But I took a breath and acted based on my character, not my feelings, so the other nations who saw me bring them out would respect me, not trash-talk me. But I did make a serious promise in the desert that I wouldn't bring them into that amazing land flowing with milk and honey that I had picked for them. I took back my promise because they hated my laws, wouldn't follow my rules, and kept disrespecting my holy Sabbaths. They'd rather live by their fake idol gods. But I didn't go all the way; I didn't completely wipe them out in the desert.

"'Then I talked to their kids in the desert: 'Don't be like your parents. Don't follow their ways. Don't get yourselves dirty with their fake gods. I am God, your God. Follow my rules and live by my laws. Keep my Sabbaths as holy rest days, signs between us that I am God, your God.'

"'But the kids rebelled against me too. They didn't follow my rules or keep my laws for living right. And they disrespected my Sabbaths. I was so ready to just dump my anger on them, right there in the desert. But again, I held back. I acted based on who I am, not how I felt, so the nations who saw me bring them out would honor me.

"'But I did make a solemn promise in the desert. I swore I'd scatter them all over the world, sending them everywhere because they didn't keep my laws or live by my statutes. They disrespected my Sabbaths and were still addicted to their parents' fake gods. Since they were so set on living bad lives, I gave them rules that were no good and laws that couldn't lead to life. I just left them to it. They got filthy, and in a twisted move, they sacrificed their firstborn kids in the fire. The horror of that should have been a wake-up call for them to realize that I am God.'

"So, son of man, speak to Israel. Tell them God says, 'And if that wasn't bad enough, your ancestors insulted me even more by betraying me. When I brought them into the land I had promised to give them, every time they saw a hill with some sketchy sex-and-religion shrine or a bunch of trees where sacred prostitutes did their thing, they were there, all in on the pagan stuff. I asked them, 'What's this hill you keep going to?'' (It's still called 'Whore Hills' today, btw.)

"So, say to Israel, 'This is the message from God, the Master: You're messing up your lives by copying your parents. By repeating their disgusting habits, you've become just like them. By burning your kids as sacrifices, you've become as filthy as your fake gods—even today!
"'And you think I'm going to answer questions from people like you, Israel? As sure as I am the living God, I, God, the Master, refuse to be questioned by you!
"'And that little thought you're having? It's never gonna happen. You're thinking, 'We'll just be like everyone else, like the other nations. We'll worship gods we can make and control.'

"'As sure as I am the living God, says God, the Master, think again! With a huge show of strength and a terrifying wave of anger, I will be your King! I'll bring you back from the nations, gather you from all the countries where you've been scattered, with my power and my anger. I'll bring you to the 'desert of nations' and put you on trial, face-to-face with my judgment.

"'Just like I judged your ancestors in the desert of Egypt, I'm going to judge you. I'll check out every single person as you come, and I'll bring you into the covenant. I'll kick out the rebels and traitors. I'll lead them out of exile, but they're not coming back to Israel.
"'Then you'll finally get that I am God.

"'But as for you, people of Israel, this is the message from God, the Master: Go on, serve your fake idols! But later, you'll change your minds and stop disrespecting me with your pagan gifts and fake gods. Because on my holy mountain, the high mountain of Israel, I, God, the Master, declare that the entire nation of Israel will worship me. I'll welcome them there with open arms. I'll expect your best gifts and offerings, all your holy sacrifices. What's more, I'll receive you as the best kind of offering when I bring you back from all the lands where you've been scattered. I'll show the whole world that I am The Holy One. When I bring you back to the land of Israel, the land I solemnly promised to your ancestors, you'll realize that I am God. Then and there you'll remember everything you've done, the way you lived that made you so filthy—and you'll be disgusted with yourselves.

"'But, dear Israel, you'll also realize that I am God when I deal with you based on who I am, not based on the evil lives you've lived and the corrupt history you've made. That's a decree from God, the Master.'"
God's message came to me: "Son of man, face south. Let the message flow out against the south. Prophesy against the wilderness forest of the south.

"Tell the forest of the south, 'Listen to God's message! God, the Master, says, I'm going to start a fire in you that will burn up every single tree, the dead ones and the live ones. No one will be able to put out the fire. The whole country from south to north will be scorched by it. Everyone's going to see that I, God, started the fire and it's not going out.'"
And I was like, "Oh, God, everyone is saying I just make up stories."

Ezekiel.title: God's Sword Is Coming for EVERYONE
paragraphs: God’s message hit me up: “Yo, Son of Man, face Jerusalem and just let this message flow out against the Sanctuary. Prophesy against Israel and tell them, ‘God’s message is here: I’m actually against you. I’m pulling my sword out, and it’s game over for everyone—the good and the bad. And because I’m not playing favorites, my sword is gonna be felt by everyone from the south to the north. The whole world will know I’m not messing around.’
“So, my guy, you gotta start groaning. Like, double over in pain and make a huge scene!

“When they ask you, ‘Bro, why are you groaning and making such a fuss?’ you tell them, ‘Because of the news that’s about to drop. It’s gonna leave everyone speechless. Hearts will literally stop, and knees will turn to jelly. For real, it’s coming. There’s no stopping it. That’s a decree from the Lord GOD himself.’”
God’s message came to me again: “Son of Man, prophesy. Tell them, ‘The Lord says this:
“‘A sword! A sword! It’s razor-sharp and polished, sharpened to kill, and polished to flash like lightning!
“‘My kid, you totally disrespected the royal authority of Judah by bowing down to every fake idol out there.
“‘Yeah, you dissed the scepter of Judah by worshiping those tree-idols.
“‘This sword is made to shine, to be held and swung. It’s sharpened and polished, all ready for the killer to go to work.’
“‘This sword is made to glisten, to be held and brandished. It’s sharpened and polished, ready to be brandished by the killer.’
“So scream and wail, Son of Man. This sword is coming for my own people! The leaders of Israel and my people—they’re all being left for the sword to deal with! So just freak out! Tear your hair out!
“Scream and wail, Son of Man. The sword is against my people! The princes of Israel and my people—abandoned to the sword! Wring your hands! Tear out your hair!
“‘A test is coming. So why did you brush off discipline? You can’t just ignore it. This is a decree from the Lord GOD.’
“‘Testing is coming. Why have you despised discipline? You can’t get around it. Decree of God, the Master.’

“So, prophesy, Son of Man! Clap your hands. Get their attention. Tell them the sword is coming down—once, twice, even three times. It’s a sword for a total massacre, a relentless sword you can’t escape. People will be dropping left and right like dominoes. I’ve put a deadly sword at every city gate, flashing like lightning, ready to kill. Go right, slash left, you deadly, sharp-edged sword! Then I’ll clap my hands too, as a sign that my anger is finally done. I, GOD, have said it.”

“So, prophesy, son of man! Clap your hands. Get their attention. Tell them that the sword’s coming down once, twice, three times. It’s a sword to kill, a sword for a massacre, A sword relentless, a sword inescapable— People collapsing right and left, going down like dominoes. I’ve stationed a murderous sword at every gate in the city, Flashing like lightning, brandished murderously. Cut to the right, thrust to the left, murderous, sharp-edged sword! Then I’ll clap my hands, a signal that my anger is spent. I, God, have spoken.”

God’s message came to me: “Son of Man, map out two roads for the king of Babylon’s sword to take. They both start from the same place. Put a signpost where the roads split. One sign points the way for the sword to Rabbah of the Ammonites. The other sign points to Judah and the fortress of Jerusalem. The king of Babylon is standing at that fork in the road, trying to figure out which way to go using magic. He’s drawing straws, rolling some kind of god-dice, and checking out a goat’s liver. He looks at his right hand: the sign says, ‘Go for Jerusalem!’ So now he’s on his way with battering rams, ready to kill, shouting battle cries, breaking down city gates, and building siege ramps.
“To the leaders of Judah, who made their own promises, this will seem like a bogus prediction. But he’s going to call them out on their guilt, and they’re all going to be captured.
“So this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Because your sin is now completely exposed for everyone to see, you’re going to be taken captive.

“‘And you, Zedekiah, you blasphemous and evil prince of Israel: your time is up. It’s punishment payday. God says, take off your royal crown. Business as usual is over. The underdog is getting a promotion, and the top dog is getting demoted. Ruins, ruins, ruins! I’m turning this whole place into ruins. And it’ll stay that way until the one who has the right to it comes. Then I’ll give it to him.’
“But, Son of Man, your job is to prophesy. Tell them, ‘This is the message from the Lord GOD against the Ammonites and their cruel trash talk:

“‘A sword! A sword! Pulled out to kill, sharp as a razor, flashing like lightning. Even though there’s all this fake news about the sword going around in Ammon, it’s still coming to slice the necks of the Ammonites, because it’s their punishment payday. Put the sword back! I’m going to judge you right in your own homeland, where you grew up. I’ll pour out my anger on you, breathing fire down your neck. I’ll hand you over to brutal men who are experts in torture. You’ll end up as firewood. Your country will be littered with dead bodies. No one will even remember you. I, GOD, have spoken.’”

Ezekiel.title: God Calls Out the Whole City (It's Bad)
paragraphs: God's message hit me up, and it was like, "Yo, son of man, are you gonna call out this messed-up, violent city or not? C'mon, are you gonna judge it? Then do it. You gotta confront them with all the wild stuff they're doing. Tell them, 'This is what God, the Master, is saying: You're a city that's murderous deep down, just asking for trouble. You're obsessed with fake gods, making yourselves totally gross. With all your killing, you've racked up some serious guilt. With all your idol-making, you've just gotten filthy. You've basically hit the self-destruct button on your own existence. I'm gonna put you on display as a total joke to the world, the biggest laughingstock. People from all over will make fun of you for being so nasty and chaotic.'"

"Your leaders, the princes of Israel right there with you, are all trying to outdo each other in crime. Your whole community disrespects parents, treats foreigners like trash, and bullies orphans and widows. You couldn't care less about my holy things and you totally ignore my Sabbaths. You've got people spreading lies and causing bloodshed, running to the hills for these weird sex parties and just going wild. Incest is a thing now. Guys are forcing themselves on women whenever they want. It's total chaos when it comes to sex. It's a free-for-all: your neighbor, your daughter-in-law, your own sister. You can even hire someone to kill for you, charging insane interest is normal, and ripping people off is just another Tuesday.
"'And you've completely forgotten about me. That's a decree from God, the Master.'

"'So look! I'm clapping my hands, like, 'Hello?!' to get your attention about all the greedy, violent stuff you're doing. You think you can handle what's coming? You think you'll be able to stand it when I start dealing with you?'

"'I, God, have said it. I'm gonna put a stop to this. I'm gonna scatter you everywhere, all over the world. I'm gonna force you to stop your disgusting lifestyle. You'll be humiliated, covered in your own filth for all the world to see. And then you'll finally get that I am God.'"

God's message came to me again: "Son of man, the people of Israel are like slag to me—you know, the useless gunk that's left over after you melt down good metals like copper, tin, iron, and lead. Just a worthless pile of junk. So tell them, 'God, the Master, has spoken: Because you've all become useless slag, I'm warning you: I'm gonna gather all of you in Jerusalem. Just like people throw silver, copper, iron, lead, and tin into a super-hot furnace and blast it with fire to melt it all down, that's what I'm gonna do to you in my anger. I'll gather you up and melt you down. I'll blast you with the fire of my fury and melt you in the furnace. Just like silver melts, you'll be melted. That should get the message through. Then you'll know that I, God, have unleashed my anger on you.'"

God's message came to me: "Son of man, tell her, 'You're a land that got zero rain when I was angry with you, not even a little shower. The leaders among you got desperate, like roaring lions just killing whatever they see. They grabbed and stole everything, leaving a bunch of widows behind.'

"'Your priests totally ignored my law and disrespected my holy things. They act like there's no difference between what's sacred and what's not. They tell people that right and wrong are basically the same. They have zero respect for my holy Sabbaths, and they make me look bad by trying to drag me down to their level. Your politicians are like wolves, prowling around, killing, and greedily taking whatever they want. And your preachers? They just cover for the politicians, faking visions and special messages. They're like, 'This is what God, the Master, says...' when God hasn't said a single word. Extortion is everywhere, robbery is an epidemic, the poor and needy get abused, and outsiders are treated like dirt with no way to get justice.'

"'I looked for someone, anyone, who would stand up for me against all this, who would fix the city's defenses, who would take a stand in the gap to protect this land so I wouldn't have to destroy it. But I couldn't find a single person. Not one. So I'm gonna pour out my anger on them, burn them to a crisp with my hot fury, and make them face the consequences of everything they've done. That's a decree from God, the Master.'"

Ezekiel.title: The Wild Story of Two Sisters & Their Bad Choices
paragraphs: God hit me up with a message: "Yo, son of man, listen up. There were these two sisters, same mom and everything. They started messing around way back when they were young in Egypt. Guys were all over them from the get-go. The older one was Oholah, and the younger one was Oholibah. They were mine, and they had kids.
Just so you know, Oholah is basically Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.

So Oholah, even though she was with me, started chasing other guys. She was obsessed with the Assyrians—these military dudes in sharp blue uniforms, important-looking officials, all handsome and riding fancy horses. She couldn't get enough. She went all in, sleeping with the top Assyrian guys and getting into all their idol worship stuff. She never quit the wild life she started back in Egypt, just kept sleeping around with anyone who'd give her attention.

So I was like, 'Fine, have it your way,' and let her go with the Assyrians she was so crazy about. They totally wrecked her life. They stripped her, took her kids, and then, the ultimate humiliation, they killed her. Her name basically became 'Shame'—a total cautionary tale.

Her sister Oholibah saw all this go down, but believe it or not, she got even crazier with her lust and wild living. She also went nuts for the Assyrians: all the big shots, the well-dressed soldiers on their awesome horses—the whole Assyrian elite. I saw she was getting just as messy. Both sisters were on the same track. But Oholibah took it to another level. When she saw carvings of Babylonian guys on the walls, all painted red, looking fly with fancy belts and turbans, all looking super important—famous Babylonians!—she went wild and slid into their DMs, inviting them over. The Babylonians came running, hooked up with her, and just made a mess of her life. After they completely used her, she got bored of them. Then she just put her whole messy life on blast for everyone to see.

I turned my back on her, just like I did with her sister. But that didn't stop her. She went even harder. She started thinking about her younger days, when she first started hooking up in Egypt. That just made her want even more intense, vulgar guys—like stallions who couldn't be controlled. She was nostalgic for the wildness of her youth in Egypt, where guys were all over her.

'So, Oholibah, this is the deal from God, the Master: I'm about to sic your old flames on you, the ones you got tired of and ghosted. I'm bringing them at you from all sides—the Babylonians, all the Chaldeans, Pekod, Shoa, and Koa, and all the Assyrians. All those good-looking young guys, the officials and governors, the elite officers and celebs, all on their fancy horses. They're gonna roll up on you from the north, fully armed, with chariots and a massive army. I'm letting them be the judges. They'll punish you their way. I'll be against you, no holding back, as they tear you apart. They'll mutilate you, cutting off your ears and nose, and killing whoever's left. They'll take your kids as slaves, and anyone who survives will be burned. They'll rip off your clothes and steal your jewelry. I'm shutting down your whole wild lifestyle, the one you started in Egypt. You won't be looking back on it fondly anymore. You won't be daydreaming about Egypt.

'A message from God, the Master: I'm about to hand you over to the very people you hate, the ones who now disgust you. They'll treat you with pure hatred, leave you naked and exposed for everyone to see. Your whole lustful, messy life will be out in the open. Your own choices brought you here, because you chased after other nations and got dirty with their fake gods.
'You copied your sister's life. So now you're going to drink from the same cup she did.'
'This is the message from God, the Master:

'You're going to drink your sister's cup, and it's a cup as deep as a canyon and as wide as an ocean. You'll be made fun of and mocked as you drink it all down. You'll be blackout drunk, and you'll be crying your eyes out as you drink from that cup of pure terror. It's the cup of your sister, Samaria. You'll drink every last drop, then you'll smash it and eat the pieces, and end up tearing at your own body. I've said it—this is a decree from God, the Master.

'So, God, the Master, says: Because you completely forgot about me, pushed me to the side, you now have to face the consequences for what you've done—pay for your messy sex life and all your cheating.'"

Then God said to me, "Son of man, are you going to confront Oholah and Oholibah about what they've done? You need to make them face their insane behavior, from cheating to actual murder. They cheated on me with their fake idols, and then sacrificed the children they had with me to feed those idols! And that's not all. They also disrespected my holy Temple and my holy Sabbaths. On the exact same day they sacrificed their kids to idols, they walked right into my Temple and trashed it. That's what they did—in my own house!

"On top of that, they sent out special messengers to invite guys from far away—and of course, they came. The sisters got all dolled up, put on makeup and sexy clothes. They lounged on a fancy bed, with incense and oils burning—my incense and my oils! A whole crowd gathered, a rowdy, drunk mob. They put bracelets on the sisters' arms and crowns on their heads.

"I said, 'She's gotta be tired of this life!' but that didn't stop them. Guys kept showing up, day and night, like men chasing after a prostitute. That's how they treated Oholah and Oholibah, these two worn-out women.
"Good people will judge them, sentencing them for adultery and murder. Because that's what their lives were about: adultery and murder."
"God says, 'Unleash a mob on them. Let them be terrorized and robbed! Let the mob stone them and chop them to pieces—kill all their children, burn down their houses!

"'I'm going to put an end to this kind of sluttish behavior in this country, so that all women will get the message and not copy you. You'll pay the price for all your obsessive cheating. You'll pay in full for your affairs with idols. And then you'll finally realize that I am God, the Master.'"

Ezekiel.title: God's CRAZY Stew Pot Prophecy
paragraphs: So, God's message hit me up in the ninth year, tenth month, and tenth day. He was like, 'Yo, son of man, you gotta write down today's date. The king of Babylon has surrounded Jerusalem, like, right now. And you need to tell this rebellious crew a story.'

'Get the stew pot out. Fill it up with water. Throw in some big chunks of meat, all the good stuff—we're talking loin and brisket. Grab the best bones from the best sheep you can find. Stack up a bunch of wood underneath, get that thing boiling, and let it cook.'
'The Lord God is saying this:
'It's over for the city of murderers, for that pot caked with so much gunk you can't even scrub it clean. Just dump out the pot, piece by piece. Don't even worry about who gets what.'

'The evidence of all the killing is all over the city. Blood is literally on the streets, and no one's even trying to clean it up. It's just out there for everyone to see, and it's seriously making me angry, like, ready to get my revenge.'

'The evidence of all the killing is all over the city. Blood is literally on the streets, and no one's even trying to clean it up. It's just out there for everyone to see, and it's seriously making me angry, like, ready to get my revenge.'
'So, this is what the Lord God says:

'It's over for the city of murderers! I'm gonna pile on the wood myself. Stack it high, light it up, cook the meat, season it, dump the broth, and then just burn the bones. Then I'll put the empty pot on the fire and heat it until it's glowing red-hot. That way the bronze will glow, all the germs will be killed, and all the nasty stuff will be burned off. But honestly, it's hopeless. It's too far gone. The gunk is just too thick.'

'Your caked-on filth is your disgusting lifestyle. I wanted to clean you up, but you wouldn't let me. So I'm not even gonna try to clean you anymore until my anger finally chills out. I, God, have said it, and I'm gonna do it. I'm not holding back. I have no more sympathy. I'm not changing my mind. You're getting exactly what you deserve. That's a decree from the Lord God.'

God's message came to me: 'Son of man, I'm about to take the delight of your life away from you—it's gonna be a huge blow, I know. But please, no crying. Keep your sadness to yourself. No public mourning. Just get dressed like normal and go to work—none of the usual funeral stuff.'
I preached to the people in the morning. That evening, my wife died. The next morning, I did exactly what I was told.
The people came up to me and were like, 'Tell us why you're acting like this. What's this all about?'

So I told them, 'God's word came to me, and he said, 'Tell the family of Israel, This is what the Lord God says: I'm going to destroy my own Sanctuary, the place you're so proud of, your impenetrable fort, the delight of your life, the thing your heart wants most. And the kids you left behind? They're going to be killed.'

'Then you'll do exactly what I've done. You won't do any of the usual funeral rituals. You'll get dressed like normal and go about your work. No tears. But your sins will eat you up from the inside, and you'll just groan to each other. Ezekiel will be your example. The way he did it is the way you'll do it.'
'When this happens, you'll finally get that I am the Lord God.'

'And you, son of man: on the day I take away the people's safe place, their great joy, the delight of their life, what they've wanted most, along with all their children—on that exact day, a survivor will show up and tell you what happened to the city. You'll break your silence and start talking again, talking to the survivor. Once again, you'll be an example for them. And they'll finally get that I am God.'

Ezekiel.title: God's Payback on Israel's Haters
paragraphs: God's message hit me up:

"Yo, son of man, face the Ammonites and call them out. Tell them to listen up to the message from God, the Master. This is what God's gotta say: Since you were all hyped and cheering when my holy place got wrecked, when Judah's land was torn up, and when Israel's people were dragged off into exile, I'm handing you over to the people from the east. They're gonna roll in, set up camp, eat your food, and drink your milk. I'm turning your main city, Rabbah, into a camel pasture and your towns into sheep pens. Then you'll finally get that I am God.

God, the Master, says: Because you clapped and cheered, throwing all your nasty shade at the land of Israel, I'm about to step in and let you be looted by whoever gets there first. I'm erasing you from the list of nations. You'll be totally gone. And you'll get that I am God.

God, the Master, says: Because Moab was like, 'LOL, Judah is nothing special,' I'm gonna expose Moab's whole side by letting its border towns get attacked—Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim. I'm lumping Moab in with Ammon and giving them to the easterners to take over. Ammon will be a nobody. I'm gonna punish Moab hard. And they'll get that I am God.

God, the Master, says: Because Edom was extra petty and went for revenge against Judah, acting all vengeful and out of line, I, God, the Master, am coming for Edom. I'll wipe out everyone, people and animals. I'll waste the whole place—bodies will be stacked from Teman to Dedan. I'll use my own people, Israel, to serve my revenge on Edom. My anger will be their fuel. And they'll know it's my payback. That's a decree from God the Master.

God, the Master, says: Because the Philistines were so spiteful with their revenge—holding onto that grudge for centuries!—and tried their best to destroy Judah, I, God, the Master, am coming for the Philistines. I'll take down the Cretans and anyone else left on the coast. It's gonna be huge acts of revenge, massive punishments! When I finally bring my vengeance, they'll know for sure that I am God."

Ezekiel.title: Tyre's Epic Downfall for Hating on Jerusalem
paragraphs: So, in the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, God hit me up with a message. He said, "Son of man, Tyre was lowkey celebrating when they heard Jerusalem was crushed.
They were shouting, 'Let's go! The main gateway city is smashed! Now all their trade is gonna come our way. They're in ruins, and we're about to be loaded.'
"Because of that, the Lord GOD has something to say:

"'I'm coming for you, Tyre. I'm gonna send a ton of nations to crash against you, just like the ocean waves crash on the shore. They're gonna tear down your walls and smash your towers. I'll scrape away all your dirt until you're nothing but bare rock. You'll just be a rocky island in the sea, only good for drying fishnets. For real, I've said it.' This is the decree of the Lord GOD. 'You'll be free loot for all the nations! And all your little towns on the mainland will get wrecked. Then they'll finally get that I am the LORD.'

"The Lord GOD says: 'Check this out! From the north, I'm sending King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon—the king of all kings—to deal with you, Tyre. He's rolling up with horses, chariots, and a massive army. He's gonna wipe out your mainland towns and set up a siege. He'll build ramps right up to your walls and his army will be a wall of shields against you! He'll pound your walls with battering rams and shatter your towers with his weapons. The dust from his army of horses will be so thick you can't see. The noise of his warhorses and chariots pouring through your broken walls will be insane. It'll be like an earthquake hitting a city in total shock. Horses will be running wild in your streets. Your people will be killed, and your huge, strong pillars will fall like they're nothing. The invaders will take all your money and valuables. They'll tear down your nice houses and throw all the rubble—stone and wood—into the ocean. And your famous parties? They're over. No more music, no more good times. I'm gonna turn you into a bare rock, a place just for drying fishnets. You will never be rebuilt. I, the LORD, have spoken. This is the decree of the Lord GOD.'
"This is the Lord GOD's message to Tyre: 'The islands are gonna shake when they hear about your epic collapse, the screams of your wounded people, and all the chaos and killing.'

"'All the princes from the coast will get off their thrones, take off their fancy robes, and dress in clothes of pure fear. They'll sit on the ground, totally shook, horrified by what happened to you. Then they'll start singing a funeral song for you:

"'No way! She's sunk! The famous city on the sea is gone, sunk to the bottom. You and your people were a sea power, making everyone who lived near you scared. But now, the islands are shaking from the sound of your fall. The islands in the sea are trembling from the shock of your collapse.'

"The Lord GOD says: 'When I make you a ghost town, a city with no one left, and when I bring the deep ocean waters to cover you, I'm gonna send you down to the pit with those who died a long, long time ago. I'll make you live down there, in those ancient ruins with the dead. You'll never see the world of the living again. I'll bring terrifying things on you, and that's it for you. People will search for you, but you'll be gone forever. No cap.' This is the decree of the Lord GOD."

Ezekiel.title: The Epic Rise and Fall of the World's Richest City
paragraphs: God's message hit me up, and it was about Tyre. He said, "Son of man, it's time to sing a sad song for Tyre. Tell Tyre, the city that's basically the world's mall, the gateway to the sea for everyone, 'This is what the Lord God has to say:'

'Yo, Tyre, you're always flexing, 'I'm the perfect ship, a total beauty.' You were basically queen of the seas. Your ship was built with the best stuff—planking from Mount Hermon junipers, a mast from a Lebanon cedar. Your oars were made from super strong Bashan oaks. The decks were cypress from Cyprus, with sick ivory inlays. Your sail? Fancy embroidered linen from Egypt that also worked as your flag. And you had these cool purple awnings on deck, also from Cyprus. Your rowers were pros from Sidon and Arvad, and your own experienced sailors were the main crew. The guys who built and fixed your ship were old-timers from Byblos. Basically, every ship and sailor out there wanted to trade with you.

Your army was stacked with soldiers from all over—Paras, Lud, and Put. They were elite troops looking sharp in their uniforms, and they seriously put you on the map. Your city's security guards were hired from Arvad, Helech, and Gammad. They hung their shields all over your walls, which was like the final perfect touch to your city's good looks.
Tarshish was your biggest business partner because you were loaded. They paid for your stuff with silver, iron, tin, and lead.
Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded with you too, but they were dealing in people—slaves—and bronze for your goods.
Beth-togarmah traded you workhorses, warhorses, and mules for your products.
The people from Rhodes also did business with you. A bunch of faraway islands traded ivory and ebony with you.
Edom traded with you because you had so much stuff. They gave you agate, purple fabrics, embroidered cloth, fine linen, coral, and rubies for your products.
Judah and Israel were in on it too. They traded top-tier wheat, millet, honey, oil, and balm for your goods.
Damascus, seeing how much stuff you had, did business with you, trading wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
Danites and Greeks from Uzal traded with you, bringing wrought iron, cinnamon, and spices.
Dedan traded saddle blankets with you.
Arabia and all the sheiks from Kedar traded lambs, rams, and goats with you.
Traders from Sheba and Raamah in South Arabia brought you the best spices, precious stones, and gold.
Haran, Canneh, and Eden from way out east in Assyria and Media traded with you. They brought fancy clothes, colorful textiles, and detailed carpets to your markets.
The huge Tarshish ships were like your personal cargo fleet, handling all your imports and exports. Man, you were doing big business, ruling the trade routes.

But then your sailors, trying to show off, rowed you into a massive storm. A wind from the east just wrecked your ship in the middle of the ocean. Everything went down—all your expensive goods, your sailors and crew, your shipbuilders and soldiers. All of it, sunk to the bottom of the sea. A total shipwreck. The screams of your sailors were heard all the way on the shore. Sailors everywhere jumped ship, and the veteran seamen swam for their lives. They were all crying, a huge, bitter song of grief for you. They put ashes on their faces, shaved their heads, and wore rough clothes, just wailing over their loss. They sang this funeral song: 'Who on the seas was ever like Tyre!'

'When you sailed the seas with your products, you made so many people happy. Your global trade made kings rich. But now, you're smashed to pieces by the waves, sunk to the bottom of the sea. And everything you ever bought or sold went down with you. Everyone on the shore is just staring in horror. Kings' hair is standing on end, their faces pale and shocked. All the traders of the world are just throwing their hands up like, 'No way this could happen!' But oh, it did.'

Ezekiel.title: The King with a God Complex Gets a Reality Check
paragraphs: God's message hit me. He said, "Son of man, go tell the leader of Tyre what God, the Master, has to say:

"You've gotten so proud, walking around thinking, 'I'm a god. I'm sitting on God's throne, ruling the ocean.' But you're just a human, not even close to being a god. You're a mortal who's trying way too hard to be a god. You think you're smarter than Daniel, that no puzzle is too tough for you. Your cleverness made you super rich; you've got stacks of gold and silver. You played the game well, made some sick deals, and earned a ton of cash. But all that money has gone straight to your head, making you arrogant.
"So, God, the Master, says this:

"'Because you're acting like you're a god, I'm warning you: I'm sending foreigners to attack you, the most brutal nations around. They're going to pull out their swords and destroy your reputation for being so smart. They'll pop that ego of yours. They'll knock you off your high horse and bury you at sea. Are you going to tell your killers, 'You can't do this! I'm a god'? To them, you're just another guy. They're killing a man, not a god. You'll die like a stray dog, taken out by strangers—because I've said it. This is a decree from God, the Master.'"
God's message came to me again: "Son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre. Tell him this is a message from God, the Master:

"You seriously had it all. You were in Eden, God's garden, dressed in the most amazing clothes, covered in jewels: carnelian, peridot, moonstone, beryl, onyx, jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and emerald, all set in gold. It was all made for you on the day you were created. You were the chosen cherub, an angelic guardian. I put you on God's holy mountain, and you walked among fiery stones. You were perfect from the day you were made... until evil was found in you. All your business deals made you violent, and you sinned. So I threw you off the mountain of God in disgrace. I kicked you out, you guardian angel. No more walking among fiery gems for you. Your beauty made you arrogant. You traded your wisdom for fame. I threw you down to the ground and let other kings watch and gloat over your downfall. With sin after sin, and your corrupt business practices, you trashed your own sacred places. So I started a fire inside and around you, and it burned you to the ground. Now, you're just a pile of ashes for everyone to see. Anyone who knew you is just shocked, like, 'No way this happened! But it did!'"
God's message came to me: "Son of man, go confront Sidon and preach against it. Say, 'This is a message from God, the Master:

"'Look, Sidon, I'm against you. I'm about to show you who I really am.' They'll know I'm God when I come to bring justice and reveal my holiness. I'm going to send a plague, and there will be violence and death in the streets. People will be dying everywhere as war closes in. Then they'll finally get that I'm not playing around, that I am God.
"Israel won't have to deal with its annoying neighbors anymore, the ones who have been like thorns in their side, treating them with contempt. And they, too, will realize that I am God."
"Israel won't have to deal with its annoying neighbors anymore, the ones who have been like thorns in their side, treating them with contempt. And they, too, will realize that I am God."

God, the Master, says, "When I bring the people of Israel back from all the nations where they've been scattered, and when I show my holiness through them for all the world to see, they will live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob. They'll live there safely, build houses, and plant vineyards. And while they're living in peace, I'll bring judgment on all their neighbors who treated them so badly. And they will know that I am their God."

Ezekiel.title: Pharaoh's Ego Trip Ends in Disaster
paragraphs: So, back in the tenth year, tenth month, on the twelfth day, God's message hit me up. He said, "Son of man, go confront Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. You need to call him and all of Egypt out. Tell them, this is what the Master GOD says:

'Yo, Pharaoh, king of Egypt, watch yourself. I'm so not on your side. You're like this big, lazy dragon just lounging in the Nile, all like, ‘This is my river. I made it. It’s all mine.’ Well, I'm about to put hooks in your jaw and make all the fish of the Nile cling to your scales. I'm gonna pull you right out of the river, with all those fish still stuck to you. Then I'm gonna drag you out into the desert, you and every last fish. You'll just lie there out in the open, becoming food for wild animals and birds. Then every single person in Egypt will finally get that I am GOD.

'You've been a totally useless support for Israel. When they tried to lean on you, you just splintered and hurt them, and when they put their weight on you, you broke and made them fall flat. So, because of that—this is a message from the Master GOD—I'm bringing a war against you. I'm gonna get rid of your people and your animals, and I'll turn your whole country into a barren wasteland. That's how they'll know that I am GOD.

'Since you were all like, ‘The Nile is mine. I made it. It belongs to me,’ I'm now against you and your rivers. I'm going to turn Egypt into a totally empty, desolate desert, all the way from Migdol down to Syene at the Ethiopian border. You won't see a single person or even an animal. It'll be a ghost town for forty years straight.

'I'm gonna make Egypt the most desolate place ever. For forty years, its cities will be the most ruined of all ruined cities. I'll scatter the Egyptians all over the world, sending them into exile in every direction.

'But,' says the Master GOD, 'that's not the end of the story. After those forty years are up, I'll gather the Egyptians back from all the places they were scattered. I'll restore Egypt and bring them back to Pathros, where they first started. They'll have to start over from the very beginning. They'll be at the very bottom of all the nations, and they'll stay there. They're never climbing back up to be a world power again. Israel will never be tempted to depend on Egypt again. Egypt will just be a reminder of their past mistakes. Then they will know that I am the Master GOD.'

Then, in the twenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month, God's message came to me again: "Son of man, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon totally wore out his army fighting against Tyre. They worked themselves to the bone and got nothing out of it.

"So, the Master GOD says, 'I'm giving Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. He's going to take all its wealth and loot the place clean. That'll be the payment for his army. He was working for me all that time and didn't get paid. So, Egypt is his paycheck. That's a decree from the Master GOD.
"'And when that happens, I'll give fresh hope to Israel—a new dawn is coming!—and I'll give you, Ezekiel, the confidence to speak boldly. And they will finally realize that I am GOD.'"

Ezekiel.title: Egypt's Epic Fail & Broken Arms
paragraphs: God, the boss, hit me up: "Yo, son of man, preach this. Give 'em the message from God, the Master. And just wail:

"'It's doomsday!' Time is totally up. God's huge day of judgment is right around the corner. Thick clouds are rolling in. It's game over for the nations. Death is gonna pour down on Egypt. Ethiopia will be paralyzed with terror when they see the Egyptians getting wrecked, their stuff hauled off, and their whole foundation demolished. And Ethiopia, Put, Lud, Arabia, Libya—all of Egypt’s old crew—are gonna go down right along with them.
"'God says:

"'Egypt’s squad will fall and their proud strength will totally collapse—from Migdol up north to Syene down south, it's gonna be a massive slaughter in Egypt. That's a decree from God, the Master. Egypt, the most wrecked of the wrecked, its cities wasted beyond belief, will finally get that I am God when I burn it down and all its helpers get knocked out flat.
"'When that goes down, I’ll send messengers by ship to sound the alarm for the super chill Ethiopians. They’ll be totally freaked out. Egypt is doomed! Judgment is coming, no cap.
"'God, the Master, says:

"'I’m gonna put a stop to Egypt’s flexing. And I'll use King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon to do it. He and his army, the most savage crew out there, will be sent to destroy the country. They’ll pull out their swords and fill Egypt with bodies. I’ll dry up the Nile River and sell off the land to a bunch of crooks. I’ll hire some outsiders to come in and just waste the country, strip it clean. I, God, have spoken.
"'And now this is what God, the Master, says:

"'I’m gonna smash all the fake gods; I’ll knock over all those giant statues in Memphis. The prince of Egypt will be gone for good, and in his place, I’ll just put fear—fear all over Egypt! I’ll demolish Pathros, burn Zoan to the ground, and punish Thebes. I'll pour my anger on Pelusium, Egypt’s main fort, and knock Thebes off its proud pedestal. I’ll set Egypt on fire: Pelusium will be writhing in pain, Thebes will get blown away, and Memphis will be violated. The young soldiers of On and Pi-beseth will be killed and the cities will be exiled. It's gonna be a dark day for Tahpanhes when I shatter Egypt, when I break its power and end its arrogant oppression. She’ll disappear in a cloud of dust, and her cities will be hauled off as exiles. That’s how I’ll punish Egypt, and that’s how she’ll finally get that I am God.'"
In the eleventh year, on the seventh day of the first month, God's message came to me:
"Son of man, I’ve broken the arm of Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. And look! It hasn't been fixed. No cast has been put on it so the bones can heal, so he can even use a sword again.

"So, God, the Master, says, I am so done with Pharaoh king of Egypt and I'm gonna go ahead and break his other arm—both arms broken! There’s no way he’ll ever swing a sword again. I’ll scatter the Egyptians all over the world. I’ll make the arms of the king of Babylon strong and put my sword in his hand, but I’ll break Pharaoh's arms and he’ll just groan like someone who's been fatally wounded. I’ll make the arms of the king of Babylon strong, but Pharaoh's arms will just go limp. The Egyptians will finally get that I am God when I put my sword in the hand of the king of Babylon. He’ll use it against Egypt and I’ll scatter the Egyptians all over the world. Then they’ll know for real that I am God."

Ezekiel.title: The Epic Fall of the World's Biggest Tree
paragraphs: In the eleventh year, on the first day of the third month, God's message hit me. He said, "Son of man, go tell Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, that arrogant old goat:

"'Who do you, sitting on top of the world, even think you are? Just look at Assyria. It was like a massive tree, a giant Lebanon cedar with gorgeous branches making cool shade. It was skyscraper-high, literally piercing the clouds. It was so well-watered, like it was plugged into the deep springs of the earth, with rivers flowing all around it and feeding all the other trees in the forest. It was huge, making all the other trees look tiny. Its branches were thick, its limbs were long, and its roots went deep into the earth's water supply. All the birds nested in its branches. All the wild animals had their babies under it. The most powerful nations lived in its shade. It was breathtakingly majestic—the sheer reach of its branches and the depth of its roots! Not a single cedar in God's own garden could compare. No pine tree was even close. The mightiest oaks looked like little bushes next to it. Seriously, no tree in God's garden was in the same league of beauty. I made it beautiful, a masterpiece of branches and leaves, and it was the envy of every single tree in Eden, God's garden.'

"Therefore, God, the Master, says, 'Because it shot up like a skyscraper, piercing the clouds, and got all cocky and proud of its height, I handed it over to a world-famous leader to hold it accountable for its evil. I was done with it. Foreigners, a seriously brutal bunch, came and chopped it down on the mountains. Its branches were scattered through all the valleys, and its broken limbs clogged up all the streams and rivers. Once its shade was gone, everyone just left. It wasn't a tree anymore—just a log. Now, birds just perch on the dead log, and wild animals dig burrows under it.'

"'That's the end of the 'big tree' nations. No more trees fed by the deep springs, no more cloud-piercing trees, no more earthly trees trying to take over. They're all destined for death—back to the dirt, just like all humans, because it's 'dust to dust' for everyone.'

"'This is the message from God, the Master: On the day the Big Tree had its funeral, I made the deep springs mourn. I stopped the rivers from flowing, held back the great seas, and made the Lebanon mountains wear black. All the trees of the forest fainted and collapsed. I made the whole world shake when it crashed, and I threw it down into the underworld to be with everything else that gets buried. All the trees of Eden, even the finest and best trees of Lebanon that were so well-watered, were actually relieved—they had gone down to the underworld with it—along with everyone who had lived in its shade and all who had been killed.'

"'So, which of the trees of Eden could even come close to you in splendor and size? But guess what? You're also destined to be chopped down and join the trees of Eden in the underworld, to be just another dead log stacked with all the other dead logs, among the uncircumcised who are dead and buried.'
"'This is about Pharaoh, that arrogant old goat.'
"'A decree from God, the Master.'"

Ezekiel.title: Pharaoh's Diss Track: Welcome to the Underworld
paragraphs: In the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month, God’s message hit me up. He said, “Son of man, it’s time to drop a funeral track for Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. Tell him this:
‘You really think you’re some big-shot lion, prowling around the world stage. Bro, you’re more like a sea monster thrashing around in the ocean, making a mess.
This is what the Lord GOD is saying:

‘I’m about to cast my net on you—and a whole squad of nations is gonna help me out—and I’ll drag you out with it. I’ll just dump you on the ground, right out in the open. Then I’m inviting all the vultures and crows for a massive feast on your dead body. I’ll even get wild animals from all over to come and get a piece. I’m gonna scatter your body parts all over the mountains and fill the valleys with your bones. The whole country, all the way to the mountains, will be soaked in your blood. It’s gonna fill up every single ditch. When I take you out, I’m shutting down the sky. The stars will go dark, I’ll block the sun with a cloud, and the moon will be switched off. I’ll turn off every light in the sky above you and throw your whole country into darkness. That’s a promise from the Lord GOD. I’m gonna shake up the whole world when I drag you off as a prisoner to countries you’ve never even heard of. People will be shook when they see what I’ve done to you. Kings will literally tremble when they see it. I’ll wave my sword, and they’ll be shaking in their boots. The day you fall, they’ll all be terrified, thinking, ‘That could’ve been me!’
This is what the Lord GOD is saying:

‘The king of Babylon’s sword is coming for you. I’m gonna use the swords of the best fighters, the most brutal nations out there, to crush your pride. They’re gonna totally wreck Egypt’s arrogance and pop that inflated ego. I’ll destroy all the cattle that graze by the river. No person or animal will ever make those waters muddy again. I’ll make their springs and streams run clear, super smooth. That’s a promise from the Lord GOD. When I turn Egypt into a wasteland and strip it of everything it has, when I strike down everyone who lives there, then they’ll finally get that I am GOD.’
This is a funeral song. So sing it. Let the young women of the nations sing it. Sing it for Egypt and for the end of all its hype.” A decree from the Lord GOD.
This is a funeral song. So sing it. Let the young women of the nations sing it. Sing it for Egypt and for the end of all its hype.” A decree from the Lord GOD.
In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the first month, God’s message came to me:

“Son of man, cry over Egypt’s flexing. Send her down. Send Egypt and her proud allies to the underworld, down to the land of the dead. Tell them, ‘You think you’re all that? Get down here and join the rest of the pagans in this cursed grave!’

“She’s gonna be thrown in with everyone who died in battle. The sword is ready. Drag her and all her hype away! All the big shots and their crews down in the grave will greet them like, ‘Welcome to the pagan graveyard! Come join the rest of the war victims!’

“Assyria is there with its whole crew, the entire nation is a cemetery. Their graves are in the deepest part of the pit, a whole field of graves, all of them killed in battle—these were the same people who used to terrorize the living.

“Elam is there with all its pride, a whole cemetery of them—all killed in battle, thrown into a pagan grave with the rest of the dead, these guys who used to terrorize the living. Now they have to carry their shame with everyone else in the pit. They made a whole section for the proud dead, decorated with pagan graves, all slaughtered in battle. They used to be terrifying, but now they carry their shame down with the others into the deep. They’re in the section for the battle-slain.

“Meshech-tubal is there with all its pride, a cemetery in unholy ground, thrown in with those slaughtered in battle—which is what they get for terrorizing the living. Now they carry their shame down with the others into the deep. They’re in the section for the slain. They’re kept separate from the legendary heroes, the ancient giants who were buried in full armor, with their swords under their heads and shields on their bones, the same heroes who once spread terror everywhere.
“And you, Egypt, you’ll be thrown into a pagan grave, right along with all the others, in the section for the slain.
“Edom is there, with its kings and princes. Even though they were super powerful, they’re now thrown into a pagan grave with everyone else headed for the pit.

“The princes of the north are there, every single one of them, and all the Sidonians who now carry their shame to their graves—all that terror they spread with their power is gone!—dumped in an unholy grave with those killed in battle, carrying their shame with the others headed for the deep.
“Pharaoh will see them all and, being the arrogant old goat he is, will actually feel better seeing all the company he has—Pharaoh and his whole slaughtered army. A decree from the Lord GOD.
“I used him to spread terror in the land of the living, and now I’m dumping him in a pagan grave with those killed by the sword—Pharaoh and all his hype. A decree from the Lord GOD.”

Ezekiel.title: The Watchman's Job is Lowkey a Big Deal
paragraphs: God hit me up and said, "Yo, son of man, tell your people, 'If I send an army to attack this land, and the people choose one of their own to be a watchman, and if that watchman sees the army coming and blows the trumpet to warn everyone, then if someone hears the trumpet but ignores it and the army comes and gets them, that's on them. They heard the warning but didn't listen—it's their own fault. If they had paid attention, they would've saved their own life.

'But if the watchman sees the army coming and doesn't blow the trumpet to warn the people, and the army comes and takes someone, I'm gonna hold the watchman responsible for that person's death because they weren't warned.'
