"You, son of man, are that watchman. I've made you a watchman for Israel. As soon as you hear a message from me, you have to warn them. If I tell a wicked person, 'You're on a fast track to death!' and you don't say anything to warn them to change their ways, they'll die in their sins without being warned, and I'll hold you responsible for their death. But if you do warn them to change their ways and they don't, they'll die in their sins, but at least you'll have saved yourself.
"Son of man, go talk to Israel. Tell them, 'You've been saying, “Our mistakes and sins are crushing us. We're just wasting away. How are we supposed to keep living?”'

"Tell them, 'As surely as I am the living God, I don't get any joy from the death of the wicked. I want the wicked to turn from their ways and live. Turn your life around! Stop doing evil! Why would you choose to die, Israel?'

"And there's more, son of man. Tell your people, 'A good person's good life won't save them if they decide to rebel, and a bad person's bad life won't stop them from turning their life around. A good person who sins can't just expect to live because they were good before. It's true that I tell good people, “Live! Be alive!” But if they start trusting in their own good deeds and turn to evil, all that good they did won't mean anything. They'll die for the evil they've done.

"'On the other hand, if I tell a wicked person, “You're going to die for your wicked life,” and they turn away from their sin and start living a righteous and just life—like being generous to those who are struggling, giving back what they stole, and living in a way that helps others—they will live. They won't die. None of their past sins will be held against them. They're doing what's right and living a good life. They will live.

"'Your people are saying, “God's way isn't fair.” But it's their way of living that's not fair. When good people stop living good lives and start sinning, they'll die for it. And when a wicked person turns away from their wicked life and starts living a just and righteous life, they'll come alive.
"'And you all still keep saying, “God's way isn't fair.” We'll see about that, Israel. I'm going to judge every single one of you based on how you live.'"
In the twelfth year of our exile, on the fifth day of the tenth month, a survivor from Jerusalem came to me and said, "The city has fallen."
The evening before that survivor showed up, God's hand was on me and He gave me my voice back. By the time the guy arrived in the morning, I was able to speak. I could talk again.

God's message came to me: "Son of man, the people who are living in the ruins back in Israel are saying, 'Abraham was just one guy and he owned this whole country. But there are a lot of us. So for sure, this land belongs to us.'

"So tell them, 'God the Master says, You eat meat with blood in it, you worship fake idols, you murder people whenever you want—and you really think you're going to own this land? You rely on your weapons, you do disgusting things, you sleep with whoever, whenever. And you still think you're going to own this land?'

"Tell them this, Ezekiel: 'This is a message from God, the Master. As surely as I am the living God, those who are still alive in the ruins will be killed. Anyone out in the open, I'll feed to wild animals. Anyone hiding in mountain fortresses and caves will die of disease. I'll turn this country into a total wasteland—no more arrogant bullies! The mountains of Israel will become so empty and dangerous that no one will even dare to go through them.'
"They'll know that I am God when I destroy the country because of all the disgusting things they've done.

"As for you, son of man, you've become the talk of the town. Your people gather on street corners and in front of their houses and say, 'Let's go hear the latest message from God.' They all show up and sit with you. They listen to what you say, but they don't actually do any of it. They'll say nice things to you, but all they really care about is making money and getting ahead. To them, you're just entertainment—like a singer with a sad love song and a guitar. They love to hear you talk, but it doesn't change anything.
"But when all this stuff actually happens—and trust me, it's going to happen!—then they'll realize that a real prophet was among them."

Ezekiel.title: God Fires the Shady Leaders & Becomes the GOAT Shepherd
paragraphs: God's message hit me. He said, "Yo, son of man, call out the so-called shepherds of Israel. Yeah, you heard me. Tell those leaders, 'The big boss, God, is saying: It's over for you shepherds of Israel who are only looking out for number one. Aren't shepherds supposed to, like, feed the sheep? You're drinking the milk, making clothes from the wool, and having lamb chops for dinner, but you're not actually feeding the sheep. You don't help the weak ones get stronger, you don't take care of the sick, you don't patch up the injured, you don't go after the ones who've wandered off, and you don't look for the lost. You just bully them and boss them around. And now they're scattered all over the place because there was no real shepherd—scattered and basically a free-for-all for wolves and coyotes. My sheep are scattered, totally exposed and vulnerable on every mountain and hill. My flock is spread across the whole world, and not a single person is out there looking for them!'

'So, listen up, you shepherds, this is God's message: As sure as I'm the living God—this is a decree from the Master, God—because my sheep were turned into easy prey, basically a buffet for wolves because you shepherds just ignored them and fed yourselves, you better listen to what God has to say now.'

'Watch out! I'm coming for you shepherds, and I'm taking my sheep back. You're fired from being shepherds of my flock. No more leaders who just feed themselves! I'm rescuing my sheep from your greed. You're not going to be using my sheep for your own gain anymore!'

'God, the Master, says: From now on, I'm taking over as the shepherd myself. I'm going to go look for them. Just like a shepherd goes after their flock when it gets scattered, I'm going after my sheep. I'll rescue them from all the places they were scattered to during the dark times. I'll bring them back from other nations, gather them from foreign countries, and bring them back to their own land. I'll feed them on the mountains of Israel, by the streams, right where they belong. I'll lead them to amazing pastures so they can chill on the mountain pastures of Israel, graze peacefully, and eat from the best pastures on the mountains of Israel. And I, myself, will be the shepherd of my sheep. I'll make sure they get all the rest they need. I'll go after the lost ones, bring back the strays, patch up the injured, build up the weak, and I'll keep an eye on the strong ones so they don't get taken advantage of.'

'And as for you, my precious flock, I'm stepping in to judge between one sheep and another, between the rams and the goats. Aren't you happy just eating in a good pasture without trying to claim the whole thing? Can't you just drink from the clean stream without making it all muddy with your feet? Why do the rest of my sheep have to deal with trampled grass and dirty water?'

'Because of this, God, the Master, says: I'm personally stepping in to make things right between the fat sheep and the skinny sheep. Because you pushed your way through with your shoulder and your backside and used your horns to butt all the weaker animals until you scattered them everywhere, I'm going to come and save my precious flock. They won't be pushed around anymore. I'll step in and sort things out between all the sheep.'

'I'm going to set up one shepherd to rule them all: my servant David. He will feed them. He will be their true shepherd. And I, God, will be their God. My servant David will be their leader. I, God, have said it.'

'I'll make a peace treaty with them. I'll get rid of all the dangerous animals from the country so the sheep can live safely in the wild and even sleep in the forest. I'll make them and everything around my hill a huge blessing. I'll send down tons of rain when it's needed—literal showers of blessing! The trees will be full of fruit, the ground will produce amazing crops, they'll feel safe and secure in their own land, and they'll know for sure that I am God when I break them free from their slavery and rescue them from their slave masters.'

'They won't be taken advantage of by other nations or attacked by wild animals anymore. They'll live in safety and peace, with nothing to fear. I'll give them lush gardens, overflowing with vegetables—no more starving, no more being made fun of by outsiders.'
'They'll know, without a doubt, that I, God, am their God, that I'm with them, and that they, the people of Israel, are my people. This is a decree from God, the Master.'
'You are my precious flock, the flock of my pasture, my human flock. And I am your God. A decree from God, the Master.'

Ezekiel.title: God's Clapback on Mount Seir
paragraphs: God’s message hit me up: “Yo, son of man, go call out Mount Seir. Drop this prophecy on them! Tell them, ‘God, the Boss, is saying this:

“‘I’m about to come for you, Mount Seir. I’m stepping in and turning you into a total wreck. I’ll make your towns just piles of rocks. There’ll be nothing left of you. Then you’ll know for real that I am God.

“‘I’m doing this ‘cause you’ve held on to this ancient beef with Israel. You went after them so hard when they were already at their lowest, facing their final consequence. So, for real, as the living God, I’m setting you up for a massive L. Since you were so about that violent life, you’re gonna get chased by it. I’ll turn Mount Seir into a wasteland. Nobody’s gonna be coming or going. I’ll cover your mountains with bodies. Dead bodies everywhere—on your hills, in your valleys, in your ditches. I’ll leave you in ruins, and your towns will be ghost towns—literally zero population. Then you’ll get it that I am God.

“‘And because you were like, “These two nations, these two countries? They’re mine. I’m taking over” (even though God was right there, watching and listening), I’m gonna flip all that hate and anger you have right back at you. You’ll know I’m not playing when I bring my judgment down on you. Then you’ll finally realize that I, God, heard all the trash you talked about the mountains of Israel, saying, “They’re toast, and we’re gonna feast.” You’ve been acting all tough, talking big, disrespectfully challenging me. And trust me, I’ve heard every word.

“‘So here’s the final word from God, the Master: The whole world is gonna cheer when I take you down. Since you were out there celebrating, thinking it was so great when Israel lost everything, I’m gonna do the same to you: total destruction. Mount Seir is gonna be destroyed—yeah, every single bit of Edom. Then they’ll finally get that I am God!’”

Ezekiel.title: Israel's Epic Comeback Story
paragraphs: “Alright, son of man, it's time to speak to the mountains of Israel. Tell them, ‘Hey, mountains of Israel, listen to God’s message. The big boss, God, is saying this: Your enemies were bragging, like, ‘Awesome! Those ancient hills are ours now!’ So, here’s what God, the Master, has to say about it: Because all these nations ganged up on you, tearing you apart, taking pieces of you for themselves, and you became the punchline of everyone's jokes, you need to listen up. This is God’s message to the mountains, hills, valleys, and all the trashed, empty towns that got looted and laughed at by the nations around you. God, the Master, says: I am seriously fired up and angry at those other nations, especially Edom. They straight-up stole my land with total disrespect and violence, just grabbing it for themselves.’

“So go ahead, preach to the land of Israel, to its mountains, hills, and valleys. Tell them: ‘This is a message from God, the Master: Look, I'm angry, and I care about you. I'm speaking up because you've been totally humiliated by the other nations. So I, God, the Master, swear to you that it's their turn now. Those nations around you are about to get humiliated themselves.

“‘But you, mountains of Israel, you’re about to have a major glow-up. You'll grow new branches and produce fruit for my people, Israel, because they're coming home soon! See? I'm on your side again. You'll be farmed and planted just like before. I'll make sure your population booms all over Israel. The towns will be full of people again, and the ruins will be rebuilt. I'll fill this land with life—people and animals. The whole country will be bursting with life, more than ever before, with your towns as full as they were in the good old days. I'm going to treat you even better than I ever have. And then you'll know for sure that I am God. I'll bring my own people, Israel, to take care of you, and you will be their special inheritance. You'll never be a harsh land that causes them pain again.

“‘God, the Master, says: You've got this reputation for being a land that 'eats' its own people and causes families to fail. Well, I'm telling you now, that's over. You won't be known for that anymore. That's a promise from God, the Master. I won't let other nations mock you or look down on you ever again. You won't be a land that brings failure. That's a promise from God, the Master.’”

God’s message came to me again: “Son of man, when the people of Israel were living in their own land, they totally trashed it with their lifestyle. I was furious with them because of the violence and corruption they spread everywhere. They were polluting the country with their murders and their fake gods, so I got fed up. I kicked them out and scattered them among other nations, judging them for how they lived. But wherever they went, they gave me a bad name. People would say, ‘These are supposedly God’s people, but they got kicked out of his land.’ It really hurt my holy reputation, which the people of Israel dragged through the mud in every country they went to.

“So, tell the house of Israel, ‘This is a message from God, the Master: I’m not doing this for your sake, Israel. I’m doing it for MY sake, to restore my holy name that you’ve ruined all over the world. I’m about to show everyone how great and holy my name is—the name you’ve dishonored everywhere. Then, all the nations will realize that I am God. They'll see my holiness on display through you, right before their eyes.

“‘Here’s the plan: I’m going to grab you from all those countries, gather you up, and bring you back to your own land. I’ll wash you clean with pure water. I’m going to give you a new heart and a new spirit. I’ll take out that hard, stubborn heart of stone and replace it with a heart that truly wants to follow me. I’ll put my Spirit inside you, empowering you to live by my rules and follow my commands. You’ll live in the land I promised your ancestors. You will be my people, and I will be your God!

“‘I’ll save you from all the nasty stuff you've been into. I’ll command the fields to produce massive harvests, so you’ll never have to deal with famine again. I’ll make your trees and crops flourish. No other nation will be able to diss you for being hungry ever again.
“‘And then you’ll look back on your messed-up past—all the evil and shameful things you did—and you’ll be completely disgusted with yourselves. You'll finally get how messed up your actions were.
“‘But get this straight—I’m not doing this for you. Seriously. You should be ashamed of the huge mess you made of everything, Israel!

“‘This is a message from God, the Master: On the day I finally clean you up from all your filth, I’ll also make your cities livable again. The ruins will be rebuilt. The abandoned land will be cultivated, no longer just a field of weeds that everyone ignores. People will be shocked and say, ‘Wow, this wasteland has turned into a Garden of Eden! And all those ruined, destroyed cities are now packed with people and thriving!’ The nations still around you will know that I, God, am the one who rebuilds ruins and replants wastelands. I, God, have said it, and I will do it.

“‘And here’s another thing from God, the Master: I’m going to do what Israel asks for once again. I’ll make their population explode like a flock of sheep. The ruined cities will be as crowded with people as Jerusalem is with sheep during the big festivals. And then they will know that I am God.’”

Ezekiel.title: The Ultimate Glow-Up: Bone Edition
paragraphs: God just grabbed me. His Spirit yoinked me and dropped me in this huge open field that was literally just covered in bones. He had me walk all around them—so many bones! They were scattered everywhere, super dry and bleached out by the sun.
He asked me, “Yo, son of man, can these bones actually live?”
I was like, “Master God, for real, only you know the answer to that.”
He told me, “Prophesy to these bones. Be like, ‘Yo, dry bones, listen up to God’s message!’”

Then God, the Master, said to the dry bones, “Watch this. I’m about to give you life, and you’re gonna be alive again. I’ll hook you up with muscles, put some meat back on you, cover you with skin, and breathe life into you. You’ll be alive, and you’ll know for sure that I am God!”

So I did what he said. As I was prophesying, there was this crazy sound, like a huge rustling noise! The bones started moving and connecting, bone to bone. I just kept watching. Muscles started forming, then flesh grew on the bones, and then skin covered it all. But, plot twist, they still weren’t breathing.
He said to me, “Prophesy to the breath. Prophesy, son of man. Tell the breath, ‘God, the Master, says, Come from all over. Come, breath. Breathe on these dead bodies. Bring them to life!’”
So I prophesied, just like he told me to. The breath went into them, and they came back to life! They all stood up on their feet, a massive army.
Then God told me, “Son of man, these bones? They represent the entire nation of Israel. Listen to what they’re saying: ‘Our bones are all dried up, we’ve lost all hope, we’re totally done for.’

“So, prophesy to them. Tell them, ‘God, the Master, says: I’m gonna open up your graves and bring you out alive—my people! Then I’ll take you straight back to the land of Israel. When I open your graves and bring you out, you’ll finally get that I am God. I’ll breathe my own life into you, and you’ll live. Then I’ll lead you right back to your own land, and you’ll know that I am God. I said it, and I’m gonna do it. That’s a promise from God.’”

God’s message came to me again: “You, son of man, grab a stick and write on it, ‘For Judah and his Israelite crew.’ Then get another stick and write on it, ‘For Joseph—Ephraim’s stick, with all his Israelite crew.’ Then, tie the two sticks together so you’re holding just one stick.

“When your people ask you, ‘Uh, you gonna tell us what you’re doing?’ tell them, ‘God, the Master, says, Watch me! I’m gonna take the Joseph stick that’s in Ephraim’s hand, with all the tribes connected to him, and I’ll put the Judah stick on it. I’ll make them into one single stick. I’m holding one stick.’

“Then hold up the sticks you wrote on so everyone can see them. Tell them, ‘God, the Master, says, Watch me! I’m pulling the Israelites out of all the countries where they were exiled. I’ll gather them from everywhere and bring them back home. I’ll make them one nation in their own land, on the mountains of Israel, and they’ll have one king—one king for all of them. They’ll never be split into two nations or two kingdoms again. They won’t mess up their lives with fake gods, gross idols, and all that rebellious stuff anymore. I’ll save them from all their old sinful habits. I’ll clean them up. They’ll be my people! And I’ll be their God! My boy David will be their king, and they’ll all follow one leader.

“‘They’ll follow my rules and stick to my commands. They’ll live in the same land I gave to my servant Jacob, the land where their ancestors lived. They and their kids and their grandkids will live there forever, and my servant David will be their leader forever. I’ll make a peace treaty with them that will last forever, an unbreakable promise. I’ll make them feel safe and I’ll put my holy temple right in the middle of their lives, forever. I’ll live right there with them. I’ll be their God! They’ll be my people!
“‘All the other nations will know that I, God, have made Israel holy when my temple is set up right in the center of their lives, forever.’”

Ezekiel.title: God vs. Gog: The Ultimate Showdown
paragraphs: God’s message hit me up. He said, “Yo, son of man, you need to go confront Gog, this dude from the land of Magog who’s the head honcho of Meshech and Tubal. Prophesy against him. Tell him, ‘The Master God says: Watch yourself, Gog. I’m totally against you, leader of Meshech and Tubal. I’m gonna spin you around, put hooks in your jaws, and drag you and your whole army out—all your horses and riders decked out in armor, with all their shields and swords, a massive crew ready to fight. Persia, Cush, and Put will be with them, also armed to the teeth, plus Gomer and its army, and Beth-togarmah from way up north with its crew. Yeah, a ton of nations are rolling with you.’

‘Get ready for a fight, you and this whole squad you’ve assembled. You’re in charge, so just wait for my signal. After a long time, you’ll get your orders. Way down the line, you’ll show up in a country that’s just recovered from a crazy war. People from all over will be gathered on the mountains of Israel, which were a wasteland for ages. These people were brought back from all over and are now living all safe and sound. You’ll roll in like a thunderstorm, like a massive cloud covering the whole land, you and all your troops.’

‘A message from the Master God: At that time, you’ll start scheming and come up with a seriously evil plan. You’ll be like, “I’m gonna invade this country that has zero defenses. I’ll attack these people who are just chilling, living their lives without a care, no gates on their cities, no locks on their doors. I’m gonna go in and just plunder the whole place, clean them out completely. This country is rebuilt from nothing, full of people who came back from exile, and their economy is booming right in the center of everything.”’

‘Sheba and Dedan and Tarshish, all these traders just trying to make a quick buck, will be like, “Whoa, so you’re just here to wreck the place and get rich, huh? You brought your whole army just to cash out?”’

“So, son of man, prophesy! Tell Gog, ‘This is a message from the Master God: When my people Israel are living securely, are you really gonna make a move? You’ll come down from the far north, you and your massive mob of armies, charging in on your horses like a tidal wave, and you’ll invade my people Israel, covering the land like a giant cloud. When the time is right, I’m gonna unleash you on my land. Why? So that all the nations will finally get who I am. They’ll see me put my holiness on full display right through you, Gog, for everyone to see.’

‘A message from the Master God: Remember years ago when I spoke through my servants, the prophets of Israel? Weren’t you the one I was talking about? Year after year, they prophesied that I would bring you against them. And when that day comes, Gog, when you attack the land of Israel—this is a decree from the Master God—my anger is going to explode. Fueled by my burning jealousy, I’m telling you, there will be a massive earthquake that will rock the land of Israel. The fish, the birds, the wild animals—even the tiniest bugs!—and every single person will tremble before me. Mountains will literally fall apart, and cliffs will crumble. I’ll call for an all-out war against you, Gog—a decree from the Master God—and your own guys will start fighting each other on the mountains of Israel. I’ll hit you with everything I’ve got: plagues, massacres, insane rain and hailstorms, and even volcanic lava pouring down on you and all your troops and the people with you.’
‘I’m going to show you just how great and holy I am. I’ll make myself known to the whole world. Then you’ll finally realize that I am God.’”

Ezekiel.title: God's Ultimate Takedown: Gog Gets Wrecked
paragraphs: “Alright, my guy, go prophesy against Gog. Tell him, ‘This is a message from the one and only God, the Master: I’m so against you, Gog, you leader of Meshech and Tubal. I’m about to turn you around, drag you all the way from the far north, and bring you down hard on the mountains of Israel. Then I’ll smack that bow right out of your left hand and the arrows from your right. You and your whole crew, and everyone with you, are gonna get taken out on the mountains of Israel. I’m gonna serve you up as a feast for all the scavenger birds and wild animals. You’ll fall in the middle of an open field. I’ve said it, and it’s gonna happen. That’s a decree from God, the Master.’
“I’m gonna set fire to Magog and all those islands way out there where people think they’re so safe. And then they’ll finally get it that I am God.
“I’m going to make my holy name known among my people, Israel. I’m never again gonna let my name get disrespected. Then all the other nations will realize that I, God, am the Holy One in Israel.
“It’s coming! For real, it’s going to happen! This is the day I’ve been talking about.

“The people from the cities of Israel will come out and build a huge bonfire with all the enemy’s weapons. They’ll be throwing on shields, big and small, bows and arrows, clubs and spears. This fire will burn for seven whole years. They won’t even need to chop wood from the forest; they’ll have plenty of weapons to fuel the fire. They’re gonna take back what was taken from them and rob the ones who robbed them. That’s a decree from God, the Master.

“When that time comes, I’ll give Gog a burial plot right in Israel, in the Valley of the Travelers, just east of the sea. It’s gonna be so massive it’ll block the road for anyone trying to pass through. That’s where they’ll bury Gog and his entire army. They’ll even name the place ‘The Valley of Gog’s Horde.’

“The people of Israel will spend seven months burying all the bodies to clean up the land. Everyone will pitch in. It’ll be a huge day for them, and I’ll get the glory for it. They’ll hire a full-time crew just to handle the cleanup, going through the country looking for any leftover bodies. After seven months, they’ll do one last major search. If anyone spots a bone, they’ll put up a marker so the burial crew can come get it and bury it in the mass grave, ‘The Valley of Gog’s Horde.’ (There’s even a town nearby that will be called ‘Horde-ville’ or Hamonah.) That’s how they’ll get the land all cleaned up.

“Alright, my guy, God, the Master, says this: Call all the birds! Call all the wild animals! Tell them, ‘Get over here! Gather around for this crazy sacrificial meal I’m cooking up for you on the mountains of Israel. You’re gonna eat meat and drink blood. You’ll be feasting on the bodies of absolute legends and drinking the blood of world-famous princes like they were a bunch of rams, lambs, goats, and bulls—the best of the best. At this sacrificial meal I’m making, you’ll eat fat until you’re stuffed and drink blood until you’re wasted. You’ll chow down on horses and their riders, heroes and all kinds of warriors at the table I’m setting for you.’ That’s a decree from God, the Master.

“I’m gonna show off my glory to all the nations, and they’ll all see my judgment in action. From that day forward, Israel will know for sure that I am their God. And the other nations will finally understand that Israel was sent into exile because of their own sins. They were unfaithful to me, so I turned my back on them. I let their enemies take them down, and they were all killed. I gave them what they deserved for their messed-up, sinful lives. I turned away and wouldn’t even look at them.

“But now, I’m bringing Jacob back from exile. I’m going to have compassion on all the people of Israel, and I’ll be super protective of my holy name. The memory of their shame and all the times they betrayed me will eventually fade away, especially when they’re living securely in their own land, totally safe and without fear. Once I’ve brought them back from other countries and gathered them from enemy lands, I’ll use them to show how holy I am for all the nations to see. Then they’ll know, no cap, that I am their God. Because even though I sent them away into exile, I’m gonna gather them all back to their own land, not leaving a single person behind. After I pour my Spirit on Israel and fill them with my life, I’ll never turn away from them again. I’ll look them right in the face. That’s a decree from God, the Master.”

Ezekiel.title: God's Epic Temple Blueprint Reveal
paragraphs: So, in the 25th year of our exile, right at the start of the year, on the 10th day of the month—which was 14 years after Jerusalem got wrecked—God’s hand came on me and boom, I was there. He took me in this wild vision to Israel and dropped me on a super high mountain. Down south, there were these buildings that looked like a whole city. He took me over, and I met this guy who was shining like bronze. He was standing at the gate holding a linen rope and a measuring stick.

The guy said to me, “Yo, son of man, you gotta watch this and listen up. Pay real close attention to everything I’m about to show you. This is why you’re here. Then you gotta go tell Israel everything you see.”

First thing I saw was this massive wall all around the Temple area. The measuring stick the guy had was about 10 feet long. He measured the wall's thickness: a solid 10 feet. The height was 10 feet too.

He walked into the east-facing gate and went up the seven steps. He measured the entrance of the gate: 10 feet deep. On both sides of the hallway, there were these little rooms, each one a 10-foot cube, with 7.5-foot thick walls between them. The inner doorway that led to the porch facing the Temple courtyard was also 10 feet deep.
Then he measured the porch of the gate: 12 feet deep, with pillars on the sides that were 3 feet thick. This porch opened up right into the Temple courtyard.
Inside this east gate, there were three of those little rooms on each side. Each room was the same size and the walls between them were identical.
He measured the outside entrance to the gate: 15 feet wide and 19.5 feet deep.
In front of each little room was a low wall, about 18 inches high. The rooms themselves were 10-foot squares.
He measured the width of the whole gate area from the roof's edge on one side to the other: 37.5 feet from top edge to top edge.
He measured the inside walls of the gate area: 90 feet to the porch that led into the courtyard.
The distance from the gate entrance to the far end of the porch was 75 feet.

The little rooms and their walls inside the gate had narrow windows all around. The porch did too. All the windows faced inward. The doorframes between the rooms had palm trees carved on them, which is pretty cool.

The man then led me to the outer courtyard and all its rooms. There was a paved walkway connecting the courtyard gates. Thirty rooms were lined up along the courtyard. The walkway was the same length as the gateways, running alongside them. This was the walkway for the outer courtyard. He measured the distance from the front of the entrance gate across to the entrance of the inner court: 150 feet.

Then he took me to the north side. There was another gate facing north, leaving the outer courtyard. He measured its length and width. It had three little rooms on each side. Its posts and porch were the same as the first gate: 87.5 feet by 43.75 feet. The windows and palm trees were identical to the east gate. It had seven steps leading up to it, and its porch faced inward. Across from this gate was a gate to the inner courtyard, on the north just like on the east. The distance between the two was 175 feet.

Then he took me to the south side, to the south gate. He measured its posts and its porch. It was the same size as the others. The porch with its windows was the same size as the ones I already saw. It also had seven steps going up to it. Its porch opened onto the outer courtyard, with palm trees carved on its posts on both sides. Across from it, the gate for the inner court faced south. He measured the distance across the courtyard from gate to gate: 175 feet.

He led me into the inner courtyard through the south gate. He measured it and found it was the same as the outer ones. Its rooms, walls, and entry hall were the same. The gate and porch, with windows all around, measured 87.5 by 43.75 feet. The entry hall of each of the gates leading to the inner courtyard was 43.75 by 8.75 feet. Each entry hall faced the outer courtyard. Palm trees were carved on its doorposts. Eight steps led up to it.

He then took me to the inner courtyard on the east and measured the gate. It was identical to the others—rooms, walls, and entry hall all the same. The gate and entry hall had windows all around. It measured 87.5 by 43.75 feet. Its porch faced the outer courtyard. There were palm trees on the doorposts on both sides. And it had eight steps.

He brought me to the north gate and measured it: same measurements. The rooms, walls, and entry hall with its windows: 87.5 by 43.75 feet. Its porch faced the outer courtyard. There were palm trees on its doorposts on both sides. And it had eight steps.

There was a room with a door at the entry hall of the gate where they cleaned the burnt offerings. Two tables were inside the entry hall, one on each side, where they slaughtered the animals for burnt offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings. Two tables were also placed against both outside walls of the entry hall—so, four tables inside and four tables outside, eight tables in total for slaughtering the sacrificial animals. The four tables for the burnt offerings were 31.5 inches square and 21 inches high. The tools for slaughtering the animals were kept there. Meat hooks, three inches long, were fastened to the walls. The tables were for the sacrificial animals.

Right where the inner gate opened onto the inner courtyard, there were two rooms, one at the north gate facing south and one at the south gate facing north. The man told me, “The room facing south is for the priests in charge of the Temple. And the room facing north is for the priests in charge of the altar. These priests are the sons of Zadok, the only sons of Levi allowed to get close to God to serve him.”
He measured the inner courtyard: a perfect 175-foot square. The altar was in front of the Temple.

He led me to the porch of the Temple and measured the gateposts of the porch: 8.75 feet high on both sides. The entrance to the gate was 21 feet wide and its walls were 4.5 feet thick. The entry hall itself was 35 feet wide and 21 feet deep. Ten steps led up to the porch. Columns stood on each side of the gateposts.

Ezekiel.title: God's New Temple Tour (Insane Details!)
paragraphs: So this guy brought me into the actual Temple and started measuring the doorposts. They were a massive ten and a half feet thick on each side. The entrance was a wide seventeen and a half feet, and the side walls were a solid eight and three-quarters feet thick.
He also measured the main Temple Sanctuary, which was seventy feet by thirty-five feet.

Then he went even deeper inside and measured the doorposts at that entrance. They were three and a half feet thick. The entrance itself was ten and a half feet wide, and the walls around it were a crazy twelve and a quarter feet thick. He measured the inner sanctuary, a perfect thirty-five-foot square, at the very back of the main one. He told me, "This is the Holy of Holies."

He measured the Temple wall, and it was ten and a half feet thick. The side rooms wrapping around the Temple were seven feet wide. These rooms were stacked three stories high, with thirty rooms on each floor. There were support beams around the Temple wall for the side rooms, but they were freestanding, not actually connected to the main wall. The side rooms got wider as you went up from the first to the third floor. A staircase went from the bottom floor, through the middle, all the way to the top.

I noticed the Temple was built on a raised base that was ten and a half feet thick all around, which was the foundation for the side rooms. The outer walls of these side rooms were eight and three-quarters feet thick. There was an open area, a thirty-five-foot-wide strip, between the Temple's side rooms and the priests' rooms that went all the way around. The side rooms had two entrances from this open area, one on the north side and one on the south. There was an eight-and-three-quarters-foot open space all around.

The building that faced the Temple courtyard on the west was one hundred twenty-two and a half feet wide, with walls that were eight and three-quarters feet thick. The total length of the wall and building was one hundred fifty-seven and a half feet.

He measured the Temple, and it was one hundred seventy-five feet long. The Temple courtyard and the building, including its walls, also measured one hundred seventy-five feet. The width of the front of the Temple and the open area to the east was one hundred seventy-five feet.

He measured the length of the building at the back of the Temple, the one facing the courtyard, including its shelters on each side: one hundred seventy-five feet. The main Sanctuary, the inner Sanctuary, and the vestibule facing the courtyard were all paneled with wood. They had window frames and door frames in all three sections. The walls were paneled from the floor up to the windows. Above the entrance to the inner Sanctuary and on the walls all around both sanctuaries, there were carvings of angel-cherubim and palm trees at regular intervals, in an alternating pattern.

Each angel-cherub had two faces: a human face looking at the palm tree on one side, and a lion's face looking at the palm tree on the other. This design was carved all over the entire Temple. The cherubim and palm tree pattern was carved on the wall of the main Sanctuary from the floor all the way up to the height of the door.

The main Sanctuary had a rectangular doorframe. In front of the Holy Place, there was something that looked like a wooden altar. It was five and a quarter feet high and three and a half feet square. Its corners, base, and sides were all made of wood. The man said to me, "This is the table that stands before God."

Both the main Sanctuary and the Holy Place had double doors. Each door was made of two hinged leaves, so one set could swing inward and the other outward. The doors of the main Sanctuary were carved with angel-cherubim and palm trees. There was a wooden canopy in front of the vestibule outside. On both sides of the porch, there were narrow windows with carved palm trees in between them.

Ezekiel.title: VIP Rooms & Secret Measurements
paragraphs: So this guy took me north to the outer courtyard and showed me these rooms facing the open area and the building on the north side. The north building was massive, like 175 feet long and 87.5 feet wide. Then, across this 35-foot gap from the inner courtyard, there were these rooms stacked three stories high. In front of the rooms, there was this long hallway, 17.5 feet wide and 175 feet long, with entrances from the north. The top-floor rooms were a bit smaller because their balconies were bigger than the ones on the lower floors. And the third-floor rooms didn't have pillars like the ones in the courtyard, so they were more compact. There was also this outer wall running alongside the rooms for 87.5 feet. The rooms facing the outer courtyard were 87.5 feet long, but the ones closer to the main holy area were a full 175 feet long. You got into the ground-floor rooms from the east, coming in from the outer courtyard.

On the south side, it was basically a mirror image. Same setup with rooms and a walkway, just like the ones on the north side—same size, same doors, everything. The main entrance was on the east, leading to the hallway, just like the other side.

Then he told me, "The north and south rooms next to the open area are the holy rooms. It's where the priests who serve God eat the holy offerings. They keep all the sacred stuff there—the grain, sin, and guilt offerings. These rooms are set apart, totally holy space. After the priests go into the Sanctuary, they can't just walk back out into the main courtyard and hang with everyone. They have to change out of their special ministering clothes and put on their regular outfits first."
After he finished measuring everything inside the Temple area, he took me out the east gate and started measuring the outside. With his measuring stick, he measured the east side: 875 feet.
Then the north side: 875 feet.
Then the south side: 875 feet.
Finally, he went to the west side and measured it: 875 feet.
He measured the wall on all four sides. Each wall was 875 feet long. These walls were there to separate the holy stuff from the everyday, ordinary stuff.

Ezekiel.title: God's Glory is Back, and It's LIT!
paragraphs: The man brought me to the east gate, and whoa! The epic glory of the God of Israel was pouring in from the east. It sounded like a massive waterfall, and the whole earth was literally glowing with His glory. It looked exactly like what I had seen when He came to destroy the city, and just like what I had seen by the Kebar River. I was so overwhelmed that I fell face down on the ground.

The amazing glory of God streamed into the Temple through the east gate. The Spirit lifted me to my feet and led me into the inner courtyard, and—no cap—the Temple was filled with the radiant glory of God!

I heard someone speaking to me from inside the Temple while the man stood beside me. He said, “Son of man, this is the place for my throne, where I will plant my feet. This is where I will live with the Israelites forever. Neither the people of Israel nor their kings will ever again disrespect my holy name with their unfaithfulness and the worthless idols their kings set up at all the shrines. When they put their worship places right next to mine, with only a thin wall between us, they dishonored my holy name with their disgusting practices. Is it any surprise that I destroyed them in my anger? So let them get rid of their unfaithful ways and the disgusting idols their kings introduced, and I will come and live with them forever.

“Son of man, tell the people of Israel all about the Temple so they will be ashamed of their rebellious lives. Have them study the layout. That will really hit them hard. Show them the entire plan of the Temple—its entrances and exits, its dimensions, its rules, and its laws. Draw a picture of it so they can see the design and its purpose, and live according to its design and intent.
“This is the law of the Temple: As it extends from the top of the mountain, everything around it becomes holy ground. Yes, this is the law, the very meaning, of the Temple.
“These are the measurements of the altar, using the long (twenty-one-inch) ruler. The gutter at its base is twenty-one inches deep and twenty-one inches wide, with a four-inch lip around its edge.

“The height of the altar is three and a half feet from the base to the first ledge, which is twenty inches wide. From the first ledge to the second ledge, it is seven feet high and twenty-one inches wide. The altar hearth is another seven feet high. Four horns stick up from the hearth, each twenty-one inches high.

“The top of the altar, the hearth, is a square, twenty-one by twenty-one feet. The upper ledge is also a square, twenty-four and a half feet on each side, with a ten-and-a-half-inch lip and a twenty-one-inch-wide gutter all the way around.
“The steps of the altar go up from the east.”
Then the man said to me, “Son of man, God, the Master, says: ‘These are the rules for the altar when it is built, for sacrificing burnt offerings and sprinkling blood on it.

“‘For a sin offering, give a bull to the priests, the Levitical priests from the family of Zadok who come into my presence to serve me. Take some of its blood and smear it on the four horns of the altar that stick out from the four corners of the top ledge and all around the lip. This is to purify the altar and make it ready for the sacrifice. Then take the bull for the sin offerings and burn it in the designated place in the courtyard outside the Sanctuary.

“‘On the second day, offer a male goat without any defects for a sin offering. Purify the altar the same way you purified it for the bull. Then, when you have purified it, offer a bull without any defects and a ram without any defects from the flock. Present them before God. Sprinkle salt on them and offer them as a burnt offering to God.

“‘For seven days, prepare a goat for a sin offering each day, and also a bull and a ram from the flock, animals without any defects. For seven days, the priests are to prepare the altar for its work, purifying it. This is how you dedicate it.

“‘After these seven days of dedication, from the eighth day on, the priests will present your burnt offerings and your peace offerings. And I will accept you with pleasure and delight! This is a decree from God, the Master.’”

Ezekiel.title: VIP Access Only: God's New Rules for the Temple
paragraphs: So then, the guy took me back to the outer gate of the Sanctuary, the one facing east. But it was shut tight.

God told me, "This gate is shut and it's staying shut. No one gets to go through it because I, the God of Israel, went through it. It stays shut. Only the prince, since he's the prince, can sit there and eat in God's presence. He has to enter the gate area through the porch and leave the same way."

Then the man led me through the north gate to the front of the Temple. I looked, and—whoa!—the radiant Glory of God was just filling the entire Temple of God! I immediately dropped to my face and worshiped.

God said to me, "Son of man, get a grip. Open your eyes, use your ears, and pay close attention to everything I'm about to tell you about the rules of this Temple of God, how all the laws work, the instructions for it, and all the entrances and exits of the Sanctuary.

"Go tell this crew of rebels, the house of Israel, 'A message from the Master God: That's enough of all your disgusting practices, Israel. You've been bringing foreigners who are uncommitted in their hearts and lives into my Sanctuary, desecrating it while you offer me my food—the fat and the blood. You've broken my covenant with all your vile acts. You haven't been taking care of my holy things. Instead, you put others in charge of my Sanctuary. So this is what the Master God says: No foreigner, uncommitted in heart and life, is to enter my Sanctuary, not even any foreigner living among the Israelites.'

"And as for the Levites who bailed on me when Israel went astray, who left me for their idols, they're going to have to face the consequences. They can still serve in my Sanctuary, guarding the temple gates and doing the work of the temple; they can slaughter the burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people and stand before them to serve. But because they served them in front of their idols and caused the house of Israel to fall into sin, I've sworn an oath against them, declares the Master God, that they will bear their guilt. They are not to come near me to serve as priests or to touch any of my holy things or my most holy offerings; they will carry the shame of the disgusting things they've done. I'm putting them in charge of the maintenance of the temple, for all its work and everything that needs to be done in it.

"But the Levitical priests from the line of Zadok, who faithfully took care of my Sanctuary when the rest of Israel wandered off from me, they are the ones who will come into my presence to serve me. They will stand before me to offer the fat and the blood, declares the Master God. They are the only ones who can enter my Sanctuary; they alone will approach my table to serve me and carry out my duties.

"When they enter the gates of the inner courtyard, they have to wear linen clothes. They can't wear any wool while they're on duty in the inner courtyard gates or inside the temple. They'll wear linen turbans on their heads and linen undergarments. They can't wear anything that makes them sweat. When they go out to the outer courtyard to the people, they have to take off the clothes they were serving in and leave them in the holy rooms. They need to change into regular clothes so they don't make the people holy just by touching them with their sacred garments.
"They can't shave their heads or let their hair get all long and messy; they have to keep their hair trimmed.
"No priest is allowed to drink wine when he enters the inner courtyard.
"They can't marry a widow or a divorced woman. They can only marry a virgin from the people of Israel, or the widow of a priest.
"Their job is to teach my people the difference between what's holy and what's not, and show them how to tell the difference between what's unclean and clean.
"In any dispute, the priests will act as judges and make decisions based on my rules. They will follow my laws and my decrees for all my appointed festivals, and they will keep my Sabbaths holy.

"A priest isn't supposed to make himself unclean by going near a dead body, unless it's his own father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or an unmarried sister. For them, it's okay. After he's been purified, he has to wait seven days. Then, on the day he goes back into the Sanctuary, into the inner courtyard to serve, he has to offer a sin offering for himself, declares the Master God.

"As for their inheritance, I am their inheritance. You're not to give them any property in Israel; I am their possession. They will eat the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings. Everything in Israel that is devoted to God will be theirs. The very best of all the firstfruits and of every offering you bring will belong to the priests. You are to give the first of your ground meal to the priests so that a blessing may rest on your homes.
"The priests are not to eat any bird or animal that has died naturally or has been torn by wild animals."

Ezekiel.title: The Ultimate Land Division & Offerings Guide
paragraphs: "When you guys are splitting up the land, you gotta set aside a massive chunk of it as sacred space for God: like, seven miles long and six miles wide. That whole area is holy ground. Inside this huge rectangle, block off a 750-foot square just for the Sanctuary, and give it a 750-foot buffer zone all around it. Then, mark off a section inside the sacred reserve that's seven miles long and three miles wide. That's where the Sanctuary and the Holy of Holies are gonna go. This is the spot where the priests will live—the guys who lead worship and serve God there. Their houses will be right there next to The Holy Place.

"Just north of that sacred reserve, block off an area about seven miles long and two and a quarter miles wide. That's for the Levites' villages, since they handle all the behind-the-scenes stuff for worship in the Sanctuary.
"Then, south of the sacred reserve, measure out a section seven miles long and about a mile and a half wide for the city itself. That area belongs to everyone in the whole family of Israel.

"Now for the prince: he gets the land right next to the east and west borders of that central sacred square. His land stretches all the way east to the Jordan River and all the way west to the Mediterranean Sea. That's his personal property in Israel. My princes are officially done bullying my people and walking all over them. They're gonna respect the land exactly how it was handed out to the tribes.

"This is the Message from God, the Master: 'I've had enough of your nonsense, princes of Israel! Stop bullying and taking advantage of my people. For once, just do what's fair and right. Use honest scales—no scamming with fake weights or rigged measurements. A pound needs to actually be sixteen ounces. A gallon needs to actually be four quarts. The ounce is the standard for both. And your money needs to be legit—no fake coins!

"‘Here's the deal on the offerings you guys need to bring: one-sixtieth of your wheat, one-sixtieth of your barley, one-hundredth of your oil, and one sheep out of every two hundred from Israel's best pastures. These are gonna be used for the grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings to make things right for the people. That's a direct order from God, the Master.

"‘Literally everyone in the land has to chip in for these special offerings, and the prince of Israel is in charge of managing them. It's the prince's job to provide the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings at all the big events—the Holy Festivals, the New Moons, and the Sabbaths. Basically, all the mandatory parties for the people of Israel. He's responsible for the sin offerings, grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings to make atonement for the people.

"‘This is the Message from God, the Master: On the first day of the first month, grab a flawless young bull and purify the Sanctuary. The priest is gonna take some blood from the sin offerings and rub it on the Temple doorposts, the four corners of the altar's ledge, and the gate entrance to the inner courtyard. Do this exact same ritual on the seventh day of the month for anyone who messes up by accident. That's how you make atonement for the Temple.
"‘On the fourteenth day of the first month, you're gonna celebrate the Passover. It's a massive seven-day feast. During the whole thing, you're only eating bread made without yeast.

"‘On Passover, the prince has to supply a bull as a sin offering for himself and everyone else in the country. Every single day of that seven-day feast, he's gotta provide seven flawless bulls and seven flawless rams as a burnt offering to God, plus one male goat every day.
"‘He also has to supply about five and a half gallons of grain offering and a gallon of oil for every single bull and ram.
"‘Then, on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, and for all seven days of that feast, he has to supply the exact same stuff for the sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, and oil.’"

Ezekiel.title: VIP Access Only: God's Temple Rules
paragraphs: Alright, here's a message from God, the Master: The east gate of the inner courtyard is locked on workdays, but it's open on the Sabbath and the New Moon. The prince will come in through the gate's entrance and stand by the gateposts while the priests present his offerings. He'll worship there on the porch and then head out, but the gate stays open until evening. On Sabbaths and New Moons, the people are to worship God at the entrance of that same gate.

The prince needs to provide the burnt offering for the Sabbath: six perfect lambs and a perfect ram. The grain offering with the ram is about five and a half gallons plus a gallon of oil, and a handful of grain for each lamb.

For the New Moon, he's to provide a young bull, six lambs, and a ram, all flawless. He'll also supply five and a half gallons of grain and a gallon of oil for both the ram and the bull, and a handful of grain for each lamb.
When the prince enters, he'll go through the entrance hall of the gate and leave the same way.

But when the people come to worship at the big feasts, anyone who enters through the north gate has to exit through the south gate, and anyone who enters through the south gate has to exit through the north. You can't leave the way you came in; you have to use the opposite gate. The prince will be right there with them, part of the crowd.
At the festivals and feasts, the grain offering is five and a half gallons with a gallon of oil for the bull and ram, and a handful of grain for each lamb.

When the prince wants to give a freewill offering to God, the east gate will be opened for him. He'll make his offering just like he does on the Sabbath. Then he'll leave, and they'll shut the gate after him.

Every morning, you're to bring a perfect one-year-old lamb as a burnt offering to God. Also, every morning, bring a grain offering of about a gallon of grain with a quart of oil to moisten it. This is a regular thing. The lamb, the grain, and the oil are a daily ritual.

Here's another message from God, the Master: If the prince gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his sons, it stays in the family. But if he gives a gift to a servant, the servant only has it until the year of liberation, the Jubilee year. After that, it goes back to the prince. His inheritance is only for his sons. The prince can't just take land from the people. He can only give his sons what he already owns. None of my people should be forced off their land.

Then the man led me through the north gate to the holy rooms for the priests and showed me a room at the back to the west. He said, 'This is the kitchen where the priests will cook the guilt and sin offerings and bake the grain offering. This way, they don't have to do it in the main courtyard and accidentally endanger the people out there with holy stuff.'

He then took me to the outer courtyard and to each of its four corners. In each corner, there was another smaller court. These four smaller courts were all the same size, about sixty by forty-five feet. Around the inside walls of these courts was a stone shelf, and under the shelves were places to cook.
He told me, 'These are the kitchens where the Temple servants will cook the people's sacrifices.'

Ezekiel.title: This River is GOATED
paragraphs: Alright, so this guy takes me back to the Temple entrance, and get this—I see water just pouring out from under the Temple porch, heading east (since the Temple faced east). The stream was coming from the south side of the Temple, just south of the altar. Then he takes me out through the north gate, leads me around the outside to the east gate complex, and whoa—the water was seriously gushing from the south side.

He walks east with a measuring tape and marks off about 1,500 feet. He leads me through the water, which is only ankle-deep. He measures another 1,500 feet, and now the water's up to my knees. Another 1,500 feet, and it's up to my waist. He measures another 1,500 feet, and by this point, it's a whole river. It's way over my head, deep enough to swim in—like, no way you could walk through it.
He asks me, "Son of man, you getting a good look at this?"
Then he brings me back to the riverbank. As I'm sitting there, I notice tons of trees on both sides of the river.

He tells me, "This water flows east, down to the Arabah valley, and then into the Dead Sea. When it hits that stagnant water, the sea will become fresh. Everywhere this river goes, life will just explode—huge schools of fish—because it's turning the salty sea into fresh water. Life just thrives wherever the river flows. Fishermen will be lined up shoulder to shoulder along the shore, from En Gedi all the way to En-eglaim, casting their nets. The sea will be packed with all kinds of fish, just like the Mediterranean.
"But the swamps and marshes won't get fresh. They're gonna stay salty.

"But along the river itself, on both banks, all kinds of fruit trees will grow. Their leaves will never wilt, and they'll never stop producing fruit. They'll have a new crop every single month because the river from the Sanctuary feeds them. Their fruit will be for food, and their leaves will be for healing."

This is a message from the Lord, the Master: "These are the borders you'll use to divide the land for the twelve tribes of Israel, and Joseph gets two shares. You'll divide it up equally. I made a solemn promise to give it to your ancestors, and I swore this land would be your inheritance.
"Here are the land boundaries:

"The northern border runs from the Mediterranean Sea along the Hethlon road to the turnoff for Hamath's entrance, then to Zedad, Berothah, and Sibraim (which is between Damascus and Hamath territories), and then on to Hazor-hatticon on the Hauran border. The boundary goes from the Sea to Hazor-enon, with Damascus and Hamath to the north. That's the northern border.
"The eastern border runs between Damascus and Hauran, down the Jordan River between Gilead and the land of Israel, all the way to the Dead Sea, as far as Tamar. That's the eastern border.
"The southern border runs west from Tamar to the waters of Meribah-kadesh, follows the Brook of Egypt, and goes out to the Mediterranean Sea. That's the southern border.
"The western border is just the Mediterranean Sea, from the southern border north to the point where the road turns east towards the entrance of Hamath. That's the western border.

"You're to divide this land among the twelve tribes of Israel. Split it up as your inheritance, and you have to include the foreigners who have settled among you and had kids. Treat them just like they were born there. They get an inheritance among the tribes of Israel too. Whatever tribe the foreigner lives in, that's where they get their inheritance. This is a decree from the Lord, the Master."

Ezekiel.title: The Ultimate Land Distribution
paragraphs: Alright, here's the breakdown for the tribes:

First up, Dan gets a slice of land. It's up on the northern border, following the Hethlon road that cuts over to the entrance of Hamath, going all the way to Hazor-enon. This means the territory of Damascus is to the north, next to Hamath, with the northern border stretching from the east to the west.
Asher gets a piece of the action too, bordering Dan's territory from east to west.
Naphtali is next, with a portion of land that borders Asher from east to west.
Then there's Manasseh, whose land borders Naphtali from east to west.
Ephraim gets a portion that borders Manasseh from east to west.
Reuben's portion borders Ephraim from east to west.
And Judah's portion borders Reuben from east to west.

Now, right next to Judah's territory, from east to west, is this special sacred area that you're gonna set aside. It's a square, about seven by seven miles, and the Sanctuary is gonna be right in the middle. This holy area for God will be seven miles long and just under three miles wide.

Here's how it's getting divided up. The priests get the area that's seven miles on the north and south sides, and a bit over three miles wide on the east and west sides. God's Sanctuary will be at the center of it. This is for the priests who are set apart, the descendants of Zadok who stayed loyal and served me, and didn't wander off like the other Levites did when Israel went off the rails. This is their special piece of the land, a gift from the land itself, super holy ground, right next to the Levites' section.

The Levites get a section that's the same size as the priests' land, roughly seven by three miles. But here's the rule: they can't sell or trade any of it. It's the best part of the land, not to mention it's holy to God.

Whatever is left of that 'sacred square'—each side is seven miles by a mile and a half—is for regular use. That's for the city and its buildings, with some open country around it, but the city itself is in the center. The north, south, east, and west sides of the city are each about a mile and a half long. There will be a strip of pasture, 125 yards wide, surrounding the city on all sides. The rest of this area, three miles of countryside to the east and west of the sacred zone, is for farming. It'll provide food for the city. People from all the tribes of Israel will come and work the fields.
This whole dedicated area, set apart for holy purposes, will be a square, seven miles by seven miles, a 'holy square,' and it includes the part for the city.

The rest of the land, the country stretching east to the Jordan River and west to the Mediterranean Sea from the seven-mile sides of the 'holy square,' belongs to the prince. His land is squeezed between the tribal lands to the north and south, and it extends both east and west from the 'sacred square' with the Temple in the middle. The land for the Levites on one side and the city on the other is in the middle of the prince's territory. The 'sacred square' is flanked on the east and west by the prince's land and bordered on the north and south by the territories of Judah and Benjamin.
And now for the rest of the tribes:
Benjamin gets one portion, stretching from the eastern to the western boundary.
Simeon gets a portion, bordering Benjamin from east to west.
Issachar gets a portion, bordering Simeon from east to west.
Zebulun gets a portion, bordering Issachar from east to west.
Gad gets a portion, bordering Zebulun from east to west.
The southern border of Gad will run south from Tamar to the waters of Meribah-kadesh, follow the Brook of Egypt, and then go out to the great Mediterranean Sea.
This is the land you're supposed to divide up among the tribes of Israel for them to inherit. These are their portions. That's a decree from God, the Master.

And these are the gates of the city. On the north side, which is 2,250 yards long (and the city gates are named after the tribes of Israel), there are three gates: the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah, and the gate of Levi.
On the east side, which is also 2,250 yards, there are three gates: the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin, and the gate of Dan.
On the south side, measuring 2,250 yards, there are three gates: the gate of Simeon, the gate of Issachar, and the gate of Zebulun.
On the west side, also 2,250 yards, there are three gates: the gate of Gad, the gate of Asher, and the gate of Naphtali.
The four sides of the city add up to a total of nearly six miles.
And from now on, the name of the city will be Yahweh-Shammah:
God-Is-There.

Daniel.title: The Ultimate Diet Challenge: Veggies vs. King's Food
paragraphs: So, get this. Three years into King Jehoiakim's rule in Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon decided to declare war on Jerusalem and basically laid siege to the city. God let King Jehoiakim of Judah get captured, and on top of that, Nebuchadnezzar also snagged some of the valuable stuff from the Temple of God. He took the king and all the goods back to Babylon, which was this ancient place called Shinar, and put all the Temple furnishings in his own sacred treasury.

The king then told Ashpenaz, the guy in charge of the palace staff, to find some of the best and brightest young Israelite men from royal and noble families. He wanted guys who were healthy, good-looking, smart, and well-educated—basically, perfect candidates for leadership roles in his government. The plan was to brainwash them with the Babylonian language and all their magic and fortune-telling nonsense. The king also ordered that they be served the same food as the royal court—the best of the best. After three years of this training, they were supposed to be ready to serve in the king's court.

Four young men from Judah—Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah—were part of this group. The head of the palace staff gave them new Babylonian names: Daniel was now Belteshazzar, Hananiah was Shadrach, Mishael was Meshach, and Azariah was Abednego.

But Daniel was determined not to disrespect himself by eating the king's food or drinking his wine. So, he asked the head of the palace staff to let him off the hook with the royal diet. By God's grace, the head of the staff liked Daniel, but he was still nervous. He warned him, "I'm scared of what the king will do. He's the one who ordered this diet, and if he sees that you're not as healthy as the other guys, he'll literally have my head!"

But Daniel went to the steward who was in charge of him and his friends, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, and said, "Just test us for ten days. Give us only vegetables and water. Then, compare how we look with the other young men who are eating the royal food. You can decide what to do based on what you see."

The steward was cool with it and gave them vegetables and water for ten days. At the end of the ten days, they looked healthier and stronger than all the others who had been eating from the royal menu. So, the steward kept letting them skip the royal food and drink and just served them vegetables.

God blessed these four young men with incredible knowledge and skill in all sorts of literature and life lessons. On top of that, Daniel had a special gift for understanding all kinds of visions and dreams. When the training period set by the king was over, the head of the royal staff brought all the young men to Nebuchadnezzar. The king interviewed them and found that Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah were way ahead of all the other young men. No one could even compare to them.

And so, they began their service in the king's court. Whenever the king needed advice on anything, whether it was about books or life, he found them to be ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his entire kingdom.
Daniel continued to serve the king until the first year of King Cyrus's reign.

Daniel.title: The King's Crazy Dream & Daniel's God-Tier Reveal
paragraphs: So, in the second year he was king, Nebuchadnezzar started having these wild dreams that were seriously messing with his head. He literally couldn't sleep. So he calls up all his go-to guys—the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and psychics—to figure out what was up with his dreams. When they all showed up and stood in front of him, he was like, 'Yo, I had this dream and it's living rent-free in my head. I'm not sleeping until I know what it means.'
The psychics, speaking in Aramaic, were like, 'Long live the king! Just tell us the dream, and we'll totally break it down for you.'

But the king shot back, 'Nah, here's the deal. If you can't tell me the dream *and* what it means, I'm gonna have you guys ripped to shreds, and your houses will be turned into rubble. But if you can do it, I'll hook you up with tons of gifts and make you famous. So, get to it. Tell me the dream and what it means.'
They tried again, 'Your Majesty, with all due respect, just tell us the dream. We'll give you the interpretation.'

But the king was like, 'I see what you're doing. You're just stalling for time 'cause you know you're toast. You know if you can't tell me the dream, it's game over for you. I see right through your little act. You're just gonna make up some fake story to try and confuse me until I give up. Not happening. First, you tell me the dream, and then I'll know you're for real about the interpretation and not just making stuff up.'

The psychics were shook. 'Literally no one on earth can do what you're asking. No king, no matter how goated, has ever asked for something like this from a magician, enchanter, or psychic. What you're asking is basically impossible unless a god reveals it—and they don't just hang out with us regular people.'

That just made the king even more mad. He totally lost it and ordered all the wise men in Babylon to be executed. When the order went out, Daniel and his friends were on the list too. They were marked to be killed.

When Arioch, the head of the royal guards, was getting ready to carry out the executions, Daniel, being super smart, pulled him aside and quietly asked what was going on. 'Why the sudden death sentence for everyone?'
After Arioch gave him the lowdown, Daniel went straight to the king and asked for a little more time so he could interpret the dream.

Then Daniel went home and told his boys Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah what was happening. He told them to pray to the God of heaven to have mercy and help them solve this mystery so the four of them wouldn't get killed along with all the other wise men in Babylon.
That night, God revealed the secret to Daniel in a vision. Daniel immediately started praising the God of heaven, saying,

'Shoutout to God's name, forever and ever. He knows everything, he does everything. He changes the seasons and directs history. He puts kings in power and takes them down. He gives people intelligence and insight. He reveals deep and secret things, he sees in the dark—he's literally made of light! God of my ancestors, thank you so much! All the praise to you! You made me wise and strong. And now you've shown us what we asked for. You've solved the king's mystery.'
So Daniel went back to Arioch, the guy in charge of the executions. He said, 'Yo, cancel the executions! Take me to the king, and I'll tell him what his dream means.'
Arioch didn't waste a second. He ran to the king with Daniel and said, 'I found a guy from the Jewish exiles who can interpret the king's dream!'
The king asked Daniel (who had a Babylonian name, Belteshazzar), 'Are you for real? You can actually tell me the dream I had and what it means?'

Daniel answered the king, 'No human can solve the king's mystery, it doesn't matter who they are—no wise man, enchanter, magician, or psychic. But there is a God in heaven who solves mysteries, and he has solved this one. He's giving King Nebuchadnezzar a sneak peek of what's going to happen in the future. This is the dream you had when you were lying in bed, the vision that was in your head:

'While you were just chilling on your bed, O king, you started thinking about what's coming in the future. The God who reveals mysteries showed you what will happen. But the interpretation is being given through me, not because I'm smarter than anyone else in the country, but so that you'll know what it means, so you'll understand what you dreamed.'

'What you saw, O king, was this massive statue standing in front of you. It looked super impressive. And honestly, kinda terrifying. The statue's head was pure gold, its chest and arms were silver, its stomach and hips were bronze, its legs were iron, and its feet were a mix of iron and clay. While you were staring at this statue, a rock that was cut out of a mountain by, like, invisible hands, came and hit the statue, smashing its iron and clay feet. Then the whole thing just fell apart—iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold, all smashed into tiny pieces. It was like dust in an empty lot on a hot summer day, blown away by the wind until there was nothing left. But the rock that hit the statue became a huge mountain that took over the whole horizon. That was your dream.'

'And now, we'll tell you what it means. You, O king, are the most powerful king on earth. The God of heaven has given you everything: rule, power, strength, and glory. He put you in charge of all people, wild animals, and birds, all over the world—you're the top ruler, you're the head of gold. But your kingdom will be taken over by another kingdom, not as great as yours, and that one by a third, a bronze kingdom, that will still rule the whole land. And after that, a fourth kingdom will come, as strong as iron. Just like iron smashes everything to pieces, it will break and crush the kingdoms that came before it.'

'But then the feet and toes that were a mix of clay and iron will turn into a messed-up kingdom with some iron still in it. Just like the toes were part clay and part iron, it'll end up being a mix of breakable and unbreakable. That kingdom won't stick together, any more than iron and clay can mix.'

'But during the time of these kingdoms, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, and no other kingdom will ever take it over. In the end, it will crush all the other kingdoms and finish them off, and it will stand strong forever. It'll be like that rock cut from the mountain by an invisible hand that crushed the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold.'
'The great God has let the king know what will happen in the future. This is the 100% accurate telling of the dream, and the interpretation is also legit.'

When Daniel finished, King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, totally in awe of Daniel. He ordered sacrifices and incense to be offered in Daniel's honor. He said to Daniel, 'No cap, your God is the God of all gods, the Master of all kings. And he solves all mysteries, I know, because you've solved this one.'

Then the king gave Daniel a major promotion, showered him with gifts, and made him governor over the whole province of Babylon and the head of all the Babylonian wise men. And because Daniel asked, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to high-up positions throughout Babylon, while Daniel governed from the royal palace.

Daniel.title: Refusing to Bow Down? WILD
paragraphs: So, King Nebuchadnezzar had this massive gold statue built—like, 90 feet tall and 9 feet wide. It was huge. He stuck it right in the middle of the Dura plain in Babylon. Then he invited, like, *everyone* important—all the big shots and VIPs—to this huge dedication party for the statue. And of course, they all showed up and stood in front of this giant statue he'd put up.

Then this announcer gets up and shouts, 'Listen up, everybody! No matter who you are or where you're from! As soon as you hear the music start—we're talking a full-on orchestra with trumpets, trombones, everything—you have to drop to your knees and worship the gold statue King Nebuchadnezzar built. And if you don't? You get tossed straight into a fiery furnace. No joke.'

The music started, and it was this epic band with all the instruments you can imagine. And just like that, everyone—literally everyone, from all over—bowed down and worshiped the gold statue the king had set up.

But right then, some local fortune-tellers went to the king to snitch on the Jews. They were like, 'Hey, King, hope you live forever! You made a rule that everyone had to bow down to the statue when the music played, or they'd get thrown into a furnace, right? Well, these three Jewish guys you put in charge—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—are totally ignoring you. They're not respecting your gods, and they're refusing to worship the gold statue.'

The king was livid. He ordered Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to be brought to him. When they got there, he asked, 'Is this for real, guys? You're really disrespecting my gods and refusing to worship the statue I made? Look, I'll give you one more chance. When the music plays, you bow down and worship the statue. If you don't, you're going straight into that furnace, and that's final. What god do you think can save you from me then?'

Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego basically told the king, 'We're not worried. If you throw us in the fire, the God we serve is more than able to save us from the furnace and anything else you can think of. But even if he doesn't, we want to make it clear, O king, that we're still not going to serve your gods or worship your gold statue. No cap.'

Nebuchadnezzar was so mad his face turned purple. He completely lost it and ordered the furnace to be cranked up seven times hotter than normal. He had some of the strongest soldiers in his army tie up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and toss them into the super-hot furnace. They were tied up, fully dressed, and thrown right into the fire. The furnace was so insanely hot because the king was in such a rush that the flames actually killed the soldiers who threw them in. Meanwhile, the fire was just raging around the three guys.
Suddenly, King Nebuchadnezzar jumped up, totally shocked. 'Wait a minute,' he said. 'Didn't we throw three guys in there, all tied up?'
'Yeah, that's right, O king,' they answered.
'But look!' he yelled. 'I see four guys, just walking around in the fire, totally fine! And the fourth one looks like a son of the gods or something!'
Nebuchadnezzar ran to the opening of the furnace and shouted, 'Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come on out!'
And just like that, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego walked out of the fire.
