All the important people, the government officials, and the king's advisors crowded around to check them out. They saw that the fire hadn't touched them at all—not a single hair was burned, their clothes weren't even scorched, and they didn't even smell like smoke.

Nebuchadnezzar said, 'Praise be to the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego! He sent his angel to rescue his servants who trusted him. They defied the king's command and were willing to die rather than serve or worship any god except their own.'

'So, I'm making a new rule: Anyone, anywhere, from any background, who says anything bad about the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego will be torn apart, and their house will be demolished. There's no other god who can pull off a rescue like that.'
Then the king gave Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego a big promotion in Babylon.

Daniel.title: King's Wild Dream & God's Ultimate Prank
paragraphs: Yo, what's up world! This is King Nebuchadnezzar, sending this out to everyone, everywhere—no matter who you are or where you're from. Hope you're all living your best life. I gotta tell you about the seriously mind-blowing miracles the Most High God did for me.
His miracles are insane, and the stuff He does is just wild. His kingdom is forever, and His rule never stops.

So, I, Nebuchadnezzar, was just chilling at my palace, totally relaxed and living the good life. But then, I had this dream while I was in bed that totally freaked me out—it was a straight-up nightmare. So I called all the wise guys in Babylon to come and tell me what it meant. When they all showed up—the magicians, the psychics, the fortune-tellers, all of them—I told them the dream. But none of them had a clue.
Then Daniel came in. His Babylonian name is Belteshazzar, named after my own god, and this dude is full of the Holy Spirit. So I told him my dream.
"Belteshazzar," I said, "you're the head of all the magicians, and I know you're filled with the Holy Spirit, so no mystery is too hard for you. Check out this dream I had and tell me what's up."

"So, I was lying in bed and I saw this huge tree right in the middle of the world. As I watched, it got massive and super strong. Its top literally touched the sky, and you could see it from anywhere on Earth. Its leaves were gorgeous, and it had so much fruit—enough for everyone! Wild animals were chilling under it, birds had nests in its branches, and basically everything was fed and protected by it."
"Then, still in my dream, I saw a holy messenger come down from heaven and yell:"

"'Cut down the tree, chop off its branches, strip its leaves, and scatter its fruit. Get all the animals out from under it and the birds out of its branches. But leave the stump and roots in the ground, tied up with iron and bronze in the middle of a field.'"
"'Let him get soaked with dew from the sky and eat with the animals. Let him totally lose his mind and get the brain of an animal instead, and let this go on for seven years.'"

"The angels are making this official, the holy messengers are delivering the message, so that everyone alive will know that the Most High God is the one in charge of all human kingdoms. He can set up kingdoms however He wants and can make leaders out of complete nobodies."

"So that was the dream I, King Nebuchadnezzar, had. Now it's your turn, Belteshazzar—tell me what it means. None of the other wise guys in Babylon could figure it out, but I know you can. You're full of the Holy Spirit."
At first, Daniel, who they called Belteshazzar in Babylon, was pretty shaken up. The thoughts flooding his mind were terrifying.
"Belteshazzar," the king said, "it's cool. Don't let the dream and what it means freak you out."
"My king," Belteshazzar said, "I really wish this dream was about your enemies and not you."

"That tree you saw that grew so huge and strong, with its top in the sky, visible from everywhere; the tree with the amazing leaves and tons of fruit for everyone; the tree where animals took shelter and birds built nests—that tree is you, O king."
"You've become great and powerful. Your royal awesomeness reaches the sky, and your rule extends to every corner of the world."

"But the part about the holy angel coming down from heaven and saying, 'Cut down the tree, destroy it, but leave the stump and roots in the ground tied up with iron and bronze in the field; let him be soaked with dew from the sky and eat with the animals for seven years'—that's also about you, my king. It means the Most High God has laid down this sentence for you: You'll be kicked out of society and have to live with wild animals. You'll eat grass like a cow. You'll be soaked with dew from the sky. This will happen for seven years, and you'll learn that the Most High God is the one who rules over all human kingdoms and can put anyone He wants in charge."
"The part about leaving the stump and roots means your kingdom will still be here for you after you learn that heaven is in control."
"So, king, listen to my advice: Ditch your sins and start doing good for others. Stop your wicked ways and start caring for the poor and needy. Then maybe your good life will continue."

All of this actually happened to King Nebuchadnezzar. A year later, he was walking on the balcony of his royal palace in Babylon and bragging, "Look at this amazing city of Babylon! I built it all by myself as a royal palace to show off my honor and glory!"

He had barely finished speaking when a voice from heaven said, "This is the final word on you, King Nebuchadnezzar: Your kingdom is being taken from you. You will be driven away from people and will live with wild animals. You will eat grass like a cow. This will last for seven years, enough time for you to learn that the Most High God rules over all human kingdoms and puts whoever He wants in charge."
It happened instantly. Nebuchadnezzar was kicked out of society, ate grass like a cow, and got soaked with dew from the sky. His hair grew long like eagle feathers and his nails grew like hawk claws.
"After seven years, I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven. My sanity was restored, and I praised the Most High God, thanking and glorifying the One who lives forever:"
"'His rule is eternal, His kingdom never ends. Life on earth is pretty insignificant, but God's army in heaven keeps everything in order. No one can stop Him or question His authority.'"

"The moment my mind came back, I also got back my majesty and splendor, making my kingdom shine again. All the leaders and important people came to find me. I was put back on the throne, and I became even greater than before. And that's why I'm singing—I, Nebuchadnezzar—singing and praising the King of Heaven:"
"'Everything He does is right, and He does it perfectly. He knows how to humble a proud person.'"

Daniel.title: The Writing on the Wall Gets Real
paragraphs: So, King Belshazzar threw this massive party for a thousand of his VIPs. The wine was flowing like crazy. Belshazzar, feeling buzzed, randomly ordered the gold and silver cups that his dad, Nebuchadnezzar, had jacked from God's Temple in Jerusalem. He wanted to drink from them with his crew, his wives, and his side-chicks. When they brought out the fancy cups, the king, his boys, his wives, and his concubines all started drinking wine from them. They drank and drunkenly cheered for their own gods—idols made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.

Then, out of nowhere, the fingers of a human hand just appeared and started writing on the palace wall, which was all lit up by a lamp. When the king saw this disembodied hand writing, he went totally pale, like he'd seen a ghost, and freaked out. His legs turned to jelly and his knees were literally knocking together. He screamed for his magic guys, the fortune-tellers, and the psychics to come over. He told these Babylonian wizards, “Yo, anyone who can read this writing and tell me what it means will get famous and rich—I'm talking a purple robe, a fat gold chain—and you'll be the third most powerful person in the kingdom.”

They all tried, one by one, but nobody could make sense of it. They couldn't read the writing or explain it to the king. So now the king was even more scared. He looked like all the blood had drained from his face. His VIPs were all in a panic.

Then the queen heard about the king and his nobles losing their minds and came into the banquet hall. She was like, “Long live the king! Don’t get all worked up. Don’t just sit there looking terrified. There’s a guy in your kingdom who’s literally full of the Holy Spirit. Back in your dad's day, he was famous for being a genius with spiritual wisdom. He was so legit that your dad, King Nebuchadnezzar, put him in charge of all the magicians, enchanters, fortune-tellers, and psychics. There was no one like him. He could do anything—explain dreams, solve mysteries, figure out puzzles. His name is Daniel, but the king nicknamed him Belteshazzar. Get Daniel in here. He’ll tell you what’s going on.”

So they brought Daniel in. The king asked him, “Are you Daniel, one of the Jewish exiles my dad brought from Judah? I’ve heard about you—that you’re full of the Holy Spirit, that you have a brilliant mind, and that you're incredibly wise. We brought in the wise men and enchanters to read this writing on the wall and explain it to me. They couldn’t figure it out—not a single word. But I’ve heard that you can interpret dreams and solve mysteries. So, if you can read this and tell me what it means, you’ll be rich and famous—a purple robe, a big gold chain around your neck—and you'll be third-in-command in the kingdom.”
Daniel replied to the king, “You can keep your gifts, or give them to someone else. But I’ll read the writing for you and tell you what it means.

“Listen up, O king! The Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar a huge kingdom and a legendary reputation. Because God made him so famous, people from all over, no matter their race or religion, were totally scared of him. He could kill or spare people just because he felt like it. He’d promote or demote people on a whim. He got a huge ego and a hard heart. Then God knocked him off his high horse and took away his fame. He was kicked out of society, lost his mind, and lived like a wild animal. He ate grass like a cow and got soaked by the rain until he finally learned his lesson: that the Most High God is the one who rules over human kingdoms and can put anyone he wants in charge.

“You’re his son and you knew all this, but you’re just as arrogant as he was. Look at you, trying to compete with the Lord of heaven! You had the holy cups from his Temple brought to your drunk party so you and your friends, your wives, and your concubines could drink from them. You used the sacred cups to toast your gods of silver and gold, bronze and iron, wood and stone—gods that are blind, deaf, and dumb. But you dissed the living God who holds your entire life in his hands, from start to finish.
“That’s why God sent the hand that wrote on the wall, and this is what it says: MENE, TEQEL, and PERES. And this is what the words mean:
“Mene: God has counted the days of your rule, and they’re all used up.
“Teqel: You’ve been weighed on the scales, and you’re seriously lacking.
“Peres: Your kingdom has been split up and handed over to the Medes and Persians.”
Belshazzar did what he promised. He gave Daniel a purple robe, put the big gold chain around his neck, and made him the third most powerful person in the kingdom.
That very same night, the Babylonian king Belshazzar was murdered. Darius the Mede, who was sixty-two, took over as king.

Daniel.title: Daniel vs. the Lions' Den: EPIC Faith Challenge!
paragraphs: So, King Darius decided to switch things up in his kingdom. He set up 120 governors to run things everywhere. On top of them, he put three main bosses, and guess who was one of them? Daniel. The governors had to report to these bosses, who kept everything running smoothly for the king. But Daniel? He was on another level. He was so smart and had such a great attitude that he totally showed up the other bosses and governors. The king saw this and was like, "Yo, I'm putting this guy in charge of everything."

The other bosses and governors got super jealous and started trying to dig up some dirt on Daniel to use against him. But they couldn't find anything. He was a total stand-up guy, super trustworthy. There was zero evidence of him slacking off or doing anything shady. So they finally gave up and were like, "Ugh, we're never gonna get this guy unless we make it about his religion."

The vice-regents and governors all ganged up, went to the king, and said, "King Darius, hope you live forever! All of us—your top officials, governors, and leaders—had a meeting and we think you should make a new rule:
For the next 30 days, nobody is allowed to pray to any god or person except for you, O king. Anyone who breaks this rule gets thrown into the lions' den.
"You should totally make this an official decree, O king. Make it a law that can't be changed, like the laws of the Medes and Persians."
So, King Darius signed the new law.

When Daniel heard the law was official, he just kept doing what he always did. He went home to his upstairs room where the windows opened toward Jerusalem. Three times a day, he got on his knees and prayed, thanking and praising his God, no cap.

The haters came and found him praying and asking God for help. They went straight to the king and were like, "Hey, remember that decree you signed? The one that said for 30 days, no one could pray to anyone but you, or they'd be thrown into the lions' den?"
"Absolutely," the king said. "It's a done deal, written in stone, like all the laws of the Medes and Persians."
Then they dropped the bomb: "Well, Daniel, one of the Jewish exiles, is totally ignoring you and your law, O king. He's still praying three times a day."
Hearing this, the king was seriously bummed out. He spent the whole rest of the day trying to figure out a way to save Daniel from the mess he'd created.
But then the haters came back and said, "Remember, O king, the law of the Medes and Persians says that a king's decree can never be changed."
The king finally gave in and ordered them to bring Daniel and throw him into the lions' den. But he said to Daniel, "Your God, the one you're so loyal to, is gonna get you out of this."
A huge stone was put over the opening of the den. The king sealed it with his own ring and the rings of all his nobles, so nobody could change Daniel's fate.
The king went back to his palace but was in no mood to eat. He couldn't sleep at all and just fasted all night.

First thing in the morning, the king got up and rushed to the lions' den. As he got close, he called out, super worried, "Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, the one you serve so faithfully, saved you from the lions?"
"Long live the king!" Daniel shouted back. "My God sent his angel, and he shut the lions' mouths so they couldn't hurt me. God knows I'm innocent, and I've never done anything to wrong you, O king."
When the king heard this, he was overjoyed. He ordered them to get Daniel out of the den. When they pulled him up, he didn't have a single scratch on him. He had trusted his God, for real.

Then the king ordered that the guys who had ratted on Daniel be thrown into the lions' den, along with their wives and kids. Before they even hit the ground, the lions were all over them, tearing them to pieces. It was brutal.
Then King Darius sent out this message to people of every race, color, and belief all over the world:

"Hope you're all living in peace! I'm making a new rule that in every part of my kingdom, everyone must respect and fear the God of Daniel. He is the living God who lives forever. His kingdom will never be destroyed. His rule is eternal. He's a savior and a rescuer. He does insane miracles in heaven and on earth. He's the one who saved Daniel from the power of the lions."
From then on, Daniel was a big deal during Darius's reign, and also when the next king, Cyrus the Persian, took over.

Daniel.title: Daniel's Epic Nightmare About Four Wild Beasts
paragraphs: So, back in the first year King Belshazzar was ruling Babylon, Daniel had this dream that was straight-up terrifying. Like, a full-on nightmare. He wrote it all down:
“In my dream, I saw the four winds of heaven making the sea go totally wild. Then, four massive beasts, all looking super different, came up out of the water.

“The first beast was like a lion, but with eagle wings. As I was watching, its wings got ripped off. Then it was forced to stand on two feet like a person, and it was given a human heart. Wild, right?
“Then I saw a second beast that looked like a bear. It was stumbling around with three ribs in its mouth. A voice told it, ‘Go get ‘em! Eat your fill!’
“Next up was another beast, this one like a panther. It had four bird-like wings on its back and four heads. This thing was made to be in charge.

“After that, a fourth beast showed up, and this one was low-key horrifying. It had massive iron teeth and just crushed and ate everything. Whatever was left, it stomped on. This one was a whole different level of monster. And it had ten horns.

“I was just staring at the horns, trying to figure them out, when another little horn popped up. Three of the first horns were yanked out to make space for it. This little horn had human-like eyes and a big mouth that was saying some really arrogant stuff.
“As I was watching all this,

“Thrones were set up and the Ancient One sat down. His clothes were white as snow, and his hair was like white wool. His throne was literally on fire, with blazing wheels. A river of fire was flowing from the throne. Thousands and thousands of angels were serving him. The court was in session, and the books were opened.

“I kept watching. The little horn was still talking all that trash. Then, I saw the monster get killed and its body thrown into a huge fire. The other beasts got to live a bit longer, but they had no power.

“Then in my dream, I saw someone who looked like a human, a son of man, coming on the clouds. He went to the Ancient One and was brought right up to him. He was given all the power and glory to rule. People from every race and nation had to serve him. His rule would last forever, no cap. His kingdom would never be destroyed.

“But honestly, I, Daniel, was seriously disturbed. These visions had me all kinds of agitated. So I went up to one of the guys standing there and asked him what it all meant. And he broke it down for me:
“‘These four huge beasts,’ he said, ‘are four kingdoms that will rise up on earth. But in the end, the holy people of the Most High God will get the kingdom and keep it forever and ever.’

“But I needed to know more. I was super curious about the fourth beast, the one that was so different, the terrifying one with iron teeth and bronze claws that ate everything and stomped on the rest. And I wanted to know about the ten horns and the new little horn that popped up and took out three of the others. This new horn had eyes and a big, arrogant mouth and was the new top dog. I watched it attack God's people and win. But then the Ancient One stepped in and ruled in favor of God's people. In the end, they took over the kingdom.

“The guy kept explaining: ‘The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that will show up on earth. It’ll be different from the others, a total monster kingdom that will chew up and spit out everyone. The ten horns are ten kings that will come from this kingdom. But then another king will show up, and he'll be different. He'll start by taking down three kings. Then he'll say blasphemous things against the Most High God, go after God's followers, and try to change all the sacred laws and traditions. God's people will be in his power for a time, two times, and half a time.’

“‘But when the court is in session, that horn will lose all its power and be completely destroyed. Then the rule and authority and glory of all the kingdoms on earth will be given to the people of the Most High God. Their kingdom will last forever. All other rulers will serve and obey them.’
“And that was the end of the dream. I, Daniel, was in shock. I felt like I'd seen a ghost. But I kept it all to myself.”

Daniel.title: Crazy Animal Battle Royale?! Here's the Deets
paragraphs: So, back in the third year of King Belshazzar's reign, I, Daniel, had another vision. This was round two for me.

In the vision, I was in Susa, the main city in the Elam province, just chilling by the Ulai Canal. Then I look over and, whoa, there's this ram just standing by the gate. This ram had two massive horns, one was bigger than the other, but the bigger one grew in last which was kinda weird. Then I watched this ram just go wild, charging west, then north, then south. Literally no other animal could stop it. It was doing whatever it wanted, walking around like it owned the place, the king of all animals.

While I was watching this, trying to figure out what was going on, a billy goat with this giant horn right in the middle of its forehead came flying out of the west. It was moving so fast it didn't even touch the ground. This goat went straight for the two-horned ram I saw earlier and, full of rage, just charged it. I saw it, completely furious, slam into the ram and break both its horns clean off. The ram didn't stand a chance. The billy goat threw the ram to the ground and just stomped all over it. Nothing could've saved the ram from that goat.

Then the billy goat got HUGE. But at its peak power, its massive horn broke off, and four other big horns grew in its place, pointing north, south, east, and west. And then from one of those big horns, another horn sprouted. It started out small but grew crazy big, pointing south and east—towards the beautiful land of Palestine. This horn grew so tall it reached the stars, the heavenly army, and it threw some of the stars down to earth and stomped on them. It even had the nerve to challenge God, the Prince of the whole celestial army! Then it got rid of the daily worship and trashed the Sanctuary. As a punishment for their sin, God's holy people got treated the same way as the daily worship. The horn threw God's Truth away. It was super arrogant and took over everything and everyone.
Then I heard two holy angels talking. One asked, 'How long is this gonna last—the daily worship being gone, this awful judgment for sin, God's holy people and the Sanctuary getting disrespected?'
The other one answered, 'It'll be for 2,300 evening and morning sacrifices. Then the Sanctuary will be made right again.'
While I, Daniel, was trying to process what I was seeing, suddenly a figure that looked like a human was standing in front of me.

Then I heard a man's voice from over by the Ulai Canal yell, 'Gabriel, tell this guy what's going on. Explain the vision to him.' He came over to me, but when he got close I got so scared I fell flat on my face.
He said, 'You need to understand, this vision is about the end times.' As soon as he said that, I passed out, face in the dirt. But he picked me up and got me back on my feet.
And then he kept going, 'I want to tell you what's going to happen when the angry judgment days are wrapping up, because all of this is going to have an end.'

'The ram with two horns you saw represents the two kings of the Medes and Persians. The billy goat is the kingdom of the Greeks. The huge horn on its forehead is the first Greek king. The four horns that grew after it broke are the four kings that come after him, but they won't be as powerful.'

'When their kingdoms are losing steam and rebellions are starting up, a king will appear. He'll be tough-looking and a master of tricks. His power will get crazy big. He'll talk a big game, super arrogant, doing whatever he wants, taking out heroes and holy people left and right. He'll scheme to make crime popular—and wow, will it be popular! He'll think he's invincible and get rid of anyone in his way. But when he tries to take on the Prince of all princes, he'll be totally crushed—but not by any human.' This vision of the 2,300 sacrifices, evening and morning, is legit but it's a secret. Keep it to yourself. It's about the distant future.'

I, Daniel, was just walking around in a daze, feeling sick for days. Then I finally got myself together and went back to my job working for the king. But I was still really bothered by the vision. I just couldn't figure it out.

Daniel.title: Daniel's Epic Prayer & A Wild Prophecy
paragraphs: So, in the first year that Darius, son of Ahasuerus, a Mede by birth, was king over Babylon, I, Daniel, was studying the Scriptures. I was trying to figure out the number of years God told the prophet Jeremiah that Jerusalem would be in ruins, which was seventy.

I turned to the Lord God and went all in with prayer and asking for help. I was fasting, wearing rough clothes, and sitting in ashes to show I was serious. I just poured out my heart to my God, confessing everything:

'O Lord, you are a great and awesome God. You always keep your covenant and show unfailing love to those who love you and follow your commands. But we have sinned and done wrong. We've rebelled against you and totally ignored the commands and regulations you gave us. We didn't listen to your servants the prophets, who spoke your word to our kings, our leaders, our ancestors, and all the people of the land. Lord, you are righteous, but this very day we are covered with shame—the people of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all Israel, both near and far, in all the countries where you have scattered us because of our unfaithfulness to you. O Lord, we and our kings, our princes and our ancestors are covered with shame because we have sinned against you.'

'But Lord our God, you are merciful and forgiving, even though we have rebelled against you. We have not obeyed the Lord our God or kept the laws he gave us through his servants the prophets. All Israel has transgressed your law and turned away, refusing to obey you. Therefore the curses and sworn judgments written in the Law of Moses, the servant of God, have been poured out on us, because we have sinned against you. You have carried out your words which you spoke against us and against our rulers by bringing on us a great disaster. What has happened to Jerusalem has never happened anywhere else under heaven.'

'Just as it is written in the Law of Moses, all this disaster has come on us, yet we have not sought the favor of the Lord our God by turning from our sins and giving attention to your truth. The Lord did not hesitate to bring the disaster on us, for the Lord our God is righteous in everything he does; yet we have not obeyed him.'

'Now, Lord our God, who brought your people out of Egypt with a mighty hand and who made a name for yourself that endures to this day, we have sinned, we have done wrong. Lord, in keeping with all your righteous acts, turn away your anger and your wrath from Jerusalem, your city, your holy hill. Our sins and the iniquities of our ancestors have made Jerusalem and your people an object of scorn to all those around us. Now, our God, hear the prayers and petitions of your servant. For your sake, Lord, look with favor on your desolate sanctuary. Act based on who you are, not what we deserve.'

'Give ear, our God, and hear; open your eyes and see the desolation of the city that bears your Name. We do not make requests of you because we are righteous, but because of your great mercy. This prayer is our only hope.'
'Lord, listen! Lord, forgive! Lord, hear and act! For your sake, my God, do not delay, because your city and your people bear your Name.'

While I was still speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel and making my request to the Lord my God for his holy hill—while I was still in prayer, Gabriel, the man I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight about the time of the evening sacrifice.

He instructed me and said to me, 'Daniel, I have now come to give you insight and understanding. As soon as you began to pray, a word went out, which I have come to tell you, for you are highly esteemed. Therefore, consider the word and understand the vision:'

'Seventy ‘sevens’ are decreed for your people and your holy city to finish transgression, to put an end to sin, to atone for wickedness, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy and to anoint the Most Holy Place.'

'Know and understand this: From the time the word goes out to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the Anointed One, the ruler, comes, there will be seven ‘sevens,’ and sixty-two ‘sevens.’ It will be rebuilt with streets and a trench, but in times of trouble. After the sixty-two ‘sevens,’ the Anointed One will be put to death and will have nothing. The people of the ruler who will come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. The end will come like a flood: War will continue until the end, and desolations have been decreed.'

'He will confirm a covenant with many for one ‘seven.’ In the middle of the ‘seven’ he will put an end to sacrifice and offering. And at the temple he will set up an abomination that causes desolation, until the end that is decreed is poured out on him.'

Daniel.title: This Angelic Battle is Next Level
paragraphs: So, in the third year that King Cyrus of Persia was in charge, a message was dropped on Daniel, whose Babylonian name was Belteshazzar. And this message was legit, no cap. It was about a huge war, and he totally got what it meant because it was like a divine download.
For three whole weeks, I, Daniel, was super bummed about Jerusalem. I was on a super basic diet—no fancy food, no meat, no wine. I didn't even shower or shave until the three weeks were over.

On the 24th day of the first month, I was just chilling by the Tigris River. I looked up, and you won't believe it—there was this guy dressed in linen with a solid gold belt. He was totally ripped and glowing, like a living statue, his face was shining, and his eyes were like lasers. His arms and feet looked like polished bronze, and his voice? It was deep and sounded like a whole choir singing at once. It was wild.

I, Daniel, was the only one who saw this vision. The guys with me didn't see it, but they totally freaked out and bounced, hiding because they thought something bad was about to go down. So I was left all alone, and after seeing that, I was literally shaking, and all the color drained from my face.
I heard his voice, and the sound of it made me pass out, face-first in the dirt. Then a hand touched me and pulled me up to my hands and knees.
'Daniel,' he said, 'you're a real one. Listen up to what I'm about to tell you. And get on your feet. I was sent to give you the scoop.'
When he said that, I stood up, but I was still trembling.

'Chill, Daniel,' he went on, 'don't be scared. The moment you decided to get humble and try to understand, your prayer was heard, and I headed your way. But I got held up by the angel-prince of Persia for a solid three weeks. Then Michael, one of the top-dog angel-princes, came to back me up. I left him there to deal with the Persian prince. And now I'm here to help you understand what's gonna happen to your people down the line. This vision is all about the future.'

While he was explaining all this, I just stared at the ground, speechless. Then, out of nowhere, something like a human hand touched my lips. I opened my mouth and started talking to the messenger: 'Dude, when I saw you, I was totally freaked out. My legs felt like jelly. I was frozen. How can a regular dude like me even talk to you, my master? I can't move. I can barely even breathe!'
Then this human-like figure touched me again and gave me strength. He said, 'Don't be afraid, my guy. Peace. It's all gonna be okay. Be strong. You got this.'
As he was saying that, I felt this new strength bubble up inside me. I said, 'Go on, my master, speak. You've given me the courage.'

He said, 'Do you know why I came to you? I have to go back and fight the angel-prince of Persia. And after I'm done with him, the angel-prince of Greece is gonna show up. But first, let me tell you what's written in the Book of Truth. And for the record, the only one who has my back in this fight is Michael, your angel-prince.'

Daniel.title: Prophecy Drop: North vs. South, Who Will Win?
paragraphs: “‘And for my part, I’ve been backing him up and keeping him strong since the first year Darius the Mede was in charge.’

“‘But now, let me spill the tea on what’s really going down: Three more kings are gonna pop up in Persia, and then a fourth one will show up, way richer than all of them. Once he feels all high and mighty because of his cash, he’s gonna try and pick a fight with the entire kingdom of Greece.

“‘Then, this super powerful king will roll in, take over a massive territory, and basically do whatever he wants. But right when he’s at the peak of his game, thinking he’s got it all on lock, his kingdom will get split into four, like north, south, east, and west. But his own kids won’t get any of it. His royal line will be totally cut off. Other people will just swoop in, tear it apart, and take what they can for themselves.

“‘Next up, the king of the south will get really strong, but one of his own generals will get even stronger and end up ruling a bigger kingdom. After a few years, they’ll make a deal, and the daughter of the southern king will marry the northern king to make the peace treaty official. But her power won’t last, and her kid won’t make it either. She, her crew, her child, and her husband will all get totally betrayed.

“‘A while later, someone from her royal family will show up to take his place. He’ll lead his army to invade the northern king’s fortress and score a huge W. He’ll take all their fake gods and all the fancy gold and silver stuff that goes with them and haul it all back to Egypt. After a while, the northern king will bounce back and try to invade the south, but it’ll be a total fail. He’ll have to retreat.
“‘But then his sons will get a massive army together and come rushing down like a flood, hitting the south’s defenses with a crazy, all-out attack.

“‘The southern king, totally furious, will come out to fight the northern king and his huge army, and he’ll completely own them. After they clear away all the bodies, the king, high on the victory, will go on a crazy killing spree, taking out tens of thousands. But his win won’t last. The northern king will just build another army, even bigger than the last one, and after a few years, he’ll be back for a rematch with his giant army and tons of supplies.

“‘During that time, a bunch of other people will jump in and fight against the king of the south. Some hotheads from your own people, all hyped up on their own dreams, will join them. But they’ll just fizzle out and fail.

“‘When the king of the north shows up, he’ll set up a siege and capture the main fortress city. The southern armies will just crumble in front of him. Even their elite special forces won’t be able to stop him. He’ll just walk in like he owns the place. He’ll take over that beautiful land, Palestine, and just make himself at home. Then he’ll try to get everything under his control. He’ll propose a peace treaty and even give his own daughter to the southern king in marriage as part of a plot to destroy him. But the whole plan will backfire. It won’t work.

“‘Later, he’ll turn his attention to the coastal areas and take a bunch of prisoners, but some general will step in and shut down his whole bullying operation. The bully will get bullied! He’ll go back home to handle his own stuff, but by then, he’s basically washed up and you won’t hear from him again.
“‘He’ll be replaced by a total loser, a guy whose reputation is already trashed. And he won’t be around for long. He’ll just disappear from history without any drama or a big fight.

“‘A total reject will take his place, a guy who was looked down on and never got a promotion. He’ll shock everyone by coming out of nowhere and grabbing the kingdom. He’ll be like a steamroller, just crushing anyone who gets in his way. Even the Prince of the Covenant will be taken down. After they agree to a truce, he’ll break the terms. With just a small crew, he’ll take complete control. He’ll just randomly invade the richest areas. He’ll be worse than any of his ancestors, just stealing and looting the country, living it up with his friends in total luxury.

“‘He’ll make plans to attack the fortress cities, but they’ll be super shortsighted. He’ll get a big army together, all pumped to fight the king of the south. The southern king will respond by getting his own, even bigger army ready. But he won’t be able to keep it up for long because of some shady stuff happening behind the scenes. His own court is full of backstabbers. His army will get wrecked, and the battlefield will be covered in bodies.

“‘The two kings, both secretly plotting against each other, will sit down at a peace talk and just lie to each other’s faces. The treaty will be a total sham and nothing will come of it. But the story isn’t over yet. There’s more.
“‘The king of the north will head home with a ton of loot, but on his way, he’ll be dead-set on disrespecting the holy covenant.

“‘A year later, he’ll invade the south again. But this second time won’t be like the first. When Roman ships show up, he’ll chicken out and run back home. But on his way through the country, he’ll be furious about the holy covenant. He’ll team up with anyone who betrays the covenant, giving them special treatment. His own guards will march in and totally desecrate the Sanctuary. They’ll stop the daily worship and put up this disgusting, sacrilegious thing in its place. The northern king will suck up to the covenant-betrayers, making them even more corrupt with his smooth talk, but the people who stay loyal to their God will stand strong and fight back.

“‘The wise leaders will teach the people what’s right by their own example. But they’ll go through some serious trials for a while: some will be killed, some burned, some forced to leave their homes, some robbed. When things get really bad, they’ll get a little help, but not much. A lot of the people helping will be faking it. This whole testing period will be to refine and purify the ones who stay true, because there’s still more to come.

“‘Meanwhile, the king of the north will just do whatever he wants. He’ll get a huge ego and act like he’s greater than any god. He’ll even brag and boast against the God of all gods. And he’ll get away with it for a bit—until the time of judgment is over, because what’s meant to happen will happen. He won’t respect the gods of his ancestors, not even the one that was super popular with the ladies, Adonis. He’ll look down on every god and goddess and hype himself up to be greater than all of them. He’ll even disrespect the God of the holy ones. In God’s own temple, he’ll set up a shrine to some new god nobody’s ever heard of, showing it off with a ton of silver, gold, and jewels. Fighting for this strange god, he’ll attack the main fortresses. He’ll give promotions to everyone who joins his side, giving them power and paying them off with land.

“‘In the final part of this story, the king of the south will challenge him. But the king of the north will come at him like a tornado, with chariots, horses, and a whole fleet of ships, destroying everything in his way. When he enters the beautiful land, people will just fall before him. Only Edom, Moab, and a few Ammonites will get away. As he goes around conquering country after country, not even Egypt will be safe. He’ll take all of Egypt’s gold, silver, and other treasures. The Libyans and Ethiopians will join his side. But then, he’ll hear some bad news from the north and east that will make him panic. He’ll get super angry and rush off to crush the threat. But right after he sets up his royal camp between the Mediterranean Sea and the Holy Mountain, he’ll meet his end. And there will be literally no one there to help him.’”

Daniel.title: The Wildest Ending Ever (No Cap)
paragraphs: “‘So, that’s when Michael, the super powerful angel-prince who’s got your people’s back, is gonna show up. It’s gonna be a time of major trouble, like, the worst the world has ever seen, no cap. But your people? They’ll be saved. Every single person whose name is in the Book will make it through.
A bunch of people who’ve been dead and buried for ages will wake up. Some will get eternal life, which is goated, but others will face eternal shame, which is a huge L.

“‘The people who lived wisely and did good stuff will shine super brightly, like a clear night sky full of stars. And those who helped others find the right way to live will glow like stars forever and ever.

“‘Okay, so this is some top-secret info, Daniel. For your eyes only. You gotta keep it secret and lock up this book until the very end. In the meantime, people are gonna be running around like crazy, trying to figure out what’s even happening.’

As I, Daniel, was trying to process all this, two other guys appeared. One was on this side of the river, and the other was on the opposite bank. One of them asked a third guy, who was dressed in linen and standing over the river, ‘Yo, how long is this crazy story gonna last?’

The guy in linen over the river lifted both his hands to the sky. I heard him make a super serious promise in the name of the Eternal One. He said it would be for a time, two times, and half a time. And when the one oppressing the holy people is finally taken down, the story will be over.
I heard all that, but I was lowkey confused. So I asked, ‘Sir, can you break that down for me?’

‘Just go on with your life, Daniel,’ he said. ‘The message is confidential and locked up until the end, right before things are about to wrap up. The people will be cleansed and made totally new. But the wicked people will just keep being wicked, completely clueless about what’s going on. The ones who live wisely will get it, though.’
“‘From the moment the daily worship at the Temple is stopped and that disgusting, disrespectful thing is set up, it’ll be 1,290 days.
“‘Big shoutout to those who wait patiently and make it through the 1,335 days.
“‘And you? Just do your thing without stressing. Relax. When it’s all said and done, you’ll be back on your feet to get your reward.’”

Hosea.title: God's Wildest Object Lesson: A Prophet, a Prostitute, and Their Kids
paragraphs: So, here's the scoop from God, delivered to Hosea, son of Beeri. This all went down while Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were running things in Judah, and Jeroboam son of Joash was king in Israel.
The very first thing God ever said to Hosea was, no cap, pretty wild.
He said, “Go find a prostitute and marry her. Start a family with her. And here’s the reason: this entire country has basically become a giant brothel, cheating on me, their God.”
And Hosea just... did it. He went and married Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim. She got pregnant and had a son.
Then God told him:

“Name that kid Jezreel. It won’t be long before I make the whole nation of Israel answer for the massacre that happened at Jezreel. I’m officially calling it quits on the kingdom of Israel. Payday is coming, and I’m going to smash all their weapons to bits in the Valley of Jezreel.”
Gomer got pregnant again, and this time it was a girl. God told Hosea:

“Name her No-Mercy. I am so over Israel. I’ve run out of mercy. There are no more second chances. Judah, though, that’s a different situation. I’ll keep having mercy on them. I’ll save them. And it’ll be me, their God, who does the saving—not their military, not their weapons, not their cavalry or their soldiers.”
After Gomer had weaned No-Mercy, she got pregnant yet again and had another son. God said:
“Name him Nobody. Because you all have become nobodies to me, and I, God, am a nobody to you.

“But hold up, plot twist. Down the road, the population of Israel is going to explode. You won't even be able to count them, like grains of sand on the beach. And in the exact spot where they were called ‘Nobody,’ they’ll be called ‘Children of the Living God.’ Everyone from Judah and Israel will get back together as one crew. They’ll pick a single leader and become an unstoppable force. That’s gonna be a goated day for Jezreel!”

Hosea.title: From Toxic to Forever: God's Comeback Story
paragraphs: “Yo, call your brothers ‘God’s People’ and your sisters ‘Totally Forgiven.’

“Seriously, you need to call your mom out. She’s not my wife anymore, and I’m not her husband. Tell her to stop acting like a prostitute, putting herself on display. If she doesn’t, I’ll strip her completely naked, just like the day she was born. I’ll turn her into a desert, a dry and thirsty land, and let her die of thirst. I won’t show any love to her children, because they’re the children of her cheating. Your mother has been a total cheater; she was shameless. She said, ‘I’m gonna go after my lovers, the ones who give me food and water, clothes and lotions.’ So I’m going to block her path with thornbushes; I’ll build a wall so she can’t find her way. She’ll chase after her lovers but won’t catch them; she’ll look for them but won’t find them. Then she’ll say, ‘I’m going back to my first husband. Things were way better for me back then.’ She never realized it was me who gave her the grain, the new wine, and the oil. It was me who loaded her up with silver and gold, which she then used for that fake god, Baal. So I’m taking it all back—my grain when it’s ripe, my wine when it’s ready. I’ll take back my wool and my linen, which were meant to cover her nakedness. I’m going to expose her, right in front of her lovers. No one will be able to save her from me. I’ll put an end to all her parties, her festivals, her new moon celebrations, and her Sabbath days—all of it. I’ll destroy her vines and her fig trees, the ones she said were her ‘payment’ from her lovers. I’ll turn them into a jungle, and wild animals will eat them up. I’m going to punish her for all the days she burned incense to the Baals. She would put on her rings and jewelry and go chasing after her lovers, but she completely forgot about me,” says the Lord.

“But get this, I’m going to win her back. I’ll lead her out into the wilderness and speak tenderly to her. There, I’ll give her back her vineyards, and I’ll make the Valley of Achor—which means ‘Trouble’—into a gateway of hope. She’ll respond to me there like she did when she was young, like when she first came out of Egypt.

“On that day,” declares the Lord, “you’ll call me ‘my husband’; you will no longer call me ‘my master.’ I’ll remove the names of the Baals from your lips; you won’t even mention their names again. I’ll make a treaty for you with the wild animals, the birds, and the creatures that crawl on the ground. I’ll get rid of all the bows and swords and weapons of war from the land, so you can live in safety. And I will make you my wife forever. I’ll commit to you in righteousness and justice, in love and compassion. Yes, I’ll be faithful to you, and you will truly know the Lord.

“On that day, I will answer,” declares the Lord. “I will answer the sky, and the sky will answer the earth; and the earth will answer the grain, the new wine, and the oil, and they will answer Jezreel. I will plant her for myself in the land. I will show love to the one I had called ‘Not loved.’ I will say to those called ‘Not my people,’ ‘You are my people’; and they will say, ‘You are my God.’”

Hosea.title: God Said Get My Cheating Wife Back?!
paragraphs: Then God was like, “Alright, do it all over again. Go get your wife back, even though she’s with her new guy. Yeah, your cheating wife. Love her the same way I, God, love the people of Israel, even when they’re out there chasing every other god they see.”

So I did it. I paid a good chunk of change to get her back—cost me about as much as a slave. Then I told her straight up, “From now on, you’re living with me. No more hooking up, no more sleeping around. You’re with me, and I’m with you. Period.”

This is a picture of what’s going to happen with the Israelites. They’re going to spend a long time feeling totally lost and alone, without a king or any leader, without any real religion or way to connect with God. It’s gonna be a rough time.

But, plot twist, they’ll come back. The Israelites will eventually start looking for their God and their true king, the one from David's line. They’ll come back humbled, totally in awe of God and all the amazing things He does. They'll be ready for the epic finale of His love story.

Hosea.title: God Calls Out the Fakes
paragraphs: Yo, Israel, listen up! God's got a major bone to pick with everyone. He's like, 'Nobody's loyal. Nobody's got love. Nobody even gets me.' It's just non-stop cursing, lying, murder, stealing, and sleeping around. Total chaos, just one person getting iced after another. And because of all this, the whole country is basically crying. Everything's messed up—the animals, the birds, even the fish are just floating around, totally dead inside.

But don't even try to point fingers. You, the priests, you're the ones getting called out. You're tripping all day, and then the so-called prophets take over and trip all night. Your whole system is messed up. God's people are getting wrecked 'cause they don't know what's real anymore. Since you priests ghosted on true knowledge, God's ghosting you. You ignored what God showed you, so now he's ignoring your kids. The more of you there are, the more sin there is. You traded your honor for cheap thrills. You get fat off of people's screw-ups and can't wait for them to do more messed-up stuff. Now, you can't even tell who's who—the priests are just as bad as everyone else. God's about to make everyone face the music for their trash lifestyle. They'll eat but still be starving, hook up but never feel satisfied. They totally bailed on their God to chase after cheap hookups.

My people are basically wasted on booze. They're out here asking dead trees for advice and expecting a stick to give them answers. They're so drunk on sex they can't even think straight. They've swapped out God for their own desires. They're having religious 'parties' up on mountains, just chilling under trees like it's a festival. Next thing you know, your own daughters are selling their bodies and your sons' wives are cheating. But God's not even coming after the girls. He's coming after the men who are paying for it, the guys who are worshipping at these gross sex-shrines. What a clueless generation, getting ruined by this stuff.

You really messed up your own life, Israel—but don't you dare drag Judah down with you! Don't go to the sex-shrine at Gilgal, and stay away from that sin-city Bethel. And don't go around saying 'God bless' when you don't even mean it, just throwing His name around. Israel is being stubborn AF, like a mule that won't move. How is God supposed to lead them into a good place like a gentle lamb? Ephraim is literally addicted to his idols. Just let him be. Once the party's over, it's all about sex, sex, and more sex. They love their shameless, dirty lifestyle. But a storm is coming to snatch them up, and their whole sex-worshipping thing will leave them with nothing.

Hosea.title: God's Done Playing Games
paragraphs: Alright, listen up, you priests! And pay attention, people of Israel! Royal family, you better be all ears too! You're supposed to be the ones in charge of justice, but what have you actually been doing? You've been taking advantage of people at Mizpah, scamming them on Tabor, and totally victimizing them at Shittim. So yeah, I'm about to bring the hammer down on all of you.

I see right through you, Ephraim. For real, Israel, I know exactly what you're up to. Ephraim, you've been messing around with your gross mix of sex and fake religion for way too long. The whole nation of Israel is just...toxic. You guys couldn't even turn back to God if you wanted to. Your whole lifestyle is a seriously bad habit. Every move you make is messed up. You wouldn't even recognize God if you saw him.

Your arrogance is off the charts, and honestly, it's a public embarrassment. All of you—Israel, Ephraim, and Judah—are just stumbling around in your own guilt. And when you finally decide to get your act together and look for God again, it's gonna be too late. I, God, will be long gone. You've been disloyal to me for way too long, and now your country is full of the consequences. A massive plague is about to wreck your trashed land.

Sound the alarms in Gibeah and Ramah! Signal the invasion of Sin City! Freak Benjamin out! Ephraim is going to be left completely destroyed, like a wasteland. I'm giving it to you straight, no sugar-coating, tribes of Israel.
Israel's leaders are just a bunch of crooks and thieves. They're cheating people out of their own land, and I am so, so angry. My anger is going to hit every single part of them.

Ephraim has been brutal, and now he's about to get brutalized himself—a taste of his own medicine. He was so obsessed with doing things his own useless way. Because of that, I'm going to be like an infection to Ephraim, and like a rot that destroys the house of Judah.

When Ephraim realized he was sick and Judah saw his nasty, infected sores, Ephraim ran off to Assyria for help from their 'great' king. But plot twist: he can't heal you. He can't fix the mess you're in.

I'm about to go full-on grizzly bear on Ephraim, and like a mama bear with cubs on Judah. I'll tear them to pieces, for real. No one can stop me. I'll drag them off, and no one will be able to rescue them. Then, I'll go back to my place and wait until they finally get a clue. When they finally hit rock bottom, maybe then they'll start looking for me.

Hosea.title: God's Tough Love: Time for a Real Comeback
paragraphs: Alright, let's get real and go back to God. He might have let us get hurt, but He's the one who can heal us. He hit us hard, no cap, but He'll patch us up. Give it a couple of days, and we'll start feeling ourselves again. By day three, He'll have us rebooted—brand-new, alive, and ready to face Him. We're so ready to actually get to know God, like, for real. His return is as certain as the sunrise. He shows up like a much-needed rain shower, like that spring rain that makes everything fresh.

But for real, what am I supposed to do with you, Ephraim? And you, Judah, what's your deal? Your promises of love are about as long-lasting as the morning fog—here one second, gone the next. That's why I've been sending prophets to give you a major wake-up call, why my words are meant to cut deep: to make you see my judgment shining like a spotlight. I'm looking for a love that's legit, not just more religious rituals. I want you to actually *know* me, not just show up to more prayer meetings. You broke our deal, just like Adam did! You betrayed me, you ungrateful bunch.

Gilead is basically Crime City now—blood all over the sidewalks, all over the streets. It used to be that robbers would jump people. Now it's whole crews of priests attacking worshippers on their way to Shechem. They have zero respect for anything sacred.
I saw some seriously messed up stuff going down in Israel. Ephraim is out here worshipping at some shady religious spot, and Israel is right there with him, getting dragged through the mud.
And you're just as bad, Judah. You've been out here living wild. Well, guess what? It's harvest time.

Hosea.title: Israel's Self-Destruct Mode is ON
paragraphs: Every time I tried to give Israel a fresh start, like wiping the slate clean to get them going again, Ephraim would just immediately mess it all up with new sins. The betrayal of Samaria was basically on full display. They're so two-faced and full of lies, they'll rob you blind and leave you with nothing. It's like it never even occurs to them that I'm keeping a running list of all their crimes. They're covered head to toe in the evidence of their sin. I see exactly who they are and what they've been up to.

They put on this whole evil circus for the king, and the princes are totally entertained by their acrobatic lies. They're just a bunch of thirsty cheaters, like an oven that stays hot from the moment the dough is kneaded until it rises. On the king's holiday, the princes get wasted on wine, caught up in the craziness of the crowd that's mocking everything. They're like old-school wood stoves, glowing red-hot with lust. Their passion just simmers all night, and then in the morning, it explodes into hungry flames. They're murderous and explosive, burning through their own rulers. Their kings keep falling, one after another, and not a single person even thinks to look my way.

They put on this whole evil circus for the king, and the princes are totally entertained by their acrobatic lies. They're just a bunch of thirsty cheaters, like an oven that stays hot from the moment the dough is kneaded until it rises. On the king's holiday, the princes get wasted on wine, caught up in the craziness of the crowd that's mocking everything. They're like old-school wood stoves, glowing red-hot with lust. Their passion just simmers all night, and then in the morning, it explodes into hungry flames. They're murderous and explosive, burning through their own rulers. Their kings keep falling, one after another, and not a single person even thinks to look my way.

Ephraim is mixing in with people who don't know God, just wasting his potential. Ephraim is like a pancake that's only cooked on one side—totally half-baked. Strangers are draining his strength, and he doesn't even have a clue. He's getting old and weak, and he doesn't notice that either. His arrogance is a huge, public embarrassment. Israel just stumbles around, completely oblivious to God, ignoring all the warning signs and paying God no attention.

Ephraim is mixing in with people who don't know God, just wasting his potential. Ephraim is like a pancake that's only cooked on one side—totally half-baked. Strangers are draining his strength, and he doesn't even have a clue. He's getting old and weak, and he doesn't notice that either. His arrogance is a huge, public embarrassment. Israel just stumbles around, completely oblivious to God, ignoring all the warning signs and paying God no attention.

Ephraim is so clueless, a total airhead. First, he's chirping for Egypt to help, then he's fluttering over to Assyria. But I'm gonna throw my net over them and clip their wings. I'll teach them to listen to me! They're doomed! They've run away from me, and now they're in for some serious trouble. They've defied me, and I'm supposed to rescue them while they're feeding me a bunch of lies? Instead of genuinely praying to me, they're just partying in bed with prostitutes and doing these wild, self-harming rituals for their fake gods, all while turning their backs on me. I'm the one who gave them sharp minds and strong bodies, and how do they repay me? By plotting evil against me. They're always turning, but never toward me—they're like a broken weather vane, spinning all over the place. Their leaders will get taken down, murdered—which is exactly what they deserve for their disrespectful trash-talk. And the final verdict? They'll be a total laughingstock on the world stage.

Hosea.title: Israel's Epic Fail: Fake Gods & Big Problems
paragraphs: “Yo, blow the trumpet! Sound the alarm! Vultures are literally circling over God’s people because they completely broke my covenant and ignored my rules. And what’s their response? They cry out, ‘My God! We know you!’ but their actions are screaming the opposite. Israel wants nothing to do with what’s good, and now the enemy is hot on their trail.

They’re crowning kings without even asking me. They set up princes but totally left me out of the loop. Instead, they’re making idols from their silver and gold, and those very idols are gonna be their downfall. Just throw that gold calf-god on the trash heap, Samaria! I’m seething with anger against that piece of junk! How long until they finally get it together? And they’re supposed to be Israelites! A sculptor made that thing—it’s not God. That Samaritan calf is going to be smashed into a million pieces. Look at them! They’re planting wind-seeds, and they’re about to harvest a whole tornado. Their wheat has no head, so it makes no flour. And even if it did, strangers would just come and wolf it down. Israel is swallowed up and spit right back out. Among the other nations, they’re seen as a piece of junk. They ran off to Assyria—like, seriously? Even wild donkeys stick with their own kind, but Ephraim is out there paying for lovers. Now, because of their wild life among the pagans, I’m going to gather them all and confront them. They’re about to reap the consequences and feel what it’s like to be crushed by a powerful king.

Ephraim has built a ton of altars, and then he turns around and uses them for sinning. Can you even believe that? Altars for sinning! I write out my revelation for them in super clear detail, and they act like they can’t even read it. They offer sacrifices to me and then just feast on the meat themselves. God is not pleased. I’m so done—I’ll keep remembering their guilt. I’m going to punish their sins and send them straight back to Egypt. Israel has forgotten his Maker and gotten busy building palaces. Judah has gone all-in on building fortress cities. Well, I’m sending fire on their cities to burn down every single one of their fortifications.”

Hosea.title: Party's Over, Israel. Payday's Here.
paragraphs: Yo Israel, stop wasting your life on wild parties with people who don't follow God. You're constantly ditching your God, selling yourselves out at every sketchy sex-and-religion street festival like a cheap knockoff.

All that party food isn't going to satisfy you. You'll just end up feeling more empty. Seriously, you won't last in God's country at this rate. Some of you will end up broke in Egypt, others will get a harsh reality check in Assyria. As refugees, you won't get to worship God much—you'll be on basic rations, and your souls will get tainted by the spiritually toxic air. You'll be starving for a real connection with God, exiled from His land. Think you'll miss the holy days then? Bet you'll be homesick for the big festivals.

But watch out. When you think you've escaped one disaster, you'll land right in another one in Egypt. And Egypt will be the one throwing your funeral! What good will all your precious silver be then, when you're just trying to survive in a field full of weeds?

Time's up. Judgment is knocking. It's payday. Israel was all talk, saying, "The prophet's a psycho! This 'man of the Spirit' is insane!" But think again. Your massive guilt means you're in for some massive trouble. The prophet is watching out for Ephraim, doing God's work, but everyone's trying to trip him up. He's being hated in God's own house, of all places. People are just getting worse, almost as bad as that messed-up crime back in Gibeah. And God is keeping receipts. He's going to make them pay for every single sin.

"A long time ago, when I first found Israel, it was like discovering grapes in the middle of a desert. Finding your ancestors was like finding the first figs of the season. But then they got to Baal-peor, that pagan spot, and they dove into sin like it was nothing, getting all buddy-buddy with their new idols. Ephraim's crew is so flaky, scattered like a bunch of birds, their potential just wasted in chaos. All noise, no substance, totally barren. Nothing to show for it—no new life, no babies.

And even if they managed to have kids, I'd have to say they're unfit parents and take them away. Seriously, it'll be a dark day for them when I just turn my back and walk away. I see Ephraim letting his kids run wild. He might as well be leading them straight to their own destruction!"
God, give them what they deserve! But what? Give them wombs that can't have kids and dried-up breasts.

"All their evil was exposed at that pagan shrine in Gilgal. Man, I hated them for that. Because of all their messed-up actions, I'm kicking them out of my land. I'm done wasting my love on them. Their leaders are just a bunch of rebellious teens. Ephraim is toast—roots dried up, no more fruit. And even if, by some miracle, they had kids, those precious babies wouldn't survive. I'd make sure of it!"
My God is so done with them. They just wouldn't listen. Now they're doomed to be wanderers, drifting aimlessly among nations that don't know God.

Hosea.title: Israel's Epic Fail: Fake Worship & Broken Promises
paragraphs: Israel was like a super productive vine, always loaded with grapes. But the more successful they got, the more they messed around with fake gods. The richer they became, the more cash they blew on idols they made up themselves. Their friendly smiles are totally fake. They're 100% guilty. God's about to smash their little worship spots and grind their statues into dust.

Then they'll be like, “A king? Who needs one? We don't even care about God, so why would a king matter? What could he even do for us?” They talk a big game, tell a bunch of lies, and make empty promises. But all their talk is just trash blowing in the wind.

The folks in Samaria are heading over to 'Crime City' to worship a golden calf idol. They're making a huge scene, dancing and shouting, totally fooled by their show-off priests. They act all important around this calf statue, but they have no idea it's all a scam and a total embarrassment. They're even planning to ship it to Assyria as a gift for the big king. That's how Ephraim is making a clown of himself, and Israel is getting shamed by its dumb idols.

Samaria is done for. Its king is like a dead branch floating down the river. And all of Israel's favorite places to sin will be destroyed. Weeds and thorns will be the only things decorating their busted altars. Then they'll be screaming at the mountains, “Bury us!” and begging the hills, “Fall on us!”

You guys have been sinning since day one at Gibeah—that crazy, messed-up, ancient sin—and you just never stopped. So, a war is coming to Gibeah to put an end to all this sinning. I'm going to show up and teach them a lesson. Nations will team up against them and make them learn the hard way what happens when you keep messing up.

Ephraim was like a trained calf that loved the easy work of threshing. I saw how strong and sleek she was and wanted to put a harness on her, get her working in the fields—with Judah plowing and Jacob breaking up the ground. I told you: 'Plant righteousness, and you'll harvest love. It's time to get the ground ready, time to seek God until he shows up with a harvest of justice.' But instead, you plowed wickedness, harvested evil, and ate a salad of lies. You thought you could handle everything on your own because you had so many weapons and soldiers. But a war is about to explode on your people. All your forts will be destroyed, just as brutally as when King Shalman destroyed the town of Beth-arbel, smashing mothers and their kids on the rocks. That's what's coming for you, you so-called people of God, because your evil is completely off the charts. One morning, you're gonna wake up and find that Israel, its king, and its kingdom are just... gone. Nothing left.

Hosea.title: God's Uncancelable Love
paragraphs: “When Israel was just a kid, I loved him so much. I called him out of Egypt, like, ‘That’s my son!’ But the more other people called his name, the more he ran away from me. He started worshipping all the popular fake gods and messing around with idols.

Still, I was the one who stuck by him. I taught Ephraim how to walk, I rescued him from getting stuck. But he never even gave me a shout-out, never admitted I was the one giving him a ride, lifting him up like a baby to my cheek, and bending down to feed him. Now he wants to go back to Egypt or run off to Assyria—literally anywhere but back to me! That’s why his cities are a total mess, the murder rate is insane, and every plan they make just falls apart. My people are just hell-bent on leaving me. They’re praying to this Baal guy for help, but he’s not lifting a finger for them.

But for real, how can I just give up on you, Ephraim? How can I let you go, Israel? How could I ever let you get wrecked like Admah or destroyed like Zeboim? I can’t even stand the thought of it. My stomach is churning just thinking about it. So, I’m not gonna act on my anger. I’m not gonna destroy Ephraim. You know why? Because I’m God, not some human. I’m the Holy One, and I’m right here with you.

“In the end, the people will follow God. I’ll roar like a lion—a massive roar! And my kids will come running back from the west, all scared and shaky. They’ll fly back from Egypt like frightened birds, and from Assyria like scared doves. And I’ll bring them all right back to their homes.” That’s God’s Word!
“Ephraim is all about lies, 24/7. You can’t trust a single thing Israel says. And Judah? No better. They’re addicted to cheap, fake gods.”

Hosea.title: Don't Get Scammed by Fake Gods
paragraphs: Ephraim is all about chasing fantasies, like they're trying to catch ghosts or something. They're constantly telling lies, the kind that really mess with your soul. Both Ephraim and Judah tried to make deals with Assyria and get on Egypt's good side.

God's basically taking Israel to court. Jacob's descendants are getting called out and punished for their actions. Back in the womb, Jacob, that little heel, totally got one over on his brother. And when he grew up, he tried to pull the same thing on God. But you can't outplay God. God put him in his place. Jacob ended up on his knees, crying and praying. God met him at Bethel, and that's where they had a real talk. God is the God of Angel Armies, the God who reveals Himself, the God we can know.
So what are you even waiting for? Go back to your God! Be all about love and justice. Wait for your God, and don't ever give up on him!

The business guys are running a total scam. They love ripping people off! Ephraim was bragging, “Yo, I'm rich! I made it! And I'm so good at covering my tracks, you can't find a single trace of scamming or sin!”

“But hold up,” says God, “I'm your God, the one who was with you back in Egypt! I'm gonna make you live in tents again, just like the old days when you used to worship in the desert. I speak through the prophets to show you what's really going on. I use them to tell stories that reveal the truth. I'm showing how Gilead is a hotbed of religious drama and Gilgal is full of empty-headed religion. Their so-called worship spots are just like stinking piles of trash in their own backyards.”

Are you seriously going to be like your ancestor Jacob? He ran away to Aram all guilty, then basically sold his soul to get rich, making it big through lies and scams. Your true identity comes from the prophets God sent, the ones who led you out of Egypt and were like faithful pastors to you. But Ephraim has just kept on disrespecting God, no excuses. Now he's gotta pay the price for his destructive lifestyle. His Master is going to give him a taste of his own medicine.

Hosea.title: God's Done Playing Games
paragraphs: Back in the day, God basically told Ephraim (part of Israel) that they were on thin ice. They got caught up in some seriously messed-up worship of a fake god, Baal, and it spiritually wrecked them. And guess what? They're doing it again, creating their own designer gods, whatever they feel like. They've got people who will literally make you any god you want. It's wild. They're sacrificing babies to these dead statues and kissing golden calves. Can you believe it? So now, these people are just empty, like ghosts, totally lost.

God's like, "Yo, I'm still your God, the one who got you out of Egypt. I'm the only real God you've ever known, the only one who actually saves you. I took care of you when you were struggling in the desert with nothing. I gave you everything you needed, and you got spoiled. You got arrogant and thought you didn't need me. You straight-up forgot me.

So now I'm coming for you like a lion, like a leopard hiding in the grass. I'm going to be like a mama bear whose cubs were stolen—I'm not holding back. I'm gonna destroy you, Israel, and who's gonna stop me? Where's that king you thought would save you? Where are all those leaders you begged for? You were all like, 'Give us a king!' Well, I gave you one, even though I wasn't happy about it, and now I'm done with him. I've been keeping receipts of all your cheating—all of Ephraim's sin is on record.

When it was time for Ephraim to be 'born' into something new, they were too dumb to even come out. The way to life was wide open, and they just stood there. Should I save them? Should I rescue them from death? Nah. Who's scared of you, Death? Your threats are nothing. I'm done with regret and sorrow. Even though Ephraim was the wild child of the family, a storm is coming.

A tornado from God is heading straight for them from the desert. It's going to completely wreck the country, leaving nothing but ruins. The cities will be trashed, and all their precious stuff will be gone. Now Samaria has to pay up for rebelling against their God. Their people will be killed, their babies smashed against rocks, and their pregnant women attacked."

Hosea.title: The Ultimate Comeback Story
paragraphs: Yo, Israel, come on back to your God! Seriously, you've messed up, but it's not over. Get your apology ready and come back to God. Just pray something like, 'God, please forgive all our screw-ups. We're coming clean. Our promises to change are the real deal. Assyria's not gonna save us, and all those fancy horses? They're not getting us anywhere. We're done calling our own creations 'god.' You're literally our only hope. It's true that you're the one who shows mercy to the helpless, right?'

God's like, 'I'm going to fix their rebellious streak. I'm gonna love them like crazy. I'm not mad anymore. It's a clean slate for Israel. They're gonna blossom like a flower in spring and put down roots as strong as an oak tree. They'll be amazing, like a giant sequoia, and smell as good as a forest of cedars. The people living near them will be blessed because of them, and they'll thrive like a field of golden wheat. Everyone will be talking about them, saying they're the OG children of God. Ephraim is so over those fake gods. From now on, I'm the one who's got his back. I'm like a tree that's always loaded with fruit. Everything you could ever need, you can find in me.'

If you want to live a good life, you gotta understand this. If you know what's good for you, you'll learn this stuff by heart. God's ways are the right ways to go. People who live right can walk them no problem, but people who do wrong are always tripping over themselves.

Joel.title: The Locust Invasion is Lowkey Terrifying
paragraphs: Alright, this is a message from God to Joel, son of Pethuel.

Yo, all you leaders and everyone, listen up! This is major. Has anything this wild ever happened in your lifetime? Or your parents' lifetime? Make sure you pass this story down to your kids, and they tell their kids, and so on. This has to be remembered.
Whatever one type of locust didn't eat, another type did. It was a whole swarm, one after another, just wiping everything out.
Whatever one type of locust didn't eat, another type did. It was a whole swarm, one after another, just wiping everything out.

Wake up, all you who are drunk! Time to face reality and cry. Your party's over, no more booze for you. An unstoppable army is invading our country, more than you can count. They're fierce, like lions or tigers. They've wrecked our vineyards and orchards, basically turning the whole country into a wasteland. It's a total disaster zone.

Wake up, all you who are drunk! Time to face reality and cry. Your party's over, no more booze for you. An unstoppable army is invading our country, more than you can count. They're fierce, like lions or tigers. They've wrecked our vineyards and orchards, basically turning the whole country into a wasteland. It's a total disaster zone.

Cry like a girl who just lost her fiancé. With no grain or grapes, worship at God's place has completely stopped. The priests are freaking out. God's crew doesn't know what to do. The fields are dead, the ground itself is sad. The wheat fields are empty, the vineyards are dried up, and there's no olive oil left.

Cry like a girl who just lost her fiancé. With no grain or grapes, worship at God's place has completely stopped. The priests are freaking out. God's crew doesn't know what to do. The fields are dead, the ground itself is sad. The wheat fields are empty, the vineyards are dried up, and there's no olive oil left.

Farmers, it's over. Grape growers, just cry. Mourn for the wheat and barley because all the crops are gone. The vineyards are dried up, the fig trees are dead, and so are the pomegranates, date palms, and apple trees—everything is dead. And all the joy is gone from people's hearts.

Farmers, it's over. Grape growers, just cry. Mourn for the wheat and barley because all the crops are gone. The vineyards are dried up, the fig trees are dead, and so are the pomegranates, date palms, and apple trees—everything is dead. And all the joy is gone from people's hearts.

And you priests, get your robes on and start crying too. You're supposed to lead people in worship, so lead them in mourning. Spend the night in rough clothes, you servants of my God. Nothing is happening at the church, no offerings, no prayers—nothing. Call for a fast, get a special meeting together, and bring all the leaders and everyone in the country to God's house to seriously pray.

What a day! It's doomsday! God's judgment is here. The Almighty has arrived, and this is serious. We're all out of food, and there's no more joy or singing at God's place. The seeds are dead in the ground, the barns are empty, and the grain silos are abandoned. The crops have failed! The farm animals are groaning, the cattle are just wandering around with nothing to eat. Even the sheep can't find anything.

What a day! It's doomsday! God's judgment is here. The Almighty has arrived, and this is serious. We're all out of food, and there's no more joy or singing at God's place. The seeds are dead in the ground, the barns are empty, and the grain silos are abandoned. The crops have failed! The farm animals are groaning, the cattle are just wandering around with nothing to eat. Even the sheep can't find anything.

God! I'm praying, I'm crying out to you! The fields are on fire, the whole country is a dust bowl, and fires are raging everywhere. The wild animals are dying of thirst and looking to you for water. The springs and streams are all dried up. The whole country is burning.
