Joel.title: The Locust Army vs. God's Comeback
paragraphs: Yo, sound the alarm in Zion! Blast the trumpets on God's holy mountain! Let everyone know what's up, 'cause God's Judgment Day is coming, and it's coming in hot. It's gonna be a dark, gloomy, straight-up doomsday. Picture this: a massive army spreading over the mountains like the morning light. There's never been anything like it, and there never will be again. It's like a wildfire that burns everything in front of it, and leaves nothing but scorched earth behind. Before this army shows up, the place is like a paradise, a real Garden of Eden. After it passes through? Total Death Valley. Nothing gets away.

This locust army looks like a huge cavalry of galloping horses. The sound is insane—like thunder booming over the mountains, or a wildfire roaring through dry grass. It's like an unstoppable army screaming for a fight, totally battle-ready. When people see them, they're just terrified, their faces completely pale with fear.

These invaders just charge. They scale walls. Nothing stops them. Every soldier is so disciplined, staying in their own lane and doing their job perfectly. They're fearless, unstoppable, and they just keep coming. They storm the city, get past all the defenses, and raid the houses, breaking in through doors and windows. It's like an earthquake and a tornado all at once. The sun and moon go dark, and the stars disappear. Then God himself, in a voice like thunder, commands his forces. Just look at the size of that army! And look how strong his followers are! God's Judgment Day is huge and terrifying. Who could possibly survive it?
But listen up, God's dropping a personal message, and it's not too late. He's saying, “Come back to me, and be real about it. Come back fasting, crying, and being genuinely sorry for messing up.”

Change your heart, not just your outfit. Come back to your God. And here's the deal: God is super kind and merciful. He's patient, puts up with a lot, and his love is extravagant. He's always ready to call off a disaster. Who knows? Maybe he'll change his mind right now and show some pity. Maybe after all this, there will be some massive blessings left over for your God!

So sound the alarm in Zion! Call for a day of repentance, a holy fast. Get everyone together for a big meeting. The whole community needs to be there. Make sure the elders come, but also the kids, even the babies. And yeah, even the newlyweds—tell them to pause the honeymoon and get over here. Right there between the Temple entrance and the altar, the priests, God's servants, need to be crying, begging for forgiveness. They should pray, “God, have mercy on your people! Don't let us become a joke. Don't let other nations take over and mock us, asking, ‘So where is your God now?’”

And just like that, God jumped into action to take back his land. He felt sorry for his people. God answered them, “Look, I'm sending you a gift: grain, wine, and olive oil. The famine is over—eat until you're full! I won't let you be disrespected by other nations anymore. I'll stop that enemy from the north and throw them into a wasteland. Half will end up in the Dead Sea, the other half in the Mediterranean. They'll rot there, and the stench will be legendary. The bigger the enemy, the bigger the smell!”

Don't be afraid, Earth! Be happy and celebrate! God has done amazing things. Don't worry, wild animals! The fields are green again. The trees are full of fruit—figs and vines are having a bumper crop! People of Zion, celebrate! Be happy in your God. He's giving you a guide to teach you how to live right. His teaching is like rain from heaven, refreshing your soul, just like in the old days. And you'll have plenty of food—storage full of grain, and barrels overflowing with wine and oil.

“I'll pay you back for the years the locusts ate—that massive locust invasion I sent. The swarming locusts, the hopping locusts, the stripping locusts, and the cutting locusts. You'll have plenty of good food to eat, and you'll be praising your God, the one who has done such amazing things for you. My people will never be ashamed again. You'll know for sure that I am right there with Israel, that I am your God, the one and only true God. My people will never be ashamed again.

“And that's just the start. After that, I will pour out my Spirit on everyone. Your sons and daughters will prophesy. Your old men will have prophetic dreams, and your young men will see visions. I'll even pour out my Spirit on the servants, both men and women. I'll show amazing things in the sky and on the earth: blood, fire, and clouds of smoke. The sun will turn dark, and the moon will turn blood-red before the great and awesome Day of the Lord arrives. And anyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. On Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, there will be a great rescue—just as God promised. The survivors will be the ones God calls.”

Joel.title: God's Ultimate Comeback is No Joke
paragraphs: Alright, so check it. When I get Judah and Jerusalem back on their feet, I'm gonna round up all the nations that don't mess with me. I'm taking them straight to a place called Judgment Valley. It's going down. I'm putting them on trial for what they did to my people, Israel. They scattered them everywhere and just took my land. They literally gambled for my people and traded them like objects. A boy for a prostitute, a girl for a bottle of wine just to get their drink on. Wild.

And you guys—Tyre, Sidon, Philistia—what's your deal? You trying to get revenge on me or something? If you are, just stop. It's gonna come right back at you, no cap. You stole my silver and gold, took all my valuable stuff for your own temples. You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, sending them super far away. But I'm about to flip the script. I'm freeing them. And what you did? It's happening to you. I'm gonna have your kids sold as slaves to your neighbors, and they'll sell them to the Sabeans way out there. That's God's final word.

Tell all the nations that don't follow God: Get ready for a fight! Soldiers, get in formation! Grab your weapons! Let's go! Turn your farming tools into swords and spears. Even the weakest person should be hyping themselves up, saying, 'I'm a beast!' Hurry up, you pagans! Wherever you are, get over here! Get ready to be totally wrecked by God!
Let all those nations head to Judgment Valley. I'll be there, sitting on the judge's bench, and I'll judge every single one of them.
Let all those nations head to Judgment Valley. I'll be there, sitting on the judge's bench, and I'll judge every single one of them.
Get the sickles out—it's harvest time. Stomp those grapes—the winepress is overflowing. The vats are full, spilling over with all their evil.
Get the sickles out—it's harvest time. Stomp those grapes—the winepress is overflowing. The vats are full, spilling over with all their evil.
It's total chaos, a massive crowd in Decision Valley! God's Judgment Day is officially here in Decision Valley.
It's total chaos, a massive crowd in Decision Valley! God's Judgment Day is officially here in Decision Valley.

The sky's going black, the sun and moon are gone, and the stars are out. God's voice booms from Zion, a shout from Jerusalem. The whole earth and sky are shaking. But for the people of Israel, God is their safe spot, a super-secure fortress. Then you'll know for sure that I'm your God, living in Zion, my holy mountain. Jerusalem will be a holy city, with a big 'No Trespassing' sign for enemies.

The sky's going black, the sun and moon are gone, and the stars are out. God's voice booms from Zion, a shout from Jerusalem. The whole earth and sky are shaking. But for the people of Israel, God is their safe spot, a super-secure fortress. Then you'll know for sure that I'm your God, living in Zion, my holy mountain. Jerusalem will be a holy city, with a big 'No Trespassing' sign for enemies.

What a time that'll be! Wine will be flowing down the mountains, milk will be like a river from the hills, and water will be everywhere in Judah. A fountain will even flow from God's Temple, watering everything. But Egypt will become a wasteland, and Edom will be a barren desert, all because of the messed-up things they did to the people of Judah, killing innocent people. But Judah will be full of people, and Jerusalem will be lived in forever. Any sins I haven't forgiven yet, I will. God is moving into Zion for good.

Amos.title: God's Official Takedown List
paragraphs: This is the message that Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, got about Israel. It all went down while Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam II was king of Israel, two years before that massive earthquake.
Here's the deal:
God roars from Zion, his voice booms from Jerusalem! The shepherds' pastures dry up, and even the top of Mount Carmel withers.
God's Message:

"Yo, Damascus has messed up three times, nah, four times. I'm done with them. They crushed Gilead with iron weapons, just brutal. So, I'm setting Hazael's palace on fire and torching Ben-hadad's forts. I'm gonna smash the gates of Damascus, kick out the king from Sin Valley and the boss from Paradise Palace. The people of Aram? They're getting exiled back to Kir." That's God's decree.
God's Message:

"Gaza has sinned three, no, four times. I'm not letting it slide. They rounded up whole towns and sold them as slaves to Edom. For that, I'm burning down Gaza's walls and all its forts. I'll get rid of the king in Ashdod and the ruler in Ashkelon. I'll even go after Ekron, and the rest of the Philistines will be toast." That's what God says.
God's Message:
"Tyre has messed up three, no, four times. I'm over it. They sold entire towns to Edom, breaking a treaty they had with their own relatives. So, I'm burning down Tyre's walls and all its forts."
God's Message:

"Edom has sinned three, no, four times, and I'm not having it. They hunted down their own brother, trying to kill him. No mercy, no heart. Their anger is just non-stop, 24/7. Their cruelty never takes a break. For that, I'm burning down their capital, Teman, and the forts of Bozrah."
God's Message:

"Ammon has sinned three, no, four times. I'm done. They literally ripped open pregnant women in Gilead just to get more land. That's messed up. So, I'm setting their capital, Rabbah, on fire, burning down its forts. There will be battle cries and war whoops, and a tornado to top it all off. Their king and his officials are getting dragged into exile." That's God's decree.

Amos.title: God's Done Playing Games
paragraphs: God's Message:

"Yo, because of Moab's three big sins—actually, let's make it four—I'm not dealing with them anymore. They went way too far and disrespected the king of Edom's body, burning it to ash. For that, I'm sending a fire to destroy Moab and its strongest forts. Moab's gonna go down with a lot of shouting and the sound of war trumpets. I'm taking out their king and all his officials along with him." That's a decree from God.
God's Message:

"Because of Judah's three huge sins—nah, four—I'm done with them. They totally ignored God's guidance and didn't follow my rules. Instead, they fell for the same old lies that messed up their ancestors. So for that, I'm sending fire to burn down Judah and all of Jerusalem's defenses."
God's Message:

"Because of Israel's three major sins—let's be real, it's four—I'm not putting up with them any longer. They're treating people like objects, buying and selling good people just to make some cash. They'd sell a poor person for a pair of sneakers. They'd even sell out their own grandma! They crush the poor and push the unlucky aside. And it gets worse—fathers and sons are sleeping with the same temple worker, which is a huge slap in the face to my Holy Name. They have piles of stuff they stole from the poor at their god's shrine, and they're sitting around drinking wine they scammed from their victims.

"But look, I was always on your side. I wiped out the Amorites who came against you—dudes who were as tall as giant trees and as tough as oaks. I destroyed them completely, from top to bottom. And yeah, I'm the one who got you out of Egypt, led you through the desert for forty years, and then just handed you the Amorites' land on a silver platter. I even picked some of your own young men to be prophets and set apart your best young people to be holy. Isn't that true, Israel?" God's asking.

"But what did you do? You made the trainees quit and told the prophets, 'Don't prophesy!' You guys are just too much for me. I'm so weighed down, I'm about to break. I feel like a wagon that's overloaded with way too much stuff, groaning and creaking.

"So when I finally make my move, what are you gonna do? There's nowhere to run, no matter how fast you are. Your strength won't matter. Your best fighters won't survive. Your skilled archers won't make it. The fastest runners won't escape. Even the chariot drivers are done for. The bravest warrior you have will end up running for his life, totally exposed and with nothing." That's God's final word.

Amos.title: God's Calling You Out, Israel!
paragraphs: Yo, Israel, listen up! God's calling you out. And yeah, I'm talking to all of you, the whole fam He rescued from Egypt. Listen!
'Out of every family on the planet, I chose you. So, because you're special, I'm holding you accountable for all your mess-ups.'

Like, for real, do two people just walk together if they're not even heading the same way? Does a lion roar in the woods if it doesn't have any food? Does a young lion get hyped if it hasn't caught dinner? Does a bird just drop from the sky for no reason? Does a trap snap shut if nothing sets it off? When the city alarm blares, don't people freak out? And when a disaster hits the city, you think God isn't behind it? Lowkey, God, the Boss, doesn't do anything without giving his prophets the full scoop first.
The lion roared—who's not scared? God spoke—what prophet can just stay silent?

Shout it out to the big shots in Assyria and Egypt. Tell them, 'Get over to the mountains of Samaria and see for yourselves what a hot mess of violence and drama it is! They literally can't do a single thing right.' God said it. 'They're just collecting violence and bad vibes. Therefore'—this is God's Word—'an enemy is gonna roll up on your country. They'll take all your power and raid your forts.'
Here's God's message:

'You know how a shepherd tries to save a lamb from a lion and only gets back a couple of legs or a piece of an ear? That's how little of the Israelites in Samaria will be saved—maybe a couple of old chairs, a broken table leg at best.'

'Listen up and testify against Jacob's family'—this is the word of God, the God of the Angel Armies! 'Peep this! The day I make Israel pay for its sins, for the fake altars at Bethel, those horned altars will be de-horned and scattered everywhere. I'm gonna wreck the winter palace and smash the summer palace—all your fancy houses. All those bougie homes will be demolished.' That's God's decree.

Amos.title: God's Dropping Truth Bombs, But Is Anyone Listening?
paragraphs: Listen up, you rich ladies living it up in Samaria. You're bullying the poor and crushing the needy. Then you turn around and tell your husbands, 'Hey, get me a drink!'

Well, God is making a promise, and He's dead serious. He swears by His own holiness that your time is up. Judgment day is coming. They're gonna haul you away with hooks, and the last of you will be dragged out with fishhooks. You'll be forced out through the broken walls, one by one, and thrown into some wasteland. This is a decree from God Himself.

God is saying, 'Go on then, go to Bethel and sin. Head over to Gilgal and sin some more! Bring your sacrifices in the morning and your tithes every three days. Go ahead and offer your thank offerings with leavened bread, and brag about your freewill offerings. You guys just love showing off how religious you are, don't you?' This is God's decree.

'You know I'm the one who left you with nothing to eat, right? I'm the reason you had empty pantries and were standing in bread lines. But even then, you didn't get hungry for me. You just kept ignoring me.' This is God's decree.

'And yeah, I'm also the one who stopped the rain three months before the harvest. I'd make it rain on one town but not another. One field would get rain, and the one next to it would dry up. People were staggering from town to town, desperate for water, but never found enough. And still, you never got thirsty for me. You just ignored me.' This is God's decree.
'I struck your crops with blight and mildew. Locusts ate up your fig and olive trees. But you still ignored me.' This is God's decree.

'I sent plagues on you, just like the ones in Egypt. I killed your best young men and captured your horses. The stench from your camps was so bad you had to hold your noses. But you didn't even notice me. You just kept ignoring me.' This is God's decree.

'I wrecked you with earthquakes and fire, leaving you like Sodom and Gomorrah. You were like a stick snatched from the fire. But you never even looked my way. You just kept ignoring me.' This is God's decree.
'So, Israel, because of all this, this is what I'm going to do to you. And because I'm going to do this, get ready to meet your God!'

Because look who's coming! The one who forms mountains and creates the wind, the one who tells people His thoughts. He turns dawn into darkness and walks on the high places of the earth. His name is the LORD God Almighty.

Amos.title: God's Done with Your Fake Religion
paragraphs: Listen up, Israel fam, this is a super important message, a serious warning I'm putting out there:
'Virgin Israel? She's totally wiped out. No getting back up. She's just left there, and nobody's helping her.'
This is the real deal, from God himself:
'The city that sends out a thousand soldiers will only have a hundred come back. The one that sends out a hundred will only have ten return. That's the deal, fam.'
God's message to the house of Israel is this:

'Look for me, and you'll actually live. Stop messing around with those fake worship spots at Bethel, don't waste your time at Gilgal, and don't even think about going to Beer-sheba. Gilgal's gonna be gone in a flash, and Bethel is all talk, no action.'

So for real, seek God and live! You don't want your life to be for nothing, just a pile of ashes from a burned-down house. Because God's gonna send that fire, and the firefighters will be way too late.

Woe to you guys who make justice a joke and treat righteousness like dirt. Do you even get it? You're in a universe created by God, with all these constellations. He's the one who wakes up the world every morning and puts it to sleep at night. He takes water from the ocean and gives the land a drink. God, the one and only, does all this. And he can wreck it just as easily as he made it. He can turn this amazing world into a total wasteland.

People hate hearing this stuff. The raw truth is never popular. But here it is, straight up: Because you walk all over the poor and literally take food from their mouths, you'll never get to live in those fancy houses you built. You'll never drink wine from the expensive vineyards you planted. I know exactly how much you've messed up, how huge your sins are. It's disgusting! You bully good people, take bribes, and kick the poor when they're already down.
Justice is a lost cause. Evil is everywhere. Good people just give up. Protesting and calling it out is pointless, a total waste of breath.
Seek good, not evil—and you'll live! You talk a big game about God, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, being your BFF. Well, start acting like it, and maybe it'll actually happen.
Hate what's evil and love what's good, and then actually do something about it in public. Maybe then God, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, will see what's left of you and show some grace.
Now, here's another message from my Master, God, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies:

'Go out in the streets and wail! Fill the malls and shops with cries of doom! Weep loudly, ‘Not me! Not us, Not now!’ Empty offices, stores, factories, workplaces. Get everyone in on the big cry-out. I want to hear it loud and clear when I show up.' God's decree.

Woe to all of you who are excited for God's Judgment Day! Why would you want to see God come? When God shows up, it's gonna be bad news before it's good news, the worst of times, not the best. It's like this: a guy runs from a lion and ends up getting attacked by a bear. A woman gets home after a long day and gets assaulted by her neighbor. When God comes, it's reality check time, not some fantasy—a black cloud with zero silver lining.

'I can't stand your religious get-togethers. I'm so over your conferences and conventions. I want nothing to do with your religious projects, your fake slogans and goals. I'm sick of your fundraising and your PR stunts. I've had it with your loud, look-at-me music. When was the last time you actually sang to me? You know what I want? I want justice—like a whole ocean of it. I want fairness—like a river of it. That's what I want. That's all I want.'

'Yo, Israel fam, didn't you worship me right for forty years in the desert, bringing the sacrifices I asked for? So how did you end up stooping to carrying around these lame statues of your so-called rulers, hauling around cheap images of your star-gods? Since you love them so much, you can take them with you when I kick you out into exile beyond Damascus.' That's the message from God, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies.

Amos.title: The Party's Over, Israel
paragraphs: Big yikes for you guys who think you're living the high life in Zion, thinking Mount Samaria is all that. You really think you're the top dogs, voted #1 best place to live. Well, snap out of it and look around. Get off your high horse. Go check out Calneh. Then visit Great Hamath. And take a look at Gath of the Philistines. Feeling a little less special now, huh? Compared to them, you're not all that.

Big yikes for you who are just sprinting toward disaster! A total catastrophe is literally right around the corner! Yikes for those living in luxury, expecting everyone to wait on them hand and foot. Yikes for those who only care about today and couldn't care less what happens to other people. Yikes for the party boys and party girls who think life is just one big rager thrown for them. Yikes for those hooked on feeling good—a life with no pain! And those obsessed with looking perfect—a life with no wrinkles! They seriously don't give a rip about their country falling apart.
But for real, here’s what’s actually coming: you're all getting forced into exile. You'll be dragged out of the country, whining the whole way, just a bunch of useless good-for-nothings.
God, the Master, has sworn it, and He's not backing down. The God-of-the-Angel-Armies says:
“I absolutely hate Jacob's arrogance. I have zero respect for their fancy forts. I'm about to hand over the whole city and everyone in it.”

Imagine ten guys in a house, all dead. A relative comes to get the bodies for a proper burial, and he finds one survivor hiding in a closet. He asks, “Anyone else?” The answer: “Not a soul. But shut up! You can't even say God's name in this trashed place.”
Listen up: God gives the orders. He's gonna smash the big houses into smithereens and the little houses into bits.

Would you ever race horses on a rocky field? Or plow the sea with oxen? Of course not! You'd wreck the horses and drown the oxen. And yet, you've made a total mess of justice and turned righteousness into a joke, bragging about your lame achievements, beating up on the weak, and crowing, “Look at me! I'm so awesome!”

“So enjoy it while it lasts, you Israelites. I'm sending a foreign army after you,”—this is your God speaking, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies—“and they're going to completely wreck you, from one end of the country to the other.”

Amos.title: God's Final Warning & A Prophet's Clapback
paragraphs: So, God, my boss, showed me this crazy vision. He was about to unleash a massive swarm of locusts. The first harvest, which was for the king, was already done, and the next round of crops was just starting to grow. Then, these locusts just devoured everything green. Like, not even a single blade of grass was left. Wild.
I was like, 'Yo, God, my Master! Hold up a sec. What's gonna happen to Jacob's crew? They're just a small bunch.'
And God was like, 'Aight, bet.'
He said, 'It's not gonna go down like that.'
Then God showed me another vision. And whoa! My Master God was summoning a firestorm. It literally torched the entire ocean and then started burning up the Promised Land. It was intense.
I yelled out again, 'God, my Master! Please, chill! What about Jacob's people? They're so little!'
God caved again.
'Fine, this won't happen either,' my Master God said.
Then God showed me this vision: My Master was standing by a wall, holding a plumb line.
God asked me, 'What do you see, Amos?'
I said, 'A plumb line.'
Then my Master said, 'Check it. I've put a plumb line right in the middle of my people, Israel. I've let them off the hook for the last time. This is it!
'Isaac's sketchy sex-and-religion shrines will be wrecked, and Israel's unholy shrines will be smashed to bits. I'm coming for King Jeroboam's family with my sword.'
Then Amaziah, the priest at the Bethel shrine, snitched to King Jeroboam of Israel.
'Amos is plotting against you from inside Israel. His words are gonna tear the country apart. He needs to be shut down. You know what he's saying?
'Jeroboam will be killed. Israel is gonna get exiled.'

Then Amaziah confronted Amos, saying, 'Look, prophet, get out of here! Go back to Judah where you came from! Do your preaching there. But no more preaching at Bethel! Don't show your face here again. This is the king's personal chapel, a royal shrine.'
But Amos clapped back at Amaziah: 'I never planned on being a preacher. I was a cattle rancher and I took care of trees. Then God pulled me off the farm and said, 'Go preach to my people Israel.'
'So listen to what God is saying. You're telling me, 'Don't preach to Israel. Don't say anything against Isaac's family.' But this is what God is telling you:
'Your wife will become a prostitute in this town. Your kids will be killed. Your land will be sold off. You'll die homeless and alone. And Israel will be dragged off into exile, far from home.'

Amos.title: God's Done Playing Games
paragraphs: God, my Master, showed me this vision. It was a bowl of fresh fruit.
He asked me, “Amos, what do you see?”
I was like, “A bowl of fresh, ripe fruit.”
God said, “Exactly. And just like that fruit is at its end, I’m calling it quits with my people Israel. I’m done pretending everything is okay.”
“The royal crew will be wailing when it all goes down,” says my Master God. “Bodies will be lying everywhere. It’ll be grim. Hush!”

Yo, listen up, you who stomp on the vulnerable and treat poor people like they’re nothing. You’re the ones saying, “When’s payday so I can go splurge? How long till the weekend so I can party?” You’re stingy and greedy, never doing an honest day's work. You totally use the poor, and when you’re done with them, you just toss them aside.

God is making a promise, and He’s serious. He swears, “I’m keeping a list of every single bad thing they’ve done.” This promise is gonna shake the whole world and make everyone cry. It’s gonna hit like a massive flood that wrecks everything and leaves a huge mess behind.

“On the day of judgment, you better watch out!” This is a message from God, my Master. “I’ll make the sun go dark at noon. The whole earth will be blacked out in the middle of the day. I’ll turn your parties into funerals and every song you sing will be a sad one. Everyone will be in rags, looking totally wrecked. Think about the worst thing you can imagine—like your only son getting murdered. That’s how bad Judgment Day will be, and even worse.

“Oh yeah, Judgment Day is coming!” says my Master God. “I’m gonna send a famine across the whole country. But it’s not a famine for food or water. It’s a famine for my Word. People will be wandering all over, from north to east, desperate to hear a word from God—but they won’t find it.

“On that day, even the popular pretty girls and the strong young guys will be fainting because they’re so thirsty for a word from God. And so will the people who worship fake gods, saying stuff like ‘I swear by the god of Dan!’ Their lives are gonna completely fall apart. No coming back from it.”

Amos.title: God's Final Word: No Escape & A Crazy Comeback
paragraphs: I saw the Lord standing by the altar, and He was like, 'Yo, smash the tops of the pillars so the whole place shakes. The roof is about to crash down on everyone, and anyone left standing, I'm taking them out. No cap, no one's escaping. If they dig down to the underworld, I'll drag 'em up. If they climb to the stars, I'll pull 'em down. If they hide out on Mount Carmel, I'll hunt them down and bring them back. If they dive to the bottom of the ocean, I'll send a sea monster to swallow them whole. If they get captured by their enemies, I'll send a sword to finish the job. I've decided I'm here to bring the pain, not to help.'

My Master, the Lord of Angel Armies, just touches the earth and it trembles. The whole world is in mourning. The land swells up like the Nile when it floods, and then it goes down again, just like the great river of Egypt. God is building His palace with towers that soar into the sky, with its foundation firm on the earth. He calls for the waters of the ocean, and they come, and then He pours them out over the land. The Lord, your God, does all this.

My Master, the Lord of Angel Armies, just touches the earth and it trembles. The whole world is in mourning. The land swells up like the Nile when it floods, and then it goes down again, just like the great river of Egypt. God is building His palace with towers that soar into the sky, with its foundation firm on the earth. He calls for the waters of the ocean, and they come, and then He pours them out over the land. The Lord, your God, does all this.
'Do you Israelites really think you're better than the Cushites who live far away?' This is God's decree.

'Aren't I involved with all nations? Didn't I bring Israel up from Egypt, the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Arameans from Kir? But for real, you can be sure that I, the Lord and Master, have my eyes on this sinful kingdom. I'm going to wipe it off the face of the earth. But, I won't completely destroy Jacob's family.' That's God's decree.

'I'm still the one in charge here. I'm about to toss Israel into a giant sieve among all the nations and shake them good. I'm shaking out all the sin and all the sinners. No real grain will be lost, but all the sinners will be sifted out and thrown away—all those people who say, 'Nothing bad will ever happen to us. It won't even get close.'

'But on that judgment day, I'm going to restore David's house, which has fallen apart. I'll patch up the holes in the roof, replace the broken windows, and fix it up like new. David's people will be strong again and will take over what's left of their enemy Edom, plus all the other nations under my rule.' This is God's decree. And He will do it.
'Yeah, for real, it won't be long now.' God's decree.

'Things are going to happen so fast it'll make your head spin, one thing right after another. You won't be able to keep up. Everything will be happening all at once—and everywhere you look, blessings! Blessings pouring down like wine from the mountains and hills. I'll make everything right again for my people Israel:'

'They'll rebuild their ruined cities. They'll plant vineyards and drink good wine. They'll tend their gardens and eat fresh vegetables. And I'll plant them, plant them in their own land. They'll never again be uprooted from the land I've given them.'
God, your God, says so.

Obadiah.title: Edom's Ultimate Downfall: A Prophecy
paragraphs: So, here's the deal with Edom, straight from God. A messenger went to the nations that don't follow God and said, 'Get ready to fight Edom!'

God's telling Edom, 'Listen, I'm about to make you irrelevant, the most looked-down-on nation. You think you're all that, living up in the mountains, thinking no one can touch you. But you're wrong. Even if you were as high as an eagle, I'd bring you down.' And that's a promise from God.

'If thieves came, they'd take everything, right? Well, Esau's going to be completely wrecked. Your allies will turn on you, your friends will betray you, and your world will fall apart. You won't see it coming. So don't be shocked when I get rid of all the wise and powerful people in Edom. Your heroes will abandon you, and no one will be left in your mountains. This is all because of how you treated your brother, Jacob. You'll be disgraced and forgotten. When foreigners attacked Jerusalem and took your brother's people, you just stood there and watched. You were just as bad as them. You shouldn't have celebrated their suffering or taken advantage of them when they were at their lowest. You shouldn't have blocked their escape or handed over the survivors.'

'God's day of judgment is coming for all nations. What you've done will be done to you. It's coming back to hit you. Just like you partied on my holy mountain, all the other nations will face God's anger. They'll be completely destroyed. But on Mount Zion, there will be safety. Jacob's family will get back everything that was taken from them. They'll be like a fire, and Esau's family will be like straw, completely burned up.' God has spoken.

Then, people from the south will take over Edom's mountains, and people from the foothills will take over the Philistine's land. They'll reclaim the lands of Ephraim and Samaria, and Benjamin will take Gilead. The exiled Israelites will return and take over the land of Canaan, all the way to Zarephath. And the exiles from Jerusalem will return and take over the southern cities. The survivors on Mount Zion will rule over the mountains of Esau, and it will be a kingdom that honors God.

Jonah.title: Running From God & Getting Swallowed by a Fish
paragraphs: A while back, God hit up this guy named Jonah, son of Amittai, with a message: "Yo, get up and head over to the huge city of Nineveh. You need to call them out. They're acting up, and I'm not gonna let it slide anymore."

But Jonah was like, "Nah," and bounced in the complete opposite direction, toward Tarshish, trying to ghost God. He went down to the port of Joppa, found a boat going to Tarshish, paid for his ticket, and hopped on. He was trying to get as far away from God as possible.
But God was not having it and whipped up a crazy storm at sea, with waves that were seriously massive.

The ship felt like it was about to snap in half. The sailors were freaking out, praying like crazy to their own gods. They started chucking all the cargo overboard to make the ship lighter. Meanwhile, Jonah had gone down below deck to catch some Zs. Dude was completely knocked out. The captain found him and was like, “Bro, what are you doing? Sleeping?! Get up and pray to your god! Maybe your god will notice we're in deep trouble and save us.”
Then the sailors were all like, “Okay, we need to figure out who’s to blame for this mess. Let's draw straws to see which one of us is the reason for this disaster.”
So they drew straws, and guess who got the short one? Yep, Jonah.
They immediately started grilling him: “Spill it. Why is this happening? What’s your job? Where are you from? What’s your country? Who are your people?”
He told them, “I’m a Hebrew. I worship God, the God of heaven who created the sea and the land.”
When they heard that, the sailors got legit scared and were like, “Dude, what have you done?!” They put two and two together and realized he was on the run from God.
They asked him, “So what are we supposed to do with you to make this storm chill out?” By then, the sea was going absolutely wild.
Jonah said, “Just throw me overboard. The sea will calm down then. It’s all my fault. This whole storm is because of me. Get rid of me, and you get rid of the storm.”
But they were like, no way. The sailors tried to row back to land, but they weren't getting anywhere. The storm just kept getting crazier and crazier.
So they prayed to God, saying, “Oh, God! Please don’t let us die because of this guy, and don’t hold us responsible for his death. You’re God. You do what you think is right.”
Then they picked Jonah up and threw him into the sea. And just like that, the sea went totally calm.
The sailors were shook. They weren't scared of the sea anymore, but they were in total awe of God. They started worshiping God, made a sacrifice, and promised to follow him.
Then God sent a giant fish to swallow Jonah. And Jonah was just chilling in the fish's stomach for three days and three nights.

Jonah.title: My Deep Sea Prayer Got Answered!
paragraphs: Then Jonah prayed to his God from inside the fish.
He prayed:

“I was in major trouble, like, deep, and I cried out to God, and for real, He answered me. From the belly of the grave, I screamed, ‘Help!’ and You heard my cry. You basically threw me into the deep end of the ocean, into a watery grave, with massive waves crashing over me. I was like, ‘It’s over. I’ve been totally canceled, thrown out of Your sight. I’ll never get to see Your Holy Temple again.’ The ocean had me in a chokehold. The abyss grabbed me and held on tight. My head was all tangled in seaweed at the bottom of the sea, where the mountains start. I was as far down as you can go, and the gates were slamming shut on me forever—but then You pulled me up from that grave, alive, O God, my God! When my life was lowkey slipping away, I remembered God, and my prayer actually made it to You, all the way to Your Holy Temple. People who worship fake gods are walking away from their one true love. But I’m worshiping You, God, shouting out my thanks! And I’m gonna do what I promised. Salvation is from God, no cap.”
Then God had a word with the fish, and it vomited Jonah right onto the beach.

Jonah.title: Nineveh's Ultimate Glow-Up
paragraphs: Then God hit up Jonah a second time: “Aight, get up and get going to that huge city, Nineveh. You gotta tell them what’s up. They’re seriously messing up, and I can’t just let it slide anymore.”
This time, Jonah actually listened and headed straight for Nineveh, following God’s instructions exactly.
Nineveh was massive, like, legit huge—it would take three whole days just to walk from one side to the other.
Jonah walked into the city for a day and started preaching his message: “In 40 days, Nineveh is gonna be totally wrecked.”

The people of Nineveh actually listened and believed God. They called for a fast across the whole city and everyone, from the richest CEO to the most random person, started wearing these scratchy burlap clothes to show they were sorry. Everyone did it—rich and poor, famous and obscure, leaders and followers.

When the king of Nineveh heard the news, he got right off his throne, took off his fancy royal robes, put on burlap, and sat in the dirt. Then he sent out a city-wide alert, approved by him and his cabinet: “Nobody eats or drinks anything. Not people, not even your pets or your farm animals. Everyone—people and animals—has to wear burlap and just cry out to God for help. Everybody needs to do a complete 180, stop living their messed-up lives, and quit all the violence. Who knows? Maybe God will see us, change His mind, and not be so mad at us. Maybe He’ll let us live!”
God saw what they did, that they had actually turned away from their evil ways. So He changed His mind. The disaster He said He was going to bring down on them? He didn’t do it.

Jonah.title: Jonah Gets Salty About God's Mercy
paragraphs: Jonah was seriously ticked off. He totally lost his cool and started yelling at God, "God! I knew it! Back when I was still at home, I had a feeling this would happen! That's why I bounced to Tarshish! I knew you were all about grace and mercy, super patient, loaded with love, and always ready to cancel punishment and switch to forgiveness mode in a heartbeat!"
"So, God, if you're not gonna take them out, then just take me out! I'd be better off dead!"
God was like, "Dude, what do you have to be so angry about?"
But Jonah just stormed off. He left the city, went east, and sat there pouting. He threw together a little shelter out of branches and sat in the shade, waiting to see what would happen to the city.

Then God made a big leafy plant sprout up. It grew over Jonah to give him some shade and help him chill out. Jonah was actually pretty happy about it and was enjoying the shade. Things were starting to look up.

But then God sent a worm. By the next morning, the worm had chewed through the plant, and it withered. When the sun came up, God sent a scorching hot wind from the east. The sun was beating down on Jonah's head, and he felt like he was going to pass out. He prayed to die again: "I'm better off dead!"
Then God said to Jonah, "Do you really have any right to be this mad about a plant?"
Jonah shot back, "Yeah, I do! I'm angry enough to die!"

God said, "Seriously? How can you go from being happy to furious overnight about a simple plant that you did nothing for? You didn't plant it or water it. It grew one night and was gone the next. So why can't I change my mind about Nineveh? It's a huge city with over 120,000 people who are basically like kids and don't even know right from wrong yet, not to mention all the innocent animals."

Micah.title: God's About to Drop the Hammer
paragraphs: This is the message God gave to Micah from Moresheth. It happened back when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah. It was all about the drama going down in Samaria and Jerusalem.
Listen up, everyone! Earth, you and everyone on it, pay attention: The Lord GOD is about to testify against you, coming straight from His holy temple.

Look, here He comes! God is on the move from His place! He's striding across the highest mountains. The mountains are literally melting under His feet, and the valleys are splitting wide open, like wax in a fire or water rushing downhill. This is all happening because of Jacob's screw-up, because the house of Israel messed up. You ask what Jacob's big sin is? Just look at Samaria—it's a giant shrine! And what about Judah's high places? Isn't Jerusalem the source of that problem?

“So I’m about to turn Samaria into a pile of rubble in a field, a place for planting vineyards. I’ll dump its stones into the valley and strip its foundations bare. All its idols will be smashed to pieces, and all the money it earned from its religious prostitution will be burned up. I’ll destroy all its images. Since it collected its 'wages' like a prostitute, it will be carried off like a prostitute's earnings.”

Because of this, I'm going to weep and wail. I'll go around barefoot and stripped of my clothes. I'll howl like a jackal and moan like an owl. Her wound is incurable; it has spread all the way to Judah. It has reached the gate of my people, all the way to Jerusalem itself.

Don't announce it in Gath, don't cry at all. In Beth Ophrah, roll in the dust. Pass on, you who live in Shaphir, in nakedness and shame. The one who lives in Zaanan won't come out. The wailing of Beth Ezel will take away its standing from you. The people of Maroth are writhing in pain, waiting for something good, but disaster has come down from the LORD, even to the gate of Jerusalem. You who live in Lachish, harness the fastest horses to the chariots. You were the beginning of sin for the Daughter of Zion, because Israel's transgressions were found in you. So you will give parting gifts to Moresheth Gath. The houses of Achzib will be a lie to the kings of Israel. I will bring a conqueror against you who live in Mareshah. The glory of Israel will come to Adullam. Shave your head in mourning for the children you love. Make yourselves as bald as an eagle, for they will be taken from you into exile.

Micah.title: God's Plan vs. Theirs: It's Over
paragraphs: It's so over for you guys who lie in bed dreaming up ways to do people wrong. First thing in the morning, you're up and at 'em, using all your energy to make it happen. You see a field you like, you just grab it. You find a house you want, you just take it. You bully a guy and his whole family, only seeing people for what you can get from them. But God is so done. He's like, "I've got some plans of my own, and it's a disaster with your name on it because of all this evil you're into. You're all on the chopping block now. There's no getting away from this one. It's your doomsday." People are gonna make up roast tracks about you, and you'll be the ones singing the blues: 'We're totally wrecked, our homes and lands are being auctioned off. They're taking everything and leaving us with nothing! It's all going to the highest bidder.' And when that happens, there will be no one to have your back, no one to speak up for you when you're facing God's judgment.

"Stop preaching," the preachers are saying. "Don't preach all that negative stuff. Nothing bad is gonna happen to us. Why are you talking like this to Jacob's family? Does God just lose his temper? Is this really how He acts? Isn't He on the side of good people? Doesn't He help those who hustle?"

"'Good people'? Seriously? You're the real enemy of my people! You jump people who are just out for a chill evening walk. You literally take the coats off their backs like you're looting in a war zone. You force the women of my people out of their own nice homes. You turn their kids into victims, leaving them exposed to all kinds of messed-up stuff. Get out of here, all of you. This isn't your chill spot anymore! You've contaminated this place, and now you're contaminated—totally ruined! But hey, if some guy showed up with a charming smile and a smooth tongue, lying 24/7 like, 'I'll preach you a sermon on how to get anything you want from God: more cash, the best wine... you name it'—you'd make him your personal preacher on the spot.

"But I'm calling a meeting, Jacob. I want everyone back—every last survivor of Israel. I'm gonna gather them all in one place, like a whole flock of sheep in a pen, like cattle in a corral—a massive crowd of people heading home! Then I, God, will bust open all the gates and lead them out into freedom. They'll follow their King. And I'll be right there at the front, leading the way."

Micah.title: God vs. Corrupt Leaders: It's a Showdown
paragraphs: Then I said:

“Alright, listen up, you so-called leaders of Jacob and Israel. Do you even know what justice is? Seriously? You guys hate what's good and love what's evil. Isn't justice, like, your main job? But instead, you're skinning my people alive, ripping the meat right off their bones. You break their bones, chop them up, and throw them in a pot like you're making some kind of messed-up stew.
But a time is coming when you'll be crying out to God for help, and He's gonna leave you on read. He's gonna turn His back on you because of all the messed-up stuff you've done.

And here's God's message to the prophets who are straight-up lying to my people: As long as they're getting paid and eating good, they're all like, 'Life is amazing! Peace and love, everyone!' But the second you stop paying them or disagree with them, their 'God bless' turns into 'God damn' real quick. So, guess what? You're going blind. You won't see a thing. You'll be living in the shadows, completely clueless. The sun is setting on you prophets. Your time in the spotlight is over. From now on, it's all darkness. The visionaries will be confused, and the experts will be all mixed up. They'll hide behind their reputations and make lame excuses for not knowing God.
But me? I'm filled with God's power. I've got His Spirit of justice and strength, and I'm ready to call out Jacob for their crimes and Israel for their sin.

You leaders of Jacob and Israel are a piece of work. You laugh at justice and twist the truth. You're building up your precious city, Zion, on the backs of the people you've killed, and expanding Jerusalem with your crimes. The judges are taking bribes, the priests are selling their teachings like merch, and the prophets are preaching for cash. And all the while, you're pretending to be tight with God, saying, 'We've got God on our side. He'll protect us.' Because of people like you, Zion will be turned back into a farm, Jerusalem will become a pile of rubble, and instead of the Temple on the mountain, there will just be a bunch of scraggly trees.

Micah.title: The Ultimate Comeback Story
paragraphs: But look, when it all goes down, God's Temple on the mountain is gonna be the main attraction, towering over everything else. People from all over will be flooding in, and nations will be like, 'Yo, let's go up to God's mountain, to the Temple of the God of Jacob. He'll show us how to really live.' The realest teaching is gonna come from Zion, God's truth straight from Jerusalem. He's gonna sort out all the drama between nations and settle fights from far away. They'll trade their weapons for garden tools—swords into shovels, spears into rakes. Nations will stop fighting and forget how to go to war. Everyone will just be chilling in their own backyard, safe and sound. The Commander of Heaven's Armies said it, and He's not kidding.
Meanwhile, everyone else is just doing whatever, picking their own gods. But us? We're sticking with our God, staying loyal forever.

'On that day,' God says, 'I'm gonna gather up everyone who's been hurt and kicked out, all the ones I had to discipline. I'll take the broken ones and make them an elite crew. The ones who were lost will become a super strong nation. And I'll be ruling from Mount Zion, from now until forever.'
And you guys, the stragglers of Jerusalem, just trying to get by in your run-down neighborhoods: the old glory is coming back. Jerusalem is gonna be the center of the kingdom again.

So why are you all freaking out? Don't you have a king? Is he slacking off or something, making you panic like a woman in labor? Well, go on, scream and cry, Daughter Jerusalem. It's gonna feel like childbirth. You'll be kicked out of the city, forced to camp out in the open. Then you'll end up in Babylon. But here's the plot twist: what you lose in Jerusalem, you'll get back in Babylon. God will rescue you and give you a fresh start, right from under your enemies' noses.

But for now, a bunch of godless nations are teaming up against you. They're saying, 'Let's take her down while she's weak! Let's see Zion get humiliated.' These haters have no clue what God is actually up to. They don't realize He's forging His people, like separating wheat from the chaff, or refining gold.

So get up, Daughter of Zion! It's time to get refined. I'm making you an unstoppable force, God's own wrecking ball to smash these godless nations. You'll bring all their stolen goods back as a holy offering to God, all their wealth to the Master of the whole earth.

Micah.title: The Small-Town King with the Ultimate Glow-Up
paragraphs: But for now, brace yourselves, Jerusalem. It's about to get rough. The enemy has you surrounded, and they're going to totally humiliate Israel's king, treating him like dirt.

But yo, listen up. Bethlehem, from David's old stomping grounds—you might be considered a nobody, the runt of the litter. But out of you is gonna come the leader who will shepherd Israel. And this ain't some random new guy; his family line goes way, way back. For a while, Israel's gonna be scattered and in a bad spot, until the time comes for the new birth. Then all the scattered family will come back home to Israel. He'll stand strong, leading with God's power, shining with the majesty of God's name. And everyone will be safe and sound, because the whole world will see how great he is—the ultimate Peacemaker.

But yo, listen up. Bethlehem, from David's old stomping grounds—you might be considered a nobody, the runt of the litter. But out of you is gonna come the leader who will shepherd Israel. And this ain't some random new guy; his family line goes way, way back. For a while, Israel's gonna be scattered and in a bad spot, until the time comes for the new birth. Then all the scattered family will come back home to Israel. He'll stand strong, leading with God's power, shining with the majesty of God's name. And everyone will be safe and sound, because the whole world will see how great he is—the ultimate Peacemaker.

And if some bully nation like Assyria tries to invade our land, don't even sweat it. We'll have leaders ready to shut them down, send them packing, and keep an eye on them. This shepherd-style rule will stretch all the way to Assyria and any other wannabe tough guys. Our shepherd-ruler will be our hero, saving us from any enemy, old or new, who tries to mess with our home.

The leftover crew from Jacob's family will be like a fresh start among all the other nations. They'll be like dew from God, like rain showers that just show up without being on the weather app—totally unplanned and out of human control.

Yeah, this small group from Jacob will be a force among the nations. Like a lion among other wild animals, like a young lion in a field of sheep—it just takes what it wants, and no one can stop it. You'll crush your enemies, and they'll be gone for good!

"God says, 'A day is coming when I'm getting rid of all your weapons of war. For real. I'll destroy your war horses and your chariots. I'll tear down your military bases and flatten your forts. I'll get rid of all your fake religion and your dark magic stuff. I'm gonna smash all your idols and sacred poles you've been worshiping. You're done trying to control everything and worshiping the stuff you make. I'll rip out all your corrupt centers of power and destroy anyone who defies me. With some serious anger, I'm gonna wipe out all the godless nations that refused to listen.'"

Micah.title: God's Got a Complaint... And He's Not Holding Back
paragraphs: Alright, listen up, God's laying it all out.

"Get ready for court. If you've got a beef, tell it to the mountains; make your case to the hills. And now, you mountains, listen to God's case; you, Earth's jury, pay attention—'cause I'm bringing charges against my own people. I'm building a case against Israel."

"My people, how have I wronged you? Have I been a burden, worn you out? Seriously, tell me! I'm the one who got you out of that terrible life in Egypt; I paid a high price to free you from slavery. I sent Moses to lead you—and Aaron and Miriam too! Don't you remember what King Balak of Moab tried to pull, and how Balaam son of Beor flipped the script on him? Remember all those stories from Shittim to Gilgal. You gotta keep all of God's salvation stories fresh in your mind."

So, how do I even show up before God and give Him the respect He deserves? Should I roll up with a ton of offerings, like some prime year-old calves? Would God be impressed with thousands of rams, or like, rivers of olive oil? Would He be moved if I sacrificed my firstborn, my own precious kid, just to cancel out my sin?

But for real, He's already made it super clear how to live, what to do, and what He's looking for. It's actually pretty simple: Do what's right and fair to others, be compassionate and loyal in your love, and don't take yourself too seriously—take God seriously.
Yo, pay attention! God's calling out the city! If you know what's good for you, you'll listen. So listen up, everyone! This is major.

"You really expect me to ignore the disgusting amount of money you've made by cheating and being fake? You think I'm cool with your shady deals and sneaky plans? I'm so over the rich and powerful bullying their way through life with bluffs and lies. I'm done. Starting now, it's over for you. You'll pay for your sins, every last bit. No matter how much you get, it'll never be enough—you'll always feel empty inside. No matter how hard you grind, you'll have nothing to show for it—just a bankrupt life and a wasted soul. You'll plant a lawn but never get to enjoy it. You'll make jelly but never get to taste it. You'll press apples but never drink the cider. You've been living by the messed-up standards of King Omri and the trashy lifestyle of Ahab's family. Since you've been blindly following their trends, I'm about to make you bankrupt. Your whole way of life will become a joke, something people laugh at. Your lives will be seen as pointless and fake."

Micah.title: Down But Not Out: The Ultimate Comeback Story
paragraphs: Man, I'm just so over it, totally bummed out. It's like when you go looking for a decent snack and the pantry is completely empty. There's literally not one good person left. It feels like decent people have gone extinct. Everyone's just out for themselves, preying on each other like animals.

They've all mastered the art of being terrible. Corrupt leaders are always looking for a handout, and the super-rich make sure they always get their way. The people who seem the best are actually the most toxic, and the so-called top-tier are just trash. But that's all about to end. It's judgment time. Just watch them all get exposed and shamed. Don't trust your neighbor, don't even tell your secrets to your best friend. You gotta watch what you say, even with your own spouse. Whole neighborhoods and families are just falling apart. The closer people are to you—your own kids, your in-laws—the worse it can get. Your own family can turn into your biggest enemy.
But me? I'm not giving up. I'm sticking around to see what God's gonna do. I'm waiting for God to come through and make things right. I'm counting on Him to hear me out.

So, to my enemies, don't celebrate just yet. I might be down, but I'm definitely not out. Yeah, I'm sitting in the dark right now, but God is my light. I can handle God being angry with me. I messed up, I sinned, so I deserve it. But I know it won't last forever. He's on my team and He's going to get me out of this mess. He'll flip the switch and show me His plan. I'll finally see the big picture and how He was right all along. And my enemies will see it too and be totally humiliated—yeah, disgraced. The same enemies who kept mocking me, asking, 'So where's this God of yours now?' I'm gonna see them get taken down like trash in the street with my own two eyes.

Oh, that's gonna be a legendary day! A day to rebuild your city, a day to finally stretch your wings and be free. All your people who were scattered everywhere will come back home, old friends and family from all over the world, from Assyria in the east to Egypt in the west, from across the oceans and over the mountains. But for everyone else, it's gonna be the opposite—a total ghost town—all because of how they chose to live and the messed-up things they did.

God, please lead your people with your shepherd's staff, your precious flock that belongs only to you. Let them live safe and sound, surrounded by your goodness. Let them thrive in the best places, just like in the good old days. Bring back the same insane miracles you did when we escaped from Egypt. And as for the nations that don't follow you? Put them in their place. Humble them, shut them up, and leave them clueless. Make them crawl away like snakes and bugs, coming out of their hiding spots to face our God. Make them tremble with a holy fear.

Where is another god who even compares to you? You wipe our slate clean of all guilt, choosing to ignore the past sins of your precious people. You don't hold on to your anger forever, because showing mercy is your thing. That's what you love to do most. And I know your compassion is coming for us. You'll crush all our wrongdoing. You'll throw our sins into the deepest part of the ocean. You'll keep your promise to our ancestor Jacob and continue to show the same love you showed to Abraham—everything you promised our ancestors a long, long time ago.

Nahum.title: God's Ultimate Clapback on Nineveh
paragraphs: A report on the whole Nineveh situation, just how God showed it to Nahum of Elkosh:

God does NOT play. Seriously, don't mess with Him. He gets back at His haters and stands up to anyone who comes against Him, full force. But, like, He's not just flying off the handle. He's got insane power, but He's patient with it. Still, nobody gets away with anything. Sooner or later, you gotta pay up. You see tornadoes and hurricanes? That's just the dust kicking up where He walks. He can literally tell the ocean to dry up, and it does. All the rivers? Gone. The mountains of Bashan and Carmel? Total glow-down. The forests of Lebanon? Wilted. Mountains are shook, hills basically melt. The whole planet is freaking out in front of Him. The whole world is in a full-blown panic. Who could even handle that kind of anger? Who can stand up to that fire? His rage is like a volcano erupting, and He smashes boulders like nothing.

But here's the flip side: God is good. He's your safe house when times get rough. He sees you when you're looking for help, and He's got you, no matter how bad things are. But for those who think they can just chill in their own little escape plans? Nah, He wipes them right off the map. You can't ghost God. So why even try to scheme against Him? He's shutting all that down. If you're a troublemaker, you don't get a round two. You're like a pile of dry leaves someone just poured gasoline on. Poof. Up in flames.

But here's the flip side: God is good. He's your safe house when times get rough. He sees you when you're looking for help, and He's got you, no matter how bad things are. But for those who think they can just chill in their own little escape plans? Nah, He wipes them right off the map. You can't ghost God. So why even try to scheme against Him? Nineveh is basically a headquarters for plotting against God. It's a think tank for lies that trick people and then stab them in the back.
And God's got a message about this: 'Yo, even if you're on top of the world, getting all the likes and the votes, you're about to get completely wrecked.'

'Judah, I know I've put you through it, for real. But I'm done with that. From now on, I'm breaking that heavy thing off your neck and using it for firewood. I'm cutting you loose from whatever was holding you down.'

God’s orders on Nineveh:

'You're at the end of the line. It's game over for Nineveh. I'm tearing down your temple. Your gods and goddesses? Straight in the trash. I'm digging your grave myself. It's gonna be an unmarked one. You're a nobody—nah, you're less than a nobody!'

Look! Someone's running over the mountains—a messenger with the best news: peace! It's a holiday, Judah! Go celebrate! Worship God and get right with Him again! You don't have to worry about this enemy anymore. They're officially cancelled. Close the book on them.

Nahum.title: Nineveh's Epic Takedown
paragraphs: The wrecking ball is coming! Post your guards, stock up on supplies. Get yourselves together, 'cause it's time for the main event.
God's restoring the honor of Jacob, the honor of Israel. Israel's been through it, for real. They've been to hell and back.

Their weapons are glinting in the sun, the soldiers looking fresh in their battle gear. The chariots are all polished and shiny, ready to roll out. It's like a whole forest of sharp spears, looking deadly on the horizon. The chariots are flooding the streets, taking over the public squares, glowing like torches in the sun, zipping around like lightning. The Assyrian king tries to get his squad together, but they're just tripping over themselves. They rush to the walls to stop the invasion, but it's a wrap. Soldiers are pouring through the gates. The palace is getting wrecked. It's over pretty quick: Nineveh is getting stripped bare, totally doomed. The maids and slaves are crying, sounding like doves, beating their chests in sadness. Nineveh is like a bathtub with the plug pulled. People are yelling, "Do something! Do something!" but it's too late. Nineveh is empty in no time—nothing left. Then you hear other shouts: "Grab the silver! Grab the gold! It's a free-for-all! Take whatever you want!" It's all doom, damnation, and desolation. Hearts are sinking, knees are weak, people are throwing up, and everyone's face is pale. So, what happened to that big, bad Assyrian lion and all those so-called cute little cubs? What about the lion and lioness, all cozy with their cubs, acting so tough and fearless? What about the lion who always brought back fresh meat for his lioness and cubs, with the den piled high with bloody food for their royal feast?

Their weapons are glinting in the sun, the soldiers looking fresh in their battle gear. The chariots are all polished and shiny, ready to roll out. It's like a whole forest of sharp spears, looking deadly on the horizon. The chariots are flooding the streets, taking over the public squares, glowing like torches in the sun, zipping around like lightning. Then you hear other shouts: "Grab the silver! Grab the gold! It's a free-for-all! Take whatever you want!" It's all doom, damnation, and desolation. Hearts are sinking, knees are weak, people are throwing up, and everyone's face is pale. So, what happened to that big, bad Assyrian lion and all those so-called cute little cubs? What about the lion and lioness, all cozy with their cubs, acting so tough and fearless? What about the lion who always brought back fresh meat for his lioness and cubs, with the den piled high with bloody food for their royal feast?

"Assyria, I'm your enemy now," says God, the Commander of Heaven's Armies. "I'm gonna set your chariots on fire. They'll go up in smoke. 'Lion Country' will just be a field of dead bodies. Your whole war business is over—you're officially unemployed. No more wars for you to report, no more victories to brag about. You're out of the war game for good."

Nahum.title: Nineveh's Epic Fail: It's Over
paragraphs: It's over for Murder City—a place full of lies, overflowing with stolen stuff, and totally addicted to violence! You hear the horns blasting, wheels rattling, horses going wild, and chariots swerving all over the place. Horsemen are charging, swords and spears out, and there are dead bodies rotting in the street, piled up like firewood. Bodies are literally in every gutter and alley, blocking every intersection! And the prostitutes! So many prostitutes. This city is fatally attractive, like a witch casting spells, luring whole nations into getting wrecked with its evil.

"I’m your enemy, Nineveh—yeah, me, God of the Angel Armies! I’m gonna rip off those seductive silk robes and put you on blast for the whole world to see. I’ll let every nation see the ugly truth of who you really are and always have been. I’m gonna throw dog poop at you and put you on a stage like an exhibit called ‘Slut on Display.’ Everyone who sees you will be disgusted and say, ‘Nineveh is a total pigsty. What did we ever see in her? Who would even look twice? Ugh!’”

Do you really think you’re better than the Egyptian city of Thebes? It was sitting all proud and unbeatable on the Nile River, protected by the water like a wall. Ethiopia was its guard to the south, and Egypt was to the north. Put and Libya were strong allies, ready to jump in and help. But you know what happened to Thebes, right? The entire city was captured and marched off to a refugee camp. Their babies were smashed to death on the streets for everyone to see. Their best leaders were sold off at auction, and their famous people were put in chains. You can expect the exact same thing, Nineveh. You’ll be stumbling around like a bunch of drunk people, wondering what just hit you, looking for a place to pass out. All your defenses are like peach trees with ripe fruit, ready to be picked. One little shake and the peaches fall right into hungry mouths. Just face it: your soldiers are wimps. You’re a sitting duck. Your borders are wide open like doors, just inviting your enemies to come in. And who’s gonna stop them?

Go ahead, store up water for the siege. Strengthen your defenses. Get back to the basics: work the clay and make some bricks. But sorry, it's too late. Enemy fire is about to burn you up. Swords will chop you to pieces. You’ll be eaten up like locusts.

Yeah, like locusts—which is kinda ironic, because you guys are a plague of locusts yourselves. You’ve multiplied your shops and shopkeepers—more buyers and sellers than there are stars in the sky! A plague of locusts that just cleans out the whole neighborhood and then flies away. Your government officials are locusts, and your brokers and bankers are locusts too. At first, they’re all super helpful, full of smiles and promises. But later, when you come back with questions or problems, you’ll find out they’ve just flown off and are nowhere to be found.

King of Assyria! Your leaders, the ones in charge of taking care of your people, are busy doing everything else but their actual job. They’re failing, and your people are scattered and lost. There’s no one to look after them. You’re past the point of no return. Your wound is fatal. When the story of what happened to you gets out, the whole world will cheer and shout “Encore!” Your cruel evil has leaked into every corner of the world. Everyone has felt it and suffered because of you.
